After a full power-off, I turned them back on and they immediately connected to my phone again. I have no complaints there. One of the really interesting features of these is the ability to turn off the ANC and use them without any cancellation, but they have another unusual mode that I have only seen in one other pair of phones - they have an “ambient sound” mode that you can turn on that dampens the feed in the buds and slightly increases the surrounding noise without turning off the ANC. Assuming the volume is not turned up too loud, this allows for carrying on a conversation without turning off the feed. I will say, though, that listening to my own voice coming through in this mode is disconcerting. I do not know yet how long the battery in these lasts. So far I have not run them all the way down. Included in the box are the phones themselves, a conversion cable so that they can be used with an audio jack (handy when Bluetooth is not an option), a cable for charging, an in-flight audio adapter, several silicone tips fo the buds so you can get the size right, and a protective carry bag. The carry bag is the only complaint I have with the whole package - it offers little protection from drops and crushes. If you only are concerned about keeping everything together and keeping the set very clean, the bag is acceptable, but if you need better protection that consider getting a third-party hard case or use the original packaging box. Sony got these right and even at the price tag these are easy to recommend. They’re comfortable (more comfortable than I expected for ear buds), they have excellent sound and the ANC function is outstanding. I prefer these to my Bose phones and will be using these instead.

title: Excellent Range, Looks Great
text: Growing up I always had a radio in my room. Times are a little different now and I tend to get my music from the Internet, but there are still times when local radio stations are a better choice - particularly during power outages or when getting local news. I have had very good fortune with Sony electronics and computers in the past so I was eager to try this AM/FM tuner and had high expectations. It did not disappoint me. Let me very clear about this unit - it is for AM/FM receiving only. It does not play MP3’s, it doesn’t play CDs and it doesn’t stream from the Internet. It’s just an AM/FM tuner. It does this quite well, though - better than most other tuners I have used in the last several years. Right out of the box, this unit looks nostalgic. It has a classic AM/FM radio look and feel, very similar to a radio my father used to have in his workshop when I was a kid. This is a big plus for me, just for the fact that it takes me back to my childhood. I plugged it in and turned it on, and I immediately tuned to one of the [relatively] local stations. It picked it up and played it very clearly, better than most other tuners I have used in the last 4-5 years. It is definitely better than the car’s radio. I “surfed” the dial and found other stations that I have listened to in the past but thought were out of range and this little radio did a good job of picking them up and playing with minimal static. That’s really all I could ask. It’s not a miracle radio though and it cannot pick up FM stations hundreds of miles away, but it has better range than most I have used recently. I like that it can be used on AC power or on batteries. That will be handy during weather events. I can’t find any real reason to complain about this tuner. It works great and looks great too. It is a little on the pricey side which is par for the course for Sony electronics, but it is a fine tuner that is worth its asking price.

title: Room for Improvement
text: I have worked with a lot of Bluetooth headphones, all of which have their strengths and weaknesses. These headphones by Panasonic are on the less expensive end. The question is whether they are worth the asking price. In my opinion, they could be better and are still priced a little high. Comfort-wise, I do not care for these but this is a personal preference. I like a headphone that fits tightly and presses down on my head, and these are very light-fitting. They adjust well enough and there should not be too much trouble getting these to fit almost any head, but keep in mind that they’re not the type that clamps down tightly. The build quality is sub-par. These are very lightweight and feel quite flimsy and fragile. I found an issue in the sound profile. The bass is good and not too heavy, and that’s good news for me. I dislike strong bass which is good for giving me headaches. The midrange is on target too and the music has some depth. Where the problem lies is in the highs. When listening to music I noticed some distortion in the highs. It’s not in-your-face and it doesn’t ruin the listening experience unless you are really fussy about your music. These will be fine for listening to speech, though. I had no trouble connecting these to my laptop via Bluetooth. These come up quickly and connect without any issue and are ready to go in seconds. These aren’t the absolute fastest connecting phones I have worked with but they are among the faster ones I have used. There’s no protective case for these phones in the box, not even a sleeve. These do fold up nice and compactly but I am not sure what is the point without a case in which to store them. As I write this, the asking price for these phones is $60 which is a bit high in my eyes. If the sound profile was perfect, or if the build quality was higher, I would be more amenable to that price but the truth is that less expensive phones can be found that have a better sound profile and are constructed more solidly - and they have a case. These are not bad phones, but I think they leave much to be desired. The build quality is mediocre, the sound profile is imperfect and the cost is a little high for what is in the box.

title: Very Good in Its Price Range
text: I selected this mouse with the thought that it would be a good travel mouse. I like the feature set, specifically the ability to recharge the mouse instead of replacing the batteries. So far, I have had no issues with this mouse. In the price range, it’s a good one. The mouse comes in a little mesh bag which sets it up nicely for use as a travel mouse. I can toss the whole in my bag and the USB dongle will stay with it even if it slips off the mouse. The mouse quickly connects once the dongle is plugged in, and I have not had any trouble with it. It’s responsive and does not skip or stutter. One of the things about this mouse that stands out to me is actually the shape. Most mice are somewhat arched but do not have enough arch to fit my hand properly. This one is much more arched than most. I still prefer my trackball, but I do not have any issue with using this mouse because the fit in my hand causes less cramping for me. Charging this mouse is fast and easy. It comes with a USB cable and it charges up quickly when plugged in. I have not drained the mouse all the way down and recharged it so I cannot say for sure yet how long it takes to charge it up from empty. I had forgotten how nice it is to have a side-scrolling mouse... This is an inexpensive mouse but that doesn’t mean it’s cheap. It works well and it seems to be well designed. It’s rechargeable which means no spending on batteries, it’s shaped nicely to fit the hand a little better than many and it connects quickly.

title: Aggressive ANC and Balanced Sound Profile
text: I have worked with a lot of headphones, active noise canceling (ANC) phones in particular. ANC phones are interesting in that while they are good at stripping out white noise they frequently do not sound quite right because they twiddle the sound profile, usually in the bass range, to compensate for the sound frequencies they filter out. Also, there are varying levels of ANC, the standard to which others are compared is Bose. This headset by Jabra came as a huge shock to me, both for the very balanced sound profile and the aggressive ANC function. This headset is on-ear, not over-the-ear. Usually I am a bit wary of on-ear headphones as they tend to be a little uncomfortable. These have very soft, leather-like pads and they are actually quite nice – for a while. After about an our of wear they start to get slightly uncomfortable for me, though taking them and shifting them a little makes them fine again. The ANC function is VERY aggressive, approaching the same level as Bose but not quite. It is able to wipe out the sounds of the A/C, a fan, engine noise and more. Like Bose, when these are first turned on the ANC gives the wearer a sensation of pressure on the ears. Using this without feeding in noise, it is possible to enjoy relative quiet when traveling, reading, studying or enjoying similar activities. The sound profile is on point. The bass is present and unmistakable, but it is not pushed forward so much as to dominate the whole profile and drown out the midrange. The midrange is bright and warm, giving music the right depth instead of making it sound like it’s either in a tunnel or in a barrel. The highs are very good – solid but not piercing. Jabra has nailed the sound profile where a lot of others have screwed up. This is also a headset for talking, and call clarity when using with a mobile phone is very good. I have had excellent results using this headset and it has worked extremely well for me. There is a caveat, though – because this headset covers both ears, it is not suitable for use while driving in many jurisdictions. It’s great when in the office, but know your local and state laws if you plan to use it in a motor vehicle. There are two ways to use this headset and connect it. It has built-in Bluetooth and it pairs and connects very quickly with my phone. It also has a USB dongle for connecting to a PC, though it can be connected to the PC via Bluetooth too. My observation there is that volume levels are reduced when connecting to a PC via Bluetooth. The headset comes in a crush-resistant case and includes the USB dongle and a USB cable for charging. I can find little about which to complain with this headset. It does get slightly uncomfortable for extended wear, but it has great ANC and a very balanced sound profile. As a headset it works great for talking, too, and the Bluetooth pairing is fast. This has already become my favorite set of headphones for streaming music, though because of laws where I live I cannot use it as a hands-free set while driving.

title: Good NAS Drive; Can Work in USB Enclosure with Some Effort
text: A NAS is a great way to add storage for the whole network where everything can be reached from any system connected. It is not as simple as a USB mass storage device like a thumb drive, of course, but it addresses a completely different issue. So far, this drive has proven to be a good one, though its reliability remains to be demonstrated over the long haul. I have the 8TB drive, and it is great for dumping huge numbers of videos, music, documents and other media needed across a small network. It is fairly fast too, so streaming video from the NAS to any given device on the network is reasonably smooth as long as the network can handle the bandwidth (keep this detail in mind if you are wanting to stream video over a slower wireless network - the lag isn’t necessarily the drive’s fault). The drive is very quiet, though not silent, and so far seems to stay acceptably cool. I did learn that it does not work all that well in a USB drive enclosure right out of the packaging. I have an enclosure that is capable of handling drives up to 8TB so I decided to try an experiment with the drive when it first arrived. I put it in the enclosure and connected it to my Windows 10 laptop. The system saw the device, and it even saw the drive and recognized the model and serial number, but it was unable to access the drive or even format it. I had more success with my Linux system which recognized the drive and was able to access the partition table and display drive parameters. I did not repartition the drive or create a file system for my experiment though I believe it would have worked. Time will tell if this drive will be reliable over the long haul. Based on my experience so far, it has worked out well and I have had no issues. It’s the largest drive I have worked with and can handle a LOT of data. If you need wide open spaces for your network storage solution (or you are willing to fiddle with it to get it working as a USB solution) this is a good choice.

title: Nostalgia
text: My parents used to have a Polaroid camera and it was everything that we remember those old cameras for – it spat out a white square of plastic that slowly developed into a grainy, faded-looking picture within a few minutes, it was bulky and it had a very distinct sound. It was a great old camera but when Polaroid quit making film for it it became a paperweight. It's nice to see that some of these old cameras are available with film again. That said, there are some oversights with this package. I will start with the two negatives (no pun intended). First, the way the camera was packaged for shipment was sub-par and the package was partially crushed when I received it. It did not appear to be damaged beyond the packaging, but it was a disappointment to open the package and find the merchandise box partially crushed. Second, the camera comes with no film or batteries at all. So, the camera by itself is still a paperweight. It would have been nice to have at least a lower capacity pack for film to get started. The camera came out of the box without a mark on it. It looks to be brand new, in spite of being an older unit. Some of the other reviewers have complained that the camera they received either was scratched up or was partially damaged, but mine is pristine. It's a simple, straightforward device too, and it does not require much thought to use. In use, it works just like it would have when new. It fires the flash, spits out one exposure with that same distinctive sound I remember and the film develops in front of you. The exposure still looks grainy and old when it is all done, but it is a real photograph that does not need a separate printer or software to get a hard copy. This is not the kind of camera a photographer would use, but rather it is for the tourist or enthusiast. Why would you want a camera like this? For me, it is a trip down memory lane to a time years ago, when candid pictures were a part of daily life and the exposures were lined up on the pinboard for all to see without needing a computer or tablet. It is not going to make pictures that look like they could be in a magazine, but it will produce pictures you can enjoy right away.

title: Very Workable Phone & Tablet Stand
text: I have a small stand similar to this one that I use for my phone when I am at the office. It allows me to see who's calling when the phone lights off and it gives me a very consistent place to keep my phone where it is out of the way and in a safe place – no more misplacing my phone. The idea is good, and the design is good, but I have one issue with this stand that keeps it from being ideal. This is a small, aluminum S-shaped stand with a plastic kickstand, designed to hold a tablet, phone or e-reader upright so that you can see the screen without holding it. The kickstand is adjustable with the push of a button and it has almost 360 degrees of movement (though it does not really need much beyond 100 degrees to be useful). It has rubber grommets to make the surface anti-slip and to keep it in place. So far, so good. In the tray of the stand is a rubber insert that serves two purposes. First, it also provides slip resistance so that your device does not move easily. Second, it prevents damage to your device's screen which is important – metal on glass is usually a bad idea when the idea is to keep away scratches. I have used another stand like this that does not have the rubber insert and the first time I put in my phone the metal lip caught the screen protector and cracked it. Be aware that there is not enough clearance between the tray bottom and the surface on which the stand is set up to allow plugging in the device without either cocking it at a weird angle or turning it on its side (or upside down). This is typical with this type of stand and I cannot count this as a flaw. The one issue with this stand is that the rubber tray insert is not permanently attached and it is not secured in the tray at all. When the stand arrived the insert had separated completely and was loose in the box. It does slip back in without issue, but it won't necessarily stay there when you move the stand in transport. Without glue or some other method of modifying the stand there is no way to secure the insert more securely, and this is an unfortunate design flaw. It's not a deal breaker, and it does stay put when the stand is set up so the stand is very usable, but care is required to ensure the insert does not fall out when moving the stand. Other than the tray insert not being securely fastened to the stand, the is a fine little stand and it works well. It's small, easy to pack and move and it provides a stable and easy way to set up even a larger tablet so that it is upright without having to hold it it place. It will see regular use in my house.

title: Small and Strong, but Unbalanced
text: I have worked with a lot of Bluetooth speakers and I have seen a good variety in features and sound quality. I have a set of Monster headphones and they are excellent; I expected the same from this speaker. It’s a good speaker, but it has a weakness in the sound profile. It pairs and connects quickly and without any issue. I was able to connect it to my computer without any problems and it was ready to go in less than 20 seconds. In terms of connection speed via Bluetooth, this one is slightly faster than most. I really like the fact that the speaker has a slider switch for power instead of a button you have to hold down. It makes knowing the speaker is on very simple and it also makes it very simple to power off. This is a big plus to me and is one of the best features in my mind. I tested the sound quality fairly extensively and make a few important observations, most of which were positive but there was one important issue. The speaker has good volume (controlled by the source) and excellent operational range - I went as far as 30’ and there were no cut-outs or crackles, a good sign. The sound profile though is slightly problematic. The bass is strong - very strong - and is enough to dominate the whole sound output. Many speakers and headsets are heavy-handed on the bass, so this is not totally unexpected but is a bit heavy for my tastes. The highs are good and everything is clear and crisp. The midrange is very flat to the point of being practically non-existent, likely because the bass is as high as it is. Because the midrange is so flat, the output has a tendency to be dull and lifeless. This is not a bad speaker and it is a decent choice if you want a small and strong speaker. But, be aware that the sound profile is unbalanced.

title: Excellent Sound Quality and Easy to Connect
text: I listen to a lot of music, usually electronic music though I listen to a little of everything. I have worked with a lot of different speakers and I have gotten very sensitive to the strengths and weaknesses that speakers bring to the table. I had high hopes for this speaker – I have always had excellent results with Yahama products so I expected the same from this speaker. It has not disappointed me. The speaker itself is about the size of a cantaloupe – not huge but not tiny either. It's the right size for a bookshelf or as part of a larger sound system. I did not completely understand what was meant by “MusicCast” until I started working with this speaker. In short, it is a wireless speaker that communicates over a wireless network (not Bluetooth). Using an appropriate device (like an Android tablet) the speaker is easily connected to the network and the software on said computing device allows for turning the speaker on and off and for streaming music to it. My service of choice is Pandora, and I had no trouble at all streaming a channel from Pandora to this speaker. The software comes into its own when you have more than one speaker, all of which get controlled separately and can stream different music from the same source device. So, given a sufficient budget (these speakers are not cheap), you can have different music playing in different rooms, all controlled from the same device. The application is not perfect though I have been able to do everything I want with it – play music from local storage, stream from a service, increase/decrease volume and twiddle the sound profile a bit. The sound quality is excellent, particularly when given a little volume. The bass is solid but not overwhelming which is great – the trend of late is to overdrive the bass which drowns out the rest of the sound profile, so having the bass not overpowering the overall profile is a big plus with me. The midrange is excellent as well and the music has the right depth as a result. The highs are bright and crisp. At lower volumes, the bass washes out which is has been the case with every speaker I have used. At higher volumes, I was unable to get the speaker to distort. I am very happy with this speaker. I primarily use with with my tablet to stream music from Pandora, though it is useful for playing music from other sources too. It is expensive, but the sound quality is definitely there. If you like the idea of being able to add multiple speakers to your sound array and you want to design your sound system from the ground up, this is a good choice.

title: Fun for Casual Get-Togethers
text: A long time ago I had access to a Polaroid Instamatic camera. It was great - snap a picture, it spits out a sheet. Wait about 2 minutes and what you have is a printed photograph. Polaroid is gone now (though the name gets licensed over and over again), and with it went all of the film for the camera that made it so useful. This new camera by Fuji brings back some of the fun of instant photos, though it is by no means perfect and it suffers from some of the same issues the older Polaroid camera had. The idea is very straightforward - point-and-shoot, and the camera ejects an exposure that will develop over a few moments and will be fully developed in approximately 2 minutes. This is great for social events and is a fun way to share candid shots. The camera is very lightweight and it is small too so it is easy to pack and carry with you. There are a few issues with the camera, though, some of which are very much like the old Polaroids of days gone by. The images do come out a bit grainy and are definitely not high resolution. If you are looking for images with nice, clean edge detail and bright, vibrant colors, this is going to disappoint you. Also, the images are really small, a little bigger than a passport picture but not by very much. And finally, the film is relatively expensive, a pack of exposures coming with only 10 slides and costing about $0.60 per exposure. On the plus side, the camera is very easy to use and the camera body itself is not very expensive at all. There are trade-offs with this camera. On one hand, it is super convenient, it’s fun and it’s relatively inexpensive. However, exposure quality is mediocre, pictures are small and on a per-picture basis the exposures are somewhat expensive. To me, the fun factor weighs heavily in favor of this camera and offsets some of the negatives. For social gatherings and recreational events, this is a fun camera and will serve well. Do not expect to have high-end results, though.

title: Good Tripod with One Negative
text: I have worked with several tripods and I have concluded that there are really two distinct classes of camera tripods: there are heavy durable tripods that are designed to be stationary most of the time and take some abuse, and there are those that are much more lightweight and are designed with mobility in mind. There is some that are somewhere in between but to be honest I have seen few of these types. This particular tripod falls under the more lightweight category and is a decent one, though there is one feature about it that gives me some pause. This is a very lightweight tripod and it comes in a nice nylon case, making the whole thing well suited for travel. The whole weighs under 5 lbs. which is great when you have to pack it for moving or need to toss it in the car. No complaints there. It’s easy to work too. The legs work via locking latches and extend in three segments, and I am able to so this with one hand (though it is much easier when using two hands). When the legs are fully extended and the head is raised to the maximum height, the whole stands about 5’ tall which is good for a majority of uses. If you need a taller tripod, please keep this in mind. The head is very smooth and it gives full motion to the camera. It is comparable to most tripod heads I have used in that it allows motion in three directions so that the camera can be oriented in just about any desired direction (though not inverted of course). Motion is smooth and does not require a lot effort, though it is tight enough to prevent the camera from moving when it should not. The head can be “locked” in place via tightening knobs to keep it firmly in place. My one complaint with this tripod is the feet. These are hard plastic feet that can be adjusted to balance the tripod slightly, but each has a hole in the bottom which exposes the end of a leg – a sharp point that is all metal. This is a double-edges sword. On one hand, the feet can allow the tripod to easily move and slide on hard floors if adjusted properly which might be the goal. On some hardwood flooring, though, they gauge the floor and leave permanent marks. I have hardwood flooring in my house and I am extremely careful with this tripod, but this is the only one I have used that poses this problem. I like this tripod, especially for travel and mobility. It is very lightweight and easy to adjust, and of course it is quite affordable. If you have hardwood floors, watch the feet; otherwise, this is a decent tripod that is worth consideration if you need one that travels well.

title: Fine Two-Pack of Cables
text: If you own an iPhone, iPad or one of the newer iPods you are familiar with the need for lightning cables. These are basically special USB cables that are reversible and are specific to Apple electronics. The problem with these cables is that they can be expensive, especially if you go with Apple-branded cables. There are some good third-party cables available, and they represent a good value when compared to Apple cables. I get offered a LOT of lightning cables for review and I have noticed an unpleasant trend: most vendors hawking their cables to not mention MFI certification at all, anywhere, and this is important. This particular cable is clearly marked in the description as certified, so it is worth some consideration on that basis alone when compared to many of the others available. These come in a two-pack, and they are a little more than 3’ in length. These have hard plastic plugs on the end and the length is insulated with a vinyl sheath for protection. So far these have shown no signs of fatigue at the plugs and they work very well. I have been able to charge my phone as well as connect it to iTunes. I attempted to pull the shielding away from the plug and was unable to do so, so I see no risk of exposing the wires inside the casing. I mentioned the certification above, and I will restate that this is a very important feature. Because these cables are certified, they are guaranteed compatible and will work. If you use a cable that is not certified you might get messages on your phone or tablet that the cable is unrecognized and it might not work as desired. I have worked with non-certified cables and sometimes they work while others do not work at all. I have never had a certified cable fail me. If you are looking for a less expensive alternative to Apple-branded cables, make sure you select a product that has been certified to work. This two pack of cables is a good choice; so far, they have given me no trouble at all and they have worked well for me. They are definitely compatible and are made well too. And, getting two of them instead of just one in the package means you can have one in the office and one at home. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Three Good Mounts in One Package
text: I have been looking for the right phone holder for the car after the one I had been using for a good while finally broke on me. The one I had was great; it had a strong suction cup and a large-opening clip that held my phone securely and could also be used as a holder for my TomTom. Since it broke I have been looking for a suitable replacement and I had the opportunity to work with this car mount. Rather, this is a set of car mounts. So far it has performed well for me and it has kept my phone secure while I am driving. There are three separate mounts in this package. The one I use most is the short dashboard mount. I have it mounted on a weighted movable base that I can slide to either end of the dash while I am driving. It holds fairly well and it has not come loose while I am driving. I did discover that the suction cup released after several hours though, which is a problem I have seen with other mounts when using this same base. The second one is a windshield mount with a flexible mounting arm. This is the most flexible and versatile of the mounts, though I am not a fan of this type of mount as the phone tends to jiggle and bounce when the car is in motion. The third one is an air vent mount and I do not use this one as my air vents do not cooperate with it, though it seems to be ok with most vent systems. The mounting brackets are spring-loaded sliders and they provide a good bit of tension when holding the phone in place. The brackets seem to be tight enough to survive the “shake test” for most typical situations though the phone can be shaken loose if you shake the mount hard enough (though this becomes an unrealistic test). It requires two hands to open the brackets which is a good sign that they will hold. The brackets attach to the different mounts via ball joints which give solid flexibility and allow for angling the phone properly. One of the problems I had with another mount was that the ball got chewed up by the bracket assembly so I look for this when I see these types of mounts, and so far the brackets have mounted properly and have proven to be well designed. Most car mounts are of a single type. This is a set, though, so you get not just one type of mount but three that you can use simultaneously, for the price of a single mount. These are made well and they work well, so at the price point this is really hard to beat. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Excellent Rechargeable Wireless Keyboard/Touch Pad; Works with Windows and Linux
text: I have worked with other Rii keyboards and every one of them has worked out well for me. The ones I have used prior to this one have been well suited for portability and are smaller than a standard-sized keyboard. This one is a little bit different – it is still small and it has a nice footprint, but it includes an integrated touch pad. It is also rechargeable, which is not new but it is different in how it works. I am using it to type this review on my Linux laptop. First things first – it is compatible with Windows as well as Linux and Android. I will assume it is compatible with OSX but I have no way to confirm this as I am not a Mac user. This is a wireless keyboard that comes with a USB dongle as well as a direct USB connection that allows it to charge when it needs it. I had hoped that the USB wire would allow for not only charging but for use as a wired keyboard, but this is not the case – the wire is just for charging and nothing more. I suspected that to be the case but it was worth trying. I am not sure yet how long the battery will last, but I do very much appreciate that this keyboard will never need new batteries. I plugged the USB receiver into the system and the keyboard was ready to work immediately. There were no drivers that required installation and no fancy setup procedure. It is literally as simple and plugging it in and turning it on. This keyboard with the integrated mouse pad is about as wide as my 15.6” laptop, so the keys are slightly smaller than that on my laptop but this has not been a problem for me so far. The layout is economized for the space so it is important to realize that the layout takes some getting used to and you are likely to make some typing mistakes at first. I am no fan of touch pads at all, and this one has not won me over either. That said, it works well and it even has a removable tab on it when it comes out of the box that shows hot to work with it. It is very responsive and I like the fact that it is beside the keys and not below so I do not end up inadvertently tapping it. Even though the tab on the pad says to remove it for use, I left it on there because the pad is still very responsive anyway. One really nice plus with this keyboard, to me, is that they keys are not shiny. They have a dull matte finish which makes them very easy to see even under direct light. On my work desk I have a bright lamp that I use to illuminate the whole desk and with some keyboards it makes it difficult to see the keys because of the reflective finish. This keyboard does not have that problem. As I use it more and I wear the keys (especially the space bar) I expect that to gradually change, but for now it is great in that regard. Though this is a small and compact keyboard it works very well for me. I like the feel of the keys, I love the fact that it does not require batteries, the touch pad is convenient when I absolutely need it and the finish is perfect for my working environment. I am very pleased with this keyboard. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Well-Made Messenger Bag
text: I prefer a good messenger bag to a backpack most of the time. I prefer the way a messenger bag looks, how it is organized and how it provides protection to the contents of the bag most of the time, the trade-off being reduced space when compared to a regular-sized backpack. This is a nice bag and I am pleased with it. It recently came in very handy when we were traveling. This is a large, canvas messenger bag. The canvas used is not the heaviest grade canvas I have seen but it is not the lightest or softest either. It seems to be the right balance of durability and softness as the bag is durable and holds up to abuse but is still soft and pliable enough to be workable in most spaces (like crammed behind a car seat). Most messenger bags I have seen of late have used magnets as the closing mechanism and this one does so too. There are two leather straps on the flap that have buckles, but these buckles are strictly decorative. Attached to the main body of the bag and to the buckles are magnets and plates that work to close the back with little effort. They hold as well as metal snaps in most cases, the exception being if you overstuff the bag. There is a zipper to supplement the flap, so if you can zip the bag then you can snap it shut too. The bag has a large main compartment that has a padded divider in the middle. This compartment is large enough to handle a smaller laptop (and I have a 10” tablet and keyboard that fits it very well) and it also is large enough to handle a couple of books. It also has a zippered pocket in the main compartment that is a good size for a phone, a calculator or a small note pad. On the front of the bag on the outside there are two small pockets that are also good for small items. This bag is about the right side for a school bag or a “go bag” with essential tools in it. This is a good bag and I like it. It is well-made, roomy and has a good layout for the space and pockets. It’s a good choice if you need a durable and useful daily bag or even an emergency tool bag. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Solid Protective Case and Good Lenses Too
text: [[VIDEOID:295eeffb98575e038333fb69d111ae57]] I have an iPhone 6s and I have been looking for a good case for it. I have found several that work well enough but this one is better than the average. It combines solid protection with a set of good camera lenses to make the phone’s camera much more capable. The case itself is a metal frame case with a rubber gasket in between the frames. The whole is held together with screws. So, there is no chance this case will come apart unexpectedly. Do be sure to get the plates secured properly- I did not the first time and as a result the case provided a gap between the screen and the glass protector and it killed sensitivity. In addition to being a good protective case it provides a set of lenses to improve the camera. The best of these is the fisheye lens which is the best fisheye I have seen for my phone. Also included is a good macro lens for magnification and a wide angle lens for getting a wider field of view. These screw in place without issue. I would have liked a small baggie with the case to make carrying the lenses easier but this is a small beef. I have been happy with this case so far. It is a bit more expensive than the average case that is available but it also provides better protection and improvements to the camera as well. If you want a solid case and a camera upgrade, this case can handle both. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Excellent Sound
text: [[VIDEOID:99ec24b728fa83828f854618bef8cc0]] Most of the Bluetooth speakers I have used have been smaller and more portable, designed to be on-the-go and useful when traveling or outdoors. This speaker by GGMM is also wireless and can go with you, but I personally prefer to keep it in my room above my desk where I can use it to listen to music. This is a much better speaker than most of the speakers I have used and I am very pleased with it. This is a large speaker, bigger than most I have used and as a result it weighs more. It is encased in a leather cover and looks very upscale when compared to plastic or rubber. The controls are straightforward and easy – power on/off, set the mode between Bluetooth, WiFi and Line-in, volume up and down and finally a bass booster. On the back there is a barrel port of plugging in the speaker, a reset button that you likely will never need to use and the port for plugging in a 3.5mm plug. The sound profile is about as close to perfect as I have seen in any speaker. The bass is on target – strong but not overdriven unless you use the bass booster. The midrange is excellent and the music sounds rich and full, not lifeless, hollow or like it’s coming from a tunnel. The highs are bright and clean but not piercing. The sound is balanced very well and I am happy. The bass booster does exactly what you think it does – it gives the bass a kick. Even with the boost, the bass is not overpowering but it comes forward quite a bit on bass-heavy tracks. I do not use the bass boost often as I prefer the highs. So far I have had no connection issues and the speaker connects very quickly when put in Bluetooth mode. This is an excellent speaker – far and away better than most smaller speakers I have seen and used. It is much more expensive, but it brings to the table great sound and fine connectivity. I use this in my home office where it sits just above eye level on my desk shelf, and I use it every night for listening to music. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Heavy and Sturdy; Eye Pieces Just OK
text: [[VIDEOID:414a05febe196c2e45d507a7445bc471]] I like stargazing with my teenage son and we will go outside and explore the night sky when we have time and when weather permits. Up to this point we have used a very inexpensive “trash” scope that is good enough to see craters on the moon and it does work well enough to help us find and see things in the sky that otherwise we would not be able to see. I was excited to have the opportunity to evaluate this telescope by Gskyer and anticipated having a better experience with it that my cheaper scope. It does work and it is a big step up from my inexpensive scope but it does have a couple of minor issues that merit attention. To summarize, much of which I discuss in the video attached to this review: PROS: - Very sturdy tripod that is easy to adjust - Three eye pieces of varying strength to make it easier to see that which you are viewing - Heavy and durable construction - Includes a Barlow lens as well as a view finder - Tray is good for holding lenses and it also locks the tripod so that it can’t collapse CONS: - Eye pieces are mediocre at best - Sensitive to slight wind and soft bumps - Expensive This is a decent scope and is a good starting place for the beginner or casual sky watcher. It is not a high-end scope, but it is suited for someone who is more casual or is just starting out. title: Good Replacement Pads - Inexpensive but Slightly Different than Bose Pads
text: I have a set of Bose QC-15 headphones and I damaged the pads some time ago. I was able to find replacements, though the original Bose pads are quite expensive. I have been looking for good replacement pads that are less expensive and I have tried some off-brand pads in an effort to save money. So far I have found none that are an exact match though I have seen some that are quite close. These are a reasonable match though they are definitely different than the original pads, but at a fraction of the cost. In appearance these are close to the originals though they are smaller and they do not fit exactly the same. When I put on the headphones with these pads in place, I have to fiddle with the phones a little bit to get them to fit right, more so than when these had the original pads. It’s a noticeable difference but it is not a real problem unless you have to have an exact match. The pads are soft, but not as subtle and buttery as the original pads. They will soften over time with use, but brand new they are slightly more stiff. The main difference I have found with these pads is that they do not do as good a job with passive noise canceling as the original pads. I replaced one pad with one of these new pads and put them on my head. With a fan on in the background I listened closely. The new pad allowed more ambient noise to reach my ear than did the original pad. As it softens I think it will fit a little better and will help with the noise isolation, but even new the Bose original pads did more for sound isolation. They still do a good job, just not as good. So, why would you consider these? There are two good reasons to buy these. First, these are a LOT less expensive than the Bose replacements. At under $10 these represent a very significant savings over the manufacturer’s own replacement pads. Second, although these are different than Bose replacements, they do a good job of making the phones look new and they do the job well enough for most people. The phones are plenty comfortable with the new pads on and unless you are looking for difference you probably would not notice. These are good pads to consider if you need replacement pads for your headphones and you don’t mind the small differences. If you have to have 100% identical pads, these aren’t what you’re looking for. If you are content with approximately 85% the same, these are a very inexpensive alternative to Bose replacement pads. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Simply Works. Linux & Windows Compatible
text: An air mouse is not something you would normally use with a PC-based system unless you are trying to save space or are giving a presentation in which case it is a convenient accessory. Such a mouse is a lot more useful for things like Smart TVs, though it is also useful for embedded systems like a Raspberry Pi. I have used several air mice and I was curious to see how well this one would compare to others I have used. So far it has worked well, under both Linux as well as Windows. I will state up front that I have not used it with a Smart TV. At a glance, this little device looks like a TV remote and little more, but it is quite a bit more than that. It does work as a remote, of course, but it also works as a mouse with a full-up keyboard. On one side of this device there are all of the controls you would expect to find on a remote for a Smart TV remote – volume control, channel settings, mode buttons, play, search and more. Flip the unit over and there is a keyboard, with 38 keys and most regular keyboard functions accessible through function key settings. The unit requires two AAA batteries, not included. I decided to try it with my Linux workstation, running CentOS 7 with a 64-bit 3.10.0-series kernel. I did not have to load special drivers and I did not need to do any special configuration at all, it was just plug and play. I was able to move the mouse just by waving the device in front of the screen and several of the buttons on the remote side worked as I would have hoped – Home took me to the browser home page, volume controls worked, Search worked, the menu button brought up the menu for the current application with focus and more. The keyboard portion worked as it should and I was able to type, though I found it a little awkward after being used to a full-sized keyboard for so long. I also tried it with my Windows 10 system and I got nearly identical results. It required no drivers, no special configuration, no extra set-up – it just works as expected. The buttons works the same under Windows as they did under Linux for me and I was able to navigate as desired. This is a good air mouse that works well under Linux and Windows. It should work fine with smaller systems like the Raspberry Pi (which uses a derivative of the Linux kernel). As an added bonus, it is relatively inexpensive. If you need an air mouse, this one is worth some consideration. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Good Phones at the Price Point
text: I have a number of headphones and I have gotten quite fussy about them and how they sound and how they fit. I was interested in this set, as they resemble a set of Philips headphones I used many years ago and my experience with them was positive. The difference was that the Philips set I used was quite expensive and had active noise cancelling functions. These are a lot less expensive. While these are not the best headphones I have used they are well worth their asking price and I think they are a good set. These are very striking-looking headphones and they really stand out. I have the blue set and they are by far the most eye-catching phones I have used. The paint is electric blue and the pads and headband are black. I like the overall design, The cord is long enough to make them useful for using at a workstation or desk without having to sit still, a problem I have seen with a number of headsets with very short cords. There are two primary considerations I have when looking at headphones – comfort and sound profile. The comfort is good. The pads are long and oval and they appear at first like they would pinch or otherwise not fit well enough to make a seal. I was mistaken. They are quite comfortable and they feel good when wearing them. I will say I personally prefer headphones that really fit tightly, and these are a lot softer than I prefer, but many people prefer lighter headphones so I cannot consider this a fault. They do get a little warm after wearing them for a while, though. Keep in mind that because these do not clamp down tightly, they are not the very best for noise isolation. The sound profile is another matter entirely. The bass is strong and there is no problem there. The midrange is sorely lacking and as a result the music sounds like it is in a tunnel – this is a problem with many headphones and I specifically look for it. It can be corrected with an equalizer which is fine if you have access to such. I will say that it’s noticeable to me but I have worked with more expensive phones that sound a lot worse. The highs are fine and are clear. I have also noticed that as the volume gets boosted higher, the sound distorts. Now, if these were expensive headphones I would be a lot more critical, but these are under $20. For a $20 set of headphones, these are just fine and they are very much competitive with others in their price range. They sound all right through they could be better, they are quie comfortable and I really like the price point. If you need an inexpensive pair of headphones, these are not a bad choice at all. title: Fine Camera Strap
text: I have a camera, a Samsung NX300, that I bought a couple of years ago that I use for everything. I prefer it to my camera phone and I like it better than my older point-and-shoot camera. It is not high-end by any means, but it is better than the average camera and I am pleased with it. It came with a neck strap, but the strap is the weak point of my camera – too short and not well made. I have been looking for a good strap for my camera and I was afforded the opportunity to review this one. So far it has proven to be a nice one and it works well for my purposes. I have the “Color10” camera strap which is a blue background with a floral pattern. It is a cloth cover sewn to a thin leather backing – not the most heavy construction but just fine for a camera. The ends of the strap are sealed with large leather connectors that attach to the thinner nylon straps that fasten to the camera itself. Looking over the strap, there are no loose threads and the seams seem to be straight and tight. There’s no problem with the workmanship. I was a little surprised when I looked in the package and there was a little envelope, with two rings and leather cut-outs so that one can attach the strap to a camera that otherwise has no suitable place to attach it. My camera has two small metal eyes that are not anywhere big enough to feel through the nylon ends of the straps but they can handle the rings without issue so there is no problem using this strap with my camera. This is a thoughtful inclusion – other straps I have seen do not come with these, so this one is better suited for more cameras. The strap seems to be about the right length and it is very comfortable when I wear it around my neck. There’s really not much more I could ask of it – it is well made and it is comfortable. I really like this camera strap. The manufacturer showed some thought in the design and made this strap workable without requiring additional hardware, and it is made well too. It is slightly more expensive than some other camera straps I have seen but I think the design and the inclusion of the rings and leather cut-outs justify the price. If you have a camera and you need a better strap than what came with it, this one is very much worth some consideration. title: Simple Plug and Play for Me, Has Been Stable and Reliable
text: With the Bluetooth receiver in my Windows laptop dying a slow death I started looking for a USB solution. I tried a different TrendNet receiver and was disappointed so I hoped this one would work better for me. It has proven to be a lot better and works more reliably. This is a micro receiver that plugs into a USB port. On my Windows 10 system it was immediately recognized and the system was able to install it and start using it without installing any drivers or third-party software. It immediately allowed me to see all devices that were in range and broadcasting, I was able to pair and connect and it works as well as the internal BT receiver in my laptop did when it was brand new. One of the things that has proven tricky with other receivers is that when I close my laptop lid, all devices disconnect and when I open the lid again they may or may not reconnect. This is a real hassle when using a BT-based mouse and/or keyboard. With this receiver, the large majority of devices reconnect automatically when I open the lid to my laptop again, which is all I really can ask. Other reviewers have complained about included software and weird errors. Fortunately for me, I have encountered none of these issues. I am not sure if TrendNet had a bad lot go out, but mine works just great and I am very pleased with it. This is a good receiver that has worked out well for me. My system recognized it right away, it works stably and it seems to recover properly after the system comes back from sleep mode.

title: Excellent Filter for SNAP! Case Users
text: A Circular Polarizer Lens (CPL) filter is a useful tool for the photographer that generally is used to reduce light during long exposure times. The idea is that it can be used to take a longer exposure of something in motion without washing out, and in the case of moving water it can make the water seem almost misty and magical. I have a CPL lens for my dedicated camera, but this one goes with the Bitplay SNAP! series of cases. In this context it is a great lens for deepening colors and reducing glare. This lens is small, designed to attach to the SNAP! case threads. If you do not have the case, this lens is very unlikely to work for you. It works by having two glass lenses, one that is fixed in place and one that rotates. As the lens is rotated, the light coming through the pair fades due to the polarization. It is easily tested by looking through this lens at a flat-screen monitor like a laptop screen. One of the issues with a CPL filter is that often there is an uneven fade; this lens does not seem to suffer from this problem as much as with other CPL filters I have used and I have gotten consistently even shots with minimal bright spots. While I haven't yet messed with my phone enough to know how to increase the shutter speed, I still have been able to take shots with reduced glare. Much like polarized sunglasses, this lens is suitable for dealing with glare and reflections, and it works well. I am pleased with this CPL filter. It works well with my phone and it is does exactly what it is supposed to do. If you have a SNAP! case for your iPhone 6 and you are looking to “up your game” when it comes to taking pictures with your phone, this is a lens that will serve you well once you learn to use it and get the hang of how it works. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Turn Your iPhone Into a Natural Point-and-Shoot Camera
text: The cameras built into smart phones are getting more and more capable and they have impacted sales of point-and-shoot cameras significantly. I still prefer using a dedicated camera instead of using my phone, and part of the reason is that using my phone doesn't feel the least bit like using a camera. This case changes that and converts your iPhone 6/6s into a camera that actually looks and feels like a dedicated camera in your hands. This is not just a cheap plastic shell with a lens port on it; it actually provides some good protection for the phone. I will start with the shell case itself. The case is a hard plastic shell, providing back and bumper protection for the phone. It snaps over the phone and holds well. It is not so tight that it is near impossible to remove, nor is it so loose that it runs a risk of letting the phone slip. Overall, it is snug and holds well. The shell itself is a hard, semi-rigid plastic that has a small amount of flex but very little. The bumper guard is a softer material though still quite stiff and it has added material at the corners to give it some extra shock absorption. This is better than the majority of shell cases I have seen and used, and on the shell itself this is a good case. In the package is everything you need to turn your phone into a point-and-shoot camera: the shell case itself, two grip bases (one hard plastic, one wood), a carry strap, a lanyard, a lens kit and a thumb rest for when you are holding the phone. There is even a small screwdriver so you can change the grips. It requires no other equipment or tools. I did not understand the purpose of the grips right away, until I removed the base plate from the shell and attached one. It made sense then – the case actually looks and feels like a camera, with a natural groove for your middle finger when holding the phone like a dedicated camera. I of course prefer the wood one, but the black plastic one better matches the shell. I also was puzzled by the thumb rest (wasn't even sure what it was) until I attached it to the case and held it up. My thumb rested on it naturally and it was actually a little more comfortable than my regular camera. The case comes with a small lens kit which is made up of a wide angle lens and a macro lens for close-up shots. I experimented with the lenses and took a picture of the field behind my house after a recent snowstorm and it definitely captured a wider view than without the lens in place. I then removed the wide angle lens and used the macro lens to take a picture of a fiber on a blanket, and it did a better job than my dedicated camera with a close-up lens. I have attached both of these pictures with my review. The one thing this kit does not include is a screen protector. A lot of cases do not have screen protectors and you have to buy them separately anymore. I would suggest using a tempered glass screen protector to get the best possible protection to go along with this case. This case is enough to make me seriously think about using my phone's camera a lot more. It makes the phone feel like a dedicated camera, it has some thoughtful features and it provides very good bumper, corner and back protection for the phone. Also available for this case are separate add-on lenses like telephoto and fisheye lenses so you can expand the capabilities even more. If you have an iPhone 6/6s, consider getting this case before you buy a separate camera. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: No Wasted Outlets!!
text: I have a workbench where I frequently have little projects underway, and the issue I have had is a shortage of power outlets so I am frequently changing the configuration on my desk to account for this. I decided to use this surge suppressor/power strip on my workbench to resolve this issue and so far it has worked out well for me. There are eight full-sized, grounded power outlets on this tower, and each one is spaced properly to handle a full-sized power adapter like what comes with many electronics. As such, there is no need to compromise when plugging in devices that have larger adapters, because there is enough room for all on this tower. Every outlet includes a ground plug too, which is great for devices that require one (in my house, it's about 50/50). With almost every other surge suppressor, I have had issues with oversized adapters crowding other outlets – this is not a problem with this one. There are also four USB charging ports on this tower which is a really nice bonus. These are all 2.1A ports so they can output a full-speed charge to devices that can handle it, but most of my devices take a 1A charge so the 2.1A is lost on me. I have not yet put a meter on these ports to check the actual power output but so far these seem to output about the same as most other USB charging blocks I have used. Power output aside, having USB and AC ports together allows choice if you have a device that uses a USB adapter to plug into an AC outlet. The circuit breaker button is on the bottom. One thing I particularly like about this tower is that the outlets are one two circuits and there are buttons (on the top) that control each circuit. This may require a little logic when planning your power usage – if you want only/all lights on one circuit, place them so that they are controlled by a single button and you can then power them all on and off together. This tower have allowed me to clean up my work area and it has enough outlets on it to cover my devices without issue. It is very easy to use and understand, it has plenty of outlets that are spaced apart nicely so there is no waste, and it includes USB outlets too. I have had no trouble with it at all and have no problem recommending it it if you are looking for a good power strip/surge suppressor. title: Small and Very Portable AM/FM/Shortwave Receiver
text: [[VIDEOID:90e56caf53bb9127a941c450bd417db8]] A battery-powered radio receiver is a good piece of equipment to have on hand when there is an emergency. It can be used to receive important information when there is no power otherwise available. This particular receiver works well and it has the distinction of being one of the smallest receivers I have ever used. It is about the size of a cell phone and it is able to receive shortwave signals as well as AM & FM stations. This unit is small enough to fit in a pocket and is comparable in size to my iPhone 6 in its case. This makes it ideal for packing along on a trip or keeping someplace where it can be out of the way but ready in an emergency. In my opinion, the size is one of the strongest selling points. Turning it on by the switch does not turn on receiving. This turns on only the power to the LCD and from there the radio can be turned on by holding down the on/off button on the front. This is an interesting way to make sure the radio is not accidentally powered on, though it is slightly inconvenient. This feature suggests the ideal behind this radio is primarily emergency readiness. There are a number of ranges set for AM, FM and shortwave on this radio that correspond to different locales. Operable range in one country may be very different than in another, and by separating these out into preset ranges enables changing the suitability for a locale a matter of pressing a button rather than tracking down a new device. This makes traveling with this radio very workable. After turning it on I have had no issue with finding stations on each appropriate frequency range, though it was easiest finding FM stations due to the prevalence of such in the area where I live. This is an interesting little radio. It works well, and it is able to pick up stations in different regions by simply changing the available range to scan. The size makes it easy to take with you. Though it is most clearly useful as an emergency radio it works well as a general purpose radio too. The price is nice too, making this an easy radio to recommend. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Polished and Feature Packed Smartwatch
text: Smart watches have gotten more popular with the release of the Apple watch. They tend to have a standard set of functions, such as access to instant messaging, email, time, alarms and a lot more, typically tied to your phone. Not all smart watches are alike, though, and offer different sets of functions, better connectivity and other various differences from one another. This particular smart watch offers the mainline set of functions, setting itself apart through the user interface which is more polished and clean than most others with which I have worked. That said, I have a couple of quibbles with it, leaving room for a little improvement. This is a standard-sized watch with a rubber wristband that can actually fit a larger wrist like mine. I have trouble finding watches and watch bands that fit me, so the fact that this one fits me is a pleasant surprise. Powering it on, the user is immediately greeted with a complex and fairly complete visual menu system with tiles for every function available to the user. This is a standard presentation for a smartwatch, but this one looks a bit more polished and clean than the others I have seen. Switching to other menu screens just requires a swipe gesture, as to be expected. I have big hands, and this means that, for me, using a stylus makes working with this watch a lot easier. This is not the fault of the watch but a reality of working with a small device. My first issue with this watch came when I paired it to my phone. The date and time on the watch were off, so I expected that it would grab the time from my iPhone when I paired it. It did not. Instead, I had to dig for the clock application and manually set the time. I dislike this and think that having it set itself when it is paired is much more accurate and cuts effort on the part of the user. For Android users, there is an application to allow for syncing up the time, date and more, but iOS users are out of luck for now. To the manufacturer's credit this is made clear on the product listing so this is not a surprise. Regardless, I am of the opinion that the watch should fetch the time, not rely on being sent the time. In the grand scheme of things, though, this is an annoyance, not a deal breaker. There is a fairly comprehensive list of functions provided by this watch in addition to time/date and phone answer. Through the menus the user has access to call logs and function, Bluetooth functions, a remote finder function, a pedometer, a sleep monitor, a reminder function to get up and move on occasion, calendar and clock functions, audio functions, video functions and a few more. One of the interesting functions that this watch offers is a camera. So, I tried to use it and it complained that there was no memory card available. Reading through the limited documentation included, I was unable to find anything about a memory card. I finally noticed that the back of the watch has a small groove where it can be popped off, and when I removed the back I found the battery which is removable (replaceable - another pleasant surprise). Under the battery is a slot for a micro SD card. Adding a memory card comes with a big catch. It requires removing the battery to get at the holder which in turn clears the clock and resets it to midnight 01-01-2015. So, adding the memory card requires me to set the time again. And again if I remove the card. Although I think the time sync functions of this watch are lacking, it is otherwise a good smartwatch. The interface is professional and polished and the whole provides access to a large number of useful functions. It's priced well too. Overall, this is a solid offering worth a look if you are wanting a smartwatch. Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Good Speedlight for Someone Trying to Learn
text: If you are seriously into photography a speedlight is a valuable asset that can help you get the lighting just right, which I have found to be particularly helpful when dealing with portrait shots. I have worked with other K&F Concept products and have had consistently good experiences with them so I expected the same from this speedlight. I have not been disappointed. I encountered a couple of minor speed bumps along the way, based largely on learning curve. This is a sizeable device, and it has a bit of heft to it when the batteries are installed. Please make sure you have proper support for the camera when you are using this light as it can unbalance the camera and make it awkward to use. This is not specific to this particular speedlight but to speedlights in general. First things first – this thing takes 4 AA batteries and that adds weight. The battery compartment is easily accessible and it is easy enough to install the batteries. The controls on this light are very straightforward though knowing what the settings do is a different matter. If you do not know what slave mode is or how the settings relate to the zoom, you are going to find yourself frustrated. It took a little bit of research and some experimentation to get the hang of this light and I have found the best use for me is to use it in slave mode to supplement the lighting my the flash that came with my camera, though through the hot shoe I can install it on my camera. Read the manual that comes with it. It will help a lot in learning how to use this light properly. The light comes with a small stand so it can be set up independently from the camera and in that manner it can be used as a standalone flash. Turning on slave mode allows for positioning it so that it can add the right balance of light in reaction to the flash on the camera and as a result you can get very good backlighting. The mode button on the back of this light allows for switching between modal settings and making adjustments, There are also 4 directional buttons that are used for making individual setting adjustments such as zoom. There is the on/off switch which toggles power but also toggles the backlight on the LCD display. Finally, there is a flash button that allows for activating the flash manually. The flash can be fired repeatedly in manual mode but seems to be on a 3-second recharge when not so. The light has 90 degrees of freedom of movement so that it can be positioned as desired. I like the fact that the neck has angular measures on it for 45, 60 and 75 degrees, Be aware that this speedlight is not universal and does not work on all cameras. It works fine with a Canon camera; my Samsung camera does not register the presence of this flash at all so to use it with my Samsung camera I have no choice but to use it in manual or slave mode. This is a nice speedlight and it works well, It is not the fanciest or most expensive but it gets the basics down very well and it has not let me down. This is an affordable speedlight and it is good for the photographer who wants to learn how to improve their lighting techniques. title: Small displays like this one serve in areas where larger displays may ...
text: [[VIDEOID:ee00283940adc73cdd08d66738c2c471]] Small displays like this one serve in areas where larger displays may be inappropriate. One example is in automotive displays, another being embedded processing such as with a Raspberry Pi or similar small platform. This is a nice display with some good features. This display accepts several display types, including A/V, HDMI as well as VGA. I have tested it with the VGA and HDMI inputs and it has worked very well. Though it is very small it is clear, bright and quite readable. It comes with a decent stand that will keep it stable and secure, and if you are so inclined you can install this display on the dashboard of your car using the included double-sided tape that fits the base. You would do this if you choose to set it up as a display for a backup camera in your vehicle. Included is a small remote for navigating through the options available to you. You can do the same things with the buttons on the face of the screen but I have found the remote to be a little more convenient. In using the remote I discovered an FM tuner – I can change the settings but I have not yet successfully made it work. I go into more detail in the video I have attached. This is a nice monitor. It's small and compact and in an emergency it will work as a primary display for a computer. It is much better suited for embedded systems where it is very good. If you are working on small systems like a Raspberry Pi this is a fine choice. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Very Easy to Use
text: As a child one of my favorite things to do was to look at things under a microscope. I vividly remember gathering a water sample from a swamp near the house and looking at a sample and finding my first paramecium. It has been years since I have owned a microscope, but with this microscope I can see how things have advanced and changed. This one does not have the same magnification as that microscope I had as a child but it is a lot easier to use and I can still see things with it that I cannot see even with a good magnifying glass. This unit looks more like a drill press than a microscope, in terms of the design. The scope itself fits on a metal shaft and two turning knobs make it easy to raise and lower the scope in relation to the base. The base has two clips for holding down your slides or paper or whatever else you want to look at through the scope. There is no eye-piece on the scope – the image is viewed on a computer screen instead and the connection is made via USB. Included with the scope is a software CD and this must be installed to use the scope. Installation is quick and painless. I installed under Windows 10 64-bit and had no issues. After installation I launched the software immediately. The software consists of a view/capture application and a supplemental application for saving your work. The main part of the view & capture app is a live window that shows what is visible through the scope. As the object or slide on the scope base is moved, the image updates in real time. I found it a little awkward to line things up just right at first but I finally did manage to get things in the viewer just as I wanted them. I started with a gray piece of paper that I thought was solid gray, but I found that the gray is actually a micro dot pattern like magazine print. More interesting was the corner of a $5 bill showing not just the print pattern detail but the fine fibers in the paper. A penny, cat hair and a very close-up view of a microfiber cleaning cloth all proved to be interesting subjects. Attached to this review are some of those detailed images, my favorite being the penny. I have not yet gone to the culvert near the house to gather water samples. The software allows for two different capture types – photo or video. I have only played with the photo capture so far but it it very straightforward – click the photo button, either on the application interface or on the USB cable where the light level can be adjusted and the image appears in a list on the right side of the application window. If you double click the image you can save the image to the hard drive, zoom in on it and do a few other operations. Linked to a tablet instead of a computer, this is a great travel scope to take with you. It is well-suited for classroom use as well as for use in the office. I like this microscope. It is very easy to use, it does a good job of magnification and images are nice and clear. It is very different than the microscope I used growing up, in ways that I like. It's so much easier viewing on a screen than looking through a viewer, making this more fun to use too. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review.
