title: Fine Small Projector
text: Projectors for home use are typically set up for home theater systems. I have seen a number of systems set up with projectors suspended from the ceiling, and I have seen a few that rely on being mounted on a table top. This is a table top model and it is a very good and easy-to-use projector. This is a 300-lumen projector which is fine for home theater systems, though it would be a little underpowered to use in a larger room or something like a small church. It is good for small presentations too and is a good option if you want to take it with you for meetings instead of keeping it permanently placed somewhere. There are several input sources for which the projector is configured. For testing and experimentation I found it easiest to work with HDMI though I was able to use some of the other sources as well. It accepts VGA (which is great for older computer systems and other hardware), it can read files from an SD card or even a USB drive. Using a USB drive or SD card, this projector becomes very compact and portable and doesn't even need an external source of input. This projector even has a pair of speakers inside so you can use this projector for the entire A/V experience, though you will get better sound from a dedicated sound system. This projector is capable of receiving sound as well as outputting it. I used the HDMI input to feed the image from my computer to the projector and it did a fine job of displaying my desktop on the wall for me. I was also able to configure Windows to use it as an extended display so I could then look at PowerPoint on the computer screen and use the projector to output the slide show. This is very, very convenient and makes this configuration ideal for presentations. I was able to adjust the focus manually and get the image as sharp as I wanted too. The remote with this unit is great. It provides full access to the projector's functions, so if the projector is on a shelf out of reach the remote is sufficient for any adjustments you may want to make. If you prefer not to use the remote or have some reason you would rather directly interact with the projector there are several buttons on the top of the projector that give access to the different functions. You can change the input source, power on and off and get into the menu system which allows you to tweak all manner of settings: brightness, change the resolution, update the firmware from USB, set the date and time and more. This projector does output a lot of heat – to be expected from a projector with a bright light in it. Make sure that you have decent ventilation in the room when using this projector unless you want the room to warm up. I did notice that when the projector is shut off, the fan stops too which is a minor disappointment – I would rather have had the fan continue for a few minutes afterward to cool down the LED. This is a nice projector. It accepts a lot of different input types, it works well for small rooms and home theaters and it is easy to take with you due to the small size. It is especially useful if you want to run your video or presentation from either USB or from the SD card. If you're looking for a small-scale projector, this is a good choice. title: Very Nice Messenger Bag
text: I use messenger bags as book bags to take books and tools to and from work every day. I favor canvas bags because they are tougher than nylon and they are a bit more masculine-looking. This particular messenger bag is a little more stylish than some of the others I have seen and so far I am happy with it. A messenger bag is characterized by the fold-over flap that snaps closed over the main compartment. This particular bag has a very colorful and decorative weave that makes up the entire flap and the result is a softer and more supple flap than if it had been made of the same canvas material as the rest of the bag. That is not a fault or imperfection by any means but needs to be mentioned as a difference. Compared to the flap, the rest of the bag is more coarse and rigid. Everything about this bag suggests quality. The stitching is very tight and the materials are even and there are no imperfections (nicks and cuts) that I can find on this bag. The stitching used to attach the shoulder strap to the metal loops on the bag, as well as to attach the leather trim to the canvas, is visibly thicker and stronger than what was used to hold the canvas portions of material together. I like the fact that there is some manner of reinforcement on the bottom of the bag (stitched inside so it is hard to know exactly what kind of reinforcement was used). Instead of actual snaps, the flap is attached to the front of the bag using magnets. These make it a lot easier to open and close the bag. In the main compartment of this bag are three pockets, one zippered and two smaller pockets that are open on the top. The smaller pockets are ideal for cell phones, small note pads, a calculator and the like while the larger pocket is big enough to accommodate a checkbook or a small book; it is not quite wide enough to handle a DVD case. There is a front pocket that is just barely wide enough to handle a 10” tablet (though I would put a tablet in the main compartment instead). Finally, there is a zippered pocket on the back that is slightly more narrow than the front pocket because of the zipper and is good for papers and maps. This is a nice messenger bag and I like it. It is made very well, it is spacious enough to handle a couple of technical books and it looks nice. title: Excellent Results
text: I have worked with several K&F Concept lenses and filters in the past and I have had excellent results with them. I am still very much a beginning photographer and I am still learning as I go but I have learned a lot in the process. One of the things I have especially come to appreciate is the fisheye effect. Up to this point I have only had the ability to work this out via software, so I was pleased to have the opportunity to work with this fisheye lens. So far I have had a lot of fun with it and I love how it works, though I have again learned a few things along the way. A fisheye lens is somewhat similar to a magnifying glass with a great deal of distortion. The center comes out clear and the edges are distorted and warped, giving the effect of looking through a lens that is very thick in the middle and thins out towards the edges. Straight edge objects like sidewalks become warped and bent. This particular lens is a chunky and hefty fellow, actually comprised of two lenses instead of just one. There is a large macro lens that can work independently of the fisheye lens and it is very good for taking very close-up shots. The fisheye lens attaches to this macro lens and relies on it. I took several shots with the fisheye lens and I discovered something I did not realize though it is fairly obvious now. When using the minimum amount of zoom, the distortion is maximized and you get the most effect. The more you zoom in the more dampened the effect though it is still noticeable. I used the lens to take two pictures of the case in which the fisheye lens packs, one zoomed in all the way and one zoomed out all the way. For the one zoomed out, you can see the warping effect on the blinds over the windows and you even can see the entire image framed in a black circle. The image zoomed in has minimal distortion. I should state that this particular lens is designed for 58mm threads. Make sure your camera can use it before you buy it. If you have a different thread size for your lens, buy the right sized fisheye for that lens. This is one of the most fun lenses I have. It works great and it does a good job of giving the distortion you want with a fisheye lens, and it is not particularly expensive. I am very pleased with it and am looking forward to working with it for many years. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Spacious and Well-Designed Backpack Camera Bag
text: I have a growing interest in photography and I have been learning as I go. One of the things I have discovered is that a good camera bag – sufficiently large to hold the camera, lenses you need and any accessories – is absolutely essential. I have a messenger-style camera bag that works well enough but I have run out of room in it and it does not have the capacity to hold all of my extra lenses and filters. I looked to this camera bag as a solution. It definitely holds more than my old bag, it seems to be made well and there are some nice features to this bag. This is a backpack style bag and it is about the same size as a small travel backpack, though it is an order of magnitude thicker. There are zippers and pockets everywhere. There's a lot of padding to protect the camera and multiple movable partitions. The main compartment is large enough to hold a small laptop if all of the partitions are pulled out. There are three small partitions and two large ones and these can be arranged in any configuration to accommodate a wide array of accessories. As shipped, the partitions are arranged to allow for the camera lens and camera to sit through the middle of the pack which maximizes the padding and protection for the most valuable parts of your setup, and the smaller partitions are about right for 2-3 lens kits. I have a smaller camera – a Samsung NX300 with the 18-55mm lens – so I need less room for my camera and rearranged the configuration to permit room for several filter kits, a telephoto lens, a fisheye lens and a few smaller accessories, all in the main compartment. I have not yet purchased additional lenses but will rearrange when I do. The main compartment also has a pocket that is suitable for either a thin book or a tablet. So, even with all of my other gear in the main compartment, I still have room for my tablet. I really can't ask for much more than that. There is a smaller zippered compartment on the front that has room for even more accessories. In this I have loaded up a spare set of macro lenses that would not fit in the main compartment. Inside this compartment there is yet another pocket suitable for holding a tablet as well as a mesh pocket for loose items, my choice being a couple of pens. However, the most interesting item in there, attached by a tether, is a waterproof nylon cover for the whole bag. So, if you need to go out in the rain with this backpack, you can do so without fear of getting your equipment wet. On the sides there are two small pockets, sufficient for holding a couple of small items like a filter or two or even a very small flashlight. On the front there is one more zippered pocket that is well suited for thin items, like a map, magazine or papers. The shoulder straps are adjustable and padded so getting the pack to fit just right is not an issue. However, there is a carrying handle loop on the top of this bag and I prefer carrying this bag using that instead (I have always preferred carrying backpacks this way). This is a very nice camera bag. A lot of thought went into the design and it can hold a lot of equipment for its size. It has replaced my other camera bag outright. title: Excellent Alternative to Wacom Intuos
text: [[VIDEOID:9c7f474d82697dfd8035b3c7cf95ccc5]] I am a longtime graphics tablet user, having started with a Bamboo small. Since then I have had several tablets including a Bamboo Fun Pen & Touch, am Intuos4 and finally an Intuos5 Medium. All of the tablets I have used have been Wacom tablets; this is my first experience with another brand, and it is the first time I have even heard of Huion as a brand. To me it makes sense to compare this tablet with my Intuos5, with which it actually compares quite well for about 20% of the cost. My test system for testing this graphics tablet is a Dell laptop, with an Intel i7 processor and 16G RAM, running Windows 10 and Corel Painter X3. Comparing this tablet to the Intuos5 it is approximately the same size (both are medium tablets). They both look very similar at a glance and there are some distinct similarities in the pen and pen holder as well. In operation they are both similar but there are some very distinct differences, and each one has advantages over the other. One of the differences between these two tablets is that the Huion tablet has a numbered gauge across the top of the writing surface and includes a replacement surface in the box; the Wacom does not. The gauge is not a big deal but it does make a nice measure if you are looking for consistency in length of lines. The replacement surface is another matter – it is easy to damage the surface and over time it does get scuffed, so being able to apply a new surface is a huge plus to me. The pens are different and there is give and take with them. The Wacom pen is sealed and does not need batteries or recharging. It is also reversible and both ends can be configured for drawing. Typically one end it set up as an eraser. The Huion pen is rechargeable and is not reversible. I prefer the Wacom pen, but I like the feel of the Huion pen and it works well. The pens both come with a stand, extra nibs and a nib extractor. The Wacom stand is slightly heavier, but otherwise they are functionally equivalent. The software is obviously different, and I have been experimenting with the Huion software to learn how to configure the buttons. The Wacom software is a little more intuitive, btu I have found the Huion software to be a bit more versatile and it provides better control. Speaking of buttons, the buttons are a little different between these two tablets with the Wacom providing fewer buttons but providing a scroll wheel. Both tablets have 2048 pressure levels, and the only real way to test the pressure levels and drawing capabilities of each is to use a drawing application and start experimenting. I loaded up Painter and selected some acrylic brushes and started playing. I was able to get very similar results using the same brushes and the application had no issues with recognizing the pen or the position on the writing surface. Operationally, these two tablets are very similar. However, the Wacom is more expensive – a lot more expensive. The Huion tablet costs roughly 20% of the cost of the Wacom and to be honest when I compare these two it is hard to justify the cost of the Wacom when the Huion tablet works as well for so much less. Working with the Huion graphics tablet has been an eye-opening experience. It compared beautifully against a Wacon tablet of similar size and capability. I am very pleased with this tablet and can heartily recommend it as an excellent alternative to more well-known brands. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Good, Inexpensive Magnification Lenses
text: The primary lens I have on my camera is a good 18mm-55mm lens and it does great for capturing images that are a foot or more away. When I get much closer than that my camera is unable to focus properly and I end up with a crummy shot and I either have to give up or back up so that it can focus – not what I want most of the time. These magnifying lenses are a good solution, but there are somethings you have to keep in mind when using them. I will start with a statement that should be obvious: make sure you have the correct lens size when you are purchasing add-on lenses like this set. This particular set can be used only with a lens where the thread size is 55mm. If you have a lens that has a different sized thread, you should consider looking for this kit in a different thread size. You can use a ring adapter, but getting the right size at the start is better. There are four lenses in this kit, a 1x, 2x, 4x and 10x lens, each increasing in power as the numbers suggest. You can somewhat view these as magnifying glasses for your camera, but that metaphor is not completely accurate. They do magnify the image for you, but they allow a closer shot as well and you can get very close to your subject when you have one of these attached to your lens. Perhaps a better way to describe them is to realize that they make your camera very nearsighted and your camera can see close-up well and distance not at all when using these lenses. The main thing to remember about them is that as they go up the scale in strength they introduce a lot more edge distortion. This is most obvious with the 10x lens. If you take this lens and hold it so that you can see things through it clearly in the center, you cannot help but notice a large area around the edge of the lens that is distorted. The effect is less then you get it close to something on which you wish to focus but it is something to keep in mind. If there is too much distortion, use a less powerful magnification lens. These particular lenses have a little bit of heft to them but they are not what I would consider heavy. Because they are glass they are a bit more substantial than resin or plastic lenses. Overall, these are nice lenses. I have been able to use them for taking very close shots that I otherwise would not be able to take with my camera, such as ridge detail on a penny or dot patterns on magazine print. These are not real-world examples but they definitely show off the capabilities of such lenses. If you are looking for good magnification lenses for your camera, this is a good set that works well. Just make sure you have the right thread size before you buy. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Fine Travel Keyboard
text: I have been looking for a good Bluetooth keyboard for some time, to pair with my tablet and use when I want to work on documents. This would get me closer to using my tablet for most general tasks for which I need a computer and allow me to repurpose my laptop. This folding keyboard is a decent one and though it is a little on the small side for me to use full-time with my tablet it works great for when I am traveling. This is a very small and compact little keyboard, folding up to easily fit in a pocket. When unfolded it is still small but it opens to reveal a full keyboard with smart use of function keys. The keyboard has all of the key functions of a normal keyboard less the keypad. Some keyboards that lack a keypad simulate a pad through the function keys, but this one does not and that's ok. As soon as it is opened the keyboard powers on and it flashes an LED on the top to indicate that it has power. However, to connect it you have to tell it to connect via a function key combination which is printed right on the keys so there is not really any mystery on how to get it to connect. When broadcasting it identifies itself simply as “Keyboard” or “Bluetooth 3.0 Keyboard” (depending on the platform) and it pairs and connects without any issue. I first paired this to my laptop as a sanity check and it connected and started working immediately. I was able to type and interact with the computer with no issues and it worked exactly as expected. I then paired it with my tablet which is an Android-based Sony. Again, it paired and connected without issue and I was able to use it in the word processing application I have loaded on there. This is really all I can ask. Included in the package is a set of instructions and a USB cable for charging. The instructions include a lot of good information which include the specifications and care for the keyboard as well as a chart that shows how the function keys are defined in each of the supported operating systems. One thing I noticed in the product description is that the Windows 8 Mobile OS is not supported. Having a Windows phone available to me I decided to try it, just as an experiment. The keyboard does connect very quickly to the phone, but it disconnects very shortly thereafter. So, the claim is accurate - not for use with Windows phone. I am not sure if this would also mean it will not work with the Surface? This is a straightforward keyboard. It is a no-nonsense product that is easy to understand and easy to use. It is on the small side so do not expect a full-sized keyboard when you use this, but it works well and it is a good option particularly when you are mobile and need a keyboard with you. title: Solid Construction Makes It an Excellent Toolbag
text: I use a messenger bag to carry tools and supplies with me to and from work. I typically have a flashlight, a power bank, batteries and any tools I need for the day in my bag. I had a different bag that I used prior to receiving this bag and I have chosen to use this bag as it is better made and is larger. I have the gray version of this bag and it is an attractive bag, to say the least. Like a typical messenger bag it has a large pouch pocket over which there is a flap that snaps down and keeps everything in place. There is more to this bag than just the basics, though. It is made of heavy canvas and it is very rugged; after carrying it with me for a month it still looks new and unused though it has been packed and repacked daily for weeks. The shoulder strap is heavy canvas too and it is of course adjustable so it is easy to find the right fit for your shoulder. The flap does not actually snap down but instead is held in place with two strong fastening magnets. On the front of this bag are two loose pockets that are perfect for carrying a flashlight, a utility blade or other tools. I have even been able to fit a power bank in there for charging my phone when I have needed to make room in the main compartment. I like these because they do not share space with the main compartment and are separated from it by a layer of canvas. On the back is a zippered pocket that shares space with the main pocket. It’s ok for very small things. The main compartment is large enough to handle a set of screwdrivers, some wrenches, a pack of batteries and more (though adding all that stuff makes the bag understandably heavy). There is a small zippered pocket inside the main compartment that is great for things like AA batteries or other small items. There are also two small open pockets inside that work well for holding smaller items, though by being open they can handle larger things that the zippered pockets. I have been using this bag as a tool bag and it is working out very well for me. I have been pleased with all of the pockets and compartments and I like the fact that this is a heavy-duty bag meant to last a long time. I had another messenger bag that I used for this, but now it’s used just for carrying a tablet and a few minor accessories. This is a high-quality bag at a good price. title: Supports Multiple Input Sources; Compact and Lightweight
text: I use a full-sized projector every week to give presentations to a fairly large group of people. This projector is configured to connect via a VGA cable across the room and is suspended from the ceiling so that it can be hung in front of a projection screen. A full setup like this is not always the best configuration for every situation and a smaller projector is a better fit for certain situations. This is one such projector and it works very well. I have the ST-038 model. This is a very small projector, measuring approximately 6"x5"x2". Because of the size it also is very light and is ideal for putting on most shelves or light desks. Because of the size it is ideal for taking along for events such as business presentations, church functions and family fun nights. This projector has a 1,000-lumen light source and it is bright enough to handle projections in an entertainment room. It is not really strong enough to work in a large auditorium though it will do in an emergency if brought closer to the screen. Overall, I would say this is a good unit for using in the home or with small businesses. There are several input sources that can be used and the projector has no problem allowing you to select from them. I worked primarily with the HDMI input during testing. If you have an older computer you can use the VGA port to project as well. It is also able to accept video files from USB as well as an SD card so in that way it can be used as a stand-alone projector, either for slides or video. There is even an audio input and a headphone jack on there so you can make it more personal. There are two ways to control this projector. There is a series of buttons on the top that allow you to change input sources, change picture settings, modify sound settings, set the clock and make other settings adjustments including updating the firmware. The other method of interacting with this projector is to use the remote that is included in the package which allows access to the same settings, using an IR signal between the remote and the projector (the IR sensor is a large red square on the back of the projector). Using an HDMI cable I was able to use my laptop to project my desktop and subsequently my videos. Done correctly, this projector is a fine second screen and makes an excellent presentation screen for PowerPoint (this requires setting up the desktop to extend the display on the second detected monitor - this projector - and then tell Powerpoint to use the second display for playing the slide show). It works very well and I am pleased with it. There are two manual controls on the side of this projector. One controls the focus and the other slightly adjusts the tilt of the image on the surface where it is being projected. The focus is unable to get a clear image if you set the projector less than 6'-10' from the projection surface - not too bad of a distance. On thing you have to remember, though - this unit puts out heat and lots of it, though less than larger projectors. It can quickly warm up a 10'x10' room so consider ventilation when using this or any other small projection device. I was a little surprised too that when the projector is shut off the fan stops instead of running a little longer to cool down the light - not a big deal but noticeable. I like this projector. It travels well, it has a lot of options for inputs, the controls are intuitive and the picture is bright enough for smaller audiences. title: Interesting Feature Set; Highs are a Little Muted
text: I listen to music all day at work and I also enjoy listening to music at home and as such I spend a lot of time with headphones on my head. This is one of the more unusual headsets I have used, more in terms of their appearance than for their features or quality. These are decent headphones with some very interesting features though the sound profile is a little off, particularly in the highs. I received the blue and yellow headset and these definitely look like headphones for kids. They almost look like toys, though in use they have revealed themselves to be a bit better than toys. The main features they offer are Bluetooth connectivity, FM tuning, direct audio connection via 3.5mm cable and hands-free connectivity. When I received these, they were completely dead and needed to be charged up. It took me a little time to realize they were not broken, but once I plugged them in to charge the problem became very clear. I was then able to work with them. So, if you receive these and cannot get them to work, try plugging them in first. I was able to pair these to my computer and they connected without trouble. The headphones identify themselves as “KB-2600”. When I had them connected to my computer they worked fine and they did not stutter or skip which is all you really can ask for. I did not try testing the range. I discovered, quite by accident, that this headset has a full-blown FM tuner and it can scan for channels and make channel presets. It actually works surprisingly well and I found myself listening to a station coming from 50 miles north and it was surprisingly clear. Most headsets I have used to not have an FM tuner so finding these to have a tuner was a pleasant surprise. I loaded up some music and listened very closely to the sound, and unfortunately I found an issue with the sound profile. The bass is good; it is about right, not overdriven and not soft. The midrange is slightly strong but still quite good. The problem is in the highs which sound muddled and flat. When listening to vocals the sound is not particularly sharp, instead sounding far away. It is fixable with an equalizer, but with small music player or phone an equalizer may not be available. Comfort-wise, these are actually more comfortable than their looks would suggest. I personally like a headphone that clamps a little tighter on my ears but these are better than some of the other sets I have used. The pads on each phone is a mildly firm leatherette material that is comfortable and does not heat up as much as one might expect. The headband itself has a very soft pad on it that provides a very nice cushion between itself and the head. These are very interesting headphones and they have some cool features. Except for having a deficiency in the high range, these work well and they are quite comfortable. If you get a two-color unit it is a very good choice for younger listeners. title: Good Clarity
text: I have a hands-free package with my car so I don’t have to use a headset when I am driving to go hands-free. However, that does not help me when I am outside of the car. I looked to this Bluetooth headset to fill that need. Other single-piece ear pieces I have used in the past have either not been clear, have had poor microphones or both. With this set I was able to hear well enough and the person on the other end of the call said I was quite clear as well - a big improvement over most single-ear headsets I have used. This is a single ear unit and it can be placed in either ear. The actual unit itself is separate from the insert which is a silicone plug with a look to hold it in place. Also in the box and separate from the actual unit is the over-the-ear hook that snaps onto the unit, and it is reversible so it can go on either ear. Because of the silicone insert this unit is actually comfortable to wear. I had no trouble pairing and connecting it to my phone. It seems to work just fine with my phone which happens to be a Windows phone. I tested this headset by making a call. Call clarity and volume is good, and I had no issue with hearing the person on the other end. The person on the other end said I sounded slightly muted but clear. This is better than most other single-ear headsets I have tried, where the person I called would complain about not being able to understand me. This is a decent headset and is better than other single-ear headsets I have used. I personally prefer a two-ear headset though it is more comfortable than others like it I have tried. If you like single-ear headset, this is a very good option. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Better than the Strap that Came with my Camera
text: I have come to understand the value of a good camera strap. It is more than just a designer item and more than just a simple strap to keep the camera hanging around your neck. It needs to be strong enough to keep the camera secure and it needs to be long enough to allow for grabbing the camera and taking a quick shot instead of having to struggle with getting the camera from around your neck and risk missing the shot by a second or two. The strap that came with my camera is functional but much too short and I expect it to rip eventually. This strap by Orota is a much better strap than that provided with my camera. This is a well-made strap. One side is a heavy weave not unlike a car’s seat belt but not as smooth and shiny. It is also quite a bit thicker than a seat belt and will have no issue with supporting the camera. Sewn to it is a decorative layer that is also a heavy weave, similar to but not exactly like canvas. These are stitched together with heavy thread and I see little risk of them separating. Each end is clamped with a leather reinforcement that is held in place with four metal rivets. The leather ends each hold a metal buckle with the thinner nylon straps that actually connect to the camera. Looking closely at each component I found no loose threads, no uneven seams, no flaws in fabric or materials. There is nothing about this strap that suggests it will fail under daily use. This is a much longer strap than what came with my camera, measuring a little less than 3' long. I like the fact that with this trap attached to my camera I can lift my camera and quickly get the shot I want and I don’t have to take it from my neck in order to focus on it. I can hold it far enough from my face to actually focus on the camera. This is a very big improvement over my old strap which was short enough that I could not get the camera in front of my face at a comfortable distance. This is a very well-made strap and I am very pleased with it. It is stylish, well constructed and it is long enough to make it much more useful to me than my old strap. title: Good IP Camera with a Couple of Minor Quirks
text: An IP camera is an inexpensive and straightforward way to add a little extra security to your property, whether it is watching a door, monitoring a hallway or even just keeping an eye on the dog while you’re at work for the day. This is one such camera by Foscam, and it seems to work fairly well in my testing. There are a couple of minor issues I have seen, though nothing that I would consider a showstopper. This is a small and lightweight camera, about the side of a baseball, and it is hinged such that it can be angled in a range of about 300 degrees of coverage if it is placed properly though in practical use (meaning, when it is placed on a wall and anchored to it) it is likely to be positioned more like 70-90 degrees. It also rotates on the base, so it can be configured to point to just about any target from where it is anchored. The base itself is detachable and the whole camera can be popped off the base with no tools. To me this represents a concern. It means that someone can simply take the camera from the mounting place if it is low enough, using no tools. I like being able to rotate the camera on the base but I also like knowing the camera is not going to get taken easily. Setup of this camera is very easy and I was able to get it connected to my network without too much effort. That said, I struggled a little bit with the Foscam software and it took me a little while to get the software talking to the camera. I have had this trouble with another Foscam camera, and the problem seems to be the software - very specifically the IP Camera Search Tool utility - and not the hardware or the network. I was able to find the camera in the monitoring client. Once the camera is connected and available it can be logged into directly. There, the user has some control over a multitude of settings including firmware updates, login credentials and more. I like the interface even though it is somewhat basic as it is easy to navigate and is completely accessible from a web browser. The monitoring client software allows for more control, which includes concentrating on a single camera if there are more than one connected, scheduling, playback and more. In addition to the software that runs on a computer, users can connect to it via smartphone if they have an iPhone or an Android. Windows phone users are unfortunately out of luck. The camera resolution is very good and is detailed with fairly accurate colors. This certainly is not the same as a camcorder, of course, but it is sufficient to recognize faces even at a fair distance. The night vision (infrared) is excellent and is sufficient that I was able to read a sheet of instructions that was held in front of the camera. I do not like the LEDs on the camera, though... It is very hard to place the camera inconspicuously and have it remain unseen in the dark when it lights up with a ring of LED lights. This is the one major issue I have with this camera that I think needs improvement. It’s not a complete deal-breaker, but consider the possibilities when an intruder sees the camera and knows he or she is being recorded. These can be turned off in the settings and I highly encourage doing so. The camera has a micro SD slot near the hinge where storage can be inserted. It is unfortunate that there are no cards in the box though this is a minor gripe. I used an 8GB card for testing and the camera was able to record to it without trouble and I was able to control this from the monitoring client. This is a decent little IR-capable security camera. So far I am pleased with it, though there are some minor quirks. It’s a relatively inexpensive camera and is an easy way to monitor areas of your house and record what is going on when you can’t be there. title: Good Eye Protection and Good Video Quality Too
text: I have always been intrigued by discrete video cameras and I really like the concept of having the camera embedded in a pair of sunglasses. I was interested in giving these glasses a try and so far they have been great. They video quality is better than I expected. At a glance these appear to be basic sunglasses with really wide arms. They are not especially stylish but they do not look bad either. The surprising part for me was that they fit very well and completely cover my eyes and form a wind barrier for me. Most sunglasses I have tried leave some gap around my eyes so that I do get a little wind when wearing them - no so with these. These serve as a Bluetooth receiver and they seem to work well in that regard. When set to pair they identify themselves as “MS2 Bluetooth” and when I paired them to my Windows phone they paired and connected without issue, both for audio and voice. The product description says these work with Android and iOS phones but do not mention Windows phone. So, for the record: they work with Windows phones. The sound quality for music is not great but it’s not bad, either. The highs are great and are very detailed. The midrange is somewhat flat and as a result the music sounds a little hollow but not unacceptable. The bass is weak. Now, all of this said, these are not designed to be a constant-wear set of headphones so the emphasis was not poured into the sound quality. If you listen a lot to music and plan to use these all the time for that, these just won’t do the job. But, for the day on the ski slopes or occasional use outdoors they are just fine. The main feature of this set of sunglasses is of course the embedded video camera. The quality is actually better than I expected and it produces a decent video, though certainly not as nice as a hand-held dedicated camera with anti-shake. The sound is not bad either, though if you are moving or are outside when it is windy you will pick up some wind noise, but it is not terrible most of the time (all bets are off if you choose to wear these on a rollercoaster or on a speed boat). Color is bright and vivid, and the detail is there. These come with 8GB of storage. Installed in one arm of these glasses is a Class 6 8GB card. According to the product description these can support cards up to 32 GB, but I have not attempted to put a different card in there at this time. These come in a hard, crush-resistant case and are in a small microfiber bag in the case. The case is lined in a velvety material that will prevent scratches if you scrap the bag. Also included are the detachable ear buds and silicone inserts of different sizes so they can be fitted better. The sunglasses themselves are polarized and are UV-coated so they provide very good eye protection when in the sun. These are a great choice if you are a fisherman and you want to capture highlights from a day on the lake - the UV coating protects your eyes and the polarization cuts down reflections on the water. These will also serve well if you are looking to spend a day at an amusement park, but be aware that there is no anti-shake so if you want to use these on a rollercoaster expect a very jumpy video. I like these sunglasses. They do a good job of protecting my eyes and they fit very well, they record video very nicely and they have acceptable sound quality. Overall, I am happy with them. title: Bass Boost Done Right
text: I have worked with and used a large number of headphones and headsets. There are some significant differences between various models and brands which include comfort, sound quality and noise isolation (or active noise cancellation for some of the more expensive headsets). I was eager to see how well these Panasonic earbuds would work out, especially since the last Panasonic headset I had was a dud. These have proven to be much, much better than my last Panasonic headset and are better in a lot of ways to most of the other earbuds I have tried. They are not perfect, but they come close. Right up front I will state that these are strictly earbuds, not a hands-free headset. If you are looking for a headset for talking, this isn’t it. Style-wise these are very attractive earbuds, with a dark gray housing and red trim. The cabling is round wire with thick insulation. The round wire is more prone to tangling than the flat ribbon-style cables that have become more popular, but for me I prefer the round wire. When it comes to comfort these are more comfortable than many I have tried. They fit my ears reasonably well and I have not had problems with them jabbing me or slipping out. I can pull them out by the wire which is good from my perspective as it means if I catch them on something they will pop out of my ear instead of pulling. I have been able to wear these for a couple of hours without any discomfort which is a good thing. The most important aspect of any set of headphones or earbuds is the sound, and this one gets it really close to perfect. The highs are very clear and bright and I am very happy with how well vocals sound when listening. The midrange is balanced nicely and the music has some depth as a result without sounding hollow or like it is coming from a tunnel. The bass is strong - very strong - and while it is a touch heavier than I like, Panasonic did a good job of not wiping out the whole sound profile with just the bass. If you like earbuds that boost the bass, this pair does it right. These also have very good noise isolation, or passive noise cancellation. I have worn these for a couple of weeks while at my desk with an air purifier running less than two feet from me and they do a good job of blotting out the sound of that purifier. I do have active noise cancelling headphones too and those do a better job of killing the sound from that air purifier but at a much higher cost and for the difference in sound reduction it’s not an appreciable difference to justify the cost. Included in the package is a carry pouch and more silicone ear inserts. I am very pleased with this set of earbuds. They are a bit pricier than the typical set of earbuds I have seen and used of late but they do a great job of blocking ambient sound and they sound great. I am not a huge fan of the bass boost but I seem to be in the minority, and to Panasonic’s credit these buds boost the bass correctly - meaning, the rest of the sound profile is very solid. If you want a set of really good-sounding earbuds with a bass boost, this set is among the better ones I have used.

title: Works Well with Canon 50D
text: I have been shooting a Canon 50D DSLR for several years, mostly outside or with stage lighting. Occasionally, I also have been using a small camera-mounted flash, but it is weak and very limited. To improve my flash photography, I decided to try the Mago Speedlight by Pixel. This is an excellent, mid-priced flash with loads of features. The Mago Speedlight comes with a nice soft case and a fold-out manual which guides you through the setup of the flash and includes screenshots of the back LCD. It also includes a small stand which is great for use in slave mode, and a clip-on flash defuser. The flash uses 4 AA batteries or an external power supply (not provided). It is even upgradable via a USB port hidden in the battery compartment (not tested). The controls are easy to use after some experimenting. The manual really helps as there are so many features. The buttons are solid and the display is easy to read, with an optional green backlight. The flash head can be tilted up and down, or rotated left or right. It also includes a built-in defuser and a white card reflector. These are very useful if you are not bouncing the flash off of a ceiling or reflector. One interesting feature is an LED model light that can be turned on/off easily via a dedicated button. This light is quite bright and very useful for setting up your shots. I tested the flash on a Canon 50D with 20mm and 50mm lenses and somewhat cooperative subjects (my kids). After learning the controls, I took several excellent pictures. The flash supports E-TTL mode, manual mode, and multi-flash mode. I tested all three. To test the multi-flash mode, I set the flash to 5 bursts at 500 HZ and took a picture of fan blades, resulting in a very interesting effect. As a final test, I put the flash in slave move (S1) and put my old flash on the camera. This flash worked great as a slave flash and I took some interesting pictures using both flashes. I also used S1 mode to slave the this flash to the camera's on-board flash. Note, I did not test the wireless flash mode (a smart slave mode) as I do not have another flash that supports that feature. Even though I received this product at no cost, I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Absolutely Outstanding
text: I work with a lot of headphones, headsets and earbuds. I am very partial to one very special set of headphones that I own, a pair of Monster Inspiration phones that includes active noise cancelling (ANC) and this is the pair of headphones against which I compare all others. Although I have worked with many sets of very excellent headphones it takes a lot for me to really rave about a specific set. To be that awesome, the headphones have to be very, very comfortable, have brilliant sound, be made well and have at least good passive noise cancelling if not ANC. These phones by Geega are nothing short of outstanding and actually complete very well with my Monster phones. These are some of the more comfortable phones I have used. They are completely over the ear phones and cover my entire ears so there is no pinch. The earphones themselves are padded with a soft leatherette that is almost buttery soft and the headband is covered in the same material. These are very easy to adjust to get the fit just right. I can wear them for long periods of time and they do not pinch or get uncomfortable though they do get warm after about an hour. Because they are over-the-ear they provide some measure of passive noise cancelling. The sound profile is excellent. The bass is at about the right level - not weak and not too forward so the bass response is very good. When the bass drops, you know it but not because it causes a headache. The midrange is very rich and full and the music has amazing depth, better than many others I have used. The highs are absolutely brilliant, bright and crisp. I would stop short of calling these audiophile headphones, but the sound profile is every bit as good as a pair of $350 Sennheiser headphones I own - better, actually, and it makes me sad to know I spent that much on those phones when I could have spent a lot less for these. I intend to connect these to a Bluetooth transmitter and connect them to a professional sound mixing board to see how detailed the sound is - I will update this review when I have done so. I have these paired to my tablet from which I stream Pandora to them. They paired and connected without issue on all of the devices I have tried - my laptop, my phone and finally my tablet. They identify themselves as “GEEGA S204” and on all three devices I tried to connect I had no issues at all maintaining the connection. These phones come in a nice, hard protective case that provides good protection from crush damage. There is a mesh pocket inside for keeping the included USB cable for charging and the AUX cable for alternate input. The range on these phones is 20' - 30' which is very much in line with most phones I have used. Interestingly, they did not stutter and cut out, they just completely cut off when I passed that threshold. I am not sure if this is just a function of my environment or if they really are that sensitive at the threshold. Overall, these are simply outstanding. I have not found any other set of Bluetooth headphones with the same level of comfort or sound quality. These are the best wireless phones, of any type, that I have ever used. These are my new reference point for wireless/Bluetooth headphones and are the standard by which I will judge any others. I will still use the Monster phones, for the ANC function and for comparison against other wired phones, but these phones by Geega will be used for listening in my home office where I enjoy listening to music most. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Fantastic Camera for a Very Reasonable Price
text: I have always liked the video footage taken by bikers as they barrel down a mountain trail or through a wooded area on their bikes (or the crazy base jumpers wanting to capture the drop). It gives a really good sense of what the rider was seeing when riding and you catch every bump in the road, every acceleration and deceleration. I have never used on of these little cameras before now so I was very excited to have a chance to evaluate one of these cameras. So far I am very happy with it and it works well, though I have learned that those with big hands and fingers will struggle a little bit with it. This is not just a camera, it is a complete kit with the camera, a waterproof housing, cables, mounting brackets, double-sided adhesive pads - everything you need to use this little camera in just about any outdoor activity you might want to capture. I will write mostly about the camera but will touch on a couple of the accessories as well. Except for cameras designed to be hidden and concealed this is the smallest and lightest camera I have ever seen or used. This is of course required for a device like this that is intended to be used on the go. It very easily can be slipped in a pocket or a bag or purse. It comes packaged in the hard plastic frame that is the waterproof case but even this case is small enough to fit in a purse or smaller bag. I will say this - read the included manual! The manual is not perfect but it is better than what comes with most electronics and it gives a very good rundown on how to use this little camera. I had no clue at all what to do with this camera until I looked through the manual. I suspected it was touch-screen and I was right. Even though the screen is touch screen and easy to navigate the interface is only semi-intuitive. It is also complicated by the fact that there is an anti-scratch cover on the screen for shipping and if you do not peel this off the screen is a lot less responsive. This is where I had the most trouble - trying to work around the plastic sheet over the screen when I didn’t really even notice it before. This camera has a lot of the same capabilities of a good phone camera. You can take still pictures, video and also play back that which you have recorded. The camera can snap stills up to 12MP resolution and the video recording can go all the way up to 1080P. These equate to very good image quality when used properly. There are a million little settings for these modes too, from white balance, ISO, anti-shake, motion detection and a lot more. Many of these will be familiar to anyone who uses their digital camera for anything more than just casual shots. In testing my images and videos came out ok. I am still learning how to balance all of the settings on my big camera so I am no expert, but what I was able to produce was acceptable, particularly the video. I did manage to get the date set correctly and displayed in the corner of the video, I got the lighting right and color straight. I spent too much time playing with the zoom and I learned I am very adept at shooting videos of my hands. This is a rechargeable device and a standard micro USB cable is provided for charging. I ran into one issue with the camera and it related to the fact that I have huge hands and the camera is so small. I found that the only way I personally can work the touch screen is to use a stylus. Using my fingers I am unable to pinpoint the spot on the screen I want to touch and I got very frustrated trying to get certain things done on the screen. If you have really big hands, consider using a stylus on the screen. There is no storage included in the package. The camera takes a microSD card so you will need one to save any pictures or recordings. The waterproof case is a perfect fit for this camera and it seals wonderfully. It snaps closed without effort and it keeps the water out. It is supposedly good for submersion up to 30m (according to the description). I have not had an opportunity to test this. There are a number of mounting solutions in the kit, including mounting screws for attaching to a selfie stick, bicycle frame/handlebars and helmets. In the case of the bike mount, it holds very tightly and a good series of bumps is not enough to rattle it loose. Having never had a sport camera like this I have no basis of comparison but so far I am happy with this little camera. It is very compact and lightweight and it does a great job of taking pictures and video (though it is obviously not a full replacement for a dedicated point-and-shoot or a dedicated video camera). It’s inexpensive too (a LOT less expensive than GoPro) so I think it’s a great option for someone wanting to capture their adventures. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Good Basic Protection for Your Laptop
text: I have a sleeve for my tablet that works out very well for me. It provides some protection for the screen and provides some limited protection against drops and bumps. This is the first sleeve I have used for a laptop and so far I like it. It is appreciably cheaper than a laptop bag or backpack, but it also has less room for accessories. The sleeve I have is the 15.6” version and it fits my laptop almost perfectly. There is a small amount of wiggle room in the sleeve so that the laptop can slide a little from side to side and it’s just enough to make slipping the laptop in and taking it back out much easier. There is sufficient padding around the edges to make this sleeve useful for bumps and bangs but it will not protect the laptop within from hard drops on the edge. The outer material is a tight woolen weave and it does a good job of repelling water (though it is not completely waterproof). When splashed with water, the majority of the water beads up and rolls off, and of what remains most can be simply brushed off. The end result is a very slightly damp surface, nowhere near enough to get the laptop inside even slightly wet. So, when toting the sleeve outside it will effectively protect the laptop inside from rain. There are two pockets inside this sleeve. One is lined in a fleece-like soft material that gently cushions the laptop and allows it to slide in and out more easily. The other pocket is zippered and it is lined in vinyl; it is a good place to put papers, smaller accessories like a travel mouse and other small items. This pocket is not big enough to handle a lot of extras like a full laptop bag. I inspected the sleeve closely and I have not been able to find any problems in the way it is made. There are no loose threads, stitching is tight and straight and there are not crooked material patches. The zipper works smoothly and so far does not catch on the material of the sleeve. Overall I am pleased with the materials and assembly. This is a very nice laptop sleeve and I am pleased with it. It does a good job of providing some protection to the laptop is holds, it is water repellant and it seems to be made very well. title: Awesome - Quiet and Moves a Lot of Air
text: Heat is the main killer of computers and computer equipment so keeping a system cool and ventilated is a big deal, especially when involving systems that see heavy use. Laptops are just as vulnerable as larger servers and require the same precautions. One of the main solutions for heat dissipation and ventilation for laptops is a chill pad (a fan-based platform that moves air under the system) and this one by AMNIE has been outstanding. I have been using it for about two weeks on my personal system and likely will swap it over to the system in the house that sees the heaviest use. This is a good-sized pad, able to comfortably handle laptops up to 17”. It has a total of 4 larger fans that move some serious amounts of air, and fans are paired two and two between a pair of switches. The frame is painted metal mesh and offers good support to the laptop it holds. The switches that control the fans are dial controls and they provide variable fan speeds for each pair of fans they control. There are no graduations so you can set the speed anywhere within the range to suit you, though having that much control is probably not all that necessary. The fans run very quiet but on the highest speed setting really move the air. When maxed out and all four fans running at top speed the fans blew cooler air from between the frame and the laptop, telling me I had the speed up much higher than needed. For my particular system under my typical use load, it seems I only need to turn them on about half way. I have worked with some chill pads that have flaws in either the fans or the bearings and they make awful amounts of noise. So far, the only noise this pad makes is a low-frequency hum. It is quiet enough that even with lower-end noise canceling headphones I can cancel out the noise completely. This pad is not silent even on the low end of fan speed but it is very quiet all the way through the range of speeds. I have been able to leave the fans on full speed all night and sleep through the sound. I have not measured the temperature difference between when the fans are on vs. when they are not, but I have noticed that the internal fan does not kick in as frequently when doing video rendering as when the fans are off. It does turn on and it still hits high speed on occasion but it is noticeably less frequently. This is an excellent chill pad for laptops and so far it has worked out exceptionally well for me. It is quiet, it moves a lot of air and my laptop’s internal fan does not kick in as high as often. Because there is a system in the house that is much more frequently used for gaming, I will be moving this pad to that laptop instead and will use the other pad for myself. title: Useful Tool for Photographing Small Objects
text: Sometimes it is necessary to take a picture of something on a solid background, often white for contrast but also sometimes black for lighter-colored objects. This is especially true when you are creating promotional materials and you want the item in question to stand out in the picture. It’s not always easy to get that kind of background. A light box is a good way to accomplish this. The Purebox is one such light box and I have had the pleasure of working with it for the past week. This is my very first light box so I have been learning as I go. The whole thing comes in a gray padded fiber sleeve that is about the size of a padded envelope. I was a little surprised at first when I opened the package and this flat cloth envelope was all that I found. Once I opened everything up and started assembling the Purebox it made sense. The sleeve does provide some protection and it is also compact enough that it can travel fairly easily, though I would discourage packing it in luggage. The box itself is made of white vinyl. When unfolding the box it is fairly straightforward to see how the box assembles. There are lengths of Velcro along the edges of the tabs that hold the box together and retain its shape. Itf you line these up wrong it results in a box that is very unstable and does not stand up right. When finished, the whole box is approximately 12"x”12"x12". The top of the box has a very bright ring of LED lights, so bright that I was able to illuminate my basement just with the box alone. They cast an almost clinical light that borders on harsh and it makes the entire box (which is opaque) glow. Included with the box are two long, wide strips of plastic, one white and the other black. By placing these against the back of the box, it is possible to get the solid-colored background desired. It occurred to me that there is no reason that a different color plastic sheet couldn’t be used to make even more color backgrounds, like light blue, pale yellow and more. It would be easy enough to make such a background from construction paper in a pinch. This is a box suitable for very small items, such as a pair of glasses, a toy car or a small computer peripheral such as a mouse. In testing I photographed several small items such as batteries, my trackball, a small rock and the like. I used the white insert and I noticed that there is very little shadow at all, though if you look hard enough for it you can see shadows on taller items. I found one thing about this box that gave me a little concern until I spoke to the vendor about it. I had trouble with the sides of the box staying open properly, and as a result I was constantly fiddling with the sides to keep them open. I finally tried a small paperclip on the sides in the upper corners and that seemed to resolve the issue. A better solution will be to add a little more Velcro, a suggestion I offered to the vendor. This is not a huge problem as I think I could resolve it by opening the box and forcing the crease in the sides to open more so they would press against the sides a little more tightly, and it is easy enough to correct if it appears. This is a nice photo white box for someone who needs a pure, clean background for capturing images of small items. The light is very bright and with changeable backgrounds one can capture the image just as it’s envisioned. I am pleased with this box and I will be working with it often if not daily. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Long Cables, Work Well
text: Most of the USB cables I have are either 3' cables or are really short ones that come with electronic devices. Sometimes a longer cable is really handy, especially when the immediate area surrounding a work space is cramped. I looked to these 10' cables to help alleviate one such issue and I learned a few things. One of those things is that a cable can be too long in some cases, though this is a failure in organization, not in the cable. These are flat USB cables. Flat cables are less likely to tangle than their round counterparts, but I will confess to preferring round cables anyway (it’s a personal preference, not a technical preference). These are shielded in woven nylon which is great; the nylon is stronger than soft plastic shielding and gives the cable a little more stiffness but does not make the cable so stiff that it’s awkward to run. The connectors are interesting - two-tone plastic that is different than anything else on my desk which makes it a lot easier to determine where both ends of the cable are plugged in. I tried stressing the cable ends at the connectors by trying to pull out the shielding from the plugs and they held firm. I tried one of these with my phone and it worked just fine, I was able to charge the phone and move data between it and my laptop. I did not attempt a speed test. There is a big difference between 3' cables, 6' cables and 10' cables. If you need a 6' cable, a 10' cable will leave you trying to figure out what to do with the extra 4' of cable. In my case this meant having to use a twist tie to bunch the cable up in the middle. This is not a criticism but rather a suggestion - get a cable that’s the right length for the job. If you need a 10' cable, these have worked great for me. These are nice USB cables. They seem to be made well and they work as expected. If you need a really long cable, this is a good choice. title: Good Looking Speaker, Innovative Design
text: [[VIDEOID:9452f3f4fe85561cedb2616d98f18348]] I have worked with many different Bluetooth speakers, and most of them are very similar in design and sound profile. The iDea Taco is a bit different and is the most innovative of the speakers I have used, not so much in the shape but more in the way it projects sound. This is a pill-shaped speaker that is angled off at the sides and styled to look like a taco, though it is deceptive to that end. The sound does not come out of the ends but rather it comes out of the bottom. When the speaker is powered on and playing, the sound is reflected off the shelf or desk where it sits and this somehow enhances the sound (I am no expert in acoustics so I can't really explain). I had no troubles with pairing or connecting. It advertises itself as "iDea Taco" and I was able to pair it to my phone and also to my computer (at different times). I had no trouble streaming to it and it was very responsive. The sound profile is good, though not perfect. The bass is very good though it is not artificially boosted like with so many other speakers (overdriving bass is the current trend and it drives me crazy as it drowns out the rest of the sound profile). The midrange is full and as a result the music sounds warm, not like it is hollow or in a tunnel. The highs are the soft spot, with very slightly muddied sharps but still mostly clear and warm. The sweet spot for the sound is when the speaker is sitting at approximately a 45 degree angle from vertical, with the actual speaker facing down. It's at this point that the sound is best. This design decision is a bit more innovative than with most speakers I have used which project either straight up or straight out. This is a solid little device and seems to be assembled well. It has a slight heft to it and it feels very solid - no give in the housing and no noise when shaken. Overall this is a nice little speaker. It's designed a bit different than other speakers I have used and so far I am very pleased with it. title: Works Great; Encountered an Assembly Issue
text: I have a Dell laptop that I use for everything - games, programming, writing and streaming digital content. It is a great laptop and it has served me well. The one hassle I have had with it is having to bundle the power supply with it. It’s not the bundling that’s a problem, it’s the way my desk is laid out in relation to the power outlets. I was given an opportunity to test this power supply bu LiveImpex and for the most part is a great drop-in replacement for the Dell-supplied unit. The one trouble I have had with it is related to assembly. When figuring out which cord to use, I interacted with the manufacturer and was assured that this power supply would be compatible with my model of laptop. The power supply that arrived is very definitely compatible with my system and when I plugged it in my laptop immediately recognized it as a valid power source and began charging. It worked just as well as the regular Dell charger and from the perspective of the system there was no discernible difference. I noticed a problem when I took it out of the box, though. The plastic casing that protects the inner components was not sealed and was held together only by the heat warning sticker. The cover came off in my hand exposing all of the components within. This was a little disconcerting but did not impact operation at all and was easily remedied with a couple of strips of Velcro. From what I can tell, this is a snap-together design, and perhaps it was supposed to be glued but it was not. Other reviewers have not reported this issue, so I suspect I am an isolated case. The trouble I had with the assembly is not enough to call this a bad solution, as it does not impact operation and it can be worked around. It is a drop-in replacement for my Dell power adapter and I am satisfied with it. The fact that it is significantly less costly than Dell-branded parts and works just as well makes it a good value. title: All Metal and Very Quiet
text: Sometimes I like to have a little air moving across my desk when I am working at the computer. Even when it is hot, a little bit of a draft can make it seem cooler. Large desk fans and box fans can create too much air flow, but a small desk fan like a USB fan is often just the ticket for getting the air flow without blowing papers everywhere. I have worked with other BTOOP products and they have all been very good, so I had high expectations for this fan. The only real issue I have had with this fan is that my son has absconded with it and claimed it for himself. The most obvious advantage of this fan is that it does not require batteries or direct AC power. It plugs into a USB port on a computer, power bank or even a charging block and that is all it needs to run for hours. What has struck me as most interesting about this fan is that it is all metal, not cheap plastic anywhere. Even the blades of the fan are metal. It’s a refreshing change from all of the plastic junk that is prevalent everywhere. I have a huge air mover in my bedroom and even that fan is mostly plastic. Considering that this is a metal fan and not a plastic one, the current asking price (under $15, subject to change) is surprising. I would have expected it to cost a lot more. This fan operates quietly but still is able to move substantial air, enough to cool down a work space. There are a couple of small improvements in design that would make this fan even better, in my opinion. It is not the easiest to adjust the tilt and having a wing nut to loosen/tighten the screws for tilt would be a big help to that end. That is an easy modification that can be made at home without really any effort. The other improvement would be a variable fan speed setting but this is not a deal-breaker. The price of the fan is compensation enough for these two minor quibbles. Overall, this is a nice little fan and I like it. I especially appreciate the fact that is it all metal and it works so quietly. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Premium Lightning Cable
text: I have only recently started using UGREEN cables and so far every one of their cables I have used has been a top-notch product. I was interested to see how well their lightning cable would work out for me and, based on my experiences with their other cables I expected this cable to be excellent. I have not been disappointed. First things first – this is an Apple-certified cable which is not insignificant. Because it is certified it will work right with your Apple device and the device will not complain about it being an unrecognized cable. If you have used cheaper cables that do not come with a certification you have seen the warning messages that appear when you connect it. This one will not cause that problem which is good right out of the box. This cable seems to be well made and so far I have found no issues with build quality or assembly. The insulation is nice and thick and it securely attached on both ends so it will not pull away from the plugs. Each plug is shielded in an aluminum sheath which protects the plug and makes it a little easier to grip. I have the 5’ version of this cable which is nice; I like that I have a little more leeway with the extra length of the cable. There’s something I want to emphasize about this cable which many might not consider or may think is insignificant. UGREEN has put their name right on the plug ends, where it is easy to see and read. This says that they believe in this product enough to brand it, which is actually uncommon. Most of the cables on my desk are not branded so it is very nice being able to identify a cable by manufacturer. When one goes bad, if it is not branded it is difficult to know where that cable came from. The very best micro USB cable I own is by UGREEN and because it is branded it is very easy for me to identify in the tangle on my desk. Now I can tell which lightning cable is theirs too. I have not had this cable long enough to see how well it will hold up over time but in the time I have had it, it has been reliable and compatible. I like the extra length too which gives me some flexibility when figuring out where to put it and the device I connect to it. title: Good Add-On Kit
text: This is a 3-piece accessory kit for a camera with a threaded lens (in my case, a 58mm thread). I use this kit with a Samsung NX-300 with the 18-55mm zoom lens and it fits that lens well. My experience with this kit has been mostly positive. Included in the kit are two lens hoods and one lens cap. I will discuss each separately. The lens cap is, to me, the best component in the kit. It does not look like a particularly exciting item, but in this case this lens cap actually fits my lens better than the original cap from the manufacturer. It is tight and is seated evenly on the lens assembly. As an added bonus is has a lanyard that allows it to hang on the lens barrel so it does not need to be specifically tracked when it is not in place covering the lens. The second item in the kit is a tulip hood for the lens and it is neither better nor worse than the one that came with the camera. It does an acceptable job of keeping the lens in the shade instead of allowing sunlight to hit it directly. Note that when the tulip cover is in place the lens cap will not fit. The last item in this kit is a rubber hood that works similarly to the tulip hood and it helps prevents direct light from angling in to hit the lens. This one component is the only one in the kit about which I have anything critical to say, and it’s this: when the lens is zoomed all the way in the edges of the hood can be seen in the picture. It does not take much to zoom out past it but it still merits some mention. I am satisfied with this kit. It includes two hoods and a lens cap that in my case is better than the original that came with my lens. This is a decent kit at a good price. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review.
