title: Very Nice ND Filter for 58mm Thread-Size Lenses
text: I have been learning more about photography and as time has permitted I have been improving my skill as an amateur photographer. I have worked with other types of filters, in particular CPL and FL-D filters, but before now I have never worked with ND filters. I have been able to achieve good results with it and so far I am pleased with this filter though I know I have more to learn about it. A neutral-density filter is used to reduce light reaching the aperture without fiddling too much with the colors. This allows one to get creative with shutter speeds. This particular filter is adjustable and turns on the lens body face, allowing the photographer to increase or decrease the amount of filtering done. At the lowest setting the filter does very little filtering; when turned up to the maximum filtering level very little light gets through and a moire pattern appears so I do not recommend turning up the filter to this level. To get a feel for how well this filter works I took my camera outside as a big thunderstorm approached and took some pictures of one of the cloud formations. I selected two pictures from that set, one where I did not use the filter and one where I did use it on about 1/4 strength. Although the filter evenly reduced light levels, the color contrast in the filtered image is much more pronounced and obvious. The most common use for this kind of filter is to reduce the light levels, then take an extended exposure for a scene with motion, such as a waterfall. This is a very nice filter and I could not be happier with it. It is very easy to use and it really works well. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Solid Sound Profile
text: The current trend with ear buds is to boost the bass to the point of overpowering the rest of the sound profile. I don’t particularly like bass that is too heavy because it can give me awful headaches. These buds have the bass boosted but it is not over the top. These ear buds are very lightweight and low profile. Smaller than many ear buds I have used they fit in my ears very comfortably. The silicone inserts are soft and do not cause any discomfort, but just as important they create a good seal in the ear canal and as a result they have good passive noise canceling (sound isolation). This is a good sign right out of the package - many ear buds I have tried do not seal properly. The sound profile is the most important aspect of any earphones or ear buds. There are really three areas in the sound profile that merit mention - the highs, the mids and the bass. This set of buds is marketed as heavy bass and that is not completely true. Yes, they do have good bass, but it is not heavily overdriven like most. The bass is a little more front-and-center, not in-your-face, if that makes some sense. The mids are good and the music sounds full as a result, not hollow and depthless. The highs are very bright and clear which is a slight surprise - most ear buds that enhance the bass do so at the expense of the highs, so having a set that had strong bass and highs together is a very nice change of pace. These buds come with a very small carrying case. It is a pinch case and has enough room for just the buds and the replacement silicone inserts. It is a soft plastic case and provides protection only from dirt and moisture (though by no means waterproof) so this is not a case that will help when the buds are crammed in a pocket or backpack. This is a very nice set of ear buds at a very nice asking price. They have a very good sound profile and they are comfortable to wear. Keep these in mind when looking for inexpensive buds and good sound. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Works Well with Linux
text: I needed a simple dock station to copy some hard disks. The All in 1 HDD Docking System fitted my needs nicely. I was able to insert an old Maxtor IDE drive in the first slot and a brand new SATA SSD in the second slot. I had hoped to test the one-button copy feature so I powered it up and tried to follow the directions. Both drives were recognized, however I could not get the docking system to perform a drive copy. This could be due to either a brand new, unformatted SSD or due to the use of the Linux EXT2 file system (not FAT or NTFS). If I have a chance I will test copying between two FAT file systems. With both the Maxtor and SSD plugged in, I added an SD card. I could mount the card and read the files from it, or copy files from it to either of the hard disks or to my system disk! I tried using both a CF card and an SD card at the same time. However, I was not able to successfully access both at the same time. When I removed the SD card, I could read the CF card. The device came with a short manual which was written in broken English. It was marginally useful and largely discussed how to use the PC Clone EX program that came with the docking device. The docking system includes a USB hub. To test it, I plugged a Seagate USB hard disk into the USB port on the front. I was able to copy files from my camera's CF card to the Seagate USB drive. As a final test, I plugged a Maple Mini embedded ARM processor into the other port on the USB hub and uploaded an Arduino-compatible sketch. The USB hub works great! Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost, I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: This Hands-Free Kit Gets it Right
text: I have worked with quite a few car kits and some work better than others. Most of them are rechargeable Bluetooth receivers that allow you to turn your car’s stereo system into a hands-free system for talking on the phone while driving, though some plug into the 12V power outlet for power. All of the others I have used have connected to the car stereo by way of the AUX jack. But, not all systems have an AUX input which makes those solutions useless in those situations. I had an FM transmitter solution years ago that allowed me to connect a CD player to my basic AM/FM radio and it worked but I had forgotten about that type of solution until now. This kit works with Bluetooth and FM to connect phones to cars and it works very well. It also has some nice features I wish other kits had. This is a basic kit that works by allowing the phone to pair with it via Bluetooth and then uses a small, low-power FM transmitter to connect to the car’s audio system on any FM channel desired (I suggest using an unused frequency). Music can be streamed from the phone to the transmitter and from there it goes to the radio frequency in the car. It’s simple in concept and it works. No more AUX jack. For power the transmitter plugs into a USB port, and the kit includes a 2-port 12V plug. This allows for powering the transmitter and still having enough power for another device like the phone or a GPS navigator. One port on the adapter is a 1.0A and the other is a 2.1A so if you have a high-speed cable and your device can accept a high-speed charge it will work with the adapter. Because the adapter has two ports and it allows for completely disconnecting the transmitter it can be used for charging two devices at once. Regardless of where in the vehicle the 12V adapter lives, the kit comes with a magnetic pad for attaching the receiver so that the receiver can be mounted almost anywhere. This is important - it means that it can be put in an optimal spot so that when speaking it has the best chance for picking up the voice clearly which is a very good thing. In my car, the 12V outlet lives under the center console so other kits sometimes do not get the best reception for my voice. Sound quality is clear for both caller and receiver, particularly because the transmitter can be placed anywhere. When there is no competition for the channel the sound is as good as an AUX-connected sound source. This hands-free kit for the car is better than most others I have used as it is easier to place the transmitter to get clear voice transmission and it does not require an AUX port on the care stereo system to work. I am pleased with it and am happy to recommend it. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Excellent Cables at a Great Price
text: I have a good tangle of cables in my home office for a variety of devices that require a micro-USB cable. Most of these cables are very nondescript and I have no idea who made them, though there are a couple of them that have manufacturer names printed on the plugs on the end. Most are plain black and are mostly indistinguishable from one another. These cables from Magic-T are absolutely the most easily identifiable cables on the desk and it has made it very easy to assign cables to every device on the desk. But, there is more to these cables than just pretty colors. The most obvious advantage of this cable set is the colors. Each of these cables is a different color and none of them are black or gray - there’s blue, pink, orange and green. And, even more important than the color is the fact that they are insulated in nylon weave, not plastic coating, which in my experience holds up a bit better under stress and the result is a more reliable cable. The plugs on both ends are metal shielding with a plastic base, sufficient to give these strength for the connections. The cables have been inserted in the bases and attached within, not attached to the plug base, but those connections are very tight and seem to be solid so I am not concerned about them pulling loose. Each cable is about six and a half feet in length which is much more convenient for me than the regular 3' cables. These cables are capable of high-speed charging so if you have a device and a charger that are both capable of high-speed charging then these cables will work well for you. I used one for my tablet and a high-speed USB charger and the tablet did charge faster than when using a lower-grade cable. I want to mention the pricing. As I write this, the price on this set of four cables is about $9. That’s about $2.25 per cable, and the cables are of good quality. The price can change of course, but at the current price this is an absolute bargain. There’s something else I need to mention. The manufacturer offers a 12-month warranty on these cables, and to me that’s just amazing. For a cable that costs less than $2.50 per individual cable the manufacturer thinks enough of their product to back it with a 12-month warranty. I doubt I would ever need to use the warranty for one of these, but it’s reassuring to know the manufacturer believes in their products. It is hard to find fault with these cables. They are made well, they are easily identifiable and they are very inexpensive. This is a fine set at a great price. title: Works Great with Raspberry Pi
text: I selected this keyboard/touchpad with the idea of using it with my tablet. Admittedly I mistakenly thought it was a Bluetooth keyboard which would have made it suitable for my tablet but this turned out to be a misunderstanding on my part. That said, it has proven to be a very handy keyboard in more ways than I had originally planned. In particular, in addition to working with Windows and Linux it works with Raspberry Pi which opens a whole world of possibilities for this keyboard. This keyboard is very small, barely bigger than a Hershey bar, and it has a full set of keys as well a touchpad and mouse buttons on the right side. This is sufficient for doing pretty much everything you’d want to do, including surfing the web, text editing and software development. Granted, the size makes it less than ideal for some of these functions but it does work as a full keyboard/mouse combination if you want to use it that way. Right out of the box, the switch was on and the keyboard had completely drained its battery so it had to be plugged in and charged overnight. This was a surprise but was not a big deal, just unusual. When connected to a Windows 8 system the OS recognized it and immediately it was usable. It required no special drivers, no configuration changes or anything else – just plug it in and turn it on. It worked the same under Linux as well. The real test for this keyboard/mouse was on a Raspberry Pi system. The keyboard connected and worked without a glitch – expected since it worked fine with Ubuntu Linux but not guaranteed as the kernel was known to work but the hardware was not yet tested. With a second external keyboard connected it was possible to type on both at the same time and also to use the other keyboard as a regular keyboard and the other just as a mouse. There are a number of other SBC types and designs out there, and there is no reason that this device should not work with any of them that have a Linux-based kernel. Embedded Windows system should also support it as well. Though I have not really tested the full range it is good to at least 10 feet. At that range the system still recognized input from the keyboard and touchpad without any issues. So far I have found only one issue with this keyboard and that’s the space bar. I habitually press the space bar in the middle, and on this keyboard the press sensors are on the ends. The spacebar is not quite stiff enough and when pressed in the middle it bows instead of pressing down on the sensors, thereby not registering the press. To get it to recognize the press I have to press on the ends specifically. This is a minor irritant and is a very small price to pay for what this device offers. This is a very small but fully functional keyboard/touchpad combination that works with multiple configurations. It connects easily and so far has given no real operational issues. Keep in mind that this thing is extremely small, though, which is great for portability, mobility and economy of space but less pleasant for systems that aren’t being transported anywhere. title: Very Quiet and Moves a Lot of Air
text: A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job. First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air. This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working. This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum. When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on. This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Solid Lightning Cable
text: It’s good to have a solid, workable cable when charging and transferring data, and lightning cables are what works for Apple products. After the original cable that came with an iPhone failed I looked to this cable as a replacement. It has filled the need very nicely. First and foremost, this cable comes with Apple certification and that’s important. It means that Apple endorses this cable to work with their iPhone and iPad products, which in turn means that compatibility is not an issue (and neither are those compatibility messages). This cable seems to be a bit better than the manufacturer-supplied cable. It is well made and I believe it will hold up longer than the cable before it which died through stress bends at the end points. It is a little thicker and a little heavier which should hold up well. And, although it has a little heavier insulation the Apple-side plug is narrow enough to fit and connect even through more bulky cases which is a problem with some cables. So far I have had no issues with this cable. It works well, is fully compatible and it appears to be better made than the OEM cable. title: Suitable for Bird Watching and Amateur Astronomy in the Field
text: My wife loves birdwatching and our teenage son enjoys stargazing so we have an assortment of binoculars and inexpensive telescopes. Before this monocular I had never used one and even though I have not had it very long at all I am already very pleased with it. Though it is ideal for bird watching and field work, it also will work as an amateur telescope. At roughly 7" long, this monocular is large enough to be usable but small enough to fit in a coat pocket or even in a briefcase. It comes in a nice, nylon-weave carrying pouch that even has a belt loop so carrying it into the field is easy and does not take up extra room. It also has a holding strap much like a camcorder does so it can be held more securely. It has a small metal tripod suitable for setting up on a desk or table. It’s not a big tripod - the legs extend to 7.5" - but is works well if you are recording or are seated and need a steady hand. Finally, it includes a microfiber cleaning cloth in the box for wiping the lenses safely without scratching them. This is a waterproof monocular and everything about it showcases that. There are two rubberized caps for either end that cover the lenses and keep out moisture and dust when not in use. These are physically attached to the barrel (one by a rubber flap and one by a nylon cord) so there is no issue with losing the caps. Most of the barrel is rubberized as well except for the focus knob assembly and where it attaches. I used it to focus on the tree line behind the house (roughly 30 yards away) and was very pleased with how sharp and clear I was able to get the image. From the front of the house I was able to focus on the stop sign at the end of the street and had no issue with getting fine edge detail even at a distance of roughly a football field. The focus is very smooth and easy to adjust and getting the image in perfect focus is not the least bit difficult. Though I enjoy cameras and optical equipment and I have learned a good bit about optical equipment I am a far cry from being an expert, so I took this monocular to work and approached two teammates who are very well-versed in optics, photography and astronomy and I asked them to look it over and give me their honest opinion. Both of them examined it and expressed their approval. They both said similar things about it: the image through this monocular is very bright and clear, the focus is very smooth and it seems to be very well made. They both made a comment about the lens and that it was very good due to not having a darkened coating. One of my teammates told me to try looking at the stars with it. I had not really considered this but knew this would be an excellent test for it so I went outside after dark and pointed it skyward. Though I can definitely see more detail through a dedicated telescope, I was able to make out some of the larger surface detail on the moon including the high point in the middle of a crater. I was hindered by the fact that it is a full moon right now so I will have to try again this weekend during the eclipse. I then picked out a planet and looked at it through the monocular. Though it is a little tough to make out, I know I found Jupiter as I could see three of the moons as bright spots not visible to the naked eye (I have looked at it through a telescope so I recognize it from seeing it already). Finally I discovered a cluster of stars I could not see without magnification. This monocular is certainly not as good as a dedicated telescope but it is sufficient when camping and it eliminates the need to pack a big, bulky telescope unless you want to see more detail. This is a great tool for use in the field. It has very good range, the image is bright and clear and it even is sufficient for stargazing should you choose to use it for everything on the road. Great product! Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Amazing Sound, Especially for the Price
text: I spend a good deal of time with headphones on or earbuds in my ears and I have formulated some very strong ideas of what makes a pair of headphones or earbuds worth consideration. I was anxious to try the Sound Intone i66 earbuds and they have far exceeded my expectations, especially considering the cost (as I write this, they are going for about $11, but price may change). For such low-cost earbuds these are among some of the best I have used. Ok, right out of the package - I received a pink pair of earbuds. Bright, bubblegum pink! That does not bother me in the least as color is irrelevant but being pink these are just perfect for a teenage girl. These also come in brown so there is a choice if pink is not desired. In the package are the earbuds and three sets of ear inserts so that getting the right fit is easy. The inserts are a little more stiff than some of the others I have used but they are not uncomfortable. The slight stiffness might be slightly less comfortable than more supple inserts but they’re much less likely to tear. To me that is a very worthwhile tradeoff. When inserted these buds create a very good seal and they do a fine job of sound isolation. Like most headphones available today these have a talk feature that allows them to be used with a cell phone for two-way conversation. I admit that I have not tried these for conversation but will try these and come back to update this review when I have done so. I do like the fact that the microphone hangs about 6" from the ear piece which positions it almost perfectly by the mouth. The most important aspect of any set of earphones or earbuds is the sound profile. For a very inexpensive set of earbuds, these get the sound awfully close to perfect. The highs are right on target and they are clear and crisp without being oversharp. The midrange is solid and full. The bass is strong - very slightly overdriven but not to the point of extreme. I compared these to headphones costing over $100 and these compete very well. I am very hard-pressed to find much to fault with these earbuds. These fit well and they seem to be well-made, but their strength is their sound quality which is tough to beat in the under-$20 price range. And, if you really want a pair of pink earbuds, these will definitely fill the need. Regardless of the color, these are surprisingly good earbuds, better than most, but definitely one of the best values available. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Very Deep Bass
text: Sound Intone makes good, inexpensive headphones and the HD-680 headphones is one of their newest offerings. I will admit to initially disliking this particular set of headphones, but a conversation with the manufacturer and persistence with a 16-channel equalizer has brought my opinion of these headphones up substantially. I can’t say these are my favorite headphones as I am not into heavy bass, but I am pleased enough with them to use them when working on my computer. Right out of the box, these are striking phones that are quite attractive. I have the blue and white edition and my teenage son’s first words upon seeing them was, “those look great!” These are very lightweight and as a result they have a light fit. I personally prefer a headphone that fits more tightly but that’s a personal preference, not a criticism. The padding is firm but not hard and I did notice that these phones get a little warm on the ears over time - again not a big deal but worth mentioning. When it comes to the build quality, the strongest feature of these phones is the cord - I am exceptionally partial to woven tangle-free cords versus plastic coated wire. The difficulty I had with these phones initially was the sound profile. The bass is exceptionally heavy, so heavy that it drowns out the highs quite a bit and the result is a sound that is muddy and unclear. It took some time to realize that this is very reminiscent of the sound you get at an outdoor concert - the bass carries forever and the highs get lost. The midrange is absolutely solid. I don’t care for bass that’s so heavy (it gives me a headache) so I fed everything through a 16-channel equalizer. It took a good bit of experimentation and persistence but I finally was able to find the balance to get the sound right and now these phones sound great. The issue is overdriven bass; once I squelched some of the bass and boosted the treble channels just right the profile is solid. They still sound a little like being in a concert hall but that’s more than acceptable. Oddly enough, these sound good when listening to straight speech, even without an equalizer. These headphones are different than most other phones I have used. The typical headphone I use does not boost the bass to an extreme. If you really, really like bass, then these phones are for you and will not disappoint. If you prefer something a little more balanced, feed the sound through an equalizer and the sound can be made near-perfect. Although I did not initially like these phones I have come to appreciate them and can recommend them. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Good Rear-View Video System; Poor Documentation
text: Many cars on the market come with a rear-view camera that allows for seeing where the vehicle is moving when in reverse. Often the view appears on a dashboard screen. This is handy when parking and maneuvering while the vehicle is backing up. For vehicles that do not have a rear-view camera the alternative is to add on a kit that provides the same functionality. This is my first experience with such a kit and so far I am pleased with it. It does require doing a little work on the vehicle to set it up but the effort is worth it. The package contains everything needed to set up this camera system. In addition to the camera and the screen, the kit includes the mounting screws for the actual camera as well as all of the wiring to connect everything together and to the power (reverse lights). There is also a mini-remote for interacting with the video screen though this is slightly inconvenient. I spent a good deal of time reading and rereading the directions and concluded that the instructions could have been better. There are three pieces of documentation in the box; one shows a generalized set of four different configurations for connecting everything together (the fourth diagram on this sheet matches the configuration you want), one is a photocopied image of a wired system and the third is a “User’s Manual” which is one half-sheet of paper with a brief summarization of the product. There really needs to be a better documentation set than this. If you are not skilled in working with electrical systems, either plan on this taking a good while or have someone you trust install the system. It’s not especially hard to set one of these up, but it does take some patience and a little bit of knowledge of the layout of the car’s wiring. I have worked on car electrical systems in the distant past so I had a vague familiarity, but it still took me a while to have everything set up and working. Once wired the system is fairly straightforward to use. If it is wired up properly (meaning everything is connected to power on both ends and the two main components can see one another) it works nicely. The image when the camera is feeding to the monitor is bright and reasonably clear; the brightness can be adjusted as needed which helps when using this system at night. Another reviewer commented that he used a different camera connected to this system - while I am personally satisfied with the image quality, it’s reassuring to know that you can use another video camera if desired or necessary. The addition of the remote will appeal to some, but for me it’s a component that can easily be lost. The menu system on the monitor provides the same functionality as the remote and this is good enough for me. This is my first experience with rear-view video systems and though it gave me a little trouble setting up it was from lack of good documentation and inexperience, not from being a bad product. Once installed this is a nice and easy-to-use video system. Time will tell how long it works. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Excellent Camera but Troublesome Install
text: FOSCAM is a well-known name when it comes to security cameras and security equipment and they make a good variety of security solutions for home and business use. The F19803P camera is a wireless IP camera that is weatherproof, has night vision and can be accessed via smartphone. One configured and set up on the network it works great but the setup process can be a very painful one. In the box is the actual camera, the antenna, power adapter, mounting kit, installation software and an Ethernet cable. The camera housing is roughly the size of a new roll of bathroom tissue - very small, compact and lightweight. The mounting kit is a small but solid painted aluminum bracket plus the screws needed to secure it. When mounted properly, this camera can be very inconspicuous. Following the included directions, I installed the software first and then hooked up the camera to the router. According to the included documentation the IPCamera application should immediately see the camera and from there one can select the camera, log into it and manipulate it as needed. This did not work for me and the camera never did appear. I tried downing my firewall, I tried connecting to a different router and even tried directly connecting to the camera and still was unable to see it. I finally managed to reach the camera by opening the FOSCAM client software and telling it to search for cameras. When I did this, the camera finally appeared, and the IPCamera application showed it too. This works but runs contrary to the documentation. I did get into the camera finally and was able to change the username and password. I also set up the wireless network settings and found other settings to adjust like IR timer, time source and more. I found that the camera’s administration settings can be accessed as needed through the IP address and specifying port 88 (unless the port is deliberately changed). I strongly encourage assigning a fixed IP address to the camera via DHCP through the router; otherwise, the IP address can change and accessing the camera gets more difficult. I learned this the hard way, when I had the Ethernet MAC defined but not the WiFi MAC in my router’s DHCP table. My fault, but this was made more difficult by the IPCamera application still not seeing the camera and I had to let the client software scan again. I made one more mistake and reset the camera via the reset button and it cleared everything I had set already: user name, password, everything. I was concerned that I would lose everything again with a power failure so as a test I unplugged the camera for a few hours and plugged it in again, and fortunately it retained its configuration. The camera cannot see my 5G network, only my 2.4G network. However, even though my computer is on the 5G network it still can access the camera. Both networks are handled by my one router so I assume that this is normal. If you have a 5G network, make sure you also have the 2.4G network configured or keep the camera connected via Ethernet. The fact that it does not support 5G networks is not necessarily a problem but is worth knowing beforehand. Once I made it through the configuration (which was all of two hours, most of it trying to figure out how to talk to the camera), the client software allowed me to add it to the configuration and stream a live video feed from it. The video quality is actually very good and when not in IR mode is in full color. When streaming IR video the image is straight black and white, but the image is very clear. Testing with the camera indoors I killed all the lights in the room and the IR kicked in, my intent being to see how clear the image is. The image is clear enough to read text off a white sheet of paper when angled right. Specifically I held up the instruction manual to the camera at about a 2' distance and was able to read the front page without difficulty. The only complaint I have with the IR is that it does not seem to kick in early enough; when in a dimly lit room the camera still tries to use non-IR and the result is a very dark feed. I have found no way to adjust this in the camera settings other than to set the IR to cut on at a specific time which may or may not be the most useful thing. I like the fact that this camera does not need a specialized hub to work and can be run from a PC or MAC instead. This makes the system a lot more flexible and easier to manage. The real power of this camera comes in the client software. It allows for adding additional cameras (the screen settings suggest up to 64 cameras) and monitoring all of them at once on one screen. Some of the camera settings can be manipulated such as setting up recording times, setting alarms and more. Adding a camera is as simple as running a search and then adding the camera to an area. There is even the ability to play back the video that has been recorded built right in. This is a nice security camera and it works well. It has very good IR capability, it works wirelessly and has full-color video that is clear and workable. Configuring this camera can be very unpleasant, though once configured it’s a great solution. If you need a good outdoor wireless camera and you have some patience for an install that’s not necessarily smooth, consider this one. title: Solid, Well Made and Very Smooth
text: Fishing is one of the activities I have loved ever since I was very young and able to hold a fishing rod. Though I have used several types of fishing reels my personal preference is spinning reels. There are a number of reputable brands available and I have tried several - Lew’s, Quantum, Daiwa, Mitchell’s, Shakespeare and more. Until recently I was unfamiliar with KastKing as a brand and had no experience with their fishing tackle, and in a short time I have come to realize I have been missing something important. I received a Triton 3000 spinning reel for test and evaluation and have been thoroughly pleased with it. This reel has some heft to it, very solid and tight. It’s more substantial than many reels I have used but it’s also not the largest or heaviest either. In terms of size and weight, it falls in the middle of the pack of reels I have used for freshwater fishing and it’s a bit on the small size compared to many saltwater reels I have used. I have larger hands and the size it about right, but someone with smaller hands might find a smaller size (like the Triton 2000 or 2500) a better match. In terms of assembly, there is nothing loose or flimsy on this reel at all and there is nothing that required tightening or adjustment right out of the box (which has been a problem with some others I have used in the past). Overall, this is a solid and well-assembled reel. Appearance-wise, this reel is absolutely gorgeous. It is a deep shade of purple, almost black, with chrome and nickel colors on the spool, bail and handle. Appearance is not really all that important but it certainly does add to the package, and this is a reel that you won’t be embarrassed to break out in front of others. It relies on simple elegance, not bright flashy colors to make its statement. This reel has a good-sized spindle on it and it can hold a good amount of line. I put at least 150 yards of 8-lb test on this reel and there’s a lot of room for more. The spindle is tall, not deep. Ok, on to the really important stuff - how does this reel perform? This reel has 10 ball-bearings for forward reeling and the reel is about as smooth and quiet when retrieving as could be. Cheaper reels (cheaper meaning lower quality) tend to grind a little bit when retrieving or they make substantial amounts of noise, and some reels even have a clicker in them to mask the sound when retrieving. Some also feel hollow when retrieving, but the Triton feels solid and smooth without a hint of inferior build quality. As nice as the reeling forward is, one of the most important features in a good reel to me is a zero-reverse clutch and this reel has it down. When engaged, the reel will not reverse even a little and to me this is worth its weight in gold. One very real issue I have seen with some spinning reels is a poorly shaped bail that interferes with the distance when casting. If the bail is too shallow and does not allow enough clearance to allow the line to fly freely off the spindle, it can seriously impact casting distance. Fortunately, this reel has a very wide bail that has plenty of clearance around the spindle and it does not impact the cast at all. I get very good distance when casting as a result. Instead of concentrating on distance, the angler can instead concentrate on accuracy (and after years of practice I am still working on improving my accuracy). I tested the drag and am pleased with it as well. When tightening the drag the dial does not get more difficult to turn like on some other reels and the drag gradually makes the spindle harder and harder to turn. It is not a graduated turn, meaning it does not increase in steps so there is essentially a limitless variance in how tight the drag can be adjusted. The dial remains easy to turn all the way through the turning range until it is tightened completely, at which point it just stops. When reeling, either forward or backward, this reel remains balanced and does not wobble much at all. It is hard to notice wobble when the reel is attached to a rod so I tried something when I had not yet attached the reel to a rod. Holding the reel in one hand by the assembly and giving the handle a good spin, I was able to feel the reel gyrating very slightly but not appreciably. I tried the same with another high-quality reel and it was similar. This is not the case with cheaper reels which may or may not balance. I love the fact that the reel is mounted on an arm long enough to prevent the bail from whacking me on the knuckles when I retrieve. A reel mounted too close to the rod due to a short arm can have this unpleasant effect and I look for this problem specifically so I can avoid it. I also appreciate that the handle is far enough from the reel body to avoid hitting my hand. In the box with the reel is a velvety microfiber cloth bag for storage and transport when the reel is not in use. This is the only reel I have ever had that has come with such and it’s a nice touch. The bag is useful for keeping the reel clean and also for keeping supplies with it, like a small container of lubricating oil, an extra spool of line or even an extra lure or two (though this is no substitute for a tackle box). I am very hard-pressed to find anything to criticize about this reel. It is a solid and well-made, looks great and works like a dream. I believe I have found my new primary reel. title: Superb 12' Audio Extension Cable
text: I work with a sound mixing board that is used to connect multiple instruments and sound inputs to an amplification system. The limitation of the system is the cabling which prevents relocating certain pieces of equipment. One of the biggest trouble spots in the system happens to be audio cabling between the mixing board and the computer used to process the data. This audio cable has helped remedy that situation. This is one of the better-made cables I have used. Instead of a cheap, plastic-coated cable made of low-gauge wire, it is instead a heavy-gauge wire insulated in a thick nylon braid. I have had bad fortune with cheaper cables as they have a bad tendency to degrade when twisted or pulled tight. Another point of failure is the connection between the plug and the cable which is usually molded plastic that is much too flexible and allows the cable to break. This cable has a metal cap that screws down over the plug and adds a lot of stiffness to the connector. This is probably one of the heaviest audio cables I have used. This particular cable is 12' and using it as an extension in the sound system it has added a lot of flexibility to the configuration. This is a very good audio cable. It works as it is supposed to work and it is designed to last much longer than the average cable. This is an excellent choice if you need an audio cable that will not wear out or break quickly, and at 12' there is plenty of cable for almost any use. title: Excellent Audio Extension Cable
text: One of the frequent frustrations with headphones is the limited cord length of the phones - typically about 3'. Bluetooth is one way around this - an inexpensive receiver can turn a good set of wired phones into a wireless pair - but this is not always practical. An extension cable is a much more practical solution in many situations and is a lot less expensive in most cases. This extender cable is one of the better ones I have used. This is not a cheap, basic audio cable. It is a heavier-gauge wire encased in braided nylon insulation. Though braided nylon is becoming more common, plastic coating is still the standard and in my experience the nylon braid holds up under heavy use much better. More interesting are the plugs on the end of the cable, though - instead of just a molded plastic grip on the end, this cable has a substantial metal cap that screws down and gives the whole cap much more sturdiness. This won’t help with constant sharp tugging at a tight angle but it does all but eliminate most stresses on the plug. I should mention that this cable is for stereo audio only and does not work for replacing a cable used for talk (never mind that there’s no microphone). It will work with other cables that are set up for talk, but once this cable is in the mix the ability to talk goes away. That’s not a defect but a design decision. So, if you plan to use this to extend the reach of a two-way headset it will not work. This particular cable is 6' and I have it connected to my headphones and that gives me much more range to move around my work area. This is a very good audio cable. It works as it is supposed to work and it is designed to last much longer than the average cable. This is an excellent choice if you need an audio-only cable that will not wear out or break quickly. title: Very Well-Made 3.5mm Audio Cable
text: I wear headphones daily and I have had difficulties with the cables either failing or getting twisted and kinked. I looked to this cable to help resolve those issues. So far, it has definitely exceeded my expectations and has worked much better than I expected. Though it’s “just a cable” there is a good bit that can be said for it. title: Superb Tablet Stand, Suitable for Industrial Use
text: I have a 10" tablet and it primarily gets used as an e-reader and as a music streaming device. It's a great device and I love it, but I do get frustrated with figuring out where to put it when I am streaming music through it. Although it is a relatively small device it does take up some room on the desk when in a stand case. I have tried suction mounts to attach it to a window and that works fine but the window cannot move and when the window is cold the suction mount lets go. This flexible mount for tablets is a very good solution for my needs and is far better constructed than suggested by the product description. This is a simple mount in concept and design. It is flexible coil tube with a screw-on vice clamp attached on one end and an adjustable frame-style bracket attached via a ball joint to the other. In the box the unit comes unassembled and requires less than two minutes to put together. When finished, the whole thing is approximately 3' long. Everything about this mounting stand suggests that it is built to last and is designed to hold up under heavy use. The coil tube is about the heaviest I have ever seen: it is roughly a half inch in diameter and is exceptionally stiff which makes it well suited for supporting the weight of the tablet. The item description here says it will support 2.2 pounds but it will support a little more than that (though I would not try to put much extra on there, particularly if the coil is horizontal). The coil attaches to the vice clamp via a threaded machine screw assembly and it has enough threading to allow the coil to turn 360 degrees without becoming detached. This allows the tablet to be swung around a work area in an arch without having to really do anything that requires any effort. While this is great, what really caught my attention is that the clamp itself can be screwed to the coil in two ways at 90-degree angles (top or side) so that the clamp can be attached to an anchored surface that is either horizontal or vertical. This is one of those design decisions that just makes sense but I have seen very few manufacturers make this kind of effort. The coil is covered by a very heavy plastic sleeve which protects the tube and makes flexing the tube easier on the hands. The mounting bracket is connected to the top of the flexible tube by a ball joint, similar to the kind of joints many GPS navigators use in cars to attach to the suction base. When I first attached the bracket to the coil I put it on upside down, which is not a big deal except that the weight of the tablet worked against the joint and it tilted downward slightly. The bracket itself is a standard slider with a lever that presses against the slider which then catches on teeth on the frame to lock it in place. There's a fair bit of padding on the bracket to protect the tablet when it's being clamped in and when the position is being adjusted. This mounting stand is of such heavy construction that it suggests the stand was designed for industrial use. While it is just fine for home use and is not out of place in a professional office, it is a good for a manufacturing assembly line or even a busy retail location. This is a great mounting stand for tablets in 7"-11" range. The whole stand is very sturdy and solid and is build to last. Based on my experience with it I can heartily recommend it to any one who needs a mounting solution for a tablet. title: For the Price, Amazing Headphones
text: [[VIDEOID:1556b033e43375c050880cc164652923]] I wear headphones daily and I use them for listening to music more than anything else. I am very particular about my headphones and I usually use active noise canceling phones as they make travel more pleasant. They also help with listening in a studio. I received a [red] pair of these iP852 phones for evaluation and I have been absolutely blown away by them - for the price they are some of the best phones I have used. As mentioned, I received a red pair of these phones, and they look exactly like the pictures. I wasn't sure what to make of them - they almost look like toys instead of real headphones. I had low expectations on these phones and I was not sure what they would sound like, but their looks are very deceiving, in a number of ways. Normally I use over-the-ear headphones as I find them to be comfortable. These phones are on-ear phones so they do not completely cover the ears. Surprisingly, they are snug enough to stay put without effort and they are still quite comfortable. They do get a little warm after a time, but this has never really bothered me. I still prefer over-the-ear phones for comfort and listening, and this is purely a personal preference. Construction-wise these seem to be well-made. One of the things I really, really like about these phones is that they have a braided cord, not a plain plastic cord. In my experience a braided cord is less likely to kink or fray. The cord is permanently attached to the phones though, so if it catches it's not going to simply pop out but probably will yank the phones off your head. So, please use caution. The most important aspect of any set of phones is the sound profile. These are inexpensive phones - less than $25 on sale and less than $40 full price - and I expected inexpensive sound. Instead, the sound profile is far and away better than any other headphones I have used in this price range. The highs and especially the bass are solid and there is acceptable midrange. The midrange is the weakest point in the profile but I have used other headphones that sound much worse and cost a lot more. I love club tracks which hit a wide range of sound, and these phones sound really, really nice when connected to my computer and not using an equalizer. When I make adjustments with an equalizer, I can get the sound profile perfected. I decided to put these against my favorite headphones - a pair of Monster Inspiration ANC phones which I use every day for listening to music. I wanted to see if these headphones could compete with a set of phones that cost more than 10x more. I was amazed that these phones do compete, and quite nicely, for a fraction of the cost. The Monster phones do have a richer midrange and come with ANC, but the sound difference between them is marginal when considering the price difference. These are certainly not perfect headphones but for the cost they are nothing short of excellent. You can find better headphones out there but expect to pay more. These are a great deal. title: Excellent Internal USB Hub for Tower Systems
text: One of the issues with some tower cases is the placement of USB ports. Some of the newer cases have USB ports on the front but often these are USB 2.0. Even when there are 3.0 ports on the front of the case it seems there need to be one or two more. AVANTEK's 5.25" drive bay USB add-on hub adds three USB ports as well as a 2.4A charging port. The hub has two internal plugs. One is for power and one is for the USB bus. Be sure that your case and motherboard can support USB 3.0 and has the proper plugs. Once installed, the three ports are immediately available to the operating system and they work like the other USB ports on the system. The USB speeds are best realized with something like a USB 3.0 storage device like an external hard drive, though USB 1.1 devices like mice and keyboards work just fine on this hub too. What makes this hub interesting is actually the 2.4A charging port. This is very convenient for charging a cell phone, a tablet or similar device. My chosen device for testing chargers is a Magellan Roadmate GPS navigator, which is an ornery device that will not charge when powered on unless using the car charger that came with it. I selected a high-speed USB cable and plugged in my navigator and it charged up quickly when powered off. However, the navigator slowly drained faster than it charged when powered on. This was expected though it was worth a shot. I am especially encouraged at how solid this device is - the ports are securely soldered to the PC board and the board itself is mounted on several posts to the frame which makes it much less likely to flex and ultimately break. I applied some direct pressure to the PC board (not a realistic scenario in use but a good test before installation) and the board really did not flex much at all. I can't find any real issues with this hub. It's a solidly built device, it mounts easily and once connected provides 3 USB ports and a charging port on the front of a computer tower case. It is reasonably priced too which makes it a very good buy. Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. title: Solid Drive Enclosure; Works with Windows and Linux
text: Drive carriers and enclosures are a convenient method for converting internally mounted drives to USB connectivity. This particular enclosure is for 2.5" SATA drives and supports USB 3.0 speeds. So far I have gotten excellent results with it and am pleased with it. This is a tool-free device; no screwdriver or wrench is required to open this enclosure or install a drive in it. The cover slides off with a little pressure to expose the plug for the drive and the drive simply pops in. In the box is a foam pad that attached to drives that are not thick enough for a solid fit when the cover is replaced. Once assembled with a drive, this is a solid and compact enclosure that feels a lot like a Passport drive though it looks a lot nicer and feels a little more substantial. I plugged the drive into a machine running Windows 8 and the system immediately recognized the drive and the partitions on it. I was able to use the drive without issue. I tried a couple of different configurations for accessing this drive under Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL). First, I tried to access it under RHEL running in a virtual machine. I was unable to get the hypervisor to expose the drive to the OS which is a configuration issue, not a compatibility issue. To determine this for sure, I plugged the drive into a machine that runs RHEL natively with the GNOME desktop. RHEL immediately recognized the drive and opened a Nautilus window with the filesystems on each partition exposed and I was able to navigate the filesystems without any issues. I could not ask for better results. I put a 500GB SDD in this enclosure and plugged it into a USB 3.0 port and got insane speeds. I could not be happier. This is a great drive enclosure for 2.5" drives and it works great under Windows as well as under Linux. For the price, this is a great enclosure that works very well. title: Subtle Differences from Bose Original Pads
text: I purchased these replacement pads for my Bose QC-15 headphones as the old pads were torn and needed to be replaced. I selected this set of pads based on the positive reviews here on Amazon with the thought that they would be the same as the original pads. While they look the same, they are indeed slightly different. First things first - these pads are fairly easy to install though they do require a little persistence to get them to snap into place. The earphones themselves have small tabs around the edges designed to snap the pads' bases into place and hold securely, and if the pads are not snapped down they simply will not stay securely. The inner foam and cloth shield that covers the electronics is easy to install but I had trouble with the double-sided tape that holds them in place - the adhesive did not want to release the cover strip and I had real difficulty peeling that strip away without ripping the actual cloth. Once in place, the phones look exactly like they did when they were new, but I found three differences. First, the phones no longer fit into the case as easily as they once did. Instead of just turning the cups to lay flat and simply putting them in the case, now I have to mess with them slightly to fit into the case properly, though they can be made to fit. More noticeable, though, is that the pads are not as effective as the originals for passive noise canceling. A fan that I have in my office used to be canceled out almost completely with the combination of passive and active noise canceling but is now more audible than when the original pads were in place. I would not say the difference is enough to render the earphones' ability to cancel noise completely compromised, but they are definitely not the same. Finally, these replacement pads are just a little less supple and soft than the original pads. It is not all that noticeable until comparing the original and replacement pads side by side. You have to really be looking closely for the difference to notice it, but it's there. The difference in noise canceling ability is most noticeable when working in an environment with reverb. I use my phones to monitor sound coming through a professional sound board because these have always done an excellent job of eliminating reverb and leaving just what comes through the sound board. With these new pads in place, I can now hear a lot of reverb, even when I press the phones tight over my ears and have ensured that they completely cover my ears so it's not a gapping issue. The material is different, plain and simple. These are not bad replacement pads by any means. They are very good, they are comfortable and they do make these phones look brand new again. That said, they were not manufactured by Bose and there are some differences. When considering the cost difference between these and Bose parts, the trade-offs balance out favorably. If you have to have an exact match with the original pads, these are very close but not 100% identical. If you are satisfied with a [roughly] 90%-95% match, these pads work nicely for a lot less than original manufacturer pads.

title: Easily and Inexpensively Extends the Camera in your Mobile Device
text: The point-and-shoot camera market has taken a nosedive due to the prevalence of camera phones that produce high-quality images. It is difficult to buy a mobile phone that does not include a camera, and since mobile phones have become so commonplace and essential anymore there's little need for the point-and-shoot camera for most users. However, what phone cameras lack is the ability to make optical adjustments like zoom and winde-angle - all of these adjustments are done via the phone's ability to digitally enhance the image it takes. The BTOOP lens kits change that and add capability to your camera phone. The concept with this kit is simple and is very similar to add-on lens kits for more expensive cameras. A lens is attached to the camera lens that enhances the zoom, creates a fisheye effect or adds wide angle capability. The lenses attach by a clip that attaches to the camera with a hole over the lens and a thread where the extra lenses attach. It works better than I would have expected and the image quality does not suffer from this arrangement. This lens kit comes with three lenses. My favorite of the three is the fisheye lens which works surprisingly well and makes great distortion effects. It is particularly effective for emphasizing the center subject in the image. The wide angle lens also works well and creates photos that have more area covered in them. This lens is ideal for landscapes and skylines. The third lens is the most amazing of all, the macro lens. Using the macro lens I focused on a penny and was astounded by the ridge detail I could see. I took the lens off the phone and put the phone back on the penny and the phone never could focus on the penny that close. The macro lens is absolutely wonderful for very close-up shots. The kit comes with a small pouch for carrying the lenses and clip, and the pouch doubles as a microfiber cleaning cloth. It's washable too so it can be run through the wash when it becomes soiled. This kit also works well with built-in tablet and laptop cameras. Taking video with the fisheye lens in place on my laptop is a fun use of an afternoon... This is a very nice kit for easily and very affordably extending the capabilities of your phone's camera. It's very simple to use and it adds optical effects that cannot be achieved to the same degree with a phone's software enhancements. It's works well and I am happy to recommend it. title: Huge Upgrade from Point-and-Shoot - This is the Camera I Always Wished I Had
text: I did a good deal of research to find the right camera. I wanted a solid camera with a generous feature set but I didn't want to spend a huge sum either - my budget was roughly $500. At Christmastime the NX300 went on sale, enough of a sale to put it in my price range. After doing a little more research to make sure I had found the camera I wanted, I committed. So far I have been very pleased with it. Every digital camera I have used before this one has been a point-and-shoot camera, the best of which was actually another Samsung. These types of cameras are great for casual use like a day at the amusement park or making memories on a day trip, but for making really exceptional photographs these cameras are usually ill-suited. Either the focus is flat (meaning everything is one-dimensional), the zoom isn't granular enough, the color is wrong or something else is off just enough to make the picture not quite perfect. The Samsung NX300 is a "prosumer" camera, meaning it's a high-end consumer and low-end professional camera. Unlike point-and-shoot cameras it has an interchangeable lens system and can be manually focused. It has a good number of features I have not seen on less capable cameras too, such as Wifi connectivity, the ability to add color filters to the lens and much more. I'll hit the highlights. Without the lens in place, this camera is about the same size and weight as a point-and-shoot camera, maybe slightly larger but not appreciably heavier. Adding the lens adds some bulk and heft to it but it's not as large as something like a Canon Rebel or a high end Nikon. To me this makes this camera a lot easier to carry around than some other models with which it competes, and that can be important when traveling. That said, if not used to working with a camera that has interchangeable lenses there's more to carry (particularly if you use more than just a single lens). A good camera case is a good investment. This camera has several modes of operation, each optimized for specific shot types and accessible through the spin dial on the top of the camera. The one I use most when experimenting is Auto, which does most of the adjustment for the user and tries to calculate the best settings given the lighting and conditions. It's a good, general purpose mode for most situations. Smart mode is a good choice too, which has presets for a good number of predefined situations like optimized face shots, panorama views, night shots, light traces, silhouettes and several more. Of those smart settings, "Beauty Face" makes adjustments to portraits to compensate for imperfections and this is a great feature. There is a mode for giving the lens the highest priority when it comes to adjustment and that's the mode that gives the user the maximum control over zoom and focus. Manual mode gives the user good control over what to focus on automatically but the camera maintains most of the control. Shutter priority mode allows the user to adjust the shutter speed which is great for when a faster shutter is needed (like an action shot). Aperture priority mode adjusts the aperture width and thus the amount of light allowed in. Program mode seems to be roughly equivalent to Auto mode; I am still learning about that one. The menu system on this camera is accessible through a nice touch-screen interface, providing access to all manner of settings. I will not go into great detail on the menu system as to do so would make this more of a novel instead of a review. I will say this, though - it is very easy to accidentally make changes when using the menu system if handling the camera in any but the most careful of ways. Just picking up the camera when it is turned on must be done with care as it is almost too easy to touch the screen and make changes without intending to do so. It's fantastic that the screen is sensitive and can be so easily manipulated but it's so sensitive that care is required. One of the greatest things about this camera is that it can take pictures that have a 3-dimensional quality to them. The main subject of the picture in the foreground is clearly in focus and the surroundings at different depths are in varying levels of being out of focus, and this gives the photo a depth that usually is very difficult to achieve with a point-and-shoot camera. I spent an afternoon playing with the camera just experimenting with this and was thrilled at how natural and easy this camera makes it to take this kind of picture. Built into the camera is the ability to connect to a Wifi network for uploading images to a smartphone or to share online. This is a nice-to-have but it is not a feature I personally need. The lens system on this camera is what makes it shine. I bought the 18mm-55mm OIS lens with the camera and this is my first exposure to smart lenses. The lens assembly itself has smarts built into it and when the camera mode it set to give the lens the most control the lens controls the digital zoom and the focus. The focus ring on the lens allows the user to determine what specifically in the picture is in focus which allows for overriding the camera's idea of what should be the main subject of the picture. Sometimes the camera gets it wrong and by using the lens to override it's possible to get the focus just perfect, even on very distant shots or shots that are very busy. Samsung occasionally updates the firmware for this camera - and the lenses - and updating is relatively simple. With a PC connection the firmware download to the camera is quick and the update is applied through the menu system. Though this camera is more than capable of taking high-quality video I do not use it for such. I prefer using a dedicated video camera. That said, video recording is easy with the touch of a single button on the back of the camera, to the right and just above the touch screen. What little recording I have done with it has turned out excellent of course, but I will not use this function most of the time. For all of the positive things I can say about this camera, I do have a couple of minor gripes. First, though it's convenient to have a removable flash I would have preferred to have the flash built-in to the camera body. It's a minor issue but it's worthy of mention. A printed manual would have been nice too, but at 200+ pages it is understandable why one is not included. At least it's on the CD in the package. It is common knowledge that the battery life is not great on this camera and that the only way to charge the battery (without buying a separate charger) is to plug in the camera, either with a USB charger or into the computer itself. I have found the camera I really wanted. It is a highly capable camera with a really generous feature set and it takes amazing shots (with some practice). There's a learning curve with it if all you have used prior is a point-and-shoot, but the effort is worth it.

title: Inexpensive Way To Extend the Capabilities of a Samsung Camera
text: I ordered this lens and filter kit to go with my Samsung NX300 with the intent of expanding the capabilities of the camera without spending a fortune. I looked at several different kits before settling on this one, based on the price. I will admit to being a bit apprehensive about the cost in relation to the number of lenses and filters in the kit (presently this kit sells for less than $35 on Amazon as I write this) but my concern was ill-placed - this is a good kit. I will start off by saying that I am not a professional photographer by any stretch of the imagination. I could be best described as an enthusiast who is trying to learn as I go. I have experimented and played with many of the various components with this kit, starting with the 2.2x telephoto lens. This is a chunky item, which should be expected as it is a glass lens. It attached without issue to my 18mm-55mm OIS lens and I was able to use it almost immediately out of the box. It took me a little fiddling at first to get the focus just right as I am still learning with the camera but once I figured out the manual focus I was able to improve the zoom range with the telephoto lens in place. This, to me, is worth the cost of the kit. One thing I did notice, however, is that when the telescoping zoom is not fully extended on the regular lens, this lens adds a shadowy blackout area around the perimeter of the image that fades when the zoom is telescoped out. My favorite component of this kit is the .43x wide-angle lens which works surprisingly well with the camera's included lens. It is another chunky item like the telephoto lens and it attaches easily as well. Even at closer ranges (15 feet or so) it allows the camera to capture appreciably more than the regular lens, without distortion. This is probably the one component I will use more than the others, and again this is an accessory that is worth the cost of the kit. This lens is not going to give the same quality result as a dedicated wide-angle lens but the price/quality tradeoff is worth it. There are four close-up lenses in this kit that vary in strength. These are fun to play with though I did start to get a lot of edge distortion when using the strongest lens. This is not a problem as there are times when this kind of distortion is a good thing. I was able to get similar close-up shots - without distortion - with the Samsung lens but it required a lot more effort. Interestingly, one of these lenses had a smudge on it when I removed it from it's cellophane envelope. A quick wipe with a microfiber cloth did a fine job of cleaning the lens but this puzzled me - why was it smudged? The wide-angle lens comes coupled with a macro lens that is absolutely astounding for close-up shots. I use this lens for taking pictures of pattern weaves, close-ups of surfaces, animal fur and other interesting subjects (the knee of my denim jeans makes a really interesting background shot). It works even a little better than the close-up lenses and is likely going to be the only lens I use for when I need a really detailed close-in shot of something. Though this lens outperforms the close-up magnifying lenses it requires decoupling from the wide-angle lens before it can be used and this is a minor hassle. The kit includes a UV filter, a CPL filter and a FL-D filter. I used the CPL filter while experimenting and the result was minorly disappointing but I figured that was due to unrealistic expectations. It did tweak the color profile just a little but not dramatically like I had hoped. The FL-D filter was another story and gave the whole picture a completely different color profile. It is designed for use with fluorescent lighting (which means it should be used a lot when indoors) so when it is used with incandescent lighting it give a very eerie and unusual hue to pictures. With my lens I can adjust for fluorescent lighting electronically so this isn't a lens I necessarily need but I still like to mess with it. I have not tried the UV filter. The cleaning kit is an important item in the kit, for removing dirt and smudges from the various lenses without using a harsh cloth. It's very basic but is a fine start - cleaning spray, cotton swabs, a microfiber cloth and a squeeze duster for puffing away particles when a full cleaning is not needed. This kit includes a couple of other miscellaneous items as well, including a miniature tripod for a desk mount and a 6-compartment memory card storage case. These are nice-to-have extras, though I confess I am thoroughly unimpressed with the tripod which is a flexible bendy-leg tripod that does not retain the position in which it is set when supporting the camera, so it really is of little use. I continue to mess with the tripod, though, as I am sure I can get it to work in certain scenarios. The main negative I encountered so far was actually the manner in which the kit was packaged and shipped to me. Everything was in a large plastic envelope bag with no padding at all. What would prevent the items in the kit from being crushed in such a shipment? Fortunately, all items were individually wrapped in small and sturdy cardboard boxes and one of those boxes was actually slightly crushed though there was no damage to the merchandise inside. Something like this should be shipped in a larger corrugated box, to better protect everything. If you have a Samsung camera for which this kit is compatible, this is a very good kit to extend the capability of the camera without breaking the bank. The various lenses add range and effects, the filters are nice to have on hand and the extras are icing on the cake. At the current pricing, this is a very good deal.

title: Very Slow Install Process but Wicked Fast Performance
text: We have a router that supports the 802.11ac standard but until we got this router we had no way of connecting to it beyond the 802.11n standard. I was very interested in trying this adapter to see if it really is that much faster. It’s absolutely very fast and has wonderful connection reliability but suffers from a very slow software installation process. I connected it to a Windows 7 64-bit system and allowed Windows to search for a driver. When that failed (as I assumed it would since this is a new product) I put in the installation CD and started the installer. The process took a surprisingly long time just to install and load the driver, to the point that I considered rebooting the box and starting over. It did finish though and then was ready to connect. It connected without effort to our 5GHz network and immediately was able to serve up content. Everything seemed to be faster but we were not sure - until my teenage son connected to a Minecraft server and started playing. In addition to a lag-free connection he noticed about a 20% gain in frame rates sustained. So far I can’t find anything beyond the clunky install that stands out as a negative. This is a fast adapter and it worth the one-time install time if you want fast, reliable connections and have a router that can handle the 802.11ac standard.

title: Outstanding
text: I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them. Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire. I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers. I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound. I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy. I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue. In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room. So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.

title: Outstanding in Their Price Range
text: I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones. First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means. The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore.
