text: After a year of owning my first Android, I've had my 32GB SanDisk used without issues. At least, that's what I had thought until I popped in the Samsung. It could be a variety of reasons (using Samsung cards with a Samsung phone, having a newer card, etc.), but the Samsung card, I've noticed, works a bit smoother and faster with my memory. I store all the apps I can onto my memory card, have quite a bit of music, books, and photos/videos, and they all load efficiently and far more quickly than my previous cards was capable of. Maybe it's just that the card is new, but I'd like to think it's because I'm using the card with a correspondingly same-brand phone.

title: Great for the features, but the stand is not as sturdy.
text: This sucker is strong, no doubt, but my phone is heavy. I have an S5 with an Anker battery case, and the stand, while strong enough to withhold the phone up, cannot grip the magnet as well, as such, the phone does slide down during my car ride, so I have to keep readjusting. That said, the actual features are fine, even if the speaker on my phone isn't the best (seriously, who thought having the speaker on the rear of the phone was a good idea?). You may find that many of the reviews for the app say it's not great, but be aware that the app requires either this stand or Logitech's ventilator mount to operate. With either of those, you'll be good to hear all the features. I tend to use the car radio more for music, so the lack of musical options on the app isn't a downer. What makes it indispensable for me is the heavy-duty stand to use Waze and to pick up or send the occasional call. Thus far, after a week of using, I've not had any issues with the phone. The suction works fine, even if the dashboard isn't perfectly flat. It grips on without any wobble.

title: More portable than my last.
text: In my last review for the GolfBuddy CT2 device, I noted that I'm not a very avid golfer. I'm still not, but that doesn't mean I wasn't able to give this a thoroughly tested and detailed try. The other I had was made to store in pockets, but that doesn't mean this one is any different. This one is about just as small, and easily fits into the caddy and pockets I used. Overall, working it was simpler as I used to the other. Just as the last one I reviewed, this was used about a couple of times, though I plan on using this one a few more times at the very least. Nevertheless, it has about half the screen ratio compared to my other device, as this is meant to be worn around the body and supplemented as a watch of sorts. The menus are easily navigable with one hand (with only a couple of fingers necessary, at most), and all information is there with just a few presses. I used with the same friend who helped me out last time, although this time I didn't need his help, especially since I had this on me at all times, so I had to force myself to use it and learn.

title: First time using one of these. Great little gadget.
text: I don't golf as much as I'd like these days, but for the couple of games I participated in recently I decided to bring this along. I've never used a rangefinder before, so using this was a nascent experience, to say the least! Another reviewer here mentioned watching the introductory video offered on the company’s website. I did so, though I used the instructions as well. The video I watched before my first use, and kept the instructions with me during the games. The video was far more helpful than I initially thought as it went into the gadget's features into great detail without being exhaustive (they even put a Table of Contents at the beginning of the video so you can jump around). Even though it made using the device far more intuitive, I found that, when it came time to actually use the device, I still fumbled through the screens; I often had the button configurations mixed, and so many times I’d enter screens which I didn’t intend. I’m uncertain if this is something to do with the design of the gizmo or if they all are like this. I s’pose I’ll just have to become accustomed to it. During one of my games, I had a friend of mine use it with me, and he got the hang of it faster than I did; his experience with other golf GPS devices was minimal, but it still was more than what I had. He was able to memorize the shortcuts better than me, and that helped me while I watched him navigate. While it’s a great learning experience for me considering I've used it only a couple of times, it was very nifty to have and helped a ton. The backlit feature is nice, but if you’re golfing early in the day you probably won’t need it much. It’s light in its weight, no doubt, and convenient to stash in any pocket. The dot-matrix display makes the experience much easier to read and manipulate; truthfully, I did think that most of the screens are organized very well from screen to screen, image to text. The company seems to have excelled in this area. I realize I became far more serious in my game with this than before; I'm not a very competitive person, but something like this will be very useful for those who take the game of golf more serious than a stroll through the field. I'm sure that, if you've used these before, the layout and button configuration is a breeze. I'm new to this world (not golfing itself, of course), so the whole experience of using these is a tad overwhelming. I just keep telling myself that it’s like adding the map features from my golfing video games to the real world!

title: Decent replacement.
text: We got this to replace our old camera, which had been knocked over. It worked well enough, but the antennae kept falling apart after the incident, and by that time it was well past its warranty. We didn't realize how much more that one had than this model, especially considering they're both around the same price. Right out of the box, though, my wife and I noticed how sturdy this one seemed. It's small, but it has some weight and over the past month we haven't had it budge from its spot at all. We use ours as a kids monitor. As such, we don't mind that this stands out. It's bright white, and has LEDs for night vision. When we need to, we use it as a security camera when we're away for long periods of time. It'll make do. Compared to our previous camera, this one was a LOT easier to set up. Because it has its own app, the camera and our phones synced perfectly and instantly. Before, we had to pick and choose from various apps since the camera didn't have its own. It was cumbersome and confusing, so we welcome this change. As far as IP cameras go, this one was easier to set up. I would still like to use this camera on a browser, but I haven't ventured into that, if at all possible. It doesn't do as much as my old camera at the same price (namely, rotate), and the cloud feature makes me wary to the point that I turn it off when I don't need it, but it's a good, sturdy little replacement for our previous model.

title: Buttons could be better. Alarm is solid, though.
text: I've been wanting one of these since I first discovered them on a tech blog last year. I have a bad habit of being a grumpy morning person; part of it is going to sleep late, the other part is the way I wake up. So I then discovered that some alarm clocks wake you by showing you artificial sunlight. Perfect, I thought. I was excited to get this set up when it arrived. I found the box a bit light, but I got out the pieces and assembled everything straight away. The settings were very easy to get done, even though the buttons seemed confusing at first. There are touch buttons on the light part, as well as alarm and volume buttons on the base. The lamp itself is a bit light, however. I mean weight-wise. It tips over my nightstand quite a bit. And that brings me to the buttons. My daughter, two, loves to touch gadgets. This is no exception. If you plan on getting this, put it somewhere where kids can't reach. Even at her slightest touch the settings are constantly reset, so I have to put them back. As of right now I have to reset the settings again, but I do love the clock and I find myself in a better mood in the mornings. But not when I see my daughter reaching for the clock as I get up. The light glows after some time, and really gets a good light in my face. The days are getting warmer here in Chicago and so the sun is shining more and more through the windows. Still, I'm able to utilize this alarm to get the sunlight less offensive. The speaker on it is really clear for the size; maybe I'm just surprised at how well speakers have gotten in alarm clocks. Overall, great. The lowest brightness for the clock isn't too bad. You can't really see it when the bedroom light is on, but at night it does get a little brighter than it seems. On my nightstand I put a pillow there to block just above the digital clock so the numerals get blocked out but I still get the light from the actual wake-up light. Overall I'm pleased with it. I could have some heft to keep it more stable, and I'd prefer harder-to-press buttons (both for my toddler and my snooze tendency). Still, it's a lot better than using my phone as my alarm clock, especially since I don't like bringing in phones into my bedroom, thus allowing me to get to sleep right away.

title: Finds my car in a pinch.
text: Got this to locate our car, and honestly it works. Left it in the glove compartment and checked in on it over the holidays periodically. Between lots of holiday shopping, eating at restaurants, and going to the theaters, we did lots of parking and had to find our car on a regular basis. The first few times I forgot I had it, but when I looked it up I was able to find the car right away. I haven't lost reception yet, so I don't know how long the utility will last. But for now it's a great convenience.

title: Frustrating.
text: I'm a burgeoning audiophile and I'm always eager to try new cans to add to my listening experience. A while back, say 2007 or so, I jumped into the deeper waters and decided to upgrade my stock Apple ear buds (why I didn't sooner is beyond me). I haven't looked back since, and continue to look forward this very day. But do these headphones do my ears and music justice? Right now my arsenal consists of some Sound Blasters I use for my computer and my trusty ol' Sennheisers which I've had since 2007 (the selfsame headphones with which I used to help me jump from Apple), along with Monoprice ear buds I keep at work. I'm not the most professional audiophile, but I sure as heck can tell some differences in quality, especially if the sound source is in FLAC. Unfortunately, I'm not the most ecstatic about SMS Audio's STREET by 50, especially at the higher premium for Star Wars branding. I've always been wary of celebrity-endorsed products; never trying Beats, I've been bombarded by them on the streets of Chicago by the candy-colored headbands on people's heads. I've always wondered about their integrity, until a fellow flesh-and-blood audiophile renounced them after she had used her ATH -M50s for some time. I took her word for it and never considered using Beats. But me, being the Star Wars fanatic, had to try the SMS Audio. When they arrived I admit I was impressed by the fancy packaging. For $200, the headphones arrived looking like it. They came in a slipcased box that was a little difficult to remove as the vacuum-sealed enclosure proved a tough fit, but they open up sweetly after that. There are some nice manuals that come with, along with some neat little Star Wars stickers and papers. There's even a cleaning cloth and nice soft zippered case. The headphones came folded inside the case. When I opened 'em up and took out the included removable cable and tried them on, I was a bit dumbfounded and how uncomfortable they felt around my head with such soft ear pads. I'm not sure if I need to break them in longer, but I've been using them steadily for a month and so far I haven't noticed a difference. My ears ache after just 20 minutes. The sound was very disappointing at first, though I admit it did warm up (or down?) after a few weeks. But are they a large improvement over my $30 Sennheisers? A little, but not considerable. I can hear more background noise--that is, in the music--but there's not much balance as I have to turn up the volume to notice any huge improvement. There's a bit more bass than I'd like, but not enough to drown my ears in it. I like the fact that the cable is detachable, but the ones they included feel a bit cheap and they tangle easily. I HATE the fact that they have the buttons, something which I've always hated since the iPhone came standard with them. But that they are removable altogether makes up for the buttons, as I'm able to change them out with custom, and higher quality, gold-plated cables. The colors are fantastic; honestly, they were the reason I was drawn to them, but they look metallic in the press shots whereas, when you get them, the material is actually plastic, forcing the colors to be a lot lighter, more matte, and cheaper in feel. I'm all for matte, but I had hoped the headphone band was metallic; alas, it's plastic. So that's my take on the cans. Take them or leave them. They're nice headphones, and I've gotten plenty of complements on them both from friends and at work, but at the steep price tag I can't recommend them, especially when you can get far superior headphones for much less (like the revered Audio-Technicas).

title: Works great, just as good as my SanDisks.
text: I use SanDisk for all my memory card needs as they've always been very reliable. But Samsung, of course, is a fine manufacturer of electronics, so I thought I'd give them a try. This microSDHC card comes with an SD adapter, but I never use them as I already own a SanDisk USB adapter that plugs in any size SD card. I've been using the card with my SanDisk Clip Zip (the treachery!) and haven't noticed any lag. The card is read just as quickly as SanDisks themselves, and it's always handy to have an extra card around.

title: LEGO iPod case
text: The case is slim and is fairly comfortable to hold, the lego plate isn't that much in the way. It is easy to snap on, only slightly difficult to take off, and the edge of the case slightly goes over the rim of the iPod. Although it is small, you can build on the lego plate and. If you have the right bricks, you can literally build up and over, you can create a stand for your phone out of legos. However, the sound and lock buttons, and the headphone and charger stations are very exposed. Other wise, it's a very good case.

title: Sturdy.
text: Works well with my wife's MacBook and our TV. We connect her laptop to a Mediabridge HDMI cable, which then plugs into our TV, and the resolution is stunning. It's very sturdy and complements the HDMI's thickness, and doesn't seem like it'll tear or rip if it's accidentally tugged on too forcefully. Or if our 2-year-old daughter happens to snatch it away when we're not looking.

title: So easy to use.
text: We have a TP-Link router, so getting an extender of the same brand seemed to fit the bill in extending our Wi-Fi issues. We live in a 150-year-old apartment building with very thick walls. The cable for the TV and Internet is located in the living room, whereas my office is on the completely opposite side of the building. There are about three walls in between, so my Internet was shoddy at best. I have an iPhone, MacBook Pro, a Toshiba PC, and some handheld gaming consoles, and the only one to get decent service in my office was the MBP. I ordered the signal extender and stuck it into our bedroom, which is the halfway point from the router to my office. Setting up the device was extremely easy, and took all of a couple minutes (half of which was me making sure I did it right). At first, I noticed no boost in Wi-Fi to my office. Before, the strength of signal reaching back there was about two or three bars on my Toshiba PC, and the first or no arc on my iPhone. However, after going about my business, I found that my Toshiba PC only once has dropped under three bars, and sometimes even reaches its full signal strength--but that's happened once. My iPhone is about the same, but sometimes it does show full signal strength as well. I never get any more disconnected webpages in my office, and I can go about my work and non-work without having to worry about taking the power off my PC and dashing to the living room. Only once in the past month or so has it lost signal, but it picked up right away. It also acts as a nice nightlight with its warm blue glow, illuminating the path to the door so I can get out for a quick midnight getaway to the throne room and back.

title: Works with my PS3. Connector on wrong side, though.
text: I use this primarily for my PS3. Since the system comes with only two USB ports, and there are a healthy amount of accessories for it, the ports usually get hogged up. Cue the Belkin hub. I've got the Eye and my Turtle Beach headphones plugged into the first port with the hub, while the second remains free for charging. It's been working fine this past week, and it's small design lets met tuck it away to the side of the PS3 without worry, save for the USB connections plugged in, obviously. It's kinda stupid that the connector for the hub is on the same side of the ports, making it kind of awkward, but what are you gonna do? The lights flash to show which connections are in use. Overall a nice little hub. We'll see how it stands in the long run.

title: Fantastic surge protector. When it's on.
text: Got this one to use in my office. I used to have the standard 6-outlet bar for my computer and gaming setup, and an additional 3-outlet plug with USB outlets on the wall. I found that I was constantly plugging and un-plugging devices on the 6-outlet one, so I decided to get one that has a couple more. I like this one in particular because it has the right amount I need for now. The last two toward the bottom are spaced a little wider than the rest, which is perfect for my bulkier plugs, namely my shredder and my MacBook Pro charger. Haven't had the chance to use the phone plugs as we don't have a landline (Who does these days?). We purchased a multi-printer with the fax option, so maybe that'll get some use in the future. Overall, great. This is my third or fourth Belkin surge protector, and I'm pretty satisfied with them all. They feel heavy-duty and sturdy, so I don't see them wearing out any time soon, no matter where we place them. About a few weeks in after using this, I noticed that the switch would be turned off every so often. It was strange, because it hadn't happened to any of my other surge protectors. I asked my wife if she had accidentally turned it off while walking around the area, but she said no. It was really frustrating, because my chargers and alarm clock would turn cease to operate because of this, and I'd have to turn the switch back on every time and recharge my devices and reset my clock. One morning, when I put my one-year-old daughter down so I could get my breakfast, I noticed she immediately shot for the surge protector and switched it off. Must be the shiny red light.

title: Five stars for the audio. The video: meh.
text: Sorry for the lengthy review. I love this sound bar. Five stars for the audio. No doubt about it. I consider myself relatively gadget-savvy, but certainly not tech-savvy. I love gadgets, but I'm an idiot when it comes to sound and sound-related technology. I only recently stopped using ear buds altogether and switched to my Sennheisers as my primary listening `phones. My family and I live on the third floor of a three-apartment house, and not once did I ever consider getting surround sound. I have the speakers for it, as they were hand-me-downs, but I don't want to set them up lest I receive the wrath of my neighbors. That, and I don't even have the connections necessary on my TV (my TV is two years old; the speakers are far older than that). I recently heard about sound bars (though the PS3 one that came out a while ago caught my eye before), and thought that might be a better fit for me. I don't normally track Vine orders, as they usually get delivered on Tuesdays. But I was so excited about this one I kept looking on UPS's website, only to be disappointed to read that it had not been delivered on Tuesday; when I got home, my hopes were ultimately crushed when I found the "undelivered" sticky on my mailbox. What's one more day? I signed the note and left it for the UPS man. When I finally got the package the next day, I realized why they needed a signature: the box was huge! And there's no outer box, so all that's delivered is the product in its factory packaging, as if you bought it from the store yourself. Everybody and they momma are going to know what you ordered. But, thankfully, I don't have to worry about theft in my neighborhood too much. So when I unboxed it, I was surprised to see how little real estate the actual sound bar took. Initially, I was surprised to see how big the box was, as I didn't think the bar itself was too big. But then I realized the box was oversized to accommodate the subwoofer. Instructions were easy enough, but the HDMI set-up was a pain. There's a disc with the manual, but I would prefer if LG's website lets you download it (as of this review, they still don't have it up). Out of three HDMI cables I had lying around (two from the same brand), only one worked. I have two Mediabridge cables, one six- and the other nine-feet, and a cheapo one which came with my Comcast DVR. Only the Mediabridge six-foot cable worked, for some odd reason, so that's the one currently connecting the sound bar. Nevertheless, the Internet capabilities are going to be wasted on me, I'm assuming, as I already have services such as Netflix on my PS3, and I don't see myself switching to the sound bar any time soon. I haven't tried the other apps, so I can suggest getting this model without the Internet capabilities for the cheaper price tag. Really, you're paying $100-$150 just to have Wi-Fi on it, when many most likely have such services on other devices. There's an optical cable included for the audio, as well as a wall mount. I won't use the mount till we buy a house, so I can't say much on that. I love that the subwoofer is wireless. I knew where I wanted to place the sound bar and subwoofer before they arrived, and I was pleased that I was able to put them exactly where I wanted. I have a 47" Toshiba, so the sound bar and TV are perfectly matched. My initial sound tests were Game of Thrones, Arrested Development, and Dexter's Laboratory (I'm a kid at heart), and the sound was amazing. I've never used other sound bars, but, considering this isn't a 5.1 surround sound system, I was blown away. The sound was perfect, exceeding my expectations. As I mentioned, I'm a newb to the audio world, so forgive my ignorance and bliss. I'm perfectly content with my sound bar, though, as our current "surround" sound system. My wife didn't like it at first--and still kinda doesn't--as she thought "it's too loud," but over the first weekend, when we watched The Last Stand (awful movie, by the way), she changed her mind. She said it was like being in a theater--at least, the next best thing. The bar itself is great, but the subwoofer really adds that punch where you can *feel* the sound. I have the subwoofer next to the couch for extra oomph. All in all, I love it. I give the audio itself five stars, but I'm taking one star away for the Internet services. Honestly, I don't see the reason for paying the extra money when the other model with audio only is just as good. I still haven't used the video options, but will update this review if I ever do. The remote is a bit large for just a sound bar, as I'm using only the power and volume buttons, as well as the occasional input button for Bluetooth. The latter feature is nice, but don't go moving your iPod/iPhone/other streaming device around, as the connection breaks easily. But when it's still, the music quality sounds great. After getting this sound bar, I no longer care what my neighbors might think.

title: Works for me.
text: Before this stand, I used another Fellowes one for my laptop at home, and it proved its worth--for a while. However, with my new desk setup, I needed something which I could use while changing the height and angle of my laptop screen in a way the old stand simply couldn't. I have a Unicomp keyboard and Logitech mouse which I prefer using, and my "home" laptop needed a better stand. Enter this Lift. I've seen many angled laptop stands, and that's what I had in mind when I wanted to switch my old one out. Plus, my old one was better suited for the monitor at work, so I wanted to take that when I had the chance. Finally, I had the opportunity to get an angled one, so I jumped on it. I'm not using this stand with my laptop by itself. I'm using it as a supplemental to "lift" it up with my home desktop setup being my keyboard and mouse. For that, the stand works marvelously. The angle and height are just about right; I no longer have to arch my neck uncomfortably forward. Plus, I can take my old stand to work and finally have proper posture there too. I can't see using this by itself. My hands would quickly become painfully uncomfortable. Heck, I can't stand using keyboards with their built-in mini stands. I honestly don't know why they're there; the angle cramps my wrists very fast. So for my use, I think the stand is great. There's even some empty real estate near the back to put things under, and it seems sturdy enough overall. It's currently holding my Toshiba 17" Windows PC, which is snugly fit.

title: Pricey, but fun for baby.
text: My five-month-old daughter loves this thing. Well, so far. We've had it for a couple weeks, and bust it out whenever we're home and she's awake, and we have some free time (which is hardly ever, but still). When I realized the apps uses with this is the same as the [[ASIN:B0080D58GA Fisher-Price bConnect Digital Soother]], I just flipped it over to the mirror and let her play with the toys. My complaints are that the mirror is embedded behind the clear film (which would prevent the baby from touching the phone), so the reflection is milky. Also, because of her size, the mirror doesn't reach her face when she plays with the toys, so it's kind of useless anyway. We don't really use the straps on the sides to hang the toys as her little arms won't be able to reach them on either side when she's lying in the middle, so we just hook `em all on the centered rings and she likes them just fine. It's easily portable, though I question its price-point. It's worth $20, in my opinion. Also, if you have newer iPhones or iPods, they won't work due to their elongated size. But my daughter could care less (yes, sarcasm), and for her it's a lot of fun. My gripes come from the paying adult's point of view.

title: Freakin' love these.
text: If you're like me and have many gadgets and other electronic devices around the house which use long amounts of cables (or a surplus of cables at that) and usually toss out the plastic ties they come with, these Velcro ties are a boon to the household. I actually didn't realize I needed them so much until I ordered them just for some TV cable ties, and then found myself wrapping cords from my video game controllers to cable box cables to whatever. They're mostly used around the TV, since video game concoles and other devices are hooked up to it, but I plan on using some more with my computer cables and accessories. They might be a bit pricey at $18 for 25, but I find them to be well worth it, and would even buy more once I ran out. I like that the whole sides are taken up by Velcro, so you can tie it as tightly as you want without any part of it hanging. I personally ordered the 8" size, but might go one size smaller next time since most of the cables I've used them on didn't require so much length. Still, I'm glad I have them, and have already recommended them to people. You really don't know how useful they are until you get them.

title: Job well done thus far.
text: I'll update this with more use. So far, the alarm clock radio proved exceptionally. The power of the sound is fantastic, and easily rivals the other top brand iPhone/iPod docks out there. The buttons don't stick, and seem to last a while (had this for a couple months now). The light is a nice hue, not too bright in the night time. The dock itself does protrude out to allow iPods of varying sizes and inside cases, so we'll see how durable it is in the long run.

title: Design is great, sound is subpar; at this price, I wouldn't recommend.
text: Perhaps if the sound was better, or if the price was lower, these would be great headphones. The design is slick, and actually comes fully black-gray brand new (I know they "customize" over the years, but the blue on the cans in the Amazon picture threw me off). The stretchiness is great, and I don't fear that the headphones would break easily if, say, someone accidentally sat on them. Nonetheless, I do have some gripes. First, the sound is absolutely awful for $100. There was some tinny noise, and because the headphones have a hard time adjusting to my skull, I couldn't get the right position for the full sound effect. It's a shame that headphones of this price can't even beat my $20 Sennheisers (which is no jab at my beloved Sennheisers). Another issue I had is with the cord. I understand that it's certainly non-tangable, but it comes with a longer cord that makes absolutely no sense. The longer cord isn't the major issue, though; it's the short cord that extends from the headphones: it's so short, it can't attach to *anything* without requiring the longer cord. Maybe if you were on your bed and the iPod/music device was on your chest it would work, but I imagine people aren't buying these cans for bed use. The longer cord is absolutely fundamental to using, so I don't know why they even bothered separating it from the cans themselves. They should've made the shorter cord longer and the longer cord slightly shorter. While the design is superb, I'd look elsewhere if you want good sound quality.

title: Like everyone else, these are great headphones, but it has its issues.
text: I was ecstatic to receive these headphones because, while I like to do some gaming before I go to bed, my wife gets shuteye earlier as her workday begins at the "buttcrack of dawn" (her expression); but while the TV is located next to the bedroom, the volume has to be kept at a reasonable volume so as not to disturb her beauty rest, which leaves me, then, with little to no volume. Therefore, these headphones seemed like a lifesaver for the PS3, but when I first received them, I could not for the life of me get them properly connected. Like everyone else, it took me a while (days, unfortunately) to realize that I would need to use the RCA cables from the PS3 to use these to their fullest potential. To start off, and due to the fact that I couldn't get them hooked up the PS3 first, I'll explain testing them on the Mac. They work terrifically. I tested out a bunch of music and some videos, and the sound was supreme. The software is a digital download from their site, and necessary to fully utilize the headphones' capabilities. At times it sounds a little overwhelming, but tweaking it to your standards with the software helps to alleviate that. It even lets you save profiles in case someone wants to set the settings to their own preferences. After one charge, I've yet to recharge the headphones and been using them for days. Once I was able to wrap my head around the fact that I'd have to dig for my RCA cables from the PS3 box, I plugged them in, followed the slightly confusing instructions that came with the headset, and played away. True, the sound isn't the greatest in terms of clarity, but it suits basically nonetheless. For the price, you're probably better off getting other headphones that are specific to consoles. While these headphones advertise as being cross-platform, the Mac/PC audio leaves much to be desired from console hearing. With that, the customer service is marvelous. I placed a comment on another's review before posting mine about the console frustration I was having, and I received an email a few hours later from a customer service rep from the company, asking me to get in touch with them about the issues I was having. With some patience and instruction, I finally realized that the HDMI cable just isn't enough to use these. If you want some good cross-platform headphones and don't mind sacrificing quality for consoles, these are excellent; if you do more computer gaming than console, then go ahead. However, if you want some headphones that are superb for PS3 and/or 360, I'd suggest other ones. I didn't get to test these on the Xbox 360 as I don't have one, but from what I've heard don't even bother.

title: Comfy!
text: I've heard about these foam tips for quite some time, but staved off as the gel ones that came with my [[ASIN:B000FUESSU V-MODA Bass Freq Earbuds (Bling Bling Black)]] worked just fine. The bass is great, and the gel bud tips enhance the sound even further. Nevertheless, I decided to order these just to see what the fuss was about. Many other reviewers seem to give them great reviews, so I, what with me being a bass freak, decided to give them a whirl. At first they're excellent, and fit extremely comfortable. After a few wears, though, they seem to lose their greatness and tightness. HOWEVER, and this is a big however, they once again expand to perfectly fit the inside of my ear. Not sure how that happened, but they went back to how they first fit, but even more comfortably. If that's not the case for everyone, and the foam tips just collapse with time, then I'd say avoid these. BUT because with my experience they retained their fit inside my ear, and were indeed customized over time to fit perfectly, then I tout these to the extreme. Just go to the product page and make sure they fit your earbud headphones. They're a bit pricey, yes, so not necessary if what you have works fine; they just provide more comfort and enhance the bass for me.

title: So far so good. Case needs a little breaking-in.
text: I ordered this to match my [[ASIN:B003ZX8B0U Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates]], and the accessories are wonderful. I was on the hunt for a good, simple case since my wife just tosses the GPS on the floor after use (don't ask; I've tried), and hopefully lengthen the life of the unit. The case is a bit tight at first, but with a bit of time the fit becomes glove-like. The additional accessories, while not entirely necessary, are perfect for frequent travelers, and I've yet to have one of them malfunction. They're basic, but that's the point of AmazonBasic's line. This is my third product from Amazon's own, and I can say I'm a happy consumer.

title: Great value.
text: I got these for my sister for when she goes to college, and here's her take on 'em: I have been using these speakers while watching television episodes on Hulu and, of course, when listening to music. They have a really high maximum value and so far I've heard no buzzing because of playing them loudly. There is a separate wired volume control that, I've found, really comes in handy so you don't have to reach for the speakers every time you need to adjust the volume. The speakers themselves are very small and don't take up a lot of space which is something I really enjoy. The wires to each speakers are definitely long enough so you can place them a good deal far apart for a surround sound effect. All in all, I have enjoyed the speakers and will hopefully continue to when I take them to college.

title: Excellent mini external.
text: This is a review of the product by the person I got it for: Definitely is the actual size as shown on the box. Nice, compact size with a requirement of only one USB port. Installation was easy to follow and complete (follow the folder-finding path on the manual though, and don't just start clicking files when the hard-drive shows up under "My Computer"). For not being a particularly tech-savvy person myself, it was fairly easy to transfer files from my old hard-drive to the new one. Fast access; doesn't slow down my computer like my older one did. Completely satisfied with the product; very user friendly.

title: Logitech Wave, but Simpler
text: What more can I say that hasn't already been about the Wave design? It's comfortable, ergonomic, easy to use, and helps me to get my keystrokes in faster. Sure, it's no IBM Model M or Unicomp Customizer, but it's the best quiet-key keyboard I've used so far. The Unifying feature is neat, as I have the Anywhere Mouse MX (which is great, by the way), and makes hooking up lots of Logitech devices that also utilize this feature a cinch. No need to get this if you already have the Wave, but if you don't, or you're absolutely dead-set on getting this for the extra features (via software) and Unifying setup, then this is a great keyboard to consider. It's easy to use right out of the box; had no issues whatsoever (batteries included, too).

title: Smooth
text: This is the first Logitech keyboard I've gotten, and now I see why Logitech is considered to be a proficient manufacturer in keyboards and other computer-related paraphernalia. Without installing any such programs or software, either from the website or from the included disc, I plugged in the USB receiver right out of the box, followed the easy-to-setup instructions engraved on the back of the keyboard, and away I went. I was able to type flawlessly at the office, and the keys are very smooth and quiet. Even though it's just a keyboard, I kept opening up different programs to test out the typing. Pure joy! (For a nerd like me, at least.) I guess the only gripes I have, and I noticed it almost immediately, is that there are no lights to indicate locks for the numbers, caps, or scroll. It's a minor gripe, but a gripe nonetheless since I have to utilize the Caps Lock every so often at work. When I used the extra buttons for various computer software, I found that the respected programs opened up right away. There was some stall, but that was the result of my slow, crunching computer. The mouse worked just as it should. Now, I have to admit, what I really wanted to get this keyboard for was my Wii at home. I know, it sounds nerdy. But the keyboard I was using before was an old office wired one that was given to me. That one worked fine, but I wanted a wireless one. So, I took home this MK300 keyboard and USB receiver, plugged in the latter into the back of my Wii console, opened up the Internet Channel and found, to my delight, that the keyboard worked flawlessly. There was some range betwixt the keyboard and receiver--about ten feet or so--but it made no matter: my sitting spot isn't too far from the console, so it's not like I'm going to be typing in a completely different room. Since this keyboard works so well, I was hoping to use it on a Mac. I've yet to buy the MacBook Pro--which is why I'm stuck with the Wii's Internet Channel for now--and since the specifications for this certain keyboard doesn't include Apple's OS, I'm assuming that there is simply no way around hardware setups (ever tried?) and will have to resort to something else, when the time comes. All in all, though, if you're looking for an excellent wireless (not Bluetooth) keyboard at a relatively inexpensive price tag for any PC machine or Wii, look no further. The MK300 works like a charm.

title: Fits perfectly!
text: While I haven't actually put this screen protector to the test with a hammer, it does seem pretty strong and protective to me! It comes with a little cleaning kit that has an alcohol wipe, microfiber cloth and basically a sticker to get any pieces of dust left before applying the screen protector. It is very simple to apply this screen protector. After cleaning the screen and removing any dust (there is nothing worse than having a piece of dust forever trapped under a screen protector!) I simply lined up the protector with the top corners, making sure the holes were properly aligned, and then I pretty much just carefully let go and let it apply itself! It has a little piece of cardboard to use to push on the protector after applying and remove any remaining air. I applied this protector within a few minutes including cleaning time and have zero air bubbles underneath. In fact, I cannot even tell it is there and I have peace of mind knowing that if I drop my Galaxy Tab, only the screen protector should be damaged as opposed to the actual screen! *I did receive this product in return for honest and unbiased opinion. All thoughts and words are my own!*

title: Do not buy!

Says I have no problems with my network connection but won't let me do anything that requires internet, so no Netflix or Amazon video, which is the whole reason I bought a new Blu-ray player in the first place.

title: Excellent product
text: For the price this is a great headset. The sound is adequate with plenty of bass. The battery lasts about 4 hours on a full charge and the headset fits my rather big head comfortably. I haven't tried the mic so I can't comment but the buttons are easy to use and the wifi connection is good. I wasn't expecting much given the low price point for a wireless headset however, it exceeded my expectations. I use it when I need to concentrate on verbal content and drown out distractions. It is ideal for this use. If I were listening to music I might comment that the bass is a bit too heavy for my liking. Otherwise, they are ideal for my purpose and I'm glad I didn't spend more for a more sophisticated set because it would have been overkill.

title: Amazing little computer
text: I was considering a Kindle until I read a review from a man who suggested getting a Fire Tablet 8 instead because of the HD quality picture. I do have some vision issues and thought I would take his advice and see if the HD made a difference. It does. The size is perfect for reading from my Kindle Library. The battery life is long, and the buttons are on the top so there are no accidental closures of the screen. I got a refurbed model and it is in pristine condition. I can't believe how inexpensive a powerful little tool like this tablet can be. I don't do anything fancy, but I can stream video with a nice, clear picture. I use a Bluetooth speaker because all of these portable devices sound like a tin can to me. Amazon has made a really easy to use and useful product. I really like it.

title: I love my fire sticks.
text: I have 2 in my RV and have little trouble streaming using the connection provided in any of the parks we've stayed at. Even under poor reception they both work. It's so much better than using cable connections. I'll never get cable again.

title: Quality cable
text: These are so superior to the typical cable provided with my phone. I'm glad they were sold in pairs because now I can keep one in the car. One less thing for me to forget, lol. I think these will hold up well. The braided fabric over the cable prevents kinks. It takes a few minor frustrations out of charging the phone. They are a very good value to, compared with similar cables I've seen elsewhere.

title: Simply the best
text: This is an outstanding product. The battery life is near 10 hours and it charges up quickly. It weighs enough to not get knocked around and it's durable in case it does. The sound is Bose all the way. They make my bargain laptop sound so much better and I use them in my car when using maps. It has made a big difference. I'm so pleased with this speaker.

title: Fire Sticks are just the best!
text: I have one on each of the TVs in my RV and in my home. I stream almost everything now because Fire stick make it so easy. With Prime, there are so many great things to watch and the music options are outstanding. Even YouTube videos play great with this device. All the premium channels can be used with a subscription. There are also at least 3 very good free streaming services that can be added even if you don't subscribe to Prime Video. And it remembers your log ins to multiple sites so you only need to log in once and after that, it's automatic! The voice command feature is a real advantage. It's very high quality and is far more accurate than my typing. The volume control addition is a great improvement, too. And it can function on weak connections over shared WIFI signals. I can't think of anything to complain of... Turning my TVs into streaming devices simplifies so many things. I just love it.

The front cover uses magnets which activates the screen when opens, and turns the screen off when closed. This does not work for the first couple of minutes as you turn on the tablet, but this is because the OS is booting. There is one gripe, and that the tablet doesn't do well with Qi charging pads. This is a minor annoyance as of now, but I am a proponent of Qi charging as I feel more devices should have this feature. Therefore, case manufacturers should make a better effort in making sure that their case will work well with such charging pads. [Update - 2014-06-28] The magnets for the case is falling out. I would have thought they would have screwed or glued the magnets in. Now, every time I open the case's cover, the magnets come along with it. title: The best case I've seen so far...
text: Received my case today for my new iPad Pro 9.7 inch and I love it. It adds very little bulk to the iPad itself and feels very comfortable in my hands. It protects both the screen and the back of the iPad. Much better quality than I had anticipated and very much worth the price especially with free shipping. title: Another great product from Tech Armor
text: I bought this product because of prior experience with Tech Armor screen protectors. I installed this on my iPad 2 with no trouble at all. It took about 10 minutes tops to finally work the air bubbles out from under the screen. These are a little thicker than some other brands, but it doesn't seem to hinder the touch sensitivity at all. I chose matte finish because it cuts down on glare reflecting off the screen. You get 2 covers for a very cheap price and if you follow instructions, you will only need one. I will mention that before I started I turned on the hot water in the shower and let it run for a couple minutes so the steam settles any dust. I think there is one teeny, tiny speck under my screen protector but it's not really even that visible. I can see it when my screen is off (black) if I look for it because I know it's there. Otherwise, while the iPad is in use, I don't notice it at all. I have a tech armor screen on my iPhone 4s as well and my coworkers can't believe that I got it on with no bubbles at all. Now I'm going to take my iPad 2 to work and show this one off too.

title: Nice 32" LCD TV Mount
text: I purchased this for my 32" Panasonic LCD TV which is in my bedroom. I wanted to get the TV a little higher up and off of the dresser surface. I asked my landlord to install it for me and he had no problems whatsoever. He works for Bosch Corp. so he knows a thing or two about quality hardware and he assured me that this thing was heavy duty. He was even impressed with the quality of the bolts that were supplied. He jokingly said that he could have mounted my Chevy Impala on that thing, so I have no doubt that this is a quality product which fit my needs perfectly. I paid less than $20.00 about a month ago on Amazon and bundled it with something else to get free shipping and I am glad I didn't wait any longer. The arm swings out from the wall and the TV also swivels so there are so many ways you can adjust the viewing angle. A 32" TV is probably the limit, but for a bedroom, that is all you need. Don't wait, buy it.

title: Good Monitor at a Great Price
text: I purchased this monitor to replace a 19" Gateway HD monitor and I have no regrets. The Gateway didn't have built-in speakers and costed me more than this Viewsonic. I had a Viewsonic several years ago and it was a nice monitor. Sold it to a co-worker when I got the Gateway and she's still using it today. Just sold her the Gateway monitor too when I got my 23" Viewsonic. The speakers aren't the greatest quality, but I don't use my computer to listen to music or watch DVD's. I don't know what the other reviewer was referring to when she said the print was too small to read. On a 23" monitor, there is no small print, at least I haven't found any. Maybe she needs to adjust her font size not the screen resolution. Picture quality is great and I love the matte finish which helps reduce glare. I would recommend this monitor to anyone looking for a reasonably priced quality product.

title: Excellent Device
text: I was skeptical at first to purchase this item. I read many reviews here on Amazon.com before I decided to give it a try. It had more good reviews than bad so I ordered it hoping that the reviews that spoke of how easy it was to set up as an Access Port were reliable. I am happy to say that I love this product. It was as simple as plugging it in to a wall outlet and an ethernet jack. I had several ethernet connnections in my apartment but wanted to have wireless Internet access for the i-Touch I recently bought and for my laptop computer. I set the switch to AP, plugged in the a/c adapter and connected the supplied ethernet cable and voila, I had wireless Internet. Now the signal is not super strong, but from one room to the next you will have no problems. I don't want the neighbors stealing my signal anyway. I didn't have to install any software or go through a modem or router, I only had to "connect" to d-link on my i-Touch and laptop when they picked up the wireless signal. I would definitely recommend this product to anyone just looking to make a small area wireless. I cannot attest to the other capabilities of this device because I am only using the one feature.

title: Nice for the price
text: I only bought this because of the low price offer I received from 6ave Electronics. This is a 32-inch LCD which I got for less than $400 including shipping. I decided to use this to replace the 20-inch LCD in my bedroom and I have to say, the new standard for bedrooms needs to be 32-inch models. I have no problems with the color and I did little to no extra tweaking. I just set it to cinema mode and it's great for me. And since it's a Panasonic, it has the viera easy link connection which I love. If I want to watch a blu-ray dvd in my Panasonic Blu-Ray player, I just insert the disc and press play, the TV tunes to the proper input for DVD viewing. It also includes an iPod dock, which plugs into the back of the TV and you can use your TV remote to operate the iPod. This is a really nice TV with lots of inputs.

title: Very good product...works as advertised.
text: This little dock adapter does exactly what it's supposed to do...allow you to dock your shuffle on a regular iPod dock. I tried it with my iHome alarm clock radio and my Phillips alarm clock radio. The dock adapter fits nicely. It will, however, come unseated if you just grab your shuffle and lift it out. You need to use your other hand to keep the dock seated. Small inconvenience. I would have given this item 5 stars if it charged the shuffle when it is docked but it doesn't. I use it at work so I just take the charging dock with me and plug it into a free USB port on my computer and charge it when necessary. It also does not work as an alarm, but that's a job for my 80 gig classic iPod. Good little product. October 7, 2008 - This is an update to my previous review. If I could change my rating to 5 Stars, I would. You can disregard the comment about not being able to charge the shuffle while in the dock adapter. I just realized there is a switch that you have to slide over to be able to charge. You can't listen at the same time, but that is a small inconvenience.

title: Great TV for the price!
text: I've had this TV for about 2 weeks now and I absolutely love it. It replaced a 27" tube TV that was not ready for the digital transition. Now I have an HDTV with a built in digital tuner. This TV paired with my DishNetwork VIP612 HD-DVR is an unbeatable combination. Great picture, adequate sound and nice variety of inputs. Ordered it from Amazon, shipped by Beach Camera and I was watching HDTV in a matter of days. I recommend this TV to anyone looking for a reasonably priced HDTV. I also have the 20 inch version in my bedroom and it too does not disappoint.

title: Love this HDTV!
text: I've had the Hitachi P42T501 42" plasma TV for about 3 months now and I have not been disappointed. The picture is crystal clear and when watching HD programming on my DishNetwork Satellite Receiver, everything looks so real. When watching a game on NFL HD it feels like you are sitting right there on the field. I got it for a reasonable price at Vann's online store with free shipping to boot. That saved some big bucks since it was delivered to my home via 18-wheeler. Sound is adequate for my living room and this TV has plenty of A/V inputs for all your electronic components. I currently have a DVD player/recorder, HD-DVD player, X-box, Wii, Gamecube, and Nintendo 64 connected and still have an HDMI and a composite input available. Also, this TV has a really good built in digital tuner so that you are ready for the digital transition in Feb. 2009. I live about 50-60 miles from most of my local TV stations and with my rooftop antenna this TV picks up the analog, digital and HD signals available. Also, this TV may not be a top pick in Consumer Reports, but it did come in on the list at number 29 which I feel is a pretty respectable number considering the number of TVs on the market.

Once docked, I could then charge my iPhone and also play songs/books from the iPhone through the radio speakers. Also, the radio controls would operate my iPhone. Apparently with my new iPhone 4S/case combination, caused it not to dock snuggly and not work with my iPhone docking radios. I purchased the dock extender cable in anticipation that all would work as it did previously. The cable appears to make a good connection and the iPhone make a sound when I plug it into the cable. Unfortunately, the iPhone will no longer play through the radio nor will any of the radio controls work with the iPhone. I guess I will have to look at getting a different type of docking radio. title: Maybe A Little QC Check Is Necessary...
text: Just received another set of these from Amazon. They have been very solid in the past. I have ordered 3 or 4 sets of these previously and they all worked just fine. But this set has a few issues. First off the slot in the screw in the pieces that hold the speaker wire in place is too small to even get a very small flat head screw driver head into. I had to use a box cutter blade (which got a little dicey!) to screw them in because I couldn't get even the very small flat head screw driver into the slot. It was just to small. Made getting the screws tightened in more difficult than it should have been. Also a few of the banana plugs appeared to be bent out of shape, enough so that it was difficult to get the sheath part screwed off. One of the plugs actually broke as I actually needed to use two pairs of pliers to try and get the sheath screwed off. Out of the 3 or so sets of these that I have used this is the first time I had any issues. So a little Quality Control check may be in order at the plant in China where these suckers are made. QC is obviously slipping. I would rate the previous sets I received four stars, but since I am reviewing this most recent set they only deserve 3 stars. They work but were more difficult to install because of the apparent QC issues. Get on the case Sewell and make sure this continues to be a good product.

title: Best Wear OS for true Android users, but not perfect
text: I will avoid the facts that this watch is outdated at launch by its hardware (processor). That, coupled with retail and even discounted price also are out of step with the competition. These two big gripes aside. The watch is good and likely the best choice going into 2023 for pure Android Wear OS users (not looking at Apple or Tizen overlay users.) Its not perfect and Pixel users will benefit the most when paired to this watch. Its lost most of the lag recent watches from other Wear OS brands. Has all the sensors the majority of buyers could want based on watch tech right now. It swipes, it plays well with the apps made for it. It gives you the info you ask of it. There are even a few nice 3rd part accessories now to avoid Google Gouging for proprietary bands. And there are few quirks I hope they iron out soon. Mainly, when the phone is in Bedtime Mode. Make the watch do it too, or add that Zen Mode feature to the watch also. It sucks to have animals tripping the security cameras outside dinging on my wrist and killing my sleep score. The snooze/do not disturb button on watch fails too easily and you have turn it on/off manually everytime. As many claim, the battery sucks. Sort of. I can go up to 36+ hours on a slow day, and many others can too. It will depend on too many factors to list. But basically your popularity with notifications and thinking you need the screen always on are the biggest battery hurdles. Most can get use to touch to wake. And maybe only having text, phone, front door doorbell and one email be allowed to bother your watch with notifications. Do you really need to know what cousin Billy had at Dairy Queen when he posts the same pic/vid on Facebook, Instagram, Tic Toc and YouTube, etc. Find a nice balance of wrist information along with what sensors you need checking if you are still alive. You can start the day and track everything till the next morning when you charge it again while you shower and get the next day started. It charges quickly. And most other Wear OS watches have the same daily charge requirements. Nobody on Wear OS is winning on battery. Or Turn every setting all the way up and have a spare charger puck ready for a mid day juice. If you go that route. I suggest a quick release band to ease the removal of the watch. So, its not up to the level or price of the Ultra Apple Watch. And if you don't care for Samsung. Your love for stock Android will eventually lead you back to this watch. Unless you forgo ECG sensors. The price will drop soon. Cases are minimizing the fragility of an ALL glass jelly bean design. But when comes to keeping your phone pocketed and yet still have info relayed in a useful way. Pixel Watch is the best current albeit not perfect solution for now.

title: Great for Steam Deck and Docks
text: I hate the price for what these are, maybe they were cheaper on a different day. But since the brand I usually buy does not make this specific item. Here I am and price aside. I am VERY happy with the throughput these offer. Don't see any power/data loss when using for my Steam Deck or the aftermarket dock. And since they make your already favorite cables magnetic USB-C. It should be the answer most need to try magnetic connector for their devices. And if your cables were already good for data/charge, these shouldn't change that unless you are using some very high spec stuff. Ever since wearing out PS4 controller charge ports from the necessity of plugging charge cables that often get tugged from excited gaming, pets and just forgetting you are tethered. I now ONLY use higher end magnetic cables and dongles like these for charging my PS5/Switch/Steam Deck/Retroid or any other item that needs frequent charging where the connector could be damaged by movement. For home use and travel these are worth the purchase if you want to extend the life of USB-C charge ports. BTW, can't mention the brand here since this "Sheeast" brand only seems to sell the dongle and no cables (starts with K and sounds like a Hawaiian dance). But for magnetic cables for data/charging that are not total garbage. Only buy the elongated, almost rectangle magnetic cables. Like the shape of these dongles. AVOID the circle cables. And don't be careless and let the magnetic ends drag on the floor. They will collect metal and crud and become useless. Be good to your stuff!

text: I only bought this to charge my PS5 controllers. I always wish I had bought them for the PS4 which would get a loose charge port over time. Trying to prevent that this time. A dozen charges in and it works great, and if my dog runs through my cable. It just falls and no damage. Time will tell how well it holds up. Happy so far.

title: Logitech Marble its not, but good for now.
text: If you want the trackball for gaming or general PC getting around. The choices I see, are getting worse. I first got hooked on the wired Logitech Marble. Loved and still own a few. Now, I needed a wireless option and tried one from Logitech and a few other brands. Just have trouble getting used to the side marble and it wasn't great for gaming and the others were cheap and felt low quality. Brings us to the Kensington Orbit. For me, it is as close to the Marble as I have found so far in a wireless version. Good range and plenty response options. Ball is in the center where I prefer to have it. 2 buttons the way a mouse was meant to be (although a couple tiny programable buttons would be nice at this price). Yet not all is perfect, but I am coping with it. The tricky bit for me that hinders a higher rating. First, the right click button is too big. There is no where for my pinky finger to rest without clicking. Please revise the design just a bit for the base to ride a bit higher or the button to get a bit smaller. Or add a flip up piece to partially cover the button to prevent pushing it (likely to 3D print something for my use). Who needs the right click button to be so prominent. Secondly, It might be me, but the sliders/scroll on either side of the ball are not great. They hesitate and don't react to my touch too well, but it might be me with rough fingers. I will keep the mouse because it works well for what I need right now. But, Hey Kensington, consider a revised model that has room for the finger to rest somewhere on the right that does no result in a button press. Can't be the only one. Or maybe that is a different model you already sell? My choices were limited when I ordered.

title: It works as described, but...
text: The bags are good for almost any remote you might have for a tv or sound system built in the last 20+ years. While I was pretty sure the bags would be that crunchy plastic you see on Easter baskets or grocery store flowers. I hoped it would be a bit closer to something softer or maybe silicone like. The heat shrink works great and fits all my remotes well. The downside is you end up with corners of hard plastic with sharp/pointy edges after the shrink (tried multiple methods or sealing and still rough corners). And getting the air out is near impossible. You end up with a balloon around your remote and some of the buttons can't be pressed (a plus if you are just storing things). Or you put a pin hole in the plastic and the seal is tight, but maybe too tight after you get the full heat shrink smooth. One remote of mine has a frequently used button 2 in from the side and it is hard to use now. You get a lot of bags and it might be trial and error to find the balance if you plan to use the item you shrink wrapped. Its a good product and serves the purpose I wanted it for. Just wish they could come up with a softer less crunchy plastic. Hair dryer is all you need to shrink the plastic. I also sealed the ends with a vacuum sealer. These bags can't be vacuum sealed though, too smooth.

text: This is the dumb type of stuff you use to just pop over to Radio Shack and the guy there knew exactly what it was and where it was and you would be on your way in a few minutes. title: So far, cables work as described.
text: As is usually the case with this type of product on Amazon. Was not familiar with the brand/name of the cables. And no reviews when I purchased. Yet, unlike many of the similar that were recommended by influencers. These are identical looking, bit longer length (I measured: 6 foot 7 inch) and cheaper as a 2 pack. They seem to work as intended for charging and the display looks good if not better than some pictures other brands had up. Should also mention they are encased in a nice Paracord/shoelace solid black material. Still lots of uses to try and of course longevity with cables is of concern. But, for the price it's worth a try and I will update if they fail before the end of the year. I have yet to have a cable truly fail. I'm also not hard on my stuff. Always pull from the barrel closest to the plugged in device and not the cable. BTW: I took a picture of an older phone charging since it was easier than a pic of the OnePlus I am currently using to write this with.

title: Light & simple, ***UPDATED***
text: Overall I think these are decent walkies. If you want basic push button to talk and small lightweight with adequate range. This is a decent choice. Choosing this model for the Secret Service earpiece can be hit and miss. Guess some earpieces can be just as bad as the black over the ear units the other companies use. In all but a library, the earpiece audio is too low to hear in outdoor conditions. ***see update*** The RT22 cost the same as other models with displays and buttons (thicker and heavier walkies) to control functions this model has to do with button combos, but it does talk to you as you change settings and channels. Sadly as with many other models I tried. VOX is near useless. VOX works as bad as any sub $100 walkie I've tried. It lags and maybe sends half the message at best. You won't know how good/bad VOX is for you till you try it yourself. Get these for size, lightweight, basic, rechargeable walkie needs. Try to catch it on sale...if possible. I paid a fair amount. Btw, my wife and I use these for trail rides on our e-bikes. The true two-way communication devices did not fit our non-helmet style and will cost substantially more. ***UPDATED*** Company did reach out to offer a refund because they thought I was unhappy. And only the earpiece was a bit of let down for me. They told me about another similar earpiece that seems to be working a bit better and now I can actually hear outdoors with the earpiece. It is still a Secret Service style, but somehow it is a bit louder. Maybe my original earpieces were faulty. Let me be clear. I still paid the retail price, kept the walkies and did not take any money/refund for my review. The walkie has so far been a great trail ride walkie. I might have received a bad earpiece. The company seems to care about their ratings and customers use of their products. And we all need to keep what we buy if it works to avoid landfill waste. I just came back to add a star and let others know. Good walkie. And maybe consider one of Retevis's many other earpieces or handset mics. Some of their other walkies include better headsets.

title: Extra gimmick/tool to keep thieves away
text: We mounted one on each of our Lectric Xp bikes. With a few real thick zip ties (the ones included are useless) they fit perfectly and solidly in the bike rack. And once you load your cargo or in my case mount a thin board on top of the rack. There will be no access for anyone to reach or destroy the alarm if it goes off. It is the perfect fit and hiding spot for those with a similar bike or rack set up. Although, I know some hide it in the seat above the post. It has enough air gap to hear the horn/alarm and can't be messed with or even found/seen. Now as for how well the alarm works. It arms and works great as a bell with the 3 tone options. No idea if it will deter thieves. But I know I would not be able to waste much time trying to cut any locks with this alarm blaring for the 30 seconds it takes to reset. You can see in my photos that it fits perfectly flush on the rear rack. So it is easy to place cargo on the rack and not touch the alarm. I installed it facing down to the fender. There is only a 2 inch gap between the fender and rack so the alarm does not touch the fender and not enough room to reach alarm this way either. Once I mount the wood panel to the rack. It will be totally covered and unreachable to the average person. Sure it will add a extra step should I need to change the batteries. But minor detail. And should this post reveal a way to defeat the location. Still likely to get enough eyes on the thief to show anyone around that a bike is being stolen. Bike is only used in daytime and mostly for trail riding. For the price. This is a worth it expense to try for a well rounded security in conjunction with one or two bike lock methods. We have three!

title: UPDATE since company reached out to help
text: Originally bought this remote keyboard last year and had to return when the usb reciever broke in the usb port when I tried to pull it out. It happened in the first few days and was easy to return. Yet, when they company saw my review. They felt this was an isolated incident and they convinced me to try another keyboard. Now that it is here and I have been using it for a bit(typing the review with it). It is still the same device I originally recieved. While it is still lighter than I expected, it does do everthing I originally wanted it for. Backlight that stays on while in use and doesnt timeout too quick. Has the range of my living room to work at a 15+ foot distance. And it is rechargeable. And since this one has a usb reciever that didn't break off in my pricey laptop. I had to come back and update my review and join many of the others who also got a good remote. Also want to add that the people at this company seem to care or at least pay attention to the reviews and don't want unhappy customers. They have a good product and a very low price point. Maybe I jumped too quick to return and leave my original 1 star rating without contacting the seller. I increased the rating to 4 star. It's a good product for a low price and is worth consideration. title: ordered this item twice and both were defective out of the box
text: I ordered this remote to use with a Kenwood head unit I already had on my boat. Upon delivery, the unit had 7 small cracks along the side edge of faceplate. The cracks coincided with the 4 screws that secure the front faceplate to the rear housing (there is a seal between the front face and rear housing). It appears that excessive clamping forces of these screws caused the cracks. Being in a marine environment, the cracks are completely unacceptable as moisture and condensation can easily work its way into the unit. I returned the remote for refund and ordered a second one in its place. When the second remote arrived, careful inspection showed that it too, had cracks along the edge of the front faceplate. The second remote had 2 cracks. Emails to Kenwood didn't help at all (i even included pictures) and they said they've never heard of such an issue before. Based on the design aspect alone, I HIGHLY doubt this is an isolated event to both of the remotes I've seen. I'm sure many MANY more of them are damaged during production. If you have this remote, make a close inspection of it but BEWARE as Kenwood customer service has warned me that they will refuse warranty work on any item that appears to have physical damage. With this unit, it comes damaged OUT OF THE BOX. Copy and paste the link to see 3 of the 7 cracks in the 1st remote. [...]

title: This Radio is Exceptional!
text: A few years ago, our cable provider stopped airing MLB games. To say my husband wasn't happy is an understatement. Because we still under contract with the company, we weren't able to switch cable providers. He was able to watch some games at friend's homes or at a local sports bar. But MLB plays games almost on a daily basis and the start times can be late if played on the west coast. He wasn't able to go to friend's homes or the bar all the time to watch the Phillies play. He decided to buy a new radio so he could at least listen to the games. He went out and spent a good amount of money on a VERY nice radio with tons of features. He was ready to listen to his first game on the new radio, sat outside in a comfortable chair and turned on his new radio. And heard static. Nothing but static. We live less than an hour from Philadelphia yet his radio couldn't even get a Philly station so he could hear the game. His radio got exactly ONE station. Our local station that plays music, no sports. Turns out, where we live, surrounded by mountains and heavy forest areas isn't a great place to get radio reception. Fast forward to now. When I saw the offer for Dingmi's excellent reception transistor radio in my VINE queue, I decided to try it. My plan was to return it if it didn't get radio stations. When it arrived, we plugged it in and turned it on and began to check out the radio stations, anxious to see if any other than our local station would come in. And boy, did they ever! The first station we came to was located in Ocean City, MD, nearly 200 miles away. It came in as clear as can be. We picked up stations in New York, Ohio, West Virginia and New Jersey as well...ALL crystal clear without static! In addition to the excellent reception, this radio is a nice size yet incredibly lightweight! All of the dials are clearly labeled and simple to use. They all turn with ease. They're also very secure and will not break or fall off any time soon. The AM/FM stations are easy to read as well. The radio also has a nice size antenna that is easy to raise/lower. The radio can operate via 4 D batteries (not included) or via the power cord (included). The AC power works great. I did put 4D batteries in but don't use them to power the radio. I have them in there in case of a power outage. ( And we experienced one a few days after the Dingmi arrived, thanks to a snowstorm. We were able to listen to the weather and storm warnings until the lights came on again. Prior to having this radio, we wouldn't have had one to use. ) The volume allows you to play the radio as loud or as quiet as you chose. There is an earphone jack on the side of the radio (earphones not included) for private listening as well. This is an exceptional radio. I am SO glad and so relieved we have it. We get fantastic reception and tons of stations from all over, even with mountains, huge pine trees and heavily wooded areas all around our home. Its lightweight and so easy to operate. This radio is perfect for outdoor use, home use, campers, RVs, take on vacation...perfect for just about any local. It definitely is worthy of gift-giving as well! I absolutely recommend the Dingmi portable transistor radio. I don't just recommend it...I HIGHLY recommend it! (BTW...I'm happy to say, MLB games are airing once again in our home! We're with a new cable company! lol)

title: A Few Wipes and the Dirt is GONE! Amazing!
text: Well, it finally happened. Thanks to 'having some birthdays '(my optometrist's polite way of saying I'm getting older), two months ago I officially joined millions all over the world and became a wearer of eye glasses! First time ever for me. I was shocked how quickly the lenses get dirty! The first time I went to clean them I was about to use a wet paper towel on them when my husband walked into the room, saw what I was doing and screamed, "NO!!!" before grabbing the towel out of my hand. lol. (My poor heart...scared the daylights out of me!) I then had to listen to a lecture about what to use to clean my glasses, along with a demonstration showing me how to clean them! lolol. He gets a box of eye glass wipes at the store for $5. and they do work well. But they left kind of a sticky residue on my fingers that I didn't care for. I did a quick check online and learned microfiber cloths do a fantastic job of cleaning glasses and do so without the use of glass cleaner (liquid) or water. I immediately ordered Fiber Promot microfiber cloths and was (still am) amazed and impressed how well they clean my glasses! And how easy are they to use? Simply wipe the lenses a few times and PRESTO! Clean glasses! That's it. That's all it takes to wipe the dirt away! But I didn't stop with my glasses....I then wiped down the TVs, my laptop, my Kindle and my cell phone all with the same fabulous results as my glasses! These cloths do an amazing job and best of all, they do not scratch items they are used on! I got the 6x7 cloth size (6 cloths included) and they're the perfect size to clean everything I listed above. I put one in my purse as well. They work great, do not cause damage and leave no sticky residue as the other wipes I previously used did. And they're cheap! Incredibly cheap! You'd think something that works as well as these cloths work and require next to no work to use them would cost far more than these cost! These are incredible and do a fantastic job. There is even a 1 year money back guarantee on them, though I doubt the company gets many returns because these are fabulous! If you wear glasses, you're going to want these cloths. And don't forget, they clean other items as well!

title: Not a Perfect System, But Works Well For the Low Cost of the Stereo!
text: I ordered this weeks ago and have been hanging on to it. I have NO clue how to begin to install a car stereo and I was not about to attempt it. My car went in for inspection (passed! YAY!) and the owner of the garage installed it for me as well. You will not say "OMG, this is the best stereo system EVER!" when you install this in your own car. You will not brag to your family and friends about how fabulous the sound is from this stereo. You will not waste time trying to decide what CDs you want to take along on your road trip because there is no CD player... But you WILL be impressed with all of the features that come with the Keshangda car stereo system and how well it works for under $50.00! Its not the best stereo system out there...if that's what you're looking for, this is NOT the stereo for you. But if you want something that works well and has some nice features, all for a low price, then this IS the car stereo system for you. I'm told it was easy to install. Again, I have NO experience whatsoever with installing a car stereo so I cannot speak firsthand, only pass along what I've been told. The camera works better than i expected which was a nice surprise. I'm a bit disappointed with the touch screen...I feel as though I have to press it harder than i should to make it work and sometimes I have to press multiple times to get it to work. Its not that doing so is a huge issue, I'm just a bit worried that it could possibly mean there is a problem with the system or that perhaps it won't last as long as it should. (The mechanic who installed it didn't think this was anything serious, however) The sound is sufficient. Bluetooth sometimes doesn't connect which can be frustrating, but most of the time it does work. You're getting a decent amount of benefits from this stereo for a very small price. Its far from perfect, it has flaws but for me, it gets the job done. I don't spend a lot of time in my car so this stereo system is perfect for me.
