text: Like everyone else on the planet, I have a drawer full of miscellaneous chargers and cords that you have to poke like snakes to get to stay in the drawer so you can close it.. not to mention that fact that when you need a specific cord, you have to visually inspect the end of every one to find the one you need, only to pull out the whole lot as they have somehow entwined themselves completely into a ball of indiscernible mayhem. I got this cable organizer from Teskyer and my cord drawer can now be described as "organized chaos". This case is double sided. The zippers work smoothly for the most part. There are multiple slots and sections of varying sizes inside. I went with the Navy Blue color and it is a little darker than depicted, but I really like it. What I like the most about this case is that no where.. on the outside, on the inside, on the zippers.. NO WHERE is there a company name or logo! So nice and refreshing to not have a logo all in-your-face the second you open the drawer!! What was I able to fit inside? When empty.. this case comes in at about 7" wide, 10" long and 2" thick. After I filled it, it now measures about 7.25" wide, 9.5" long and 3.5" thick. Yes.. the material is a tad stretchy. • 23 x USB charging cords of varying lengths (from 6" to 6' long) • 10 x USB charging bricks (Samsung and Motorola brands.. AKA "the fat boys") • and a couple of SanDisk microSD cards and adapters All in all, a great solution, and at a very reasonable price, for organizing your cord chaos.

title: Nice to have for emergencies
text: I got this Lukasa Emergency Hand Crank Portable AM/FM/NOAA Weather Radio to have on hand for emergencies. I live in a very rural area so it is possible for us to be very out of the loop if anything major happens. Having this radio will help us stay informed, if even a little. The radio itself is easy to use, is compact enough to fit anywhere I want to store it and I appreciate the bright yellow color, making it easy to spot whether in a dark cabinet or from a distance outside. The front flashlight and the flip top light bar are bright and the tuning and volume knobs work as well as you could expect on any manual tuning radio. We will be testing it this summer while camping to get an idea of battery life and to play with the solar panel charging. So far though, we are impressed.

title: Works
text: Coming up a little short of the advertised 3ft in length, I was still able to use it. This HDMI cable is a steal for the price and works as expected for my needs. I used it to connect a tv to an older Dell PC tower as a backup home desktop system and the picture and sound are as good as my system will allow. While nowhere near the best available, this HDMI cable will serve you well if you're in a pinch and need a cheap reliable option.

title: PERFECTION!!
text: This is the case I was looking for! I recently upgraded my tired 2013 Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" to the new Fire HD 8+ and I needed a new case. I wanted a case where the front flap would stay connected to the back when folded open.. a case that can stand up in portrait mode for easy reading.. a case that would also stand up in landscape mode for easy movie viewing.. and if it was a decent color and felt good to the touch then those would be a bonus. This case checks all of those marks!! I absolutely love it!

title: Great for non-gaming laptops
text: This AICHESON Full RGB Lights Laptop Cooling Cooler Pad works pretty good. It's easy to setup and get going. I like the colors and that the fans are not too loud, even on full speed. The cord is long enough and there are plenty of height adjustment levels so you can find the perfect angle that works for you and your desk setup. It's not the best, but it will certainly do for any non-gaming laptop.. I'd recommend a model with more fans and a higher output for those.

title: Thick, sturdy fast charging cables
text: Like most households today, we have so many cables. It seems like every device needs a different type of cable, be it HDMI, USB-A, USB-C, USB-mini... it's nuts! I personally can't wait for all of our devices to be switched over to the current industry standard USB-C so I can at least reduce *some* of the clutter! But until that day comes (if ever), I am trying to at least organize our cable collection to where we can grab what we need without having to sift through a sea of black cables, examining all of the ends looking for the right one. Enter these Avyxm USB C to C 4 foot cables. I chose the red and LOVE THEM!! They are very vibrant and bright making it stupid easy to quickly grab the correct cable for our USB-C devices!! The cables are nice and thick but still with a bit of bend allowing for maneuvering around furniture legs or nightstand lamps without putting a kink in them. And one of the biggest props? These cables FAST CHARGE everything I've connected them to. Our Samsung Galaxy S8 and S10 phones, my new Fire HD8 Plus tablet and my kids' Samsung S10 plus phones. The 4 foot length is perfect for bedside nightstands although it is a little too short to reach the couch and still use the phone or tablet in a comfortable position -- so I'll be grabbing a couple of the 6 foot cables for living room use. Bottom line... the color is fantastic, the build quality is supreme, I don't expect they'll ever kink given their thickness, I love the braiding and feel of the fabric -- overall a high quality product that I have and will continue to, highly recommend!

title: Flawless Installation
text: I just installed this product on my Ellipsis 8 HD and, I must say, the installation was more smooth than most other similar installations I have done on previous phones and tablets. This was not my first rodeo as I have installed my own screen protectors (both plastic and glass) on numerous devices in the past, so I had an idea of how to approach this one. That being said, I appreciated the company's installation video. Unlike other's I have seen, it is presented with clear audio and served as an easy to follow step-by-step guide. My screen protector went on quite easily. I have an extreme case of OCD so this process took me nearly an hour (though I can see how it could take much less time for others who are not as meticulous). My result pleases me to no end! I have a crystal clear display.. no lint, no bubbles, no hazing and no rainbow effect.. and I just installed it. I am not reporting results after the mentioned 48 hour waiting period for allowing any bubbles or such to dissipate.. my results were immediate and flawless. I am extremely pleased with this product and am glad I gave both the product and the company a second chance. I ordered this product twice.. the first order was broken/cracked upon delivery. I returned it to Amazon for a refund and ordered a second one. This one arrived in one piece, installed beautifully and should protect my tablet for quite some time. However, should it ever break or crack, the company does boast a lifetime replacement warranty so I should be covered for any mishaps in the future.

title: Acceptable
text: I work for the United States Postal Service and recently purchased the OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth speaker for use in my LLV truck on my rural mail route. The speaker performs beautifully and I wanted to protect it to, from and while at work so I purchased this case. I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker, but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route. I received the case and used it at work yesterday. The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket and the carabiner clip. I have no need for them now, but I'm sure they will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along and want to clip the case to my day pack. As for playback while in the case? Yeah, it was terribly muffled. It didn't work for me as it apparently has for others. Yet, the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work. I like how smooth the zipper is and how heavy duty/reinforced the stitching for the zipper is. The interior is not as thickly padded as I would have expected, however it does protect the speaker. I deducted one star due to the mediocre interior padding. I hope that, if the company ever revamps this case design, they beef up the padding a bit.

title: USPS LLV Comparison: OontZ Angle 3 Plus vs Anker SoundCore
text: First off, I am not an audiophile. This is a review from a simple person who wanted music at work. I am a Rural Carrier for the United Stated Postal Service. I deliver mail in an LLV truck and these vehicles are basically mobile tin cans. Every panel rattles, making for quite an unpleasant environment, audio wise. I tried playing music directly off my phone, but alas my speakerphone is only so loud and is constantly drowned out by the LLV. So, I researched Bluetooth speakers and, based on the reviews and popularity, recently purchased two: -[[ASIN:B016XTADG2 Anker SoundCore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Foot Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Black]] -[[ASIN:B01LZV6TYQ OontZ Angle 3 PLUS Splashproof Bluetooth Speaker - Designed & Engineered by Cambridge SoundWorks for Richer Bass, HD Sound, and 30-Hour Playtime, 10W+ Power, Water Resistant, Portable Wireless Speaker]] The Anker SoundCore is being returned while I am keeping the OontZ Angle 3 Plus and here is why. I tested both speakers in my home at first. My very first impression, out of the box: OontZ Angle 3 Plus - was nice to touch and just felt solid and very well built. Anker SoundCore - just felt like a simple lightweight brick. It really didn't give the impression of longevity or durability. The set-up guides were quite different from each other. OontZ Angle 3 Plus - Extremely easy to read, follow and understand (remember, I am not a music nut lol. This was my first time ever using a Bluetooth speaker and was in completely uncharted territory.) It was all in English, and only English and the diagrams were detailed and made the entire set-up process seamless and carefree. Anker SoundCore - This guide was very hard to follow. It is printed in darn near every language, in tiny print and the diagrams were quite small as well. I ultimately did get the speaker paired with my phone and figured out what buttons did what, but it took nearly 15 minutes to do so. Bluetooth Pairing With both speakers and my phone lined up on a table (well within the proximity specified in each set-up guide), both speakers paired, however: OontZ Angle 3 Plus - MUCH faster in pairing (mere seconds!). Anker SoundCore - took nearly two minutes to complete the pairing process. Pause/Play Button Since I dismount to deliver packages to a customer's door routinely on my route, I really need to have a simply way to pause my music. I really like how both speakers offer this function on directly on the units, saving me from having to handle my phone. OontZ Angle 3 Plus - I barely press the Play/Pause button and the speaker immediately reacts. There is NO hesitation. Anker SoundCore - I press the Play/Pause button and there is a delay of about 5 seconds.. just long enough to make me think I didn't press hard enough and reach to do it again only for the speaker to finally react. Volume/Overall Playback Quality OontZ Angle 3 Plus - Wow. Just wow. It is truly unbelievable to hear such full sound, and bass(!), coming from such a small unit. I found myself perfectly pleased with the output without ever reaching max volume on the speaker itself. So I am looking forward to how well it will work in my LLV during my first road test. As for now, I am thoroughly impressed! Anker SoundCore - I maxed out the volume on my phone and the speaker and was just not impressed. If I could guess, I'd say the max output this speaker achieved was only about 25% more than my speakerphone alone (while the OontZ Angle 3 Plus blew it out of the water with close to double, if not more, output than my speakerphone alone). I also noted some kind of distortion or interference type background sound with the Anker SoundCore at mid volume and above. Speakerphone/Mic I was able to answer an incoming phone call on both units as described in each set-up guide. The quality of in-call sound on each speaker differed: OontZ Angle 3 Plus - My husband's (the caller) voice was crisp and clear, as if he was sitting talking right next to me. There was no distortion or feedback out of the speaker. Husband reported nothing but a clear voice on his phone. Anker SoundCore - Husband's voice was clear, but echoed horribly. No matter what volume level I used. There was no distortion (I was expecting this given the distortion with the music playback) bu the continuous echoing is a major issue for me. Husband reported a slight "faded" type of echo on his phone. Road Test (in my LLV) OontZ Angle 3 Plus - The sound is amazing in the truck! Thinking I would need it, I maxed the volume on both the speaker and my phone then pressed play on my music. Well, I certainly don't need max volume. I reduced the volume on both the speaker and my phone and found a very happy medium output. This speaker performs perfectly in the loud, rattling setting of a USPS LLV.. even while bouncing down rural dirt two tracks and washboard gravel roads. I am extremely pleased with this tiny speaker. Anker Soundcore - Even with maxed volume settings, I could not get this speaker to perform anywhere near as well as the OontZ Angle 3 Plus. It had volume and was loud enough to hear over the vehicle's own noise, however the distortion/interference mentioned earlier was still present and in the truck during the road test it had what I would describe as an echoing effect on the music, specifically the singers' voices. It just wasn't clear. (I hope that makes sense.) Battery Life/Listen While Charging OontZ Angle 3 Plus - So far, the battery life is impressive. After receiving it, I charged it overnight (as recommended). I then had it connected to my phone for about an hour of home testing. Turned it off and I next used it at work on a Saturday.. had it powered on and connected to my phone and actively playing music for about 5.5 hours. I then used it again on Monday (much longer and busier days in the USPS, FYI).. had it on, connected and active continuously for nearly 9 hours. I have yet to see the low battery light come on. I plan to see just how many days of work I can get out of a single charge. Anker Soundcore - I have no information for this section on this speaker since I am returning it. Exterior/Cleaning At first, I had the OontZ Angle 3 Plus setting on the dashboard of the LLV. This didn't last more than two stops. Despite having the four rubber "feet", the speaker still slid around causing more of a distraction than I would like. I ended up setting it on top of my personal bag, in a bin by my feet with the speaker facing up. This move really helped my piece of mind, knowing it will not go anywhere. This speaker has a soft rubber exterior. It is quite nice and feels luxurious, however... this exterior attracts all dust particles within 50 feet! USPS LLVs are *not* known for being the cleanest and even though I moved the speaker from the dust-ridden dashboard to a bin, it was still slathered with dust and dirt by the end of my route. I figured it was a fair trade, sacrificing the appearance for the gain of having decent music. But.. I got home and went to clean it. I will tell you, my expectations of this working were very low. I didn't think the dust would come off that supple rubber. But with a wet paper towel and a few slow wipes, it did. So, it can be cleaned up! Case I did purchase the case for this speaker ([[ASIN:B01NBDY6VP [Official] OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth Portable Speaker Carry Case, Neoprene with Aluminum Carabiner, reinforced zipper, by Cambridge SoundWorks [NOT FOR OontZ Angle 3]]]). I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker, but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route. I received the case and used it yesterday. The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket. I have no need for it now, but I'm sure it will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along. As for playback while in the case? Yeah, it was terribly muffled. It didn't work for me as it apparently has for others. Yet, the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work. It is not as thickly padded as I would have expected, however it does protect the speaker. Overall, for my specific purpose and intended use for a Bluetooth speaker, the Anker SoundCore simply won't cut it. However, it is still a nice speaker and will perhaps fit your needs perfectly. After all, most people don't drive LLVs and have the same high demands that go along with that. For me, the OontZ Angle 3 Plus is what I'll be bopping down the road to, mailbox to mailbox. Happy hunting! Hope this review helps you out!

title: This cable fit the bill nicely. It fits in my Kindle USB port perfectly
text: I needed a longer cord to plug my Kindle in at night in my bedroom. This cable fit the bill nicely. It fits in my Kindle USB port perfectly, no shifting side to side and my Kindle recognizes it on the spot. The extra long 6ft length serves my purposes and allows me to charge my Kindle while simultaneously reading while in bed.

title: Sticks very well to brick
text: Purchased these clips to use on my mantle. I lay a pre-lit garland on top of my mantle every year for Christmastime and the cord always hangs freely off the end down to the outlet near the floor. I always have to compensate for the weight of the dangling plug by placing other decorations on top of the garland here and there to keep it from sliding off the mantle. I ordered these clips and placed one on the brick under the ledge of the mantle, then pressed the garland's cord into the clip. Due to the angle, the cord was threatening to pop out of the clip, but never did for the near month it was on display. I had concerns that the clip's adhesive would not stick properly or for long when placed against my brick fireplace, but it held quite well and is actually still there. I tried to remove it but the adhesive began to separate from the clip when I pulled slightly so I have decided to leave it in place. As the clip is black and is tucked up under the mantle ledge, it blends in well and will be fine left there year round until I need it again next December. That is the reason for the one star reduction.. the clips appear to be a one time use. To be fair, I've only used one and on brick at that.. but if it sticks this well to a rough brick surface, I have to only assume that it will stick just as well, if not better, to smoother surfaces.. thus making them nearly impossible to move and reuse in multiple locations.

title: Perfect Replacement For M505
text: My M505 finally quit working dependably for me after nearly 3 years of dedicated service. I loved the design and how I never had to change the batteries, not even once in those 3 years. So I sought out another one only to find they are no longer made. But I did discover this M525 and after a little research I purchased. I am extremely happy with this newer version of my older mouse. It is nearly identical to my M505, so close in fact that I have yet to notice any major differences except for the color. I recommend this M525 to anyone who likes the freedom of a wireless mouse and doesn't want to bother with changing batteries!

title: No bubbles BUT lost sensitivity
text: I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament. This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive. Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far. Pros: It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation. Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening. The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free. Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time. The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up. I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it. Con: Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus. After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.

title: Protects but hinders the camera app
text: This case fits my new Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" very snug which satisfies my concern of whether it is protected or not. There is no chance that my Kindle will slip out of this case. The sleep/wake feature is very nice and handy in keeping the battery from draining if you forget to turn the screen off before closing the lid (which causes the Kindle to finally time out based on the time you have specified in the settings). The only complaint that I have with this case is the Kindle camera app thinks the Kindle needs to be slid upwards in order to take pictures with the rear facing camera. The 'slide up' instructions are displayed in the center of the screen when you open the camera app making it difficult to take a picture. You can still snap a picture, but you cannot see whatever is in the center of your screen. This makes for an extremely annoying experience. I should not have to remove my Kindle from its case in order to take a picture. That is ridiculous. Pure and simple. I have purchased a more professional case which also has the same issue when it comes to the camera app so I am not sure who is to blame for this problem, but it does need to be remedied soon.

title: Great case! (But read below about problems with features!)
text: ***The first part of this review is for the Red option*** I needed more than just a simple case for my Kindle as it pulls double duty serving as my tablet and my planner. I also needed something that would provide it with supreme protection as it accompanies me to and from work every day. I purchased this case/portfolio in the red color in hopes that it would make it stand out at work. Many of my co-workers have Kindles as well and I didn't want mine to accidentally get picked up. The red is nice, but way too much for me. I have been considering exchanging it for the black and the following issues are what sent me over the edge and led to my returning the red case. This case/portfolio worked nicely for my needs. However, I removed two stars for two reasons. #1 The case stunk to high heaven. It was so bad that I thought a stink bug had gotten into my house. Though the "scent" did lessen over a few weeks, it was still very present after five weeks. #2 The description claims that this case has the ability to put the Kindle to sleep when you close it up. Not true. After my battery died over night, I realized that the sleep/wake feature was not working in my case. I had to physically turn my Kindle off before closing the case (may not seem like much of a hassle, but it quickly becomes a time consuming annoyance). There was one benefit to this case though. It is the first case I have had for my Kindle that does not have any issues with using the Camera App while still encased in the removable inner sleeve. This was a very nice feature, however not nice enough to get me to keep it. **This is the review of the Black option** So, I just returned the red case and opted to give the black version a shot. It arrived this evening and wow, what a difference! It doesn't stink at all and the sleep/wake feature is functioning properly! I do, however, now have the ghastly on-screen message of needing to slide my Kindle up in its case to take a picture. But this does not bother me very much as I have not used my Kindle for taking pictures more than a handful of times in the month that I have owned it. All in all, it is a nice, professional case/portfolio that offers the features for my Kindle that I was needing. It also has a fair amount of pockets inside, though do not expect to be able to store much bulk as you will run into two problems.. #1 If you add too many things to the pockets, you run the risk of the pockets bulging and possibly damaging your Kindle's screen. #2 Also, if you add too much to the pockets, you will possibly not be able to close the case. And if you manage to close it, you may run the risk of stretching the zipper and ultimately damaging the case. Personally, I keep a small stack (about 10) of my business cards, five gift certificates and a little cash in the pockets and the zippers still flow smoothly with no issues and nothing from the pocket side comes in contact with my screen. Overall, I would recommend this case, as long as you are willing to take a risk on getting one that has the features you are wanting/needing as it seems to be a completely random toss-up as to which case has which features. On a side note, the included stylus/pen is a great idea, but it isn't executed very well here. The plastic tip leaves a lot to be desired - it takes more force than I care to apply to my screen for the Kindle to register the stylus' contact on the screen. I did some research and purchased [[ASIN:B00E0GV9IC The Friendly Swede Bundle of 6 Micro-Knit Hybrid Fiber Tip Universal Capacitive Stylus Pens 4.5" for Smart Phone Touch Pad + 6 x 15'' Elastic Tether Lanyards + Cleaning Cloth in Retail Packaging]]. These stylus' are VERY nice in appearance and easy to use without requiring much force on the screen at all.

title: Too small
text: This is a sturdy and well made little case. But that was my main problem.. it was too small. I purchased this case to use with my new [[ASIN:B005MTMFHU Canon SX40 HS 12.1MP Digital Camera with 35x Wide Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7-Inch Vari-Angle Wide LCD]]. This case was absolutely too small to carry the camera, extra batteries and the battery charger. I returned the Ape Case to Amazon and purchased the [[ASIN:B0000CCVC9 Canon 100DG Bag for Canon SLR Cameras]] from Best Buy, mainly because my trip was closely approaching and I did not have time to have the new Canon case delivered prior to my departure. The Canan 100DG is much roomier and allows for a ton of space for everything I could possibly need to take along with my Canon SX40. If you have a smaller camera or are not going to need to haul all of your extra gear with you (say, going out for a day long hike, etc.), then this Ape Case may fit the bill for you. If not, then I highly recommend purchasing a larger case for your camera and all the related goodies.

title: The Superb Stubby!
text: **UPDATE February 15, 2021** Just here to update my review and report that this little Stubby is still performing as I described in my original review below. I've had this installed on my Ram 1500 for eight years now and have had countless trips through hundreds of different car wash locations, both regular and touchless, and my Stubby is still intact and in perfect, like new condition! It's been one of the best and long lasting purchases I've made for my truck! I would upload a current picture but it looks the same as my original picture.. no fading or discoloration at all. I am extremely pleased! **ORIGINAL REVIEW: February 19, 2013** Vehicle installed on: 2012 Ram 1500 Laramie CC I purchased a brand new 2012 Ram Laramie 1500 Crew Cab last October and the extremely tall factory antenna drove me bonkers. I had to take it off every time I went through a car wash (which may not sound like much, but it gets to you after the first few times, trust me!) and it whipped around in the wind, even at slow, city street speeds and sometimes when the truck was just parked! My first antenna replacement was a 14" rubber Euro style aftermarket antenna off of eBay. It ended up just annoying the hell out of me.. at 14" and plastic, it bent real bad at higher hwy speeds (65mph+) and then took more than a day to straighten back out.. so yeah it got replaced with The Stubby from Craven Speed. I cannot express how pleased I am with this little baby! Easy 'install' (just screw on - it actually took more time to remove my Euro antenna than it did to simply screw the Stubby on) and looks superb! It's so short (3") I can't even see it from the driver's seat.. huge difference from the stock antenna for sure. And no more removing it for car washes! I read multiple reviews for this before ordering.. as far as radio reception/quality, the reviews were half and half.. some experienced a much worse to no signal at all and the others said they weren't affected. I live in the country so it does not surprise me to be one of those who has very little AM/FM signal much at all now. I listen to Sirius all the time anyway, so no problem here! All in all, a sleek way to modify your truck and give it a little touch of class!

title: Ultimate Computer Screen Cleaning Product!
text: This is, by far, the BEST product I have used to clean my laptop screen! Extremely easy to use, small enough to fit into one of my laptop case pockets.. it is the only product I have used that doesn't leave ANY streaks behind! A clean screen, just as good as the day I purchased it, is worth it to me. I will never use anything else on my laptop screen again! I like that the cloth can be removed and rotated to a clean section then reinserted.. and when the cloth is completely soiled, you can simply toss it in your washing machine (just don't put it in the dryer!). For the customer who had the bottle dribbling problem.. mine did at first, but like any other pump product, you have to pump it a few times to get all the air worked out of the pump line. I pumped the bottle over my kitchen sink until the gel sprayed out evenly on the side of my sink (about 6-7 full pumps). For the customer who had issues with the design for removing the cover.. I found that this was not an issue at all. I did not have to pinch the cover to remove it.. it is more like a 'press with your thumb and slide outward' motion. No pinching at all. It does snap into place really well which is a good thing.. not exactly something you want to just pop off all the time.

title: Affordable and effective
text: My husband and I bought two sets of these three years ago from Circuit City during their going out of business sale. We both travel quite a bit and were in need of decent headphones for longer flights (let's face it, the ear buds provided by the airlines just don't cut it). My husband accidentally left his set, in their pouch, in the seat back pocket on a flight last year and was in need of a replacement set for our trip to Germany last week. I was amazed by the price when I came onto Amazon to check - $29.99 was a steal compared to the $80 we spent a few years back! This headset is not the top of the line, but it is effective in canceling out the low aircraft drawl while in-flight. (They are also quite nice when you need to drown out the crying child in 23F. ;)) The battery life is remarkable. I have had to change the battery on my set only twice in the three years I've owned it. The only complaint that I have, which results in the four star rating instead of five, is that after wearing the set for a few hours (i.e., Amsterdam to Houston, TX), my ears begin to ache on the outside. It is almost like the headset becomes to tight over longer periods of time. I tend not to wear earrings on airplanes, so I can rule out the possibility of pinching. Other than that slight achy feeling, these are wonderful for the casual traveler and the price simply cannot be beat!

title: Amazing little card
text: I bought this card for use with my new Canon ([[ASIN:B005MTMFHU Canon SX40 HS 12.1MP Digital Camera with 35x Wide Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7-Inch Vari-Angle Wide LCD]]). I traveled to Germany and Amsterdam August 17-26 and wanted to ensure I had enough space for any pictures I wanted to take. I took my laptop along to transfer pictures over for safe keeping in case I accidentally deleted while learning to use the new camera. Turned out that this card was more than enough storage! Over the course of my ten day trip, I took over 2000 pictures and the display on the camera today says I have room for 7056 more pictures still. Simply amazing. AT the time of my purchase, the item title stated that this card was a 30MB/s speed and the description stated that it was 45MB/s. I wanted the 45MB/s so I contacted live chat and the representative confirmed that the title needed to be updated to reflect the correct specifications for the item. I am glad to see that Amazon is on their game as the title has now been updated less than two weeks later. I highly recommend this card to anyone who needs a SDHC card for everyday/travel photography needs!

title: Perfect for the amateur photographer
text: I am a photography-holic. I take thousands of pictures on each trip I go on. I purchased this camera to replace my five year old Kodak Easy Share for my trip to Germany last week. It was a complete dream to use! I took over 2000 pictures over eight days and never had an issue (except for figuring out how to take panoramic pictures - my Easy Share stitched the pictures on screen, this Canon requires you to load the pictures onto a computer that has the imaging software installed and then use that software to stitch pictures together to create the ultimate finished panoramic image). Easy to operate and learn its functions. It does not come with a printed manual (the manual is on the included CD) and this did not work for me as I am one who requires a good old fashioned printed manual. Easy fix: I copied the pdf file to a USB thumb drive, took it to my local copy shop and had a printed version the next morning. The only negative thing on this purchase for me is that now, two weeks after my purchase, the price has dropped by $30. :( Would have been nice to have that extra cash in Germany.

title: Small Size and Quiet
text: I have a super large keyboard that I only use a fraction of, so I thought a smaller keyboard might make it easier for me to use. It immediately began working the moment I plugged in the nano USB receiver into my Chromebox. Worked flawlessly and quietly. As a writer, I am on the keyboard 6-10 hours a day and I have worn out two keyboards by wearing off the lettering, but to be truthful, I put the small keyboard away after the day's end, not for any problems with it, just that I realized that I needed to weight and feel of the heavier, larger keyboard. But I am keeping it because I like it and I can use it on my Chromebook. So as I can't attest to longevity, I can say it works well, is light, and instantly connected to the computer.

title: New ! Ads. Ads, and more ADS!
text: I have Echo's all throughout my house. But, as a writer, I quickly learned that recently, distraction has now become the norm with Echo Show. Pop-Up Ads show up every 5-10 seconds, disrupting my photo collection and my train of thought. And then to integrate Avatar items into responses is annoying as can be! title: The Great Sound and Alerts to Orbs!
text: [[VIDEOID:c4a7ee3d38a2fad3bcb6b7e00f0ac70f]] At first, I didn't understand the camera and gave a bad rating, that's because I have 6 WYZE cams. The WYZE cams give a sharp picture and I pay for extended camera coverage when motion is detected. BUT WYZE cameras have the worst sound. title: Beautiful HD photos show
text: I have two Echo Show 8s and this is my third Echo Show 5. Started out with Echo Dot, given as a gift, but I wanted more... I wanted sight as well as sound. I had a problem with some ads, but I contacted Amazon and techs immediately took care of the problem. It seems to hold photos longer than the 6 seconds it is slated to change, but I am not going to go through the process of restoring it back from a complete re-boot. I'm hoping one day to be able to afford an Echo Show 10, because even at 76, I love AI and all the technology.

title: This One Is Great!
text: I needed my Echo Show 8 to be vertical so the camera wasn't showing the ceiling. I had bought another brand that offered so little motion range that it was useless, but I had to get something I could use that was affordable for me. As soon as it arrived, I took it out of the box and it mounted on the Echo Show 8 within seconds. It's sturdy and those magnets are strong. It raised the Echo Show 8 up from the cabinet shelf which helps with the sound vibration I was having when there was direct contact. A definite 5 stars!!! Photo shows Amazon's notification of delivery of the stand I love this and wish I had seen it in the first place.

title: Not flexible enough
text: The amount of movement for flexibility is ridiculous. It is so little that it is useless. I tried to save money and now I have something that is useless. The photo shows maximum tilt, but with this, the Echo Show still shows the ceiling when the camera is on. Not enough tilt.

title: So behind on keystrokes showing up on computer, keys are hard, lights are a joke!
text: If you want a conversation piece to show people the lights, make sure they don't blink because lights turn off so fast and you are left with a dark keyboard until you touch a key or wake the mouse. The keys are HARD and that makes typing difficult for a writer that thinks on the keystroke. The price is outrageous for such a piece of plastic garbage. My daughter bought me one for HALF the price and the keys are so easy and the response time on that wireless keyboard is instant. So unless you just like an arcade 'lights up' type of toy, spend half the money and get a real, functional keyboard and mouse and forgo the quickly vanishing, uneven lights. Never will fall for a 2-only reviews of item, when only one shows. Going back as fast as UPS can drive. Added note: Company offered a $20 gift card if I would delete this review. This review stands, I will not delete it for a price, that alone should warn you about this company!

title: Big Battery Savings!
text: I just could not justify buying more batteries for my Dymo label maker, it used up the expensive batteries (Dymo tells you to buy) within 5 uses! Finding an accessory adapter for it was difficult until I found this one on Amazon. Plugged it in, works perfectly, no more batteries to buy. That's a big savings!

title: Awesome! Everything Fits!
text: I need more of these! It ends the clutter and ends the hassle of trying to get oversized plugs to not overlap the other outlets. Until there is a universally sized plug standard, plugs come in all different sizes and shapes and when using a normal end-to-end power strip, sometimes only 3 plugs can fit when there is room for 5. I don't know why I waited so long to try a tower outlet, but now that I have, I will buy more of these to replace my narrow strip outlets. I did my due diligence and checked all kinds of towers and read all the reviews and GLCON seemed the best. My bulky plugs are now spaced away from the outlets so instead of having to unplug one plug to use the vacuum cleaner, I now have 5 empty slots to choose from. At age 75, always learning and I am glad I learned about this tower's capabilities.

title: Nothing Like My Old Fire
text: My old Fire ran out of space and it had no way of adding more memory. There was nothing left for me to delete. When I finally could afford a new one, it came as a huge disappointment. Yes, it's larger, yes, it has more features. It also has ads because I couldn't afford one without. Very difficult to navigate and although it took files from the old one, not one of my purchased books can be found on it, not in cloud (where is the cloud?). I'm 75 years old and pretty computer savvy, but this Fire is just too annoying to have to spend so much time trying to get what I need from it. My Gmail? Oh hell, I have to open a brand new account, seems it didn't transfer, and won't transfer. Not impressed.

title: Very Attractive
text: The moment I unpackaged the cover, I was getting compliments on how beautiful it is. It snapped onto the Fire easily and fit well. I like the magnetic closer. The con: I used my older, smaller Fire with a cover that opened like a book. With this model cover, it opens on the opposite side. Instead of a book-type opening, it opens on the other side and that is awkward. If I find it too awkward after some use, I will need to look for another brand cover. And yes, I know I can simply turn it upside down and open book-like, but that puts the on/off button on the bottom. For many, it may be too insignificant to bother with... But for me, that is awkward. But, I did want to mention it for any people out there that are like me and want a 'book-type' opening.

title: OMG!!! STOP THE ADS!!!!
text: Yes, you can choose your wallpaper and background, but for what purpose? There is a constant non-stop show of ads, requests for your re-ordering of previous purchases, sports events to watch, children's movies to see. OMG!! Stop it!!! I paid enough for this to want some enjoyment from it. Half the time I ask Alexa something, my Echo Dot in the kitchen responds instead of the Echo Show in the living room, where I am sitting within two feet of. You can 'adjust' your preferences and I have, but to no avail. Why am I paying so much for 24 hours worth of Amazon ads flashing before me? You should be paying me for advertising. Not happy! I'm 75, I don't want to see all the 'kiddie' movies available or sports for that matter. I should have the right to choose.

title: Adds Length To Cam Cord
text: I needed this because my 6 ft. cord that came with my WYZE CAM was not long enough. Although pricier than I hoped, it also came with the metal disc and adhesive stick-on for mounting, which is great because I have a few WYZE cams, and this way, I can move a cam to a different area with a secure mount. WYZE makes its cams and products affordable for even a senior such as me, on a fixed income. Okay, I couldn't resist getting a 'bat cover' making it my 'Batcam'.

title: Cannot Straighten out Cord
text: I can't use this plug in any way, shape, or form. Plug it in and the tightly curled wire will not straighten out. This is so ridiculous. The length I need just isn't there and the thickness and curliness of the wire take up so much room because it will not flatten out. Would it be so difficult to wrap this plug in the way that all other plugs are wrapped for sale? I need to return this cube so I can get one that the wire lays flat.

title: Roomy for Large Plugs
text: I like the way it looks. I like the way it offers spacing for plugs and it has 4 outlets for USB plugs. It is safe and protective for my devices. My problem lies with those product manufacturers that insist on using gigantic plugs that take up at least two outlets, even with this roomy power strip. Compared to my previous power strip, I was able to end up with one opening left.

title: So Easy to Set Up.
text: Works great. Installed immediately but the sound is kind of tinny. I can live with that. Excellent compliment to my Echo family.

title: Set Up Flawless & Fast
text: The little booklet tells you how to set up your new Smart Plug and explains that if prompted by the app during setup, you can scan the barcode printed on the back. I never had the chance. When I went to my Alexa app, she promptly informed me that she had added the plug to my 'set of lights'. I was up and running in less than 30 seconds! I do have a few different brands of plugs that work well with Alexa, but nothing as fast and seamlessly integrated as the Amazon Smart Plug. That's the only plug I will buy from now on. I am more than delighted with this!

title: Perfect Fit
text: It took me less than 5 minutes from box to wall. Since Alexa (the Echo Dot), moved into my kitchen because the Echo Show was now in the living room, counter space is very limited. What a wonderful solution this is. Matter of fact, I never realized how nice the Dot lights up before mounting it so I can see the top easily. Great idea!!!

title: Love this cam!!!
text: Great picture quality during the day. I can hit the photo button or the record button and save it to my phone and even send photos. I can set a 'detection' zone within the camera's view to narrow down the area for alerts. I know the photo doesn't look like the Wyze Cam v2, but I just had to add the adorable cover for it even though my porch is partially enclosed. I get alerts on my phone while away from home if someone comes onto my porch. It offers a nice wide area of coverage. The night vision is not that great, but then I live in the mountains and it gets pitch black after dark, so I expected that. You can listen to sound and you can even speak through it. Yeah, that nearly caused my UPS guy to drop the package when I spoke to him through the camera. For the money, it's fantastic!!!

title: Video Makes All the Difference (new rating, new reasons)
text: I love my Echo Dot 'Alexa'. She turns on and off my lights, reminds me to take my meds, and plays any song I request on my Prime music list. That said... When my daughter moved to Fl. and video chatting was all we have, I decided to get the Echo Show 5. The sound of the Echo Show is far richer than the Dot. At first, I did not like the fact that Alexa's voice was now muted by bass. I solved the problem with the Amazon Alexa app, where I was able to go to audio settings and adjust the bass and treble. Any music played on the Echo Show is far superior to that of the Dot (no offense to my Echo Dot, I still love it). REVISION: I'm 'old school' and believe in 'manuals, paper manuals' for guided instructions. I had to 'Google' how to change the settings on the Echo Show so I could access options on what would be appearing on the screen. This was after I complained to Amazon and they said they would forward my complaint about too many ads appearing. They never told me to check my settings and I had no manual to guide me. So I think I have now gotten rid of 'cooking recipes' and movie suggestions for little children. I LOVE TECHNOLOGY, but please, give accompanying manuals.

title: I'm Charging Again!
text: I can't believe my fancy navigation device doesn't have a wall charger packaged with it. Sure, I can recharge it with my laptop, but I don't want that. Call me old fashioned, but I want a wall plug. Charger City had just what I needed and at a great price and super fast shipping. All I needed and more.... Thanks!

title: Forget the other guys, Tom Tom is the best!
text: Wow! Tom Tom has certainly come a long way since my first little Tom Tom. You can give commands verbally and it replies in a Siri type voice. Free lifetime of maps is worth the purchase of this alone. Large screen that even splits to help you make the right decision when coming upon a confusing area. I know my children and my friends have all bought these high end navigators and had them constantly break down and have to get new ones... They never learn. I've had my first Tom Tom for over 5 years without problems and only replaced it because I needed a bigger screen. Plus with Tom Tom, you can add comic and celebrity voices to guide you. See if you can get Homer Simpson to get you where you're going with those higher priced gadgets. I love my Tom Toms, they have never failed me! Incredibly smart with a touch of humor!

title: Incredibly beautiful picture.
text: I never thought the day would come when I would state that I love a t.v. But at the age of 69, that day has come. I knew from the start that I wanted a Vizio and no other. I have been in enough stores to see the difference in Vizio's picture when compared to other brands. I also did my research and decided that the 4K Ultra HD was the way I would go. Let me tell you, when it was hooked up and turned on, I was left breathless... The clarity and color just blew me away. I purchased a 4K blu-ray dvd player and then a 4K blu-ray dvd (which they really need to produce a greater variety of, by the way) and turned them on. Stunning, is the first word that came to mind! Now I have signed up for Netflix Streaming and will get the Ultra HD as well as 4K movies. Yes, I was around when the tiny black & white t.v.'s first came into being with the rabbit ear antennas and very limited channels and fuzzy pictures so I think I qualify to say that this is the most amazing picture I have ever seen. I love Vizio and I know I made the most perfect choice in buying this.

title: So Easy to Install that even a 69 year old lady can do it!
text: I am female and 69 years old. That said, I must tell you that I installed this all by myself for my new 50" t.v. They gave great instructions that were easy to follow. My review doesn't include how you find things when you're out of bluetooth range..... but I think there's an alert for your phone when you're about to leave your wallet somewhere, etc., or about to exit bluetooth range.... pretty sure that's how it works. title: Shop around.
text: I've had WD drives for decades, and the only issues I ever had were with WD Green and Black drives. Red, Red Plus, and Red Pro work where they're intended to work, as they're intended to work. So do WD Blue. Before buying a WD drive, learn what each color is intended for. The Black drives I've had fail were due to insufficient cooling. Blue are to be used in a PC with one or two drives that sees daily use. That's daily, not 24/365. Not in an array. Each level of Red drive is intended for arrays of different numbers of drives. They are not quiet desktop drives. You really want them somewhere other than next to where you sit. More importantly than all that, carefully check prices in several places. Don't pay the absurd prices that some people want after buying their stock at retail price. They'll go back down. WD will make more.

title: Enterprise/LTE/4G version works with Verizon
text: Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all. I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't. This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two. I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps. So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon. Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed. Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU. From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged. Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.

title: Usually cheap enough for off-line storage
text: The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.

Using internal storage, the videos load into the editor almost instantly, and using PIP I can include one 4k track and three 1080 tracks with no issues. I've produced videos up to 2 1/2 hours long. A laptop that would do all that would cost thousands. I wasn't expecting it to work this well. That's a lot of processing. I'm normally disappointed by the gadgets I buy, and was expecting this to work, but not as well as it does. I was impressed. It far exceeded my expectations. TexasHillsurfer

title: Limited output, but perfect for some applications
text: Update: I'd recommend the 7800mAh batteries for the difference in price. They're not much bulkier, and they provide about 8-9 hours of charge at 1080/30 for a GoPro Hero 5 Black. I haven't tested them other than that so far but the 7 should be comparable. Note: Both batteries require a compatible camera case and cable to be waterproof. Previous review: I've been using these batteries for years to power GoPros, and they work great up to a point. If you're recording 1080/30 video using GoPro Hero Black 5-7 they're fine. They really don't provide enough amperage for 4K. They'll record, but you may lose the connection if you're using GoPro Quik. It seems the cameras shut down WiFi and Bluetooth if the voltage drops. I have no way of knowing if that's actually the case, but that seems to be the weak point. At 1080/30 with a GoPro Hero 5 Black, they'll record from 5 to 6 hours of continuous video. Using WiFi to view the captured image will shorten that considerably. I normally use a Bluetooth Remote GoPro app to start and stop recording. It uses far less power, and can sync several cameras.

title: Does what I need it to do.
