Don't get suckered into buying this junk.

title: After 1 year = Junk
text: After using this player about 1x every 2 months for over a year now .. it can no longer play newer BLU RAYS (even after firmware updates) In addition the menu's lock up, the load times are awful and the unit itself becomes un-responsive whenever I put a BLU RAY into the unit. The streaming video options were appealing when I bought this unit, but honestly this feature has never worked from day one locking up or buffering so often it's impossible to watch anything. This is the first truely awful piece of equipment I have got from Samsung in a long time, but thought it was worth sharing. For BluRay players .. look elsewhere

title: Home run
text: I’m becoming a Vocolinc fanboy. Every device I’ve tried has been nothing but well designed and dependable and the PM2E powerstrip is no exception. It was simple to setup - it took all of ten minutes, including an initial firmware update, and most of that time was for cable management. It integrates with and works well with Apple Homekit.

title: So far, so good
text: Imagine my happiness when I took my Ryobi string trimmer out of storage this spring only to find the battery (which was working fine when I put it away last fall) refused to take a charge. Imagine my further joy to find that a ‘genuine’ Ryobi replacement battery costs (are you sitting down?) ONE HUNDRED FORTY DOLLARS, US. This, for a string trimmer which - with the original battery and charger - only cost $10 more than that. But I digress. THIS battery is the functional equivalent of the Ryobi branded device but about 40% less expensive. Still overpriced, but what choice do we - the Ryobi indentured - have? It fits, charges, works and lasts as long as the Ryobi device did when new. Have no worries about whether it will work - it will.

title: Minor complaints, but generally a decent buy
text: I’m not a DIY kind of guy, so I went with the cheapest, simplest mount I could find. It’s okay, but be prepared for some minor adjustments. The Pros: price. It’s much less expensive than most of the others. It’s also quite minimalist - no thick bezels. It’s made of a flexible silicone material - that’s both a pro and a con - the pro - it’s soft on your tablet - no scratches. It’s also somewhat flexible - I installed mine vertically in a tight space and there’s no room to slide the tablet in from the side. Instead, I have to seat it in the bottom mount and sort of snap it into place in the top. Given the flexibility of the material, this works fine. The cons: included with the mount are 6 each screws and wall anchors - no spares and no washers. The anchors don’t have any lip on the end so a couple of mine dropped into the wall cavity, making it necessary to go buy some spares. Also, the screw heads easily pull through the holes in the mounts when tightened. I fixed that with a handful of small washers which should be included with the mount kit. Also, my tablet (an old iPad Air 2) Is quite slim and doesn’t fit snugly in the mount so I put a short strip of thin silicone insulation behind it to better hold it in place. There is a slot in the center of one mount to allow access For a charging cable. Thoughtfully, it appears to be even wide enough for the old style wide Apple connector. Included is also a paper template for various size devices and a stick on cable retainer. Aside from the minor complaints about washers and wall mounts, I’m satisfied with the kit.

title: An alternative to Apple’s silicone tips
text: I have trouble with the OEM silicone tips keeping a good seal. If I do something wild and crazy (like turning my head /sarcasm) the seal breaks and noise cancellation is diminished. I’m used to using memory foam earplugs and decided to try these memory foam AirPod tips. Not as good as I had hoped, but not a complete waste either. They fit more snugly and hold a seal better than Apple’s silicone tips, so that’s a plus. However, they aren’t as comfortable for long listening sessions. I tried the smaller size, thinking maybe the issue was size... nope. I’d also suggest being very careful when removing them as well - the Apple tips are surprisingly resilient (seemingly indestructible, despite the impression that the silicone is easily tearable. It isn’t.) but I destroyed one of the memory foam tips in the process of unsnapping it from the AirPod.

title: Powers up my old iPad 1 👍
text: I was hoping for a braided cable, or something a little thicker than the cheap ones that Apple includes with their devices. Nope - same thickness, but at least this one has strain relief on both ends. Plus, it’s a fraction of the cost of the official Apple cable and twice the length, so that’s worth a couple of stars.

title: Treble! Hooray, I can understand Alexa now!
text: I have Echo devices of one kind or another in every room and have had others that I’ve decided to let go (original Echo and Echo Auto). They’ve all performed their smarthome duties acceptably well. My biggest complaint across the board is sound quality. Alexa always sounds like she’s talking to you from underneath a pile of pillows. Bass? Sure, on the Echo Show, at least. Treble? Nada. Sure, you can use the app’s “equalizer”... but it’d take an oscilloscope to detect the minuscule difference that makes in the sound quality. I’d given up on getting any more devices... until I saw a review of the Flex on Paul Hibbert’s YouTube channel... he liked it, but said (I think) that it sounded ‘trebly’. Trebly?! That’s a magic word to my ears. I ordered one up and found that it indeed sounds ‘trebly’ (call it tinny of you like) but who cares? Who seriously listens to music on these tiny little devices anyway?! I can understand what Alexa says now - all the plosives are there. I still wonder why Amazon can’t tune the rest of the Alexa enabled devices for better higher frequency clarity.

title: Happy camper
text: It’s a lot less expensive than the Nikon branded battery and it works. 👍

title: It works
text: I added a few of these to my system - they’re an updated from the previous square version and now attach via a magnet to a ball and socket base which, in turn, attaches to your wall (or wherever) with a sticky pad. The ball and socket design is great - makes it so much easier to change the angle of view or remove the device to swap out batteries; however, I’m not a big fan of the sticky pad. Make sure you want it to stay where you put it because the sticky won’t let go without a fight and will probably take a little paint or wallpaper with it if you DO remove it.

title: A solid and inexpensive solution
text: Built like a tank. I bought it, I plugged it in, I forgot about it and it’s been running flawlessly ever since. What more could you ask for?

title: Bright but eats batteries
text: I guess it depends on how long you want to read, right? I haven’t actually timed it, but I only use the light occasionally for an hour or so at a time but have had to replace the batteries several times. Three tiny little Phillips screws (don’t drop em!) and a couple more CR2032 batteries and we’re good to go again. Wish this was rechargeable...

title: Fail

title: Works with USB-C iPad Pro, but...
text: I bought a 3rd party (3 pack) which didn’t work with my 2018 iPad Pro. They were (apparently) well made, but no sound, so I bought Apple’s dongle to be reasonably certain of success. Well, it works, but I don’t have a lot of confidence in the quality. VERY fragile. I’m thinking I might wrap it in heat shrink tubing to avoid a premature failure.

title: A good value
text: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: I’m a satisfied customer
text: After reading the many critical of Blink’s customer service I wanted to add my two cents. I don’t have a LOT of experience with support, but did just have one of my cameras (indoor) fail on me after several months of trouble-free use. I tried an assortment of things before emailing Blink (reset, replace batteries, uninstall/reinstall) and had pretty much determined it was a hardware issue. Blink support had me go through the same troubleshooting steps and came to the same conclusion. The entire process from my initial contact to their resolution took less than a day. They had a replacement camera and an RMA label in my hands in about a week, and the replacement is working fine (along with my other cameras - both indoor and XT outdoor). I’m satisfied with my system and Blink’s support. My only criticism is minor - the iOS app doesn’t support iPad in native landscape mode and I live on my iPad. Battery life has been great - I’ve had most of my cameras for almost a year and haven’t had any batteries die yet. Blink’s servers have been down (maybe?) three times since I’ve been using their gear (that I’ve noticed) and one of those times was a widespread outage which couldn’t be blamed on them. Acceptable service, especially considering it’s provided at no cost. I’m sure you can buy better security cameras, but I don’t know of anything better, easier to setup or more flexible for the price.

title: Mixed feelings on the case, but STELLAR customer service
text: I've owned///used this keyboard since the iPad Air 2 was introduced. It wasn't inexpensve. As I'm typing this review I'm having to fight with one of the more annoying issues - repeating keys. And gods forbid you should hit the delete key to get rid of some of the repeating characters because the delete key will repeat and delete what you've just typed. The rubber pads on both sides of the keyboard mysteriously started peeling off not too long ago. They don't seem to be absolutely necessary, so I stopped trying to stick them back on and instead, peeled them off and cleaned the glue residue they left behind. Battery life is waning - I have to charge the case almost nightly or the orange light starts flashing and it loses connectivity or shuts down. Other than those issues, it still works. It looks good and fits well. I haven't had any magnet issues and the backlight is a godsend. ** update ** It's only fair to also point out that Belkin must monitor Amazon for comments about their products. I didn't contact them - they proactively contacted me and arranged a replacement for my QODE case/keyboard. The unit is two years old, and given my experience with most other manufacturers, I wasn't expecting anything, so this is a nice surprise. Kudos to Belkin customer support for what I consider to be service above and beyond. I've received the replacement and have been using it for a couple of weeks - no sign of the connectivity or repeating key issues and (of course) the rubber bumpers are intact.

title: meh
text: Keep in mind: this is a $40 device. If you're looking for reliable home surveillance, probably best to skip this one, and maybe D-Link altogether. That having been said, I found it fairly easy to setup. Video streaming to mydlink.com is at best undependable, however, so I wasn't sure at the time if setup was working or not. After messing with it for about an hour I had to leave and wasn't able to access the video stream. I checked in later and it had magically started working on its own. Go figure. You can access the camera directly via IP address or via their freebie app locally, but remote is a crapshoot. Resolution is low quality (320x240). Night mode is okay close up. I'm unable to access mydlink.com on my Mac - apparently there's no support for the current MacOS (Sierra). I emailed D-Link support with questions but received a generic "this is how to reinstall the camera" response, so I don't know if they eventually plan to support Sierra. It seems possible that this device has been orphaned in favor of newer models. The camera is small and light and the base is quite adjustable to allow easy positioning. (note: indoor use only) I bought it to enable watching for animal activity in my wooded back yard - I haven't managed to get it set up to email me activity alerts yet but it's (barely) adequate for that purpose.

title: if you're anything like me. My CoolPix P510 has a lens leash ...
text: This was exactly what I was looking for. Lens caps are a nuisance - ya gotta have em, but what do you do with them while you're shooting? Lose them, if you're anything like me. My CoolPix P510 has a lens leash included/built in - why does my DSLR - at 4 times the price - not? No matter, these are the babies you're looking for - elastic loop around the barrel of your lens, little sticky tab on the cap and a string between. No more fiddling with or losing lens caps. This was also the best price I found on Amazon. Go for it.

title: the ear of the beholder
text: Everybody has an opinion and they're all different. I finally settled on a pair of MDR-EX51LP buds for my iPod. The buds that come with the iPod are poor sounding and uncomfortable, no matter how trendy it may be to have a white wires dangling from your ears. I tried several different types and brands and settled on these. They have a more balanced sound than the other headphones in the sub $50 bracket that I tested - good bass, clean highs and mids. Do they compare with premium studio cans? No, but neither do the price tag, size or weight. They block office noise at a reasonable SPL and allow me to concentrate on my work without distraction. I can still hear some outside sound if I keep the music volume low enough - as has been mentioned before, that can be a good thing. They're very comfortable - I wear them for hours at a time on a daily basis. I don't get the uneven cord length, but it really isn't a big deal. Headphones are like operating systems - there is no such thing as one size fits all. Get the ones that work for you (and your audio device!) and don't start a holy war with someone who prefers something different.

title: Great Product
text: I purchased this to replace my five year old antenna from a box store. I live in an apartment and on the north side of the building; second floor. Most free transmission TV stations and satellites seem to have better reception on the south side. Anyway, I have this installed in a utility bucket filled with gravel on my apartment patio(we are not allowed to secure anything to railings or the building) My old outside antenna worked this way and this antenna does as well. Value of this product: First it was easy to assemble but you will need two AAA batteries for the remote It has more reception loops (5) and that helps tremendously The motorized 360 is a nice feature (my old antenna required me to turn it manually) Reception: is outstanding; especially where I reside; full of signal obstructions. I get a lot of channels including all the major ones (NBC, ABC, CBS, FOX, CW, Star 64, and lots of local channels Overall this is a 5-star product and great value!

title: Just OK for the Keyboard
text: I try real hard to be honest in every review. Some vendors take offense to honesty and products that are not a 5-star rating. But, we on Amazon, truly depend on each other and honesty for products that we want to purchase. We are all different but for me this is my honest assessment. The tablet case does secure the LG G f8 (8inch) tablet well. But, I have had a similar case in the past for my Kindle Fire and never had any issues. It is very strong and durable. My issue is with the keyboard and how it secures with the tablet case. The keyboard is a sturdy construction and not a silicone keypad. BUT, there is not tiny mouse pad within its design. That means to make my LG G tablet truly functional for writing documents, emails and the such I need to have an additional item - a wireless mouse; otherwise why need a keyboard. So, I had to order a mini mouse as well which doesn't exactly fit anyplace but in my pocket or carry bag. The other issue is the way the tablet, case and keyboard are designed to be closed. The case elastic strap is actually the same as the one on my kindle Fire and slips around the secured tablet and does it well. However, add a keyboard, which was NOT a design to this tablet holder and you have to decide if you want the keyboard face against your tablet, tight, as that elastic strap secures them both. that means the keyboard is actually not secure by the case but ONLY by the outer elastic strap. Or, you flip the keyboard so that the back of that keypad rests against your tablet screen and it is still only secured by the outer elastic strap. Both methods require that you ensure you keep this tablet case upright so that the keyboard does not slip out of this elastic band as time and use deteriorate the elastic and its tension. So, in essence, this is a case that has been around and works well for Kindle Fire and probably this tablet. but, this case was NOT designed to include a keyboard. this was a vendor added item with an existing product. When you pay $200 for a tablet you want to ensure you do not scratch the screen or damage the tablet. And if you like the use of a keyboard, note that a mouse will also be required and that it may be best to look for alternative cases to accommodate your needs in one neat package Update: July 2016: well after very limited use the key board is no loner functioning. It's not the charge it is a dead key board. I am a senior and disabled Vietnam veteran appreciate each dollar of my disability pay and do not have that luxury of repeat purchases. So, even though I am only one customer I would consider other products that have a higher reliability and that are not tied to a protective case purchase.

title: Great Carry Bag
text: First, this is an excellent company and their partnership with Amazon shipping makes it worry free. The product is really of great quality. The affordable price and excellent quality make it an excellent buy. I bought the 17 inch laptop size so I have options on my next computer purchase. Lots of space. Zippers are strong. The strap is the right size although the I replaced my strap end clips (to attach the strap to the bag) with metal clips used for key holders. In the past, on other bags, my constant use did result in a broken clip, but that was my daily and constant in and out of my car use of my computer bag. This product has good secure clip straps but for an expensive laptop I did my only upgrade to this bag for a few bucks. Anyway, the padding is great and do is the internal strap to secure the laptop. Pocket areas are sufficient however the bag has no pen holders. This is my "go to bag" and it works great. I got it because it opens as a brief case, with zippers, and adds the perfect touch for frequent use. Great buy

title: Works Great

title: Maybe it was my fault for not understanding how it worked but very disappointed
text: I thought that a wireless SDHC card was genious, i can upload my pictures automatically as long as I am in range of my wireless connection! Brillant, that means they'll automatically transfer whenever I come home, i don't even have to take my camera out of my purse. NOPE, that's not how it works. First of all your camera has to be ON in order to transfer, so you have to physically get your camera and turn it on near your computer. That's about as much work as taking the memory card out. Secondly, you have to leave this giantic bulky USB connected plugged into your computer which is annoying and not at all convenient. By the time you've done those two steps it would have been easier to take out the memory card and stick it in the computer. Then i realize my computer has an SDHC slot in it making this whole thing even more stupid. I'm going to try and send it back if I can. I don't really see the appeal unless you are a professional that wants to be able to display pictures on a screen as he's taking them, then that's cool but if you just want an easier time transfering them to your home computer this isn't a benefit. Considering how much more expensive they are than regular SDHC cards it's a total waste.

title: the device I didn't know I needed
text: I've been a cynic of wearables for a long time by debating the need to charge a watch daily, and the slew of available features that I swore I'd never use such as calling, and texting from my watch... I was wrong. I find myself relying more on the watch than my phone for setting alarms or timers. I use the phone feature to have brief calls, or send a quick reply to a text message. The features for tracking my daily sleep, steps, and heart rate, help make me more conscious of my life style. Before purchasing this watch I was looking at cheaper alternatives, but I am glad that I purchased the iwatch because it works well with my other devices and is a welcome member of my slowly growing gadget family. There are a few annoyances by saying "hey siri" i summon the total of 3 siri's fighting over which device will answer my command. I am a big guy and was worried the watch band would'nt fit but I am happy to report that it comes with 2 band sizes and the large band fit my beefy wrist.

The left and right buttons have a nice clicky snap to them that gives it nice feedback whenever you interact with them. And the surface area your fingers interact with to move the cursor has a slight texture but nothing significant. It's not smooth like glass but not rough like sand paper. For the price it meets my expectations. My hands are quite bad and I can't use a traditional mouse. I prefer this over a trackball style setup and would recommend it to anyone in my situation. I'll admit the one thing I forgot is that there's no middle mouse button, but that seems common among all trackpads and just highlights my oversight during pre-purchase.

title: 70 LBS Down and counting!
text: I credit Fitbit with my loss of 70 lbs over a period of approximately 9 months, a loss I've kept off for going on a year. Using it regularly made me realize how little exercise I was getting, and made me focus on increasing my efforts. I'm not one for group exercise, but competing daily against myself--my previous Fitbit results-- stirred my competitive juices, and I tried to better my numbers every day. Now I'm at the point where I feel restless if I haven't walked my five miles a day, and I try to shake up my routine a bit by finding new and different forms of exercise--like skydiving! When I think of all the money I wasted over the years on exercise equipment, weight loss plans and so forth, I'm grateful for the simplicity and effectiveness of Fitbit. Not to say that it would work for everyone--motivation is key--but at this price, it's well worth a try.

Especially when I'm curled up on the couch, surrounded by dogs and the occasional cat, and don't want to get up and disturb everyone. This Sony has worked perfectly so far. title: Great bag!
text: I very seldom review products I purchase on Amazon but felt this one merited a few minutes of my time. I received this bag the day after I placed the order- faster than the shipping speed I paid for. It is a beautiful, beautiful bag. The look is just what I was going for- vintage, without actually being old. The material and craftsman ship is superb. It looks lux, without the lux price tag. It is sturdy and lightweight and the front buckles keep things secure. The strap is adjustable which is great, since I typically like to wear my bags/purses cross body. The inside is padded and also adjustable. It has three "compartments". I have a Cannon Rebel T3i and when unassembled, the camera body fits in one compartment and the lens fits in the second compartment. These compartments can be adjusted so I can combine two of them into one large compartment and store the camera assembled...which is great if you don't want to constantly be removing and adding the lens. Either way, that still leaves a third compartment to hold other things, as well as a back pocket for additional storage. Overall it's just a fantastic bag and a price that can't be beat. It doesn't look like a camera bag so really could be used for all sorts of things. I am excited to take this with me on my next trip!

title: Good Frame!
text: I had never heard of the brand "Micca", so I was a bit skeptical. But I was pleasantly surprised when I received the product and began learning how to use it. The frame is simple and attractive- will fit most decor. Displaying pictures is as easy as inserting the memory card and pushing the "photo" button on the remote. The resolution is pretty good for the price you pay, the sound quality isn't bad, and the video display is good as well. The remote is great, as are its quick press buttons for "photos", "photos and music", and "video"....it's great for the less technically inclined. I gave this as a gift to my grandmother for Christmas and she LOVES it, and it's SO easy for her to use. It doesn't have all the bells and whistles that pricier models have, but if you're looking for a simple, easy to use digital frame to display your pictures, you can't beat this price!!

title: Don't have to worry about my husband when he travels!
text: Great navigator, it does everything except steer the car and work the pedals! Love the larger screen and the voice prompts make it impossible to get lost. My husband travels all over for work and some places are just not too safe. Right now he's working just outside of DC, a very dangerous city with some very confusing routes. He pulled his car over to check his map & some up to no good folks tried to box him in! That was it! I ordered this gear in, he can use his phone hands free and before he leaves each week he programs addresses and no more maps no more looking the vulnerable tourist. An added benefit, first time he used it back in DC it shaved 20 min off his drive time from the route plotted by mapquest. Truly this is worth it's weight in gold. I worry so much less when he's driving those strange cities in the late hours knowing he has his Garmin. Of course you can get a navigation system w/ most rental cars but, you pay extra each time and you have to program it in the lot, so you need to keep all addresses handy. It is cheaper and more efficient that he has his own.

title: UPDATED REVIEW!
text: Update 2/9/23: My (cognitively) young son, who has that very expensive iPad mini I mentioned below in the original review, now pushes his iPad to the side at least 50% of the time and 'steals' my FirePad. There are apps and games on the FirePad that aren't on Apple's AppStore - granted, they're usually pretty basic, or else I imagine they'd be available across multiple OS platforms - but he's very young, cognitively, and he doesn't care. I am 100% certain that whenever this iPad he's got needs replacing (because Apple does that way more than is right, IMO) we will be going the 'FirePad' route. Our family has had so many iPads, iPad Airs, iPad minis... and I can say that - when bought brand spanking new, at the time of release, we were in love. Honeymoons don't last forever, unfortunately, and neither do the tablets. NOT ONCE did we break them beyond being fixable; every single time they've 'updated out' and none of the apps worked. They're not even good for internet after awhile, because even Safari and Chrome have to be updated for use... and the updates will not work with the outdated IOS. Yknow, because $600+ for 2-4 years is acceptable. NOT. But dumb sheeple me, kept on buying them. 🤦🏼‍♀️ I bought my son a 6th Gen iPad mini last November. It was newish and on backorder til about early-mid December. I gave it to him as a gift IN A CHILDPROOF CASE. So it has been protected since I got it. Since before he got it. And two weeks ago it quit charging. Now, he uses his iPad for everything: Communication. Education. Entertainment. Besides the $600 I paid, and even with the $3.49/month AppleCare, it's just totally unacceptable. After taking it to two localish Apple Premium partners, neither of which wanted to fix it and both of which wanted to just sell me a new one, and because all our other iPads (4 that I haven't tossed yet) won't allow him to access his communication apps anymore, I cried and then ordered the Fire Mini on my 23% interest credit card because he needs accessS to something he can communicate on. I'm, erm, a girl of a certain age. Getting more and more stubborn about learning new technology stuff. So getting used to this has been a mite frustrating for me. My son, 25 with the cognitivity and resilience of a 2 year old, hasn't skipped a beat. It's early days - and I did buy the 2 year Amazon Protection with the 'FirePad' as we call it - but for $200 plus tax, tag & title 😉 this little Fire Tablet is at least the quality equivalent of the $600 iPad Mini. The only cons... the display IS just as good as the iPad, though the colors aren't quite as vibrant/vivid and the brightness isn't as bright. Is that worth $400 more... not for anyone I know. It just takes a little getting used to (I'm talking maybe 2 days with minimal usage by a stubborn adult) and then it's not an issue anymore. The biggest con, though, is that Google won't hop in bed with Amazon - apparently - as willingly as they do Apple. No Google app, no Chrome app, no YouTube app. I just use the Silk browser (Bing... YUCK!) type in Google for Google searches or YouTube to watch videos. Maybe 3 seconds of frustration but it does remember my YT log in after the first time, so there's that to help lessen the annoyance for when I use it. (My son watches YouTube on his TV anyway.) CLIFF NOTES: 🔩🍎. 💸🔥 (Screw Apple. Buy Fire.)

title: Seems to help and (weird to me) gives me options
text: Maybe it makes sense to techies... I swear I was really tech savvy like 5 years ago... but in my DSL house (CRAPPY most of the [AT&]Time because all they want is to get everyone on their cellular data plans so they purposefully buffer their DSL speeds during peak times, according to their employee that I've spoken with) this product gives me options now... my wifi went from "ATT1886" (my modem) to "ATT1886_2.4GEXT" and "ATT1886_5GEXT" as alternatives. So if my original wifi starts buffering or is so slow I cannot stream with it, I go into the settings on my phone or Roku or SmarTV and change over to one of the alternatives and I'm back up and running. Well worth the money until I can get on another DSL/Fiber Line ISP. Set up was so easy that I somehow made it hard by overthinking "oh, surely I should do this first". Because what ended up happening was the device pretty much just connected itself as soon as I plugged it in next to my modem (per included instructions) rather than my having to go through steps outlined in all the instructions. title: BEST. THING. EVER.
text: My 'kid' is 24 (cognitively he's about 2) and takes his iPad with him to bed. Doesn't use it, just that's where he puts it when he goes to sleep. Between his pillow and the wall. And every night the iPad was sliding off the bed (even though it is in a silicone case) and I was having to dig it out in the mornings for him. Not once have I had to do this. I had contemplated a few Pinterest 'hacks' that suggested (for example) using Command Hooks attached to the wall and then sitting the iPad down into those (the big 5# ones) hooks. Problem for us is my kid has seizures that are not well controlled by meds, so all I could 'see' in my mind's eye was him seizing and in the convulsing or 'rooting' he does with most of his seizures (or unconsciously standing up then falling back down) one of those seemingly harmless plastic Command hooks gouging his eyeball out or ripping a nostril open. (If you knew all the off the wall sh** that can and does go wrong with seizures, you'd get why all the one-in-a-billions go through my head!) Anyway, this was the best $ I've spent in a long time. It holds the iPad without any sliding or moving (the device or the pillow) and it came in his favorite color. He loved it. I love it.

title: It's pretty good -
text: 3.5 STARS. I rounded up because it is more good then bad: Bought as a Christmas gift for the boyfriend. We are long distance and we FaceTime a lot. Well, actually, I FaceTime with the underside of his kitchen cabinets, the blanket on his bed, the ceilings in all his rooms, or the top of his nightstand. He talks away, oblivious until I say something. It's funny mostly but sometimes in a relationship you need all the connection you can get, even if it's their face on your device while they smile or laugh or talk you through a bad moment. So, I got him this for Christmas so that he could hands-free me and I could still see his pretty face. He finally put it together and started using it the other day... with an asterisk. *THE INCLUDED SCREW/BOLT IS GARBAGE. It was machined badly. Really badly. So it only screws maybe halfway into the arm/neck or whatever it is called, which sits in the weighted base. Thankfully he really doesn't need the screw/bolt because the arm/neck (like a metal dowel, I suppose, that inserts into the base maybe half an inch. The screw/bolt is inserted from under the base and - if it fits correctly) recesses into the base when it's tightened. As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk. The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

title: For my Dad...
text: It stayed in the 90-degree range here in Georgia into October... okay maybe it was high 80s but when ya still feel like a pig at a luau, sans apple in the mouth, when you walk outside, nobody cares if it's technically 87 or 91. Georgia was HOTTTTT this year. That said, my Daddy is an older fella - 73 - and loves his tractors and his loader and anything that puts him working outside but it was TOO FLIPPING HOT for a spry 20 year old, let alone someone fresh off major heart procedures!! I got this for him to try and he laughed... then wore it religiously. Even to sit down in his 'man cave' and watch TV without air conditioning - lol. If you have a loved one that is in heat for their job or just for fun -certain generations still do this ;) - get them this little fan! They'll laugh until they're using it.

title: Bomb. Dot. Com.(even after 2 years of usage)

Rarely does the charge expire before I put it back on to charge on Sunday night (if it does it is Sunday morning). The sound quality is unparalleled and the durability is fantastic (I'm not constantly dropping it or anything but I've probably dropped it a few times). Original Review: My ex-boyfriend had one and he’d bring it when he’d come over. All I had was a giant early 2000s Apple speaker that weighs 20 pounds and had cost over $400 new... it doesn’t move off the top of my fridge much - lol. This is AWESOME!! The sound, the portability. Highly recommend!!

title: This camera has given me a semblance of freedom!!
text: Mother/legal guardian/sole caregiver of an epileptic, mentally handicapped, Autistic adult son. After a hospitalization for a brain bleed, in which the hospital policy would not allow me to spend the night in his room and the night nurses were IMHO 25% the quality of the day shift nurses, he has become SUPER CLINGY. He naps every day and I’ve been afraid he’d wake up, alone, while I was in the yard and become more traumatized (I suspect he was waking at night and finding himself alone, as I was with him every minute from 6am to Midnight unless his Dad was with him or a nurse in the daytime.). I was super excited when I found this camera...last time I’d checked they were $150 each or more. The setup was super easy, the picture quality is INCREDIBLE. High-def 1080p. The sound is great. The app works phenomenally, just take a bit to learn the controls (mute, moving the camera, zooming, etc). I have been able to get out and get a brisk walk around my little acre, do some yard work, or just sit and enjoy the sounds of a lovely summer night. I am so thankful for this camera!!

title: Great Cable Modem - BUT...
text: I have nothing but high praise for this Netgear CMD31T Cable Modem. The instructions were clear and no-nonsense; the physical installation took less than two minutes. I would however, like to give NEGATIVE 5 stars to Comcast's ridiculous telephone service. I called the toll-free number that is provided on my bill and with the modem's paperwork. After wading through endless automated prompts, I was told that my waiting time would be 39-50 minutes. I sat and waited... After about 15 minutes, my call was disconnected. I went through the same ordeal again. After a total of close to an hour, I finally got to talk to someone - just to be told that they couldn't help me there; I needed to call a different number. I called the new number. When I finally talked to someone there, she told me that she couldn't help me; I needed to call a different number. She read the "different" number to me - yes, the same number that I just called her on! I finally talked her into transferring me. The person that I was transferred to didn't speak English very well. After repeating the Serial Number and the Mac ID many, many times to him, he finally got it. But it ends up that he couldn't actually help me either - he said that he would put me on hold to contact the correct person to do the switch over. When he put me on hold, he disconnected me... I called again. 'Got someone else that barely spoke English. He said that my new modem was now in their system and that he would send a test signal. The signal did not make it to my modem for some reason. He asked me to unplug the modem from the power strip that it's on and plug it directly into the wall. I told him that I wasn't going to do that; it was obviously getting power. He then asked me to hold, so he could transfer me to tech support. When he put me on hold, I was disconnected again. I decided that if the modem was showing up in their system now, maybe I could getting it working myself. I unplugged and replugged the power, and waited about 10 minutes. Then I unplugged and replugged my router's power. Success! It's working fine now.

title: It works, but not so well...
text: I'm keeping this unit only because it fits the space that I wanted it in very well - I'm not at all happy with the performance of it. I purchased this TV to mount on a very large desk that I have. The mounting is pretty straight-forward (they supply a cardboard drilling template and a few different spacer options). One thing to keep in mind on the mounting - make sure to allow for extra space for the speakers when drilling your mounting holes (the template does not have this space added). Electronically, this is just a very average to below-average unit. I'm using cable as my video source. The TV that was in this location previously had an excellent picture. This unit has a snowy picture, and very poor color balance (I have tried adjusting it many times - it never does get a "good" picture). The sound is awful. You have to create a balance between two different volume sources - one on the front of the main unit, the other on the TV itself (controlled by buttons on the TV, or by the remote). Between the two, if you turn it up to the point of what I would consider normal volume, you hear a faint but noticeable high-pitched whine (my Jack Russell Terrier hears it too...). The quality of the sound is pretty bad too - very thin and tinny. They should have added an Audio Out Jack, so that you could hook up a decent set of amplified speakers to it. The Power button on the front of the unit is a cheap, spring-loaded design; I can tell that it will create problems in the long run (it has already stuck a few times). The clock display is a bit annoying also - most digital displays will display the single-digit time without a zero in front nowadays - 3:00, for example. This clock displays it as 03:00. The remote must use very unique frequencies - I was not able to program my regular Tivo remote to it (not even when cycling through the hundreds of preset codes that the Tivo remote has). I then purchased a "learning" Tivo remote - even that remote wouldn't accept the "power" or "volume down" functions ("volume up" was the only button that would accept the programming).

title: It's ok...
text: I did not purchase this keyboard for gaming, I purchased it to use mostly as a higher-end computer keyboard. I'm using it in conjunction with [[ASIN:B003BIFI6E the Razer DeathAdder Left-handed Gaming Mouse]]. I like the feel of the keys on this keyboard - the rubbery surface is nice; the bumps on the F, J and 5 keys are easy to feel. The lighted keys look very cool in the dark, and have a good, solid feel when I press them. What I don't like: ~ The lights in the keys are too dim. You can barely see them in a lit room. There should be a way to adjust the brightness of these lights. ~ The Num Lock, Cap Lock, etc. lights are too bright. There should be a way to adjust these also. ~ The Keyboard sits at too low an angle for my taste - the back feet of the keyboard should be raised higher. ~ The smooth finish of the area around the keys shows fingerprints horribly. This surface should be matte. All in all, I like the keyboard (and will keep it), I just wish that a few things about it were designed differently...

title: 'Just one problem, but it's a VERY annoying one...
text: I do like the angled keys - I thought that it might take a while to get used to them, but it did not. Even after getting used to these keys, I don't find it difficult to go back to the "regular" keyboard on my other computers. The keys are a little taller on this keyboard than I'm used to, but that's a quick adjustment also. The one thing that I don't like is that the \ key is located on the right-side of the right "Shift" key. Every other keyboard that I've ever used has a Shift key that extends to where that key is located. When I'm using the other keys (the numeric pad, arrow keys, "Home", "End", etc.), quite often I'll reach for that Shift key, and hit the \ instead - 'very annoying... If that one key wasn't there, this keyboard would get five stars from me. For those of you that will reply that this one problem doesn't warrant a one-star review, I disagree - it is VERY frustrating to have to stop working to delete the \, when they could have simply put that key where it is on most other keyboards...

title: Had to return it due to connectivity issues
text: I got this internet radio and tried it for a few weeks. At first I was happy with it - the sound quality is quite good, it seemed pretty easy to set up, and I was able to find my favorite NPR station streams as well as connect to my Pandora stations. But after the first two weeks or so, I started having problems with connectivity. - I'd come home from work and the thing would be on, not playing, with "error connecting to network" or some similar message flashing on the screen. The best way to solve this seemed to be to turn it off, then turn it back on, and then it would work (for a while). - While listening, it frequently stops playing in the middle of a song. Then the display says either "Buffering" for a few minutes, or more frequently, will actually say "Connecting" for up to five minutes at a time! This happens, on average, every 4-6 minutes. The thing is, I have a wireless router upstairs on the same floor as the radio (Apple Time Capsule) and the wireless signal is quite strong. The other devices that connect to this router never have a problem with connectivity - devices that include a Roku box, a Chumby, my iPhone, my HP netbook, my Macbook, etc. The problem with losing connectivity started infrequently but got worse and worse over the past two weeks or so, to the point where I can't really listen to music on it at all anymore. So I'm returning it. Too bad, because in terms of looks, sound, and basic functionality, it had everything I wanted.

title: An upgrade from my previous Nuvi!
text: I previously owned a Garmin Nuvi 360 which I loved. I specifically need a GPS that includes Bluetooth, since I use it both for directions and for hands-free phone use (which is rare, but important when I need it). I loved my 360 and used it daily until just a few months ago, when the Bluetooth suddenly stopped working. After troubleshooting with Garmin's tech support, it was determined the unit would need to be sent in for service, and since it was out of warranty, the flat charge for service was $79, which didn't include insured shipping costs. Well, do the math. Obviously, one can acquire a brand-new GPS for not much more than $79, so I started shopping. That's how I ended up with my new Garmin Nuvi 265T. And I LOVE IT! I'm almost glad that my old unit went on the fritz, because it gave me an excuse to upgrade to this newer, fantastic unit. The 360 was great for accurate directions, easy to see and read display, and consistent Bluetooth (until it broke). Here's how the 265T is even better: - Smaller, lighter, and thinner, but with a slightly wider screen. - No "antenna" on the back to flip up and fiddle with - it just works. - Uses my existing mount (from ProClips), so no change to that was necessary. - Includes FREE traffic notifications, which so far seem to work pretty well. - When you power it on, it seems to bypass the warning screen that you need to "Agree" to quicker, and then shows a simple display: Where To, and View Map. On the 360, if you didn't do anything else, it would sit on the menu indefinitely, but the 265T automatically switches to map display after a few minutes if you don't select anything else. Basically, you can start your car and just forget about it, until you need it! The traffic feature is ad-supported, so occasionally very small banner-type ads appear on the display, usually offering coupons for local restaurants etc. They are quite small and not intrusive in any way, so I don't mind them. I guess there's also an option to upgrade to a paid traffic service that would not include ads, but I don't see a need for that for my own use. In general I am thrilled with Garmin products, and this Nuvi 265T is no exception. What a great deal, and a nice early Christmas present for myself!

title: I May Not Know Much, But I Know I Love These!
text: I'm not an audio expert by any means, but I know what I like and I have owned many, many pairs of headphones in the past. Noise-cancelling, non-noise-cancelling, earbuds, headphones, in-ear, out-of-ear, surround-ear, you name it. It seems like headphones and headsets are kind of an obsession of mine. I use larger headhpones such as these Sennheisers primarily for playing video games on my computer after my toddler has gone to bed, and occasionally for listening to music (also on one of my computers). (When it comes to my iPod, I generally use something smaller and more portable, such as earbuds.) When I took the HD201 headphones out of the box, I was first amazed at light they are. They seem to weigh almost nothing, though they don't feel flimsy by any means. I tried them on, and they were immediately very comfortable. They surrounded my ears comfortably, and the adjustable length on each side allowed for a perfect fit. I also noticed that the cord on these is nice and long, which is a plus. So far, so good. So I plugged them in for the real test. WOW. These sound GREAT! It's really kind of amazing to me that Amazon can offer these for under $20. I read the other reviews and paid attention when some reviewers said that they weren't loud enough, or sounded funny on "s" sounds. I did not find that to be the case for me. They sound just fine on all types of sounds and music, at various levels, and the volume is not a problem. Pros: light-weight, comfortable, great sound, amazing price Cons: too big for my taste to travel with, since they don't fold I kind of wish they had an attached microphone, because then I'd never need another headset for gaming! However, for listening only, these are top-notch and I was very pleasantly surprised by the terrific quality at such a low price.

title: Cable too short!
text: These are really, really high quality earbuds, especially for the price. The sound quality is actually pretty amazing. I had a middling-quality pair of those "Inked" earbuds attached to my laptop at work. The sound quality was always disappointing, but I had sort of assumed that it was probably due to the laptop sound card, etc. Then today I attached my new Sony Fontopias and wow...what a difference! Yes, they have bass boost, but not so much that it overwhelms the music. These headphones are also surprisingly comfortable. They aren't the typical in-ear shape that gets jammed all the way into your ear, but there's a little more to them than the default "sort of hang in the outer part of your ear" that you get with the default iPod earbuds, for example. I like the hybrid, in-between quality and they fit me pretty well. They're not noise-cancelling, but the sound is so good that I really don't notice other office sounds (not even my disgusting cubicle neighbor who eats cookies like the Cookie Monster and sounds completely disgusting - now you know why I need to listen to music at work!). I'm so happy with the sound quality and comfort of these headphones, I'm willing to give then four stars in spite of one very major drawback: THE CORD IS RIDICULOUSLY SHORT. I have NEVER seen such a short cord on any pair of headphones, earbuds, headset, etc. that I have owned. I measured the cord from the jack to the point where the "Y" that goes to each individual bud starts, and it is barely 2 feet. TWO FEET! People, that is SHORT. So I'm going to go to Radio Shack at lunch today and buy an extension cord/adapter. So unless you're going to sit right next to the source you are connecting the headphones to, whether it's a computer or MP3 player or stereo, you'll need to add the cost of an extension cable to the price. Trust me - it's way too short as sold, like it wouldn't even stretch from my iPod in a backpack to my ears if I was walking around. Otherwise, awesome headphones.

title: Portable, Quality Means for Listening to Music
text: I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone. What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use. The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired. There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged. Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.

title: Connects With Ease
text: I have several flat screen televisions in my household. But for those times when I need to connect a laptop or something else to the flat screen, an HDMI cable is needed and a very good choice for the task is this HDMI from Talk Works. Six feet in length, this cable is designed for relatively short distance connections. Both ends of this HDMI are the same, so it doesn’t matter which end you use on which device. title: Secure Connection and Made to Last
text: In the information age in which we live, electronics are part of our daily routine. Sometimes, it is necessary to connect electronics and a HDMI cable like this one from SIREG is ready to help. Heavy duty in construction, this cable is designed to connect devices like laptops, monitors, projectors, etc. You simply plug in one end to the device you’re sending data from, and the other end to the device you want to send to. title: No Cords, no Noise
text: A mouse is a must for most people. Unless you use a laptop or some other computer that already has a built- in mouse, you need a way to navigate and if you want to eliminate messy cords, a good option is this wireless mouse from BreSii store. I’ve used other wireless mouses, but this one is better. It’s wireless by way of Bluetooth, which makes connection about as simple as it can be. You just plug it into the usb on the laptop or desktop pc and your ready to use. The mouse fits comfortably in your hands and is easy to use and control. There are no lights on this mouse or sounds made, but it does what you need it to do. On the subject of sound, this brings me to what I consider this device’s greatest attribute: It’s quiet! You can’t hear the clicking sound, like you can with most others. This is great for those who get irritated listening to someone in another room, constantly clicking away on their mouse. With the silence of the clicks, there is no distraction. This is something I wish more manufacturers offered. A computer mouse is a must- have item. If you want a better mouse that functions intuitively and keeps quiet while you work, then this wireless mouse from BreSii is the tool for you. It hooks up to most any computer or laptop and will navigate your way without cords or sounds.

title: No Batteries Needed and Cool Lights
text: Navigating on a pc screen requires a mouse of some sort. They have come a long way over the years, with more features and more comfort. One that is great for those who like to add a little color to their navigation is this wireless mouse from PEIOUS. Shaped for your hands, this mouse is comfortable to hold and click. You can change the lights to different modes and even shut them off completely, if you prefer. I consider this feature a plus, as I hate having to search for batteries when the need arises. To conserve power with this mouse, there is a switch to shut it off. Plus, it will automatically shut off, to preserve power, if there is no movement for several minutes. This is good because, with regular use, you will need to recharge this more than you realize and saving power makes a difference. Computers need a means for navigation and that requires a mouse of one type or another. You could go for the boring, ordinary mouse with buttons to click and nothing more, or you could have a little fun and get this wireless mouse from PEIOUS. I vote for the latter. It might only be a mouse, but the lights and the elimination of batteries make this a standout mouse and one I recommend.

title: It Works, but There are Some Issues

title: Give Your Monitors the Raise They Deserve

title: Protect Your Electronics from Harm
text: When you own and use many electronics, you need a place to plug them in- something that goes far beyond the standard 2 plug wall socket. A surge strip is ideal because it not only serves as an extension cord, it also helps protect valuable electronics from harm. And a good tool for the task is Tripp Lite 6 Outlet Desk Clamp Surge Protector Power Strip. UL listed and with a long cord, the Tripp Lite 6 Outlet Desk Clamp Surge Protector Power Strip is practical and useful for most home office needs.
