title: Pay the extra and get rid of ads but find out if it gets rid of ads in games too.
text: I have NEVER hated an electronic device more than this one. I don't know why it doesn't show that I purchased this in 2022 (and also in 2010 - before Version 1 died). I hate it, I really hate it. I detest Alexa and all the things she doesn't do but get in the way of letting you do what you want. I hate her. I LOVED my previous FIRE the ads were just a few seconds long and I could live with that. But to play my favorite Spider Solitaire game I've had ads go on as long as 10 minutes, I've had it forget to navigate back to the game and I end up having to go home and locate the correct version of Spider I was playing. EVERYTIME I open the thing It is pure HELL trying to get to what I want. For example, today all I kept getting was movies. I'd go back to home, and it would still show me movies, I turned it off and back on - more movies. When I did a search for either the book I'm currently reading (Spare) of course OR my favorite Spider Solitaire, Alexa kept displaying some kids Blue's Clues music that didn't have any of my search words in its name. After a number of tries Alexa finally found my game. If I pay the extra to get rid of ads will that include all the ads every 10 seconds on any game, you play so you can get your points and move on with the game? All I do is play this ONE game and read books and now I go through hell to be allowed to do it - between Alexa and Ads the device is barely usable. Oh and get this - I was eating in the dining room (I live in Senior Independent living but I'm VERY competent on computers} I was in the dining room reading Spare when suddenly Alexa decided she should show me how it sounded with audio and Harry started reading it to me at full volume until I figured out how to turn the volume off. It startled me and a number of others in the room - I was seriously pissed off. I could do this on my computer, but I always use my kindle when I'm doing 4 different breathing treatments that takes over an hour or when I just want to curl up in a chair and read or every time, I get hospitalized due to lung issues. How can I get rid of both Alexa and the ads? I'll pay whatever it takes. I really only have a few years left to live assuming I don't get a bad case of COVID or Influenza (I have a weak immune system) and I don't want to waste it on Alexa getting lost or screwing around with ads and games.

The only time I need a smart anything is when I'm in my car and need directions - Siri does that quite well most of the time and I don't need to buy anything else. In my home I have two computers, my iPhone and television. All are pretty smart and keep me well informed on news and weather. I have enough noise in my life - I don't need a device that just adds scratchy noise. As far as music streaming Sirius is a huge waste of money so I stopped that service and decided my hundreds of CD's and/or an MP3 player can play all the music I want to hear. I don't need any more complications in my life and I'm sick of trying to get devices to talk to each other - and the echo is the worst example of this.

title: Good Picture, Poor Camera and Support
text: Hi! I was very excited about this camera, having used the GoPro exclusively until now. However, I have to say that I was extremely disappointed with the camera, the website support, the smartphone apps, and the PC software. I found the camera manual extremely short on important info, such as what I could and could not do while the camera was attached to my computer via the USB cable. There are no instructions anywhere (that I could find) for using the Connect app. I guess they figure people will just touch the screen in various places to see what happens. I was surprised to find that I could record from the Connect app, as info online said that all I could to was "frame" camera shots. In addition, the camera itself did not work well. The Storyteller software did download and install the latest firmware. Here are some of the things I encountered: 1. The camera would "hang" regularly, as in every time I used it. The only way to "reset" was to remove and replace the battery. 2. Bluetooth communication only worked about 50% of the time, using iPad, iPhone, and iPod. 3. I often had to "reset" the camera (battery re-install) for it to be recognized using the USB connection. 4. Record OFTEN didn't work!! I tried to demo the camera to several people and it would not record unless I re-installed the battery. 5. The camera often would not STOP recording! I would slide back the record switch and the RECORD light would remain on under it and on the bottom of the camera. Again, the only resolution was a battery re-install. I could find no help for ANY of these issues on the website. I am VERY frustrated by the fact that they do not offer telephone support. The Storyteller software is terrible, and very lacking in support. It is necessary to eject the camera every time its configuration is reset! This is very frustrating when the camera was only recognized by my computer on a seemingly random basis (I tried all my USB ports and even a different cable!). I like many things about the Contour much better than the GoPro. However, GoPro has the industry momentum, and if Contour wants to slow that down and gain some traction of its own, their product will need to work better and be much better supported. I think the Contour is a better camera, but the few problems I had with the GoPro were resolved quickly and easily with the information they provided. I hope this product gets better. Until it - and the support - improves, I can't use it or recommend it to anyone else! :) hb UPDATE: Received a call from Contour Tech Support. They "schooled" me on the fact that everything taking place in this camera requires the SD card. There isn't even a little on-board memory. Thus, if the SD card doesn't work exactly right, neither will the camera. Without an SD card working perfectly, all you have is a piece of hardware! They suggested that I format the SD card with the utility at [...] (SD Formatter), and then re-format in the camera. I have already sent back the camera, though!

text: I'm hard to please when it comes to wireless earbuds. I've got a dozen or so mostly samsung and a couple of random purchases. But anker's battery life blows them all away. My phone's microphone is not functioning well, so I use ear buds pretty constantly. I would have to charge the other ones daily, sometimes more than once. With these I'm charging the case about once a week and the buds about once a day. And they are usb-c, so that helps immensely with travel and only having to bring one type of charger with me. I was a little nervous about getting a renewed pair, but these have been perfect.

title: Sort of worth it
text: *Update* after trying to use these for a few days, I'm disappointed. They are great except that they won't stay in my ears. There's nothing to hold them in place. They are okay for emergency use, but only if I'm using just the right one and I'm laying on my left side so it stays in. I've got several versions of Samsung wireless earbuds. I get a new set about every other year. The case on these is about the size of two samsung charging cases put together. It's just massive. But it charged quickly and the wireless charging works just fine. I called my mother to test the call quality since she is the most discerning about my earbud call quality and she was impressed at the quality for the cost. My galaxy buds were a refurbished buy from Best Buy and she could never understand me when I used them (no one else really had a problem hearing me with them). The galaxy buds live has good sound and call quality, but very poor battery life and comfort in use. They always popped out of my ears if I smiled or laughed and they pushed against that little flap and caused pain. So far, these little things are doing pretty good. I have weird shaped ear canals so the left one didn't hold in very well (but it almost never does with any of these) but, the right one is holding in good. I'm not thrilled with the shape because it's hard to know where to line it up, but for the money, I'm sold.

And the buttons are marked and with 3 individual buttons so it's easy to know which one you're pushing without looking. I also love the shirt clip, minor as that may seem. text: Horrible customer service. Not quite ready software app. Ordered two direct from Wyze. One was defective, with a purple tint to the video. Followed advice on their support forum to clear it (night vision on/off/on/off), move the case away from the magnet, update the firmware. Nothing worked. Tried calling "we are experiencing high call volume...unable to take your call...try email". Filled out the web form, attached the photo, 5 days later, no response. I guess I may have received a defective unit, but now I can't even get any support. Software app OK, but one key feature not quite developed. These are indoor cameras with motion detect alerts. I can't disable alerts based on my schedule. There is only one daily on/off allowed. No accommodation for morning evening routine, no accommodation for weekday/weekend schedule. So, with my alerts off for the afternoons only, I'm forced to have alerts on in the morning with contact beeping most of the day on weekends. So, yes, these work, are inexpensive, include some cloud storage. But they don't work well enough for me to pay to replace the defective one. I'll have to keep looking for a better solution.

text: My previous wireless keyboard, the Logitech K800, had stopped working, yet I needed something I could control from bed. Basically I got a great deal on a 4K display TV, which I'm using as a 3d monitor. I use this keyboard to easily search YouTube or control VLC etc when watching movies & shows in bed. The extra mouse keypad on the side is the real reason I bought this, I didn't want to use a small nib (some keyboards have small red "button" in the center of the keyboard to move the mouse pointer) to move the mouse pointer or try to use a wireless mouse in bed...so this worked out great, and actually does work great. title: A pleased long-time user
text: Although this review may seem to be "a little late", I do think that my experience with the earlier model of this Sony is appropriate. I bought a KDS-60A2000 in January of 2007 so I've had it for a few months over a year. As most of you will recognize, my unit is a 60" SXRT from the previous model year. Like many of you, I did a lot of Internet research before settling on the Sony - it was very highly rated by a number of sites. The final straw was live viewing many sets side-by-side on the same program from the same source - it was a no-brainer - the Sony had at least as good a picture as any Plasma in the store and the price couldn't be beat. I use Verizon's FIOS fiber optic service and have the unit hooked up through my home theater audio. The picture - indeed the HD experience - is simply awesome - especially live sports - like ice hockey. I did "tune" the picture using the DVE (Digital Video Essentials) HD optimization DVD and it remains the sharpest, most accurate picture that I have personally seen (including the high-bucks plasma sets). I've had absolutely no problems of any kind and there have been no regrets on purchasing this set. Another tidbit: I also purchased a Logitech Harmony 880 remote control and am able to control the Sony, the Verizon HD receiver, a Yamaha home theater receiver and a Sony upscaling DVD with a single click. It's programmed via the Logitech Internet site (using a USB connection) and can handle about any peripheral you might have. I've got a bowlful of unused remotes now. It's a little pricey at $150 but it has contributed to my HD enjoyment by simplifying the mechanics.

title: You really need this remote
text: Like so many others with multiple remotes, I view this unit as a very attractive alternative to a sixpack of remotes. A single button turns on (in sequence) my Sony HDTV, Yamaha receiver, and FIOS DVR/receiver. Or, alternatively, the Sony, receiver, and Sony DVD - depending on the selection. It even switches the input on the receiver appropriately. A single button turns off whatever units are "on". And one of the best features is the ability to re-program the remote via the Logitech website if/when something is upgraded or replaced. The only downside is that (obviously) a "universal" remote can't select EVERY option that may be available with the manufacturer's OEM unit. But those options tend to be little used ones. Another peeve is that sometimes I must shake the unit to get the display to light up. Otherwise, I don't see how most folks can get along without one. I really like mine. UPDATE (4/3/2013) I don't know if anyone will be interested due to the original date of this review, BUT just to show the utility of this remote, I thought I'd post this update. I recently replaced the previously mentioned Yamaha receiver with a new Denon unit and the Sony DVD was replaced by a Sony Blu-ray AND I added a Roku streaming box. I went to the Logitech site and created new profiles using the new equipment and now I control all of the new units just as well as it had controlled the original units. So, the point is - the remote can grow with your system when you change or add new equipment. Pretty great, huh?

title: Great power bank
text: I’ve owned this power bank for 2 years and it has been an exceptional and reliable source of power. I use it about once a month for a week at a time when I go RV camping to power my laptop. On its own, the laptop’s battery would only last at most 2 hours. But with the laptop plugged into the power bank, after I’ve used my laptop for 2-3 hours, the power bank charge has only dropped from 100% to as low as 77%--that extrapolates to 8-13 hours which is way more than I would usually need. So I no longer have to worry about my laptop running out of power. When I’m done, I plug the power bank into my RV’s 12V outlet and it recharges back to 100% in about 4-8 hours depending on how low its charge is. Between my monthly camping trips, when the power bank sits idle, it maintains its full charge without my having to recharge it.

The home screen is always slow to load (and sometimes freezes, which means I have to restart the Fire Stick). The only reason I have kept the Fire Stick is for Amazon music streaming, so the $34.99 cost seems okay to me (I bought the Fire Stick on sale during Amazon's Prime Day 2016). text: I received the Sonos Beam Shadow after winning a company raffle! What a great speaker! I already have my A\V set up for the TV so I am using this to stream music from my PC\Phone. The setup was very easy. I despise apple products so not sure if I can the the fancy tuning using Apple phone. But my Android connected and did it's thing with the Sonos app that was very easy to download, configure and use. The sounds quality is really awesome! I was using a small-ish BT speaker for playing music from my PC before while I WFH, but this soundbar took the music to a WHOLE NEW LEVEL! I wonder if I am going to work too hard and not get paid enough! :-D Sounds is deep and clear. The App allows to adjust max volume, bass and treble. I am really impressed!

title: Great little helper!
text: Perfectly sized and worked perfectly the first time. Transfer rate was great! No issues. Love the fact that it can read\write both the old and the new USB-C ports!

title: Really impressed after 2 years!
text: I have been using these headphones on and off for about 2 years. Received them from Otium as a replacement for something I don't recall, but at that time, I was really impressed with the sound quality and the NC feature. Changed jobs a few times and didn't really get to use these until covid and I started working from home. I rediscovered these headphone and was again surprised and impressed how well they sounded. I think the best part I like about it is that the sound is really well-balanced. It's not a studio quality headphone, but to listen to streaming music while working, with just enough bass and a good mix of mid and high is really a boost to the mind while working on complex computer codes. I like the ear pads because it covers my whole ear and the passive NC is very effective. I tried to turn the ANC on a few times, it lowers the volume and I think produces the counter frequency. I find that a bit uncomfortable. Overall material and construction is first class. I like the case and it's sitting in a shelf somewhere. I bought a little standing headphone holder from Amazon for cheap and the headphone cradles it quite nicely. Now if it could only give a neck massage too! ahahahaah!

title: Fantastic buds!
text: I used to think name brand products are a big hype! But these Sony buds have changed my mind. The sound quality is just absolutely FANTASTIC! I like a bigger bass on my music while I ride my road-bike and usually had to give up the mid and high freq for that. But these buds takes care of all of that without any equalizer on my phone! I am so blown away. I have Sony everything else: TV, Amps, Game console...not sure why I held up getting headphones. Oh wait, yeah, it was the price! But got a great deal thanks to Prime Day 2021! I am a proud dad of these gorgeous Sony buds!

title: Great mouse!
text: Just upgraded from my M570 and it was a very good decision! I got the white one, because, well, why not! I am not a Apple user though, just a hardcode programmer that likes to mix things up. This mouse also has BT connection but I am pretty sure I will use the USB. The feel is very comfortable and slightly heavier than the 570. It also has a "ribbed" surface so looks and feels different. Precision is just as good as the 570. So I would definitely recommend this upgrade!

title: Good solid product
text: Really well made. It is handling the fast charging pretty good as well. I got the 3ft versions and they are perfect for my need.

title: A great little - BIG speaker
text: I was really amazed at the sound! A tiny speaker the size of a soda can that creates a wonderful sound environment. I have it hooked to my Echo dot and the sound clarity is really good! And the bass coming out of the top is pretty precise. It's not the thundering bass but the correct one (to my ears). Takes up really a very small space. Set up was very easy. Pressed a button to pair it with Echo using Bluetooth. My phone and Echo both picked it up really quick. Can't really tell if it's going to work in long distance but I have no reason to doubt what the manufacturer is claiming. The only issue I had was figuring out how to use the volume buttons. I assume it's a quick press to lower or increase the volume but it's actually a long press. And then I am not sure how long to hold down the button to increase and decrease since there's no visual cue. But once I found the right volume it's OK. I can control the actual volume from the source as well. I got the black one so it sits very nicely behind a few Knick Knacks and not really visible. The sound is "surround" so it's not directional. I have not paired it up with a twin to test out the stereo effect. But that's not how I intend to use this speaker anyways. Very happy with this purchase. Kudos to the engineers for putting together such a nice speaker!

title: Spectacular! Maybe not the best quality check any longer.
text: Update July 7, 2021: Got the replacement today and tried it. Thankfully both side works. But it sounds HORRIBLE! Can't believe they took a perfectly engineered product and messed it up so bad! Not worth sending this back. Update July 3, 2021: Tried it for the first time at the gym and the right bud won't work at all! What a disappointment! The control that's attached to the right bud works so I know it's not the whole right side that's bad. And I got a second pair because the first one that I got a year or so ago is still working and sounds so good! Maybe they are mass producing these too much and forgetting to check for quality. I have asked for a replacement, let see if the new one is any better. REALLY disappointed! Update June 2021: Gave it a 5, now 4. Got a second pair because the first one is awesome! Not sure why but they changed the angle slightly of the wire where it attaches to the buds and it's making it not fit too snugly inside my ear anymore. Why change a perfect thing? The sound is still awesome! I want to keep the second pair because I am taking a trip overseas and don't want to without one if the first one breaks or gets "lost". 2020 Really perfect for sleeping in! I use the smaller of the tops and it rests very nicely just inside of the my ear canals. The sound isn't bad at all. I listened to a lot of soundscapes and brain-training stuff while I sleep so these are perfect. I am really impressed by these.The wires are pretty thin. I hope I don't damage them too soon. The price is very economical so I am not too worried about getting replacements. The right bud do sound a little different from the left, doesn't seem to have the same sound dynamic as the left one. The left one has more bass. But I am not going to complain too much about it since I am not planning to listen to any symphonies or grunge using these.

title: Very cute!

title: Purrrfect!

I like the blue light, makes me feel like I am in mission-control or something. I turn off the light (FN+ up/down arrow) after work. Kind of a nice mental way of signing off for the day. The keys are a little more raised then the usual keyboard. Since this is my first mechanical keyboard, I'll have to get used to it. I never really had formal training in typing but have been typing for many decades. I usually have to look a the keyboard out of habit. But with this keyboard, I seem to just don't have to do that anymore. I think it might be a combination of the raised keys, the clicking noise and the general feel of the keys. I am very excited with this keyboard and that's very unusual for me. I usually get excited with food and travel. Not typing!

text: Whenever I need to capture some action footage and i'm worried I may damage my good camera, I use this little guy. You really have to kick it in the arse to get the white balance set. But once it's set, she's a beaut'. Don't recommend it at all for low light. The color reproduction is in par with its price range. Also, don't rely on the audio unless your in an acoustically treated environment. The mic is not true stereo. The manual zoom function (on the lcd screen) gets skiddish on high speed turns. It's still reliable for 720p HD footage and can make your action cut scenes look good when you push the camera to its limits. It'll always be my in the pocket action shooter.

title: I'll be buying more of these!
text: This camera is a decent camera. What makes it great for me is it's ability to add-on. It has a powered microphone jack (3.5mm), an external av jack (3.5mm) which I use for headphones. It has a usb port, hdmi, and ilink. What I love even more is the way the camera handles colors and lighting. In low light, it needs a-tweekin'. Keep the scene lit properly, give'r a small adjustment, and you're good to go. The grain is acceptable and even adds a classic style to it. If you're making crisp high octane cinematic productions, you'll be very frustrated. But, this camera is great for field work and less formal production. I'll be getting more of these because I see artistic potential in its short comings.

text: I had been looking for earbuds that wouldn't continually fall out of my ears and started researching here on Amazon and was immediately drawn to these "earhook" headphones. I was a little worried that they might be uncomfortable because I have very sensitive ears but I was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable these are. I would have thought that after wearing them for a while, they would start to feel heavy wrapped around my ears but they don't! I just love the fact that I can wear them on my walks and while running around town and not have to worry about my earbuds falling out every few minutes. The sound quality is very good and it blocks out other noises because they fit (and stay) in your ears so well. There are three different size rubber ear tips to help you find the perfect fit and I've found myself listening to more music than ever because they are so easy to put on and take off that I've even started using them while working in the yard and cleaning around the house too. I would definitely recommend these earhook headphones for anyone who is tired of having their earbuds fall out of their ears all the time.

title: I love the Oasis. I love the Oasis so much.
text: Okay, I think that by now everybody who knows me knows that I have zero control when new iPads or Kindles hit the market (though I actually have managed iPad control!). Anyhow, the insanely expensive Kindle Oasis is introduced. I'm not gonna buy it because, seriously, it's ridiculously expensive and my Voyage is awesome, thank you very much. Then I get about $400 from the Big 5 Publishers settlement. And I cave. It's FOUND money, not real. All those reviews mocking the 2 ounce difference in weight, it weighed on me. I couldn't buy it, I couldn't be that person. But the $400 bucks lay in my pocket and it was shouting at me to just do it. It came today. Jesus Christ, it is the most beautiful e-reader I have ever seen. I literally gasped when I opened up the package. It is perfect. Am I saying you need to buy it? No. The Paperwhite is a perfectly good reader. But this? This is like heaven.

title: This is the best e-reader I've ever seen
text: It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is. I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G. First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2. The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top. Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about. Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery. Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.

title: Needed to wait a day before writing a review
text: I've been using the Kindle since it first went on sale, buying every generation as it became available. My 3G KT arrived yesterday, and let me tell you, I was not impressed. Nothing worked in a way that seemed at all intuitively. It seemed awfully clunky. But I know me and knew I just get used to this version. It's a really good reader. Once you figure out how it works, it does become fairly intuitive and works well. I'm used to buttons, where they are, how hard to push, etc., so this was new for me, at least on a reader. It took very little time for it to become an extension of my hand. If you already have the KK, you don't need this. You may like it a great deal, and think it's cool and all, but you don't need it. If you're coming from a K2, yeah, you kinda do. Regarding not being able to use 3G to surf the web on this device. I don't care. The web on the Kindle has always been pretty awful, so less accessibility is meaningless to me. However, if it does to you and you have the KK, don't switch. The one thing I really don't like is the fact you can no longer rotate your books to landscape or flip it upside down. When I'm in the middle of a book and running out of juice I flip it upside down with the plug on top and that's not doable with this. I'm sure that's something that will be addressed in one of their updates. All in all, it's a really decent device, and super great looking, but lacks the spectacular awesomeness I'd decided it had without ever having actually seen it.

title: My favorite hurricane weather radio
text: Living in Houston, I have owned several weather radios in this price range over the years. This radio is my favorite. I like the fact that you can re-charge it easily with AAA batteries (not included). I have found that re-charging with a hand-crank is too slow. Solar re-charging works well on most devices if you keep the device stored on a windowsill for the year so that it is fully charged during a weather event. Having the option to use three AAA batteries is great because the radio can be ready to use immediately. Another feature that I like is that no screwdriver is needed in order to open the compartment in order to change-out the batteries. This is important when evacuating and also when the power goes out. During Hurricane Ike, I evacuated to a friend's home. The storm made landfall around midnight or so. In the dark, it is hard to find anything, so it's good to be ready before the lights go out. I can remember lying in bed alone listening to my friend's radio (not this radio) in the dark as the NOAA forecaster reported the progress of the surge up through Galveston Bay and into the bayous, lakes, and streams inland. It was so helpful to know exactly what was happening to the area in which I lived. My friend's radio was a very expensive radio, and the main difference between her radio and this radio seems to be the reception. Hers ran all night with no interruption with reception. With this radio, I do have to turn the radio off and then back on if I lose reception to the channel. A really expensive weather radio would probably have better reception if you want to listen non-stop. For my needs, however, this radio is excellent and is the best that I have owned in its price range.

title: Excellent desktop computer
text: I have typically bought and loved Dell Inspiron desktop computers for use with school and business purposes and have been very satisfied over the years. When we were told that we needed Windows 10, I tried to download it to my old Inspiron but was not successful because my Dell equipment was really too old for a successful install; I really love the Inspiron and Windows 7. In February 2020, I bought a new desktop and had a really stressful experience. There was something wrong with the configuration, and the tech support people could not get the computer to perform properly. After many hours online with tech support, the situation started to seem hopeless. The pandemic began to become worrisome both here and in India (tech support), and I returned the desktop for a fully refund. Last week I started again trying to find a desktop with Windows 10. I didn't want to spend a small fortune for a computer that I use primarily for shopping, email, browsing, and, rarely, online banking transactions. I found this Acer after reading good reviews. Since my current desktop is an I3 and has basically the same specs, I chose this computer rather than the I5. One of my siblings told me that Acer has a long history of excellent quality and that I would be pleased. He was right! This desktop is great. PROS: Comes with Windows 10 pre-installed. Plug it in. It's ready to go. Norton Security is pre-loaded with a 30-day trial period. The computer is extremely user friendly. I had no struggles with glitches with any of the programs. Bloatware is easy to recognize and easy to remove (a Windows 10 feature). CONS: There really are no cons except that the "feel" of the plastic components is not as hefty as some of the desktops that I have used in the past (other companies). The plastic casing of the tower, the keyboard, and the mouse are beautifully designed but not quite as heavy as prior desktops that I have owned. That isn't necessarily a "con," and I like the keyboard, mouse, and computer case. Very attractively designed. MY RATING: 5 STARS The price, the ease of use, the beautiful performance -- a great buy!

title: EDITED: Not a good buy
text: I have owned two LG "budget" smartphones through Verizon, the second of which was bought during H Harvey when the first LG ceased working in the high humidity. Last week I lost the LG smartphone, and the only "budget" phone available was the Galaxy J7. It has been hard to use. For one thing, malware with ads almost immediately downloaded with eithr a Verizon or a Google Play app; Google Play Services are partnered with the phone. I called Samsung, which remotely took control of the phone but was not able to delete the malware. Second, and more importantly, the phone freezes A LOT. Despite the fact that the Samsung agent set all of the APPS and controls to optimum performance, the phone does permit many system overrides. Compared to the LG phones that I owned, this phone, while beautiful to look at, is not operating well. It is "buggy" and, consequently, time-consuming to operate easily. EDIT: I have been able to improve the performance of the cell phone by working to uninstall or disable the many, many apps that are pre-installed on the phone. Many are system apps but seem to serve no purpose. I also discovered that the Messages app is not quite the same as the Messages+ app and that some of the problems that I thought were "freezing problems" were user-error problems associated with the fact that the two apps delete messages differently. So I have upgraded my rating from ONE star to THREE stars because I have learned how to speed-up the response time of the phone. The popup ads are still a problem. As noted before, a Samsung agent took-over the phone remotely but could not remove the popup ads. The suggestions made by the Verizon agent did not remove the ads. I have been using FORCE STOP with the Game Launcher and Game Tools apps and hope this will correct the problem. Have cleared cache of the browsers and apps numerous times already.

title: Easy Move from Analog to Digital Over-the-Air Broadcast
text: I have been using a converter box and analog TV ever since we were required to make the change to digital TV. My 29" SANYO analog TV was a gift and has been a great TV. However, I have wanted to make the change to a digital TV, as well. Today I received the Samsung UN40H5003 TV and am very pleased. I also purchased the byone HDTV window antenna with a stand. Byone offers black, white, and clear antennas in a paper thin plastic. I bought the clear and mounted it on a byone stand, purchased separately. I liked the fact that this antenna offered a 20 ft cable since I needed to place the antenna in another room, and most of the antennas do not have cables longer than 10 ft. The TV and antenna arrived on time from Amazon and were packaged beautifully. The delivery service brought the large shipping carton into my home. If you live alone, you will want to proceed very carefully so that you do not damage any of the items in the shippng carton or the Samsung TV box, but you should be able to gently move the Samsung box out of the shipping carton. The instructions suggest that you assemble the stand first. Basically, a shell-shaped post slips onto the shiny black base and is secured using 4 screws. Once that step has been finished, the other end of the shell-shaped post screws onto the back of the TV. This step is the most delicate step of the entire process since the TV has be to placed gently, face down, on a table or flat surface that is covered by a cloth. The post will be attached to the back of the TV. Instead of using a table, I used the Samsung TV box, lying flat on the carpet, as the table so that the TV was never at risk of falling more than a few inches. The instructions are pretty simple as you begin to program the TV. Batteries are included with the remote, which you will use to turn-on the TV and scan for channels. The instructions suggest that all components (such as a DVD player) be added before the TV is turned-on. The single most important step is to be sure to select AIR as the source if you are not planning to use cable or satellite, etc. To do this, you press the button labeled Source on the remove. Then you will follow the prompts as they appear. Many of the prompts are pre-selected (highlighted), so you simply press the Enter button, which is positioned at the center of the up/down/left/right arrows section on the remote. There is a bit of a lag sometimes with the TV's loading of some channels. For that reason, it's best to re-scan often until you are sure that your TV has captured all channels within your viewing range. I don't know whether or not this lag is due to the antenna or the TV set. If you get an antenna stand, as I did, you may find it hard to get the posts that support the antenna into the base of the stand. Just keep working with them. Eventually they pop into place. The shipping carton was heavy, but the TV box inside the shipping carton was not heavy. I took the carton and box to the carpet and worked on the soft carpet, taking care to keep the TV set upright as instructed. Everything looks great, and I'm delighted that I am able to get a few extra channels that I had not received before. I live about 35 miles south of metro Houston. I want to add that Amazon shipped everything beautifully, as mentioned above. This TV is available at other stores, but I knew that Amazon would ship the item beautifully and would help me if there were any glitches with the shipping or delivery or return, if needed.

title: Not a good design for hurricanes
text: As many reviewers have written, the operating buttons are under the handle. They are very small and are marked with very small print. I had to hold the unit under a lamp and tip the unit to read the print. Having spent most of the night in pitchblack darkness when H Ike made landfall here in Houston, I don't think that this radio is really a great fit as a hurricane radio. It may be better suited to other kinds of weather events.

title: So far, so good
text: My neighbor Mariam and I are in our mid-sixties. Her husband recommended this device so that we could get help during long walks just in case Mariam, who has a heart condition, begins to feel bad. We have great Verizon coverage in our area, and she has been very pleased with her tests of the device. I didn't have any problems during the activation of my device: I thought that the steps were explained clearly by the Customer Service representative, who talked with me clearly and politely during our approximately 20-minute telephone call. I have not yet retired and like the fact that this device can travel with me to work and back. The only problem that I encountered was that initially I could not get the device to turn off. Consequently, I really couldn't figure-out whether or not it was "on" because I didn't know how to tell the difference between off and on. After several days, the "off/on" button worked properly, and I've learned that a voice speaks when it powers off and on in a way that is similar to the procedure that a cell phone uses when it powers on and off. Because of the problem above, the cell phone was actually "on" for several days. I didn't recharge it during that time. The unit has a small "ready" light that blinks to show that the device is operating properly. The device continued blinking all week, and I am re-charging the device now and hoping to restore the full battery charge, indicated by a steady green light on the battery indicator. It couldn't be simpler. I understand that a cell phone can be used to call 911, as well; however, it takes awhile for my cell phone to power up. It's not always easy to use. This device is simple and, hopefully, works as well as promised. I am pleased with the battery life and so far am pleased with everything. Hope it isn't needed but am glad to have it.

title: Beautiful smartphone and tablet / Good for first-time smartphone users
text: First, let me say that I purchased the Lucid 2 through Verizon, a fact that may be important to readers here who want to read reviews only of products purchased through Amazon. I am a very active Amazon customer but have a Verizon landline account; it was easy to move forward using my existing account. The Lucid 2 looks like a beautiful tablet. It offers two modes: a mode for the first-time smartphone user and a standard mode for the experienced user. I chose the starter mode since I had not previously owned a smartphone. The hardest part of the learning process was inserting the SIM card. You have to pop-open the back cover (also called the battery cover) using the same opening as the charger port. A new user does not want to damage the charger port, and it takes a little patience to be sure that you are handling the delicate SIM card and the removal of the back cover with proper care. After inserting the SIM card and battery, one is instructed to charge the battery. A blue light shows that the battery is charged. At a later time, you can add a battery charging screen (three are available and are stored within the smartphone) so that you can view the progress of the charge. There are video tutorials stored within the smartphone and a very fine series of help screens located at Verizon.com under Support. The smartphone feels very much like a tablet. I was able to watch movie previews by accessing the App (icon) to an online movie site. One of the main reasons that I wanted a smartphone was for weather-watching during hurricane season. There are various ways to use Apps (icons) that are basically shortcuts to features that you wish to use. The weather App also functons like a pop-up screen to give you instantaneous viewing of local time and temperature. My primary interest is the tropics, however, and I am able to access [...] easily. I will download the App from that site at a future time. By the way, you can use Voice to access sites on Google. You can also use Voice to display the name of a person or a telephone number (that you had previously entered); you can then touch the name or number and then send the call. Voice can be used for text-messaging as well. As a young senior (age 63), I really like these Voice features. I own a Canon digital camera and did not buy the Lucid 2 for photography. Those people who do use a smartphone for photography may wish to read reviews about this feature on Lucid 2; my understanding is that three or four other smartphones might be a better choice if photography is one of your priorities when buying a smartphone. I have read some online, professional reviews that criticize the Lucid 2 as being plain from a design perspective. I disagree. One reviewer -- whose opinion matches mine -- said that the Lucid 2 is gorgeous. It is. It is elegant and fun to use. UPDATE: I am having a lot of problems with freezing and lack of responsiveness. A LOT of problems.

title: Rubber covering over ports/plugs will not stay in place

However, the case is beginning to age and deteriorate -- possibly due to humidity when we lost power. title: Buyer Beware - the 4G is not as advertised

I will update this review if it appears that a fix is on the way.

title: Delighted with the Kindle Touch 3G
text: Before buying the Kindle Touch 3G, I visited a Target store to see and handle the different Kindle e-readers. I immediately loved the simplicity, elegance, and convenience of the Kindle Touch 3G. My sole desire is to read books easily without any distraction by the device that I am using. The Kindle Touch 3G is simple to use: "intuitive" is the word that ideally describes the operating features of this e-reader. You can swipe the page to turn (as with any paper page) or tap. Two toolbars disappear while you are reading, but both are accessed simultaneously with a simple tap at the top of the screen. A functional toolbar (allowing you to shop at Amazon, see battery status, etc.) appears at the top; a reading toolbar (allowing you to change font, etc.) appears at the bottom. Both are easy-to-use: just tap the choice you wish to make. You have only two buttons to click on a regular basis: the on/off button at the bottom edge of the device and the Home button (looks like a tiny speaker) located just beneath the viewing screen. You must hold the on/off button for approximately 7 seconds in order to power-off completely; otherwise, the screensaver will appear indefinitely. Other features are available and are easy-to-master; however, you can begin reading out-of-the-box if you have a Kindle on your PC. The system automatically duplicates your archived items. If you do not have a Kindle on your PC, you can begin reading once you register by entering the email and password that you use at Amazon.com. It is VERY, VERY easy to register: very user friendly. The screen and enclosed guide "walk you through" the simple process. The Kindle Touch 3G is elegant. I also bought the case ($39.99). Together, the two items are almost as slim as a DVD and case rented from a Red Box. The design is sleek, slim, and pleasing to use. Convenient? I found myself yesterday racing to an emergency room at my doctor's request. While waiting to be seen, I pulled-out my Kindle Touch 3G, began reaading a Sherlock Holmes short story, and had "no worries" about battery life or connectivity. I heartily recommend the Kindle Touch 3G to anyone with an older relative who loves to read and may not have WiFi access OR who needs larger type in order to better enjoy the reading experience.

title: Very Satisfied with the Kindle Touch Leather Cover
text: The cover is elegant -- well made and slim. It is perfectly designed to protect the Kindle Touch yet convenient to hold while reading. I bought a black cover because I had read that covers for tablets sometimes get scratched; I thought it would be easy to touch-up a scratch on a black cover. I plan to carry it with me daily.

title: Very happy with the Canon ELPH 100 HS (Grey)!
text: The Canon ELPH 100 HS is beautiful, and the Smart Auto feature takes great, no-stress photos for the user who has little or no experience with camera equipment. Before buying the Canon ELPH 100, I read reviews and did a lot of research online to find a point-and-shoot camera that I would enjoy within the under-$200 price range. There are a lot of good products from which to choose. I next went to Best Buy, Office Depot, and Sears to hold different point-and-shoot cameras made by the major producers: Canon, Nikon, Sony, Olympus, etc. For me, these visits to different retailers is an important part of the process of buying a point-and-shoot digital camera for the first time. Another important step is to learn whether or not the camera's software is compatible with your desktop computer. Because my computer is old (2006), I had to research compatibility with the different cameras that I liked. You can find the information at the product websites. Canon has a very user-friendly website that influenced my purchase considerably. I had XP Service Pack 2 on an older Dell Dimension E310. For the Canon, I had to download XP Service Pack 3. I ordered the camera from Amazon.com. From the moment I opened the box of the Canon ELPH 100 HS, I liked everything that I saw. The instructions are clear and organized well. Finally, I love the pictures that I am taking. No, they are not the same quality as those taken by friends and family members who own thousands of dollars worth of camera equipment. However, these photos are beautiful and fun to take. I am practicing now so that I will be ready to take photos at baby showers and graduations in the next couple of weeks. Is it easy to learn how to use the Canon ELPH 100 HS? It is VERY easy to learn how to use Smart AUTO. The sliding Smart AUTO button is on the top of the camera: you slide the latch to Smart AUTO, and you are finished. The camera "decides" whether or not to activate flash and also determines other settings. To learn to use all of the optional features (P mode) is fun but not essential to photographing great photos right away. Another reason that I bought the Canon ELPH 100 is that it is considered to be among the best in its price range -- and possibly THE BEST -- in low-light conditions. The only time the colors seemed to be distorted somewhat was when I took photos of pets sitting in a semi-darkened room while they were directly under the strong light of a table lamp. I found that the bright light from the lamp washed over all objects close to the lamp; the objects outside of the lamplight were fainter in color. Since then, I've taken the precaution of composing photos more carefully so that I am not creating a spotlight effect. I read that the ELPH 300 could be a better choice if you plan to use the video features a lot. For me, the video features on the ELPH 100 are fine. While in Playback (viewing photos that I have taken), I am learning how to use the displayed menus to select options such as Slideshow and Erase -- so far, so good. While not as easy as Smart Auto, the menus are fairly intuitive. I have been very pleased. The sheen of the dog's coat, the warm expression in her eyes, and the mysterious, bold gaze of the cat -- all captured beautifully.

title: Good Speaker Unit
text: I have one of my Amazon Echoes hardwired to the stereo and set up in my living room. The speaker has nearly great sound, not top of the line but quite good enough to kick back and read while listening to music. I also keep this plugged in so I've only used the battery once. I got a couple hours and there was still power left in the battery. I like this. It serves my needs quite well.

title: Works
text: Every couple years I replace the rechargeable batteries in my Panasonic phone set. After two years the battery life begins to fade. These batteries went in, charged and are operating my phones just fine. I've left them off the base for up to 48 hours and still had power left to make a fairly long call. Well worth it.

title: Had to Hire a Handyman
text: Trying to get this together and installed was a nightmare. I am disabled so I struggle at a lot of tasks but this was just a royal pain. Glad I've only got a 28" TV on it, would be nervous if it were bigger or more expensive. Got the handyman out, he used some choice words, got it installed properly. Would not buy again. Handyman told me he wouldn't install another if I did.

title: Useless Emergency Radio
text: I have an older NOAA emergency band radio that's showing its age and has issues with the battery compartment so I picked up this as a replacement. My current unit is 5" tall with a 1" antenna and pulls in the emergency and NOAA forecast channel everywhere in my house. This on the other hand will not. I've tried it in every room. I've tried it out in the driveway to be clear of the structure though an emergency radio that only works with you exposed to the elements is kinda stupid. The only time I've gotten any reception on the emergency band was holding the radio over my head, one hand on the fully extended antenna and then I could only hear one word in three. This was completely useless.

title: Not The Greatest Covers
text: I really liked the skull & crossbones design, I wanted to use this on my new Lenovo tablet but the bezel was too narrow so I installed them on the laptop I use as a part time print server. There are three of these in a pack. I put the first one on. Note: you need to slide the door carefully open so you can ensure proper positioning. I tried to move the 1st one I put on and it just fell to pieces. I got the 2nd one in place and it works. This material is kinda flimsy so it takes a cautious hand to open and close without breaking the door off. The glue they used is quite sticky. I like the design, the quality is lacking. If your device sits in one spot and you never or rarely ever use the camera, these should do an okay job. For something used a lot I think these are too fragile and would break too soon.

title: Good Little DVD Player
text: Well, I've had this for a week or so now. It's honestly cute just because of its size. I've had books that were bigger than this is. The power cord is just a bit over three feet, that's a hindrance. I was lucky enough there was a plug just in range but an extra foot of power cord would be better. The unit comes with a set of thin but serviceable RCA cables. I have some pro level RCA cables I obtained when I worked for a TV station, springs protecting the cables at the connectors, super heavy cable and insulation. . . and when I tried them with this DVD player the weight of the cables literally pulled the player off the antique dresser I use as a TV stand but the picture using the included cables is fine, playback is sharp & crisp. The unit has a functional set of controls on the front of the player which are sometimes missing in this modern era. The remote is a little small for my hands and the layout is a bit cramped and wonky but it works as long as you're in the fairly narrow field that the remote and device can see one another. I've binged a few of my older DVD sets so far. The unit has a resume feature that picks up wherever you left off. Actually there's quite a decent set-up menu for the unit. Enough to get you going but not so much you need a degree in sound and electrical engineering to figure things out. My only complaints so far have been; 1 - the device when loading or searching for tracks can be a bit loud but while watching content its whisper quiet. 2 - occasionally it reverts to turning the closed captioning on. There's a control on the remote, 2-3 clicks and its fixed. 3 - the already mentioned too short power cord. Pluses are many. The player is supposed to be region free, I have no foreign DVDs to test this with. The small form factor means you can (within the limits of the cabling) put it almost anywhere. It easily fits under the corner of my large screen TV with room to spare. The display is orange, I don't know why. It's not attractive but it is easy to read from across the room (maybe that's why it's orange). It does have a voice reading function for people with impaired sight. It will read every control or function as you select them. Not a complaint and not a plus. Most devices have a single LED that stays on to let you know it's in standby mode and ready to go. This unit steps things up a notch. When it's off it literally displays "OFF" on the screen for all to see. I've been quite happy with the functionality of this unit. I have a decent DVD collection I haven't been able to watch for a while so I'm pleased to be able to watch these old favorites, Serial Experiment Lain, Robot Chicken, Wonderfalls and many others. Edit - I received the instructions from the manufacturer and another user on setting this unit up as Region Free. I followed them, several times, reverting back to Region 1 each time. When set to Test - Region 0 (supposedly the region free setting) Region 1 discs become unplayable! See the image I posted. The menus load but try to play any content and the message screen I shared "This Disc Not Formatted to Play In This Region." is all you get. Manufacturer was unable to offer a solution.

title: Beautiful Screen, Does Not Have a Qualcomm Processor {Edited 05-17-2021}
text: Edit - I'm leaving the original review below but. . . Rating dropped to two stars, not sure it even deserves that. Don't buy this tablet. It's truly horrible. I can't go a day without Lenovo's own built in software; screen assistant, dolby, etc. crashing. This won't run casual games like Angry Birds 2, even trying to browse the web is a painful chore. Chrome lags horribly with only a couple tabs open. The display might be nice but when you can't even reply to a YouTube video without the keyboard disappearing and taking forever to reappear, often I have to clear the memory just so the keyboard will stay on the screen. Less than a year old and I hate it. I don't even want to try a warranty claim because I just don't want another slow, kludgy, poor quality tablet. I would not recommend this tablet. I was on my third replacement Fire 10" tablet and the same issue started happening again. I wanted no part of a 4th replacement so I decided to get this Lenovo M10 Plus. It was a recent release, had good specs and the price was comparable with the latest Fire 10" (that I had NO intention of even considering). One big selling point was in the Amazon description which stated "Throw in seamless Qualcomm Snapdragon octa-core processing. . ." Imagine my surprise on getting the tablet running CPU-Z and discovering it does not have a Qualcomm processor. CPU-Z reports a Cortex A-53, Lenovo's website says (as does the system information) that it has a Media Tek Helio P22T. This didn't make me happy. Trying to contact Lenovo made me even less happy. But. . . I needed a tablet, I have a tablet, I'm going to keep it. Simple as that. It does have a really sharp and clear screen. Color reproduction matches my laptop pretty well. I like the side firing stereo speakers. The remind me of my old Samsung 10" tablet that had speakers in the bezel that were aimed at your face. These are a close second. The Dolby Atmos controls take a while to tweak but sound reproduction is above average. I'm a little disappointed at how restrictive Lenovo is with Android 9. My settings menu, even with developer options turned on, I look like a strict business product that the corporation doesn't want the employees messing around in. Performance is ok, this isn't a gaming rig and it shows. I tried Castle Wreck which I play on my Galaxy S9 phone and it ran, horribly, but it didn't crash. But again, I needed a tablet because I'm disabled and spend a lot of time flat on my back. I watch videos from several sources, surf the web and my casual games, cribbage, backgammon, etc. run fine. I had to get a case for it. The tablet screen is slightly bigger 10.3" vs my old Fire's 10.1" but the tablet itself is significantly smaller than the Fire. It's thinner, lighter and the bezels are almost non-existent. That, plus the incredibly slick aluminum back made holding the tablet while laying down difficult to say the least. Found an affordable 3rd party cover that does what I needed. All in all? The screen is stunning. It runs everything I need it to though not all I wish it would. Price was right and it had a full year warranty. It'll do.

title: Drastically Increases Size of Tablet, Poor Magnets {Updated}
text: I tried my M10+ tablet for a day without a case, I only use it in my bedroom and it's stored in a pocket on my bed rail. I just couldn't hold the slick sides of the tablet and the small bezels just screamed I needed a case. The one from my defunct Fire 10" tablet wouldn't work and let's face it, this was the cheapest option I could find. I didn't care about the magnetic on/off function. I just wanted a case to make it easier for me to hold the tablet and something to protect the screen was needed as well. The magnets are weak, seriously cheap and weak. They don't hold the cover closed unless it's laying flat on its back and then it's gravity and the weight of the entire cover. I put the tablet vertically in my bed rail pouch and in either orientation (cover in or facing out) it doesn't really sty closed. Maybe after it breaks in after a few months but the magnets themselves are not going to get stronger. They barely hold now. I don't plan on traveling with this. . . I don't plan on traveling period, so this case does enough. It's easier to grip though it takes an extremely thin and sexy modern tablet and bulks it up to look like something from years ago. Small price to pay. I don't like that the slightest movement causes the magnets to disengage and I can see the tablet come on while closed and in my bed rail. I've adjusted the self-timer on the screen to shut off sooner than I normally have my tablets set just to save battery life. The inner lining is a soft either felt like or microfiber material so the screen won't get scratched. The case has enough texture to make gripping it while laying in bed (adjustable bed) much easier than the aluminum table alone. That's what I needed, that's what I got. Better magnets would really have helped. I really haven't used the foldable cover to make a stand, I don't sit or use a tablet where that would be useful. Again, I bought this because: 1 - It is held by tension on all four corners and nothing else. Some cases for this actually cover the bezel area which I tried years ago on a Samsung tablet and absolutely hated the design. 2 - It literally was the most affordably priced cover. The same seller has several different colors and designs, a couple I'd have preferred but the plain black of their own products saved me a couple bucks over a colorful design. 3 - Access to all the ports, speakers, microphones and controls is well done. Not 100% happy. . . maybe 75% pleased. It'll do. It was way cheaper than the Amazon brand cover I had to buy for my Amazon brand tablet. If all you want is a cover to add grip to a slippery tablet and something to protect the screen from scratches this will do. I think that covers a perfect TL:DR "This will do." Update - Review dropped to 2-stars, the magnets in the cover were almost never turning the device on or off. The cover would never stay closed. The cuts/thin places that allowed the cover to be bent into a stand after a week became so bendable the cover would flop open leaving the screen vulnerable. I have returned the cover. The TL:DR is now "This just won't do."

title: Clear, Solid Glass
text: The 90mm solid glass ball is as far as I can tell clear and without flaw. It's a little hard to keep clean and to keep fingerprints and dust off which are very noticeable when doing up close photography as in the examples I posted. I used a flashlight and a cigarette lighter in my samples. The stand this comes with is. . . okay. I worry that it being metal it might scratch the ball if you torn or move it while on the base. The legs are plastic and feel a bit fragile but will do for displaying the ball or using it in photography. I think the base is a standard tripod thread so it might mount on a standard tripod. I haven't tried this. There's a case that comes with the ball that's just big enough for the ball, if it were a little bigger you could put the included cleaning cloth in with the ball but you cannot. This can be quite fun for photographers or anyone wanting a large crystal ball for gazing or just looking at.

title: More For Looks Than Protection [Edited]
text: When was the last time you broke a remote? I can't remember going back 30-40 years. Maybe one? So, you really don't need to protect a remote which is good because this is pretty thin and doesn't offer a lot of protection anyhow. It does add a bit of a cosmetic upgrade which isn't bad. However, no matter how you position and reposition it the buttons become a little mushy with the cover on. As you can see in the 2nd picture the buttons are below the level of the cover. It isn't pressing on any of the buttons but it does give them a soft feel when accessing them. Occasionally I've had to press the power twice to get everything to turn on. What this cover does not address which id should is the roundness of the back of the remote. The rubber does add a bit of traction to the shape but just reaching over and pressing the power button is difficult, The remote rolls. If they had added a bit of squaring off material to make the case sit still so you could use it without having to pick it up, that would be a game changer. Keep the remote from rolling and wobbling on the table. How about that for an idea? I will probably keep the white one on for a while. I like the contrast and it matches the color of the work table I have my junk on. The black cover that came in this set. . . will remain unused. Remotes don't need to be protected, all the cover does is look nice'ish and make changing the battery a pain in the butt. Yeah, it was a pain to get on, it's going to be just as bad coming off. I hope the battery lasts a LONG time! Edit - I got tired of this cover making pushing the buttons on the remote difficult. It was annoying. Every button had to be pressed hard, often twice. The cover offered no real protection and, as I suspected, was a pain to remove. I've done so and tossed it. Not worth the hassle.

title: Anker Makes a Good Cable
text: I come back to Anker products time and again. No cable is perfect and when they're plugged and unplugged repeatedly daily and left with a rather radical bend close to the plug, it can't be avoided, eventually they all fail. Anker cables just fail well after most others have given up the ghost. If I can get close to a year out of a single cable for my tablet. Which, as mentioned, is used and abused daily I'm okay with it. Anker is also a company who will stand behind their warranty and has made things right for me without a lot of stress and argument. Sometimes I'm taken in by a better price but I always end up regretting it and going back to Anker. They work. They last. They stand behind their products.

title: Better Than the One I Bought In 2014
text: I bought the original Fire TV Stick in 2014 when they first announced it. I used it on and off but we had cable and a DVR so I put it in a drawer. Recently I had some financial setbacks and canceled all the cable services. At about that time Amazon sent me an email offering a major discount on the new Fire TV Stick with Alexa integration. I bought it, delivery took a while and was even delayed beyond the promised delivery date. Installation was cake. Plug the wall wart into an outlet, plug the HDMI extender (recommended for better streaming) and USB power cable into the Stick. Mine oddly wasn't preregistered to my account but that took only a few minutes time to resolve. The longest time drain was downloading and applying the numerous firmware updates that were available. That took the better part of an hour, hour and a half or so. Once done and running everything's been fine. Any streaming quality issues I attribute to my cable company constantly needing to work on the equipment in the area. I often had problems with the cable TV quality dropping or cutting out entirely. The new Stick is a bit snappier than the old, it's got a bit faster CPU though, sadly in five years the storage hasn't been updated. It still has the same 8gb the original came with. Alexa integration is nice, though mostly good for asking for specific shows to be played or asking for the next episode to be played before waiting for the onscreen prompt. Getting the weather displayed as on a Show is a bonus. I think the best part of the whole purchase is the Stick's remote controlling the power and volume of my television keeping me from needing two remotes to watch TV. With the bargain price I'm glad of the purchase. I don't think I'd have bought it at full price but I'm glad I did when it was for sale.

title: New Kindle is New
text: I've been buying Kindles since the Kindle Keyboard was known as the K3, a long time. The PaperWhite is the Kindle to buy. It doesn't have all the lights and features of the defunct Voyage or the Oasis but at its price point it can't be beat especially as you can often find them on sale for a good discount. Now water resistant (not waterproof) that adds a feature from the much more expensive Oasis. They've also made the bezel and screen the same height so it's smooth all the way across the face. This looks nicer but it's also much easier to clean now there are no deep corners for dust and debris to get into. Touch screen is nicely responsive. Lights are even and comfortable to read with. I don't see any dead/stuck pixels. Other than that this is a Kindle PaperWhite, you really can't go wrong with one of these for your reading needs.

title: Fits, Works
text: Magnet turns the device on and off as expected. Case is, for now, square and true the cover doesn't drop or wiggle. Fit's the new Kindle like Amazon designed it to fit their device. It's nothing new or exciting but it protects the device and operates the magnetic function of the Kindle just as we'd expect. The cloth gives nice purchase to hold the Kindle. Pleased with the color and purchase.

title: Stylish Speaker
text: This speaker seems more designed for more modern music somehow. Maybe it's how current music is mixed. I'm not sure but newer music like Billie Eilish has much more bass than music from the 70s, Led Zeppelin, etc. and even heavy metal from the 80s such as Iron Maiden. The older music, streamed from the same source, comes across flatter with a duller sound. It doesn't sound bad just newer stuff is clearer, has sharper highs and clearer bass. The speaker is stylish with a nice modern design. There are rubber feet to isolate the unit and keep it from moving. Controls are. . . difficult to use. They're on the back, out of the way. They're dark although somewhat intuitive. Wireless connectivity was easy although the connection drops and reestablishes a few times a week at random times. Issues with the speaker. I use this in my bedroom. The power/Wireless light is on the front and is a brilliant bright blue. With no other lights in the room this is almost bright enough to read by. I've had to resort to putting a piece of black duct tape over the light so I can sleep at night. The speaker has a narrow band where it sounds good; with the volume low the tone is flat and dull. Crank the volume and something, I think the passive bass radiator, buzzes horribly. Inside that volume window where the sound is good it's pretty darn good but it has it's limits. Not sure if it's my app or the speaker but every, single, time it loses wireless connection for more than a few seconds my volume, bass and treble settings reset back to flat defaults. It's only a mild annoyance but it's there.

title: Not Really Impressed
text: I have had several water resistant shower speakers and none, not one, my $600 Samsung Galaxy phone isn't. . . nothing is waterPROOF. It's a lie. Many advertisers and sellers like to claim waterproof status but what they mean is water RESISTANT. IPX7 means a device can survive immersion, up to 1 meter (3 ft 3 in) depth for up to 30 minutes. Let's also be clear here; those tests were with pure, likely purified, filtered water not highly chlorinated pool water. Not salty sea water. Not brackish lake/pond/river water. And also not water containing soaps, shampoos and conditioners. All that. . . stuff in every day water is going to reduce the effectiveness of the water resistance of any device. So, I unbox this and it's light. Lighter than just about any speaker I've used. I look at the specs. . . 3 watts. THREE watts of power? Okay it's supposed to be primarily used in a small enclosed indoor space but it also says it's great for camping, hiking and general outdoors stuff (please, don't blast music when you're hiking, wear headphones, show some respect and restraint). I've never seen a non-novelty speaker that was less than 5 watts. It feels light and cheap and thin. The suction cups; they send two likely expecting one to fail. Neither worked. The best I could get with the cup wet with soapy water, alone, no speaker, stuck to a mirror for maybe five minutes. I can't get these suction cups to stick to my desk. No worries, my shower has a shelf. I turned off my oontz Angle 3 and connected this to my phone using Samsung Music as a player to take advantage of the Dolby Atmos and excellent sound (only PowerAmp sounded better of the half dozen players I tested and PowerAmp is a paid app only) quality it offers. I guess if you wanted noise in the shower this would work. Sound quality was about as bad as you'd expect. Distorted bass, harsh highs, muddy midrange. No EQ settings I tried made this sound good. It's just not worth it. You can for just a little more money get far better sounding water resistant speakers. You should enjoy the music in your shower or bath not suffer with it.

title: Good Quality Memory Card
text: Always liked SanDisk products. Have used them for years and never had an issue. This worked great with my mom's new 8" Fire tablet once it was formatted by the device. Got this on a Christmas sale so even happier with the bargain. Would recommend.

title: Secures Your Camera Nicely
text: I had no issues getting the backing material off. I used a pair of precision needle nose tweezers to peel the backing and to place the cover. Even with my shaky and arthritic hands I was able to get the cover 99% where I wanted it and just about perfectly level. I checked camera functionality and this cover doesn't seem to interfere in any way. Adhesion seems fine. I didn't touch the sticky material and I got it in place on the first try. If I'd needed to reposition or if I'd fumbled and gotten my fingers all over the adhesive I'd have discarded the cover and tried again. That's the good thing about having a multi-pack. Operation is okay. The cover slides open and closed with reasonable ease. It stays open or closed, wherever you put it. It doesn't interfere at all with the closing of my HP Pavilion gaming laptop. I'm going to put one on each of our tablets as well. I'm glad I finally got a cover. Have wanted one for peace of mind for a while now.

title: Nice Backdrop
text: Hung this up at a Halloween party as a decoration and everyone started using it as a photo background. I've used the reverse side to moderate success as a dark backdrop for photography. The size is great, covers a lot of area. Considered using it as a tablecloth as the product description suggested but just couldn't take the risk of stains or damage. Getting the wrinkles out was a bit of a pain. I don't have one and had to ask five friends before I found one with an iron I could borrow! Great for parties or just as a decoration.

title: More Fun Than a Wooden Container of Densely Packed Primates
text: Have followed Nathan on Facebook and Instagram for a while. Facebook even says I'm a top fan (I whirl in joy!) and his art has brought a smile to my face almost every day. I didn't get the chance to pre order (sorry!) but I just had to support the artist who makes me smile. As Spider Robinson said, "Shared pain is lessened; shared joy, increased — thus do we refute entropy." Strange Planet is the epitome of that quote.

title: Useful But Flimsy
text: Years ago I had a similar stand in aluminum that was too small for the tablet I had at the time. These are pale copies of that device. They work and my mother is delighted to be able to stand her Kindle PaperWhite up in it. It works with the case on but even pulling the silicone tray liner out you have to leave the cover of the case off to the side. Not really that big of a deal. The aluminum stand I had locked in position. You pressed the button that was the end of the hinge set the stand how you like it and it locked in place. These stands have some mild detents inside the hinge mechanism that hold the place you set. . . more or less. It's okay with a Kindle and gently tapping the screen to change pages but I didn't like how my 10" tablet felt in landscape mode and I decided not to even try portrait. So, good for light use and light devices. Somewhat flimsy plastic. Not sure how long they'll last but we'll see.

title: Loving My New Phone
text: I had a Galaxy S4 for several years. It was suitable and did the job. . . mostly. I was having some battery issues and my phone wouldn't update past Android 4.4. I was running into apps that needed a newer version of Android. I could have bought something cheap but I decided to treat myself and found the blue Galaxy S9 on sale for a decent price. I have to say I'm loving this phone. The 5.8" Quad HD+ Super AMOLED screen is GLORIOUS! I run this is high performance mode with the brightness cranked up. Games, movies, even YouTube and TikTok videos look amazing. The curved edge I worried might be distracting but honestly I only notice in a couple games. Sound is really good for a cell phone it has stereo speakers. Volume is more than enough. Performance from the Octa-Core processor and 4GB of ram have not struggled to run anything I've thrown at it. The camera is great. Maybe struggling a little in very bright light with a light colored subject. Otherwise, night mode gives great low light results. Video shooting is very nice with great slow motion results and a nearly unique super slow-motion recording mode at a mind boggling 960 frames per second is a lot of fun to mess around with. Battery life is good, I got most of a day is high performance mode and could easily extend it by cutting things back to save battery. The fingerprint sensor is quick to unlock and easy to use. A trick I found online to improve performance of the fingerprint sensor is to register the same finger more than once. It really works like a charm. The look is sleek and sophisticated though I'm protecting that glass body with a nice Otterbox Symmetry case. The only real minor negative to the whole thing is this weighs more and is larger than my S4, a little hard on my hands and pocket but really, it's worth it. I can't express how happy I am with this phone. I'm even buying props and things to use in creative videos and photo shoots.

title: Handy Case, Somewhat Fragile
text: This is something I've needed that I never knew I needed and, until I was offered it to review, I didn't know such a thing existed. I spent a few hours coming through my house gathering up adapters, SD cards, micro SD cards all in old clamshell cases, sitting loose in a drawer or in devices I forgot I had and had forgotten I had cards in them! Everything friction fits in this case, you just press things into place and they stay. In a couple spots I had to stop and compress the case itself because fitment was tight enough to flex a couple of my micro SD adapter cards. There's plenty of space for full size cards, micro SD cards but not any spots for mini-SD adapters. Granted I only have one and I've never had a device that called for it but they exist and I hate not having all my cards and adapters in one place. The case is quite sturdy except for the latches. Hard plastic in a stiff mount are a recipe for breakage. They should have been designed better. So, while it really is useful there are enough flaws to drop the rating a couple stars. Use caution when first inserting cards to ensure things aren't too tight and be wary of the latches they unfortunately feel fragile. And hope I never need my mini-SD adapter, I have no idea where I left it!

title: Okay Cable
text: Decent quality cable, very stiff and material is rough against the skin (worse between the toes, ask me how I know). Connectors on either end are solid for now with little to no wiggle. I get high speed charging using my Samsung wall wart. Will update as time goes by if necessary.

title: Nice Fast Card For My Galaxy S9
text: Class 10, U3 nice and speedy for burst mode, slow motion and even Samsung's amazing 960 frames per second on my Galaxy S9. Have had no issues whatsoever. Affordable, good storage to double my phone's capacity.

title: Expected Better Quality Sound
