title: Good for desktop laptop cooling
text: I had to replace my current laptop cooler. The fans were going bad (very noisy). I use this with a 17" HP dv9000t laptop with two high speed hard drives generating a good amount of heat. The laptop is a desktop replacement. If you use your laptop actually ON your lap, this cooler is not for you considering the open back on the fan. If you use the laptop on your desk, it is very effective, especially for the price. It is VERY quiet. In addition to the large fan moving a lot of air at low speed which reduces the noise of the cooler itself, it is so effective at cooling, the fan IN my laptop has not had to go to high speed since I started using it. This lowers the overall sound. Just by having my hands on the top of the laptop when I type, I can tell the laptop is running much cooler. The cooler is a third of the price of the last one I had, but more effective. It does raise the height of the keyboard up more than my last cooler, but not to the extent that it causes a problem. Happy with this purchase.

title: good mouse that doesn't quite fit my hand - yet
text: howdy y'all, i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*] for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ... - the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while. - the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self. - the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel. - the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*] - the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse. these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use. - the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*] - the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems. ***** the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons. this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it. ***** i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short. ***** rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd. take care, lee

text: I'm an old fart and have had telescopes for a main portion of my life. I love the sky and stars. Astronomy has always been my major hobby. I'd had Meade telescopes before and because of the name, I went with the Polaris 130. Wow!!! Way WAY better than I expected. Excellent manufacturing and machining. The optics are superb. When I took it out on my first night, I figured it would take a while to collimate the glass. Surprise!!! Everything was dead on. Impressive since the telescope was made in China, shipped across the Pacific to California, then to me in Massachusetts. The only drawback for telescopes such as this is the fact that they are bundled with cheap eyepieces. Uuugghhh! I knew that when I ordered this telescope and bought a decent set of Meade Plossles to go with it. What I can't figure out is the price. title: This is a bargain!!!
text: Xfinity sent me a new "upgraded" cable modem and it was a nightmare. After mucho hours with tech support and diagnostics, I was told my speed/performance problems must be due to my Roku TV, my PC, my tablet and my cell phone and that I should contact their respective manufacturers. Funny that I didn't have any problems with the old, obsolete modem Xfinity replaced. Well, maybe the frustration was a good thing. After researching, I decided to get my own modem and chose the Motorola. I'm glad I did. After I unpacked it and set it up, I braced myself for what I thought would be installation purgatory. Nope. I turned on the modem and watched it go through it's power up sequence. Then I turned on my PC and went to the browser. There was Xfinity's activation screen. Here you must be patient. You'll go through a few screens where the PC seems to hang/freeze and gives you prompts to retry. The modem restarts a few times during activation. When the modem lights are normal, just hit retry and all will be well. The whole installation takes about 5 minutes. No human interaction required!!! Don't forget to reset the modem's ID, password and network info. Performance is great. I can have my Roku TV (I stream everything), other TV with a Roku stick, PC, tablet, cell phone and magicJack all working at the same time. Amazing. Plus, this modem will pay for itself in 10 months versus the $11 modem rental fee I would otherwise be paying ad infinitum.

title: Nice little SW radio!
text: When I was a kid 50 years ago, I asked for a SW radio for Christmas. We got our presents on Christmas Eve and when I took it up to my bedroom, I opened a storm window just enough to hang the extension wire out. I was able to listen to stations all over the world. Russia, England, Japan, India, etc. Didn't matter that I couldn't understand anything but English. These were voices from around the globe! I felt the world was in my hands. AM and FM, too. Big dial. Yes, the radio was big and bulky and forget any batteries. Power cord was it. I bought this VITE just to see if SW would interest me still. I've only had it for a few hours, and it sure does. It's like my big, bulky radio was somehow shrunken down and forced into this tiny unit and with even more bells and whistles. Seems to be built very well and solid. Powered by 2 AAs. If you had a handheld transistor radio in the 60s, it's even smaller! Speaker is nothing to brag about, but so what? It's $20 bucks. Nice little SW. I might eventually look at something more powerful.

title: Definately worth the cost
text: Forget the Wi-fi. After plugging this cable into my PC and then my cable modem, online became an incredibly new experience.

title: Excellent protectors
text: Really nice power strips. Went through an all night thunderstorm with plenty of lightning. Not a flicker on my TV or DVD player, even when lights blinked on and off. Should I need to, will buy more.

title: You won't regret getting these!
text: Incredible sound. After my first Panasonic earphones went dead in the right earpiece, I tried several others and most wound up in the landfill. Sony, JVC, etc. One of biggest problems I had was even if a set of plugs sounded okay, I would get a splitting headache and I don't play my music loud. I should have stuck with what I knew. Got these and it was like the world opened up again. From bass to highs, Bach to Skynyrd, all encompassing and beautiful. Also, no headaches!

title: Terrible
text: Bought this after reading reviews. For benefit of the doubt, maybe mine are defective. Terrible sound, no matter which rubber eartips I used and I sealed them tight. Even when I adjusted the equalizer on my MP3 to what I thought was "acceptable", these gave me a headache after 5 minutes. Bought these to replace my Panasonic set which died after about a year but sounded great. I should've gotten another Panasonic set.

title: Impressed!
text: Surprised. Nice little speaker. Bass is nothing to brag about, but mids and highs are clear. Nicely packaged and it's great having the extension cable. I can put it and my MP3 player on mid volume and (I live in a small apartment) hear it my bedroom, bath and kitchen from my living room. Seems like the company cared and was fussy about it's product.

title: Excellent quality
text: High quality. Connectors fit like gloves.

title: Update
text: Incredible. I've heard sounds I never heard before. Skynyd's "Free Bird" is now a totally new song for me. UPDATE : They only lasted about three months.

title: You have to break these in. Takes a while but once you do, WOW!!!
text: Have some patience with these. I needed a new pair of plugs since my five year old Altec Lansings started falling apart. I tried many others as replacements, but none were as good as the Lansings, most notably on the bass side. I read the reviews about these and figured what the heck. When I first got them and fitted them to my ears, they were terrible. Why would Panasonic make this junk? 2 stars at best. Bass was horrible. But as time went by, I started to notice that not only the bass but the high end frequencies were getting better. Now I am more than satisfied!!! These even beat my old Lansings. In short, have some patience. These need a break in period. You won't be sorry.

title: Nice little case for my Coolpix S3500
text: Nice little case with a loop to mount on your belt. There's even a little pocket on the inside back where you can store an extra battery and memory card. Also, the amount of Velcro to keep it closed is very generous. Other cases I've used had a simple little not-so-secure strip. My Coolpix S3500 fits in it perfectly.

title: Not for Coolpix S3500
text: Have to give it three stars because I honestly can't say how it is. I purchased a Nikon S3500 camera and below the item, the battery was included in the "Customers who bought this item also bought..." Since my camera was the S3500, I assumed it was the right battery because it said it worked in a Nikon 3500. Nope. Too big and the contacts are wrong. I gave three stars only because I've had Nikon products before and they were always good.

title: Wish I could give it ZERO stars
text: A pure headache. A supreme instrument of utter junk. Out of a 6 drives, it finally worked on two (after a couple of hours of different configurations). There aren't any directions, so do I plug the power supply in first? Or the USB cable into the PC first? Do I power down, then attach everything and reboot? How about power up the drive, then plug the base unit into it? That worked on one of the drives. UUUUGGGHHH!!!! Also, when you do get the drive to power up, it gets hotter and hotter, and I mean hot. The only time it didn't was when the system actually recognized it. It was trial and error. I gave up after drive 4. One year warranty? No phone #. Just a little tiny sticker on one corner of the box that says "Cybertech." Talk about generic packaging. Don't be an idiot like me. Carefully read the reviews and get something with those that are positive. Yeah, it'll be more expensive, but it'll be worth the aggravation and temper tantrums.

title: Quick delivery, and what a difference!
text: I placed this order on July 11, and received it on July 15 with the weekend in between. Quick service from Amamax, the seller. Of course, I installed it as quick as I could. Wow!!! What a difference just this 2GB made. I have an HP All-in-One PC that came with 4GB and Windows 8, and it was like it went into turbo. I really wanted to get 4GB but with me in "economy" mode, had to settle for 2GB, bringing my system to 6GB. For the price (plus free shipping from the seller to boot), I couldn't be happier.

title: WOW!!! Great keyboard!!!
text: I've only had it since yesterday, but this keyboard is wonderful. The different colors are adaptive to different times of the day (and depending on the mood), and the large key characters are easy to see. The keys themselves are responsive and have both a nice feel and "click" to them. Well built and it's plain to see that a lot of thought went into it. The box says Win 7 compatible but I'm using Win 8 with no problems. Well worth the money.

title: Great product. Bad shipping box.
text: I've never had a problem with Sony discs, and these are same. The packaging was terrible, otherwise this would be 5 stars. The box was WAY too big and the plastic wrap around the discs broke and the discs came off of the spindle. I had a box full of scattered disks. I was surprised that only 3 failed.

title: Great for the price.
text: Don't expect Bose sound quality. There's only one little speaker on the right end. For it's sound, however, the speaker is halfway decent for it's size. Decent reception. The buttons can be a pain at first, but once you've had it for ten days or so, you get used to them in the dark. I wish Sony had added another speaker on the other end to make it stereo. Then I'd give it five stars.

title: No Coasters Yet
text: Must have burned over 100 DVDs with it hooked up to my Acer Aspire One. So far so good. All the DVDs have been read by other devices without a problem. Great little inexpensive drive.

title: Great watch...when it works...battery/phantom messages
text: Galaxy Watch 4 Classic LTE. Bought 10 months ago as an adjunct for health and training goals. Watch features impressive, but some notable issues. Battery Life: is less than a day even with screen off and minimal use. Many software glitches with notifications, specifically phantom Voice Mail messages and incomplete messages from applications. Watch sent for repair once and now going in for second time. Not confident issues will be resolved. The other features, especially health and exercise work well, but the frustration level is terrible

title: Solid mount for Wahoo Bolt
text: Excellent mount for Wahoo cycling computers. Quality materials and construction. Easily mounts to handlebars.

title: Refurb unit gives muffled audio
text: Purchased as a backup, which became my primary BT phone headset after my other unit flew out a car window at 70 MPH. Refurb unit functions well except the audio is muffled compared to the identical unit this replaced. Good for price paid

title: Keys stopped working otherwise exceptional
text: Purchased October 2017 for use with Android Phone. Design and footprint absolutely wonderful. Easy to carry, keys easy to use (yes, there is a placement issue for touch typists). The BK03 was a go to accessory whenever I traveled -- didn't need to bring a laptop for writing long E-mails or editing documents on the fly. Suddenly in September 2018 some of the keys stopped working. Tried unpairing and re-pairing the device...tried pairing it to other phones and tablets...nada. Not much assistance from iClever. So the keyboard is kaput after about a year. As I purchased the keyboard on a discount, I'd say it was worth the price. Will I replace it? Probably not for the full retail Amazon price. It's a shame too, this is probably the best BT keyboard "ive used with my smart phone -- just not durable over time.

title: Be gentle, be kind
text: Bought 2 of these and one cracked inside my NEW mobile phone. Very dicey removal.

title: Five Stars

title: Wobbly view of maps -- great if you can shake in syncopation DO NOT BUY
text: I had to purchase this in a hurry when my el-cheapo universal mount cracked just before traveling. The kit is constructed well and I've had no problems with the suction cup falling off the windshield -- YET. I'll reserve judgment until the summer months when windshield-mounted holders fly off heated surfaces.. Here's my issue: the bendable arm isn't rigid enough to prevent constant wobbling of anything in the mount. My lightweight mobile phone is unreadable even on smooth roads. My old cheap (under $10.00) model was far superior in keeping my device in view AND readable. Update: 1/8/2015. After less than 2 months the mount connection to the gooseneck FAILED. flimsy plastic piece holding the tension spring flew off and now the mount cannot be attached to the gooseneck. TomTom doesn't want to know ....at nearly $25.00 this is a complete rip off.

title: Bus Basics -- save big money

title: Great Product - One minor flaw
text: Purchased this to have remote control of my iPod Classic when playing through my home audio system. Remote works great and overall I am satisfied. The ONLY flaw is the audio quality when connected through the unit base. Audio is low and distorted when connected via the base...solution, plug audio into the iPod headphone jack. For the price, this product is an excellent choice.

title: Great little echo dot. LOVE the clock and temp display, wish it came in more colors.
text: We have 3 echo's in our house and this is my favorite. This has taken the place of a regular echo dot and alarm clock in my daughter's room. We love the clock display and the fact that it dims when it is dark in the room so it is not crazy bright when she is trying to sleep. We also love the fact that it displays the temp when asked. What a neat little dot. Wish it would have come in other colors as well, might have purchased them to replace the other 2 in the house.

title: Great size and nicely built

title: Cute, but not very functional!

Also, the scroll button for the volume does not turn easily and when it does it takes a LOT of turning to change the volume up or down. Returning this immediately - Hope I can find something both cute and functional!

title: Won't work with Rode Go Wireless to connect to GoPro
text: I am not sure if this product works for anything else, but it does not work as an adapter for connecting the Rode Go Wireless lavalier mic to a GoPro Hero 7, despite fitting the connector specs. I thought I would try it since the price was <1/5 what GoPro charges for their adapter, but I knew that it was possible it may not work. I plan to keep this adapter anyway since I may need it for something else in the future. The build quality appears nice and the connections fit accordingly.

title: Got this after a tip from an online forum - best advice I ever took!
text: This little filter was made with witchcraft. It is fantastic at bringing more clarity, color richness, and tone to my images. It basically lives on my 35mm prime lens. I plan to get other sizes for my other lenses. Great filter for the money. Doubt you could be disappointed with this purchase.

title: Great inexpensive prime lens for crop sensor
text: Can't beat the quality/price ratio with this lens. It ain't great for macro (min. FD leaves a little to be desired, but there's another 35mm Pentax lens for that), but this little fantastic plastic excels on my K-3 in every other way.

title: Works
text: It works. It is plastic. I got this to try some extreme macro shots with some old lenses. The threads fit well. Good value for the price.

title: Guess I got a bad one...
text: I ordered this lens about 2 years ago and right out of the box the AF motor sounded like it was 'too tight'...made a high-pitched, almost abrasive sound whenever it would focus. Being the first prime lens I got for my T2i, I didn't suspect anything at first. After about 3 months, the AF stopped working entirely. I sent it off to Canon to fix under a warranty claim and they had it back to me in about 3 weeks. From that point, it worked for about another 8 months before reverting back to the same state of disrepair. I resolved to just use MF on it, however, just having this lens attached to my camera nearly instantly drains even a full-battery....must be some kind of short in it. Regardless of the failed mechanics and weird behavior, the glass was good and I really liked the way it handled indoor light....great colors and warm tone, nice FOV. Nonetheless, this lens is basically worthless to me now and just sits in the top of my closet. Because of this experience, I am very weary to invest in more Canon lenses and have since only purchased Sigma lenses, with mixed emotions there as well. One day....I'll get a good one...hopefully.

title: Not bad as a replacement kit lens, but don't expect too much
text: After reading some of the other reviews, I've concluded that I got one of the 'soft' lenses...meaning that the majority of the time, images don't turn out as clear as they do/did with the Canon kit lens. But, honestly, what do you expect for $200 glass? I'd say it's worth it for the price if that's your budget and you need a kit lens replacement. I've heard great stuff about Sigma and wanted to give them a shot with something small before getting their 10-22mm or other more expensive lenses...this, however, didn't fully convince me that they're on par with Canon, but I appreciate the potential they provide for competitive pricing.

title: Works, but Lens Cover sucks
text: This case does what it says as far as keeping your camera/lens dry, but the lens cover gets scratched way too easily and absolutely robs from the clarity of the image. For $70, it's worth it to be able to bring my DSLR along in the kayak through rapids and so forth, but I didn't expect to sacrifice so much quality on my images. Also, the finger slots for the lens gets in the way if you have to attach your lens to the body through the lens port, not to mention what an invitation it is to dust/debris in your camera from having to attach the lens from inside the case.

title: Not Bad, Not Great
text: For the price, it's ok. If $50 is a big deal to you, I would advise not getting it as it's not really something of top quality. I've had this for about six weeks now and have had a little fun with it, but the construction seems to be a little loose as there is already 'debris' underneath the glass....weird since I keep it in the provided pouch and inside my bag whenever I'm not using it....a disappointment indeed. Nonetheless, you can have some fun with shooting a limited range of stills, although it takes a little bit of a learning curve to compensate for the focus lag when shooting fast moving subjects.

title: You Will Not Regret Buying This!
text: If you have a mid/high-end DSLR, or shoot lots of video....then this is the card for you.....it performs unbelievably better than my class 4 and 6 cards...seriously, if you think you get good quality with those classes and don't think it's worth spending a few more bucks on the big daddy class 10, you are a fool, yo! And go with Sandisk, no one else....

title: Lacks Consistency...
text: I bought this backpack for my gf last year and it was so awesome that I just bought one for myself. Side by side, mine is a tad bit smaller/tighter. I used hers for a few trips and was able to easily put my 19" HP laptop in it (despite other reviews regarding this), so I felt very comfortable ordering the same pack for my new 16" laptop, which barely fits in the new backpack. My only guess for this is that NG has outsourced this bag to a different (Chinese) manufacturer, as the color is slightly off and the size is tighter/smaller. I'm sure, overall, NG is reliable, but who knows how well they're watching the tolerances in the manufacturing process. In my experience, Chinese manufacturers allow much more tolerance in their process than typical American manufacturers. Nonetheless, it's a great pack, with lots of pockets, rugged integrity, and very comfortable.

title: Great Laptop for the Money!
text: I ordered this laptop about a month ago and have been very impressed with both the performance and the look/feel of the notebook. This is my first ASUS after bailing off of the HP bandwagon for the last few years. The slim design and light weight package are very attractive. The keyboard gives a nice resistance when typing (almost as if it has some kind of magical 'type-assist'#....as well as plenty of space between the keys. The other comments regarding resolution are somewhat right, depending on what you're doing with it. The Video Magic software from ASUS allows for enhancement for videos, and I've been impressed with the output. The only disappointment would be if you do a lot of work in PS CS4...the resolution isn't the best for fine-tuning high-res photos. Not really a big deal. The only other downside is that my webcam is upside down. Jeers to ASUS for not yet addressing this problem with this model on their website. I used a 3rd Party workaround and it seems to work now #in most cases#. Otherwise, great speed....loaded CS4 in under 30 minutes and it boots Photoshop CS4 in under 10 seconds, twice as fast as my duo core HP. Overall, for the price, this laptop is hands-down a GREAT value.

text: Received this item today.. Well packaged, Amazingly easy directions, Like others i took the easy or lazy way out and went this way rather than piece together myself and safe 10ish bucks... OWC made a excellent kit that provided everything needed.. IF you run into the error of the usb drive not reading the correctly installed update file.. Remove the .PUP from the save file ( change name ) then move it over to the usb.. Worked for me the .PUP was causing the issue of it not locating the file originally... Took roughly 20ish minutes to remove the drive, install new one, download the software, and trouble shoot that remove the pup part to get it up and running... Once your into the system working again id install all your games again then go and reinstate the licenses just to make sure they all work properly with no issues... It turned out to be that the first bank of SATA connectors of the MB were nonoperational. Secondly, I kept getting error messages that the USB device(wireless mouse, keyboard),were drawing more current than the connector could supply. There is virtually no repetitive wrist movement when using this mouse...but...after long-term heavy use, there is a lot of wear & tear on a person's thumb, which is used to click the primary mouse button. Sure, you can reverse the buttons, but imagine your hand over the top of this mouse. You'd use your index & middle finger together to roll the ball, probably, while your thumb clicks the primary button, and the secondary button is clicked with the ring finger or palm, not parts of the hand that have the most dexterity. I'm left-handed, and have the buttons reversed, but some games & application don't recognize the reversed buttons, so the primary mouse button becomes the one I click with my ring finger or palm, and that's not good for gaming. Also, if this mouse has an alternative to a mouse wheel, I've never been able to find it, and, again, lots of games incorporate the wheel into the controls, so that's an issue for me. Eventually, the ball, which is normally smooth as silk to operate, loses its finish and begins to feel less accurate, harder to roll & rough...but that doesn't happen for years. In fact, I can't remember when I bought the one I'm here to replace. Despite the minor annoyances, which are few, this is a comfortable, sturdy mouse, and the best mouse I've found for my left hand. Plus, no carpal tunnel surgery. What's that worth?

title: Wow! No more, "What'd they say?"
text: Thank you to all you wonderful Amazon reviewers. I'd never purchased a Bose product before, with the exception of possibly headphones at some point in time. We know the Bose sound is legendary, but I never really needed a Bose radio or CD player. The Solo caught my eye because I love my flat screen TV, but the speakers are only so-so at best. Like many other reviewers, I have trouble understanding some dialogue on TV. It's fine as long as there is someone around to annoy endlessly by asking "what did they say," but watching TV alone, I miss big chunks of the story & plot. The doctor says it's just "one of the vestiges of old age." Oh. Another one of those. Thanks, doc. So, I wondered if the Solo speaker might help, and thanks to all my hard-of-hearing contemporaries here (or should I say THANK YOU), I saw all the reviews promising that I wouldn't have to ask "what?" every 2 minutes any more. I could jump for joy after hooking up the speaker and giving it a listen, although my doctor would probably advise against it. On my TV, unlike some others mentioned here, the TV speakers work along with the Solo speaker, so it's easy to mute the Solo and hear the difference between it and the TV speakers. It's amazing. The sound is rich, and big, and crisp in a way that my surround-sound system isn't. Most importantly, in answer to my wildest hopes, I can understand every single word of dialogue, even Christian Bale mumbling behind his Batman mask. No kidding. The Bose speaker took 20 years off my age, and reduced my waist by four inches. Ok, I am kidding about that. As if all that isn't reason enough to get one of these gems, it has to be the simplest piece of electronics to hook up, set up & operate. It's simply two cords, one to the power outlet, and the other to the TV. They include all the cables in the box: digital optical, HDMI & RCA. Plug, plug, power. That's all. The remote is four buttons: power, mute, up & down volume. It's hard to believe that such intricate, complex sound can come from such a simple device. Thank you, Mr. Bose, wherever you are. Not only would I highly recommend this to my friends, I think everyone with a flat-screen TV owes it to themselves to get one. Seriously. This is the audio-visual experience I thought I was already having with 5.1 surround system.

title: Perfectly Fine Keyboard, but Be Aware of What You're Getting
text: I don't really feel the need to criticize the keyboard since it is, and does, everything the manufacturers say, but I'm back to Amazon today to buy a different lighted keyboard and I'll keep this one for emergencies. First, the positives. The keyboard is sleek and visually appealing. I love the blue back-lighting. It would probably be a good keyboard to take along for use with a laptop, and that may have been the intent because the condensed keyboard is laid out like a laptop keyboard. That, unfortunately, is also part of the problem. The layout of the keys makes it difficult for me to use, with keys like the backspace, which I use a lot, surrounded by other small keys such as Home & End, which sends your cursor all over the page when you hit them by mistake. It's probably not the best keyboard for people who do a lot of typing. In fact, I plugged in my old keyboard to write this review. For the price, I am not displeased, and it will be a good standby in case I need it, but for long-term use, a different keyboard is probably a better choice.

title: Use it all the time...
text: The last time I tried a device like this, I couldn't get it to work. I didn't have much faith in products that transmit an FM signal to my radio, but this product works like a charm. I use it with an iPod Touch, along with an app that tells me the best empty FM frequencies in my area by zip code. Once I found the right frequency, the device works amazingly well. It does drop out of sync for a few seconds sometimes, but that's a minor occurrence that doesn't present a problem for me. Much will depend on the location of your cigarette lighter or power source, since it may block some controls on your dash, but, again, it's a minor problem considering the great music I can now hear while driving. You can't beat the price.

title: Perfect in every way but one.
text: Have had this TV for about 3 years now, and it was one of the best deals I've ever found. I did a lot of research, and this model had everything I needed (at the time) at an unbelievable price compared to other brands with the same specs. The picture quality if wonderful, especially the HD channels on my cable. Every time I'm in a store with HDTVs on display, none of them seem to compare to the great picture I get on my Soyo. However, I've just purchased a PS3, mainly for the Blu-ray player, and realized I wasn't getting full resolution because the TV resolution goes to 1080i only, but full Blu-ray needs 1080p. I had bookmarked a review from 2006 saying there was really no reason to buy 1080p at that time, and I took that advise. That's no longer the case. If you don't care about Blu-ray (the TV does an amazing job with regular DVDs), then this is probably still a great deal. As another reviewer mentioned, this model had an update somewhere along the way. Mine is the older model with just one HDMI input, so perhaps they've updated to provide 1080p resolution.

title: Great Little Camera...
text: I was concerned about some of the complaints regarding short battery life, noisy zoom lens and an overall cheap plastic feel of this camera, but it was a great value & I decided to give it a try. Luckily, I havn't had any of those problems with the camera, and after several months, am perfectly happy with it. Yes, the camera has a plastic body, but it's been very durable while travelling and seems no flimsier than any other electronic device made today. The plastic body is one reason why the camera is so easy to take everywhere. It's light, compact & not a chore to haul around, which is nice. Rather than a short battery life, I have been suprised at the long life of the battery that came in the camera. I bought an extra battery because I expected it to run out quickly, but I've never used it. I've never needed to. During a 4-day weekend in the mountains, I plugged the camera in at night, and was able to record any time and every time I wanted all day long each day. The noisy zoom lens? I don't know. My model doesn't have a noisy zoom lens. I can barely hear it when I use it, and have never noticed the sound of the zoom during playback. Maybe it happens with some of them. Granted, the built-in microphone doesn't produce the best sound, but it's been good enough for my casual use of video. The video has been clear, sharp & colorful. Would I use it to record a wedding? Probably not. To record my mother's belly-dancing recital? You bet!

title: They work in all areas of my house
text: This is my second and third purchase. Bought these to get channels the cable companies want to charge you $10 a month for. I fooled them. This worked in my bedroom great so I bought two for the living room and guest room. They work great in all rooms with a bit of adjusting placement. I have to say that those who complain they don't work must live in areas where there are obstacles. I get 50 or 60 channels clearly and with Roku TV I get another couple hundred channels through streaming using this antenna. Please note that the 200 miles range claim isn't possible because of the curvature of the earth. 80 miles is about the limit on any antenna, so you won't be picking up signals from cities 100 miles away. Just to take another step towards cutting the cable, I ditched Comcast internet last week in favor of $50 a month T-Mobile Home Internet (which also works great at high speeds) recently available in my area, so these antennas are still paying dividends. I'm a streamer and this digital HD Antenna is a screamer!

text: So far. after a few months this cooling pad works great. Quiet fan. Enough motion to cool my laptop. Thick enough not to bend when I pick it up with computer by one hand. My Cooler Master was two thin and eventually squashed fan to the point of not working. Pretty lights are hidden though, but I didn't buy it for that. My only gripe is the way the configured the extra USB connector. Not on the pad. One side plugs in to the laptop and it has a universal connector opposite the plug in on the same wire. Kind of funky and it always has me guessing which one to plug in to my laptop. Hint. It is a tad smaller, which I have to look at both and size them up every time. I'm thinking of putting a dot o nail polish on the insert end so I can more easily tell at a glance. It is a constant nagging chore. I only took one star off but maybe I should have taken 2 stars off for the inconvenience., If you don't need the fan or your eyesight is better than mine, then no problem. Otherwise be forewarned. This is a constant pain. I went back and took another star off after writing this. I'd just as soon not have the replacement USB port.

title: UPDATE: Seller made good and replaced old earbuds after Windows 11 made them outdated.
text: UPDATE: Nrw ones work fine after old ones couldn’t handle Windows 11. Really good earbuds only half good now after Windows 11 update. They connect but no sound. They still work on my iPhone but not on W11. Contacted Tozo and they say its up to Windows to come up with a fix. Don't think this is going to happen since this has a been a problem since June. So if you ever plan to update to Windows 11, skip this product. I bought a second pair in case I lost my current pair (I've been known to do that) and now they are pretty much useless too. ---- Earlier Review: Bought the T6 because it was on sale for the same price as the T10 with more features and it is the new model, plus I like the case better. You can put it on a wireless charger and this is the reason I chose them. Really? $25 bucks and it goes on a wireless charger? My old Apple Airpods don't do that. The sound is impressive, much better than I expected. Also better than Apple airpods. I can only assume Apple's Pro model has also improved. On the T-6, I have to turn the damn things down sometimes. You can hear the symphony bass and treble and its full and rich. The controls are touch and work well once you learn them. Tap once to pause, again to play. Hold down for volume. Tap Twice for Forward on right bud and twice on left earbud for Reverse Also hold down for 10 count to activate pairing. The only thing I don't like about the Tozo 6 is how hard the magnetic airpods are to retrieve from the case. There is no easy way to find a grip to lift them. It takes several tries to get one, then the other out. Apple airpods can be difficult at times, but the magnet is stronger in the Tozo 6 and there is no logical spot to dislodge them with a finger. Still, I'm not taking off any stars for that. I think this is an excellent product. I bought these because I kept misplacing my airpods, I found them in the crevice of my recliner, but guess which ones I use now. That's right, the T6 Tozo. They really are impressive and well built. Can't believe they sell as cheap as they do--although I see price increases on the horizon. Thinking of buying another pair in case I lose these.

My guess is at least three hours, maybe four if you don't do a lot of heavy usage. title: Went with a cheaper Brand to see if it worked and It does
text: I decided to go cheap after seeing some online YouTube reviews because one of them compared a $3.99 antenna with a range of price point antennas and said it pulled in most of the stations with a few fuzzy channels. Couldn't see spending $50 on a Leaf or other models cause I tend to be cheap. If it didn't work I could always buy another. I read that the limit for reception is 80 miles because of the curvature of the earth and Amazon features a lot of Antennas that claim 100-200 miles, which is impossible. Also impossible, 4-K. Free view stretches the 80 mile limit too., claiming 130 miles. New ATSC technology is supposed to be coming out that can extend ranges, etc., , but you can bet it won't be in the $50 and under price range. I hung the Freeview near a window in our bedroom and it pulled in all the channels in our area including UHF, and most of them were crystal clear. The Freeview comes with an amplifier, which I think helps. I don't like draping the cords along the wall, but I draped it above the bedrooms patio door and to a window. It is sensitive to location and I found it didn't pull in behind the TV, when I wanted to see if I could hide it. . Depending on where you need to put the antenna, you may have better or worse results than me, but what the heck. For $16 bucks you can't go too wrong. My only suggestion: Offer it in white, please. All of these antennas seem to come in black. I don't want a black antenna hanging on a white or beige wall.

title: Changing my Review From 3 stars to none
text: UPDATE 4/14/21: I'm giving up on this watch. It's always something. The sleep mode is mostly better now but won't register some nights. Now the weather fails to sync so I have ghost clouds instead of weather forecasts for the week. When I try to sync it manually it just cycles and cycles for several minutes and still no weather. I've updated location to allow the watch full access and still nothing. DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME WITH THIS WATCH. IT HAS MULTIPLE ISSUES DEPENDING ON THE LAST UPDATE. Now the battery has gone from 14 days to 3 1/2 days after one year. PREVIOUS UPDATE: After switching to an iPhone this works better even though a previous update killed it on my Android phone. The Thing that irks me now after another update is that the sleep app is way off. Lately I am told I've been awake for 3-5 hours a night which earns me a 30 to 50 rating. Never got better than a 80 rating so far. They did include the REM sleep to the graph which is nice. Since they changed the app name to Zepp it hasn't really been the same. The few other things I use it for, steps and watch faces and time of day and compass work okay. Battery life is the best feature. The price has gone down $40 from when I bought it; maybe because of the Zepp app you have to use on your mobile phone. It's not the best. I bought this watch to use in counting laps while swimming, but the Covid has put the stops on that this year. It was the only watch in this price range--since reduced-- that offered a swim mode although it is GPS distance (miles) rather than laps counted. The battery lasts 10-14 days. My wife's Fitbit Versa 2 needs charging every couple of days. I don't leave the face always on. If you leave it always on, you'll probably have to charge it in 3 days. In the econ mode you have to tilt it to your face or click on the stem to make the face visible. A good trade off for not having to charge your watch all the time. My main gripe about this watch is that when someone sends me a text message, it repeats 3-4 times on my watch. This seems to be a problem with several of the Amazfit watches according to some of the forums I have visited to remedy the situation without success. It's annoying and difficult to see texts from others in the long line of repeat sms messages. UPDATE: Buying an iPhone to pair with this watch seems to have solved this problem for me. I tried the music mode and it works if you already have music playing on your phone. It will display the song playing, the Album or CD Title, volume control, pause and play, next and previous song controls. However if you are on economy mode, the music face disappears and you have to search for the music control again. I used the Find Phone and Found it easily, but your phone must have power obviously. It will ring or force volume higher if playing music, lol. UPDATE: This find phone function no longer works. Beware updates. It's like Microsoft. Everytime they update to make it better it causes glitches. If they could fix the multiple repeat sms messages and tweak the sleep mode with more info this would be a pretty good watch. Right now its only good. Would I buy it again? Maybe, if the swim mode is good. I'll have to wait to find out.

title: A really good laptop cooler, but . . .
text: Update 10/21/21: The thinness I talked about below finally did this cooler in. I was thinking about how long I'd had it without it breaking and . . . you guessed it. I picked up the laptop and cooling pad together with one hand as I'm want to do and the fan struck plastic when i squeezed laptop and cooler. The fan went non-stop while making a scraping sound. I slapped it lightly and the fan stopped. ---- My wife got me this for Christmas after I searched a ton of coolers. It's better than the Targus I had before which was too small and the cord short-circuited so laptop had to be situated a certain way for fan to work. The Cooler Master put the cord on the side of a small thumbdrive-like device which I hope will protect the cord connections. The fan is quiet enough and keeps my laptop cool, but it's probably the screened top and multiple larger vents on the bottom that let it air circulate better. Unfortunately the pad is made of plastic, is thin, and when you set it down on an uneven surface--like my leather couch-- it hums louder hitting the plastic. Likewise, when I pick it up with one hand I squeeze the cooler pad into the ban and get the buzz saw effect. Don't worry, its fine on your lap. I just have to unplug it when I set it on the leather sofa. Other than that minor flaw, I do like this cooling pad. It's lightweight and fits my 15 1/2" laptop perfectly. If you have a 17-inch laptop it may overhand an inch or so on each side.

Unfortunately I didn't have any spare monitors sitting around so this ended up being the most expensive component but was worth it as it fits perfectly if the width or length of your mirror is 24 inches like mine (24x18). I just removed the from bottom portion of the bezel so the screen can lay flat, no need to remove the back. Nice and bright too. Awesome.

title: Reliable source of variable temp lighting
text: Nice led panels that feel pretty solid! These little guys provide fairly even and diffused lighting with selectable lighting temp. I was actually surprised they felt as substantial as they did given the price point. I've paired them with generic NP-F750s and get about 2.5 hours at 100% brightness using these mostly for ecommerce and macro work. The only negative I have is that the stand these come with is absolutely flimsy and if you plan on using a battery bigger than the NP-F550, I'd suggest spending 10-20 bucks on some new base stands for these. I found some cheap table top tripods made of aluminum and work perfectly since the panels have 1/4 inch threads. Great lights and it sure helps that they are affordable.

title: Holy smokes the bass is amazing.....
text: I wont bore you with similes about the response, or speak to clarity, soundstages, v shaped tuning, etc. Go to headfi for that sound snob stuff. I'll tell you what I like about these: the bass response. Holy smokes these rattle my head. I know it is my imagination but I was just listening to liquid drum and bass, I honestly thought I felt the bass compression in my chest. Just like you might get when standing next to a row of large bass bins at a club. I had no clue you could get this low with ear buds. The caveat for me was I had to ditch the provided tips and got some large spiral dots. The new tips made all the difference. If you listen to any sort of EDM, you really should try these with proper fitting tips.

title: Bought because it is plastic, not despite of.
text: I purchased this precisely BECAUSE it has a plastic case. I like to get extremely familiar with ONE keyboard and only use that board for work and home. I have found this is best way for me to increase speed and accuracy. Whatever I have to type is only done on this 1 board. So that board has to commute to work with me everyday and as such I need it to be light weight. I have seen some complain about it being plastic but I think this is a feature not a cost saving measure. What are people doing to their keyboards that a hard plastic case doesn't give the durability you need? I mean this stuff lasts for thousands of years in a landfill so I am sure it can handle your office environment just as well as those heavier fire hardened/tempered steel or aluminum whatevers can. Excellent board that goes almost everywhere with me.

title: Prevents keys from bottoming out
text: Sometimes I like to really hammer on my keys as I type, especially as I finish a thought or am really happy with something I just thought of. This prevents the loudest sound coming from most mechanical keyboards regardless of switch type, the sound of the keys bottoming out.

title: Excellent caps for cherry mx switch mechanical keyboards
text: Excellent doubleshot pbt keycaps in a classic colorway. What's not to love? Shipping took forever but that was my fault for ordering right before the Chinese New Year.

title: Probably better to buy a cheap mech keyboard for testing
text: A little flimsy feeling, keys slide right out, no need for the key puller. Does what it says and allows you to test feel/sound of various mx cherry switches. I just picked up a gigabyte cherry mx blue switched board for not much more than the cost of this. Wish I had just done that instead of wasting money on this.

title: Works as described
text: Purchased because my wacom mobile studio pro (5 yo) charger was bent. This was a pricey but efficient replacement.

title: Worked for less than 1 year.
text: As I have to work from home, I had to make sure I had a good internet plan and modem/router. This provided reliable internet for maybe 6 months and now I'm being told I "need a new router" although this is one of the accepted ones on the list. Everyday when I wake up for work I have to restart the modem which eats 30 minutes into my workday. It randomly turns off during the day. They only have a 90 day warranty and when you call customer service after that 90 days, you're told to purchase a plan if you want to troubleshoot. Well what if I dont know if I want to troubleshoot? What if I want to ask a question? Pass on this product.

title: AirPod! I'm sure you would love this case!
text: I already dropped it like 15 times! This strong and great looking case works!!!! Love how easy to set it up on the case. Best $6 I spend this month!

title: Comfortable, awesome sound
text: Can blast music and can't hear it from the outside. Nice design, very comfortable. Only thing I would be wary of is these definitely slide off the head easily if you're moving around, at least for me. I wear these when I'm working, chilling, and that's it. I wouldn't expect to wear them working out or anything like that. Haven't tried the bluetooth much so I wouldn't be able to comment on the battery life, but the pairing was very easy. Just download the app on your phone and you're ready to go. I just wish the sound went a little louder ;)

title: Does what it needs to do.
text: Does what it needs to do. Affordable and durable.

title: Impressed!
text: Apple keyboard is light and smooth. IClever is light and smooth. It does the job! Last long on one charge! Smooth and buttons are so perfect! There's an on/off button to save energy. And battery life light that would tell you when it needs to be charged..

title: Good!
text: Good to have but didn't notice much!

text: This is my second one! I love the switch my first one lasted 10 years and it still works fine.

title: Great deal!
text: Great deal! Plenty of space and solid material! Love it.

title: Only Bluetooth INPUT
text: This is a flimsy but functional turntable. The speakers aren’t great. It’s advertised as “Bluetooth,” which to me signals you can use a Bluetooth speaker with it, but I should have read carefully that it was Bluetooth input only. I was hoping to digitize a record from my childhood with it by playing it through my computer and capturing it, but it will not work for that. It does have an RCA output, but you need a full stereo setup to make that work.

title: Beautiful but cracked after a few months
text: It’s very pretty and fits well, though it adds more weight than I would have expected. Unfortunately, after a few months of light use, the corner cracked today. In light of this, I wouldn’t recommend it.

title: Good for plugs, not so much for charging
text: This is a clever design, as the sphere takes up less space than a traditional power strip, but the charging ports are agonizingly slow.

title: Way too bright at night, otherwise great.
text: I got a new Kindle to replace my 6 year old one that started to get lines in the display. There’s not an enormous difference, but the type is a bit crisper. The interface is still slow (which is fine). My big issue is the light is SO BRIGHT. Even at the lowest setting, it is many times brighter than the older kindle, which makes it unusable at night when I’m trying not to wake my partner. This can be fixed with a firmware update, so fingers crossed.

title: but works fine so far
text: The cord feels a little flimsy, but works fine so far!

title: Great travel case
text: This is a great way to organize cords. It has a pretty small profile, so I am able to slip it in a pocket. I keep a set of travel cords in there so I don’t have to repack them every trip. My one quibble is the wasted space for SD cards and the like, which I imagine most of us don’t use anymore.

title: Perfect once you figure it out...
text: It took a few tries to figure out how the wrap secured to the cord, but once I did, I use these on everything: not just phone and mic cords, but my hair dryer and travel steamer, too.

title: Beautiful, but inconsistent quality
text: I’m on my third case. They are all lovely and protect my kindle in my purse or jacket pocket. The Van Gogh faded, but stayed intact, so 5 stars to that one. I bought the black case with the phases of the moon, which I love visually, and the first one broke after a couple of months of light use (I tuck it in a pocket of my bag). I bought another, thinking I may have gotten a dud, but that one, too broke around the magnet. I glued it together and that lasted a few more months. It’s really too bad, because it’s gorgeous and does the job. Trying to decide if gluing it again is worthwhile.

title: These headphones have good sound when the buds are seated well in the ...
text: These headphones have good sound when the buds are seated well in the ear, but they fall out a lot, and the gels fall off easily (I've lost one of each set that came with the packaging, so I'm looking for replacements. They are also not good for running or other vigorous exercise, but fine on the elliptical. They do not work well with a coat that has a collar. The battery life is great, as far as I can tell. I use them with my iPhone, so the functionality is limited, but what I can do is useful.

title: A little buggy. Poor sound
text: The plug I’d pretty buggy and must be reset. This version of the Echo doesn’t have a very good sound. Not recommended.

title: Guitar not speaker plug
text: Ordered for speaker, only compatible with guitar and too poor a quality to use for that. Total waste.

title: Sound quality poor.

title: Awesome!

title: SAVE YOUR MONEY
text: THIS IS ANCIENT TECHNOLOGY THAT'S PROBABLY SAT IN A WAREHOUSE FOR YEARS. MINE HAD A SHORT, BUT THE VENDOR IS DOING NOTHING TO MAKE IT RIGHT.

title: Big sound in small box!
text: Sounds like a gigantic speaker. My daughter had one of these from Amazon and I loved it on her coffee table to use with TV across the room, so I bought it and was impressed when listening to my Amazon downloaded music. Hubby heard it and bought himself the next version up to enhance his ipad music. Amazing sound from a small unit. We've use it in the garage to practice our dance steps and the quality is excellent.

title: Second time buying this great case!
text: Second time we have purchased executive Roo case - first for an iPad2 four years ago and most recently, for an IPadAir2. The newly designed/changed velcro placement is a big improvement! Our favorite iPad case and the price (for real leather, not plastic) is unbeatable. Works like it was designed to work and it's a durable, safe case for the iPad. Zip up for sleep mode. Zipper very tough and strong.

title: Great value! Pleasantly surprised!
text: Searched more than a dozen stores for a good looking portfolio for my husband's iPad. He wanted leather or faux leather, zipper closure, separate/removable jacket for iPad, wake/sleep capability, no silly exterior logo (for professional/work use), heavy duty construction, stand option, and I was hoping for less than $100 price tag. This item had all that and more. The logo is impressed into material on the front and hardly noticeable. Plenty of room inside for business cards, a pad, a stylus (holder is in the spine), zipper is sturdy, etc. Amazon had the best value (in store and online) including Best Buy, Walmart, Sams Club, etc. We could hardly believe the quality when it arrived. For less than $40. All comparables were $75-175 before shipping. Great value. We plan to order another for my iPad3. Nice item and very inexpensive.

title: Very efficient ...
text: I had an outdated charging cord for my phone hooked up in the car, and bought this as a replacement. It works a treat! Much faster, so it's the cord, since it's the same car.

title: Good value ...
text: I keep losing the cord for my Kindle Fire ... hope this is the last one I’ll buy although I guess that’s up to me! Very fast and a great length for bedside charging. A good choice.

title: Just as expected...
text: Nice little USB hub with a slightly longer than average cord; the on/off switches are very useful.

title: The little speaker that could ...
text: It's small but has very good sound quality, great available volume, nice & compact. I bought it for my desk top although it's designed for a laptop because it's USB powered and my cats have a tendency to gnaw cords that are too long & tempting (this one is shorter). It sits comfortably below my computer screen and let's me listen to music or dialog from movies that comes through loud & clear.

title: Finally! Earbuds that fit my weird ears.
text: I have always had trouble finding in-ear headsets that don't hurt and/or don't fit. These have three sizes of buds, which stay in & are very comfortable. Great find.

title: Will not fit 2023 Forester!
text: Like other reviewers have said this will not fit on a 2023 Subaru Forrester. The screen is slightly curved and this will peel up at the edges and look absolutely awful. This is super cheap so it’s not a big deal but even if it was free, I still would put in on my screen. Absolutely do not buy this product.

title: Impossible to fold out
text: These legs lay so flush to the bottom of my laptop when they aren’t in use that they are impossible to pull out again without some sort of knife to slide in and pry them out. Maybe if you have a super long fingernails you can deploy the legs but otherwise they are more of a nuisance. And good luck if you don’t stick them on perfectly the first time because they’re impossible to get off and you’ll be stuck with a wobbly laptop.

title: Perfect for video meetings
text: No more setting my laptop on a stack of books! Puts it at a perfect height and allows you to utilize the space underneath. I’ve looked at a few products to elevate my laptop and they all seem so involved and over engineered. This is simple and sturdy. I have a MacBook Air and it fits perfect.

title: The bottom will fit
text: I purchased this before and the bottom did not fit. It wasn't a huge deal as the top fit and thats what I really was interested in protecting. I figured I just got a bad one. I ordered this again in green and the bottom didn't snap on just like the first one I got. Apparently its not a case of getting a defective one but rather they are not designed to fit. If you get this product for your MacBook Air know that you will only be able to protect the top of your computer.

title: Bottom does NOT fit 2020 MacBook Air 13”.
text: This product is extremely poorly made. The bottom would not snap into my computer. I have the new 2020 MacBook Air 13 inch. It seems like it was either made for a different laptop or it’s of such low quality that it’s a crapshoot whether it fits or not. The one that fits on top is fine. The bottom is the problem. If you snap in one side the other side pops out and vice versa. Also, if both pieces are on, opening the laptop will pop off the bottom piece. Look for something better.

title: This will not add any height to a large TV
text: I bought this because I wanted my TV to be a little bit higher than it is now. They claimed this can be used on a 65 inch television. My television is 60 inches and it did not work at all. First of all, the back of your TV needs to be completely flat. If there is any bulge or anything like that (like mine) this stand will not work. It needs to be flush. The description implies that it will add height but it will not. If anything it would’ve made my television lower than using the current pedestal that it’s on. I would suggest that this product would work for something the size of a computer monitor or any TV that is 30 inches or less. If you are looking to replace the stand on your current TV and you don’t care about it having any extra height this product might work for you. For reference the back of my TV is 400 mm x 400 mm and this product says it can fit on 400 x 800. If I was able to attach it it would’ve been basically flush with the table that it’s on.

title: Cheap knock off but decent.
text: I bought this to replace one that was similar that I purchased in a store for about $40. This one is definitely made cheaper but seems like it’s pretty good. I don’t really tap on the screen while it’s sitting on a table or anything, I just use it to protect my iPad when I set it down and things like that. The only thing that I don’t like is that the case doesn’t cover the entire edge of the iPad. The shorter sides are completely exposed and could be prone to chipping. I suggest you go with a more rugged case if you travel with your iPad. The only place I really use mine is while I’m sitting on the couch.

title: Why am I just finding out about this thing now!
text: I eat lunch in my car just about every weekday because I drive for work. I’ve been doing this for over a decade and just found out about this thing. I wish I had one since day one.

title: Great!
text: Inexpensive comparatively and started working (charging) immediately. Super easy to change out the old and put in the new. I was concerned my computer was going out just as I am about to graduate nursing school and sick about losing all my info from school but turns out it just needed a new battery :)

title: Five Stars
text: The adapter worked just fine in Ireland. Delivery was prompt.

title: Wish it had lasted longer, but nice
text: Nice, as long as it lasted, which was almost two years.

title: Excellent Product!
text: Does just what it's supposed to do and is of a perfect traveling size!

title: What's Not To Love!
text: What's not to love about such a product that fills a need!

title: Works Well
text: Form to function; works well.

title: When you need a corded mouse
text: ... this is a great and inexpensive choice. I am a researcher, and my solitary foray into the realm of cordless mice taught me rather quickly that batteries don't last long when paired with long workdays. If your need is for a sturdy, apparently well-made computer mouse, choose this one!

title: New to webcams, but this is a great experience!
text: I have been intimidated with the thought of actually entering the 21st century & getting a webcam, but this little gem is perfect! Easy to set up and operate, and delivers a good picture and sound! Two thumbs up from someone who just wanted to be able to communicate with friends at a distance, and this is a fine product!

title: Great Surprise!
text: Logitech, THANK YOU for this great product! Having always had poor speakers for my PC -- until now -- I never realized what great sound could be delivered! All I can say is Wow! I am very impressed by the facts that these speakers are inexpensive, but clearly well-made, and the sound is pure and powerful. Two thumbs up!

title: Good product
text: It seems that wired computer mice are going the way of the dinosaur, so I bought two of these, and have only used one so far, but it's doing a great job! I'm thankful to have located these; my work as a researcher means that any wireless mouse would be in constant need of recharge. I made that mistake only once! If you need a good wired computer mouse, this one does the job!

title: Only slightly less than Perfect!
text: My decision to purchase this keyboard was based on a glowing review by someone that had been using his keyboard for a few months. I was seeking a keyboard that was quiet and ergonomic (fatigue-diminishing and user-friendly). My old H-P keyboard, after 4+ years of daily use, had become so "clattery" that it was a nuisance; plus, I'd worn the lettering off several keys! This new keyboard, though not 'whisper-quiet,' is definitely quieter. It took 2 or 3 days to get used to the different hand positioning and smaller "Enter" key, but was a breeze to adjust to. I'm hoping now to find a quieter Mouse! Would recommend this to anyone using a keyboard for several hours each day and in need of the relief provided by a soft-touch keyboard and quieter keystrokes.

text: Price,ease of installation and very good views day or night

title: Super cute
text: Super cute and easy to apply. It's a little too small though doesn't cover all edges. Update: it doesnt hold very well, I have to constantly press it back down because it'll start peeling up on its own.

title: Jammed first time I used it
text: I inserted a floppy after connecting the drive to teh computer, and it promptly jammed. The computer does not recognize the floppy as being inserted, and the eject button is impossible to depress. It looks like I may need to open the drive to get the floppy out. Overall, a failure.

title: Impossible to install
text: The information for these states that the pads can be used with Sennheiser HD4.50BT headphones. They in fact cannot be because the flap on the back that is supposed to go into the groove does not fit. Additional problems include lack of instructions and collapse of the headphones while trying to put the pads on. And I am assuming that the orange "pick" was to help push the material into the way too small groove, but I have no proof of this as I never got that far. I should have been suspicious when they had to take the headphones off camera during the "instructional" video. Totally turned off on the brand now because the pars failed much sooner than they should (a year), the cost of replacements was high (>10% of my purchase price) and the basic inability to use them. I now have some great sounding paper wights.

title: Bought refiurbished, did not work, tech support worthless
text: I bought two of these refurnished expecting them to be reset to factory settings. They were not. As a result, I could not get into them. Called tech support, and they were never able to give me any useful suggestions. In the end, they turned into landfill because my time to return them expired. Never buying refurbished gear from this company again.

title: Very good cables
text: These cables seem to be above average in quality and construction. The wire appears to be reinforced well an should last for a long time. Value for the money is good.

title: Great for laptops and otehr mobile devices
text: I damaged my audio jacks and needed a replacement for my laptop. Rather than spend $1,000+ for a new laptop, I bought this. It works fine and produces good sound quality. It should work with other devices with a suitable USB port.

title: Excellent audio quality and small footprint
text: I placed this under my 55" HDTV. It is a narrower but is a good width for getting stereo sound. I used a stand for the TV, and the speaker sets on the foot with about 2" to spare. The subwoofer was hidden behind my computer desk. Connection is by Bluetooth, so there is no wire out the back. The speakers and subwoofer both provide plenty of volume. If anything the subwoofer is overwhelming, but you can adjust its volume independently. The visual feedback through some blue LEDs hidden behind the speaker mesh works well. There are multiple preset buttons for music, conversation/voice, etc. They shape the response of the system and tend to work okay but are not exceptional. Overall sound quality is very good across the entire audible spectrum. My biggest complaint is that the speaker will go to standby way too often and revert to the ARC input while I use the AUX input. Ut results in a lot of pushes of buttons to get the speaker system awake and on the right channel again. Small things like this prevented me from giving it 5 stars, but the speaker system is very good and a good value.

title: Mixed thoughts
text: These are good, solid Velcro fasteners, but the way that the end goes through the buckle and back has proven to not work well for me in a couple of cases.

title: Great fill lights
text: I used AI bought these for fill lights. They can provide the equivalent of a 20 W incandescent light, which is plenty of light with modern DSLRs. One or two can fill int he shadows when shooting in low light or backlit situations. battery life is excellent with no problems getting over 90 minutes of life at full power and much longer with even a small decrease in output. If I had any ideas for improvement, it would be to have presets for common light sources (daylight, tungsten, etc.) to better match the primary light source. The value of the unit is great, and I highly recommend it.

title: Revived my dead laptop
text: The battery was hard to get into the laptop and lacks the foot to raise up the back of the laptop that I have on my old battery. Once the difficulty with getting the battery in was solved with some sharp blows with the heel of my hand, it charged right up and is doing a fine job of powering my old Dell.

title: No box, no manual, bit so far no problems
text: This is as basic as it gets. It was shipped in a non-ESD plastic bag with little protection. It has no privacy cover. You can get access to the manual on-line, but a print copy would have been nice. I found out there that you can tilt the camera rather than needing to hang it cocked downward. It has sufficient range of motion to work on a 55-inch monitor. Picture quality is acceptable to good. I have some issues with backgrounds being blown out that I need to address.

title: Some issues
text: The unit is particularly sensitive to even minor line fluctuations. It was constantly making noises until I went to the Web sote and found the cause. Decreasing the sensitivity seems to have cured the problem.

title: Works as advertised
text: Pops into the printer easily, does not jam, is easy to remove the backing and adheres well. What more do you want?

title: Gemnerally works well but some issues noted
text: I like these panels. They provide an even diffuse light. They have multiple filters, if you want to add colors or adjust white balance. They have a range of heights. The on/off and power setting buttons work well to control the lights. My negatives are stability and power. The tripod legs are a trade-off of space for stability. They work, but the lights are prone to being easy to knock over. This is a common issue and hardly unique to these lights. The panels do not provide as much light as I was expecting, though it is generally adequate. The need to supply your own USB power block was a "hidden cost" that needs to be considered. If you have plenty of high current extras laying around, it is not an issue. If you have to order some, add the cost to your buying decision. UPDATE: I dropped the rating to stars because the ON/OFF membrane switch on one of the lights died and the ilght is dead after much less than 100 uses. They need better switches.

title: Not as good as I was hoping it would be
text: I live in a major metropolitan area with several TV stations. Most work fine, but at least two that should have a very strong signal are giving consistent problems, and a third can be problematic. The other stations work fine. If you are on the fringe of the broadcast area of a TV station you want, I would look at a different antenna. If you want something for casual or occasional use and have good signal strength, the value for the price is okay, but you are never going to get the weak signal station with it.

title: Will not work unless you create a Roku account!
text: All I want is a TV for the (None of your business) room. I was forced to create a Roku account to even get started. THIS IS NOT RIGHT! The TV tuner is all I want or need. If I want streaming, I will get an Amazon Fire Stick. The sole reason that this is not heading back is that I did not have to setup payment for Roku. If they demand payment, it will be! The questions required to srtup the account were intrusive and unneeded. Value your privacy or just do not want an unwanted service that will probably track your viewing> DO NOT BUY THIS TV!!! As for the TV itself, it fir where it needed to go and works well. Picture quality is good for a 1080p 32"-class screen. Sound is acceptable, but I will be routing it to a stereo as soon as I figure out how to connect the two. Without the Roku issue, this would have been a solid 4 Star unit.

title: Does what I need it to do
text: Shooting miniatures and figures in a tabletop studio can result in some color shift due to reflected colors from the background or even the item being photographed. This card gives me white balance and color checks. I cannot speak to its absolute accuracy, but visually it is consistent with the advertised values. Once I get the images into Photoshop, I use the values to give consistent color rendition. (See the Web for hundreds of tutorials on how to do this.) It is quick , easy and gives superior results. It ir even a simple white card can really increase your photography game in these situations. The second card can be taken on the road for when you are dealing with a lighting situation where you have LED, fluorescent and tungsten lights and need help deciding what to use for the white balance. (That was me at the IX Center during a prior Cleveland Auto Show.) You still might not be able to reach perfection, but you can examine the trades.

title: Solid case with easy access
text: The case is very stirdy with an anodized aluminum shell that should protect the cards inside against all but the heaviest of loads. The molded foam interior holds the cards securely and will nto allow them to fall out when you open the case. You can store micro-SD cards underneath full-sized cards or adapters. The case is still slim enough to go into my camera bag easily. My only small complaint is that the design of the slots does not allow me to flip the cards over to indicate that they have been used and are full. I bought a second case for that. The multiple colors made it easy to used blue for ready to use and red for ready to download iamges.

title: Great for VOIP and virtual meetings
text: These work very well for taking calls int he computer or doing a virtual meeting. They are faily comfortable though they could use more and better padding. Sound quality is good, and the microphone works well.

title: Solid batteries, good price
text: Sometimes unexciting is good. These are good batteries at a low price that come with a charger that can be used virtually anywhere that has power.

title: Good stand with a couple of small issues
text: The stand went together easily and works exactly as advertised. I have a 55" monitor weighing 50 pounds on it, and it is rock solid. I can rotate the screen side to side with no concerns. It also gives no indication of tipping over when pushed or pulled. I really liked the compartmentalization of tools, fasteners, screws and spacers. If there is a screw needed to attach the monitor that is not included, I would be very surprised. Hanging the monitor on the stand can be done alone, but get someone to help if you can. The one thing that loses this stand a star is the base. I was unable to get all four screws installed because the hole locatins were too far off. The sheet metal is also thin and will easily depress if you put something onto it or lean on it. Overall, this is a very good choice for a stand.

title: Extremely small large storage option
text: These are so small that I can put the into my laptop USB ports and leave them there for tons of extra storage for my photos and other files. They are also great for sharing. The only downside is that they are so small that they can be easily misplaced or lost. I suggest a storage container for them when they are not in the computer.

title: Did not work for me
text: I had two spots on my sensor. I went through the cleaning process, and I still have two spots on my sensor. There was no noticeable change in the spots after cleaning. My conclusion is that I put my sensor at risk for no gain.

title: Impressive lens that is a bot difficult to focus well at first
text: Toss out everything and start from scratch with this lens. First, on an Olympus OM-D EM-1 camera, the distance markings are worthless. Ignore them and use the screen to focus. Be absolutely certain to use electronic magnification while adjusting the focus, or you are going to miss more than hit. I find working in Manual Mode with Manual Focus is the best. An aperture around f/ 8 is my preference for bright subjects, but I have worked all the way down to wide open and gotten good shots. If you develop a mental checklist and go through it /every time/, you can get great results with this lens. For my EM-1 and all other micro-4/3 cameras, the top and bottom of the circle are cut off some. I estimate that I still get over 80% of the circle area in my photo, and I am very happy with it. Some subjects that seem to work well with this lens include landscapes, wind farms, museum falleries and cars. Example photos are from The Early Ford V-8 Museum in Auburn, IN USA.

The second is the lack of a VESA mount, though there is apparently an adapter (another $60+) of questionable mechanical design. Overall, you can probably get a better monitor that is more up-to-date for a lower price, especially if you want/need a VESA mount.

The second reason is the total lack of support from Western Digital when I sought help with the problem or to return the drive for a warranty repair/replacement. My request for help was ignored. The last thing I want to do it hold the camera at arms' length. That is how you get shaking and other problems. It would have been far preferable to have had a second mark or guide. Adjust the dot so that the camera lens, subject and sight are are aligned, and then you can hold the camera in close and use just the dot sight to follow the action.aligned If you use dot sights like this and have no qualms about holding your camera a couple o feet from your body, it might be worth something to you.
