title: Definitely not worth the price in my opinion...
text: Maybe it's just the set I received, but on a few levels I can advise against these. For starters, the price. I do not feel these are worth what they're charging. Although the filters look nice with the colorful trim, etc, that's about as far as I'd go with them. The case is okay. It's plastic and has a snap style latch to keep it closed. However, the filters just sit in foam. When I received mine and pulled them out of the box, all of the filters were out of their foam slots and just floating around in the case. After pushing them back into their foam spots, they seemed to hold in place. There's a lot more case than needed for the 6 filters so if you're trying to consolidate space, you may want to put them in something else. The huge issue I have with all of them is how loose they fit the Mini 3 camera. Each one of mine can practically fall off. I'd understand if maybe one of them was super loose, but for all of them to behave the same it seems like a design flaw to me. I've used other brand filters that hold in place equal to that of the stock attachment but I'm afraid these are going to fall off too easily. Maybe not necessarily in flight since it's on a gimbal that accounts for turbulent air but I almost guarantee they'll fall off when fiddling around with the drone in your hands. A suggestion to the manufacturer would be to create a little more tension where they lock onto the camera like DJI and other brand filters do to prevent them from spinning back the very slight distance it takes for them to come off.

title: I am impressed but I feel for what you're getting the price could be cheaper
text: I'll preface by saying I feel all companies that sell things like this charge more than they should. They're mini drone ND filters. We're not talking about a set of ND filters for a full scale DSLR here. Regardless with that being said, I do think you're getting a good product. They work as they're supposed to. Snap on to the drone securely and easily. The case they come in is nice. It's magnetically sealed which is awesome. Feels sturdy enough to know the filters will be protected in my bag or case. If I were to give one complaint (and it's not really a complaint), I wish the company would have made the case a little taller. The filters are secured in place by the foam they sit on so it's not as if the lid is what's holding them in place. So if they were to make the lid a little taller, we could stick the stock DJI attachment in the case while the ND filter was on the drone. My biggest concern is losing the DJI attachment. It's just a suggestion. Certainly not a deal breaker on whether or not these are good filters.

title: It's fine...
text: I'll preface by saying I do prefer the hand style straps where the padding goes around the back of your hand and if you let go it can hang from your wrist. I was just in need of a wrist strap and figured I would give this one a shot. This wrist strap is fine. I can't really rave about it or complain about it. The price point is not terrible. I'd probably have valued it a little lower but I'd have said the same of any strap like this of similar quality. I already know by looking at it, in time the leather will undoubtedly separate like I've seen with similar wrist straps. I'm not entirely sure the purpose of the plastic clip. It's just as easy to remove the whole thing from the camera as it would be to unbuckle it. I also view that as potential point of failure where my camera could end up on the ground if the buckle wasn't secured properly, unbuckled, or something else went wrong. Like I said, "it's fine". If it's the style you're after and you don't to spend a crazy amount of money on something as simple as a wrist strap, you'll be content.

text: The keyboard on the back of this remote makes searching on Amazon, Netflix and Hulu so much easier - no more having to navigate that onscreen "keyboard". I was hesitant to purchase this item since it was not clear from the product description or from the Vizio website that this remote would even work with my model TV, which came with the VR17 remote. But I decided I would take a chance, and return if it it did not work. The front of the remote contains three quick-access buttons for Amazon, Netflix and Vudu, and then all of the same keys found on the VR17 in the same positions, with one minor exception. The XRV1TV 3D is designed for use with a 3D TV, which mine is not. Where the VR17 remote has the "WIDE" key in the lower left corner position, this remote has a "3D" key. But that is not an issue for me, since I rarely use that function, and it is available through an on-screen menu anyway. The one thing that keeps me from giving this remote a 5-star rating is that I find the remote a little awkward to hold and use without accidentally pressing a key on the reverse side. It takes some getting used to having to hold this carefully to prevent that happening.

title: Very nice, but....
text: I purchased a Kindle Fire as a reconditioned unit during a recent deal. The unit arrived in good and clean condition, boxed as if new. I could not tell it was not a new unit. It functions perfectly. Access to my home WiFi was easy to set up. Videos, apps, MP3 player, web access and e-reader function are great on the Fire. However, I find that I prefer my Kindle 3 (keyboard) for reading - it's much lighter and more comfortable to hold, and the screen is easier on my eyes. And, for anything that involves typing, I find I prefer to use a real keyboard; it's too bad the there is no option on the Fire to attach an external keyboard. For what it does, the Fire is a great little gadget at $139.00, but for my purposes, my Kindle 3 combined with my laptop is still a better option.

title: I love this light
text: I have been using this light for over a month now - it works very well. The light given out is just right for me, not too dim or too bright. The movement of the gooseneck is a bit stiff at first, but gets easier with a bit of use. I was pleasantly surprised that it does not seem to drain the battery much faster than reading without the light. Prior to this I used a clip-on light that worked well but used batteries quickly. Although this light is more expensive, the savings in batteries easily makes this more cost-effective. The light seems well-made and connects securely to the Kindle. The color and appearance of the plastic is a close match to that of the Graphite Kindle Keyboard. I use this in conjunction with this case: [[ASIN:B0043CBP32 rooCase Flip (Red) Leather Case for Amazon Kindle Wireless Reading Device with 6" Display 3G + Wi-Fi (3rd Generation and Latest Generation) - With rooCASE Retail Gift Box]]

title: Looks & feels good - fits fine, can't beat the price.
text: Looks & feels good - fits fine, can't beat the price. I no longer need to worry about scratches. Satin finish has a nice feel - not as slippery as the bare ipod, less likely to slip from my hand. At the same time, slides easily from the leather slipcase I use.

title: Sanyo Eneloop NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargable Batteries w/ Charger
text: These are great batteries. They keep their charge longer than any battery we've tried. We use them for our cameras, video games, smoke alarms, flashlights, etc. They have AA, AAA, C, D & 9v. We love them.

title: Fit great
text: These really cancel out the noise quite well. I had a set of similar earbuds but one found it’s demise in the toilet (not a good day). I tried to find the old pair since I liked them but no luck. These popped up as an item that was similar. I liked that the charging dock shows the battery power as my wife has a set from a different seller that doesn’t show this and it’s quite frustrating to gauge battery life. The standard ear plugs that came with the device worked for me but there are a couple more size options. The sound is great and since they snug right in your ear it’s easy to keep them in and not falling out. I don’t notice any static and have actually found they are louder than my other pair (I’ve had to adjust the volume down on my walks from my previous pair). Great set. They are a little hard to get out of the case but that’s the same issue all of these earbuds have since there’s not a tiny handle piece to grab hold of (just a rounded top of the earbud). Great and highly recommend!

title: Works good
text: I got this because I have a 2 pack of lights that have usb ports and rather than two plugs I got this product. It works as advertised. Doesn’t have cheap product materials. Very pleased with the purchase and works as expected.

title: Not great
text: I am finding more and more that these Amazon Basics products are getting lower and lower grading. This was a replacement cord and didn't work right out of the box. Luckily the original still works. The gold plating just seems low grade and the materials just look poor. Was hoping for better.

text: This light is supposed to work for my Panasonic DMC-FZ300 but doesn't properly seat in the shoe. I have tried various means and it won't work. The light itself is quite bright when the flash is manually used, but it doesn't work for my camera. There is a similar design from Neweer so I assumed this was going to mirror that but it doesn't. I had the neweer for a few years and lost it awhile back. I went to go buy another and the price of that had doubled. I was hopeful here but it doesn't work with my camera.

title: Worked Great
text: I am unsure of the need for 5 of the same style ports (I thought it was a universal adapter) but in any case, this one worked well. The foot massager I purchased ended up with a bent end due to the cord over stretching. This worked great for a Breo Foot Massager replacement.

title: Really impressed
text: My son ended up accidentally yanking the cord out of the flat antenna we had. It’s the one most commonly sold that looks like a flat sheet of vinyl. I wanted something that had a good signal but could sit on his dresser rather than drape on a wall (how the cord got pulled, I can’t explain, but with the tv being mounted on a wall that runs perpendicular to the outside wall, it happened). This sits about 5 feet inside the house (upstairs where his room is) and the signal is far better than the previous model we had. We have a decent bit of tree coverage so I was hoping the extended range would help and it did here. The unit is smaller than my mind told me it would be as I thought it would be about 15” tall. It’s somewhere around 8-10” without measuring exactly. Works great, cord shouldn’t ever come out of this one. Very pleased.

title: These are great
text: I wanted a dual set because we have two backseat drivers that need distraction. Well, maybe they just need a better driver but in any case I needed a DVD player set. I decided on these based on the reviews and am thoroughly impressed. There is a built in battery which has served us well given I didn’t realize that at first and while driving the DVD player stopped. I thought it was broke and then realized it had just not been plugged in properly. After reading through I was pleasantly surprised by this feature. My kids like the ease of access and to be able to use the remote. I really like the lack of skipping that occurs while driving as a previously set we had would skip and then restart the disc. No issues in that regard here. The audio is great though we have the kids wear headphones as usually we have a few different sounds happening (radio, wifes phone, older sons phone, and DVD player would just add to that). I did listen to it at first as I didn’t want to have the headphones given it’ll only be a few years before he wears them all the time (teen years are fun). If there were a downside to these, it is something that happens to all DVD players in that when cold, the laser reader has to warm before it can read the disc. That happens with all players though so it’s more of a tip than anything. Highly recommend

title: Didn’t work
text: The first camera failed so they sent another. Now they deleted my account after a bad review?

title: Center button is Power
text: I want to kick this review off with a key point, as the title states, the center button on the front of the speaker is the power button. I didn’t read the directions to see if this was mentioned, I just charged it and struggled to power it on when it was charged. Outside of that the sound quality and overall volume on this is great. When it first powered on, the automated voice had me concerned as it doesn’t sound clean, but it seems to be just how it was recorded. I turned on a song and naturally had to crank up the volume to see what it could do. I was pleasantly surprised and it didn’t have issues with quality (sometimes speakers get louder in volume and it sounds like someone just singing closer and closer to a microphone). This does include a short Aux cord (2 ft) and the charging cable (but no plug). The charging cable is USB C that goes into the speaker (but still plugs into a standard usb plug). I am very pleased here!

title: Better than I thought
text: I am really enjoying the sound quality from these as I needed to switch from a corded headset to something wireless. This is Bluetooth but the Bluetooth chip works well and doesn’t seem to have issue where it disconnects from my laptop and connects to my phone (I’ve had this with a few speakers). The mic works great as I do user testing and the sound quality is important for good feedback as a tester. I was pleasantly surprised to find out that the chip isn’t needed unless Bluetooth isn’t available on the device. There was no issue with connectivity either as my laptop recognizes the USB Bluetooth chip and automatically paired with the headset. A plus for me since my laptop tends to lag. The headset has a good/decent look to it. The earpieces are squishy and comfortable. The headset adjusts easily. The plastic seems to be of decent quality so putting them on and taking off repeatedly should not be an issue. Very pleased overall.

title: Fantastic
text: I bought this adapter because the other one I have always caused static and I’d have to turn my stereo up quite a bit to get the volume at a decent level. I have had far less issues with static when this is plugged in while listening to the radio (weaker channels are always going to be an issue either way). I am also able to turn the volume up about 25% less than with the other (knob was at 22 with other adapter and this one works well on 16 or 17). Thoroughly pleased with this one and I got it because we are slowly moving toward the USB c style charging cables (as newer items seem to also be doing the same).

title: Great camera, cloud isn’t
text: I liked the camera so much I bought the outdoor one as well. This camera has motion detection that will follow the motion. It actually made my son nervous and thought someone was controlling it. I explained that it detects motion and follows that which is ideal should someone get inside the house. The camera does have two way Audio that works well and only has a slight lag but is fairly clear. I am able to monitor the cameras from the app but this is where the problem starts. The app is adjustable to some degree, the problem that I’ve explained to the manufacturer is they require each camera to have separate cloud storage at a separate fee per month. The cloud storage should be based on the account and total account cloud usage. This helps with better networking as well as retaining cloud activity in one central location. If the motion detection were capturing someone who did eventually make it inside, that sequence from camera to camera would be great if it all linked in one cloud account. The problem is that LongPlus has not done this and you pay separate fees per camera. Not pleased but it is the only company I’ve seen that has an indoor camera and an outdoor camera (where the outdoor camera is battery powered).

title: Poor camera, poor cloud
text: Update: arrived 4/16, installed after charging on 4/17. Died today on 5/3. Roughly 2.5 weeks of battery life. I really enjoy the camera overall. It was easy to install the app using the QR code in the manual. Then following the manual to register the camera and have it read the QR code to register the camera to the account. I wanted a camera brand that had both Indoor and Outdoor cameras but needed the outdoor camera to have a battery and found that in LongPlus. There is a slight lag in the camera but the quality is solid. The motion detection can be adjusted which is nice as it is fairly sensitive. The big downside is regarding the future of the online world which is their cloud service. There is only a 7 day free trial, not 30 days (and nowhere to add a code to get the 30 days that is promised in the description). Outside of that, rather than having one cloud service payment per month, you pay for each camera. The cost saved appears to be made up with their cloud services costing money if you want a full network of cameras. Very disappointed by something so simple. There is no easy customer service portal for questions in the app, only app feedback (which I submitted but there should be an easy line of communication). There are also many misspelled words within the app itself adding to the confusion and overall trust. I rarely have one star for my reviews but this is just really a simple fix on the LongPlus side.

title: So far so great
text: We picked up this camera because we were getting a new puppy and needed to keep an eye on him during the day. The clarity is pretty solid overall given the cost and can be seen in the photo above (which includes our little pup). The camera can take snapshots which I am not able to save to my phone (or haven’t quite figured out how to save to my iPhone but they do save in the app). I don’t really need this for motion detection but have tested that feature out as a just in case measure if we used in the future. The sensitivity can be adjusted but overall a very nice feature. The camera does have a micro sd slot that would allow storage of footage (like movements) but we use the live footage as our means of checking the feed. The connection to the device was fairly smooth but we did have to refresh our router when completing the process. It could’ve been a bandwidth issue given we have more Smart items than ever. The app is fairly user friendly and my wife and I can both view the live feed at the same time. The feed itself is about .5 -1 second slow which we haven’t found as a problem. The audio in/out is also quite clear which was fantastic. We try not to talk to our pup too much but it definitely was a nice feature for the first 2-3 days of him being in the crate (and being able to hear him as well as talk to him if he got frustrated). Highly recommend this one!

title: Weak Signal
text: I was setting this extended up to help boost the wifi at my parents house. Getting connected to the device was fairly difficult and I had to get into the router settings to provide special permissions for it to be visible on the network. I had to reboot the router a few times for it to finally take hold and connect. From there I moved it to the location (router in attic) this would be on first floor of a two story house, almost directly below the router (two-ish floors down). I wanted a better signal in the attached garage as in some corners in got weak. Unfortunately this did nothing to increase the signal of the Wi-Fi. I ended up going with a different model that worked successfully and allowed it to go from 1 bar to 4 (of 5 bars) for signal strength.

title: Weak

This was the same specs as the fan it was replacing and. The air generated made it look like a dying Christmas tree. That was my purpose, maybe it would work in other applications but again the specs lined up with the other fan it was replacing.

title: Don't last long
text: These cords are quite thick and I was hoping that would help with quality, however these seem to have worn out the fastest. It isn't like the ends have the tradition wear marks where the cord connects into the phone, it's just that they stop connecting to the phone (incompatible notice) then when that is no longer displaying they just stop working. I did find that manipulating the cord itself (not the end connected to the phone) helps make it connect so it's possible a wire just isn't fully connected inside the cord and is causing the failure. All in all these have lasted the shortest length of all the chargers I've purchased (which it's usually just the part plugged into the phone that normally wears and then won't connect).

title: Great headset
text: This is actually my second headset of this type because I let my son use the last one and he decided to stretch it until it broke. I really like that it has a clean sound quality as I do usertesting and that requires clear sound quality. They are also very comfortable and I enjoy they go on the ear versus in the ear which tends to irritate my ears. The cable is also of solid quality which seems like it plays a role in producing clear audio. Great buy!

title: Perfect!
text: I am very pleased with this purchase and I wanted to write a review on things start to finish. Packaging -Fantastic overall look and also care in terms of making sure the watch face was protected and sitting in its' own section of the box. The bands were not attached but were easy to slip on (there's a small little nub on the band end that attaches to the watch, color side will face down). There is also a screen protector to peel off the watch face. The charger is magnetic and the charging process may have taken an hour (I just plugged into my computer). Directions -These were really fantastic. They lay things out in detail but also keep it brief for the many different options available. Turn on the bluetooth mode on your phone. I found the app "Da Fit App" from the product description, though the directions only show a QR code. From there it was opening the app and doing a quick profile setup (Sex, Height, Weight, Birth Year). It automatically scanned for the phone and the letters displayed on the screen and it was the only one shown so that was quick. I do wish it would pop up a notification that the pairing was successful but there is a watch icon in the app at the bottom. If you click that it displays "Connected" right at the top and shows your exact watch. It also let's you customize the "face" of the watch from within the app. I like Dial 3. The App -Very well laid out and some details were provided earlier but you can adjust the notifications you receive and it all pairs through Bluetooth so as long as they are on (and you accept push notifications on the phone) you'll receive the notifications on the phone. You can make a lot of the adjustments you want through the watch, but the app can allow for a faster level to set all at once. The Modes Phone calls, sleep (need to leave on during sleep), heart rate test, steps, training (stopwatch), blood pressure, SpO2 Test, Weather, Reminders, Shutter (photos/video), start/stop songs, Alarms, Timer, Stopwatch, Theater Mode (turns off vibrating and brightness), Move reminders, Drink reminders (stay healthy), Health reminders (menstrual, pregnancy, gender health). The watch will sync to your timezone once the app is set and you can also get weather notifications which I set inside the app. I am really thrilled to use the watch and was able to even deny a call earlier without having to grab my phone (unwanted caller). Excellent product and totally worth it!

title: Good sound, not good audo
text: Here me out here in that the sound on these is solid (not a whole lot of bass) but the sound is clean. They also can go quite loud which is also nice given that sometimes bluetooth reception can be limited. These pair quickly with my phone too. The issues I have are the popping these into and out of your ear, you are likely to hit one of the buttons to either pause music or adjust sound. The other major issue is the audio quality for taking a call is terrible. I did test these out against airpods as that is the ultimate goal here (great deal and to not have to buy those, right?). Well, if you want to use these for taking calls, you will end up with a good deal of static (again with an even comparison in the same situation as airpods which I was able to borrow from a friend who helped with the test).

title: Cheap, but effective
text: These mounts seem to be mostly set to as long as they fit your tv size, you've got endless options. The big key is price and this one fit the bill. It came in a fairly small, light box which is fine. The mount does not need to be massive. The materials these pieces are made from are steel but incredibly light weight. The brackets that go on the backside of the TV are L shaped rather than the U shape or even Square shape I've had for other TV mounts I've purchased. Outside of that, assembly was quick. The other small note is this did not come with a small level that is common to see on these mounts (but cheap versions of those can be less reliable also). It is a super bare bones item but has handled a 46" TV with ease and that's what we needed.

title: Get these!
text: You NEED braided if you want these types of cords to last. I bought two standard style white cords and they were flimsy and ended up melting. These have worked exceptionally well and the long cord has been really nice as 3' is just slightly too short and pulls my headphones down. 6' is the way to go. The sound quality is as expected. The audio plug that goes into your headphones is a little large but still ended up fitting in my headphones but I had to push a little bit. No loss of sound and I am incredibly pleased!

title: Great little mic
text: The microphone easily attached to my camera. I did like that there was a replacement camera mount included (the red piece) as I’ve heard of people breaking those for similar looking mics. This one DID come attached to the red mount so there were no issues and I have a spare. The red piece is fairly flexible which has both pros and cons as the mic can move a little and not stress this piece, but the con being the mic can move. As far as the mic audio, there was a good improvement when about 3 feet away and a major improvement when up closer. The audio is cleaner than the on mic camera which makes this a nice minor cost improvement. There are different cables which allow you to attach the camera to a standard audio port or a TRRS port like on some iPhones. The mic does not need batteries so there are no issues with needing the check the batteries before each use. This does seem to have a downside somewhat in that the mic doesn’t really have a power boost which would come from the batteries. The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition. The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter. I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: Unfortunately this item was far better than expected. I know that sounds odd but the item was well made, with a solid cord length. The cord itself was of thick material/casing which helps add durability. I was pleasantly surprised by this item.

title: Holding up well
text: The issue with most cords is the connection between the cable and head of the cord don't seem to hold up over time. This cord solves that issue with a flexible piece of rubber that allows it to have some additional stability for long term use. They connect as expected and haven't worn down as some other cords have over time. The cords also don't have the "device not compatible" issue which can occur with some cords. Very satisfied with this purchase overall.

It does work but will require some tech knowledge to get it to actually store files. I would not deem this as a ready to go item.

title: Wall plug, laptop, car usb - does not work
text: I purchased this unit because it appeared like it would work in my cars’ USB port. That didn’t work though the unit lit up its blue light. I tried a few different cables in each slot with no luck. I tested the port alone with a cable after and that worked fine. I then tried it in my wall outlet. The units light lit up blue. I tried the same tests as above with no luck. I tested wall plug with single cable after and my wall plug worked fine. Finally I tried my laptop’s usb and using the same testing sequence above it also didn’t work. I am returning this unit.

title: Solid accessory for the videographer
text: This mic came in a nice package that was foam packed so it had a very professional look. The mic is solid plastic so it does seem like it would be easy to break (this review could be edited later should an incident occur). The mic quality is much more improved over the mic on my EOS M (video difference is shown in my yt video, LiftingDad). The +10db gain is a nice addition to the mic and really helps with improving the overall sound volume. The shotgun aspect of the mic is decent but not the best from what I've truly seen from shotgun mic's (i.e. The sound picked up best is directly in front of the mic and dissipates from the sides to the back of the mic). It still pick up sounds fairly well from the sides and back. This is NOT ideal when shooting an interview or similar which is the common method for these mic's. It does come at a nice price point and is a great piece for those on a budget (like myself).

title: A Bit Deceiving But The Right Price
text: Why the 3 stars? This package deal comes with items that seem to be drawn from an overstock bin of items in a similar category. So you DO get the items listed, just with different brands names. The kit altogether is priced well and you "get what you pay for", however here you get what's given. It'd be better if they showed the varying brands given to customers. Most of the cleaning kit was Polaroid which is great. The lens protector kit is a brand I have not heard of but appears decent. The bag (as others have mentioned) is not what's pictured. I need the tripod otherwise I'd return the package due to the seller knowingly sending items not accurately described. Suggestion to the seller: Add accurate photos so people are more aware of what they may be getting versus what's expected from the provided pictures.

title: This is one solid unit which is great. The arms are their own pieces

text: Once I found the insertion slot, it worked just fine. Great help from prior customers and Amazon email feedback. Happy!

title: Good Product
text: Case is very nice and easy to keep clean. Looks good too.

title: Good
text: Easier to use than gen 2. So far do good.

title: EXTREMELY POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE
text: I was very excited when I got my Kindle 1 1/2 years ago. All worked well until about 2 months ago. The wireless connection could not be maintained. My laptop is fine as is my smartphone. So I contacted customer service. What a disaster. I contacted their chat many, many times to no avail. Some said it was hardware and others said it was software. They do not have remote access capabilities nor a service repair center. Today it got to the point where I got such ridiculous highly technical instructions so I ended the chat. They are poorly qualified to provide technical support. Of course they will not send a new one . So unfortunately, I have no use for a dead kindle. So sad. I paid well over $250 1 1/2 years ago and now it's a throwaway.

title: Great Product!
text: Fast shipping! Cute looking compact radio combo. Worked perfectly as soon as I took it out of the box. Very glad I bought this .Great value.

title: Excellent for more than tripods
text: I purchased the 25" model of the same bag from this brand in August 2021 and it has held up admirably. No tears; the zipper is solid and the outer material is tough. My primary use is to use the bag for some drum hardware. I have a dedicated hardware bag for stands, etc., but for individual parts like floor tom legs, shell-mounted cymbal arms, and bass drum tom mounts I prefer this bag and found that the 25" model was larger than I normally need. The only bass drum tom mount that I use that will NOT fit in this bag is the Gretsch GS1THSL single tom mount that comes with modern Catalina and Renown kits. Obviously the double mount will also not fit. However, my other mounts do and this bag is the perfect way to transport drum kit-specific hardware and leave my general hardware bag separate. My first one has lasted nearly a year and is still going strong. I expect many more years of use from that bag and see no reason why I won't have the same experience with this one.

title: Nicely constructed, but the product photos are deceptive
text: The product page photos when I purchased this showed two bags. I assumed that was how many I would receive. After only one arrived I noticed that the photos were meant to depict the fact that the length was adjustable. I returned the order (no hassles by the way.) I did take the time to carefully examine the bag before returning it and was impressed. The material was extremely sturdy, there was some padding and the zipper was first rate. Had it met my overall needs I would have kept it. Despite returning it I will not hesitate to highly recommend the bag or its value. Just bear in mind that you will be receiving a single bag, not two that the product photo [when I purchased mine) depicted.

title: Some minor issues, but a decent alternative to subscription cable
text: I purchased this to upgrade an old Roku HD that I purchased in 2012. While the older Roku worked well for Netflix and YouTube, Amazon Prime discontinued support for it. This has what I suppose user interface designers call a modern look, but I honestly preferred the older, less slick look of the HD model. However, that is not a show stopper for me. My only complaint is I have to reboot this model every few weeks or it hangs. The ancient HD model was a solid performer that maybe needed to be rebooted two or three times a year. On the other hand, I can once again watch Prime video, and the price of this device is pretty inexpensive, so I am mostly a happy camper.

title: Exactly what it claims: simple and reliable
text: I needed a spare mouse as a backup for one that is over fifteen years old and is starting to show its age. I purchased this based on price and reviews and am going to grab another one. Plugged right into my aging Lenovo T400 running Windows 7. Even a utility called WizMouse recognized it and the settings (for a Logitech mouse) of that app worked perfectly as well. Plugged into a Windows 10 laptop, same result: immediately recognized and worked perfectly. Definitely plug and play in the Windows world, included a legacy, unsupported machine and laptop. I also tested it with a Chromebook ... works perfectly. Durability? Haven't had it long enough to say one way or the other. The cord is about the same as the Logitech mouse, and every other aspect of construction appears to be close-to-identical.

title: Perfect for the way I use it
text: I subtracted a star because this battery does not last as long as an OEM one when you are not on external power. However, I am always plugged into external power when working, so I use it as a safeguard to give me time to shut down my laptop when we have a power outage. Those are sadly frequent where I live in central FL. For the price and the fact that it supports my ancient Thinkpad model I consider it a bargain. If you are looking for a replacement battery that will allow you to work untethered from external power you probably should invest in a genuine OEM battery from Lenovo. If you use it the way that I do, though, this is an ideal solution.

title: Perfect fit
text: This fits my Galaxy Tab S7 FE 2021 perfectly. It's a tad awkward, but only because of the size of the tablet itself. It had decent protection, precision cutouts, and is priced well below covers at the big box stores. I have zero complaints!

title: Not disappointed
text: I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015. This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015. I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected. What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality. If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

title: Make sure you read the description
text: I ordered this and had to return it simply because of my own stupidity: I did not carefully read the product description. This is specifically for newer laptops and other devices that do not have VGA out, but have HDMI out. It is designed to allow you to connect your device to a legacy monitor or TV that has VGA in, It will NOT work in the other direction. For what it does and its intended market this is an inexpensive way to continue using a legacy, VGA equipped monitor or TV with newer devices that are HDMI only.

title: Allowed me to add a 2009 TV to a 2008 laptop via HDMI
text: This device connects to the VGA port and from there connects to a monitor or TV HDMI port, It WILL NOT work in the other direction, and it requires a source of 5V 1A power (any standard phone charger will work.) It comes with a USB charging cable and a 3.5mm cable for transmitting sound. Apparently it will not send sound interlaced with the HDMI signal through the HDMI cable (that you will need to supply.) For me this is not an issue because I am using it on a legacy laptop to send video only to a legacy TV, which I am using as extended video under Windows 7. Yes, it's using some ancient gear. But that is why I rated it five stars. Limitations: even if your TV or monitor is capable of higher resolutions this is not going to provide more than 720p from an old laptop or PC to an old monitor or TV. I know the specs say that this will go higher, but I could not get it there. Yet, going straight VGA from my T400 to my Sanyo TV it went into higher resolution as an extended screen. I am OK with the limitation because I am only using the TV as a second screen with MS Office, On an old Windows 7 system it's truly plug and play. I had it up and running without the scant instructions in mere minutes. For me it is a perfect solution.

title: After two years still working perfectly
text: I own a Blu-Ray player, but have that attached to a different TV. This DVD player has been my main device since my DVD collection outnumbers my Blu-Ray discs about ten to one. I've never had an issue with this player, and it has outperformed (and outlasted) the Sony players that I had been using. I purchased this two years ago (April 2019) and it was immediately apparent that this was solid from picture quality to the simplified controls on the remote. The only complaint - and it's a small one - is the latency between pushing the open tray button on the remote and when the tray actually opens. Overall, this has proven to be reliable and considering that it's two years old and still going strong, a great value as well as solidly functional.

title: Perfect for a Samsung Tab S6 Lite
text: Holds the Tab S6 Lite (a 10.4 inch tablet) firmly in both portrait and landscape positions. There is a cutout in the arm clamps the tablet in place to run your charging cable. I left my tablet in its third party folio style case, so connecting the charging cable to the tablet was a bit tricky. That is not the fault of this stand. Chalk it up to me being too lazy to remove the case. Do note that it does not come with instructions. However, the instructional video on this product page is, in my opinion. a lot more effective than a piece of paper and showed how to assemble and fine adjust the stand for both phones and tablets. This stand is stable and infinitely superior to the built-in kickstand that came with the folio cover.

title: Use it more than I thought I would
text: I purchased a pair of these in September 2020 - one for me, and one for my wife - and am surprised by how much I have become dependent upon it. It reads from my google calendar two hours from a scheduled event, so that is one useful feature. If I cannot remember a fact or quickly need to look up something, all I have to do is ask. I also use it as a clock. Except for the visual display of time and date, I could have accomplished everything I mentioned with my old hockey puck, A.K.A. "Dot." However, for some reason I did not use that one as much, so, perhaps the visual display catches my eye and reminds me that I have a fairly useful appliance that will do things for me. At any rate I use this a LOT more than I did the Dot. The real user in the house if my wife. She is constantly interacting with her Echo, but she was the household power user when she was using a Dot as well. While I feel as though I have gotten my money's worth from mine, the truth is my wife's daily (hourly?) use of hers makes the pair we have in our own home work spaces a bargain. Bottom line: cool device that has numerous uses - many of which I don't personally use. For some reason the screen inspires me to use mine a lot more than the screenless Dot, and honestly I rarely use the Echo visually.

title: Nice workhorse tablet
text: I finally upgraded my circa 2018 Galaxy Tab A to this. The Tab A and this one represent lower tier Galaxy tablets, meaning that they were not the flagship models. This one does everything I want. That said, my needs are relatively simple: mostly web browsing, and streaming movies from Netflix and Prime. Things that I absolutely love: - the old Tab A had 16GB and this has 128, a major increase in storage. - screen quality is amazing. Streaming videos is noticeably better from a visual standpoint. - in the same price range as the old Tab A, so when I upgraded I felt as though I was getting a much better tablet for about the same price as I paid for the old one in 2018. While the battery life on this new tablet is much better, it longer than I thought it would to charge it. And, yes, I am using the included fast charger and cable. When I was transferring my data and apps from the old tablet the power consumption of WiFi, CPU and whatnot resulted in the charging rate crawling to a snail pace. It was as though it was consuming power at close to the same rate as it was being charged. In normal use, the charging is faster, but still not as fast as I guessed it would be using a fast charger. Not a real issue, but I thought I would mention it to set expectations. As for the S-Pen, I am not currently using it. I am using an old fashion stylus in lieu of fingers to navigate (old habits die hard), and have not found a use for the S-Pen that requires its power and capabilities. It is certainly more than just a stylus, and is designed to integrate with some specific apps. I did watch a Youtube video explaining and demonstrating it, and it is impressive. But that is for a later time when I feel like experimenting and exploring. Overall I love this tablet and am not only pleased with its features and capabilities, but am very happy with its modest price tag.

title: Thick. Excellent protection
text: I purchased this for my wife to house her new Galaxy Tab S6 Lite (purchased at the same time.) The tablet is pretty thin, but this adds some girth to it. Not complaining - I (and my wife) appreciate the protection that this case affords. The case for her old tablet held the old one in place with straps, which were functional. This case has a synthetic material frame into which the Tab S6 snaps in. It is like having a bumper surrounding the edge of the the tablet, and it provides excellent protection. It is also why the S6 is no longer slim. Like I mentioned that is not an issue for her. Five stars because the tablet is a perfect fit. There is room for the pen that comes with the S6 on the inside of the cover (and it attaches via magnet without interfering with opening or closing the cover). The outer material of the case provides a bit of added padding, further protecting the tablet.All of the buttons, the camera lens, and the other cutouts are precision cut and perfect placed. Icing on the cake: the graphic gracing the cover is vivid and the coloration is both subtle and nuanced.

title: Reliable
text: I've been using this constantly since October 2020 and it's totally reliable. I cannot speak to speed because it's housed in an old Levono T400 running Windows 7. I have a separate one of these that I purchased as an external drive that I use to move files between my Windows 10 and my Chromebook laptops and it, too, is totally reliable (and is used many times a week.) If I find myself needing another external or internal SSD I will probably go with this particular brand because of my experiences thus far.

title: Works like a charm
text: In the nine months since purchasing this cable I have used it often to move large file systems from my work to personal computers (and even a Chromebook.) Never a problem, and the connections are as solid as the day it arrived. I have reached the point where I take it for granted that it will work every time I connect it to a different computer (usually with the same external drive attached.) Cannot ask for anything more than that.

title: Solid construction and performance
text: I've owned these since February 2021 and they have performed without a hitch. One of the cables is used in my vehicle and it is being constantly inserted into my phone. The C connector is just as good as the day I started using it nearly seven months ago, and the outer protector layer does its job. I use it with a Samsung A51 and my wife uses one of the cables from this pack with a Samsung A50 - both powered by a fast charger. I can say that these cables are one hundred percent compatible with our phones in particular, and fast charging in general. Plus the price is right.

title: Inexpensive replacement for an old dongle
text: My twelve year old bluetooth dongle gave up the ghost so I ordered this one based on price and reviews. The key feature was fast shipping via Prime. It worked out of the box (after I downloaded and installed drivers for my Windows 7 PC per the included instructions.) I can't make claims that this dongle is any faster or better than the dead one that it replaced, but it is just as fast and reliable. And easy to install. If I were not using an ancient version of Windows (by choice) it would literally be plug and play. Even with my need to add drivers it was a simple, quick job to get it up and running.

title: Amazing price (and performance)
text: I purchased this to replace a GLS Audio 20-Feet Ethercon CAT 6 cable that would not transmit phantom power because GLS stupidly cut one end of the shield for "ground lift". I was attempting to use that cable to connect a pair of LyxPro 4 Channel 3 Pin Multi Network XLR Cable Breakout boxes. Since I needed phantom power I went searching and came across this cable. I was dubious since the price was so low (and half the price of the GLS cable), but the reviews were good so I took a chance. This is the perfect solution and a cost-effective one at that. Nicely made too.

title: Excellent quality as long as you do not need to transmit phantom power
text: I am using this with a LyxPro 4-Channel pair of boxes connected via Ethercon. The quality of this cable is excellent, especially considering the lower price. It transmits noise-free too. And, finally, it is more flexible that I thought that it would be. If you are an old timer who remembers 10BASE2, this has about the same semi-flexible quality as that cable. Unfortunately it will not transmit phantom power, and I suspect that is because one end of the ground is lifted. However, if you don't need phantom power this is a great value based on price, quietness and overall construction.

title: Heavy duty and perfect for my Canon T7i
text: I stupidly broke my main tripod my accidentally placing a heavy crate on it. I wanted something sturdy and took a chance on this. It turned out to be even better than my more expensive tripod that it replaced, and the extra quick release plate is an added bonus. It allows me to quickly swap between my Canon and the also included cell phone mount for when my wife takes quick videos of my band's performances. Initially I thought the bottom leg extensions were a bit flimsy, but while they have flex they are rock solid. The flex allows them and the movable feet to provide a stable platform on uneven ground. The only thing that I don't care for is the center post that uses a crank to lift and retract. My gear is not that heavy, so a tension knob or ring would have worked better for me, but if you are using this for precision positioning (which I am not) you may find that feature to be to your advantage. The bag that comes with it is more than adequate for my needs, but is pretty basic. If you venture into harsh environments you may want to order a more robust bag.

title: Heavy duty and large capacity for the price
text: I purchased this as a drum kit hardware bag for a Tama Club Jam (small size) drum kit. It easily accommodates the center tom holder, the bass drum mounted cymbal holder, a Tama classic straight cymbal stand and a Tama HP30 bass drum pedal. I was also able to fit the floor tom legs. I could have managed the Tama classic hi-hat stand and classic snare drum stand, but that was pushing it and I was afraid that those last two components would have damaged the zipper. I am using a separate, small Tama hardware bag for those, plus a throne base and small stick bag. The padding is superior to the Tama hardware bag, and the overall construction, including zipper is as good if not better. This bag actually holds more than the Tama one that was designed for drum hardware, and is about half the cost. I also own a nice camera tripod that this case would easily protect and I will probably order another case for that. However, this case is a lot larger than the tripod, and I so rarely transport it, that the value proposition is nowhere as good as for my current use as a drum hardware bag. I am totally pleased with this bag!

title: Flimsy when fully extended, but good deal for casual use
text: I purchased this to mount a dB SPL meter. For that purpose this is an excellent deal and all the tripod one needs. For SLR cameras like my Canon T7i, this would be OK (and merely OK) as a table top tripod with the legs fully retracted. It wobble too much otherwise. For me this is all I need. Had I purchased for my camera it would have been returned. Bottom line: if you need to mount a stationary device or use it as a tabletop tripod you will love it and the price. Otherwise I recommend spending a few extra bucks and getting a tripod that is sturdier.

title: Fairly generic, but well made
text: Not too many years ago purchasing charging cables was hit-or-miss. No name brands like this one were usually shoddy and would not work will some phone brands. That has changed, so these days I shop strictly for price and have never been disappointed. I purchased these based solely on price and long length and am not disappointed. As an aside, I purchased this pack to power a device that required 5v via a micro USB cable. These cables do the job and are sturdy. For me it was a safe purchase.

title: Handy and sturdy
text: I've ordered these multiple times because they are reliable and come in lengths that are convenient for me. My only reason for reordering additional cables is they seem to walk off after I make one available to visitors or loan them. There is nothing fancy or particularity innovative about them - but I value reliability, price and convenience more than innovation. If you want cables that are easy to spot in a sea of black or white ones, and are dependable these are a safe purchase.

title: Cloning? This is probably not your best option
text: I thought that I'd save a few bucks and grab this instead of the Crucial SSD in approximately the same size that was about ten bucks more. Unfortunately I did not read the full description and discovered that this does not come with cloning software or any software. The Crucial drive comes with cloning software that is easy to use and effective. All is not lost, however. Although this is listed as an internal drive, the case is sturdy enough to use as an external drive without purchasing a separate enclosure. All you need is a SATA to USB cable and a spare USB port on your device, and you are good to go. I am using a StarTech cable that supports USB 3.0 and everything works like a charm. For the price and the capacity this is a decent deal if you are looking for extra storage. If you are thinking about cloning, though, look elsewhere. Make sure that whichever brand that you get comes with bundled software. A number of other brands, including that one that I ultimately purchased for the cloned drive, come with OEM versions of an app called Acronis True Image. The bundled version will only work with the brand of SSD that it comes with, but for replicating a drive for safety, upgrading, etc. it works well.

title: Pretty solid and reliable.
text: My initial purchase was in May 2020, and they had proven to be so reliable that I ordered more in August. The cable is flexible, but well protected. The strain reliefs are solid. The reliefs are not flexible, but their rigidity ensures that the ends going into the connectors do have leeway to flex. The mating connectors fit snugly and stay inserted. I am using one on a Chromebook, and the others on two Samsung A50 phones. The durability is why I purchased more, and I will purchase even more from this brand if I need more or additional spares.

title: OK for the price. Keyboard not that great, and the DVD player did not work.
text: Not bad for the price, but there were some issues. The biggest is the Lenovo DVD app for playing DVDs kept crashing. I remedied that by downloading a free player that was stable. The keyboard is atrocious. I purchased this thinking that it had the same, superior, keyboard that my Lenovo T400 has. Sadly it does not. Yes, it's a step up from the "chicklet" style keys that Apple made in vogue, but not by much. If you are looking for something inexpensive to browse the web and are not ready to commit to a Chromebook, this is probably a decent choice. I do recommend that you lower expectations (especially is a quality keyboard for touch typing is important to you.)

title: Vast improvement in performance and capacity over mechanical drive
text: The company for which I work sent me this to upgrade my Levono T400. I was running out of space on the mechanical, 250GB SATA internal drive. Not to mention that the drive was starting to make alarming noises. When this drive arrived I used a SATA to USB cable to connect it to one of my T400 USB ports, downloaded the free app that was recommended in instructions that came with the SSD drive, and cloned my mechanical internal drive to the new one. That process took about four hours since the old drive was getting very full. While that was going on I went on Youtube and found a video that showed how to remove the original internal drive from the laptop. I was expecting a nightmare, but lucked out because the Lenovo T400's internal drive takes less than five minutes to swap out. Obviously your experience is going to be different depending on the computer that you are swapping the internal drive. If you are using this as an external, then you don't need the app, nor do you need to swap out anything. Just get a SATA to USB cable, connect it, format the new drive and you are done. Some reviews complained about this drive being slow compared to other SSD drives. I cannot comment on that. I will say that compared to a mechanical drive this one is blazing fast. And since there are no moving parts, very quiet. A few final notes: raw capacity of my drive was a little over 953GB, but formatted capacity is 887GB. Also, my install was on a computer running Windows 7 Professional and there were no issues.

title: Very sturdy and rack-friendly
text: I purchased mine to use as a shelf for a small mixer. Although this shelf is overkill for the relatively lightweight mixer, it will hold a LOT more weight. I am guessing that it could easily accommodate twenty-plus pounds. The reason I cited this as rack friendly is the mounting holes have enough play in them to work with 19" racks that are not precisely constructed. The extra slop allowed me to easily mount this in a rack that was a little off in exact dimensions. Overall I am thoroughly pleased with the construction, finish and price.

title: Excellent value for 'vanilla' configurations
text: I needed to extend a 15 foot HDMI cable from an HDMI switch box to an HDMI port on a smart TV. The switch box is carrying video from a camera, as well as a signal from a ChromeCast. While the above application is relatively simple and just about any HDMI cable will handle my requirements, this cable's cost point and the fact that each end mated perfectly with the target connectors made it an ideal solution for my needs. It has worked flawlessly since I received it and I expect a long service life.

title: Rock solid and holds my Canon T7i in any position
text: I purchased this to mount an independent light source (a RALENO Led Video Light) but also tested it with my Canon T7i camera. The Led video light is light and is no real test. The camera is heavier, yet this small ball head held it steady at any angle with no need to overtighten. The threads (male and female) mated perfectly with my tripods, camera and other adapters. In my opinion this is a precision-machined ball head that is heavy-duty and reliable. I have yet to find any flaws or other issues with it after a month of frequent use.

title: Perfect for my application; battery life is less than advertised
text: I use this to illuminate objects that I am photographing (mainly small items that I sell on various sites), but also to provide extra light for smaller rooms when I am making videos of my band at rehearsal and/or on gigs. The battery life is touted to be 90-110 minutes under maximum illumination power, but I have gotten around 75 minutes. For me, this is still pretty good I especially like the fact that the battery is integrated, so there is no need to purchase extra batteries and chargers like the other lights that I investigated before purchasing this one. Moreover, this will work with the same external batteries that I use for my tablets and phones, as well as the wall chargers and cables for those devices. Illumination is soft and can go from warm to cold, depending on your shooting environment. Since I am by no means a professional (or even an advanced) photographer, I found this light to be all that I need for easy to shoot videos and stills. One thing that I am on the fence about is the mount. It is a little shaky in that it tends to not firmly hold the light steady when installed in my camera's hot shoe. I can live with it since I keep my rig stationary, but if you are on the move that mount is going to be the weak spot. Despite my dislikes I intend to purchase one more of these as both a spare and as a second light source for some shots that will benefit from the added illumination.

title: Works perfectly with my Canon 800D
text: No issues whatsoever with this battery in my Canon 800D (T7i.) There are a few things that I don't like. First, the battery life per charge is about 75% of my genuine Canon batteries. for someone on a budget these are an alternative to Canon batteries if you are willing to compromise. Another issue is the charger is flimsy and not as travel-worthy as I would like. But you can use it in a vehicle or powered by an external battery pack. Just make sure that you have adequate protection for the charger if you are planning to use it in the field. Also, note that only one battery can be charged at a time. Overall, I knew the main limitations when I purchased this set, so am pleased (especially by the fact that my camera accepts them!) If you are a casual photographer who wants some spares without spending a fortune these are a good deal. If you want the same performance as original Canon batteries, you will be better off getting those.

title: Thick and heavy, but fast and beautiful screen
text: I upgraded from my old Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 8.4-Inch, and the difference is like night and day. This is a fairly basic tablet, but much faster than the Tab Pro, and the screen is exponentially nicer. Do know that this is not some slim, light and trendy tablet. It's surprisingly thick and heavy. However, it is not so thin that it will bend like yet another Samsung that I own - a Tab Pro 12.2. The 10.1 inch screen has a lot more real estate than the 8.4 this table is replacing. The major reason why I rated this so highly is the price, combined with the obvious difference in both speed and display. It's not cutting edge, but is a workhorse.

title: Extra heavy duty
text: I purchased both a 15 and a 25 foot cable to run from a splitter box to two monitors. The video and audio were perfect, especially since the splitter input was fed by a 10 HDMI cable (a different brand), making the total length for the longest run approximately 35 feet. Be aware that these cables are stiff and not easy to work with right out of the box. Since my use was to have them permanently attached to the splitter and monitors there were no issues. On the other hand, if you are planning to run one of these from an adapter connected to a DSLR, I would recommend checking out lighter duty cables. Overall, I am more than pleased with both the construction and the price. For my specific use they work perfectly and are a solid value.

title: Simple, easy to set up and works well
text: I purchased this splitter to both simultaneously display video output from my Canon T7i camera, as well as stream video via a ChromeCast to two monitors in my rehearsal space. For less than twenty bucks I was able to accomplish that. Set-up was as simple as plugging in the HDMI cables and power supply. I was a little confused about the tiny switch that has two modes: Copy and Auto. I selected Auto and everything worked. The instructions are not nearly as useful as the product description on this product page. The unit is fairly small. I plan to glue some Velcro on the bottom of the case and affix it to one of my monitor stands. Bottom line: I am pleased with both the price and ease of use and awarded it five solid stars accordingly.

title: Heavy-duty and all metal except for decorative parts
text: This was actually overkill for me because I mounted a light, 24" monitor on it. However, I was able to assemble it without reading the instructions step-by-step. It only took a give minute glance through them to get all the information that I needed to assemble it. Note: it comes with two tools: a hex wrench and a stamped wrench. I needed to add in a screw driver, and found that using my socket wrench was a lot more effective than the stamped one that was provided. With the exception of the end caps on the feet and a piece that fit over the center post where the pole connected to the foot assembly all of the parts were solid metal. That includes the wheels, which are very heavy duty (the actual wheel component is a high density synthetic material that is heavy duty.) This stand has a fairly small footprint - at least when compared to the speaker stand and adapter that I had been using - and is easy to roll around. Overall, this is a high quality stand that is not likely to tip over by accident due to both its weight and design.

title: Solid protection and vivid colors
text: My Tab A fit perfectly. I was initially concerned that it did not feature the plastic snap-in holder like many covers, but the faux leather arrangement that holds the tablet in place offers good protection. One feature that I like is the thickness of the case, which is why I have confidence in its ability to safely house my tablet. A plus that I did not notice when I purchased it is it comes with a stylus and has a loop to accommodate it. Since I use a stylus (and my other cases do not have that feature, nor a look for holding one), this quickly became my favorite case. Unfortunately I use my tablet flat on a table, desk or across my lap, so I cannot vouch for the ergonomics of the stand feature. Also, do read the instructions. In my haste to insert my tablet into it I struggled with the faux leather part that houses the tablet without realizing that there is a velcro strip that needs to be separated to allow you to slide in the tablet. The fault is mine for not reading the instructions, which are clearly written and illustrated. Overall, this is the perfect case - for me - and the price was right earning it five stars in my opinion.

title: Nicely constructed and a bargain for simple mounting without need for adjustable viewing angles
text: Easy to install. Using the supplied anchors I was able to securely mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465SMH 24" 1080p LED Monitor]]. Granted, the ViewSonic is lightweight, but the built-in bubble level on this mount made the entire install process a breeze. Note that you do not have a lot of flexibility when it comes to adjusting viewing angle. My install took that into account since I wanted my monitor mounted like a picture frame. This is well constructed and perfect for thin monitors like the one I installed. My main reason for the the high rating is price, followed by construction, and finally the integrated bubble level. This is a bargain if you are mounting a lightweight, thin monitor and are not concerned with viewing angle flexibility.

title: Keeps my iPad charged while controlling my Yamaha P-115 keyboard
text: I purchased this to power my iPad Pro while using it as a controller for my [[ASIN:B00UHBGE7A Yamaha P115 88-Key Weighted Action Digital Piano]]. I had been using the [[ASIN:B014VGHG0U Apple MD821AM/A Lightning to USB Camera Adapter]], but while it worked as an interface to my piano, the iPad's battery would drain too quickly. This adapter solved that problem. You can power from a wall charging unit or one of the many external battery packs on the market, while simultaneously controlling your Yamaha P-115. The iPad stays charged, and that makes this adapter a godsend to me. Note: I have NOT tried connecting drives, or other USB devices to my iPad using this adapter, so cannot comment one way or the other about those scenarios.

title: Identical to Yamaha's OEM power supply at a fraction of the price
text: Identical to the OEM power supply in all respects. The cable length is the same eight feet, the strain relief is the same, and even the wire gauge is identical. The most important part is that it works, and does not heat up any more than the original Yamaha part. Plus the price, which is about half that of the original Yamaha power supply, makes it a bargain. I purchased mine as a spare to ensure that we do not cancel performances because of a lost or failed power supply.

title: Needs some improvement, but is truly useful (especially for the price)
text: I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple. The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use. Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. The same for the calendar: you can get all events for a single day, but not for a week, or weekend so you still have to fire up a calendar app on your phone, tablet or computer if you want to get a sense of how busy you will be over a period longer than a day. Still, for fifty bucks each - plus the discount for purchasing a three pack - this is a decent device that has proven to be surprisingly useful in my home. My girlfriend instantly took to hers too. In the week or so that I have been using it I find that I am growing increasingly dependent on mine for streaming music from Pandora, looking up quick information while I am reading or watching a documentary, and letting me know what is on my calendar for a specific day. I have one of mine connected via bluetooth to a [[ASIN:B019PGACR0 LD Systems MAUI 5 Channel PA System]], and my girlfriend has hers connected to a [[ASIN:B00W8O6MJO Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker]], both of which greatly out perform the larger Echo. However I also use my other Dot with just its integrated speaker and it is more than adequate, even for streaming music since I have it on an end table. Overall, for the current fifty bucks this is a bargain (warts notwithstanding), and while I purchased mine more out of curiosity all three have proven to be useful and practical.

title: Runs a little warm, but works with Amazon Basics batteries
text: Runs a little warm, but works as well as my three year old [[ASIN:B00MPWFO3O Knox 16-Bay Rapid Ni-MH AA/AAA Battery Charger]]. In fact, this and the Knox look similar (except for color and logo). I charged a batch of [[ASIN:B007B9NV8Q AmazonBasics AA Rechargeable Batteries]] with no issues, so this charger and those batteries are compatible. I also charged four Knox AAA batteries after the Amazon ones finished. No issues other than the batteries from the AA batch were warm when I removed them. This (like the Knox unit that I also own) comes with both a wall and a car charger. For me that is a major selling point because I use AA batteries in some wireless microphones my band uses for some gigs. I can keep standby batteries charging in my vehicle in case some need to be swapped out of the mics during intermissions. Bottom line, I am not sure what the heat does to my battery life, but I do love the convenience of this charger.

title: Sturdy and electrically well constructed.
text: I am totally impressed with the cable. The outer jacket appears to be tough, but the best thing is both ends are precise fits. I am using a pair of these to extend the distance between powered speakers and surge protector strips on stage. These can take some abuse being dragged across less than smooth surfaces (although I am not sure about rough-finished concrete or brick). The key, though, is the 25 footers that I purchased do not get hot during prolonged use, and are rated at 125 VAC at 10 Amps. For me the safety factor is important, and I am one hundred percent confident that these are safe in indoors environments. I am so impressed that I plan to order a pair of 10 and 15 foot cables for times when 25 feet is a bit much.

title: Easy to use in receiver mode - a little tricky in transmitter mode, but still solid
text: I received mine as a free review sample. This is physically smaller than the photos lead you to believe (about 2.5x1 3/8 inches), but the switch and button, and charging port are easy to access and use. If I have a single wish it would be that the short 3.5mm cable were removable instead of fixed. That would allow you to not only use longer cables if you wanted, but also make it easy to replace that cable if it were to become damaged. This is easy to use - there is a quick reference card in addition to an instruction sheet. I was able to have this up and running in receiver mode within minutes. Placing it in transmit mode took two tried, but that still took less than five minutes. Mine will auto-reconnect as long as I do not connect to any other bluetooth receivers between uses with this one. Since I usually connect to a different receiver at home I need to manually reconnect to this one after using the other. However, if this is the last receiver to which I have connected, it will reconnect to my Note 4 phone when I power this on. My main use is as a receiver going into the 3.5mm AUX port of a Fender Mustang Amp. In that capacity it works perfectly, especially when I stream a backing track into the amp via this receiver. I did test the transmitter mode to make sure it worked, but honestly do not use it. Overall, this is as reliable as any of a half dozen bluetooth receivers that I own. It does not drop out or flutter even if I am separated by a wall, although it is sensitive to distances further than twenty meters AND a wall. The nice bonus is it can be placed in transmitter mode for enabling remote speakers, but for me it's the receiver mode that is going to be the primary use. In that respect it's rock solid.

title: Excellent construction and will allow plugging into AUX ports of devices encased in OtterBox Defender cases
text: I received these as a free review sample. I also own various other high-end cable brands and this is the equal of most of them (I do have a few that are world class, but they are also a lot more expensive.) In that respect I consider these to be a great value. My main use is to connect this cable to dual RCA tape out on my mixing board using an adapter. I then run the angled end into an AUX in on a small speaker array that I sometimes use as a monitor. Note that I have not used this for studio applications, so cannot comment on how noise-free this cable truly in. For live performances, though, it's solid and as noise-free as I need. While testing this out I discovered that either end will fit the AUX jack on my Note 4 phone, even while it's encased in an [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] if you own and use a Defender series case you already know that many cables will not work with it. Overall, the construction is first rate, and for live applications (or plugging phones into a device protected by a Defender series case), this cable is a bargain and is super reliable.

title: Inexpensive solution for upgrading some older vehicles
text: I received this as a free review sample. Since Vince McLaren's exceptionally helpful review of August 21, 2016 covers what I also discovered, take the time to read his (and mark it helpful because he did an excellent job.) It took me a few weeks to get around to writing this review because I needed to order an adapter for the 1998 Ford Explorer it was destined for, and also to have it professionally installed. The adapter I purchased is [[ASIN:B01ES32D7C Fits Ford Explorer 1998-2001 Double DIN Stereo Harness Radio Install Dash Kit]]. There are other kits by different brands for most vehicles. One of those will allow you to install (or have professionally installed) in older vehicles where this system will add some modern touches. The reasons why I subtracted a star are the touchscreen is not as sensitive as I had hoped (not unusable, but frustrating sometimes), and the instructions are not that great. A professional will have no problem installing this unit, and there is a comprehensive wiring diagram in the product photos on this page. If you are planning to do the install yourself, refer to that photo to get an idea of the complexity of the job. For me, the bluetooth capability and radio make this is great bargain in my opinion. I have a back-up camera that attaches to a license plate holder that adds that feature (you will need to provide your own camera, but they are inexpensive.) While this will display videos, you will need to load them via the TF card slot because this has no DVD (or CD) slot for that kind of media. Frankly, streaming music via bluetooth obviates the need for a CD (in my opinion), and I do not foresee myself ever needing to use any video player in the driver/front passenger compartment of a vehicle. If those are important to you, this is not the in-dash solution for you. My overall impression is this is a good - and very inexpensive - solution for upgrading in-dash entertainment and hands free solutions in older vehicles. Before you plunk down your money, though, make sure that this will fit your vehicle, and that there is an adapter kit available for installing it in your vehicle's make, model and year.

title: Excellent use of storage space, great construction and innovative features (but one shortcoming)
text: I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I docked it a star is the active tablet window needs improvement (and that could have been one of the stand-out features if properly designed.) Here is the problem: it's the perfect size for an iPad Air 2, but could not accommodate my Tab 2 10.1 inch tablet. It did hold my Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 (even in an Otterbox Defender case). The vinyl window wrinkles and also reduces sensitivity when you interact with your tablet. If the active tablet window is unimportant to you, then the rest of this backpack is a winner. Pairing my phone to the bluetooth speakers was as simple as flipping a switch and scanning for it on my phone's settings. And the speakers are loud with better than expected sound quality. I was pleased with that - some thought went into the speakers. The padding is more than ample for protecting electronics, and there are sufficient pockets for the geekiest geek. What I like, though, is the storage areas are not overly complex. I own a Booq bag that is a storage dream come true, but almost requires a photographic memory to remember were all of the pockets are. This one is designed much simpler, but still efficient and effective. Construction (except for the active tablet window) is first rate. The tablet window is marred by a difficult zipper, whereas all of the other zippers on this bag are sturdier and smooth. The outer fabric seems tough (I have not had it long enough to make any claims beyond that), and all of the seams are reinforced, straight and tight.
