It's very comfortable and can be adjusted to evenly distribute the weight of a fully loaded pack. Considering that the bag itself is somewhat heavy this is a major plus for me. I do want to note one thing about the backup battery: it is rated at (and stores) the full 4000mAh. However, like all batteries using this one's technology it's only 70% efficient, so expect about 2800mAh of usable capacity. That is not a flaw in this bag, but a reality that I wanted to point out so your expectations are properly set. Overall, this is a well made bag with some innovative features (battery back-up and bluetooth speakers). If the active tablet window is not an important feature it's definitely worth considering. This one will be replacing my Booq because the storage is there without the complexity.

title: Beautifully made from quality materials (and NO split leather or other shortcuts)
text: I received this as a free review sample. Frankly, this is probably the best crafted bag I have owned in the past twenty years (and I have one from Booq.) The reason for the high rating is the leather parts are the real thing. Too often these days you get split leather, which is a thin veneer of leather over polyurethane. Not the case here - the leather is not only the real thing, but is generously cut. The construction is excellent in every respect. The canvas is high quality, all of the stitching and seams are straight and tight, and reinforcement points are heavy-duty. Moreover, the zippers are as heavy-duty as the other parts. Unlike many bags (even high end ones) that have a chemical odor when you unpack them for the first time, this one does not. The lining is synthetic, which resists water (but I would not claim this to be waterproof.) The snaps, reinforcing rivets and other metal are designed to look like brass, but are probably steel since a magnet will stick to them. The pockets and compartments make this an excellent work bag that can accommodate smaller laptops. I use mine for my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet]], which is an easy fit. That leaves me room to spare for other odds and ends, as well as music charts. The main interior pocket is about 13 7/8 inches wide by 10 inches tall. If you are purchasing this for a laptop use those dimensions to determine if this bag will work for you. Overall, I am not only pleased, but surprised by how well this is made and the quality of the materials. I want to emphasize that this may not fit many of the larger laptops on the market, but is still a great bag for books, tablets and assorted other gear. I hate gushing, but in this case I think the bag warrants it.

title: As good as an OEM Samsung cable at a greatly reduced price point.
text: I received these as free review samples. Since there are other reviews extolling the virtues of these cables I will keep my comments short and to the point. The biggest plus is these cables both synch and charge my Note 4 phone. Nearly all cables will charge it, but not all will synch. Also, when using an OEM Samsung charger that is QC certified, the cables in this two-pack will fully support the QC specification. Using other than Samsung cables I commonly get a message telling me that my charging is slow because of the cable. Not so with the cables in this pack. While the braided metal jacket on these is sturdy, I am not sure one way or the other that is a plus. I did wonder if it would pick up electromagnetic radiation interference, but the one I am using in my vehicle has not as far as I know. I do know that the pair of cables in the pack I received cost less than a single Samsung OEM cable and the performance is identical. For me that warrants the five star rating I awarded.

title: Inexpensive DAC that is easy to install and performs nicely
text: I received this as a free review sample. I actually had a need for one of these because I wanted to run an audio signal out of my Yamaha receiver to an older analog reel-to-reel recorder. The receiver had a toslink out, and the recorder had RCA in. This box was the perfect DAC. My signals were noise free, but understand that I was not running the analog cable more than a meter. So in that respect I did not have an adequate test of noise characteristics for longer cable runs. Moreover, I did not really use the volume feature. I set it mid way and used controls on the recorder for volume level. However, for my needs this worked perfectly. The instructions are a little weak, but anyone who knows what a DAC is should be able to connect and use this without them. The power supply is a standard 5V DC at 1 Amp with a center positive connector. I ran it for an extended length of time and it did not overheat (I have learned from experience to test power supplies because of occasional failures and issues.) Overall, this is a reasonably priced DAC that I found to be easy to use. The performance was what I had hoped, so am pleased with it.

title: A little noisy and not exactly a micro-sized projector, but versatile and a cheap way to get a big screen
text: I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because in small quarters the fan can get irritating, and also the picture area is a little skewed. The latter is not enough to ruin a video, but combined with the fan noise I felt that this falls into the four star category. To be fair, this is about on par with other portable projectors in this price range and sharing the general form factor. On the plus side, this is an inexpensive way to get a large screen TV (assuming that your wall is the screen), that does a credible job of projecting movies, TV and presentations. I tested it using a Chromecast and streaming video from YouTube to my phone, then casting from my phone to the Chromecast dongle connected to one of the HDMI ports in the rear. No issues and it was actually a treat. I also tested it with an old Roku in an HDMI port streaming a movie from Netflix. To be sure, neither experience compares to my HD TV screen and surround sound system, but this does not come close to the price tags of those. Bang for the buck this is excellent if you are in a budget. Frankly, I did not test the other ports, but do want to point out that the 'SD' card port is really USB A that will take a flash drive or an SD card using an adapter. Actually, I think that is a plus as well because flash drives are cheap and a 32GB one can hold a respectable amount of movies, home videos or presentations. Sound quality is not spectacular, but is definitely adequate. Overall, this is as good as any projector among the four that I have either owned or tested, and is better than some. It would easily be a five star projector if it had a quieter fan. If you can live with that you will probably love it.

title: Especially useful if you use 18650 batteries; fast charging and auto-detect works very well
text: I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because it does not center AA batteries very well in the left slot for some reason, and I got a spark at the plug the first time I plugged this into an outlet. That did not recur after a few more tests, but once was enough to give me pause. Up front, note that this WILL NOT work with alkaline rechargeable batteries and the instructions clearly state that. It definitely works with the batteries listed, and I am thrilled to have this charger for the growing pile of 18650 batteries that I have accumulated. My testing was confined to Ni-MH AA and AAA, 18650, and a few battery backups I use for phones and tablets. I let this device auto-detect instead of attempting to manually set voltage and current, and it was spot on in every case. It is relatively fast charging (especially for the Ni-MH AA and AAA batteries), and aside from the spark mentioned above has proven to be reliable. My only direct comparison for recharging speed is for the AA and AAA batteries that charged up 25% faster with this unit than with the Knox charger I had been using for those. I have no baseline for the 18650 and backup batteries that I tested. I did not test the protection features cited in the specs other than polarity because I did not have depleted or non-rechargeable batteries. I also did not receive the optional car charger adapter, so cannot discuss that. I will say that for the batteries that I did test this performed flawlessly. A final note: the display is a bit confusing, and the instructions will put you to sleep. However, I highly recommend that you carefully go through the instructions because there are some important caveats and safety precautions of which you need to be aware. Overall, I am pleased with this charging solution and highly recommend it if you use any if the IMR type batteries and especially the 18650 size.

title: Surprisingly good phones at an entry level price - not optimum for all styles of music though
text: I received these as a free review sample. They are one of three different models of Spider phone that I have tested, and these are the loudest and deepest from a low frequency perspective (to my ears) among the three. Like another reviewer, I noticed that the right and left channels are inverted, but that is not a problem for me. The sound quality is very good across the high, medium and low frequency bands. These are compressed at the high end, with a definite bias in the mid and low frequency ranges. The mids are very realistic, while the low end is a bit on the processed side if you are listening to acoustic jazz, or similar styles of music. For modern music they are perfect. Factor that into your purchase decision. I do need to mention that these can get a little on the loud side, especially if you are listening from a device that automatically attenuates SPL levels on phones and you opt to override that setting. For example, my Note 4 phone will attenuate direct AUX connections, but I can override that and listen full volume. These phones can actually damage hearing if you do that and listen at max for prolonged periods of time. For me the attenuated setting is still plenty loud. Overall sound quality and level is perfect for modern music, especially genres that are bass and drum centric. For acoustic music (jazz, Americana, older country and the such), these are a little too processed. For those styles I recommend that you consider the [[ASIN:B01BY0262O Spider USA SPEB112-BK Jade Series Metal Earbuds]].

title: Decent, but not the best - there are some caveats
text: I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the grabbing arms are not spring loaded. Indeed, they are a friction, pinion design that makes it a little more difficult to insert and remove your phone while the assembly is attached to your windshield or dash. Also, before you make a final decision, make sure your phone will fit. The maximum width is 3.5 inches, and that measurement is absolute. My Note 4 would fit when I removed it from its case, but with two of the cases that I swap it between, it would not fit. Take that into account. This will definitely stay where you attach it! It even adhered to the pebble grain covering on my vehicle's dash, but it was a but too awkward there for me. It is perfect on the windshield, though and that is its final resting place for me. It's also rock steady, so if you are on bumpy roads the display is not apt to jiggle, which is a nice thing of you are glancing at your phone's GPS map (something I do often.) Basically, this is a decent mount, but not the best (in my opinion.) On the other hand, it's definitely not the worst either!

title: Entry level price; upper intermediate level performance - worth checking out
text: I received these as a free review sample. Note: these are NOT bluetooth. They are wired ear buds that should fit any device with a 3.5mm output jack. My rating is based on both sound quality and price. The list on these are in the twenty buck range, but the sound quality, in a blindfold test, would fool you into thinking that these are a tier above other buds in this price range. The mid range and lower end of the frequency spectrum seem to be emphasized, with highs a bit compressed. These are perfect for casual (and even some critical) listening. An audiophile would probably not like the bias and compression, but most other folks will appreciate it. I mentioned the 'lower' end of the frequency spectrum. At the lowest end it is deep, but not thumping (although it will reproduce 20Hz, which you can feel if not hear.) For anyone listening to acoustic or lightly amplified music, and especially music that uses a big chunk of the audio frequency spectrum (for consumer phones), these are surprisingly good. There is a disparity between the product description's claim that there have flat, tangle-free cable and the actual cable, which is tangle-free, but round. I want to point that out because one of the things I check when reviewing is any differences between product specs and claims, and what you actually receive. Basically, these are priced at the upper end of entry level phones, but are good enough to pass for high end intermediate level phones.

title: Convenient and perfect for up to 60 Watt devices
text: I purchased one of these from a different source to power a 12V portable fridge that was designed to operate from a lighter socket. This converter puts out a full five Amps, which is 60 Watts (5 Amps x 12 volts.) In addition, this will easily charge tablets and phones if you use a multi-port USB vehicle charger with it. In fact, any 12V DC device like an air pump, etc., that is designed to operate from a vehicle lighter socket is fair game as long as it does not require more than 5 Amps or is rated at 60 Watts or less (and to be on the safe side I would probably lower that to 50 Watts.) This runs fairly cool as long as you are not operating it at the edge of its capacity or for sustained periods, and mine has never gotten so hot that it alarmed me.

title: Light duty, and good for hanging banners indoors - not for outside use
text: I purchased this to hand a band banner behind us on stage. In that respect this is perfect because the dimensions are totally as described in the product description, the product photo is accurate, and I knew up front that this was going to be a lightweight support. There are some limitations. The first is although you can extend the tripod legs to provide decent stability, this is not for environments where passers by can bump into it. Also, with a banner or backdrop clipped to it, it is not going to work well outdoors unless there is zero breeze. It would not take much to catch a light breeze in the 'sail' area of a backdrop or banner and topple this. However, for me this is a major plus because it's light and easy to carry. If you are a musician you already know the advantage. The cross-member sections are about an inch in diameter, so you will need large clips. The bag was a surprise. I was expecting some cheap, vinyl bag that was an afterthought. While the bag is lightweight, it is designed specifically with pockets for the two stands and the four cross-member sections. Assembly and disassembly are fast and easy. I marked the posts with small pieces of tape so I could quickly level it after I initially got it to the correct height and leveled it. I recommend that you do the same because the first time it takes patience and a bubble level (or tape measure) to get it set up correctly.

title: Truly useful and if you are a musician who uses pedal boards, this is very handy
text: If you are a musician who deals with pedals and pedal boards, or has other gear that uses DC power within the range of this power supply, this can be a life saver. Since I own pedal boards that use both 9V DC (Boss and a few other guitar effects pedals), and 12V DC (TC Helicon), this is a spare that sits in my gig bag in case I misplace or damage one of the wall warts that powers those pedals. Also, because this can put out up to 1.2 Amps, it can power three of my TC Helicon pedals off of a power cable chain. I usually employ a TC Helicon power supply for that, but since I use this one as a spare, it is always ready if needed. I have tested it with the pedals and verified that it will power all of the ones I use simultaneously. If you do get this and find that the adapters that come with it are not the sizes you need, you may want to consider this add on set by another brand: [[ASIN:B00CMMO6AE Generic Universal 28 DC Power 5.5x2.1mm Jack to 28 Plug Power Adapter for Notebook]]. For my needs, though, this is all I require and I am very pleased with it.

title: Excellent cable at a bargain price, but read on if you are using it on a crowded pedal board
text: I purchased this cable based on my very positive experience with some other cables that I ordered from this brand ([[ASIN:B003L18XKE Monoprice 104749 1.5-Feet Premier Series XLR Male to XLR Female 16AWG Cable]].) Like the XLR cables, this one is slightly different in size that what is described. Overall length is 18.5 inches and the cable that is approximately 17 7/8 inches when measured from the housing of the connectors. For me that is not a real issue, but what may be an issue of you are planning to use these with pedals mounted on a pedal board, the length from the strain reliefs to the top of the connector housings is 2 inches. Also, the TRS end's tip to the top of the housing is 2.25 inches, with 5/8" of the housing protruding when the TRS end is fully inserted. Those numbers should help you to determine if this will work in your particular pedal board. The cable is noise free in my application, which is interconnecting a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1G9O TC Helicon VoiceTone Correct XT Vocal Effects Processor]] to a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1SHO TC Helicon VoiceTone H1 Vocal Effects Processor]]. I did notice that the housing ends are split, two piece design that are held together by the strain reliefs. Also, at the end of the strain relief, the bend radius of the 16AWG cable is very tight, which was a pleasant surprise. Bottom line: the only potential issue I see with this cable the it may not work well on a pedal board with tightly spaced pedals. In all other respects it has proven to be mechanically and electrically sound, and I intend to order more.

title: One of the easiest-to-use and install dashcams I have come across
text: I received this as a free review sample. M.Erb's extremely detailed and helpful video review of May 14, 2016 covers this in a great deal of depth. I'll add my thoughts and reasons why I also rated this five solid stars. First, I have tested and used at least a dozen dashcams, many of which were excellent in their own right. However, the shortfall in each was the screen and a complicated array of controls. With this one your screen is your smartphone or tablet, and your controls are those that are provided with the app you need to download (for free) to control the camera and settings. There is a separate remote control, which is really just a clicker that does one thing: triggers a short video and a snapshot. Another thing I personally love is the mounting kit. This one, properly used, will run your power cable in an unobtrisive manner (well, as unobtrusive as possible), and the cable is sufficiently long to run the cable from close to my rear view mirror to my dashboard lighter socket in my 2016 Outlander. Other dashcams either forced you to put up with dangling cable or - in one case - have the power and video feed cables professionally installed. Plus this uses a standard USB cable with USB A on one end and micro USB on the other. Some dashcams require a proprietary cable with a barrel connector that makes it difficult to replace if necessary. Video quality is not award winning (indeed, the camera lens is a fisheye), but is still more than sufficient to capture accidents and even scenic drives. You can also use this for other than a dashcam. I discovered that will fit in a standard microphone clip that fits a Shure SM58 (i.e., a very common size.) You can use up to a 64GB micro SD card, which will store almost eleven hours of video. Most dashcams are limited to 32GB. The instruction manual is adequate, but not comprehensive, and it also does not cover the software and its capabilities. I hope the company rectifies that, which will make this dashcam even more user friendly, especially for novices. However, most folks do not want to wade through a manual anyway, and the one that comes with this will get you going. Bottom line: as far as dashcams go, this one is probably the easiest one to use that I have come across. My FAVORITE feature is simplicity that allows my phone or tablet to be the screen and controls.

title: Decent construction and great for my Tab 3 10.1 tablet
text: I received this as a free review sample. It nicely accommodates my Tab 3 10.1 tablet, but is just a bit too small for my Tab Pro 12.2. Up front, there is a chemical odor that lingers for about a day, but it dissipates afterwards. You can hasten the removal of the odor by wrapping a teaspoon of baking soda in a washcloth, securing it with a rubber band and leaving it in the case (opened) for an hour. This is somewhat spongy feeling, and affords a little protection against falls. Frankly, it is not going to protect a tablet against a waist high fall on an irregular, hard surface unless the tablet is in a ruggedized case. On the other hand, it was not designed for that, so I am not docking it any stars. It's as good as any other case that I own. Other things I like are the sturdy, dual zippers, and the bottom reinforcement. I would have loved a handle, but this is a portfolio style case, so I am still very pleased.

title: Decent as an external USB storage device, but read critical reviews carefully if you plan to use it as a boot drive
text: I received this as a free review sample. Since there are reviews that cite premature failures I waited a full month before writing a review. In the ensuing time I have been using this as backup storage on two laptops - one running Win7 and the other running XP. I have had zero failures, although this is not the speediest SSD I own (which accounts for the subtracted star). Over the course of any given day this drive is used about thirty minutes to backup Outlook files and any new documents that I may have created or edited. When I first initialized it the usable storage was around 111GB, so be aware that there is some overhead if you are expecting the full 120GB. This is NOT uncommon so I did not ding it another star for that. Mine is housed in a [[ASIN:B00K6I9NL8 Patriot Gauntlet 3 SATA III 6 Gb/s USB 3.0 Compatible Hard Disk Drive Enclosure]], which is suitable for my uses and not a bad enclosure if you are planning to use this drive the same way I am. If you are planning to make this a primary boot drive I recommend that you carefully read some of the critical reviews and take them into consideration because there are reported latency issues that make make it untenable in that role. For an external USB storage device, however, this one has been performing for me reliably and I would not hesitate to get another if I need more space.

title: Easy to use, but some caveats
text: I received this as a free review sample. I'll get the reason for subtracting a star out of the way first: (1) once you place a drive in the case bed removing it is difficult. (2) It runs a little hot. I had the circuit board exposed while initializing a 120GB SATA drive and by the time it was done the printed circuit board was hot. Not enough to cause blistering, but still hot to the touch. If you plan to install a drive permanently this is not a bad case. It easily slides together (after a little finagling to get the drive in and lined up), and the USB 3 connector is a big plus. The drive that I installed was not the fastest on the market, but this enclosure and associated electronics got good results when I transferred a 5 GB set of MP3 files from my laptop to the external drive it housed. This comes complete with screws (too many, in fact and the only ones that work are the black ones), and a screw driver. The cover precisely lines up with the bed that houses the drive, and the USB 3 cable that is included is decent. I've been using this for a month with no issues, and have to admit that despite my complaints above it is an easy way to transform a SATA drive into an external USB storage device.

title: Functional hands-free solution for vehicles with 3.5mm ports in their stereo, but some limitations
text: I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more. Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?' Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected. Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.

title: For folks with USB C devices. Reliable file system and decent performance
text: I received this as a free review sample. The reason for five stars is the design, which is convenient for folks who own USB Type C devices. My acid test is to overfill a drive. On a poorly made thumb drive once the file is at capacity the files will become corrupted and are impossible to remove. In essence, the drive is useless. This one passed that test with no problems. I did not test the transfer rate because the only port I had open on my Thinkpad T61 was an ancient USB 1.1. It was slow (as expected), but the transfer was steady and error-free. If there is a flaw, it's the loop for attaching this to a key ring is too small for one. Not a show stopper for me since I normally do not keep a thumb drive on my key ring, but if you do, this is NOT going to fit (and that I know of.) This is definitely for folks who are now using USB C. I would have loved it even more had it come with a piggy back adapter on the C side for a USB micro adapter as well. Perhaps the next version will, but since USB C seems to be the coming thing, perhaps my personal wish is not practical in the long term.

title: Good entry-level speaker - OK sound quality and very LOUD
text: I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because the sound quality of calls using the hands-free function is a little tinny, That is curious because when streaming music the sound quality if more than adequate. What distinguishes this speaker - for me - are two things: (1) it's loud, and (2) the controls contain separate volume and skip buttons. Especially the latter because on speakers that combine those buttons I am forever skipping a track when I really wanted to increase or decrease volume. Not so on this speaker. Some reviewers complained about hiss; I did not experience that at any volume level, even when the speaker was on, but not connected to my phone. Other complained about a loud announcement letting you know power on, pairing and the such. Yes, that is true. And you cannot change it or turn it off (that I know of). For me it is not a problem, but if stuff like that irritates you then you should be looking at different speakers instead of this one. Sound quality is decent for a small speaker. The high frequency is stable and does not break up or get tinny at max volume. There may be a little compression, which most people like. I prefer truer reproduction. The mids are rich and I suspect that they are purposely biased to emphasize that frequency band. It definitely enhances casual listening, but if you are accustomed to true fidelity it may drive you nuts. The bass is not especially boomy. It's more than adequate if you listen to acoustic music and other genres, but for bass-centric music it's a little weak. Volume is a surprise. This is a small speaker, but puts out a lot of sound. You can easily hear it from five to eight meters away when you have the volume cranked. Do be aware that you will more than cut play time in half if you max out the volume while on batteries. Still, you will get close to eight hours of play. The volume will cut through ambient noise, though, so this is ideal at the beach. Bottom line: I view this as an entry-level speaker that is priced accordingly, but has some nice features compared to others in its range. Can you find a better speaker for the price? Possibly, although you will have to dig through a lot of product pages. Is this a safe choice? In my opinion, yes, as long as you can live with some of the issues that I mentioned.

title: Superior sound, but not so good app and instructions
text: I received one of these as a free review sample. Up front, the reason I subtracted a star is the set-up using the libratone app is maddening (to say the least.) On the other hand the sound quality is simply the best I have come across for a wireless speaker. That means I have to eat some recent words along the lines of there is no bluetooth speaker that is truly audiophile quality. This speaker disproves that. Out of the box this quickly pairs and connects to bluetooth devices. I tested mine with a Note 4 phone and it took literally seconds to have it up and running. I was so blown away by the fact that this speaker reproduces music in a neutral manner by default that I was ready to sit down and give it a glowing review. Then I downloaded and installed the app. The app is the Achilles heel. It had trouble finding the speaker, and the scant instructions were not very helpful either. Some how, some way it finally found the speaker, then was totally confusing when it came to setting up my personal profile (speaker location, bias and other features.) It also presented me with radio stations that were accessible via WiFi, and after connecting to my router I was able to access those. However, I am not personally interested in those offerings so did not explore them too deeply. Basically, the app is good for linking multiple speakers, and some basic controls. Since I still cannot get the profiles set correctly I cannot speak about those. I will say that out of the box, without the libratone app and just connecting from my phone via bluetooth this speaker is spectacular. That is why I gave it the four stars that I did. Bottom line: if you are looking for [possibly] the best bluetooth speaker on the market (and, yes, that includes Bose), this is it. If you want a speaker that can do everything this one is supposed to do, including fine tuning it for your room and musical tastes, you may be disappointed or frustrated. With a more intuitive app and more detailed instructions this would easily be a solid five star product that would keep Bose engineers and marketing up late at night. Until that happens, though, it's merely a superior bluetooth speaker that has crossed over into audiophile country.

title: Almost perfect (and works as a music stand light)
text: I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things. Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most. I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet. Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.

title: Excellent entry level tablet with Samsung's features and performance
text: I purchased this specifically because I needed a knock around tablet that was more compact than my Tab Pro 12.2. I was looking more for basic web access, calendar and email on the go, so power and storage were not principal considerations. Also, as an FYI, mine was refurbished and provided by Direct Distributor, and since sellers vary I want to cite my experience with the specific one from which I purchased this. As a basic tablet this is excellent. It has the Samsung user interface to which I have grown accustomed, and even though this is an older tablet with little storage it was still pretty snappy for browsing the web and other common tasks. I also love the display. Despite the lower resolution than most tablets in 2016, it's still vivid and easy on the eyes. I thought 7 inches would be hard to read (after using a 12.2 inch tablet), but it isn't. I did increase the memory with a 32GB SD card I had laying around (a [[ASIN:B010Q57T02 SanDisk Ultra 32GB microSDHC UHS-I Card]].) This arrived at 90% battery charge, so I was able to use it immediately. The initial set up screens take about ten minutes. An original Samsung charger and charging cable was bundled with it. Aside from the SD card the only other accessory I bought was a [[ASIN:B013XZXIXE Tab 4 Case, Galaxy Tab 4 7.0-inch case, OMIU(TM)3-Piece In 1 (Black+Purple) Durable Silicone Plastic Combo Shockproof Case]], which was less than fifteen bucks and almost as good as a more expensive OtterBox Defender. So total cost of this tablet, extra memory and a decent case was less than 150 bucks! Bottom line: I am thrilled with this tablet - for what it is and what I paid - and have recommended it to friends who are considering a tablet, but are not sure. The performance and features, combined with the low price of a refurbished unit make it a relatively safe, entry level purchase.

title: Not for road warriors, but is one of the few projectors I have tried that works in a range of lighting conditions
text: I received this as a free review sample. Since there are ample specs and two very detailed reviews before this one I am going to stick to some observations and why I rated it so highly. First, though, if you are looking for a portable projector for a road warrior who needs to travel light this is NOT it. It's light enough, but bulky. As a home or office projector, though, this one has a lot going for it. The main reason why I rated this so highly is it works in rooms with some ambient light. I tested it in normal lighting conditions in my living room with typical morning light with open drapes and sunlight behind partially closed blinds. I could read a newspaper in that light, so was surprised and pleased that the picture quality of a video I was displaying through it was adequate. What I mean is I could see all of the details in the video, but, of course it would have been sharper and more vivid in lower light or even a dark room. I also own a high end business projector that would not display any discernible picture in the same lighting conditions. What I did not care for is the fact that I needed to included remote controller to access all of the features. Since this is a home and office projector I can live with that. On the other hand, unlike another reviewer's experience that this did not default back to the last input setting, mine did. Consistently. Another reason why I rated this so highly is the array of inputs - you have two HDMI ports, two USB, a VGA and AV connectors (the latter employ RCA jacks). I tested this from an old Lenovo T61 laptop via its VGA connector as well as using a Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 using an [[ASIN:B00K76A732 Addao® 5 in 1 Multifunction MHL Micro USB MHL To HDMI HDTV Adapter Connection Kit]]. Bottom line: this is an inexpensive way to get a wide screen TV for streaming movies from the web. It's also perfect as a fixed projected in corporate settings. It comes with all of the cables you need, a terse - but useful - user guide and a lens cover.

title: Very good quality cable at a reasonable price
text: I received this cable with a keyboard bundle similar to [[ASIN:B014G8W338 Casio Privia PX-360 Digital Piano - Black TMS CABLE Bundle]]. While I have not used it with the keyboard, I have used it for other connections. It has proven to be reliable and noise-free in a number of roles and environments. The outer sheath is actually pretty beefy, but does not hamper the flexibility of the cable. The strain reliefs did give me pause because I was initially unsure if they would allow for a decent bend radius, but after literally dozens of times of using this cable as a patch or primary connection cable between amplifiers and bluetooth receivers, and other connections it has not failed. It has proven to be so reliable that it's now in my gig bag and I am planning to purchase a few spares for my home studio and other uses. Bottom line: I go through a lot of cables. Some because they are cheaply made and fail (unlike this one), and others because I either misplace them or need more than one. For minijack cables I have settled on this brand and model for patch and short connection cables.

title: Outstanding protection, although bulky and heavy
text: I purchased this solely because of how happy I am with the [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] that I have been using for the past five months. That case has saved my Note 4 twice from falls, so I did not hesitate to purchase this along with my Tab Pro 8.4. This case WILL add a lot of bulk and weight to your tablet, so if you are looking for sleek, this is NOT the case you want. For me I wanted the assurance that my tablet would be protected and this is the only case that I have found that will do that. The way the rim around the screen is beveled and how it recesses the screen is a nice level of protection. I am guessing that the included screen protector is effective, since I did not use the included one with my Note 4 case (I opted for the Zagg for that phone, but I am using the protector that came with this case and it does allow complete sensitivity. Time will tell. Installation is straightforward and easy. I had mine completely installed in about five minutes. Of course I had prior experience with the Note 4 case, and there was a learning curve because the instructions are a little terse. All of the cutouts are also precise. The case does not hamper access to any feature or interfere with the camera. Ports have tabs that seal them against water and dust. Frankly I do not need that level or protection and actually cut off the tab protecting the charging port. However, if you work in harsh environments those are nice features. Also, I do not use the back cover that has the kickstand for propping the tablet up. Mine spends most of its time on a music stand, but if I were to use it outdoors or in harsh environments, the back cover is an additional layer of protection. Bottom line: if you want protection this is a great case. If you want slim and trendy you will probably not like it, though.

title: Almost five stars, but not quite - it's still a decent light and a bargain
text: I received this is a free review sample. For the price this is a bargain, but there are two things that kept me from giving it five stars. First is this does not use a standard micro USB style cable for charging. That means that unless you can find an easy source of cables with USB A on one end and the barrel connector this one has on the other, you are stuck with a three foot limitation of cable length. I have USB micro cables that are double that, and would have made this light all the more useful. Also, since I am using this as a music stand light if I misplace it for a gig I am out of luck because I do not own a similar charging cable (although I always have spare USB micro cables in my gig bag.) If you intend to use this as a fixed table lamp the cable issue will not be the problem for you that it is for me. Second, the gooseneck is sensitive. If I bump a music stand with this light clamped to the shelf it will move far out of place. It's not stiff enough to hold if you do plan to use it with a music stand. For tables, bed stands, etc. it should work fine, though. Here are some of the strengths: the lowest setting of illumination is perfect for stage use or if you want to read in bed without waking your partner up. At the highest setting it is definitely bright when lose in (about 1.5 meters), and - as Goldilocks said - the medium setting is just right. Another feature is untethered to the charger this will operate for three hours at the brightest setting and half more than double that at the lowest. That means that if you are camping, on stage (or in front of a lectern) without a power source nearby you can still use it. Finally, the included wall wart has a 2 Amp port for phones and tablets, as well as a 500mA port for charging this light. That is handy and all the more reason why the cable style for this lamp is a frustration - it could have easily been a five star product, and especially at the going price.

title: If you need to connect HDMI to AV composite or expand AV composite to HDMI this is a good solution
text: I received this as a free review sample. Note that this only accepts HDMI as an input and converts that signal composite RCA out. It cannot go in the opposite direction (connecting composite RCA devices to HDMI). For me this is a great way to add an additional HDMI port to a monitor I own that has a single HDMI and a single set of AV composite ports. I can also use this on an older TV that has HDMI and a dual set of AV composite ports. I did test this using a Blu-Ray player on the HDMI and to the TV and it worked beautifully as long as you do not set your video resolution to be higher than 1080p for Blu-Ray, but will support ancient 640x480 all the way up to 1920x1080.It also supports 480i or 480p up to the 1080p I mentioned above. Of course, if you are using this to add HDMI to older display devices you are probably going to be limited in resolution anyway. Then converter itself is small, hassle-free and does not require any external power. For expanding to an additional HDMI port on a TV or monitor with a spare set of AV composite ports, or connecting HDMI devices to legacy equipment that only has AV composite input this is an inexpensive solution.

title: High quality and versatile
text: I purchased these based on the shorter [[ASIN:B00FC4Z842 Hosa HSS-010X2 Pro Dual Cable]] set that came bundled with a keyboard that I purchased. The construction is excellent in all respects. As a point of comparison to Monster, I also own a set of [[ASIN:B001UAM2ZU Monster StudioLink Interconnects - 2 Meters - 1/4-Inch to 1/4-Inch]], which are much more expensive inch for inch, and these are their equal in both construction and noise-free performance. I've used these to connect the L and R outputs to a mixer, and I also have used them as L and R out to a pair of small powered speakers from my Soundcraft Ui12 Digital Mixer with Wi-Fi Router and they worked equally well in that role. They are siamesed together, but ou can easily separate them if you need two separate cables to run to separate speakers (if you use them in that way.) Or you can leave them as are to keep your cable runs cleaner. If you do decide to keep them as are I highly recommend that you tape the places where the pairs split because they are very easy to peel back and separate. Basically, if you want a high quality set of interconnect cables for stereo that take 1/4 inch connections these are well worth considering.

title: Very high quality cable
text: These came bundled with a keyboard I purchased from a different source ([[ASIN:B0130VVOOG Casio PX360BK Key Digital Piano]]. I have not only used this cable pair to connect the L and R outputs to a mixer, but I also have used them as L and R out to a pair of small powered speakers from my [[ASIN:B00UBJ6ZM2 Soundcraft Ui12 Digital Mixer with Wi-Fi Router]] and they worked well in that role too. The construction is excellent in all respects. They are siamesed together, but ou can easily separate them if you need two separate cables to run to separate speakers (if you use them in that way.) Or you can leave them as are to keep your cable runs cleaner. If you do decide to keep them as are I highly recommend that you tape the places where the pairs split because they are very easy to peel back and separate. A final factor is price and quality. I also own a set of [[ASIN:B001UAM2ZU Monster StudioLink Interconnects - 2 Meters - 1/4-Inch to 1/4-Inch]], which are much more expensive (and shorter), and these are their equal in both construction and noise-free performance.

title: High grade optics and constuction - professional quality lens
text: I received this as a free review sample. It it intended to be used with the [[ASIN:B018JVE7PU 001 | bitplay SNAP! PRO iPhone Case for iPhone 6/6S]], and like that kit, this is a professional quality lens. However, this will work with any camera or adapter that has 13mm threads. Before you purchase you need to know that this lens has a polarizer than can be rotated to reduce reflections and/or enhance color. The caveat it this lens will NOT work properly if you have your camera's flash active. The lens itself is high grade optical glass with no distortions that I could detect. If you are accustomed to pro quality optical gear you will appreciate this lens. On the other hand, if you are a point-and-shoot type who is content with clip on lenses or the basic video capabilities of your iPhone this is probably overkill. I am not trying to discourage anyone from purchasing this, but I do want to point out that this is a lens for pros or serious hobbyists, and, moreover, will require either the aforementioned kit or an adapter for the 13mm threads for either an iPhone or a camera that has that lens mounting size. Bottom line: this is constructed with the same quality as lenses used with my vintage Nikon SLR (although different form factor) and intended for high-end users. I did some test shots and it has zero distortion and can be adjusted to control some reflections and color saturation. If you are serious about photography this one merits serious consideration.

title: Well designed and pro-level construction and features for transforming an iPhone 6 into a camera
text: I received this as a free review sample. When I accepted this for testing and review I was a little skeptical. However, this has turned out to be a high-quality kit that will transform an iPhone 6 or 6s into a decent hand held camera, yet it will not interfere with other iPhone functions. With the case and attachments in place you can still make and receive calls, text, browse the web, etc. This is actually the foundation for a more sophisticated set of lenses that will accept add-on lenses like the [[ASIN:B018TQUEYI 010 | bitplay Portable Add-on 3X Telephoto Glass Lens Compatible]]. As you can see from the product description this kit already comes with a basic wide angle/telephoto lens combination. It is not plastic junk, but a serious lens with a precision metal body that screws into this case. It has two parts - one lens screws into the other for combined or separate effects - and it is as good in quality and construction as the lenses that I used with a vintage Nikon SLR. The case itself can be quickly removed to reconfigure your phone back into a ... phone. But while it is in camera configuration mode it feels just like a hand-held with a choice of grips, an integrated tripod adapter and even a leather strap. The case does not interfere with any phone function, and especially the iPhone's camera and flash. More importantly - for me - the case offers excellent protection. The lip that is slightly raised about the iPhone's screen is curved inward and adds protection for that critical area. The body of the case and two of the grips are textured so you can maintain a firm hold on the phone while shooting, even if your hands are wet. Bottom line: this is not a gimmick or novelty - it is designed for folks who take photography seriously. I could not find a single flaw in the design from a photographer's perspective; nor could I find any faults from a build or design perspective. This is obviously not for casual users, but if photography is your passion and you own an iPhone 6 or 6s, this case merits serious consideration.

title: Works perfectly in my Note 4
text: I purchased this because I had run out of space on my old [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10 for Galaxy Note 2 II]]. That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down. This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card. Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it. As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me. Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

title: No brainer solution
text: I've been using Sabrent products for a few years - most were free review samples. When I needed a SATA enclosure I was happy to spend my own money on this model because I have come to trust the brand. This is simple and straightforward. I literally unscrewed the panel with the supplied screwdriver, mated my [[ASIN:B013J7PP96 ADATA USA Premier SP550 120GB 2.5" SATA III Solid State Drive]] to the connector, attached the supplied USB A cable and was up and running. No fuss and the entire set up took mere minutes. I did need the instructions to make sense of the supplied USB cable because it was a Y on one end. The USB A connector in the Y end, on the thicker part of the split cable, goes to the target machine and the single USB A connector attaches to the enclosure's USB port. One thing I truly like is the small, blue LED that indicates that the SATA drive is powered and operational. Also, a quick examination of the printed circuit board revealed a clean design with no issues. For the price this is perfect for 2.5" SATA drives and for the ease of use earned five solid stars from me.

title: Works perfectly with Note 4
text: I received this as a free review sample. Although the Note 4 is not on the list of supported devices my Note 4 came up immediately on my monitor's display, so I can confirm that it works with that phone. It also worked with my Tab Pro 12.2 tablet. This is a quick and inexpensive solution to connecting compatible phones and tablets to monitors and TVs. Frankly I have been using a wireless dongle for that, but this, plus an HDMI switch, has allowed me to access my monitor using my old Note 3 phone as a controller (it's otherwise been sitting around collecting dust since I upgraded to a Note 4.) The cables are thin gauge so I am not sure how much wear and tear they would sustain if you were constantly connecting and disconnecting devices. I have been using this for a week, but the Note 3 to which I am connecting it is relatively stationary. For devices that are supported this is literally plug and go - no drivers, and I did not even have to invoke screen sharing. As soon as I made all of the connections my phone's screen was immediately displayed on the monitor.

title: Simple and effective, but documentation needs improving
text: I received this as a free review sample. Up front, the reason for only four stars is the documentation is too scant and that can be a problem. When I received this I asked a friend to download the app to her iPad Air 2 (running iOS 8.3) and connect to the device. She claimed it would hang. I borrowed the iPad and was able to easily connect and set up a specific room for monitoring. Same app and same hardware, but because the documentation was so terse and the app itself a bit confusing I concluded that this can be frustrating to some folks. You can set this up for different rooms and once you get the hang of the app's user interface that process is simple. Do note that you need to leave the sensor in a specific location for at least a week so that it can monitor and establish a trend. For my home the main measurement and trend I am interested in is indoor air quality because of the pollens that manage to creep inside. I received this after our major pollen season in Central Florida, but the display shows at a glance some small spikes that I will investigate (checking weather stripping, and door and window seals. Bottom line: this is easily a five star device if the documentation is rewritten to show even novice users step-by-step how to connect and get it running. In my personal opinion the installation and configuration screens should be redone too because it seems as though the software designers were more interested in a cool, modern look than whether or not less experienced users would catch the visual cues. If this were for geeks I'd give it a pass, but it's designed for a wider audience and can frustrate folks who just want to get it up and running, and monitor air quality, temperature and humidity.

title: Stable fixed height tripod that fits Note 4 phones and relaible remote release
text: I received this as a free review sample. The tripod is fixed height and can raise your camera or phone 5.5 inches. Depending on the device, the lens can be raised even more. For example, with my Kodak Easyshare the center of the lens was elevated to a little under 6.5 inches when mounted, and my Note 4 phone just under 7 inches. While the legs are fixed the head will rotate to just about any position you want within its range of rotation. It will rotate 360 degrees and the tilt angle appears to be 45 decrees (I did not have a protractor of drafting angle handy to measure it.) The increments, within the movement range, are infinite. Note that the tripod can support up to 2.2 pounds and size-wise, a camera with an 85mm lens. My Note 4 fit within the phone adapter, so that is not an issue. The shutter release is somewhat generic. That is a god thing because like every other one I own it will work with an app called Camera 360 if your version of Android or iOS is not supported. You will not need the app if you are running Android 4.2.2 or newer, or iOS 6.0 or newer. This works for movies and stills, but you have to first place your 'cursor' on whichever mode you want manually, then use the button to control off and on. Also, it functions like a mouse of sorts until you invoke the camera app. On my main screen when I pressed the Android button it brought up the app on which its 'cursor' was resting on. Another feature is you can still stream music to phones or speaker via bluetooth while the shutter release is active.

title: Works nicely if properly applied
text: I received this as a free review sample. Mine has been affixed to the back of my vehicle for nearly a month, and has even weathered a storm and a few hot days. If you properly prepare the surface of where you intend to affix this sticker it will stay put. The reason why I docked it a star is because there were no instructions other than a terse three step blurb on the package. Frankly, that did not go far enough. You need to make sure the surface to which you are going to affix the sticker is ABSOLUTELY clean. A good rubdown with alcohol or even Windex, followed by a thorough drying with a lint free cloth works wonders. Also, do not affix it in the hot sun, and also let it sit in the shade or garage for at least eight hours before driving. I did mine in the early evening and by morning it was firmly in place. One nice thing about this, aside from the decorative aspect, is it's highly reflective. Since there is not much continuous surface in the design, it is not going to reflect back to a driver behind you and blind him or her, but there more than enough reflection to be easily seen on a dark night.

title: Decent basic protection and a value in this price range
text: I purchased this to compare to another case that I own - the [[ASIN:B00V6I7NBE TOUGH Cardioid Condenser Microphone Hard Case with Dense Foam for Audio-Technica AT2020 / AT2020USB / ATR2500-USB / AT2035 Studio and USB Microphones]]. I am using that case to house a [[ASIN:B00DYD77WY Samson Concert 88 Handheld 16-Channel True Diversity UHF Wireless System]], and it was a tight fit. This one will hold my second Concert 88 system, and it does so with a lot more room and flexibility. This case is significantly better than the Tough case. For one thing the diced foam is easy to remove. I had to use a box cutter on the foam in the other case because it was not completely cut through. For another, the three bottom layers of foam (described in the product description) make it more convenient to work with, as well as the extra depth and overall inside dimensions of this case. Bear in mind that this and the case to which I am comparing it are the same price. I do wish there were more dividers included, and also that the long dividers would go across the entire width. However, for my purposes what came with this case is more than sufficient. One final point of comparison - I believe that in the long run the Tough box will outlast this one because of design and materials. That one is all plastic, while this one is a combination of materials that over time are going to break if roughly handled. That said, I prefer this case and will probably order a few more for some other microphones that I own.

title: A little complex, but excellent protection
text: I received this as a free review sample. I am not using it for drones, but to house a [[ASIN:B00378GEAM BEHRINGER EUROLIVE B205D]] along with some mics, DI boxes, a tablet and miscellaneous cables. From a protection perspective I truly trust this backpack. It's well padded and the convex form factor combine to provide excellent protection for the electronics I carry. I do want to point out that if you use it as a carrying case instead of as a backpack the tablet compartment is not as protected. On the other hand, using it as a backpack will protect any tablet, even ones without their own covers and cases. Plus that particular compartment is more than large enough to accommodate my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2]]. The complexity comes in with the myriad of clasps, pockets and system of dividers. It actually takes a good hour to become thoroughly familiar with the pockets and other features. The dividers are versatile enough to be reconfigured to accommodate smaller (or larger) items. I am not using all of the dividers since I am storing a fairly large speaker, but the dividers from the set that I am using allow me to separate and organize the peripherals and cables that I mentioned above. One nice thing about the dividers is that they, too, are heavily padded and well constructed. Overall construction is excellent. The zippers are smooth and come with convenient pull tabs. The material is water resistant and will take a lot of abuse. Also, the straps are nicely padded and are not going to fray or wear out even if you are rough with this backpack. Bottom line: this is perfect protection for more than drones. For the equipment I am using it for this is a little on the expensive side. However, since I am using the gear in live performances I feel that the assurance that the equipment will be operational when I need it to be. That makes the value proposition more sane for the way I am using it.

title: Works with Samsung's 12.2 inch Note and Tab Pro tablets
text: I received this as a free review sample. I was not expecting it to accommodate my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2]], but it did. That earned it automatic high rating from me. You have to insert the Tab Pro into the supporting arm hooks in landscape mode, and if you attempt to adjust it to portrait there are no top and bottom supports. More importantly, it also attached to the upper rod of a [[ASIN:B0018TAITA Musician's Gear Die-Cast Mic Stand]]. If you have any idea what a tablet mount for a microphone stand costs you will understand my enthusiasm. It will NOT work with the tripod mic stand that I tried, except for boom stands and attaching this to a boom was not only awkward, but unstable. Do note, though, that I had to remove the tightening handle on this unit and also remove the cup type washer to get it to fit to the die-cast mic stand's upper rod. Assembly is easy to figure out so I cannot complain that the only instructions were printed on the box - and those were scant. It is super adjustable and in its current role as a tablet mount for a microphone stand it can be positioned exactly where I want it with my iPad Air 2 or smaller Samsung Tab 10.1 tablets. I am stuck in landscape mode with the Tab Pro as I mentioned above. It's a shame this does not come with a clamp that will grab to tripod type mic stands because at the sub twenty buck price it would sell like hotcakes to musicians - especially those of us who have the larger Samsung tablets.

title: A vast improvement over fabric type pop filters
text: I purchased mine on an impulse, not totally convinced that it was any better than the fabric type pop filters I use. How wrong I was. For evidence of that see Thomas G. Umstattd Jr.'s very helpful November 18, 2013 video review for a compelling demonstration of this pop guard. Currently I am using this on both a MXL 550 and a MXL V67G mic (I am swapping the guard back and forth until I can purchase another one.) What I love is this fits directly over the two mics I cited. More importantly, there is no clumsy gooseneck and clamp, and even more importantly I can clean this one without destroying it. As shown in the video I cited, this is as effective as the fabric pop guards. I will say that they will NOT make a good windscreen outdoors (I tested that and they pick up a lot of noise.) For indoors, though, they completely control pops and plosives. One final reason why I love this: my fabric pop filters are prone to moving from their position if I accidentally bump into a mic stand. It seems that I am forever fine adjusting them, whereas this fits right over the mic and does not budge.

title: Packs a lot of sound into a small form factor
text: I received this as a free review sample. Volume is surprisingly loud for such a tiny speaker. I was able to clearly hear music I was streaming from nearly seven meters away. Most small, personal speakers are good for up to three meters, so it's ahead of most speakers in its class regarding sound volume. Sound quality is equally impressive. I happened to have [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]] queued up on my phone when I went to test the speaker and the quality was superb. Every note in the high, medium and low frequency bands was crystal clean, even with the volume cranked to max. I tested a few other tracks from other albums to listen to the sound across all frequency bands with no problems. The claimed play time is up to twelve hours. I got eight with the volume turned to maximum, and ten with it half way. If you keep the volume level at a quarter it will provide the full twelve hours. That is not an issue if you are listening to this close in like on a night stand or desk. At a quarter it's plenty loud. It does have an auto shut-off feature that turns it off if you are not playing music through it for fifteen minutes. One final note: this comes up in bluetooth mode as soon as it's powered on. That means that even a novice can pair and connect to it by following the simple instruction sheet.

title: Perfect solution to bypassing built-in TV speakers
text: I received this as a free review sample seven months ago and have finally used it to solve a very real problem. Specifically, connecting my Blu-Ray player to a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] and still getting decent sound. The monitor has a gorgeous display, but the speakers integrated into it are, well, lame. Using this I was able to send the video from the Blu-Ray player to the monitor, but split out the audio and send it to a [[ASIN:B00K6QKWWY Turcom TS-404 2.1 Channel Stereo HDTV Home Theater Surround Sound Soundbar]]. I used the RCA out on this box to the RCA in on the sound bar, and now have the best of both worlds. There are other ways that I could have accomplished this. The value of this particular box is that it made it much easier and with a minimum of wires. It's also fairly straightforward to use.

title: Works with some Android boxes
text: I received this as a free review sample eleven months ago and am only now getting around to using it. When you need one of these, you NEED one. I wanted to connect my [[ASIN:B00M933WUQ Keedox MXIII Amlogic Android 4.4.2 M82 S802 Quad Core Smart 4K TV Box]] to a monitor I have. The monitor's HDMI ports were fully populated, but the VGA port was open. The MXIII did not have a VGA out, but did have HDMI. This adapter did the trick - it was truly plug and play. A great feature (in my opinion) is the ability to split video and audio. I ran the 3.5mm audio jack to a better speaker than the one integrated into my monitor. I did use a third party cable that I deemed better than the three foot one that ships with this dongle. Bottom line: this is a great product. Not everyone will need it, but if you have the same situation as the one I described this is an effective solution.

title: Excellent bargain and can be used as disposables or permanent
text: I purchased these based strictly on price. They are not the heavy duty ties that are also offered by Velcro, but have a wider range of uses. For one thing at five cents per tie I can use them for temporary cable management when setting up for performances, and not worry of I lose of miss one. Since they come in four rolls of twenty-five each I keep one roll in my gig bag, and the other rolls in a drawer at home. A single roll was all it took to get my morass of wires in my home studio under control, so the hundred-pack I purchased for less than a fast food meal will probably be six to nine months worth of cable management for gigs even if I treat them as disposable. These are thinner than the heavy duty ties and are prone to stretching. However, they are every bit as strong when you are wrapping cable bundles. Do note that you need to separate them by tugging each tie from the roll. But you do need to be careful because the short head that contains the loop will also separate. If you are a musician, computer tech or just want to get wires and cables under control a pack of these is a cost-effective want to do it.

title: Very heavy duty
text: I purchased this to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] to a speaker stand (a very light weight [[ASIN:B006H0DY3C Adam Hall SPS023S Speaker Stand]]. Frankly this mount is far sturdier than the stand on which I mounted it, and is so well constructed and heavy that it's overkill for the monitor. My monitor weighs less than eleven pounds and I am pretty sure this mount could easily support a monitor twice that weight. Note that you can rotate your monitor 360 degrees, going from landscape to portrait, and every angle in between. However, you cannot tilt the viewing angle. I am not sure why not since the gimbal upon which the VESA mounting plate looks as though it should allow it, but it doesn't, The clamp that mounts to the pole has a thick, anti-marring insert that will protect poles. It's also one of the reasons why this mount is so heavy - the construction is very heavy duty. All of the tools you need are provided to mount this to a pole and adjust it. The four bolts that come with it are a bit on the short side, although they worked with my monitor (and you need to provide a screwdriver for those.) I am thoroughly pleased with this mount, especially since I almost purchased an [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]], but took a chance on this at the last minute. That decision saved me a lot of money and accomplished exactly what I wanted.

title: Great starter phones for sports
text: I received these as a free review sample eight months ago. Since there are a lot of detailed reviews I will focus on my experience with these and also compare them to other sports phones. First, these are good quality for twenty buck phones. But do be aware that sports phones are designed for comfort more than sound quality. Not that these are marginal - they have a typical bias towards the mid range, with compressed highs and adequate bass. They are not going to win acclaim from audiophiles, but do reproduce music that is clear and perfect for background listening. Another thing I like is comfort. I can wear these for a few hours at a time without even noticing them. For sports phones that is a major plus. These allow in a little ambient noise for safety, but it does not appreciably affect the quality of music. Volume is somewhat limited. If you like music super loud these are not going to make you happy. On the other hand, high volume defeats the purpose of sports phones since you need to be aware of ambient noise and your surroundings. I cannot emphasize strongly enough that these are NOT general purpose phones. Finally, the specs claim about four hours of music play time. That is true with the volume at about a third. If you crank the volume to max you can cut that time in half.

title: Very close to in-ear monitor quality sound
text: I received these as a free review sample. I want to point out that these are hard-wired only. They use a 3.5mm connector and ARE NOT bluetooth. If you want phones for critical listening and transcribing music (or listening to a raw feed before mixdown) these are perfect. Bluetooth always entails some loss of sound quality, but these, and other direct connect phones, do not. They are neutral enough to pass for high end in-ear monitors (IEMs), but there is a little bias on the low end. As long as you take that into account you can mentally compensate when listening to raw feeds. One of the things that I found impressive is I could not detect any bias towards the mid range frequencies, nor do the high end frequencies sound compressed. For me this means that I can listen to acoustic jazz and hear the music as originally recorded. This is especially important for a lot of mid 1950s recordings before engineers started playing games with the mix. For these phones I sampled tracks from [[ASIN:B00CJYWUM6 At the Showboat / See What I Mean? / Settlin' In]] and [[ASIN:B000QQV5FM Dorothy Donegan Live]], and listened to the entire two hours and forty-eight minutes of Erroll Garner's [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]]. That test proved that these phones are absolutely superb for folks for love music. While this is claimed to be for Android, I tested it on an iPad Air 2 and a ThinkPad T61 - it worked beautifully on both. In fact, on the ThinkPad I was playing from CD instead of an MP3 file and the sound quality was better than a direct connect from my Note 4 phone. A few notes about the physical characteristics and features: I tested out the control block using my Note 4 phone and found it to be less than intuitive. I prefer controlling functions using those integrated in my Note 4 (including EQ.) I love the tangle free cord, and the comfort of the phones though. Everything about the construction and sound are of the highest quality. Bottom line: if you are fanatical about sound quality these phones are ones that I highly recommend. I own other IEMs that cost twice as much that are close to these. Granted the expensive ones have completely neutral low frequency response, but if you are not mixing down these are as good in the overall scheme of things.

title: Works perfectly, but there are things you need to know
text: I received this as a free review sample five and a half months ago and it's been invaluable. If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive. This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. However, it can interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved. If you are set in your ways regarding keyboard height know that this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two. One final note: if you live or work in a high dist environment take the time to shut this fan array down and blow it out with compressed air. It will greatly prolong the life of the array and will also ensure that it doesn't become noisy.

title: Excellent for electronics and other items
text: I received this as a free review sample nearly a year ago and have been using it at least twenty times a month. I use it for carrying microphones, adapters and miscellaneous electronics I use when performing as a musician. For protection this is ideal, and the inside and outside zippered pouches make this even more versatile. It does an excellent job of protecting the delicate microphones and adapters that I store in it. I am not using the dividers as vertical separators the way they were designed. Instead, I lay them on top of the mics, and then store the cables on top. That arrangement is perfect, and the bag and insert are relatively light and sturdy. Close to a year of constant use is testimony to just how sturdy this bag is, especially considering the times it have been accidentally stepped upon. Since the canvas part is so sturdy I am guessing that the insert will probably last even longer. One of the reasons is the overall construction, though lightweight, is of the highest quality. I am betting that if this were used for its intended purpose of protecting a DLSR or other photo equipment it would do as great a job as it does protecting my mics and other items.

title: Inexpensive solution for two things
text: I purchased this sight unseen, and solely to give my eyes a break from the much smaller laptop monitor I had been using. Since others have gone into the technical details (which are also amply described on this page), I'll stick to what I love about it and how I am now using it. The main thing was price. At less than a hundred fifty bucks I took a chance. Hooking it up was super simple: a power cord, a VGA connection to my laptop (using the included cable), and screwing in the VESA adapter from my [[ASIN:B005C2914C Mount-It! MI-705, 3-Way Adjustable Tilting Desk Mount Bracket]] took literally ten minutes. This comes with a pedestal base that is more than adequate, but I wanted the mount I mentioned to free up desk real estate as well as to make this monitor a grab-and-go solution for a second use, which I'll get into below. If there is one thing that I do not care for, it's the cramped area for connecting cables. The cable adapters for VGA, HDMI and power are inserted vertically, and the VGA and HDMI connections are closer together than necessary. Since I am connecting and disconnecting cables often this is a peeve, but if you plan to install it and leave it in one spot it's not even an issue. The speakers are not the loudest when you are running sound via the HDMI port, but are more than adequate when you directly connect to the audio in port. This monitor comes with a 3.5mm cable for that purpose. For my laptop (an aging ThinkPad) it is literally plug and play. I have finally migrated from XP to Windows 7 and this monitor's model was immediately recognized. My second use is to press this into service as a large sheet music display. I am mirroring the screen using an [[ASIN:B00ZWOU5R2 EZcast 5GHz Wireless HDMI Streaming Media Player]] to display [[ASIN:B00WLIDHA4 MobileSheetsPro Music Reader]] mirrored from a tablet screen.
