Since this monitor weighs less than ten pounds it is fairly easy to set up at a gig. As a side note, if you do intend to use this on a gig or as a karaoke display this is an excellent mount: [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]]. Do note that the HDMI port will not power devices. For the EZcast dongle I have to use either a battery backup or a small wall wart (the same kind I charge my phone and tablet with), but that is not an issue either. I figured that for the price some corners had to be cut. Although this is designed to be a desktop monitor I do wish there was a remote option for it. When I am using it to extend my laptop display it's perfect. For the screen mirroring use I mentioned a remote would be helpful. The bottom line is I am thoroughly pleased with this monitor and may, in fact, purchase a second one so I am not swapping my laptop monitor out to take on gigs.

title: Rock solid for my ViewSonic 24-Inch monitor
text: I purchased this specifically to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]]. It definitely holds the monitor - steady - in any position within this mount's range. Note that my monitor weighs in around 9.5 pounds, so factor that into your own needs. Assembly is a snap. It comes with everything you need to mount the VESA adapter to your monitor, including washers and spacers. I had anticipated having to purchase bolts to fit, but that turned out to be unnecessary. One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier. Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.

title: Perfect for low draw USB devices
text: I received this as a free review sample. First, this is for low draw devices like mice, keyboards, thumb drives and the such. It will NOT support an external drive that gets its power from your machine's USB port. For me this is perfect because it's USB 2.0 only (although it will also kick down to USB 1.1). I am using it on an old ThinkPad T61, which immediately recognized it as soon as I plugged it in. I did not test the Ethernet connection (which needs a separate driver on my XP machine), but the USB ports are problem free. As a test I tried this hub on my Note 4 phone using a [[ASIN:B00LM4PDUU LinkS Micro-USB 3.0 OTG Adapter]] and the USB ports worked like they did on my T61. Again, I did not test the Ethernet port, but did populate two USB ports with a keyboard and mouse, and both were immediately recognized by the phone. Bottom line: this is a nice way to expand USB ports for low power draw devices. The Ethernet port is a bonus and especially if you need to direct connect to a router, but you may need to download a driver to get it working.

title: Spectacular sound quality
text: I received this as a free review sample. This is NOT a bluetooth device. These phones are strictly for 3.5mm stereo connections. That means that this will work with a wider variety of devices. The sound quality to my ears is why I awarded it five stars. There is definitely a crossover built into these phones because I could hear the separation of low and high frequencies, with a prominent bass in one ear. Also, there does not seem to be any compression at the high end of the frequency spectrum, which gives these phones a more natural sound. I listen to mainly acoustic jazz (piano jazz trios, vocalists, and similar), so I appreciate the realistic sound these phones provide. There are a few areas that I would love to see improved: the cable is long and would be nicer if it were flat, tangle-proof. Also, the controls are a little too high up on the cable in my opinion. I can easily reach them, but when testing them I could not see the buttons. Of course, those are not show stoppers - just my own preferences. And regarding the controls, I already am familiar with their placement from use and memory, so that is really a non issue. The phones are comfortable. They ship with small, medium and large tips and I used the ones that were already installed. The fit was perfect. These also ship with an extra set of premium, noise blocking tips. I have not tried them since the regular tips are more than adequate for me. Other nice features are the zippered, hard case, velcro cable wrap and shirt clip. To be sure, they are value-added items, but the real value is the sound quality and these phones have that without a doubt. Bottom line: if you want hard wired phones that allow you to listen critically to music (or transcribe it), this is a surprisingly inexpensive solution. I have used everything from high end studio in-ear monitors and premium phones, and these come close at a much more affordable price. I am not saying that these are as good as the expensive phones, but am saying that bang for your buck these are hard to beat and will surprise most audiophiles.

title: Very compact and with a micro B adapter does wonders for phones and tablets
text: I received this as a free review sample (six months ago), and only sporadically used it with my laptop because that ancient thing only supported USB 2.0. It worked perfectly with the laptop, and was instantly recognized as soon as I plugged it in. The only reason I did not keep it plugged in is I was using an externally powered hub to power some thumb drives and external hard drive. An unpowered hub, no matter which brand would not cut it. When I purchased a [[ASIN:B00LM4PDUU LinkS Micro-USB 3.0 OTG Adapter A male to Micro B adapter]] this small hub became my best friend. I Use the adapter to connect this hub to my Tab Pro 12.2 tablet (and on occasion my Note 4 phone), which allows me to use a real keyboard and mouse. I can also plug in a thumb drive, but the minute I do that the Tab Pro 12.2's battery starts getting consumed too quickly. However, when I need to transfer data (mainly movies and music) quickly, this hub truly supports USB 3.0 speeds. What I have come to love about this is the small size easily fits in the padded bag in which I keep my tablet. Also, I always know when this hub is active because of the indicator light. As long as I keep my eye on remaining battery capacity on my Tab Pro when using a thumb drive I am OK. The key thing is this hub is appropriately sized for phones and tablets, and will support the transfer rates of which my phone and tablet are capable.

title: For non-bluetooth and very comfortable
text: I received these as a free review sample six months ago and use them mainly on my laptop. I have also tested them on Samsung Note 3 and 4 phones, Tab 10.1 and Tab Pro 12.2 tablets, and an iPad Air 2. It works flawlessly with all of them, although some of the features like forwarding and skipping songs using the multi-function button only work with Apple IOS devices. The main reason why I rated them so highly is sound quality. These phones are balanced across the high, mid and low frequency bands, although there seems to be some emphasis on the mid range, with slight compression on the high end. They are perfect for critical listening and even transcribing if you are a musician. Given the slight bias, though, these are not ideal for listening to monitor or raw tracks. Of course they were not designed for those tasks. Another set of features I like are the flat, tangle-free cable and the comfort of the in-ear pieces. This ships with silicone ear adapters, but the default ones work well for me. Still, if you have smaller or larger ear canals the chances of this fitting well is good. Ear adapters provide decent noise isolation, but not totally (not necessarily a bad thing if you are using this for walking and need to be aware of your surroundings.) Overall, these are well constructed and have excellent sound quality - at least on the devices on which I tested them. Just know that all of the features are not available on anything but Apple IOS devices.

title: Excellent single-purpose monitor
text: I received this as a free review sample five months ago and have been using it for around four months. This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used. Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine). What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost. If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.

title: Great gig bag
text: I received this as a free review sample and have been using it often for the past eleven months. My main use is to house some microphones, adapters and miscellaneous electronics I use when performing as a musician. For that use this is ideal. Plus the inside and outside zippered pouches make this even more versatile. The does an excellent job of protecting the delicate microphones and adapters that I store in it. I am not using the dividers as vertical separators the way they were designed. I lay them on top of the mics, and then store the cables on top. That arrangement is perfect, and the bag and insert are relatively light and sturdy. Eleven months of use are testimony to just how truly gig worthy this bag is for what I use it. Based on this the insert will probably last a long time, and the overall construction, though lightweight, will probably last if this is used for its intended purpose of protecting a DLSR or other photo equipment.

title: Excellent performance and has withstood eight months of use
text: I received this as a free review sample eight months ago and it have been in service ever since. This one has performed in two critical areas with no problems or errors. The first is, of course, charging. The second in synching. After eight months of use (with an iPad Air 2) it's still going strong. That alone makes this a five star product in my opinion. Another reason for my high rating is this is certified by Apple under their MFi (Made For iPod/iPhone/iPad) program. It's a level of comfort for me and helps to separate the cables that I know will work from the ones made by fly-by-night companies that you find in many discount stores. Aside from the MFi logo the construction shows the quality: the outer jacket is substantial, as are the strain reliefs on each end. Plus the USB A and Apple Lightning connectors were precision fits into their respective ports.

title: Vast improvement over the iPad 2, but ...
text: Since there are nearly two thousand reviews at the time I am writing this one I'll stick with a few observations. First - and this is important - do not make the same mistake I did and opt for the 16GB model. Go for the 64 or 128GB version because, frankly, the 16GB capacity is insufficient for the newer operating system. Coming from a 16GB iPad 2 that was not at capacity I thought saving a few bucks and getting the same capacity here would be prudent. It's not and I have already run out of space before completely transferring my existing apps and data. Second, this looks to be the same size as the earlier iPad I own, but the screen is so vastly superior that there is no comparison. Plus the speed difference is amazing. Other features, especially the camera and battery life, are giant improvements as well. If you are hanging onto an older iPad like the 2 model I had, this one is well worth the upgrade. Just be aware that the 16GB model is not going to cut it, even if you are nowhere near capacity on an older 16GB iPad. For more specifics on features and benefits read through the spotlighted reviews here.

title: This has come a long way since the Roku 2
text: I'll keep my review brief because there are a number of excellent ones that go into the features and benefits. I am approaching this as someone who owned a Roku 2 and was on the fence about moving up. Here are the features I personally like: integrated YouTube access. When I got the Roku 2 a few years ago that was only possible with a third party service and forced me to also purchase a Chromecast to conveniently access YouTube. So for me, this feature alone justified the upgrade because that particular channel is important to me. Another improvement - for me - is you can now select Paypal in lieu of a credit card. I do not use credit cards, and had to purchase a prepaid one to install the earlier model. You cannot get through the install process without some payment method. There are no hidden charges, but the payment method is required to be on file in case you may want to pay for a premium service. If you have Paypal and do not want to (or cannot) give a credit card number, you can still proceed with the installation process. Installation, like the earlier model, is a breeze. I had mine up and running in practically five minutes. As for the voice feature - I honestly never bothered with it so cannot say one way or the other if it's good or bad. Check other reviews for that. I will say that the upgrade was worth it to me. If you are still on a Roku 2 and are happy with it in all respects this is not going to be a bargain. If you want expanded features and channels and faster response this is a good choice. If you are new to Roku and are considering cutting the cable this is worthwhile - I am using Netflix at less than ten bucks per month and am getting all the entertainment I want from just that. It's certainly a bargain for me compared to local cable services, which I deem to be way overpriced. This may be the first step in 'cutting the cable' if Netflix, Prime Movies or other inexpensive services have offering that satisfy your needs.

title: Even works on my ancient Windows XP machine
text: I received this as a free review sample. I immediately plugged it into one of the USB 2.0 ports on my ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP and was up and running. No drivers, no fuss. Since I do not have any laptops with USB 3.0 I could not test that speed, but a directory containing 19.4GB transferred via my USB 2.0 port in a little over twenty minutes. Blazing fast? Not by USB 3.0 standards, but darn quick form the ancient laptop (which may have actually slowed the process down.) The real reason why I rated this so highly is the cost. I recall purchasing a 64GB SD card a year ago that was vastly more expensive (at the time) than this half terabyte drive. Of course the SD card was miniscule, but this drive will fit in a shirt pocket. For me this is a convenient way to not only back up my two laptops, but also my phone and two tablets. Those are backed up via a hard connection to my laptop because they require FAT32 while this drive out of the box is NTFS. I would have reformatted it, but it worked so well with my laptop that I left it as is. If you are planning to use this with an Apple IOS or Android device only, you will need to reformat it via those operating systems. This comes with a cable that is USB A on the end that connects to your laptop or OTG connector, and USB 3.0 for the end that attaches to the drive itself. The 3.0 end is a little tight in tolerance, but once it's perfectly aligned it slips in and holds firmly. Bottom line: this is inexpensive mass storage that is great for backing up files and documents, storing large media such as movies and music, or transporting files to and from work.

title: Same protection in a different form factor
text: In 2011 I purchased a [[ASIN:B000WJB1AW Tripp Lite TLM825SA Safety Surge Protector 120V 8 Outlet Metal 25ft Cord OSHA]], which is still going strong. A few months age I purchased another and recently purchased a pair of these. That alone should tell you how satisfied I am with the brand. This is a heavy duty protector, both physically and electrically. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. The main reason why I own so many is I am a musician who owns amps, a PA and keyboard and the power in many venues is marginal at best. This is inexpensive protection and I have witnessed other musicians' gear getting fried in the same venues in which I play, so I know these surge suppressors work. My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly. I do want to note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. If the devices that you want to plug this into exceed the rated specs on this product page this is not the outlet for you.

title: Excellent sound quality and small form factor
text: I received these as a free review sample. Note that these are NOT bluetooth. They are strictly hardwired and require two connections: (1) 3.5mm into your device's audio out or earphone jack and USB A for power. Sound quality is excellent. I was impressed with the bass in particular because it sounded natural. Many speakers I test have a bias towards bass, which is great for a lot of contemporary music that is bass-centric, but sounds artificial playing music that is more acoustic in nature. Since I listen to a lot of jazz piano trio albums these speakers are perfect for me. The high end will not break up at the highest volume, but does sound a little compressed. Again, that is not necessarily bad because high frequency compression makes some music sound better. The mid range is very rich and one of the reasons why these speakers sound so good to my ears. Volume is more than sufficient for a 20x30 foot room. There are no controls on the speakers, so you need to control the volume and EQ from whichever device you plug these into. My phone, tablet and laptop all have hardware/software to do this and chances are so will your devices. My laptop's spare USB port was sufficient to power these speakers, and the big plus is you do not need to worry about batteries, wall warts and the such. I was able to also test these with my phone connecting the USB cable end to a charger. To be honest, that is a little inconvenient because the cables are hardwired into the speaker master unit. I would have much preferred separate ports and cables for the 3.5mm and USB, which would have allowed me to purchase cables of specific lengths for my own needs, as well as easily replace one or both of the cables if they were to become damaged. Despite the cable issue I mentioned above these are nice, compact speakers that sound great. More importantly (to me) there are no batteries to worry about, and they take up very little desk space.

title: Excellent portable light
text: I received this as a free review sample. Up front I want to explain why I subtracted a star: two reasons, foremost is the instructions are in Chinese. That is not a show stopper because no instructions are needed. The second reason is the USB charging cable uses a barrel style connector at the end that connects to the light itself. That means that if you lose the cable you will not be able to easily replace it. Standard micro USB cables are available from even grocery stores. This style is not. Normally I would not subtract a star for just one of the issues I cited, but I think both, combined, prevent it from being a five star product. It has a lot going for it. It definitely illuminates, and I love the fact that I can go from dim, to medium that is sufficient for reading, to very bright that is suitable for hobby work. For example, I restore vintage fountain pens and at the brightest setting, plus a magnifier, I can see exterior details that I normally used an illuminated magnifier to discover. The gooseneck stays put in any position I place it. That is mainly because the LED array is so light that it imposes little weight. I am on the fence about the base. I like it and it does stay put, but is easy to knock over, which can be a pain if you are using this for detail work. What I would love to see is a magnetic strip on the base, which would allow me to place it anywhere. In fact, I am probably going to glue a magnet to it. Bottom line: this is a relatively inexpensive light that definitely does the job.

title: Excellent protection, but ...
text: I received this as a free review sample. As advertised the protection is excellent. The construction is as well, and you actually can turn it inside out to change the color scheme. Here is the 'but': this case literally fits the Sound Blaster Roar 2 like a glove (and it is only for the Roar 2 model.) The stretching and pulling required is a bit onerous. I thought it would be a learning curve issue, but each time I use this bag it is as difficult as the last time. Difficult, but not impossible. On the other hand, had this been designed for an easier fit I am not sure the same level of protection would be there. Also note that this is strictly for transporting the Roar 2. Once it is inserted in this case you cannot access controls. I kind of like that because I do carry my Roar 2 around and appreciate the fact that this will keep it from getting dinged. One final thing: the top cover does not completely close. There is a gap and there is no zipper. That is why you can turn this inside out. Bottom line: this provides excellent protection and is well made. On the other hand, there are challenges as I noted above and you will need to weight those into a purchase decision. I do use mine a lot and have a love/hate relationship with it.

title: Better for a night light than for music stands
text: I received this as a free review sample. As a music stand light it's functional, but not ideal. As a night light or even a clip on to a book for night time reading when your partner of sleeping this is truly useful. Be aware that it's small and even at max illumination with all LEDs active it is not glaring. That is a good feature, but the tradeoff is as a music stand light you may have to keep adjusting the goosenecks to get optimum illumination. The goosenecks are a little on the thin side, which is another reason I think this is best suited to clamping directly on a book or headboard (if you can find a spot that the clamp can grip). On a music stand turning pages too briskly can change the position of the LEDs; not a problem when reading a book, but not the distraction you want when playing an instrument. Bottom line: if you are looking for a light for your music stand carefully comparison shop. If you are looking for a portable and effective reading light you will love this one.

title: Excellent sound quality and LOUD
text: I received this as a free review sample. I'll spare you a regurgitation of the product specs or paraphrasing the previous two reviews, but will focus on what sets this one apart from the pack. The biggest surprise I had was volume. This is a relatively small speaker and most bluetooth speakers in this one's size and price range are designed as personal speakers that are meant to be nearby on a desk, night stand or counter top. I can clearly hear this one two rooms away indoors and even outdoors in areas with high ambient noise this can cut through and project sound. Sound quality is neutral, and I mean that in a good way. While there is some bias towards the mid range frequencies it does not 'color' the sound of music being streamed to it. To be honest, this is not going to crank out heavy bass, so if you listen to bass-centric music you may be disappointed. On the other hand, the highs and lows are practically seamless, with a slight emphasis towards the mid range, so if you listen to jazz, blues or some forms of rock and Americana this speaker will probably please you. One review discussed bluetooth range issues so I specifically tested that. Even two rooms away, which normally causes drops in quality, I was able to get crystal clear streaming with no drops in the music quality streamed from a Samsung Note 3. The distance is approximately twenty feet, but definitely not line of sight, so I am happy with that aspect. While the product specs claim six hours of music, you can realistically expect somewhere between four and four and a half hours if you have the volume cranked. If you drop it to about a quarter - perfect for near listening up to two or three meters - you will get the claimed play time.

title: If you are in the Samsung camp this is great
text: There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution. I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones. Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one. You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure. If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.

title: Perfect for my needs
text: I purchased this for a single application and for that it works perfectly. Specifically, I wanted a way to mount a tablet to a microphone stand. I know there are numerous solutions to do that, but I have been using a [[ASIN:B00PXC5HU8 Grifiti Nootle Universal iPad Tablet Tripod Monopod Mount]] that is designed to mount tablets to photography tripods. There are times when I want to use a microphone stand instead and many of the adapters for that do not give the flexibility of movement and adjustment that this one does. This assembly is more than capable of carrying the weight of my Samsung Tab 3 10.1 plus the Grifiti Noodle mount. And when I position the tablet at a specific angle the ball assembly can be firmly locked in place and will not budge. For me this solves a narrow and specific problem and does so inexpensively and well. I cannot speak to other scenarios, but in my book it's a five star solution and I will probably purchase a spare for contingency.

title: Perfect for its stated purposes
text: I received this as a free review sample. This is not a zoom type telescope. You can adjust focus for your objective (the 52mm end) as well as the eye lens (the 16mm end), but you will not be able to zoom in. Think of this as a mono scope that can bring a far object into sharp focus. Another thing to note is the field of vision is less than the 18 degrees marked on the body. It's about half that, and the night and day marking does not imply that this is a night vision scope. You will still need an external light source in low level lighting conditions. For example, moonlight will work, but in total darkness you will not be able to see a thing. For me this is very useful for a hobby of mine, which is reptile spotting. Where I live there is an abundance of species, especially turtles and snakes, but we also have alligators and many interesting lizards. I prefer observing gators from a distance, and when walking down trails in parks (and there are many in my area) it's nice to be able to sit in a stationary point and scan for gators on banks as well as swimming. Same for various snakes, both land and water. What I love about this scope is it's rugged. There are no lens caps, but the nylon case that comes with it makes it ideal for outdoors activities in harsh environments. It's outer material appears to be rubber, and I have dropped mine a few times without damaging it. When you do bring an object into focus it's sharp and crystal clear. The field of vision may seem narrow, but you can actually take in a lot of details by slow scanning. It may take a little time to get accustomed to viewing wide fields of vision with it, but once you do, it's easy to use.

title: Superb protection
text: I received this as a free review sample. Although it's designed for notebooks, I am using it for my 10.1 inch tablet and for that it's perfect. One of the main reasons why I rated this so highly is the protection that it affords. Part of the reason why it's so slim and light, yet protects so will is the interior has an arrangement of raised, circular shapes. They provide cushioning on both sides of the interior. They also greatly reduce shock in the event of a fall. I tested that by taking a functioning - but no longer used - Acer Aspire One notebook and dropping it from waist level inside this bag on a hard floor. There was no physical damage to the exterior of the Acer and it powered up and operated normally. The exterior of the bag has a spongy feel that also diminished shock, so the protection is twofold. Other features I love are the heavy duty seams and zippers, and even the color scheme. On the latter, there is enough red to catch my eye when I am packing my gear and doing a visual scan to make sure I did not leave anything behind. I have 'forgotten' black cases in the past, but this one is hard to miss. Do be aware that there is a slight chemical odor to this bag when you first unpack it. That will go away in a day or less, but it's there and you need to know about it before you make your final purchase decision. Also carefully read the part of the product description that states, ' If your laptop screen size is 14 inches, and the maximum thickness greater than 28mm (0.11"), please do not select this bag.' That will save you some frustration if your laptop is too large for this bag.

title: Rock solid with some advanced features
text: I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made. Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly. Dimensions are: Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom. Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios. Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points. This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees. Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.

title: Allowed me to use a condser mic with my Samsung tablet
text: I purchased this specifically to connect a condenser mic to my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. I needed two other devices to make it work - an XLR M to F cable and a phantom power source (for the latter I am using an [[ASIN:B00KAPGLQC InnoGear® 1- Channel 48V Phantom Power Supply]] and the combination works like a charm. The cable itself is not especially heavy gauge, but the connectors and strain reliefs are high quality. I live the precise fit of both the 3.5mm and XLR connectors, and the strain reliefs are such that the critical areas on both ends will not be subjected to bends that will fray or harm the inner conductors. Of course, the main point for me is this works with my tablet, and it not only does for it, but also for my Note 3 phone. I use my tablet as a video camera for recording musical performances and until I added a condenser mic (an MXL 551R) the sound quality was poor. Since using the mic - made possible in part by this cable - the sound quality has dramatically improved. Basically, I carefully checked out a number of similar cables and this is the one that had the best reviews and specs. I paid more for it, but feel that I also received commensurate value because of the construction and overall solid performance.

title: Very effective. Does change the typing height of your laptop
text: I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows. This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.) Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved. Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two. If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.

title: As good as the OEM Samsung card
text: When I purchased my Note 3 from Verizon I also purchased a 64GB Samsung card that has served me well for nearly eighteen months. I decided to purchase another 64GB card to back up the one in my phone and I took a chance with this one. It has yet to let me down. Since my files are nearly static on my phone (the only major charges are new music and photos), after I synched my Samsung's card to this one I swapped this one into the Note 3 as my primary card. I figured that any issues with streaming music, shooting video clips and photos would show up fairly quickly with constant use. That is why I am pleased. I honestly cannot discern any difference in either performance or reliability with this card. I am so pleased that I am going to purchase another to back up my laptop. At present the price of these cards have dropped dramatically since I paid Verizon nearly ninety bucks for my Samsung card. I am sure that brand has also dropped in price, but this one is so solid and reliable that I am going to stick with it - at least for the time being. The bottom line is if you own a phone or tablet that will recognize 64GB this is an inexpensive way to upgrade an older 16 or 32 GB card.

title: Almost plug and go
text: I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions. My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap. What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong. There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.

title: Not for hi-draw devices, but handy for common peripherals
text: I received the four port model as a review sample. Note that this is a quick way to expand or multiply USB ports on a PC or laptop, but you cannot plug external hard drives into it along with other devices because you will quickly max out the USB power limit. I use mine for my mouse, a camera synching cable and a 32GB thumb drive. That leaves me a spare port for synching (but not charging) my phone or tablet. For my purposes this hub is perfect. It gives me the expansion for the low power peripherals I use, and it is handier to plug those into this hub than to fumble around with ports on the back and sides of my laptop. As for full speed, I cannot test this because my old laptop only supports USB 2.0. The speeds that I get from that, though, are on par with what I get if I were to directly connect my phone or tablet (or thumb drive) to the laptop's integrated USB ports. I will leave it to others to discuss USB 3.0 performance. This is truly plug and play on my Win XP and Win 7 laptops, and I tested it on my Note 3 phone with an OTG adapter and it worked in that configuration too (I connected a keyboard and mouse for that test.) Bottom line: if you are planning to plug in hard drives and other high power drawing devices you will need a hub with an external power supply. For mice, synching and other low power peripherals this is both convenient and well made, and is at the least the equal of every other USB hub I own or have tested.

title: Interesting design
text: I received my headband as a review sample. I want to note that I did not experience any drops in streaming as noted by other reviewers when using this with my Samsung Note 3 phone, but did have some issues with my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. The latter has some bluetooth problems that are well known, so I am attributing my issues with Tab 3 flaws and not this headband. I briefly tested this with an HTC One Remix with no problems either. This headband is unique in that it was designed with real, strenuous sports in mind - or at least activities that make you work up a sweat. As such I tested my streaming as noted above with my source devices (phones and tablets) at least twenty feet away. That simulates where you would place those devices during a game of tennis. It does seem impervious to sweat, although I would not call it sweat-proof. If you use it heavily and frequently you'll need to clean it at least weekly - see some of the top rated video reviews on this page for instructions for that because it is a bit tricky disassembling it the first time. Also note that it's a snug fit on my head, which is size 6 7/8. I am guessing that if you wear a men's hat size above 7 1/4 it will be too snug. Take that into account. Sound quality is excellent in my opinion. For the past nine months or so (at the time of this review) all brands or phones seem to have taken a major leap in that respect and these are no exception. The high frequency response of the phones is clear at max volume and the bass is deep (but not thumping). The mid range seems to be the sweet spot, and is rich and full. The volume itself is not super loud, and it is not noise-isolating. It does keep out most ambient noise though, and while these are not perfect for critical listening they are excellent for casual listening during sports and other strenuous activities. If you want phones that stay in place regardless of that you are doing, and also demand respectable sound quality these merit consideration. I have not researched the market, but these are the only headband phones I have come across among the dozens I have tested to date.

title: The solution I needed
text: I have gone through a few mounts for my Samsung Tab 3 10.1, only to be disappointed each time. My main use was to mount to a microphone stand, but none - including the [[ASIN:B00BMUARHI Gator GFW-UTL-TBLTMNT Microphone Stand Tablet Mount]] - would hold it securely when in a case. In fact, the Gator did not fit it at all, which was the catalyst for me to give up and seek another solution. This mount works perfectly. True, I had to settle for a camera tripod, but even that turned out for the better because tripods are inherently more stable than microphone stands, and also with pan heads allow me a lot more flexibility in placement and viewing angle. What I really love is this mount will work with the two cases I use with my Tab 3: a [[ASIN:B00LIQJ1DW Samsung Galaxy Tab3 10.1-Inch Case Cover]] (my favorite and one the Gator case absolutely would not accommodate) and a [[ASIN:B00E8C8NCI Fintie Folio Slim Leather Case]], that did allow me to use with the Gator mount, but the fit was so tenuous that I never trusted it. Much to my surprise this mount also securely holds my [[ASIN:B00GJ3MF9Q Verizon Ellipsis 7 4G LTE Tablet, Black 7-Inch]] tablet, so if I need to use that too, this mount will fit it. I am so happy with this mount that I am purchasing a spare. As an FYI, it also holds my iPad 2, so it's truly versatile. Plus it beats any microphone stand mount that I have tried, and I have checked out a half dozen of those.

title: Nice quality mat
text: I received this mat as a review sample and own a number of brands to which I compared it. First, there are only nominal differences between and among most of the silicone baking mats on the market, so the main factors are price and construction. For former is highly variable, but if you comparison shop what you are looking for are size and overall construction. These are about 3/10ths of an inch thick so are well constructed in my opinion. They are designed to fit an 18 x 13 baking sheet, and have a slight textured surface that makes them ideal for not only baking, but for rolling out dough. Another factor is this one will withstand heat up to 450F, whereas some brands will only go as high as 425F (and others will go higher at 480F). Consider those factors too when selecting a baking mat. If you have never used one of these from any brand they are infinitely better than parchment paper, and you do not have to use any kind of grease or shortening because they are naturally non-stick. Do note that you cannot use them in direct contact with flame or heat source. I mention that because I gave a similar mat to a friend who tried using it on a stove eye. Don't! If you opt to use these without a baking sheet know that your times will need to be slightly adjusted. That is because the heat transfer is a little too efficient, but also these will cool a lot quicker as well, so when you first use them keep a close eye on baking times by visually checking on what you are baking a little earlier than usual and making sure that this mat is not causing the process to over bake. Cleaning is a snap and these can actually be cleaned in a dishwasher. More importantly, they are perfect for rolling out dough (I sometimes use a pair of silicone mats - regardless of brand - with one on top and one on the bottom of the dough. When I roll out the dough by rolling over the top mat I can get a more ever, thinner dough. Bottom line: this mat is well made, has a fairly wide operating range and a slightly textured surface for true non-stick.

title: Reliable, no-frills tablet for folks on a budget
text: I received this as a review sample and have been using it for a little less than a week. At the time of this review this tablet is shipping with Android 4.4.4. Before I dive into what I like and why I rated it so highly I want to set expectations. This DOES NOT come with bluetooth, and the screen and cameras are not especially spectacular. The screen is readable (easily so) and has nice, vivid colors. However compared to even my Note 3 phone it falls short. As the cameras, for some reason tablet makers seem to skimp on those as though they are an afterthought. Since there is no bluetooth you are stuck with the internal speaker or using phones. The internal speaker is not what I would call optimum for listening to music, but the included phones are surprisingly decent. I also connected one of my bluetooth speakers that accepts 3.5mm input and the sound was excellent, so while this does not have bluetooth, you can still stream music to it. Another thing it does not have is bloatware that every other tablet (and phone) seems to be plagued with. That is one of the reasons why I rated this so highly. But the real reason why I gave this tablet five stars is price. At the time of this review it is selling for sixty bucks, which is not a bad deal for an entry level tablet - especially if you want to browse the web, stream music or wile away the day on facebook. It is a complete package that includes a stylus, soft bag, charger and cable, and OTG adapter. The latter allows you to connect USB peripherals to the micro USB charging port. I tested it with a keyboard, then a mouse and it recognized both. The USB charging port is another thing I like - it;s a micro USB type, which is a major improvement over some entry level tablets that I have tested that use a non-standard barrel connector. You can add a 32GB SD card using a TF adapter. I tested it with an old SanDisk Ultra 32GB MicroSDHC Class 10 UHS Memory Card that was immediately recognized. The application manager allows you to move some apps to the SD card, so as you add your favorites some will be eligible for running off an external card (depending on the app, of course.) Browsing the web, using Google's location feature and maps, and Youtube all performed with no lag or issues. In fact I would put the performance head-to-head against my Verizon Ellipsis 7 4G LTE Tablet, Black 7-Inch 8GB tablet. Do note, though, that if you have all services turned on and are constantly using this tablet you are going to get about 2.5 to 3 hours of use time if you are not connected to a charger. For some folks that may be a deal breaker, so take that into account. Basically this is a stripped down, but very functional tablet for folks on a budget. If you can live without bluetooth and will be using it near a power source it's a decent tool (or toy, depending on your outlook) at an affordable price, It is a perfect first tablet for someone who also has an Android phone, and is definitely useful for folks addicted to the web.

title: Works well with my cable and holds the connection
text: I use this to occasionally connect two [[ASIN:B0002E38EE Monster Keyboard - 12' Instrument Cable - Straight to Straight 1/4" plugs]] together when twelve feet is not sufficiently long. For that cable brand and model this connector works like a charm. A few things I like are the fact that this does not introduce extraneous noise into the signal path, and the cables I cited snap firmly into the female ends and hold firmly. I am not doubting other reviews that claim they need tape to hold cables in, but that comes down to the cable itself. For the higher end Monster cables this is not an issue for me. Since I only occasionally need to use this connector I cannot speak to the overall longevity. Time will tell on that and if it prematurely fails I will update my rating and review to reflect that. Thus far, however, this has performed as a five star product for me and has allowed me to avoid buying a longer instrument cable.

title: Works perfectly for me and no issues as others have reported
text: I purchased this to transform a [[ASIN:B0002E38EE Monster Keyboard Cable - Straight to Straight 1/4" plugs]] to right angle at one end. The female connection mated perfectly with the Monster cable. Note that that cable is relatively high end with beefy plugs, so I did not expect problems with this adapter and have not experienced any. Since my instrument is a keyboard there is practically zero movement or opportunities for the connections to jiggle. In addition to no issues or complaints about the female end, I am as happy with the male plug, which has firmly mated with a few amps and a PA. If there is any issue, it's the fact that this adapter adds a lot of bulk to the end into which you plug a cable. On my keyboard it does protrude, especially with the cable I cited above. But the sound quality is noise free with my arrangement, and as I said, the connections at each end are firm and solid. It may just come down to the quality of cable that you intend to use with this adapter. For the Monster model I am using this is a perfect way to change one straight end to angled.

title: Better sound than I expected
text: I received this as a review sample. I had low expectations regarding the sound quality, but was pleasantly surprised. In particular, the mid range response is rich and full, with a decent high end that does not break up, and a low end that turned out to be unexpectedly boomy. Not in your face boomy, but not anemic either. Also, this paired and connected easily to my Note 3 phone. I did not make test calls with it so cannot credibly discuss that feature. I also only wear it occasionally and normally for an hour or two in the evening or morning if I am outside, so cannot validate the battery life claims. Even if those are in the ballpark (and I suspect they are) then their specs are excellent for any speaker in this price range. Finally, the cap keeps my head and ears warm in thirty and forty degree weather, which we actually have in central and north Florida Granted it is not many days out of the year, but when we do have sub thirty degree weather a cap such as this is greatly appreciated, and is a key feature in my opinion. Regarding the speakers protruding as claimed by another reviewer, that is true to a point. But they do not look horrible (or not to me anyway). My high rating is based on the sound quality, ease of pairing and play time, and the fact that they keep my ears warm.

title: Interesting, but not terribly practical and could be improved
text: Up front I received this as a review sample and as much as I would love to love it, I just do not. Here are a few reasons why, which I will get out of the way first so I can end this review on a more positive note. However, first I am going to try to describe what this is: an Android tablet in a camera form factor. Foremost among the reasons why I subtracted stars is the instructions do not begin to scratch the surface. Even the quick start instructions did not disclose any illustration details of the buttons and ports. In fact, there were no details about inserting the paper for prints or even specs like charging times and how much use you can expect on a full charge. For an experienced Android phone and tablet user some of the missing information is a mere inconvenience. For someone accustomed to IOS or other types of phones and tablets the learning curve can be daunting. Second, since this is a full blown tablet the screen should have been larger in relation to the overall form factor. Instead the printing mechanism takes up real estate that would be better suited to allocating to the screen. Indeed, the mere fact that this has a printer at all is a head scratcher for me because the near seamless connectivity to remote printing that this device's software allows obviates the need for on the spot printing. In this day and age photos are mainly shared in digital form with only occasional need for hard copies. Especially when thirty prints from a pack of Zero-Ink paper runs about fifteen bucks at the time of this review - see [[ASIN:B008GVVTPU Polaroid 2x3" Premium ZINK Zero Ink Paper 30-Pack]]. Since this is camera-centric the lack of a 1/4-20 threaded mount for tripods is a glaring omission and yet another reason why I subtracted two stars. THE GOOD: this is a full fledged Android computer that is a breeze to set up and configure. I had that part up and operational in less than five minutes. Do bear in mind that not only am I a retired IT professional, but have extensive Android experience, so for folks like myself the dearth of documentation is not an issue. Even a novice user can follow the basic set-up instructions, which allow you to skip steps and come back later. Although the screen is not as large as I would have liked, it is more than sufficient for most tasks and is a lot larger than my Galaxy Note 3 phone's screen. The computing part is relatively fast too. I was able to browse web sites at brisk speeds, and uploading photos to facebook was as fast as from my Note 3 phone or my Samsung Tab 3 10.1 tablet - both of which are fairly quick. Bottom line for me: unless you absolutely need the ability to print 3x2 inch photos you would probably be better off with a small tablet, which makes more sense and does everything else that this camera does (except the hard copy prints.) Of course, if you need hard copy prints and 3x2 inch ones are adequate, this may be just what you need.

title: More than a power strip
text: I purchased the [[ASIN:B000WJB1AW Tripp Lite TLM825SA with 25ft Cord]] four years ago and my experience with that one convinced me to purchase this one when I needed a second set of outlets. The only difference between the two is this one has a twelve foot cord where the other one had a 25 foot one. Since I have only owned this one for two months I cannot make sweeping statements. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. I will say that this one seems to have the same high quality as the older one. Plus I have already used this in locales with marginal power and it has protected my music amplifiers and keyboards. Note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. If the devices that you want to plug this into exceed the rated specs on this product page this is not the outlet for you. My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly.

title: Hand's free on a budget
text: Note: there is a [[ASIN:B00QEY99DU Newer version] of this earpiece that I have also reviewed. Like that one I received this as a review sample. This one is still impressive for the following reasons: foremost is price. Even at full list this is an ideal way to use your phone legally in locales that enforce hands free laws (and the number is growing.) It's also comfortable, which is surprising to me because I hate in-ear buds. In this case, the array f provided ear pieces in various sides ensures a good fit regardless of your age or size. Ironically the medium fit me perfectly. Sound quality for music is not spectacular, but more than adequate for casual listening. I made and received calls and the clarity of those on both ends were also adequate. Not spectacular, but not terrible. When you consider that this is less than twenty bucks at the time of this review then in that context you are getting more than you are paying for in that department. This may not be the best single ear headset on the market, but it's by far among the best in its price range - and since it is so inexpensive and does what it should do I am rating it five stars.

title: Perfect for critical listening
text: Since there are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews already I will focus on where these phones are best suited. I received mine as a review sample and have been using them for nearly a week to make sure I thoroughly test them. For me these are best for critical listening, and especially raw mixes if you do recording. Of course they are not limited to that. The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day. If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce. A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]). While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.

title: Great for active folks in harsh environments, but biased towards higher frequencies
text: I'll get the things I do not like about the review sample that I received out of the way first so I can finish on a positive note. Basically these phones have a distinct bias towards the higher frequencies, with a crossover to bass in my right ear and flat mid range response. In other words, if you are a critical listener you may want to consider other phones on the market. I was able to get decent bass response in my right ear using my phone's EQ app, but could not get any decent mid range. The net result is music sounds one dimensional (even with the bass response in one ear.) I am guessing that the crossover threshold is such that you get high frequencies in one ear and low in the other, with the mid somehow cut out or deemphasized. For folks who listen to audio books and inspirational or educational material this will not be an issue. I will say that even with the volume cranked the high end did not break up or become tinny. From a comfort perspective I had no problem wearing these for three hours with the medium buds that ship with it along with small and large ones. And I love the way they were securely held in place with the ear hooks. Another feature that I like is the cable is flat and tangle-free. Of course, the nicest feature is they are, indeed, waterproof. Bottom line: sound quality for music is lacking. However, if you are a casual listener and are into jogging, strenuous activities and wet environments these may be perfect. As much as I complained about the sound, I cannot find fault in the construction or ability to withstand harsh environments.

title: Compact and very effective as a music stand light
text: I will not regurgitate the product specs since they are not only complete, but have been validated by more than a few previous reviews. I'll stick to some key observations about the review sample that I received and why I think this light deserves five stars. The main reason why I love this light is price and performance. I own a few other music stand lights and they either perform on par with this one, but are priced twenty-five percent (or more higher), or they are not as well made. Features are also more than I expected for a twenty buck light. For one thing you can easily get seven hours of continuous use on a single charge. I did a rundown test on mine and it remained illuminated for a little over seven hours before it started dimming, That was with both LEDS in each head switched on. I ended the test when it started appreciably dimming, but even at seven hours this is more than adequate since I actually do use this as a music stand light and the longest performances are less than three hours. Another feature that I love is the LED indicator in the USB A end of the charging cable. It will be red until the light fully charges, then it will turn green. Note: there are two things that I do not care for: (1) the charging end is a barrel connector instead of a micro USB connector, so if you lose of damage the included cable you are going to have difficulty replacing it, and (2) the barrel connector does not completely seat into the charging port. It charges, but I would be hesitant of using this light in a studio where you wanted to suppress all electrical interference. I am not sure there is any from this light, but the fact that a conducting connector is partially exposed gives me pause. Bottom line: for stage performances this light is better and brighter than most other two-LED models and illuminates sufficiently to read music or lyrics. It holds firm when clamped to my music stand, and the flexible arms allow me to position the lamp heads for optimum reading while staying put.

title: Breathe new life into legacy gear
text: My primary use for review sample that I received was to dust off an old flat screen TV that I owned. It has the usual array of video and cable inputs, plus VGA in, but no HDMI. This cable allowed me to connect a cheap (and new) DVD player that has HDMI out so I could watch instructional videos in my music room. A few things to note: the construction is first rate. All of the connectors are precision fit and the cable itself is practically tangle-free. Plus at six feet it gives me some leeway as to where I place the TV and DVD player. The micro USB connector for power is a godsend because some devices will not provide sufficient power to transmit the converted signal. Any standard wall wart that you would use to charge a smartphone or tablet will power it if needed. What I love is the clear signal. To be sure this is not going to give a legacy TV or monitor HD quality video, but what you do get is going to be clear, stable and with no pixelation. Bottom line: if you need such a converter, this one is high quality and relatively inexpensive.

title: Excellent protection
text: I am not going to repeat other reviews, which cover most of the details of this bag nicely. For me the review sample that I received is one of the best when it comes to protection. The raised diamond design on the exterior is not for looks or 'coolness'. Those form a well engineered solution for protecting your Notebook computer. They absorb shock from accidentally dropping your computer, and are augmented by additional foam inside the case as well as the retaining straps that other reviewers have pointed out. Overall construction is excellent as well. The zippers are easy gliding and of sufficient design for the purpose of the case.The reinforcing piping around the case is not only strong, but padded as well, so a drop on the edge of the case will be somewhat mitigated by the piping. There are fancier and even more expensive cases available, but this is my first choice for the protection features alone. That is the basis of my five stars.

title: Excellent protection
text: Before proceeding I want to state that unlike some other reviews the sample that I received had no strong odor, There was a slight one from the synthetic material from which it is made, but nothing lingering or particularly obnoxious (to me anyway.) What I love about this insert is it's truly padded to the point that you can entrust delicate gear to it. Another feature that I like is the bottom and the top open and can be sealed with the velcro strips incorporated into the insert. In fact, do not lose sight of the fact that this is an insert that is designed to go into another case. I am using mine to store a wireless microphone, received and power supply. I store those in this insert and this insert in an [[ASIN:B000HZGFMA Arriba Cases Ac-140 Padded Gear Transport Bag]]. The Arriba case offers very little protection, so this insert is important to me. The material is water resistant, but the case itself is not because of the way the top and bottom flaps close. Again, this is designed as an insert and not a carrying case, so I am not complaining about that. Overall, this is a wonderful way to protect delicate equipment that is carried in unpadded (or lightly padded) bags. It has dividers for camera lenses that can be arranged to accommodate other kinds of equipment, or removed for larger gear. I am so impressed with it that I am considering ordering another for my second wireless microphone set up.

title: Clever design for a headrest mounted case
text: The review sample that I received had a sturdy elastic band that did not break on me. I do not doubt the earlier reviewer who claimed that theirs did, but my experience was different. When I claimed in the title that this is a clever design I am comparing this one to other headrest mounted tablet holders. I have tested literally dozens of other models and all required that either you remove your tablet from any case you may be using, or you endure less than optimum grips of the mount will accommodate a case. This one is a case plus headrest mount. There are some trade-offs in this one's design. First, you can only mount your tablet in landscape mode. Since that is the mode I always use this is perfect for me. If you need a mount that will accommodate portrait mode, or you need to switch between the two, this is NOT the mount for you. Some physical details that I do like include the heavily padded case when you are using outside of vehicle back seats. While the holder into which you insert your iPad is not the hard plastic, snap in design that affords optimum protection, it does dampen and absorb some shock. The covers are thick and provide a great deal of protection. In fact, that feature is better than ninety-five percent of every case I have ever tried. The organizer is handy, and all of the cutouts and accesses are perfectly aligned to an iPad's camera and various buttons and ports. If you need a case that will function as both a case and headrest mount this one is worth considering - as long as you understand the limitations that I have cited.

title: Extraordinary sound and ruggedness; volume requires close-in listening
text: When I put my review sample through my normal tests I was impressed with both the sound quality and amount of play time between charges. The sound pressure level (volume) though makes this more of a personal speaker than one for group listening on a patio or beach if there is a lot of ambient noise. This will really go for a full twelve hours at with the default volume. If you crank it all the way up expect about seven hours, which is still longer than most bluetooth speakers. This one sports an internal 3200mAh batter, which is the same capacity as the Samsung Note 4 phone. I found this speaker to be particularly excellent in two areas: ruggedness and sound quality. I will not go so far as to say that it's totally waterproof, but it is water resistant. The sound quality is spectacular. The full frequency spectrum of highs, mid range and lows is seamless. What I mean by that is there are no abrupt changes as those frequency bands are exercised. My test album is always Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]] because the instruments in the ensemble cover the full spectrum. When I played that album I could easily pick out every note of the trumpet, alto and tenor saxophones, piano, bass and drums. No range was distorted, and the entire album sounded full and rich. I also noticed that there is no particular bias in the way this speaker reproduces music. Some speakers are designed to emphasize bass and/or compress highs and the higher end of the mids. This one is fairly neutral in that respect. A very quick test of incoming and outgoing calls provided clear communications on both ends. I normally do not belabor those features, but had an opportunity to test them with this phone (I was on my screen enclosed patio at the time and the ambient noise was not an issue.) Overall this is an excellent personal speaker that is not particularly loud, but has a long play time and excellent sound quality.

title: Superb protection buy has a learning curve
text: I received one of these as a review sample and for what it does it deserves a full five stars.However, I am docking a star because there is a learning curve, due in part to sketchy documentation. I''ll get the challenges out of the way first. Even with the included documentation it's difficult to figure out some aspects of this case. Some examples: there is a pull strap on the hard, snap-in holder for the iPad that is held in place by two labels that say 'do not tear'. That strap is intended to remain as is and the friction and pressure of the iPad will hold it in place. The instructions do not mention this and I removed it anyway because it looked like a temporary shipping solution. Secondly, there are adjustable straps on the right and left sides of the case that prevent it from fully opening and remaining open. They are probably unnecessary and do create confusion. This case is not designed to fully open like a conventional case - it's designed to slide the iPad in and out using the T-shaped track. If you do want to use this as a conventional case you need only unfasten the two side straps and it will operate as such. On the plus side, this case if one of the best I have come across with respect to protection. You can literally drop it from shoulder height and it will protect your iPad. The shoulder strap is designed to function as a set of pockets as well as a comfortable way to carry your iPad. And the material from which this case is constructed is built to take a lot of abuse and last much longer than your iPad. Bottom line: this is a little over complicated and under documented in my opinion. However it's also ideal for folks who need a fairly rugged case. While the video on this page implies the target customer is a business user I think it's more ideally suited to first responders and folks who work in harsh environments.

title: Stylish, flexible and total protection
text: It may be a bit pricey, but is definitely at home in a conference room and does make an impression. However, the key is the protection it provides and the folio's flexibility in accommodating right- or left-handed folks. You can change the orientation of the sketch pad and tablet by simply turning the folio upside down, reinserting the sketch pad from that direction, and doing the same with the tablet holder, which is held in place by a magnet. In addition, this offers two different viewing angles as well as a typing angle when the folio is configured as a stand. See my customer-supplied images for details. I love the absolute protection that this folio/tablet holder provides. The holder into which the iPad snaps in is tough and shock resistant, and the folio itself is equally so. This comes with a screen protector to add yet another layer of protection. Of course, with the paper sketch pad covering the face of the iPad when this is closed gives maximum protection to the screen should you accidentally drop it. While the functionality and protective features are outstanding, this folio has looks too. If you like understated elegance this has it. Or it does in my opinion. I love the feel of the exterior, which is akin to a fine suede, but is truly tough. The pad itself can be replaced with 6x9 inch refills. The actual size of the one that ships with the case is slightly undersized, but I did test a standard 6x9 and it fit.

title: A vast improvement over the earlier generation of boxes
text: The product specs and RatherLiveInKeyWest's excellent November 23, 2014 review cover all of the highlights of this box. I'll confine my review to a few details that I love about this and why this one is yet another milestone in the evolution of these boxes. First I'll share my opinion about the lack of bluetooth. Frankly I do not feel that it's needed since this box is designed to integrate with a TV and usually that means a home audio system as well. If bluetooth is truly important to you there are two USB ports on this box, so you can purchase a blutetooth dongle and add that capability. One of the features that I love is you can not only control this with the remote that comes with it, but also wired or wireless keyboards and mice, and a Miracast-enabled phone. The instructions cover all of these options, including the Miracast one. I do recommend using a keyboard and mouse for the initial set up because the remote is tedious. The instructions are terse, but sufficient to get this box up and running. If you own an Android phone or tablet you will have an easier time than if you are more in the Windows or IOS camp. But even then it's not a steep learning curve. Like the control options you have an array of connetions options as well. They are covered in the product specs so I am not going to repeat them here. Suffice to say, this box is flexible and will connect to legacy TVs as well as the latest and greatest. Another feature I like is this will recognize SD cards up to 64GB, which provides more than ample space for media files. Plus this box is both stable and blazing fast compared to the previous generation. Bottom line: the boxes I have used in the past were better suited for geeks who loved tinkering. This one is a major step towards a friendly addition to your home entertainment system that an average, quasi-technical consumer can effectively use. It is also a key building block to seamless integration of home computing and entertainment system. For all of the above reasons I rated it five stars.

title: Simplify your life
text: Tinfoot's gushing review has merit. Like him I received one of these as a review sample and it not only worked as claimed, but the Wii was much more vivid. I will confess that the main program I use is the bowling one. Even had this maintained the original resolution quality it would still be a five star product in my opinion. First, because cabling is simple, Second, because of that simplicity you can move your Wii from one TV to another with a little less hassle. The final reason is this will extend the service life of a Wii since some TVs are now coming out with only HDMI ports. If you own a Wii and have one of the HDMI-only TVs this is a bargain.

title: Ready to go out of the box
text: Like the previous reviewers I received this as a review sample. I'll try to avoid repeating the other reviews and the product specs so you do not have a deja vu experience reading through them. What most impressed me is this was ready to go as soon as I unboxed it. All I had to do was pull it out of the carrying bag, remove some bubble wrap from the gooseneck and unfold the legs.
