For the beach or lawn this is essential fare for folks who are glued to their tablets. I tested the tablet holder out with a Versizon Ellipsis 7" tablet, a Samsung Tab 3 10.1 and an iPad 2. It easily accommodated each of them, making this universal. The pockets and cup holder are nice touches, This also makes a perfect chair for dorms, studio apartments and small home offices. I am currently using mine in an enclosed patio, but like the fact that I can fold it easily, slip it into the carrying bag and take it to outdoors events or the beach. I will say that this is not the most comfortable chair for prolonged sitting, I was using it in my living room (the joys of being a bachelor), but after a few hours I found that I had to stand and walk around. On the plus side, though, is the feet will not mar a wooden floor, so there are some nice features that make it worthwhile. Since others have exhaustively covered the tablet holder I will note one thing: the turn screw for the bottom part is for assembly only. It comes pre-assembled, but I thought it was to adjust the height. It's not. If you unscrew it the gooseneck lowers, but the turn screw pops out and you have to carefully realign the screw to the hole in the gooseneck. It's not a flaw, but I wanted to point that out in case you want to play around with the chair. Leave that part alone. Bottom line: this is actually useful. I had no idea how tied I was to my tablets until I tested this chair and started using it all the time. Not only is it worth every penny (to me and despite the comfort issue), it is also one of the most functional, portable chairs I own. If you cannot be away from your tablet this is well worth considering.

title: Very convenient and a true surge protector
text: J. Chambers' November 4, 2014 review provides the complete specs that are missing from the product description at the time of this review as well as a helpful video. I will not repeat his information and encourage you to read it. Like him I received my station as a review sample. What I like about this versus other surge protector solutions is this one actually has features that protects against electrical surges and spikes and provides the specs to back them up. That may sound like a no-brainer, but I have reviewed 'surge protectors' in the past that were really power strips with no real protection. What I especially like is the small, convenient footprint. That, plus the three outlets (one what is spaced to accommodate wall warts), and the convenience of two USB charging ports. I will say that the charging ports are slow. On my Galaxy Note 3 phone using a high speed wall charger I get a 1% per 2.5 minutes charging rate. It's over 5.5 minutes with this station, but for overnight charging is not an issue for me. Do factor that into your purchase decision, though. Another thing to take into account is the slide out holder for phones is 7/16 inches fully extended and may not accommodate most phones unless you remove them from any protective case. I charge my phone flat on my desk top, so it's not an issue for me, but if you want to take complete advantage of this station's features you should measure your phone's thickness in its case. Bottom line: I am totally pleased with this station despite some of the noted limitations. The convenience to me outweighs the compromises, which I cited to ensure that you are armed with enough information to make a purchase decision.

title: Design is more than just looks
text: As 'cool' as the cloth covered outer jacket is, this retro look on this cable has a real purpose. Most cables use PVC for the jacket and the dielectric properties will cause some signal distortion when they go through their store/discharge cycle. Granted, the amount of charge a PVC jacket will store and eventually discharge is minute and also will not affect charging. However, many of us use our cables to sync to laptops and other devices and with the cloth jacket this effect is so minimized as to be nominal. There are other reasons why I awarded the review sample I received five stars. At the top of the list is this cable not only supports charging my Note 3, but also is flawless when it comes to synching it. Not all cables I own will synch (sounds incredible, but unfortunately true), This one will and my guess why it's done so without errors so far is the gold plated connector that do aid in conductivity. Another reason for the five stars is the heavy duty housing for the connectors and how they manage to be both thin enough to be unobtrusive and substantial enough to assure a long service life. There are even strain reliefs on each end of the cable to minimize wear that can eventually cause diminished transmission at the weak points in any USB cable. Finally, the ends mate perfectly with every device with which I've tried them. I have only tested the micro USB end on my Note 3, but have tested the USB A end on my laptop, various chargers and battery backups and the fits on all are precise.

title: Great sound, a little anemic on volume in the shower
text: I received one of these as a review sample. I am not going to regurgitate the product specs, but will comment on some of them as they pertain to my own experience. First, the sound is very good. Not excellent, but close. I have a few albums with which I test speakers and this one was clear across the frequency spectrum when I tested it with Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]]. That album exercises the high, mid and low ranges of speakers and this one passed. The bass was a little on the weak side, but still deep. The highs and mids were as good as any bluetooth speaker in this one's class that I have tested. The volume in a shower is a little anemic. I an still hear music over it, but when the nozzle is at full blast it comes close to drowning out the sound. On the topic of shower - I had no problem securely affixing the suction cup to my tiled wall, even when the cup overlapped tile seams and grout. If you have the speaker cranked do not expect more than 3.5 hours of use time. The ten hours provided in the specs is a figure that assumes you will be playing this at thirty percent volume. Outside of a shower this is sufficiently loud at that setting as a close in speaker, but for showers or other high noise environments I am betting you will have it cranked to max. Overall, this is a nice speaker, especially for the thirty-some buck price that is listed at the time of this review. It stacks up well against other speakers in this price range.

title: Full solution with more than adequate performance
text: I am not going to repeat the product description, which is complete with regard to basic specifications and what this package contains. I am going to confine my review to personal observations and actual use of this camera. Note two things: I received this as a review sample, and I have not extensively used this camera. Thus far I have been using it for approximately a week, which is sufficient for basic functions, but not for long term reliability. This is a complete solution, down to an 8GB SD card and a pair of batteries that are included in the package. The main limitation with this camera is you will get about an hour of use for every three hours of charging. That is not bad for extreme type videos for which this camera was designed, but do understand up front that this is not going to replace a DVR or even your phone's video camera capabilities (depending on your phone) for regular video capture. Again, this is not designed as a general purpose video camera so I do not view that limitation as a detriment. The 8GB card that ships with this camera holds an hour of video at full 1080P 30FPS resolution. The camera will accommodate up to 32GB SD cards, and if you have an external battery pack like a [[ASIN:B00KX2DUU2 Lumsing® 4000mAh Ultrathin Portable Power Bank External Battery Pack Backup]] you can, in fact, capture up to four hours of video. Using an external battery pack is probably not a good idea when trying to mount this for extreme sports videos, but will allow you to use this camera for more general purpose uses. One feature that I particularly like is the fact that this uses a regular micro USB connection for charging and transfer. I have a few cameras that use barrel connectors and they limit your charging options, so this use of standard cables is a plus. Note that his this camera has no options other than MOV files for video. I had no problems with that format on my Windows XP laptop and it's fairly common with both Microsoft and Apple environments, but not all applications that run on those platforms. Another feature that I especially like is this camera comes with just about every conceivable attachment that you can think of. If you are directly comparing this to a GoPro the value proposition of this package is apparent. I am not saying that this is better than a GoPro because that camera has become something of a standard, and also I do not have enough direct experience with that camera to make a valid comparison. What I am saying is if this camera will meet all of your needs and/or if you have a set budget this one offers more value. The real decision, though, is yours. Overall, I am very pleased with this camera and the video quality. It's reasonably easy to operate and is versatile for the uses for which it was designed. While I cannot credibly compare this to the GoPro I can compare it to the [[ASIN:B00NEYHIHM Polaroid POLC3 Cube HD Digital Video Action Camera Camcorder]], which I do own, and between the two this one is hands down the better choice. In the class of value-priced action cameras this one gets a solid five stars from be for both performance and value.

title: Reasonable quality and is backwards compatible to 1.1 specs
text: When I received my review sample I tested it on a legacy system (a ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP) and a phone running Android 4.4.2. I tested the USB 2.0 compatibility on the ThinkPad and USB 3.0 on the phone using an [[ASIN:B00GLKI258 [OTG HUB with SD card reader] Unitek usb3.0 hub with OTG adapter Bus-powered HUB ALL IN ONE USB 3.0 HUB OTG Function]]. As a previous reviewer warned it's not advisable to plug hubs into bubs, but I wanted to text the transfer speed. In the case of the ThinkPad I plugged in an extra keyboard, mouse, flash drive and camera (the latter for transfers only). The load of devices did not exceed the 500mA that this hub kicks down to for power consumption when connected to USB 2.0 ports. this can support up to 900mA when connected to USB 3.0 ports, but note that it's still only viable for lower power peripherals. Plugging a single USB 3.0 external drive into this into USB 3.0 ports can eat your entire power budget, rendering the other ports in the hub unusable. Be aware that this limitation applies to all unpowered USB hubs, not just this one. I tested the USB 3 speeds using the set up described about to my Note 3 phone. This hub, even daisy chained into another hub, supported copying 10 GB from the phone to an SD card reader in about 30 seconds. That is blazing fast. While this is not the prettiest hub on the market (there seems to be a trend towards brushed aluminum these days), it performs per USB specs and has an integrated switch that I like. I had no issues whatsoever with either of the test beds I used. As long as you heed the limitations of unpowered hubs this one is worth considering if you need to expand your ports in a cost effective manner.

title: Basic protection at a basic price
text: I received this as a review sample. I am not going to repeat the product description, but do want to point out that this is designed for counters with outlets near the work surface. I mention this because although the specs clearly state that the cable is two feet long, some folks may miss that. This is basic protection. It is more of a breaker than a true surge protector, although the response time is one nanosecond. That's impressive. The clamping voltage, on the other hand is 600 volts, which is reason enough for me to use this on less than valuable gear like inexpensive power tools or lighting. Since this is priced at eight bucks (at the time of this review), it has a basic price tag, so it's a decent deal for what it is. And basically, that is a power strip with integrated protection that amounts to a circuit breaker. Better than just a six outlet strip, which costs about the same. One thing that you need to also take into account is the fact that this does not have 'wall wart' spacing. As long as you are using two or three prong power cords it's fine. If you are using any type of transformer you are going to lose an outlet or two for each of those. For what this is it's a decent deal as long as you understand its limitations. I am happy with mine, but I am using it on a workbench with low power and low cost appliances and tools.

title: Depends on where you are and your local market
text: I am not going to refute the other reviewers who had more success than I with this antenna. For one thing my house is located a good twenty-five miles from the nearest station (I am in west Volusia County, Florida and the nearest station is in Winter Park). I have had issues with other antennas, so am inclined to believe my problem has more to do with the local market and transmitters, as well as my home. The latter is because my house is framed in cinder block, which will attenuate an already weak signal. Assembly was easy and connecting to my TV easier still. I was able to get ghosted signals of a few stations but were unable to dial them in by repositioning the antenna or the fine tuning knob. I tested my TV reception without this antenna and got rasterized static, so the fact that it pulled in anything speaks highly of the design. Instructions are on the back of the box and easy to follow. I recommend that you do a web search for TV reception problems and signal strength in your area before making a purchase. Obviously this antenna works because there are customer reviews from verified purchasers who are happy with it. I received mine as a review sample and blame location and the other circumstances that I described.

title: Tiny form factor and big functionality
text: This is two inches long with the cap on, so it's tiny. I received mine unexpectedly with a shipment of a keyboard, so had no idea it was coming. I fell in love with it because it actually works with 64GB cards (I tested it with a [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10]]). What I love is it plugs right into my Note 3's charging port on the right side (that phone has a 2-part charging and synching port that supports USB 3.0 and the right side attaches regular micro USB connectors.) It's immediately recognized, You access the micro USB connector by removing the rounded cap. Flip it on the swiveling frame the other end is where you insert the SD card as well as plug into an USB type A port. It does not look like it has the larger USB connector, but that end does mate with any USB port. Speed wise it's no faster or slower than any other USB 2.0 device I own. Considering the convenience of having this I am not going to quibble either way. There is one thing that could be improved: the documentation, I could not make heads nor tails of this thing when I first received it. This product page and the previous review cleared it up, though.

title: Getting harder to find, especially MFi ones
text: This cable bears the MFi (Made for iPod/iPad/iPhone) logo on the packaging and looks nearly identical to the real thing. The only things different are there is no Apple logo on the cable and it does not carry the Apple price tag. I tested it both as a charging cable and a synching cable with an iPad 2 and it performed flawlessly. The thing that is the same is this is manufactured to Apple's specs and did earn the MFI certification. Why this is important to me is most third party manufacturers have dropped this legacy cable and are now licensing Apple's Lightning cable (if they are even MFi certified). Decent 30 pin cables are becoming scarce, and the ones from Apple are pricy. That leaves a lot of fly-by-night cables that have a high failure rate, and I am frankly tiring of replacing cables on a monthly basis (I had been purchasing them from a well known big box store as well as a nationwide electronics chain.) When I was offered this one as a review sample I could not resist. I've been using this as my sole cable for over a week and am not disappointed. The construction is identical to Apple's, and the performance is too. If you are in the same quandary as I - experiencing high failure rates on 30 pin cables - check this one out.

title: Works with Androids and plugs right into Win XP boxes too
text: I received this hub as a review sample and just had to test it on a [[ASIN:B00KCG95M6 Keedox® M8 TV Box With Remote Control]]. It was immediately recognized and worked perfectly. I also use it to extend my USB ports in my [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] with the same results. That one was connected to a Samsung Tab 3 10.1, then a Galaxy Note 3. All of those tests was using the hub unpowered. For connecting high power devices like external hard drives and DVD ROMs, I powered this hub using a [[ASIN:B00MRGKPH8 Sabrent 5V 4A 100V-240V to DC Power Adapter]]. I only tested a single external hard drive and a DVD player with this test and then only using the USB 2.0 speed since it was connected to a ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. The arrangement worked and I was able to get expected USB 2.0 performance - not blazing, but not molasses slow either. The only USB 3.0 device I currently own is my Note 3 phone and I could not adequately test this hub using that. I do love the looks of the hub, but the important thing for me is I was able to use it on some legacy devices as well as three Android devices with no problems whatsoever. I also like the fact that you can transform it into a powered hub with an optional power supply, or just use it out of the box for low power devices. Just be aware that if you opt to use it as a powered hub using the Sabrent power supply make sure that the devices that you intend to plug into it do not exceed 4 Amps total. Some of the larger external hard drives can easily eat into the power budget. Also note that of you attempt to use this as a charger (which you can do standalone with the optional power supply) you are only going to get 1 Amp per port and no over charging protection. I recommend not using it for that unless you are in a pinch. Bottom like: this is a versatile hub that has worked with every device I tested, and it looks good as well.

title: Versatile and works a long list of products
text: Like most of the other reviewers I received this as a review sample along with a [[ASIN:B00N38TQJC Sabrent Premium 4 Port Aluminum USB 3.0 Hub]]. This will actually work with just about any of Sabrent's hubs as well as most other 5 volt (DC) devices on the market that require up to 4 Amps of current. The barrel connector comes with an adapter to a larger size barrel connector to cover Sabrent hubs. I have checked every source I could find to get the barrel connector specs, but none are to be found. This is frustrating to say the least because this is truly a multi-purpose power supply that can be used on non-Sabrent products. Since it is not claimed to be universal I am giving it five stars because it works perfectly with the hub with which I tested it. One feature that I particularly like is the fact that the cable is heavy duty with good strain reliefs on both ends. This is not your typical, flimsy power supply cable. Another thing I like is this runs cool even with constant use. I am using it to power a hub with a disk drive and both the hub and this power supply are running cool even after a twenty-four hour period. This is capable of providing up to four Amps, but will only 'push' what the device requires. What that means is if you are powering four devices that draw .6 Amps each this supply will only push 2.4 Amps, so there is no worry about overloading. On the other hand if you are attempting to power a hum that requires over 4 Amps this is not the proper power supply and will not work. If you own a Sabrent powered hub this is a safe choice, Do make sure you know the total current draw of the devices into the hub and make sure that the total does not exceed four Amps.

title: Excellent for multiple low power devices
text: Before reading through my review I strongly encourage you to read Robert J. Newell's very helpful September 17, 2014 review. His discussion is spot on. I can only add my observations from testing the review sample that I received. One reason for the split cables that connect to your device's USB ports is to prevent overloading because these are for low power peripherals like a bluetooth dongle, keyboards, etc. This hub partitions four devices per port on your computer so that you do not overload a single USB port. If you want to connect devices like external drive that draw higher current I recommend that you consider the [[ASIN:B00N38TQJC Sabrent Premium 4 Port Aluminum USB 3.0 Hub ]] and associated power supply ([[ASIN:B00MRGKPH8 Sabrent 5V 4A 100V-240V to DC Power Adapter]]) instead. My test included connecting into each four-port bank a mouse, keyboard, thumb drive and an iPad 2 into one and a Samsung tablet into the other. I used the tablets for test synching. By plugging the split cable into two USB ports on my aging ThinkPad T61 I was able to move documents to and from the tablets while using mice and keyboards. It's weird having essentially three mice and keyboards, but this hub enabled that. Frankly I did not bother to test the claims Newell made because they made sense and I have come to trust his reviews. This is a perfect solution for those of us who are constantly testing USB devices, as well as folks who have a lot of low power ones. I love the way Sabrent designed this hub to partition into two four ports instead of trying to provide an 8-port mega hub that would quickly run out of power.

title: More than just a personal speaker
text: There are two things that I immediately noticed when I tested the review sample that I received: (1) the controls are on the bottom of the speaker, and (2) it's louder than other speakers in its size and price range. As for the placement of the controls, it isn't an issue for me because I usually control the volume level and track skipping from my phone. Regarding the volume it's capable of putting out, it's more than just a personal speaker. I can stream music to the speaker in my kitchen and hear it clearly in my living and dining rooms. That's pretty loud. The heart and soul of a speaker is the sound quality and this one is very good in that category too. It has good frequency response across the high, mid and low bands, but emphasizes the mids, then the highs and finally the low end in that order. While the bass is surprisingly prominent for such a tiny speaker it is not the dominant frequency band. The mids and highs are very clear and you can hear nuances in music in those frequency bands better than the bass. One final thing that I love is the ease of pairing and connecting. As soon as you power it up and scan for it from your phone or other device it shows up in the list of available devices. A simple touch of the device name on your screen and it pairs and connects. If you want to use the aux port (the 3.5mm one for headphones) all you need to do is press the button on the speaker that has a bluetooth and phone logo for three seconds and it switched to aux port mode. I test a lot of speakers and this is one of the better ones I've come across. Not only does it perform, but I like the styling, which counts for something. It's an easy five stars the way I rate, which factors price, ease of use, performance and sound quality. This one has it all.

title: Great for low current draw peripherals
text: I received one of these as a review sample and it works wonderfully when used to expand ports for low draw peripherals. You can charge a phone with it, but it's going to take forever. Also, it you are planning to use it to connect high-speed storage, you may be able to squeeze two of those, leaving two ports empty because the max output is 900mA. And if your high speed storage is using USB 3.0, just one device may max out this hub. For me I use this to synch my phone and sometimes a tablet to an ancient laptop, as well as hang a mouse and occasionally a camera for also synching to my photo album on the laptop. For those tasks this is sufficiently powered. What I love is this will work on my old ThinkPad T61 without additional drivers of any other hassle. More importantly it allows me to synch my finicky Galaxy Note 3. That phone balks at a lot of third party cables and even some USB hubs, so the fact that it works with this one is a major plus. Of course the synching rate is only at USB 2.0 speeds because the T61 does not have 3.0 ports. It's still fast enough for me, though. Another feature that I love is the heavy-duty cable that is attached to this hub. Some hubs that I own have flimsy cables that actually wear out if you are constantly moving your hub, but this one will probably outlast me. Indeed, since I am 65 that is sadly possible. Overall, as long as you are not plugging in high current draw devices like external drives, gaming keyboards (which can take up to 500mA of current), this is a great hub. Just bear in mind that this is designed with low power devices when making a purchase decision.

title: Perfect for reading new and legacy cards
text: I received one of these as a review sample and as soon as I plugged it into an old ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP it was recognized and operational. What I love is you can read the newer SDXC cards, as well as the legacy TF ones. Although I did not test this with USB 3.0, on my 2.0 laptop it was a lot faster than older card readers when I opted to write. Reading seems to be about the same speed as other readers. This page has a full set of product specs and I normally do not regurgiutate them, but I do want to rememphasize one bit of information that will set your expectations: 'SD card and TF card sharing one channel can not be read simultaneously.' By channel I am guessing that these two slots share the same bus since they are ajacent to one another on the bottom of the reader chassis. One thing that I love that is not technical is the form factor and the looks. This is small enough to fit in a shirt pocket (pigtail and all), and the brushed metal look is gorgeous. In fact I own a hub from a different brand that looks like this reader's cousin, and it's perfect paired with a Macbook or even a [[ASIN:B00F2ENU92 Lenovo Yoga Multimode 10-inch Tablet]] via an OTG connection.

title: Very surprised by the sound quality
text: The review sample that I received is priced in the intermediate range of phones, yet this one sounds as good as some I own that were in the hundred fifty dollar price range. What impressed me the most is the reproduction of frequency bands. These phones sound as though they are biased towards the higher frequencies, although the mid and low ranges are full and rich. No matter what volume the highs are clear and articulated, and the mids are also very clear and full. The bass is more than respectable and come in at the standard 20Hz. The upper end is at 22KHz, which accounts for the superb high end response. The response curve is fairly smooth and linear across the spectrum, so you can easily use these for transcribing music or critical listening. I love the comfortable, gel buds that ship with this set. It comes with small, medium and large buds that will accommodate just about any ear size. I have no problem wearing these for four plus hours at a time (and I normally dislike ear buds). Another reason why I awarded these five stars is the tangle free, flat cable. It's not only a joy to use, but noise free. The product description claims that these will attenuate ambient noise. It does, but not greatly so - or in my case anyway. I normally insert buds lightly into my ears, so that may account for my experience with them. One final note: I did not test the microphone function. I was so taken with the sound quality that I lost interest in that feature. I will say that if sound quality is important you will probably love these. I am still pondering how phones of this quality can sell for less than fifty bucks, but I am not going to look a gift horse in the mouth.

title: Immediately recognized by both my Galaxy Note 3 and Windows XP laptop
text: Long story short, my review sample was immediately recognized by my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone when I plugged the dongle into one of the ports on my [[ASIN:B00KMKKJWW Unitek USB 3.0 hub 4 port Bus-Powered OTG hub]]. It was also immediately recognized and functional on my ThinkPad T61 running XP. As great as it is, you need to pay attention to details when unpacking it. Specifically, the cardboard insert in the retail packaging has a web site for the manual. That is important because this thing will make no sense to you without it, unless you have used one of these before. The manual you will want to download is for model KP-810-10. Basically, the dongle is cleverly stored in the body of the keyboard, and the key is to find the small power switch, which is on the upper left side. After that you are literally up and running. While this makes a wonderful remote for a PC doing presentations, it's even handier connected to any android phone or device that recognizes an OTG connection. That is where this thing excels. However, for Windows PCs this is also optimum because it has Windows keys. If you need a remote for a Windows PC, or want a convenient way to interact with your OTG-capable phone or tablet this may well become your best friend. I can actually get real work done using this and my Note 3 phone. That is why I gave it five solid stars.

title: Rock solid
text: These are a precise fit for the Benro models listed and are well constructed of aluminum alloy. They can take the weight of heavier cameras, including film SLRs. The key to why I like them is they are precision made to mate with the Benro heads, and have the non-skid surface. Of course, another reason why I love these is they can remain permanently attached to your cameras to allow for quick swapping on the tripod. Finally, price is a factor for me and these are a convenient way to add plates to all your gear without going broke.

title: Worth it for the app alone
text: Kimberly R. Norton's helpful August 3, 2014 review thoroughly covers most aspects of this card. Actually, after spending a lot of time with the review sample that I received, this is a solution more than a mere card. First, a caveat. This card requires a reboot of a Windows XP system before it's recognized as a removable disk drive. In a real medical emergency this could be an issue. Granted, XP is obsolete, but Murphy's Law would probably go into effect if you were in a time-critical situation. Plus, this is strictly a Windows based solution. Now for the reasons why I love this. Foremost is the app itself. It leads you through the creation of medical information that is needed if you were being treated while unconscious or unresponsive. The text files can be read by any system, as well as uploaded to your phone. I have labeled my data card to note that the information is also on my smart phone - just in case the card fails for some reason. The heart of this solution is the app that created the medical data and the files that it produces. The card itself is clever in that an 8GB flash drive is contained in the form factor of a credit card. The USB 2.0 plug slides out of a protected channel that does not appreciably add to the thickness of the card, so it will easily fit in a wallet. In addition to the medical data this solution provides a scanner guard that you can use to sandwich your credit cards between that and the Medic ID Guard card. What this part does is guard against RFID identity theft, which is a very real problem. It does not take much to thwart thieves - wrapping credit cards in aluminum foil will do the trick - but this solution is much cleaner and is actually a side benefit. Prior to getting this solution I had been using [[ASIN:B00GC4RTKC RFID Blocking Secure Sleeve]]s. This solution, however, is a lot more convenient. Bottom line: there are some things that I do not like about this solution, but the benefits greatly outweigh them. As I mentioned, the app alone is worth the cost of this solution because it allowed me to create complete medical data in a structured way. I could have never done that on my own without additional hours of research to discover what information is actually relevant.

title: Perfect for the working photographer
text: If you own any of the Vanguard tripod models listed as compatible and multiple cameras this set allows you to keep two of them configured for quick swap. The construction is precise, although these are not magnesium alloy like Vanguard's shoes. That is not an issue for me because they have near the same feel and the same precise fit. I can say for certain that these will work with the [[ASIN:B003BQ71MA Vanguard SBH-250 Magnesium Ballhead with Sliding Quick Shoe]], with which I tested it. As for the other models I am going to take the word of the product description. They also come with a pair of allen wrenches, so in that respect these are a complete solution. If you own a Vanguard tripod with a compatible head these are as good as the more expensive Vanguard counterparts in my opinion.

title: Incredibly loud with above average sound quality
text: There are a few things that set the review sample I received apart from most other bluetooth speakers. At the top of the list is sound pressure level because this is the loudest bluetooth speaker I have ever tested. Literally, this can compete with waves on a beach, which can get pretty loud when the tide is changing. I tested it from three rooms away from my writing desk and it could easily be heard. In that respect it could provide background music for a flash mob, which is way beyond the power of most other speakers, which are designed for personal listening on a desk or night stand. The sound quality is also a cut above. While I have tested speakers that are better, this one is still on the short list of my favorites. The speakers are large and powerful, and they do a remarkable job of handling the high, mid and low frequency bands. As advertized the bass is pretty intense compared to ninety percent of the bluetooth speakers I have owned or tested (about fifty!) In addition to volume and sound, this is ruggedized. I mentioned that it could compete with wave noise at the beach. It can also withstand moist and sandy environments and being banged around. It's not waterproof, but is designed to resist it. While the product description and specs are complete I do want to highlight a few features that I personally love. First is ease of connecting this to my phone. When you turn it on it immediately beacons its presence (and announces it in a human voice.) Do a scan from your device for other bluetooth devices and this pops up immediately. A simple touch pairs and connects it. If you have an NFC-enabled phone like my Galaxy Note 3 it's even simpler. Just touch the device to the NFC logo on the speaker and you'll get a message on your screen asking if you want to connect to the speaker. Finally, time and distance claims are accurate. This actually will play longer than most speakers. The claim is twelve hours. I had it on and playing for ten and it probably would have lasted another two hours. So say at least ten hours to set expectations. It also claims to work from 25 meters, which is significantly more than the normal 10 for bluetooth. I tested mine at about 18 meters and it did not falter - the music streamed with no breakup or dropouts. Basically, if you want to play your music loud and still get decent sound this is the speaker for you. It has a lot of features that I did not mention (but are listed in the product description), but the defining one is sound pressure level.

title: Excellent low end as claimed with a qualification
text: The qualification I mentioned in the title is as long as this is used as a close, personal speaker the superior bass frequency response is there. Since M. Erb thoroughly covered most of the characteristics in his excellent July 24, 2014 review I am going to focus on the sound quality and a few observations. As stated, this speaker provides high quality sound in the lower frequency spectrum as long as it's within one to three feet. Even at twenty feet the sound is excellent, but the effect of the bass diminishes. The woofer is in the bottom part of the casing and do emphasize that part of the frequency spectrum. Although this is marketed as a 'bass machine' the high and mid range response is actually better than the bass (to my ears anyway), and the overall sound quality makes this one of the best personal speakers that I have tested. In fact, while I normally use Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]] to test speakers because it does exercise the full spectrum, for this one I used two other albums. First was Scott Lafaro's [[ASIN:B007CSETZU The Complete Live At The Village Vanguard 1961]] because Scott LaFaro's bass is prominent. That is how I arrived at my assessment of the bass response that I described above. I also tested this with a Chico Hamilton Trio album titled [[ASIN:B0089PCUT2 Jazz Essentials]] that contained a fuller range of instruments, including cello and flute. The reproduction of frequencies across the full spectrum was so spectacular that I had to give this speaker five stars. For features and characteristics read (and watch) M. Erb's review. If you are picky about sound quality, as far as I am concerned this should be on your short list of personal speakers. It will not fill a room with sound, but you'll be able to hear every nuance if you have it near by.

title: Exceptional sound
text: Normally when I receive a review sample I can do a thorough evaluation and write a review within two days. This one took longer. The reason is that it took me a while to hear the differences in this model versus the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]], which also impressed me (and I also own). After going through a pile of albums to try to understand what the product description meant by smoother bass I finally found an album that allowed me to hear it: [[ASIN:B00492ANTS Portrait In Jazz]]. When Scott LaFaro's bass came in on Autumn Leaves I started switching back and forth between this and the S1, and also hauled out some studio reference monitors. These phones are capable of going down in the 18Hz range for the low end, which is lower than most in ear monitors and phones that are usually in the 20Hz range at the low end. I am not sure my ears can discretely detect the differences between 18 and 20, but I was able to detect nuances that the lower end provided. These also go up a little higher than more phones, which are usually in the 20 KHz range, Again, I am not sure I can truly hear sounds at 24KHz, but there is a discernible difference. I tested that end of the frequency spectrum with a few Ahmad Jamal albums since he tended towards the right side of his pianos. One other thing that took me some getting accustomed to was the over-the-ear way of wearing these. I am use to in-ear or the old fashioned over-the-hear phones and I had to play around with these before I figured out how to place them in my ears perfectly. If you are use to over-the-ear you will probably not experience the learning curve that I did. A few other features that I have come to expect from this brand are here: extra tips of different sizes, a hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) and a 1/4" adapter. I love the flat, tangle-free cable that is tougher than it feels. And it has an adjuster like a chin strap on a cowboy hat that aids in keeping these firmly in place with the over-the-ear way of wearing them. This is definitely a five star set of phones (according to my way of grading, anyway), and one that I will not hesitate to recommend to fellow musicians. We tend to spend a great deal of time listening to music and these do an excellent job of reproducing it. My advice, though, is to take your time when you first get them because their true power is not immediately apparent. When you do start hearing the difference you will understand why I rated them so highly.

title: Truly are studio quality
text: I received these phones as a review sample and wanted to test the claim that they are studio quality. In point of fact they are very close. What I mean by studio quality is they are neutral sounding - there is no bias towards any particular frequency band. These are fairly even on the highs, mids and lows. Of course, if you are listening to modern music that emphasizes low frequency response with a lot of bass you may want to check out other phones that do a better job. I will say that while the frequencies are naturally divided, the separation is excellent so I am certain these phones have a crossover. Since there are ample specs in the product description (and two video reviews at the time of this one) I will spare you a recitation of that information. I tested these using a few key albums, and also plugged the 1/4 inch connector directly into my Roland RD-300NX keyboard to hear that instrument's natural responses. Both tests confirmed that these are studio quality. However, audiophiles who want unbiased sound will also love them. I played some of my favorite test albums like Miles Davis' Kind of Blue, Ahmad Jamal's Live at the Pershing and some 20-bit mastered CDs. In all cases the frequency response in each band was perfect and the ability to hear nuances (including the natural reverb on Kind of Blue) was a treat. More importantly I heard the albums the way the engineers wanted me to hear them. To be sure I do have other phones that are at this level of quality, but most are in a much higher price range. I did not expect to be impressed with I accepted a review sample, but not that I've had time to put these through their paces I am impressed. They are now in my practice room/music studio and there they will remain. Definitely recommended.

title: Perfect for headphones
text: I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers. In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half. What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases. These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.

title: Excellent composite audio cable
text: Note: at the time of this review this cable set is described as '3.5mm Male To 3 RCA Cable' when it's really a 3-RCA male to 3-RCA male for composite signals. My HDTV has legacy composite jacks to connect older DVD players and I am using the review sample that I received for that purpose. I replaced it with a premium grade cable by Monster, which cost me significantly more than this one is priced at, and there is no discernible difference in video and audio quality. The outer shield is slightly different in appearance form the standard 6 cut ones that most RCA connectors employ, but the fit of this set is as precise as others that I have used, and the integrated strain reliefs are some of the beefiest I have ever seen on any brand of RCA composite cable. Among the reasons why I awarded this five stars is value (relatively low price with high quality construction). This set sports construction features that are not usually found in sub ten dollar cable sets (the price range at the time of this review). For example, the connectors are gold plated, and the copper wire is oxygen free. The overall cable is both flexible, but heavy duty and is not likely to fail if properly used. My advice is if you are shopping for composite cable, consider this one before investing a lot more in a 'premium; brand that does not really outperform this one.

title: Superior quality
text: This is one of my favorite patch cables, and I especially love the fact that they come in a variety of them to color-code by function. I received mine as a review sample and it is one of the best constructed patch cables that I have used. Since I am using them is my music studio the best thing is they are low noise. Actually this is about noise-free as you can get. Part of the reason is the double shielding, but part is the overall construction. I also love the precision fit. I use these to patch bluetooth receivers in some of my amps and PA mixers for backing tracks. Lesser cables that I have used had a sloppy fit, These have a firm feel inserting and removing. Construction is top notch. Everything from the heavy duty strain reliefs to the plated tip, ring and sleeve are well made. I also love the flexibility of the cable itself. If you are looking for high grade patch cable for 3.5mm male-to-male, this is it in my opinion.

title: Handy for small peripherals and charging
text: Stephen M. Charme's incredibly helpful June 19, 2014 review covers this device in exhaustive detail. I'll attempt to not repeat him, so will confine my review to why I awarded my review sample five stars. Foremost, I love the convenience of having an all-in-one power and charging station for my phone, tablet and a few smaller electronic items. It takes up one full two outlet wall connectors in my music studio where I am using it. One of the plugs is a dummy that does not draw electricity. This ensures that you do not overload a circuit as well as providing stability to the rather large unit. At 15 Amps (1675 Watts) this is more than sufficient for the small amperage devices I am using (although I do have a 5 Watt RMS output tube amp plugged into it as well.) Where I live the power fluctuates too wildly to plug anything of value directly into a wall outlet, so this is essential. It's also a convenience with respect to the swivel. Most of the devices I am powering with this use wall warts, and even with the swivel I can only plug four in at any given time. While that blocks two of the outlets, had it not swiveled I would have probably lost one more outlet. I have found this so useful that I intend to order another to place in my gig bag for playing out. There is always a dearth of outlets on most of the small venue stages where I play, and the power in most of those places is usually abysmal. One of these for a small PA and keyboard will afford adequate protection as well as being conveniently small.

title: Inexpensive and reliable storage
text: Capacity is more than adequate for my needs, and the price is right. But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws. I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians. Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port. I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle. Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.

title: Great feel, easy to connect and decent battery life
text: I received the universal model as a review sample and tested on a few devices. Those were a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone, a Samsung Tab 3 10.1 and iPad 2 tablets. It paired and connected to each effortlessly and without going through a bunch of technical steps like the earlier generation of bluetooth keyboards. I pressed the connect button on the keyboard, scanned for it in my devices and - viola! - they paired and connected at a touch of my finger. I love it when stuff is that simple. The key feel has the tactile feedback that sets this apart from cheaper keyboards, In fact, I would say that the feel is equal to the one on my ThinkPad T61 laptop. It's about 9 3/8 inches wide, which gives a lot of typing space. A point of comparison is my laptop's keyboard is about two inches wider. Because this has an aluminum casing it is not going to creep away while you are typing, and it also keeps the keyboard from flexing when you are handling it. Again, some other keyboards that I have used were flimsy and did not last very long. One final thing I love is the micro USB connector for the power cable is sturdy. I actually had a keyboard from another brand that failed because when I pulled out the charging cable the internals of the port came out with it. I have been using my keyboard for over eight straight hours, untethered from a charging cable, and it's still going strong. In fact I am writing this review with it to test it. This is a five star product in my opinion because of construction, feel, and the fact that it does everything the specs claim for less than twenty bucks (at the time of this review.)

title: Refreshing and better than soda, but not a true coconut water
text: I purchase this locally so am going to confine this review strictly to the product without factoring price or shipping. This is not a true coconut water, but a drink that contains coconut water, nata de coco (a gel made from fermented coconut water), and flavoring among the ingredients. I love it because it's refreshing, especially on humid days, and uses real sugar instead of substitutes that I try to avoid. Each eight ounce serving contains 70 calories with 18 grams of carbs (16 of which are from sugars). Contrast that with the same serving of Classic Coke, which comes in at 95 calories and 26.4 grams of carbs (all of which are from sugars) and this wins from a nutritional perspective. This drink is much lighter than most sodas and I have personally found it to be good for suppressing my appetite as well. While it does quench thirst, it does not have the sodium content to be ideal for rehydration. Gatorade, for example, contains roughly 100mg of sodium for the same serving size, which is significantly more than the 15mg this drink contains. Moreover, this drink is missing potassium, which is also recommended for rehydration. I am mentioning this because there are coconut waters that are formulated for rehydration, but this one is more of a beverage. The main ingredient is mineral water, followed by nata de coco, organic cane sugar, coconut water, calcium lactate, citric acid, sodium citrate, gellan gum and grapefruid seed extract. Bottom line for me: I consume about sixteen ounces of this per day, and during exceptionally hot and humid days about twice that. Although this is no substitute for a rehydration drink, it does quench my thirst and the sugar gives me a boost without causing cramps in my fingers and toes like a soda does.

title: Perfect TV Box control
text: There are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews of this keyboard, so I will stick to how I am using the review sample that I received, and a few of my impressions. First, this is not a bluetooth device (it was described as such to me when I was asked to review it.) The only weak point is the documentation, which is terse, but well illustrated. Had it contained specs and compatibility data it would have been significantly more useful. However, this is not a major flaw. I first tested it with an ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It was immediately recognized and functional. My next test was to see if it would work with my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone running Android 4.4.2. I connected with wireless dongle via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]] and it worked. To be honest, that arrangement is a bit on the clumsy side for me. My final test and where this keyboard shines is when I connected it to my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 Smart TV BOX]] running Android 4.2. This keyboard made a lot of sense connected to that box because I rarely used it prior. I was using a corded keyboard and it was a trip hazard. Plus most of in interaction with it included few keystrokes, so this mini keyboard is perfect. In fact I find myself using the TV box a lot more frequently now that I have this keyboard. I think of it as a smart remote control - which it is - and have quickly grown to love it. As for prolonged typing, this would not be my favorite solution. However, that is subjective. I hated my Blackerry when I was required to carry one back in my consulting days too. But for occasional use this is wonderful. Bottom line: I would have never guessed that this would be the missing link between me and my TV box. Had I only tested this with phones and tablets I would have probably written a single word review: meh. Now, though, I see the wow factor.

title: Great for folks who love full size KBs
text: There are some excellent reviews already, so I will attempt to provide my reasons for giving this five stars without repeating what others have said. The biggest reason for my rating is this keyboard has a great feel. I normally hate chicklet style keys (it reminds me of my very first computer back in the 80s - a Commodore PET), but these are a breeze to type on. A few things I look for in a keyboard are tactile feedback and the elimination of key bounce. The tactile feedback is in the zone that I prefer, which surprised me because I initially thought that this was more of a gimmick than a serious keyboard. Key bounce - when you press a key and more than one of the character appears - is common on cheap keyboards and tha bane of my existence. This keyboard is rock solid and does not suffer from that effect. I love the weight of the board too. It's not overly heavy, but is heavy enough to stay put on a desk while I am typing. Moreover, while the ability to change the lighted key colors is somewhat cool, I touch type and was happy to discover that I can turn the lights completely off. One final reason why I awarded this five stars is that I plugged it into my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 Smart TV BOX]] and it worked immediately. I expected that level of plug-n-play from my Windows laptop, but was pleasantly surprised when it also worked seamlessly on the Android as soon as I plugged it in. This may look like a glitzy keyboard laden with bling, but it's really a pro grade one that fast touch typers will love.

title: Incredibly easy to install and use
text: When my review sample arrived I tested it on a few devices and it worked perfectly on each. The first device was my ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. I inserted the dongle (look in the battery compartment for it), and it was immediately recognized and activated. As soon as I turned on power to the keyboard I was able to navigate using the touchpad, bring up an editor and type. The next tests were with my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 1080P 5G 2.4G HDMI Bluetooth 4.0 Smart TV BOX]], then using a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] I connected the dongle to my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Tab 3 10.1 tablet respectively and was texting and performing other functions. This is truly a plug-and-play keyboard/touchpad. One final thing I love is the battery is a standard BT51 that can be purchased just about anywhere if you are such a power user that you need a spare. It's set up for thumb style texting, so most folks will be immediately comfortable with it. I love the tactile feedback from the keys, which were a pleasure to type with, as well as the array of function keys and buttons. If you spend a lot of time on smaller devices this is a dream come true. At about thirteen bucks at the time of this review it's a bargain for folks who are heavy texters.

title: Excellent sound and interesting features
text: First, I will disclose why I gave this speaker only four stars: when the review sample I received arrived it was not very intuitive and the instructions were little help. In fact, it took me ten minutes of fiddling to realize that this is not a bluetooth device and it would have probably taken longer had I not read Comdet's May 27, 2014 review. Mind you I am not subtracting a star because it's direct connect only, but because they instructions were obtuse at best. That is a minor fix on the manufacturer's part and one I hope they rectify. The sound is absolutely incredible. Not for it's size, but incredible period. The full spectrum of sound frequencies blew me away. The bass is what impressed me the most. Since this is a direct connect only type of speaker you will be listening to it fairly close, so the volume is more than sufficient. One of the interesting features is you can daisy chain up to three of these together. To be honest I do not see the point since it's designed as a personal speaker, but the technology is embedded in the device and it can be done. This would have been more impressive had this speaker been bluetooth-enabled. Controls are simple to use and cleverly designed to take up as little space on the unit as possible while still providing an array of functions. I love the SD card slot, but do not much care for the hardwired 3.5MM connector that plugs into a phone port on your tablet, PC or phone. A port and separate cable would have been a better solution since it's one less failure point. As it is, if you break the 3.5MM pigtail you are out of luck unless you can repair cables. Quibbles aside, this has the makings of a five star product and especially the speaker technology that this is based on. The sound quality is incredible.

title: Gorgeous design and sturdy cover
text: The motif on the review sample I received is a beautiful example of Mexican folk art. In that respect it's strikingly beautiful and unique. The review sample that I received had a strong chemical odor that was briefly overpowering when I removed the protective cellophane wrapping. I was forewarned about that before the sample arrived. So expect it and do not be alarmed because it dissipates within hours. Aside from the motif and its vivid colors I loved the texture of the outside of the case. It has a fine, pebble gain feel so it will not get slippery on a wet day or if you are sweaty. The plastic holder into which my iPad 2 snapped provides very good protection. It's thick enough to protect the edges of the iPad, but with enough give to cushion shock. Of course, the outer part of the case does an excellent job of cushioning and absorbing shock if you accidentally drop your iPad. On the inside of the front cover are three strips that augment the cushioning across the screen, which is a nice feature that also shows the attention to detail when this case was designed. They are also the slots that allow you to angle your iPad. Other features that I love and which inspired me to give this case five stars are the 360 degree rotation, the three viewing angles that should suit most people, and the cutouts. All of the cutouts were precisely done and even the camera one ensured that nothing interfered with the lens or caused flashback that some cheaply made cases do. I've tested and owned at least a dozen iPad cases and this one is as good as the most expensive ones, but has a design that truly stands out.

title: Best in class for sound, quality and comfort
text: I have tested a number of in ear monitors (IEMs) from Brainwavz and other brands and the review sample that I received is the best in its price range that I have come across. In fact, it's best in sub one hundred dollar IEMs. The best feature to me is comfort because I normally do not care for in ear style phones. I can wear these for hours without even noticing them, and they ship with an array of tips that fit just about any ear size. However, sound ranks right up there with comfort because I listen to a lot of music from a critical perspective as well as enjoyment. Nothing interferes with the sound quality, including ambient noise from the cables or other physical factors, and they do a great job of isolation. Every album to which I listen comes across with no gaps in any of the frequency bands. You can hear any note (and sometimes flaws) that musicians and recording engineers made, which is extremely important to me. What truly sets these IEMs apart from other phones in its class are is the attention to detail. The cord is tangle free and practically indestructible. I have yet to worry about breaking or wearing out the inner conductor like I do with some other brands I own (including some pretty expensive phones). The plug is gold plated for and at a ninety degree angle - nice touches - and the phones ship with a protective hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) that is not only convenient, but functional. If I had to recommend a sub one hundred dollar set of IEMs to a friend or fellow musician these would be it. The performance, comfort and price make them a bargain in my opinion.

title: Works, but for geeks only
text: I had the same issues with the review sample that I received that rpv's May 10, 2014 described. The camera and accessories are first rate; the documentation is not. What I like is this is a full solution with various mounts, a waterproof case and all of the cables you need. All you have to do is add an SD card, and you can insert one up to 32GB. To be honest, all you need is a 4GB card since the camera itself will operate for an hour fully charged. For the extreme sports type videos this was designed to capture, an hour is a long time, so the operating time is certainly not a limitation. Video quality is respectable and after you spend some time experimenting to fill in the gaps in the documentation you will fall in love with the camera. I attempted to use mine mounted to a microphone stand to capture practice sessions with me and a pianist. It can be done, but the results were less than spectacular. However, strapping this to a handlebar or helmet and dirt biking, skydiving or similar activities would result in some priceless shots. For the right audience this is a great camera. All you need is a 4GB SD card, some technical savvy, and the patience to experiment. If the documentation were better I would give this a solid five stars for what it is and does.

title: New life for my ancient router
text: Since there are detailed specs in the product description I will not repeat them here. Instead I'll use my personal experience with this kit to explain why I rated it five stars. I used the review sample I received to extend the range of my ancient [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] (which is still working as well as when I purchased it ten years ago!) I removed one antenna from the Linksys, used a [[ASIN:B005IKGTXY Bluecell SMA female to TNC male Coaxial Adapter/Converter]] to adapt the included cable to the antenna connector, plugged it into the power supply and checked my home dead spot. My dead spot is the master bedroom and my phone is always complaining about 'unstable WiFi connections' when I am in the room. I used an app called [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]] to perform the before and after tests. Before I installed this booster kit I was getting a strong reading of -45 dBm near the router and an absymal -80 dBm in the dead room. After installing this kit the signal boosted to -55 dBm in the bedroom, so this booster kit works as advertised. It's practically worth its weight in gold if you do have dead areas in your WiFi coverage. Based on my experience and how easy and fast this is to install I rate this as a five star product.

title: Outstanding control & great feel
text: When my review sample arrived I had no problem connecting it to an old ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It also connected without fuss to an Android TV box and functioned immediately. On the ThinkPad the settings out of the box took some getting accustomed to because the mouse was super sensitive to my every move. After downloading the driver and manual - neither of which are included in the box - I was able to fine tune this mouse to my personal movements. In fact, I am not sure I can go back to a plain vanilla mouse again! I am not going to repeat the very detailed specifications on this page, including actual dimensions, nor am I going to regurgitate the roduct description. I have included user supplied images of the manual and screen shot of the driver menu that will show the incredible array of settings and features. Here are a few of the reasons why I personally love this mouse and awarded it five stars. First, every possible setting and button a gamer or power user could wish for are included. You can assign just about any function to any button, and set sensitivity levels at the inch-pebble level. Even the lights and display are configurable. Second, this is a quality product from the braided, five foot cable that will probably outlast my sixty-five year old body, to the buttons, which feel solid and provide excellent tactile feedback. Finally, while I had to downgrade mine to conform to my less than steady hands, I did use the maximum sensitivity on a few Visio drawings I quickly created. If only I had this mouse when I was a consultant who cranked out system and network diagrams like a demon possessed. As it is, the shape feels natural and ergonomic under my hand. And for good reason: the design provides for two controlling points (index and/or middle finger and thumb), and a pressure point where your palm rests and a support point at the heel of your hand. I could babble on and on, but the images I uploaded show most of the settings and an overview of the mouse. As for the lack of documentation and drivers in the box. that is a smart move because you can download the freshest ones as soon as you log onto their site (URL is printed on the front of the box).

title: Buy it for the sound
text: This speaker has some convenient features like hands-free calling and receiving calls, but it's the sound quality that makes it stand out. Before I list the many things I love (and why I awarded this five stars) I want to toss out the one thing that is keeping this speaker from being totally perfect: the older generation bluetooth pairing and connecting process. The newer generation of bluetooth speakers automatically beacon their presence when you turn them on. This one requires you to hold down a multifunction button for six seconds before you initiate a scan on your phone or tablet. It's not a big issue or deal breaker, but this would be the perfect speaker otherwise. It is all about the sound and the review sample I received from the manufacturer passed my usual tests with flying colors. Among the tests are playing a handful of favorite jazz albums. The main one I always use us Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B003GIK2LU Kind Of Blue]] because it exercises a speaker's ability to reproduce the full spectrum of frequencies in the low, mid and high ranges. A truly great speaker will also reproduce the nuances from the natural reverb effect of the 30th Street Studio in NYC where it was recorded. This speaker did! As I listened through this speaker I wondered how it would sound with something a little more in your face than circa 1950s acoustic jazz. I grabbed some old rock albums, dusted them off and gave them a spin. Since I am sixty-five my idea of rock is probably ancient music to many folks. However, back in the day the following albums did stretch the woofers in stereo systems: [[ASIN:B001NCT8X4 Fresh Cream]] (Jack Bruce's bass and Ginger Baker's double bass drum kit came through as though I were in a small club), and [[ASIN:B0011Z5IUK Led Zeppelin II]] (same for John Paul Jones' bass and John Bonham's drums, especially on The Lemon Song). Part of the reason the sound is so full and rich is the 360 degree speaker coverage. Another factor is the design raises the main speaker cabinet about a quarter of an inch off the base of the unit. This allows the low end frequencies to reflect a bit and sound deeper. Do be aware, though, that this is not an exceptionally loud speaker. It's perfect for most listening up to five meters away. That's about fifteen feet, so you can crank it pretty loud relative to its size, but as you increase the volume beyond three quarters the fidelity drops if you are too close. At the three quarter mark and a distance of five meters you can hear every note and nuance in the older jazz recordings with which I tested this speaker, and pretty good fidelity with the older rock albums. If you listen to music with a critical ear this speaker is one that you should consider if you are shipping for a bluetooth model. Obviously there are wired speakers that are better, but in the bluetooth domain this is one of the best that I have tried from a sound perspective.

title: Works with a Galaxy Note 3 battery
text: When I first received a review sample I was dismayed because the specs claimed that it would only fit batteries that are between 42 and 71 millimeters in length. In inches that works out to be 1.65 to 2.79 inches. In actual fact, that dimension should have read width instead of length because my long Samsung Galaxy Note 3 battery (which is in excess of three inches long) not only fit, but charged perfectly. I also tested this on an HTC Driod Incredible and it worked perfectly on that phone's battery as well. There is a spring-loaded arm that opens to accept batteries with widths within the range I cited above, and they hold the battery firmly in place during the charging cycle. What I love is the ability to charge a spare battery while simultaneously charging a phone with a battery installed. That feature makes this perfect as a travel charger (the folding prongs add to the function for that use. It is also ideal as an office charger for folks who frequently spend most of their work day in the field. Do heed the two prominent notices in the specs (1) it is ONLY for phone batteries, and (2) it will only work with batteries that have contact points on the end (not the front of back). Indeed, the contacts on your battery (the metal strips that mate with your phone) cannot be closer than 3/8 inch from the edge of the battery, nor more than 5/8 inch away. If they fall outside of that range then this charger will not work for you. For batteries that do fit this charger will automatically detect the type and capacity and charge it properly. So there is some intelligence built into the circuitry. These are great for those of us who have spare batteries for our phones and want to keep them charged and ready to go. It worked perfectly on the phones with which I tested it. Measure and examine your battery before ordering to save disappointment.

title: Great idea well executed
text: For bicycle enthusiasts this is an excellent speaker/radio combination that has decent sound and a lot of convenient touches. I received mine as a review sample from the manufacturer. I'll cover the sound quality first. In a word, it's adequate. Not overly spectacular, but sufficiently loud to be heard over road noise while trekking through streets and paths. I do not view the quality as a problem because in most biking environments the sound level is more important than fidelity. Plus, the safety factor of having a hands-free solution is the major reason for getting one of these. What impressed me is when I turned this on all I had to do is scan for bluetooth devices from my phone and it popped right up. I did not have to press a multifunction button and chant, hoping the device would show up like other bluetooth speakers - it was immediately there. Another thing I love is the buttons are on the top of the case and when the speaker is turned on they light up blue. I have stationary speakers which have buttons that blend into the case so well I cannot readily find them, so this feature removes one major distraction when you are on the road. In the dark the lights are soft enough to not affect your night vision. The only improvement that I can think of is to use red lights instead of blue because those would actually promote night vision. Perhaps the designers will do that in the next generation. Some of the other nice touches are the ample inside space for a phone and other incidentals, plus a ring clip on the outside for your keys. I also love the three point attachment to your handle bar and steering post. It is easy to attach and remove. In fact, that takes mere seconds. Having a removable battery is yet another design factor that makes this a value. Most bluetooth speakers on the market have a fixed, internal battery that will eventually wear out. When the battery in this one inevitably dies you can quickly replace it with a new [[ASIN:B0006HP7NC BL-5C Extended Li-Ion Battery]] and you are good to go another 500 or so charging cycles. Finally, the semi-hard case, heavy duty zipper and construction are all first rate and clearly designed by someone who understands the rigors of biking when it comes to gear. This entire unit is built to withstand the outdoors in most weather conditions.

title: When you need one - you NEED one!
text: This is a great way to use HDMI devices on TVs that have no spare HDMI ports or are not equipped with one. I tested the review sample that I received on a 2008 Sanyo TV that came equipped with two HDMI ports that I quickly occupied with a Roku and a Chromecast, and with a 2011 model Samsung. Both displayed the transformed signal from this box beautifully. It has come excellent features like the array of color encoding schemes and outputting either the most common PAL and NTSC ones with the flip of a switch. I also love that this is powered via USB, which one of my TVs as, so it's one less wall wart. Do be aware that this only converts in one direction: HDMI in (from Blu-Ray players, etc) to composite out via RCA jacks on a TV or monitor. I tested this going the other direction - RCA to HDMI - and it did not work. Of course it was not advertised as such, but I felt compelled to try anyway. I would love it if I could flip a switch and change directions of the signal transformation because I could then connect my old VHS player to an HDMI port on my TV. Regardless of my personal wishes, this does exactly what it claims with no problems or issues, and that merits five stars according to how I rate.

title: Excellent entry level IEM
text: The review sample that I received proved to be a nice, low-to-mid range In Ear Monitor (IEM). It can compete with much more expensive IEMs from both Brainwavz and competing brands. To keep my evaluation in this brand I am going to compare the review sample of this model to two other Brainwavz IEMs: [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]] and the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]]. To provide some context please bear in mind that I listen primarily to acoustic jazz, so my listening needs may be vastly different from yours. The first thing I do with I test phones or speakers is to play Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] to get a feel for how well the various frequencies are reproduced. That album has instruments in the low, mid and high bands, and these phones seemed to have more bass than the R1 or the S1. The mids and highs on those models, though, had more clarity. I tried a few other albums that had heavier bass and these definitely did a better job of reproducing those frequencies. When I switched to some tracks with female vocalists the R1 and S1 were better phones, and both of the other phones were clearer with higher register instruments. From a comfort perspective these phones were a little lighter than the other two IEMs against which I compared them, although I would consider it a tie among them for overall comfort. These phones and the R1 had a value-added bonus in that a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] is included. These are obviously designed for lower end audio gear like MP3 players, phones and tablets. For higher end audio in the audiophile range I would probably use the S1 model because to my ears that one sounds better. However, you cannot go wrong with this one for everyday use when you want to listen to your music without disturbing others.

title: These won me over
text: Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack. I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]]. Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum.
