Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these. Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music. If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.

title: Perfect for casual listening
text: I own a number of Brainwavz models, all of which compare favorably to more expensive in ear monitors (IEMs). I am going to compare the review sample of this model to two other Brainwavz IEMs: [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]] and the [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]]. What I will try to avoid is repeating the other reviews - many of which are excellent - and the product specs on this page. Here are my impressions of these phones. Bear in mind that I listen primarily to acoustic jazz, so my listening needs may be vastly different from yours. The first thing I do with I test phones or speakers is to play Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] to get a feel for how well the various frequencies are reproduced. That album has instruments in the low, mid and high bands, and these phones seemed to have more bass than the R1 or the S1. The mids and highs on those models, though, had more clarity. I tried a few other albums that had heavier bass and these definitely did a better job of reproducing those frequencies. When I switched to some tracks with female vocalists the R1 and S1 were better phones, and both of the other phones were clearer with higher register instruments. From a comfort perspective these phones were a little lighter than the other two IEMs against which I compared them, although I would consider it a tie among them for overall comfort. These phones and the R1 had a value-added bonus in that a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] is included. My conclusion is these are nice low-to-mid range IEMs that can compete with much more expensive IEMs from both Brainwavz and competing brands. I am impressed with the quality, completeness of the solution and the way these sound on lower end audio gear like MP3 players, phones and tablets. For higher end audio I would probaby use the S1 model because to my ears that one sounds better. However, you cannot go wrong with this one for everyday use when you want to listen to your music without disturbing others.

title: Convenient if you use your phones a lot
text: Shortly after I received this as a review sample it quickly became a permanent part of my home studio. Right now my [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]] are mounted for immediate use, and I tested this with some smaller phones I also use like the [[ASIN:B0002F74E8 Sony MDR7502 Professional Stereo Headphone]] and they fit perfectly as well. This is a tall, thin stand that measures ten inches tall with a relatively short five inch base. Despite the proportions this sits stably and is not apt to tip if you accidentally bump into it. I love the contoured top over which the phones rest. That holds the phones in a natural shape. For expensive phones that is not especially a problem because the over the head mechanisms on those devices are usually very well made. The material (I am guessing plexi-glass) is 8mm thick (about a third of an inch), and is flexible. Complaints about the large logo are valid if you want a cleaner look, but since I am currently using Brainwavz headphones - and this is in my music studio - the aesthetics are a non-issue for me. I care more about function and convenient storage and this stand provides both of those. For me the convenience of having my phones readily available is important because I use them often. This stand is an inexpensive way of accomplishing that.

title: Not just for Brainwavz products
text: This case came bundled with my [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]] and I was struck by how nicely made and perfect it is. I will not parrot the other excellent reviews on this page with regard to physical characteristics, but will confirm that they are spot on. Although these are bundled with a Brainwavz product do not let that deter you if you have invested in another brand because these will work with most of them. I tested the fit with the following phones and they are a perfect match: [[ASIN:B001EZYMF4 Sennheiser CX 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass Earbuds]] [[ASIN:B004PO10E2 Shure SE215-CL Sound Isolating Earphones]] [[ASIN:B000XPG2QI Etymotic Research HF5 Portable In-Ear Earphones]] Of course I also tested them with the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]] which I expected to fit and they did. Although many of the phones with which I tested these come with their own case, none of them are are as sturdy or as protective as this one. For low-end phones this will probably outlast the phones themselves, and will be ready their their replacement. For the higher end phones this is an investment - and an inexpensive one at they - for protecting the instrument from damage.

title: A real contender
text: I had the opportunity to directly compare my review sample to the [[ASIN:B001EZYMF4 Sennheiser CX 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass Earbuds]], which is a highly regarded IEM (in ear monitor) in the same price range. This one actually sounded better to my ears although both were nearly identical in specifications. This is my third Brainwavz phone model, and I have quickly come to regard this brand as a real contender in the market. I will not lie - I much prefer the [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]] model because I love over-the-hear style phones. However, this set of phones, at about a third of the cost, is also close in sound quality as the HM9. In fact, the bass in this one is much better than the HM9 (or the Sennheiser CX 300 II to which I am directly comparing these.) For me comfort is everything because I listen to music much of my time. These are perfect for both pleasure listening where I sit back and enjoy the music for its own sake. These are also good enough for me to hear every nuance when I am transcribing or studying a track to learn. In that respect these phones are good enough for professional musicians, but I will admit that they would not be my first choice for plugging into a high-end sound system. Since I spend more time listening to MP3 tracks than off vinyl these do the job since MP3 files lose some fidelity by their very nature. I will say, though, that these phones passed my basic test suite, which includes Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]]. That is my reference model for sound because it contains high, mid and low frequency instruments that exercise any sound system. I listened to that album both from CD and from an MP3 file. Reproduction was superb. Not only do these phones have respectable sound and comfort, the package is complete. They come with a zippered hard shell case, which protects the phones. However, they come with more extras that add to the value and provide versatility: a 1/4 adapter for plugging directly into standard headphone jacks, and an airplane adapter. If you are in the market for mid-range IEMs give these serious consideration. In my opinion they are easily the equal of better known brands like the Sennheiser I mentioned and can be a better value if you need the extras that this set includes.

title: As good as the OEM cable that shipped with my Note 3
text: I wanted a spare charging cable for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and took a chance on this one. By that I mean that that other USB 3.0 cables that I have tried with the phone would charge it, but would not support full speed data transfers and synching. This one performed without issues and identically to my OEM Samsung cable that came with my phone. The blue outer jacket is much thicker than the Samsung cable. Although it is slightly stiffer it's also pliable and easy to bend and coil. Part of the reason for the extra thickness is probably from the the foil and braid shielding. In fact, the shielding is one factor in this cable's ability to transmit data at such high speeds without error. Another factor is the gold plated connectors. The bottom line is this cable seems to be the equal of the more expensive Samsung OEM cable. In my experience anyway. I have owned it for three months and it has been problem free in every respect.

title: Love the size and performance
text: My desk gets crowded with the bulky 10-port USB hub I had been using so when this review sample arrived I was immediately pleased with the size. It is the perfect complement to my ThinkPad T61 which comes with three USB ports to begin with. I will not repeat the exceptionally helpful review that Daisy S posted on February 11, 2014 - she thoroughly tested the specs and gave some pointers for also using this via the OTG interface on tablets. This also works on any OTG-capable phone using her approach because I tested it on my Galaxy Note 3. A big plus is this not only works with USB 3.0 interfaces, but is backward compatible to earlier versions of the USB spec, including 1.0. That means that I can use this on my legacy devices around the house, as well as my newer 'toys'. The final thing that I like about this hub is the construction. The manufacturer did not cut corners on cable gauge and the small details like strain relief, precision made connectors and other areas that cheaper brands do. The quality is there and this does work as advertised.

title: Excellent (and affordable) basic protection
text: What I love about this case is the value. Most of the ones I checked out in the usual brick and mortar stores were priced at two to three times the cost of this one, and none of those seemed to be any more substantial than this one when it came to aesthetics, function and protection. This case has all three. Although it's synthetic leather it looks like the real thing. So much so in fact that it goes perfectly with the [[ASIN:B00ESAGVLK Bear Motion for Galaxy Note 3 100% Genuine Lambskin Folio Case]] that I purchased for my Galaxy Note 3 phone. Functionally it is a snug fit that provides me access to all buttons, ports and features of my Tab 3 except the SD card slot, which is covered. I view this as a plus, though, because I do not have to worry about the slot cover popping open and losing the SD card. I love how thin this case is - it's like a book. I also love the way a magnet holds the cover closed when the tablet is not in use. The protection is basic and perfect for in home or office use. It is not for use in harsher environments, so factor that into your purchase decision. For what I do, it's perfect. Bottom line: for the price this cover is hard to beat. There are no major flaws or problems that I can find after extensively using this with my Tab 3. If you are looking for basic protection with no frills this is worth checking out.

title: Perfect for primary and temp storage
text: I have tested this card in both a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and a [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch]] and it was immediately recognized by both devices. As I write this review the card has been running in my Tab 3 and constantly used for over a week. Other reviews have dissected the specs of this card, so I'll share how I use it and why I prefer these over the 64GB cards (which I also own and use). The price point on these 32GB cards have dramatically fallen and as of the date of this review they are priced as commodities. I use a few pairs of these to rotate backups on my laptop, so I always have a daily snapshot of my documents. For that purpose alone these cards are well worth it. For my tablet I have divided my extensive music library into genres and have them backed up to these cards. A 32GB card will hold about 150 CDs, so the space savings along over the physical media is significant. In fact one of these cards cost about the same as a rack for 150 CDs. These are also excellent for saving practice sessions that I sometimes record using my phone or tablet. I pop my primary SD card out of the device and swap one of these in to video record. Since this card will hold about six hours of video it's perfect for that use. Overall, these are reliable cards that have worked in a number of devices I own. I can assure anyone wanting to use them in a newer Samsung Note 2 or 3 phone or Tab 3 tablet that this card will work, and it is also excellent for HD video recording. At the price point it's an absolute bargain.

title: Excellent sound for some types of music and very comfortable
text: I tested these on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and my Tab 3 tablet and was impressed with the sound. Note: I always test using a Miles Davis album titled Kind of Blue because the instrumentation covers the high, mid and low frequency bands. However, the acoustic bass in jazz is different than electric bass in modern music so factor that into my comments when making a purchase decision. I did try a few tracks on an album with with electric bass that were not as deep sounding. Bottom line: for jazz these are superb, and especially for acoustic jazz that was recorded in the 1950s, but I am not sure about other genres of music. What I love is the comfort of the ear buds. Normally I avoid them, but I received these as a review sample so decided to wear them and listen for a few hours straight. I found that the small ear tips that shipped with these fir me the best, although the medium ones were comfortable too. The large pair were definitely 'large', so there is a tip size for everyone. I did not care for the foam tips, preferring the silicon ones, but that is my personal preference and not an opinion of which is better. I was able to wear these for hours without the chaffing or discomfort that other bud-style phones cause me. One note: once in-ear the tips eliminated a lot of ambient noise, which allowed me to listen critically to the music itself. That is a big plus for in home (or in studio) use, but I would not recommend wearing these while driving because it cuts down on outside noise to the point that you may be unaware of traffic situations. Another thing I love is the relatively long cable, which is slightly over four feet long. In my home studio it allows me to practice to backing tracks on my tablet what is usually on a nearby music stand. I also appreciate the fact that the connectors are gold plated, which ensures a good, clean signal to the phones. Bottom line: these are relatively inexpensive phones with performance that can compete with phones costing two to three times as much. The sound is superior for the types of music I enjoy, but the bass may be too light for some modern, bass and drum heavy music.

title: Wow! But be careful if there are children around
text: UPDATE August 18, 2014. I just received a newer model without the USB ports (the [[ASIN:B00KBO619E Arctic Breeze USA]]. Aside from the patriotic USA motif, this model has some improvements. First, the fan blades have a more efficient pitch and size, so it throws a nice breeze. I have mine running next to the earlier model and the difference between the two are significant. A second feature is this newer model is safer. I can put my finger into the spinning blade and it will stop without as much as a nick. The earlier model that I reviewed below was a safety hazard around small children. This one has corrected that issue. In all other respects the two models are very close in specs. [END OF UPDATE] About six months ago I tested and reviewed the smaller version of this fan: [[ASIN:B003XN24GY ARCTIC Breeze Mobile]]. When I was provided with this one as a review sample I was able to compare the two side-by-side. This one is hands down a more sophisticated and functional cooling solution. I love this one because it is serious competition to my [[ASIN:B0000DJ27I Lasko #2500 12" Oscillating Table Fan]], and this one takes far less power to operate and the breeze can be focused. On warm days this is a godsend, but it also works to keep my hot running laptop cool. It's also so quiet that I cannot hear it three feet away. A key difference between this model and the earlier one is this has a variable speed knob that allows me to go from a light 800 RPM to a very brisk 1800 RPM. One caveat is at the higher speeds this fan cannot be stopped with your fingers like the earlier model and there is no fan guard. This is a safety hazard if small children are around and is not a solution I recommend if that's the case where this will be used. Another thing I love is the earlier model was a gooseneck that plugged directly into a USB port. This one has a cable that is just a little short of six feet and can be placed a lot more conveniently. The base is very heavy, so there is little chance of knocking it over, and the base also contains four USB ports. Note that these are 2.0 only. You can plug this directly into your PC or laptop, but I also found that the Samsung wall charger that came with my Galaxy Note 3 will power this fan as well. Bottom line is this is a great cooling solution for child-free work areas, and it will definitely cause rapid cooling at the full 1800 RPM setting.

title: Works perfectly on some devices, not so well with others
text: Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy. Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear. I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars. Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store. Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.

title: Great price and excellent performance
text: Because of the low price I almost passed on this card because it was suspiciously low. I am glad I didn't because this not only works perfectly in my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] tablet, but I also tested it in my Galaxy Note 3 phone with the same results. I have not exhaustively tested the read and write specs and probably will not. I have put this card through its paces by first doing an over the air transfer from my music library on my phone to this card on my tablet. I transferred over 30GB of files that literally took hours. Cards that I have used in the past would have hiccuped with transmission errors or overheating. For this one I experienced no lags, I/O errors or overheating. That is the true test for me. During my tests this card easily kept up with the more expensive [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10]] model in my Note 3 phone. That is all the evidence that I personally need that this is a quality SD card. At the time of this review his card is priced forty percent less than the Samsung card I have in my phone and the performance is roughly the same for my purposes. That, to me, is the definition of value and the reason why I rated this at five stars.

title: Works perfectly for my uses
text: This is not the best adapter in the world, but I knew that going in. I use mine to transform a 3.5mm jack in a [[ASIN:B004VQDAQK Powerwerks PW50 Portable PA System]] into a third channel and this adapter works perfectly for that. Note that I am not expecting stereo signals and have not tested this adapter to ensure that it supports that function. Reading over other reviews complaining about flimsy construction and myriad other problems leads me to conclude that the adapter I received is a new and improved version. It's not particularly flimsy and both sides mate with their respective plugs with no tolerance issues. Since I am using this to reclaim a channel on a relatively inexpensive powered mixer I cannot comment on signal quality. It's not especially noisy, but on the other hand if I were using this to enjoy music through headphones I would have probably purchased a higher quality adapter. Bottom line: I am pleased with this adapter, but note that you do get what you pay for. If you want a quick fix like for what I am using mine for it's a bargain. If you want an adapter for high end stereo gear you may want to consider a higher end adapter like the [[ASIN:B0002E51CQ Planet Waves 1/8 Inch Female Stereo to 1/4 Inch Male Stereo Adapter]].

title: Surprisingly great feel
text: I received a review sample and tested this on an ancient Acer One netbook running Windows XP. The netbook immediately recognized the wireless dongle that is included with this keyboard and I had the keyboard operational in minutes after inserting the included rechargeable batteries and charging them up. Frankly, I thought I would hate the keys because they resembled the 'chicklet' style of a circa 1977 Commodore Pet's keys. These, though, have beautiful tactile feedback and are exceptionally responsive. You can touch type at at least 120 words per minute (my max) with no problems. Although this key board comes with a retractable USB cable, that is for charging the two batteries that power the unit. This is strictly a wireless device, so you will need a spare USB port for the required dongle, and access to one or a wall charger that accepts USB cables to recharge the batteries when they run down. You can go two months between charges as long as you remember to switch the keyboard off between uses. There is an on/off switch on the underside of the board. One final feature I love is this keyboard has some heft to it. It is not going to slide across your desk like some cheap, flimsy ones that I have tried in the past. The bottom line is of all of the portable keyboards that I have tested (well over two dozen), this one is the best of the bunch for me. The size and feel earn it five solid stars.

title: Precise, but has a learning curve
text: I received a review sample and after I got this up and running there was a slight learning curve before it felt natural. After I did become accustomed to it, going back to a regular mouse was a slight letdown. While the instructions are a bit terse I am still giving this four stars because it's easy to set up. The subtracted star is for lack of clear explanations in the quick start guide for how to precharge the unit or even for explaining that the retractable USB cable that ships with it is only for charging and will not connect the mouse interface to the host system. This mouse operates wirelessly via an included dongle. My old ThinkPad running Windows XP immediately recognized the dongle when I plugged it in, and the mouse as soon as I inserted the included battery and charged it up. Once I became comfortable with the mouse I found that it was a lot more precise for graphics applications and games than a regular mouse. Note that the base is fixed to the pen-style handle. You move it as though it's a pen affixed to a sled. After you become accustomed to the buttons and the wheel placement you will be using this like a pro. There is a LED on the top of the unit that shows the charging state. Once that light turns green you can disconnect the USB charging cable. I initially did not like this feature, but have grown to love it because the battery is rechargeable. Other wireless mice I have used in the past seemed to have a voracious appetite for batteries, so plus one for the rechargeable feature. Bottom line: this is an excellent mouse that is less stressful than using a normal one. Set-up is a bit confusing, but if you have issues leave questions in a comment to this review and I will answer them to the best of my ability. If the company redesigns the documentation to make it clear to complete novices this would be a five star product.

title: Superior construction and extra long cable
text: I received a review sample of this cord and charger combination and have been testing it thoroughly. The most striking feature is the three meter cable, which is the longest I have seen for any iPhone (or Android phone for that matter.) My first inclination was to test the cable for failures because the length seemed excessive. It performed every data transfer and synching operation flawlessly. It also fast-charges like an Apple OEM cable. I was a bit surprised that this and the charger were not MFi certified (Made for iPhone/iPod/iPad). Other cables and chargers that I have received from the manufacturer were, but this is indistinguishable from the MFi and Apple OEM cables that I have tested - both visually and from a performance perspective. The contacts on both the USB and Lightning connector ends are precision made and mate perfectly to the ports to which they were designed to connect. The outer jacket is thick, but not too stiff to make handling it a problem. There are strain reliefs on both ends to ensure a long service life. This set includes a bonus wall charger with folding prongs. This has the same well made construction, and also puts out a steady 2.1A for fast charging. This charger is perfect for iPads too because of the output rating. If I had one wish it would have a second 1.0A port for those of us who want to simultaneously charge a phone and tablet - perhaps the next generation of this product will have that feature. Bottom line: when size (in the form of cable length) matters this is one of the very few on the market that is a full three meters long. Add in the fact that this one is made to perform like an Apple OEM cable and the value should be apparent.

title: Great product that is being marketed to the wrong demographic
text: When I accepted a review sample of this holder I had visions of using it to entice my constant companion to sit in the back and play with her iPad. Indeed, this hooked right onto the two posts of the front seat headrest that would allow a backseat passenger to watch movies and do whatever else they use the iPad for. My companion did not take the bait, so I was left with a review sample that, frankly, I could not give away. Necessity is the mother of invention and the best use for this mount was in my music room. This hooks into my [[ASIN:B000CDUDQG Belmonte Orchestra Stand Deluxe Black]] to mount an iPad and still have room left for sheet music and a [[ASIN:0961470143 The New Real Book - Volume 1]]. I have uploaded customer-supplied photos to show how this securely attaches to the stand and holds an iPad in place (it will work with any tablet up to 10 inches.) I love how this holder allows you to place your tablet at practically any viewing angle, and also how it positively and absolutely holds the tablet in place. For the record, these claims apply equally to the dual headrest posts in my 2014 Outlander and to the music stand cited above. Personally, the manufacturer is missing a major market because tablets are now common on stages and in studios and I suspect that there is a much larger market for this holder than significant others who refuse to be relegated to the back seat. I am so pleased with this holder that I have already recommended it to fellow musicians.

title: Excellent solution for 1/8th inch (3.5mm) signal splitting
text: First, this is not a flimsy cable - the construction clearly indicates that this is built to last. I received a review sample and initially put off testing this splitter out. When I finally got around to it I was actually impressed with the quality of construction. Most cables and splitters fail quickly because they are subjected to bending and handling, which eventually fatigues and/or cracks the inside conductor. This one has a heavy-duty strain relief on the male end and a thick housing for the female jacks that is practically unbreakable. One additional advantage to the female end is the housing will also provide a modicum of radio frequency shielding. Another factor is the housing is .75 inches across with 3/8ths of an inch separation (center to center) of the female jacks. I thought this was a clever piece of engineering and is indicative of the overall attention to quality. The cable itself is 2 9/16 inches with an overall length of 4.5 inches. All jacks perfectly mate. I tried a few 3.5mm cables with the female ends and all fit snugly, and the male end was a perfect fit not only into my phone, but a PA system that I own that has a 3.5mm input for playing backing tracks. The signals in a and out (I tested this splitter both ways) was crystal clear. I love purchasing items that are made to last and this splitter easily qualifies as one of those. If you need one this is the one to get.

title: The best shower-style speaker I have tested
text: I received a review sample and put this through its paces right after I charged it. The first thing I noticed is the sound quality and the volume. My test music is [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] because it has multiple instruments in the low, mid and high ranges. This speaker passed that test by allowing me to hear each instrument. I will say that the low end of the frequency range is a little thin. Not terrible, but I want to point that out. For overall volume, this beats two other shower-type speakers I have tested in the past. The previous ones could not be heard clearly with water spraying and cascading in the background. This one can. It easily cut through the ambient shower noise and I was able to enjoy music in the shower. The instructions consist of a single-sided sheet of paper that is clear and concise. Pairing this with my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 took seconds. Switching to FM radio is as simple as depressing and holding the On/Off button after you have turned the device on. I get poor reception no matter which radio I use in my area, but I did manage to find a clear station, so if you listen to FM radio that feature is as rock solid as the bluetooth speaker feature. This is definitely waterproof. The power cable is a hybrid with a standard USB connector on one end and a tip type DC connector on the other. I tested it with a few wall chargers in the house and all work. The included cable is relatively sturdy, which is a plus given its non-standard configuration. Of course that configuration is one of the keys to ensuring that this speaker is waterproof. Overall this is the best shower-style speaker that I have tested to date. The sound quality is a cut above most on the market, and the unit itself is perfect for listening anywhere. For example, the hanger hook would make this ideal for hanging off a rear view mirror in a car for hand's free calling, which this speaker also supports.

title: Exceeded my expectaqtions in more ways than one
text: I purchased this on a whim because I needed to add a ten dollar plus item to qualify for super saver shipping on an order. I was always curious about these dongles, and the product started earning five stars before it even arrived. Shortly after placing my order the manufacturer sent me an email with a link to the latest drivers and software. That alone is an unusually high level of service. When this adapter arrived today, I had it up and running - and connected to a bluetooth speaker - in less than ten minutes. Step one was to install the drivers on the accompanying CD ROM (I could have downloaded them had I been diskless), then the software itself. The wizard stepped me though discovering the devices to which I wanted to connect and I was done. A great feature is when you connect to a speaker it appears as a headset and you have the option of hands-free operation or not. As an experiment I decided to check if my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 would connect. It did. Unlike when the adapter streams music to a speaker, I could move files from my phone to my laptop via bluetooth. For the record I installed this on an ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP, SP3. No problems and no issues. The laptop immediately recognized it as a new piece of hardware as soon as I plugged it in. One final feature I love is I have this plugged into a port that is closely adjacent to a second USB port and there was sufficient clearance with both ports occupied.

title: Versatile for users with multiple USB devices
text: I received this as a review sample and tested the claimed specifications on a few platforms. The following are my observations that, with Debbie Lee Wesselmann's excellent review, should give you a complete picture of this hub. First, word about using this hub for charging devices. The specs on this product page at the time of this review claim that this hub will NOT charge devices. Actually, it charged my two phones and another device while I was doing other tasks. Perhaps the specs mean it is not intended to be a standalone charger. The only thing that I do NOT like is the wall wart type power supply that is approximately 3x2x2 inches. It can (and does) block adjacent plugs in my surge protector. However, I can live that that considering the functionality I get from this hub. My favorite feature and the reason I awarded this hub five stars is the integrated electrical safeguards that protect against over voltage, over current, leakage and short circuits. This may not be a big deal for cheap peripherals like mice, but for an expensive hard drive or my Galaxy Note 3 it's a welcome feature. If you have a computer and peripherals that are USB 3.0 compliant this hub will boost your transfer speeds significantly. For example, my new Samsung Note 3 will transfer at the 5gbps speed, but frankly I do most of my data transfers over WiFi. However, if you wanted to attach an external 3.0 hard drive to your laptop this hum will allow it to operate to it's full potential - which is lightning fast. Set-up is easy. You literally connect the included power supply, plug it into your system's USB port and switch it on. All of platforms with which I tested it immediately recognized the hub and the things I plugged into it (which included a flash drive, mouse, two snart phones (Galaxy Note II and Note 3), and a speaker that is powered by USB. This hub works with Windows 98 (I have an old Sony running it and this hub plugged in and worked with it), and above. I know it works with Win XP, Vista and 7 because I also tested the hub on those platforms. I do not have access to a Windows 8 system so am taking the manufacturer's word that it works on that too. If your experience is different please leave a comment. One final feature that makes this a five star hub in my opinion is the fact that this will simultaneously support maximum data transfer of up to four high speed devices (three of which can be USB 3.0) plugged into it. Of course the host system needs to be USB 3.0 too, but the hub will sling data as fast as the host can accept it. Not all hubs will operate in this mode, and I suspect that the external power supply has something to do with that level of performance.

title: Love mine - upgraded from a cracked screen Note II
text: Before giving my opinion and experiences with this phone I want to start with some advice if you are upgrading from another Android phone. Search Samsung's site for an app called Samsung Smart Switch. It's free and easy. If you find issues with that app for any reason you can move all of your text messages from your old phone to this one by loading a free app called [[ASIN:B0075A5S0K SMS Backup & Restore]] and following the directions I outlined in my November 30, 2013 review of that product. Another free app you may want to consider is [[ASIN:B006FJMDTG Software Data Cable]], which allows you to back up your old Android phone to a laptop or PC, then move it to your new phone from that backup. You will need to load that app on your old phone and the Note 3, but it's simple and very handy. While the size difference between this and the Note 2 is only a matter of inches, the screen on this one is brighter, has more vivid colors and can be easily viewed in direct sunlight. The 32GB of internal storage is a big plus because the 16GB on my Note 2 was beginning to get full. When I added in my 64GB external SD card I swapped from the Note 2, total storage comes to 16GB more storage than my 80GB laptop. It's easy to forecast that the next version of this phone could finally wean me off computers. As it is I am spending a lot more time on my phone doing stuff I use to do on my computer. This is also a much faster phone. I do not use it to anywhere near its capacity, but it zips along from one screen or app to the next with no lag. I was more than pleased with my older Note 2, but this one is even better. I take a lot of pictures and video, so I appreciate the greatly improved camera resolution and the easier and more intuitive interface. But what I truly love is there are no major differences in the user interface even though this one runs under Android 4.3 versus 4.1.2 on my Note 2. In that respect there was zero learning curve. After tweaking a few settings that did not come over when I restored my old ones, I was up and running as before in practically no time. This ships with a cable that supports USB 3.0 and has what looks like a connector that is incompatible with existing micro USB chargers, that is not the case. You can still use existing chargers, battery packs and the such because their micro USB connectors will plug into one side of the charging port. If you have a computer capable of USB 3.0 your transfer rates will be lightning fast. The battery is about the same as the Note 2 for use time between charges. Since the Note 3's 4.3 Android operating system does include Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) support you may notice a slightly improved use time if you use bluetooth a lot. As it stands there is a very slight difference between the Note 2's 3100mAh battery capacity and the 3200mAh one in this phone. I am still exploring the nuances of my new phone, so as I discover noteworthy features that I have missed or emergent problems that I should warn about I will update this review to reflect them. In the meantime, if you are considering an upgrade to the Note 3 from the previous model and are wondering if it's worth it - I say yes.

title: Powerful and an easy install
text: I received a review sample from the manufacturer and was pleasantly surprised when I opened the box. I was expecting an 'erector set' of many pieces that I would need to put together. Instead I received a complete solution that literally unfolded and snapped into place in minutes. Set up entails the unfolding and snapping step, plus connecting the antenna to a powered booster box with coaxial cable in from the antenna and out to your TV. Once connected you need to go into your TV's settings, select antenna as the input, then do a scan for available channels. Since I live close to a major metropolitan area - Orlando, Florida - I decided to test this at a friend's home in Ormond Beach, which is about sixty miles from Orlando and roughly the same distance from Jacksonville. This location tested the claimed forty mile radius for the device. The true power was when I did a quick test by temporarily setting it up, plugging it in and seeing what channels were available. With the device sitting on the floor the first scan found seven digital channels. Bear in mind that this was laying on the floor for the initial test, which is hardly optimum. Test number two entailed raising the antenna towards the ceiling (but not permanently mounting it) and moving it around to various spots in a 15x10 foot room. That increased the total channels received to twenty-two, including Orlando and Jacksonville channels that were twenty miles beyond the claimed range, as well as a few channels in Cocoa Beach (right at the edge of the range). Note that in both tests the Central Florida terrain is relatively flat. In other geographic locations the results may have been vastly different. Installation does require access to 110/120 AC power for the signal booster module. The mounting hardware that ships with this antenna is heavy-duty and complete. You can use one of the clamps to mount it to practically any pole of beam, but there is a pipe assembly that provides you with even more mounting options. The kit also includes fifty feel of high quality coaxial cable, with a removable double male connector in one end in case you need to run it even farther. You will need to purchase a second coaxial cable to connect the booster box's out port to your TV. For outdoor mounting (or in a ceiling that is not close to a 110/120 AC outlet) I recommend running the longer cable from the antenna to the powered booster, which can be placed close to the TV. If you decide to place the booster closer to the antenna's coaxial connection make sure you can do with without using an extension cord, which could be a safety issue. The bottom line is this antenna works beautifully. Since it picked up signals fifty percent farther than the claimed range it greatly exceeded my expectations. For the record, although I received the antenna as a review sample I donated it to a worthy cause after I completed my testing and had enough information to write this review. I do recommend it as a wonderful solution and an alternative to cable if local programming meets your news and entertainment needs.

title: Very pleased with this phone (upgraded from a Note 2)

If for some reason that app fails you, move all of your text messages from your old phone to this one by loading a free app called [[ASIN:B0075A5S0K SMS Backup & Restore]] and following the directions I outlined in my November 30, 2013 review of that product.
