Read the other reviews for other perspectives and information too because combined there is a high level of customer satisfaction.

title: Comfortable with exceptional sound quality
text: I received a review sample and put these through their paces. I want to disclose that I enlisted the aid of a friend to test these because she loves ear bud style headphones and is a demanding consumer. Both of us tested the sound quality and we were both impressed. For me the album [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] is the acid test because of the number of instruments and the dynamics and subtleties of the music. After I connected these to the 3.5mm jack on my Galaxy Note II I was treated to spectacular sound quality. While these are not noise-canceling phones the ambient noises in my car were completely attenuated. My friend tried these out with her iPhone 4S and could not only clearly hear folks to whom she was calling, but they confirmed that she was coming in crystal clear on their end. That confirms that the microphone is of the same excellent quality as the phones. I found these to be extremely comfortable, which is saying a lot because I am not an ear-bud person. In fact I fell in love with them, but gave them to my friend as a token of my appreciation for her help in evaluating them. Construction is impressive. The 3.5mm is gold plated and the cable is heavy-duty with strain reliefs. Even the in-line mic switch is sturdy. There are some wonderful touches in the packaging and included components starting with one of each size of ear gels (small, medium and large). The phones also come with a nice carrying pouch that is not only attractive, but also functional. Overall these are premium quality earphones that will please even the most finicky audiophiles. They are a perfect solution for folks who use their phones as an MP3 player because you can immediately switch into answer or call more with a flick of a switch.

title: Handy and convenient
text: A friend gave me a pack of these and I am surprised by how much I use them. First, the color coding - two of each color - allows me to use these for specific tasks. The gold ones are for my glasses, the blue for my Galaxy Note II phone and the green for my laptop. The others are in a drawer as spares in case I manage to wear one out. That's highly unlikely though because these seem to be an 80/20 blend of poly and nylon. The weave is super tight and I assure you that they are absolutely lint free. What I love is the size. If you take a sheet of paper and layout a seven inch by six inch rectangle you will see just how large these are. They make short work of LCD screens and I have not scratched anything I have cleaned with them. I accidentally threw one in the wash and it came out none the worse, so they are machine washable if you manage to badly soil them. I have been told to not use fabric softener (which I do not use anyway.) Judging by how well mine have held up I am guessing that the pack will last five plus years as long as you use them for cleaning lenses, LCD screens and similar uses. That's a lot of bang for the buck.

title: Incredibly cheap back-up
text: This review is of the 64GB SDHX card. I use it for a specific purpose: backing up my document folders on my two laptops. It works perfectly with my Windows XP systems over ancient USB 2.0 ports. I can still back up a full card in less than an hour, and if I were on a more modern system with USB 3.0 it would take only a fraction of that time. This particular card will NOT work in my Samsung Galaxy Note II (I had to try anyway). In fact, make sure your device will actually accept SDHX cards before purchaing this 64GB model or you may be disappointed. Most Microsoft Windows systems running XP service pack 2 or later, Windows CE and Server 2003 will recognize this card, as will Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6.5 or later. Phones, tablets and devices running Microsoft Windows RT will also recognize this card. Beyond that check first. Back to how I use this card: the price for this card is around forty bucks at the time of this review. I could have gotten an exernal hard drive in the terabyte range for twice that, but this has no moving parts, fits in my wallet and with a [[ASIN:B00FSDKBYY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 Flash Memory Card Reader]] plugs into any computer (with an operating system that supports the format) via USB ports. For me it's convenient, especially since I am only backing up working documents and never come close to the 64GB capacity (which is closer to 56GB formatted.) In fact I use two of these in rotation for safety, overwriting the older one completely since it takes less than an hour. I always keep the other one on my person. As the SDHX standard becomes more established and ubiquitous this type of card may work with more devices. At 64GB this is probably the smallest size since the SDHX format was designed to accomodate up to two terabytes. So unless you have a device that is compatible with this format, or you are using it for a single purpose on a supported operating system, you may want to get an SDHC card instead.

title: Reads legacy and modern cards
text: I received a review sample from the manufacturer along with two of their other readers. This one is very close on functionality to the [[ASIN:B00FSFZ8AY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 12-in-1 6 slot]] model except this one does not have a slot for Sony's M2 cards. Since the product description on this page has all of the specs and ample photos I will not repeat them here. What I love about this card reader is that you are covered if you have a mix of modern cards like the micro SD that just about every phone, camera and other electronic devices now use, and the ancient CF and XD cards that one of my old cameras uses. Plus this will work with Sony's memory sticks, which many universal card readers will not. For this review my test beds were an old Dell laptop and an Acer Netone netbook, both of which are running Windows XP. Both machines immediately recognized the card reader, and when I inserted a card it was recognized and mounted as file systems. I tested this with an ancient CF card, an MMC card, a Sony memory stick and a micro SD card - all simultaneously. This hub allows you to transfer files between and among cards in the reader as well as to and from your computer and does so with no overheating that I could detect. One feature I like is the detachable USB cable that is included. This is a heavy duty cable, unlike the flimsy ones that some brands bundle with hubs. At a little over two feet long it gives you some flexibility regarding where you place the reader. It also will plug into USB ports that are adjacent to one that is already occupied. This is important to me on my Dell laptop because there is little spacing and it's a tight fit when I have two devices plugged into both ports. The construction is rock solid and built to last. It's a versatile card reader that will meet your every need unless you also have Sony M2 cards, in which case I recommend that you consider the model I cited above.

title: Comfortable and excellent sound quality
text: Two things up front: (1) I received this from the seller as a review sample, and (2) I have never used an over-the-ear headset before. This was tested with a Samsung Galaxy Note II and an Apple iPhone 4s. Since the product description contains specifications I will not recite them here. I will say that the installation instructions are slightly different from that the device displays. Where it claims that a blue light and green light will flash in an alternating sequence mine flashed orange and green. That set me back about ten minutes when doing my initial pairing, but when I figured out it paired and worked flawlessly. One other part of the install and pairing instructions that did not apply to my device was the need to enter a 0000 code to connect. Mine paired and connected without that step, but it may be how my phone is set up. Once paired and connected the sound quality is crystal clear. Surprisingly so for me - but remember that I have never used this type of device before so have nothing against which to compare. It is extremely comfortable and after about five minutes I did not notice that I was wearing it. The big test came when I made a few calls. The folks on the receiving ends claimed that I was coming through loud and crystal clear. While this is designed to be a headset for hand's free calling I tried listening to music through it. I did not care for that, but bear in mind that it was all going into one ear when I am accustomed to left and right phones or ear buds. The sound quality was excellent, but just not in stereo. In addition to a volume control rocker button there is a multi-function button that is located inconspicuously on the mic part of the headset. This button allows you to answer, end or reject a call, and to redial the last called number. For answering a call you can do it using your phone or the multi-function button. Out of the box this is designed to work with your right ear. I prefer my left, and at first could not figure out how to adjust it to work that way. I contacted the manufacturer and they showed me how - the mic can rotate on two planes and can, in fact, be adjusted for left ear use. I uploaded a a customer-supplied image that shows how to make the adjustment. One final note: charge it for two hours (or until the indicator light on the device turns solid green) before trying to use it for the first time. I have grown to love it despite my personal ear preference, and the packaging is so attractive that I am probably going to buy a few of these for stocking stuffers for the upcoming holidays. I have a feeling that some friends and family members will be pleased. I sure am.

title: A complete solution that is a snap to use
text: I received a review copy of this receiver and put it through its paces. I am going to compare it to a receiver that I've owned since 2011 and have been thoroughly pleased with: [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]]. It's a complete solution: the box contained easy-to-follow instructions and two sets of cables: one 3.5mm male at each end and the other with a 3.5mm male splitting into two RCA males. Those are a nice touch because some speakers require one or the other. With my Belkin I had to purchase an adapter to use it with one of my powered speakers. So having a complete solution right out of the box is a plus. The receiver looks like a wall wart that plugs directly into a wall socket. It's about two inches tall and 1.75 inches wide, so it does eat up come space. Since the speaker cable comes out the bottom of the device you are pretty much locked into plugging it into the bottom receptacle. One feature I loved is this also has a port for USB charging that allows you to keep your phone or MP3 player fully charged while playing music. This, of course, is based on later technology and it shows. I greatly exceeded the ten meter distance limit by taking my phone to the opposite end of my house, two rooms apart from the receiver, and still managed a clear signal. Believe me, on its best day the Belkin struggled to receive a line of sight signal within a ten meter limit. I even took my phone outside and could hear clear reception coming from my speakers inside my house. While the instruction sheet will step you through connecting to and using this receiver I did not bother to read it. I opened the bluetooth settings on my [[ASIN:B00AB7FVCY Samsung Galaxy Note II]], scanned for new devices and when BrightPlay Home showed up in the list I tapped it to connect and started streaming music to my speaker. It took longer to unpackage the receiver than it did to start using it. It does not get any easier. The sound quality is markedly better too. I switched back and forth between the Belkin receiver and this one - attached to the same powered speakers - and could tell the difference. Not by much, mind you, but it's discernible. I had a friend listen and she agreed. Overall this is an excellent receiver that exceeded the recommended specs in the instruction sheet and it a breeze to use. If I had to replace this it would be with an identical receiver and that is the highest praise I can bestow.

title: Works perfectly in my Note II
text: Like others I opted for this more expensive card because I wanted peace of mind that it would work without problems with my Note II. I literally popped this in and it was immediately recognized and works like a charm. I upgraded from a 32GB card that I managed to outgrow in six months (music junkie). Transfer from my old card to this one was simple. I used the following steps: (1) Removed the old card from my Note II and placed it into the USB adapter which came with it. (2) Plugged the USB adapter into my Windows XP laptop and mounted it as a drive. Marked the drive as sharable on my WiFi network. (3) Inserted the new card into the Note II - it was recognized with no need to format. (4) Connected to the shared drive (old card connected to my laptop) over WiFi and copied the contents to the new card. For some reason I lost my playlists, but all of my music and other media came over perfectly. It's as though my storage magically doubled. One thing I noticed is unlike my older card that heated up when i did the same procedure moving up from 16GB to 32GB is this one runs cool. The older card was a Sandisk, which was otherwise flawless and reliable. I just did not want to push the envelope with a 64GB card buy using anything but a genuine Samsung card because I heard there could be issues with cards in that capacity range. To me it was worth the extra bucks to be safe. As for speed, I am going to take the lower numbers reported by others at face value. Assuming that this card is nowhere near as fast as Samsung claims, it's still fast enough for me. If you have a Note II I highly recommend this card if you need the extra storage on your phone. It's a safe choice and works perfectly out of the box.

title: Built to last
text: My 'Amazon Verified Purchase' badge for this cable dates all the way back to September 23, 2002 according to my Instant Order Update. Ironically the cable is in the other room connected to a printer and still transmitting flawlessly. The moral is this is one well constructed cable and has returned my investment many times over. The connectors still mate and disengage smoothly like the first day I used it, and I am pretty sure that the beefy strain reliefs on each end are responsible for keeping the conductors inside the thick insulator intact. Indeed, as I inspected this cable before writing this review I marveled at the construction and materials. Both are first rate. This cable has traveled extensively - it was part of my travel kit when I was a road warrior consultant, and served me well in many US states as well as the Middle East on long and short assignments. Back to the strain reliefs: I would hastily pack and literally ball this cable up and throw it in my laptop case, yet the ends never damaged, which I attribute - in part - to the strain reliefs that kept crimps from breaking or fraying the conductors. Bottom line - this model is now USB 2.0 compatible and is built to last. In other words, you cannot go wrong.

title: Solid and convenient for my application
text: This is a rock-solid clamp and post assembly that is rated for 30 pounds per insert for a total of 60 pounds. I use it for a pair of [[ASIN:B005DSTO92 Powerwerks 50 Watt Self-Contained Personal P.A. System]] that weigh in at less than fifteen pounds each. I typically mount this on a [[ASIN:B002M8GBT2 On Stage SS7745 Adjustable Subwoofer Attachment]]. My application does not begin to stress this assembly because not only is the total weight half the recommended maximum, but my PA cabs easily fit within the 20" center-to-center distance between the inserts. That is actually a lot of space, so measure your speakers from the center of their pole inserts and if they do not exceed 10" (or 9 to be safe) on each side from the center of the insert they will fit this unit. Construction is an attractive, powder coated steel and heavy-duty. The tightening knob has a sufficiently large diameter to give you leverage to comfortably tighten the friction mount to your pole or stand. This has high quality and a low price - a combination I love.

title: Excellent bang for the buck
text: I did not experience the problems cited in the October 20, 2012 review, although that reviewer came across as knowledgeable. Either I was lucky or that unit was a lemon. Mine runs quiet with no signal distortion or bleed, and even the dual fans are whisper quiet. I have uploaded photos to show how I have mine configured. Some of the things I love are the form factor, which is a tiny 1U, the flexible outputs (Speakon or binding post), and simplicity. Another thing that I love is you can start with a single amp, then add another if you need more amplification. For me 300 Watts is more than ample for any live venue with a 300-patron capacity - or more, since I play low volume jazz and blues. Of course, the price is a major plus, especially considering that not only has my experience been positive, but a quick search will reveal that these enjoy a solid reputation for reliability and owner satisfaction.

title: Perfect for my specific use
text: I read the reviews and was aware that this was not a general purpose bluetooth adapter. However, it was exactly what I was looking for: a way to stream the large collection of music on my netbook to a [[ASIN:B00062QY5W Bose Companion 2; Multimedia Speaker System]] that I wanted to connect to via a [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]]. For this it works like a charm. Set-up was simple - so simple, in fact, that I first thought I had missed something until I started streaming music from across the room to the speakers. For reference I was using an old netbook running Windows XP and had zero problems with the system recognizing this device or getting it working. I would say the range is approximately 20 feet, but that may be limited by the Belkin receiver as much as the transmitting characteristics of this adapter. However, to be safe, I would not count on it transmitting farther than that. Bottom like: if you want to stream music from your computer to remote speakers and there is bluetooth receiver in the path, this will work. As others have said, you will not be able to transfer files with it. If that is what you want, look elsewhere (I wish I could offer suggestions, but do not have direct experience with any devices that will support that function.)

title: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth
text: I purchased a few of these as an impulse since I wanted to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]] components to my stero and a pair of powered speakers. For the price I was expecting cheaply made and flimsy cables that would be great for mating the receivers to RCA jacks in the stereo and in the powered speakers. Suffice to say I got more than I expected - and especially for eighty-eight cents and free shipping. For adapting 3.5mm to dual RCA the six inch length is more than adequate. What surprised me was the quality of the connectors, which are anything but cheap junk, and the gauge of the cable which is a step above what you would get at a dollar store. It makes one wonder how they can sell for such a low price and ship for free. Even more impressive, they seem to be noise-free, which is something I cannot say about some of the adapters I've used. I know that when something that's too good to be true should raise red flags, but in the case of these cables they are one of the rare instances when you get a lot more than you bargained for - and in a good way.

title: Two sets of RCA inputs make it perfect for me
text: Up front I will say that these fill a niche for me that was made possible because of the two sets of RCA inputs in the back of the main speaker. I cannot speak to the value for general purpose use or compare it to similar or competing products. I use my speakers to connect both a bluetooth receiver (a [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]]) for streaming music from my smart phone, and a netbook to my TV. Please see my customer-supplied images at the top of this page for photos that depict how. The bluetooth receiver allows me to stream music from my Droid X smart phone to the speakers. This is an important feature for me because I have most of my music collection on that device. Using the second set of RCA inputs, and a [[ASIN:B00004Z5CP Belkin Audio Y Cable Splitter 1-Mini Plug/2-RCA Plugs (6 Feet)]] I am able to transmit my netbook's audio to the speakers, while a [[ASIN:B0002AHT0M Standard 15-Pin VGA Male to VGA Male Cable]] connects the netbook to my TV. Regarding the sound: these speakers pump out clear sound that allows me to easily enjoy the full richness of my music up to 25 feet away. It favorably compares to my larger, power hungry surround sound system in quality, clarity and volume. A nice feature that I personally don't use is the headphone jack in the front of the master speaker. For folks who are connecting these speakers to a desktop or laptop system to extend their sound capabilities, this is a plus because at night or in an office it gives the privacy you may need. My only complaint is the power supply, which is more like a brick. Because of its size it takes up three outlets on my surge protector - one for the power and the size blocking two more. Please see my third customer-supplied image at the top of this page to see in detail what I mean. As you can see, my use is somewhat unique. If you are looking for a set of speakers for your laptop or desktop, plus a smart phone audio or MP3 player and do not need bluetooth streaming, then you can dispense with my configuration that uses the [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]] and replace that device with a simple [[ASIN:B00004Z5CP Belkin Audio Y Cable Splitter 1-Mini Plug/2-RCA Plugs (6 Feet)]] that will connect to the audio out jack on most smart phones. If you have any additional questions leave a comment to this review and I will respond.

title: A snap to set up and install and a cost-effective alternative to cable
text: I purchased this model(Roku HD) for a friend's birthday and set it up a few hours ago. While I am not going to rush out (yet) and buy one for myself, I admired the design and functionality of this slick little device. Here are my thoughts: - Ease of set-up: easy for anyone who can operate a PC, Mac or smart phone. Once you plug it in, power it up and select the video mode to which it's connected the screen will walk you though the process. I have an extensive technology background so I did not bother to read the manual beforehand and had no problems following what were simple on-screen instructions. And to Roku's credit, there were few of those. To be clear - you absolutely need a wireless internet router (WiFi) and a computing device to perform a few simple steps in order to install and activate the Roku HD. Including date entry and the time to explain some things to my friend for whom I was setting this up, the total time to get it running was less than 15 minutes. - Establishing your account. You will need some form of computing platform to access the Roku site via the web and complete this step. It's relatively painless. - Payment options: you can use a credit card or a Paypal account. I believe the latter is a relatively new option that shows that Roku is paying attention to complaints registered in these reviews. The Payment option is there to remove barriers to adding for pay services. Of course, it makes it so easy that you are almost lured into it. Smart move on their part. Just be careful because fees can add up. - Remote Control - Information that needed to be entered with the remote is a bit awkward at first, but I quickly adapted to it. One note about the remote: it is what we engineering geeks call elegant. Simple, functional with only the essential buttons. I absolutely loved the Netflix, Pandora and Crackle bottoms to quickly get most users to popular services. I would have loved it if Hulu Plus had a button since that is the service my friend plans to use. But that would have detracted from the elegance factor. - Manual: Although I did not need the manual to set ths device up, I did take the time to read through it afterwards to make sure my non-technical friend could depend on it if a problem arose. I was impressed with the clarity and how well the technical writing team made it simple, friendly and anticipated possible support problems by weaving in information that would preclude those. The default channels were merely OK, but a good start. The free content, especially from Crackle It, did not excite me nor my friend who would be using it. A word about economics: the friend for whom I purchased this and set it up wanted this so she could scale back on expenses. At one point she was paying approximately seventy dollars a month for cable service. She scaled that back to local channels that entailed a monthly recurring charge of three times the monthly fee of Hulu Plus. In fact, had she wanted, she could get Hulu Plus and Netflix's unlimited content for two thirds of what she is paying monthly for local cable channels, and nearly a fifth of the cost of her original subscription that did not provide near the content of Hulu Plue and Netflix combined. It's easy to see that this device pays for itself in very short order if you deem that the content from the services that you can stream via the Roku is as good for your purposes as the content you are currently getting from cable or satellite services. Everyone will have a different breakeven point after which your return on the initial investment is substantial. If you are considering this device do a little analysis. Of course, make sure the services to which you will subscribe with the Roku meet your needs. There are also services at various price levels that allow you to stream video, music and send photos directly from your PC or Mac to your TV via the service, which sends that content to your Roku. Four such services that you can easily find via a search of the web are: Roksbox, Play on, Chaneru and RoConnect. This device is so cool that I was tempted to get one for myself. I have not subscribed to any cable or satellite services for nearly a decade, but I do purchase a lot of DVDs and spend far too much time on YouTube. I am still on the fence, but was disappointed in the lack of YouTube support, and was not impressed with the available workarounds and services. The most promising, RateRix, seemed to me to be kludgy and unreliable. I was also put off by Netflix, which wanted me to sign up before I could ascertain that they had the content I was looking for. One part of their FAQ mentioned that their mail service was still available and had vastly more videos than their streaming service. Since I watch a lot of foreign langiage films, as well as jazz performances and concerts I decided that the Roku would not meet my immediate needs. One other (and puzzling) deal breaker for me is the Roku will not stream my music stored on Amazon's cloud. That is odd considering that it will stream music from Pandora and video from Amazon, but not music from Amazon. UPDATE (JULY 8, 2012): While my friend continues to love her Roku, I found an alternate streaming solution that gives me access to YouTube and even more content: [[ASIN:B00882OHL0 D-Link MovieNite Plus Streaming Media Player]]. See my July 8, 2012 review that compares and contrasts that device with the Roku, I am an old curmudgeon who is set in my ways. This device certainly met the entertainment and economic needs of my friend, and I am sure that anyone who pays for TV services has the potential to greatly benefit from it. The device is beautifully designed, not only from an engineering perspective, but also from a human-factors perspective. The minute Roku works a deal with Google for a YouTube channel is the minute I purchase one. I have a feeling that will happen sooner than later. In the meantime, the smile on my friend's face when this was up and running is proof of its value.

title: Quality construction and good design for my use
text: I use this to adapt my [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]] to the input jack on my [[ASIN:B0036B8A20 Kustom The Defender 5H Class A Guitar Amp Head]]. This is a power-saving solution I discovered for listening to music through the amp in my music room versus firing up my power-hungry stereo system. I then play music via my bluetooth-enabled phone. It's a kludgy solution that keeps my power bill down. It also shows how this adapter can work in one of an almost limitless number of situations. What I most like about this adapter is it is designed around a block with no dangling wires like, for example, a [[ASIN:B000068O4W Hosa YPR102 TRS Male To Dual RCA Female Y Cable]]. The key advantage is this adapter will not break at the weakest point - the wires. In the past I have had the wires on the Hosa-style adapters go bad or even break due to frequent handling. Every time you insert male RCA jacks into a Hosa-style adapter you are putting stress on the wires, which will eventually break down internally. In some cases the result is a noisy connection with intermittent static, but in others the signal is lost due to an internal break in the cable. The design of this adapter has none of the above mentioned points of failure. However, it does have one disadvantage that the Hosa-style does not: it will not fit into cramped places. Since I am plugging mine directly into the front of an amplifier the design does not matter. If you were to use it as an adapter to an amp or mixer that connects at the rear, you may run into space problems. Also, my amp connection does not have space constraints to the left or right, so, again, the design is perfect for me. For connections that have knobs, or other components close to the 1/4" connection, you may find that only a Hosa-style adapter will meet your needs. One final thing: while the design allows for stereo signal input at the RCA connection end, this adapter sums those signals into mono. That means that your stereo source will not be heard in stereo with this particular adapter. The Hosa model mentioned above will maintain stereo separation of the RCA signals, so if you want to maintain stereo, the Hosa is the way to go.

title: Inexpensive and handy on stage and in the studio
text: I mainly use [[ASIN:B002GOYU0O 12 pc Velcro Ties Reausable Electrical Wire Cable Strap]], which meet most of my needs. I also use these and like them a lot. Where these come in handy, and even augment my preferred strap, is they are nearly immovable once you tie them to a brace of other anchoring point. For example, if you are setting up with a keyboard, the stand makes a good anchor point for cross-stage cable runs. This is especially true of Z-style stands like the [[ASIN:B0002F6JH6 On Stage 2 Tier Folding Z Keyboard Stand]] (although X-style stands work well). This does take some pre-planning because you do not want to interfere with other musicians or, worse, create trip hazards. Because you loop the narrow end through the eyelet on the wider end and pull this strap has more holding strength than someone who is only running cables on stage and in a studio will ever need. Frankly, I augmented my preferred brand and model with these because of cost - and they are worth every penny. At 8" you can safely run more than a few instrument, speaker and microphone cables through one anchored to a frame like the Z-stand I mentioned above, and still keep the strap sufficiently loose to prevent stretching or breaking cables run through it. Think of it as one more handy tool in your bag of tricks if running and managing cable is one of the things you do. I purchased a half dozen packs for my needs.

title: Perfect for musical instruments
text: I use this both indoors and outdoors as a protected outlet for two keyboards (my other gear is protected by two rackmounted [[ASIN:B003TUO6U8 Merit Series Power Conditioner]]s.) One rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. The two keyboards I plug into this does not come close to overtaxing this device or power outlets into which I plug it. Some features I love include the 25 foot cord, which is heavy duty and os sufficiently long for any conceivable placement situation I will encounter. And because the cord is heavy gauge, and the housing is metal, this protected outlet is designed for rigorous use. Tripp Lite's reputation for quality, reliability and safety is another reason I purchased this unit. I am a firm believer in safety and will not cut corners. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. Thus far I have had zero problems, and judging from other reviewers I expect that to continue. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for.

title: Great for music lovers and important for hands-free calls
text: I purchased this for two specific reasons: (1) safety because too many accidents are caused by drivers with a phone to their ear, and (2) I love music and my Droid X has become my MP3 player (among other things as well as a phone. Installation was a snap, although I did have to read the directions, which were clear and easy to follow. In less than 5 minutes after removing it from the packaging I was listening to music through my car radio! This device comes with a fairly short USB charging cable that connects to a port on the head. The length made it inconvenient, and it was pretty flimsy too, failing after about three months. I added a [[ASIN:B0042X8XQO PowerLine 90310 Auto Socket Splitter with USB Power Port]] (which cleared my console in my 2008 Mazda 3 with the GOgroove and [[ASIN:B000S5Q9CA Motorola Vehicle Power Adapter micro-USB Rapid Rate Charger]] plugged in), and the combination, while unwieldy, has worked perfectly ever since. Music and calls are reasonably clear. I do have to turn my radio volume up when a call comes in, but that may be an issue with my phone and not the GOgroove. And, like a hands-free system should work, when there is an incoming call or you wish to make an outgoing one, the MP3 player feature in my Droid X pauses the music until I am finished using the phone. After calls are terminated any paused music will automatically resume. For long trips where you pass through areas with radio stations, your clear signal set in one location may start to degrade and you will notice static. That is caused by you coming into the range of a strong FM signal that is competing with the one you selected. You will need to seek and switch to a new frequency when that happens. For example, if I am traveling from, say, Ormond Beach, FL to Jacksonville, FL, I will need to change my frequency twice going up and twice again returning. It's the nature of any such device and there is nothing that can be designed into the GOgroove to fix it - at least not at the price point at which this device is selling. I've had friends connect to it with their iPhones, and it works without a hitch. The icing on the cake is the GOgroove remains paired with my Droid X, and automatically connects to it as soon as I start my car if I am playing music. This is a convenient feature that I wish my [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]] that is connected to my home stereo had - I have to manually connect to that device anytime I want to use it. Overall I am thrilled with my GOgroove and if it dies I would not hesitate to purchase another. In fact, I am considering purchasing a spare anyway because I spend a lot of time in my car and life without this wonderful gizmo would not be the same.

title: Cannot live without mine
text: Range limitations notwithstanding, this receiver has dramatically expanded the usefulness of my Droid X by allowing me to play my music through my home stereo system, as well as through my friend's [[ASIN:B001DLTDQC Bose SoundDock Series II Digital Music System for iPod (Black)]] (using an [[ASIN:B000068O51 Hosa YRA154 1/8 Male To Dual RCA Female]] to adapt the Belkin to the Sounddock since my Droid will not fit the iPod cradle.) One reason I do not have a problem with the range is I am usually in the room where the stereo is, and sit fairly close to where I have the Belkin receiver located. And, with the Bose rig, that is for taking out to the patio or in the kitchen, so I am in line of sight and pretty close as well. The signal is consistently strong between my Droid X and the receiver, and the sound quality is more than adequate for my old ears. The only thing I would want is for the Belkin receiver to automatically connect with my Droid X in the same manner that the [[ASIN:B003PPGOC0 GOgroove FlexSMART X2 ADVANCED Wireless In-Car Bluetooth FM Transmitter with Charging, Music Control and Hands-Free Calling for ANDROID, iPhone, Blackberry and Windows Smartphones]] I have in my car does. As it stands, I always have to go into my Droid's settings and manually connect the paired Belkin before I can transmit my music stream to it. Overall I am very pleased with this receiver and intend to purchase two more (one for a PA system I own, and a dedicated one for the Bose Sounddock.)

title: New sheriff in town
text: Prior to Alesis coming up with this and its larger sibling, the [[ASIN:B005NIVLX4 Alesis Mic Tube Duo Stereo Tube Microphone Preamplifier]], I was sold on the venerable [[ASIN:B0002D0KG4 PreSonus Tubepre Single-Channel Vacuum Tube Mic Pre]] as the "gold standard" in lower end tube microphone tube amps. I personally think this and the 2-channel model that Alesis offers are game changers, mainly because the features and reliability are on par with the PreSonus competing products, and the price point is significantly less. In other words, bang for your buck. Before rushing out and getting one of these (or its larger sibling - or even the competing PreSonus), make sure you need it. I have found that on a reasonably decent PA system this product makes a dramatic difference with the older technology mics like [[ASIN:B000CZ0R3S Shure SM57 Microphone]] and the [[ASIN:B000CZ0R42 Shure SM58-LC Cardioid Vocal Microphone without Cable]], or the lower end SM58 clones that are bundled with PA systems and otherwise flood the market (the [[ASIN:B00009W40D NADY SP-4C Dynamic Microphone]] comes to mind). On the other hand, not only have I found that these tube pre-amps not very useful with more modern design microphones like the [[ASIN:B002SQJL9U Blue Microphones enCORE 100 Studio-Grade Dynamic Performance Microphone]], the [[ASIN:B00006I5R7 Sennheiser E835 Dynamic Cardioid Microphone]], etc. In fact, with the more modern designed microphones, which run much hotter in signal, a pre-amp in a live PA needs to have the gain turned to the lowest level in many cases or feedback becomes a problem. If you do need one of these devices, I recommend - unless your budget is severely limited - that you consider the [[ASIN:B005NIVLX4 Alesis Mic Tube Duo Stereo Tube Microphone Preamplifier]] instead. The reason is for a slight increase in price you get an extra channel that you may not need now, but may find to be a requirement in the future.

title: Absolutely solid!
text: I use this cable with my [[ASIN:B0036B8A20 Kustom The Defender 5H Class A Guitar Amp Head]] and my [[ASIN:B004XFHWKE Kustom Defender 15 Watt Class A Guitar Head]], both of which I connect using this cable to [[ASIN:B0036B8A2K Kustom The Defender 1 x 12 Guitar Extension Cabinet for 5H Head]]. The CBI cables are well constructed (built like a tank, actually), and the 1/4" fittings mate perfectly with the amps and cabs. I am sure that the clear, clean signals I get from my amps are because of the exceptional construction of these cables, which appear to be engineered to provide optimum signals over a wide range of conditions. They are sufficiently heavy duty to meet the rigors of constant use, and are components that can make or break your sound. I highly recommend this model, especially for connecting amps to cabs.

title: Beware - uneven quality
text: The features and price make this regulator a bargain - except, there are those whose reviews indicated quality problems. I went with the positive reviews and purchased two of them. I had to return both. The back cover was loose on one, which is a safety hazard, and the other rattled when I handled it, indicating loose parts and a possible safety hazard. I would love to have two safe units that I could trust because the reviewers who had no problems are obviously happy with theirs. You may get lucky and receive one of the good units, or, like me, receive a product that is defective and, worse, potentially unsafe.

title: Perfect for my needs & great value
text: I was using an older 128 MB flash drive as the file system for e-mail on two older laptop computers. This allowed me to keep my mail synchronized on my primary home system and the one I take on travel. The problem was that I outgrew the 128 MB, and since both of my systems were older circa 2001 laptops that used USB 1.1 and ran under Windows 98 SE none of the gigabyte flash drives would work with it - all of the others required either USB 2.0 and/or Windows ME or 2000. This drive, however, is backwards compatible with the older USB 1.1 interface, and a Windows 98 SE driver is available for download from the manufacturer's site. Download and installation of the new driver went perfectly. It was literally done in a few mouse clicks. I plugged the drive into each machine and it was immediately recognized by both my Sony and IBM laptops. I also tried this on a Windows 2000 system and it was immediately recognized and assigned as a disk drive without drivers. Not only does this device work as advertised with no problems, but it also leaves room for a second USB device on laptops that have adjacent ports (my Sony is configured like this). My old flash drive required me to use an USB extension cable in order to have room to plug in my mouse, so the form factor is yet another feature I like about this particular model. One final feaure I very much like - you can encrypt files on this device, and since I am using it as an email file system the privacy and protection this affords me is important. Highly recommended if you want a high-capacity flash drive that will work on older Windows 98 SE systems, or just a reliable and easy-to-install flash drive for any system. It will not work on Windows 95 and below systems (none of the flash drives of which I am aware will).

title: Good performance and value
text: I purchased this DVD ROM device to perform a specific primary task - as a back-up device for my laptops (I have three) - with some secondary needs, such as transferring some of my older VHS tapes to DVD. It meets all of these needs perfectly. Set-up is easy, and the software that ships with it is perhaps not world-class, but does the job. Installation and user documentation are clear and easy to follow; however, I have not needed to use the manufacturer's technical support, so I cannot comment on the quality of that. Note - I purchased this device based more on price than features, so if you are looking for a full featured DVD ROM, or one with more sophisticated software, you may want to shop around and compare others on the market. If your needs are relatively simple, such as mine are, and want to burn data, music and video at an affordable price, this model is a solid buy.

title: Excellent features & performance, with some problems
text: Installation is easy and performance is solid. There are some nice features, such as the ability to use this router as an access point that can bridge systems operating under the older 802.11b standard (11 mbps), as well as the blazingly fast 802.11g standard. It also comes with the usual features: DHCP server, NAT, and firewall. I also like the fact that the wired ports are based on switching instead of shared as a hub. However, there is one major aspect of this router that you need to consider before purchasing - there is a firmware flaw (as of firmware version 2.02.7) that exposes the remote administration feature to hackers who will attempt to exploit ports 80 and 443. Worse, turning off the remote administration feature does not close the vulnerability of ports 80 and 443. This vulnerability was reported widely by Jason Meserve in the 6/3/04 NW Virus and Bug Patch Alert, and a workaround was provided by Alan W. Rateliff in a 4/31/04 port to the Security Focus bugtrack list. The workaround is to set the port forwarding to send ports 80 and 443 to non-existent hosts. Rateliff further noted that forwarding the ports to any hosts (including listening ones if you are actually running servers) will override the default behavior. He also recommended immediately changing the default admin and password before connecting this router on a live network. There is another issue with Linksys in general, and that is the quality of their technical support, which I consider to be poor-to-mediocre, depending on how lucky you are when dealing with them. Overall, this router has a lot of excellent features and performs very well. The downside is the security issue cited above and my opinion that they have less than great technical support. Therefore, if you are a highly technical user and can perform the workaround described above, and can solve most common problems without needing Linksys' tech support you'll probably like it. However, if you are a non- or quasi-technical user who wants something that works out of the box and does not expose your network to security problems, you may want to look elsewhere.

title: Inexpensive solution to problem
text: My need for this device was to extend signal strength in my new home. I recently moved from California where houses are basically wood framed, to a new, larger home in Florida where houses use blocks for outside and load bearing walls. This heavier construction, combined with the distance between my wireless router and where I use my computer, severely degraded my signal and throughput. I purchased this device to rectify that problem - which it did. Installation, including putting it in wireless range extender mode, took mere minutes after unpacking it. I was communicating with an incredible 100% signal strength in practically no time after setting it up, which was a dramatic difference from the 20% strength before it was installed. I did an experiment by walking outside with my laptop and was still connected to my home network with 80% or better signal all the way to the end of my property. I like the fact that this device seems to interoperate flawlessly with other vendor products. One of my systems has an SMC wireless card, and another uses a Linksys. My wireless router is an SMC. Installation instructions were a bit sparse. I am a highly technical user, so I didn't need them, but a novice may have problems. Since I have not needed to use technical support I cannot comment on the quality of D-Link's support. Since I have not used this device as an access point I also cannot comment on how well it works in that mode. However, if you are seeking a simple and cost-effective solution to extending the range of your existing wireless LAN, and have some technical skills this may be the solution you are looking for. Even though I am pleased with this product I rated it at four stars because I have not used all of the features or D-Link's technical support, and do not think the documentation is novice-friendly.

title: Finally - something that works for me
text: This device isn't for everyone, but it fits my needs perfectly. It represents my third attempt to find an affordable, easy-to-use solution to getting scribbled meeting and design notes and drawings into my computer for quick dissemination to interested parties and stakeholders. I've previously tried the A.T. Cross-Pad (no longer made) and the Logitech IO Personal Digital Pen (ASIN B00006JP23), each of which fell short for various reasons. Here is how I use it - during meetings I take notes, do sketches (user interfaces, high-level system design diagrams, etc.), and list follow-up items. This material is automatically beamed to my Palm Vx as pictures of the sketches and/or notes. I upload these to my PC and email them as attachments. This gets information out quickly, which can be followed up later with more refined notes transcribed into a word processor (by hand) or better drawings (I use Visio). It does one thing only - captures pictures of what you write on plain paper - and it does that exceptionally well. I liked the easy set-up, the fact that it comes with a QWERTY tap keyboard (it's under the pad), and performs as advertised. If your needs are similar to mine stated above and you have either a Palm or Pocket PC PDA you will probably love this notepad. However, it does not perform optical character recognition, so it that is what you're seeking you need to keep looking.

title: Great product, excellent value & standards-compliant
text: I am pleased with this print server for a number of reasons: - administration is web-based and set-up is simple and straightforward if you're experienced - the documentation is a bit too terse for the non-technical (home) user who needs detailed guidance. - you get two USB ports and one parallel port, making this both flexible and an added value if you plan to locate all of your printers in the same space. The added value stems from the fact that most single-port print servers are in the same price range, and almost all of them only support printers with parallel ports. - it works in network environments based on Microsoft Windows, Netware, Macintosh, UNIX, or any combination, making it standards-compliant and open. I especially like the step-by-step instructions on the manufacturer's web site for integrating this device into Linux-based LANs. It can also be queried and managed via SNMP in an enterprise network. I am less pleased with the supporting web site. Although it is rich in useful content and has up-to-date driver downloads, well written FAQs and a wealth of technical information for Linux and UNIX users, the pages do not display properly in Netscape 4x. Considering the excellent UNIX and Linux support for the product and in the FAQs this was a surprise since most of those users will be using Netscape 4x as their browser. This is more of an inconvenience than a problem however. Overall, this is one of those rare products that does exactly what the manufacturer claims it will do, and it works flawlessly.

title: Entry-level - packed with features
text: The fixed 16 MB, which cannot be upgraded or swapped out, makes this camera suitable for entry-level buyers or those on a budget, but who want a digital camera with a suite of features and software. It's the features that make this camera such a value - it can function as a webcam/video conferencing camera, a digital camcorder (although you're limited to 3 minutes and 20 seconds of relatively low-resolution 320 x 240 video with voice annotation), and a digital still camera that can take 450 shots at 640 x 480 or 2000 shots at 320 x 240 resolution. It can also serve as a voice recorder that can hold up to 30 minutes of voice only recording. In addition to the features that are built in, the camera also comes with an up-to-date version of Microsoft NetMeeting, Ulead PhotoExpress 3.0 photo editing software, Ulead Cool 360 panoramic creation software, and Ulead Photo Explorer to manage your photos. If you are a casual user or primarily want a webcam that can sometimes function as a still camera or camcorder you may not outgrow this device. However, if what you really want is a digital camera, but want to start with a modestly-priced starter camera you'll probably love it. It installs easily and performs to specifications - two of the most important features of any camera in any price range.

title: Rock solid, easy set-up & great value
text: I'm using this device with a Motorola SurfBoard cable modem to connect to the Internet. I'm communicating with it using a Linksys WPC11 Wireless PC Card from one laptop and a direct Ethernet connection from another. It's worked flawlessly from the moment I unboxed and set it up. Set-up and configuration is simple and straightforward - connect to it via any browser using the default address given in the instruction manual, select your connection type (fixed or ISP-assigned IP address and Cable or DSL), and you're ready to go - using these settings I was on the Internet within minutes of getting cable modem service. However, the device has many more options and parameters that you can set to provide additional protection, to block workgroup users from certain sites, and to make services such as a web server using a private address accessible from the Internet. More importantly, you can configure it for remote administration. There are a few minor annoyances - although part of the configuration is to set your time zone, it will not give the correct time unless connected to an outside DSL or cable model service (I suspect it uses Network Time Protocol for to keep time. Another annoyance is the fact that it logs every event even if you turn off security. These are not genuine problems and certainly don't detract from its functionality or reliability. From a performance standpoint, mine has been so reliable that I take it for granted. I also have had no problems with it dropping wireless connections that were reported by others - it came immediately up as soon as my wireless-enabled laptop was turned on after three, and the laptop immediately connected and was communicating. If you are considering this device for a small workgroup you should consider the SMC Wireless 4-Port Cable/DSL Router with Print Server (ASIN B00005ARK4), which works identically to this model, but includes a built-in print server.

title: Well designed and easy to install and configure
text: Through no fault of this excellent product I was only able to use it for a week - I inherited an old Lexmark Z11 inkjet that I wanted to share between two laptops in my corporate apartment, but wound up replacing the Lexmark with an USB-only printer. What makes this such an excellent product is the ease of installation and the fact that it flawlessly works. Installing it consisted of attaching the device directly to the printer's parallel interface, connecting an Ethernet cable to the RJ-45 port on the other side of the print server, running the CD ROM installation and being able to immediately print to a shared printer. One of the things I most like is the installation and configuration utility that ships with this device. You get an administration program (you can also access and administer the print server through a browser or through a telnet session), and an "add printer" wizard that makes configuring other computers on your network easy. In fact, the "add printer" wizard is a quantum improvement over D-Link's earlier Pocket Print Server products - I own an older model and set-up and configuration was somewhat confusing, which is no longer the case with their newer software. I also link the small power supply, which takes up little space in a power strip or on an UPS. Overall, this is a high quality product that has a plethora of features (it supports Windows networking, AppleTalk and TCP/IP, and it can be managed via browser of by using TCP/IP telnet), and can be installed and configured by a novice.

title: Excellent value for a basic, high-capacity USB flashdrive
text: This device is a no frills, high-value peripheral that you can literally plug in and use to transport files or extend your file system. Unlike some other USB flash memory devices that come with password protection and additional utilities, this one is simply storage with no features beyond that. The value stems from the cost, which is among the least expensive of the devices I considered. One unique feature that I especially like is that it does not require drivers for Windows 98 - all other USB flash drives I considered required them. ALthough I haven't tested it, the manufacturer claims that it is compatible with all versions of Windows from 98 to XP, and also for the Mac OS. I initially purchased mine to use for transporting files, but found that the best use (for me) was to use it as file system extension for my e-mail client. This works remarkably well for me because I use both an IBM ThinkPad and a Sony Viao laptop (both of which are running Windows 98 SE) and synchronizing e-mail between the two machines is a chore. I now have my e-mail client configured to store my e-mail on the flash drive, and plug the flash drive into whichever of the laptops I happen to be using at the time. This alone makes the flashdrive invaluable. Note that on some systems with side-by-side USB ports that the flashdrive may prevent you from using the other port because of its width. My ThinkPad has a port in the rear and one on the right side, so that didn't pose problems, but the Sony laptop's USB ports are close together and when the flashdrive is plugged I couldn't squeeze the connector for my mouse into the adjacent port - I solved this by purchasing a mini-USB hub that is powered by the USB port, but this is something you need to know before purchasing this particular flashdrive. Despite that minor problem I am pleased with the device and am especially happy that I now have a solution to the e-mail synchronization problem that has plagued me for years.

title: Beautiful watch, great size, simple to use, awkward app, find phone almost useless
text: [[VIDEOID:d3ebc84f3d3fd77b0d4bf01d2a1d3ade]] I had very specific needs/wants with a smart watch and this watch takes care of those. However, I knew what I was getting into and it was a choice - appearance, size, basic function vs feature rich and huge!!! This is a beautiful watch that suits for a delicate, feminine appearance without being bulky. While not light, it is very comfortable to wear, even while sleeping. My previous regular watch was a simple Timex Indiglo. Small, silver, lovely and functional. But I wanted the notifications and step tracking so I wouldn't need a separate fitness device. I then got an ASUS Zenwatch 2. Loved it! Feature rich, great interface, but larger than I wanted and looked like a calculator on my wrist. I lost it and have been attempting to find something to replace it. I purchased a modern fashion smart watch, but the dial was huge and didn't suite my taste. Then I found this one. Right size, right look, right features (steps, find phone, notifications, etc). I've had it a week and here's where I am. Physical - beautiful silver appearance with a delicate look. Band is flexible, very comfortable and easy to put on and take off. I have a 7" wrist and removed one link using the INCLUDED link removal tool. This is a fantastic add on to this watch. Display and interface - bright and clear. Images are simple, but pleasing. Fonts are nice. Scroll is reasonably responsive. Lots of options for faces including your own custom. My only gripe with the faces is that I wish you could choose the custom features to display. I would have liked a battery status with my custom image. Touch screen is responsive, though I find my fingers are large and I have some issues periodically controlling the small buttons for stopwatch and timer. Stopwatch and timer can't run in the background, so you can't scroll through the watch while using them. Would need to set an alarm from the phone instead. The find phone feature is virtually worthless. If you're any distance from the phone then the Bluetooth disconnects and you can't send the find signal. Notifications - I am happy with notifications overall in that I actually receive them and can read enough to get the gist. However, you can only see the last message received. Also, you can only scroll to a set number of characters. The messages are prefixed by all of the people in a thread. So if you have a group of 6 people in a message, all of their names will be displayed, and then you'll see who sent the message, and then it will start the message, but it will be truncated to a limited number of characters. Phone app - leaves A LOT to be desired. The grammar in English is awkward. Determine to select, state for steps, etc. The tracking is wonky in that it's per day and you have to select each day from the calendar. There are no charting or trends with the exception of a chart for the single day of sleep. Tracking for blood ox, BPM, and blood pressure in the phone only keeps if it's started from the phone. If you start it from the watch, it doesn't log it. Battery - Goes for at least 3 days so far with the tilt-to-view and auto heart monitoring off. I like that the charger is a plate that the watch sits in. Even with all of this, I am happy with my watch. I know the limitations, but until there is a comparable alternative, I'm good with this one.

title: Perfect... for my needs
text: I have had the latest gen Kindle DX since October 2010. I am a singer in a choir and use it to display my sheet music. It is well suited to my needs. The display is clear and crisp and is the size of a standard music hymnal. The catch is getting the music onto the device. Most publishers are starting to provide PDF versions of at least melody with accompaniment. However, being an alto in a choir, that isn't sufficient. I need the 3 or 4 part choral version. Also, it is formatted for an 8.5 x 11 inch page with headers, footers, and page numbers. I only need the music staff and lyrics. So I do it the hard way. I scan my (purchased & owned) hymnal or sheet music, crop it down to what I need, then convert it to a PDF. Lots of work, but the payoff is worth it. I no longer carry around 100+ lbs of sheet music and hymnals twice a week! Keep in mind this isn't for everyone. It requires a lot of time and patience, but once the music has been prepped and imported, it's done and ready when you need it. I assume after a year I'll have perhaps 80% of my library scanned. Then I'll only need 5-10 minutes each week to add the relevant music to a collection for quick access. I also use the Kindle not so much for reading, but for listening. I love the text-to-speech feature. I use it for casual reading as well as my Cisco tech books. Funky digital voice and some unusual phrasing and pronunciation, but you can't beat having it read to you while your hands and eyes are otherwise engaged in other things such as driving or crocheting :D I have used the web feature while camping. Nothing great, but you can check email, news, Facebook and other text or mobile supported sites. I've also used it when traveling to get directions or check Yelp while on the go. Since I don't have a smart phone this is actually a huge plus! One thing to keep in mind is that image intensive sites may crash the Kindle (due to lack of memory) and you will have to reload it to clear the issue. The music player is lacking, but for an e-reader, I guess that's expected. You can load music and it will play in the order you loaded it. You can pause and skip, but that's about it. No actual controls or playlist features. One major feature that is currently lacking is hands free page turning. Since there is no USB driver or bluetooth support, I don't foresee this ever being available, but it is definitely something to keep in mind. I also play flute and am unable to use the Kindle to display my flute music unless it is a single page. So, for my needs, it's great. However, if you're looking for more media support or better web access, you should look elsewhere.

title: Contender for best mouse I've owned
text: Contender for best mouse I've owned, going up against the Logitech g900. They are very different mice, for different people though. PROS: -excellent feel. the ergonomics are on point, and it's honestly a pleasure to hold. slides nicely on any surface, weight is perfect, and fatigue is zero. -separate buttons. so tired of the trend of mice that have one piece of plastic on top, rather than individual cut out buttons. (e.g. razer deathadder) it looks nice, but feels like crap. -the auto switch scroll mechanism. I miss it on all other mice now. my G900 has a mechanical button to switch modes, and while that is nice, it's not as incredibly satisfying and intuitive as the MX master -beautiful. my office mates are jealous -LONG battery life. I forget it needs to be charged after 3 weeks to a month, which is about when it starts blinking at me. (I use it 4-8 hours a day at work), and when it does charge, the charge port is in a perfect place to not impede your work. -excellent bluetooth. I leave it on my desk at night, and when sit down with my laptop it wakes right up and immediately works. I've had some input lag issues with it, but those are few and far between, and can be fixed by flipping the switch. Neutral: -the side scroll wheel. It's a nice feature, but doesn't respond all that well in GIMP or chrome. it's always either too sensitive or not enough. that said, it's the best side wheel i've ever used. they must be hard to do right or something. CONS: -mine came with a bump in the scroll wheel, due to bad molding. normally this wouldn't be a complaint, but for a $100 mouse (at time of purchase) it better be absolutely perfect. -back and forward buttons are tiny. you get used to them for sure, but a more conventional layout would be a lot better, and more efficient. -the gesture control button. might as well have just omitted it. It has its uses, but it's so awkward to press (the actual button is on the seam of the plastic and the metal) that it is 99% of the time easier to just do the thing the gesture was replacing. now, if the button had been under where your thumb rests naturally, this might have been in the pros category. -the omission of side clicks on the scroll wheel. I can see why they wouldn't on a non-gaming mouse, but I would like them just to assign controls to.

title: Just what I was looking for.
text: I give it 5 stars with 2 caveats. First, it's not stated in the description that it recognizes fewer formats when in BT mode and the instructions seem to be lacking in detail, so it took a while to figure out how to access all of the functions. Hint: You can only access playback functions while in BT because BT, itself, is a sub-folder, so you have to back out of BT to do other things. Ultimately, I gave it 5 stars because a) i had just a few songs in the missing formats and b) once I got past the navigation issues, it works quite well and the company was very helpful when I needed them. Update: Turns out as I loaded more music I found a lot more music that wasn't found while in BT, including some albums where some of the songs appeared and some didn't. Al in all, it's kind of clumsy to navigate in BT and BT was the feature I wanted most. However, it sounds good with the earbuds that they provide and it's size makes it convenient. The 8gb are plenty if you don't have a lot of music. I do, so I added a 32gb sd mini-card which is as large as it will take.

Not a problem if you use headphones but if you plan on relying on these speakers ( which i don't) then you'll have to turn up the volume and itll still be a muffled.

title: Pleasantly surprised with this Kindle case!
text: I can’t believe I’ve had my Kindle Paperwhite (6th generation) for ten years. I am usually very careful with my things and this Kindle has held up well. I read every day mostly at home and just take it with me on a few trips. It basically sits on my nightstand when I’m not reading. I originally bought a Kindle Smart Cover (ten years ago) and it also held up extremely well…except the other day the magnet flap on the edge started to come off. I decided to look into buying another cover and was concerned the quality wouldn’t be as good since this is a different brand. I did, however, really like the color so decided to go ahead and purchase it. My case just arrived and I couldn’t be happier. I would call the color more of a teal than “blue” which totally suits me. I find it easier to find when it’s sitting on my bed or other surfaces, since the case is lighter in color than black or gray. The material is very soft (they say waterproof) and the edges are not so “sharp” against my skin as the first cover I purchased. (It took some time to get those edges smoothed down during its original use.) The wake/sleep function on this new case works perfectly and my Kindle fit into the case snuggly. The cover folds back on itself so I can easily hold it in one hand…the inside of the cover is a nice soft gray material. I think this “ultra thin” case might even be a bit lighter in weight than my original cover, so that’s a plus for me. I think the value is quite good…assuming it lasts a good long while like my first cover. I am very happy and would purchase again.

title: My all-time favorite mouse for work
text: I work full-time from home and have been using this same Logitech mouse for years. When it’s time for a replacement, I do look to see what other options are out there…but I just keep coming back to this one. It’s comfortable in my hand and responds well to my touch. The only reason I need to replace it is because I often eat at my desk and sometimes that’s hard on a mouse. Also, when you consider how much time we spend using a mouse, the surface is just bound to wear down. I like the size…I have tried the mini versions but that size isn’t practical for me working all day at a computer. I probably don’t use all the features…just the wheel and left/right clicks. It rolls nicely and the battery life lasts quite a while. I like the little green light on the top to tell me it still has a charge. I use a basic mouse pad with a built-in wrist rest and my hand and arm do not feel any strain. The rubberized grip really helps me hold onto it comfortably. I have seen this mouse in other patterns but I stick with this dark gray version. I have a black desk and I would just prefer to keep everything monochromatic, since my office is in my home. Definitely plug and play once you put in the USB receiver. I think this is a quality item for the price and I will continue to purchase, as needed. I highly recommend its reliability.

title: Best TV in the house
text: I bought this TV a while back and absolutely love it. I wanted something for my bedroom…proportional for me watching while sitting on my bed…and I find myself wanting to watch from here more often than the newer TV we have in the living room. The colors are vibrant and the sound great. Many times google just does its screenshot mode and flips on gorgeous photos. I keep my TV most of the time just to have this background. It’s like having an ever-changing 55-inch picture frame. This particular screen is perfect in size for my standard master bedroom. The remote is easy to use and balances well in my hand. I can find the typical buttons pretty well just by feel. I feel that the value is certainly there for the quality and would buy Samsung again.

title: Many uses for this sturdy industrial-looking stand
text: I work full-time from home and originally bought this stand to raise my monitor. Then I bought another stand to raise my laser printer on one side of my desk. Since I recently bought a new larger monitor (and don’t need to use a stand to lift it up), I now use that first stand for my color printer on the other side of my desk. I love how it is now so much easier for me to grab my printed documents. Such a simple solution to just raise everything up. I put rubber feet on my monitors to avoid any slipping that might occur on the metal stands…so no problem there. The stand allows me to put papers or folders underneath, so any extra storage is always helpful. The vents are quite functional to keep electronics cooled down, and the stand has an industrial look to it that appeals to me. Each stand comes with its own rubber bumpers which helps keep it stable. There are probably many uses one could find around the house or office for these stands. They are sturdy metal and I’ve never seen a scratch on them. The quality and value are there and I highly recommend… I would certainly buy again.

title: This monitor is great for my multi-window work
text: I work full-time from home and, over the years, have increased the size of my monitor because…why not, right? I’m online all day long and currently working with so many windows, it just made sense for me to upgrade again recently and go with this 34-inch monitor. I have always been drawn to the curved screens and decided I would just treat myself. It’s almost comforting to have that curve kind of wrap around you visually. I think it actually helps me stay better focused. I set up a pleasant and not too busy (for me) background that frames whatever I’m working on. Sometimes I just center everything in the middle and other times I spread many of my windows out so I can drag and drop, reference something, etc. I honestly think this speeds up my work and makes me more productive. I’m still learning what works best for me but look forward to turning this screen on every day. I’m not yet into gaming but perhaps someday I will make that leap. I can see this wider monitor immersing the player in the game. The colors are rich and there are all sorts of ways to customize your preferences. I’m sure most gamers know what to look for, so check out the specs to see if this is the monitor for you. I’m reviewing from a working aspect and am very happy with my purchase. I’m glad I went with the height-adjustable model. I had my last 23-inch monitor on a separate monitor stand and that took up some valuable room on my desk. This LG monitor has the curved base (I’m sure to better have it balanced) and I work around that quite nicely. My keyboard can sit on the base comfortably, if I have to move it for paperwork I need to review. I feel this is a good value and I trust LG products. I do recommend and would purchase again if needed.

title: A great option for behind my night stand
text: Recently I found a need for me to have multiple devices hooked up at my nightstand. (Remember the days when it used to be just a lamp and a clock?) With this unit I have the choice of three USB ports and four sockets. I wanted something with the USB ports on the top so I could easily reach them, as well as keep the cord length closer to me. This power “strip” has met that need and has certainly come in handy. Instead of attaching it permanently to the wall or nightstand with screws, I used Command tape for a more temporary solution. Two Command strips have held it up with no problem. It has never fallen off, even when I plug items in and out. I have my google home hub plugged into one of the sockets. I also have my Bose sleep bud charging case and iPhone charging stand plugged in. All things I want close to me when I’m in or on the bed. Recently my eye doctor said I should be using warm compresses on my eyes, so I bought an eye mask with a USB cable. I leave the USB cord plugged in and just attach the other end to my eye mask when I’m using it. So convenient and really speeds up the process. When I’m done, I disconnect the cord from the mask and tuck the cord back behind my night stand. So easy to pull out and tuck back away. Sometimes I need to plug in a heating pad and this is the only convenient place to plug it in while I use it from the bed. Since I don’t use the heating pad all the time, it’s easy enough to just plug it in when I need it. I like that it’s low-profile enough to allow my nightstand to stay somewhat close to the wall. You wouldn’t even know it’s back there without leaning over and looking down. I found this to be a good value and I would purchase again.

title: I feel like I have a new phone!
text: I am so pleasantly surprised by this Caseology phone case. I bought my iPhone 6S plus phone over two years ago and ended up with the rose pink. At that time I could not find a transparent case online so ended up buying one at the Apple store for almost $50! It was a Tech21 case and I really liked it at first, but about a year later the transparent plastic started to discolor. Now it just looks dirty and embarrassing. It’s definitely the plastic turning a dirty looking brown. When I recently found this Caseology case online I thought I'd give it a try since it had so many good reviews and was very reasonably priced. I am so happy! Someone mentioned it being slippery, but I find the sides have a nice grip to them. Better than my original case. My phone fits in it nicely and I see no gaps. All the ports show up nicely and the buttons all work. Plus I can once again see the pretty color of my phone. This case color also matches the rose gold phone nicely. Five stars!

title: Are we beta testing a terrible product? NOT READY YET!
text: NOT Ready Yet. Sigh. So many issues, it's a joke at this point. Sorry, developers/owners of Ring.com but your product is not ready for release yet. 1) Android support is abominable. If the app isn't OPEN (and I mean you looking at the app) it's completely unreliable. Do anything else on your phone and it's a 50/50 gamble whether you'll get an alert. Even if you're standing inside the door. So this means that as a doorbell, it COMPLETELY FAILS. I can't have a doorbell that works 10% of the time, or 50% of the time, or 75% of the time. I need virtually flawless execution on the DOORBELL FEATURE OF THE DOORBELL. Until you have that, STOP SELLING DOORBELLS. 2) The default (and only) chime you get is super annoying. This is 2015 - I can't choose between chimes or upload my own? 3) The button is really hard to press - and the worst part is visitors won't know they're SUPPOSED to push harder to activate it. So they'll use normal pressure, nothing will happen, and nobody will know the difference. 4) You have a webcam connected to your wifi - and will be charged to store the content in the cloud - but you can't access the camera from the app. What a waste of a feature. So - it's completely unreliable. It's feature set is terrible. And it's expensive. PASS. This is getting returned immediately. What a disappointment.
