text: This is my first running watch. Although this is listed as a "Smart Watch", it's only "Smart" when it's liked to your phone. I use it as a running watch and a fitness tracker and it works great for a beginner like myself. It has built in GPS which is great for tracking runs and walks. It gives you all the basics like pace, cadence, distance, and time. You can configure the data fields to your liking, change watch faces, and download other apps. The GPS is very accurate, I compared the distance on the high school track and after 14 laps it was within a few feet of the track distance. An app using my phone's GPS was 1/2 mile off. (My guess is that measuring a distance from one point to another will be easier and more accurate than 14 laps around a 400 meter track.) The watch screen is optimized for outdoor running and it works great in the sunlight. As it gets darker you need to tilt the watch at an angle to see the screen. I've run at sun up ad sun down without issue. The screen is backlit but you need to push a button. That's a little awkward when your running, but I rarely run in the dark. I have not had any problems seeing the screen indoors with normal lighting. I picked this watch because of the low profile, large face, and relatively low price as it is an older model. It has made collecting data easy, and I can compare my progress as I work to become a better runner. Battery life is acceptable, I'm charging every 5 days while using GPS 30-45 minutes a day. The Garmin Connect App works well. Link it to myfitnesspal and you have a fairly complete fitness tracking app. Garmin also links with mapmyrun, Nike+, and Endomondo to name a few. This watch also works with an Garmin hear rate monitor. (010-10997-00). There are many great running watch choices available, so you will want to do your research. Of course you can always just use you smart phone and any of several great free running apps. A lot of those have voice feedback so you don't need to look at your phone.

title: Works as advertised for me
text: I've owned this for just over 1 year and it has worked well. I've used this device to track steps, flights of stairs, active minutes, and to help estimated calories burned. I've used the Fitbit app to count calories and counting calories has helped me lose 40 pounds. In my opinion, the device does a good job of counting steps. I have never had problems too many or too few steps. Wearing this fitbit while driving has never given a false reading. It may not be 100% accurate, but it is close enough. I have had a couple of problems with not syncing, but rebooting the device has solved them. I also had an instance where it counted too many flights of stairs but a reboot fixed that also. About the weight loss: The app is great and counting calories made all the difference it weight loss. Steps help you get in shape, but without changing eating habits you weight won't change much. ************************************************************************************************************************ Everything the fitbit helped me accomplished can be done with a smartphone and free apps. It can also be done with a cheap stopwatch and a notebook. However, the fitbit one and the fitbit app made it much easier for me to count calories and track fitness. **************************************************************************************************************************

title: Works well
text: This card works well in a cheap LG Tracfone. I have not had any issues with it and have had no problems with any apps or files stored on the card. I have not conducted any speed tests and can not say with 100% certainty this this card is better than any other card. However, this card has worked flawlessly for me so for that reason alone I give it 5 stars.

title: An excellent Bluetooth mouse for under $25.00
text: Smooth and quiet. The scroll works well and tracking is great. This mouse is much better than the Microsoft Wireless Mobile Mouse 3500. I'm using Windows 10 and I simply followed the directions on the box it the mouse paired easily. Microsoft includes a Duracell battery instead of some "knock off" brand so that's a plus. The battery door is easy to open (very nice touch). Being Bluetooth, no transceiver is needed for Bluetooth enabled computers. Bottom line: this is an excellent Bluetooth mouse for under $25.00.

title: It works, but...
text: This mouse is fine, but nothing special. The small USB transceiver is nice. It's out of the way and won't catch on anything. The mouse itself tracks on just about anything and is very reliable. The battery compartment is easy to access, no hassle replacing the single battery. I comes with a brand name battery uninstalled which is very nice. No software to install these days, the old Vista machine recognizes it without issue. However, it's too lightweight for my tastes. The “click” feels cheap to me and the scroll wheel is stiff. I have an older Logitech wireless mouse that has the larger USB transceiver and the batteries are a hassle to change, but it feels solid and works great. To be fair, this is a “Mobile Mouse”, so maybe lightweight should have been expected. I just didn't realize how much I would dislike the weight difference. I won't send this Microsoft mouse back, but I wouldn't buy it again. I haven't had any problems with this mouse, it's just personal preference. I'll just use the Microsoft as a travel mouse. I suppose it's also possible that operation becomes smoother with use, but I'm in no hurry to use this mouse.

title: No issues with this cable
text: It's cheap and is delivered fast with prime. I see no problems with it's construction or performance. I'm using it in an uninsulated garage and it's 5 deg. F outside now (if cold has any effect on Ethernet cable). It will be a while before I'll know how it handles hot weather (if heat has any effect on Ethernet cable)

title: Works as Advertised
text: I use this surge protector / timer when charging phones, tablets, cordless tools, and headphones. I bought this model for the settings of 1, 3 and 6 hours. It's nice that I recognize the brand name and it has some surge protection, but I bought it for the timer feature. I have a nasty habit of plugging in chargers and forgetting them and I prefer not to leave electronic devices on their chargers. Set this device for 1 hour and it shuts off its outlet in 1 hour. (I timed it at one hour and take it at its word for 3 and 6). I don't know if it would ever save enough money to pay for itself, but it does what I want it to do. It works as advertised. Also, I don't leave it plugged in when I'm not using it, but that's just me.

title: Pretty Good
text: I have three and have never had a problem. I use them behind furniture on outlets that are top wall switch controlled and bottom are always live. I put them in upside down so that the outlets are always live. Potential Issues: The six outlets are horizontal compared to two vertical wall outlets. This means if you are plugging something that uses one of those "power bricks" the cord is going to stick out instead of stick down like when it was plugged into the wall. This can be an issue if you bought this to use behind furniture that must be close to the wall. All six outlets are powered by one plug. If you use it on outlets that are top wall switch controlled and the bottom are always live you will end up with all wall switch controlled or all always live outlets. Because of the bulk, you take the original screw out of the outlet face plate, plug this unit into the outlet and screw it into the wall. This works very well, but if you want to remove it you'll need to unscrew it. Can you remember where you put the original screw?

title: Good value flash drive
text: No problems with this drive. I only transfer small files and usually transfer only a few at a time, so I don't need top class performance. I picked this flash drive for two reasons: 1) Great sale price 2) Never had a problem with the SanDisk items I have owned. I also like the Amazon frustration free packing.

title: Does the job well
text: I bought this as a "Like New" Amazon Warehouse Deal. It looked new and has worked as advertised. This does charge the Kindle Fire HD quickly, but this is the only charger I have ever used on the Fire so I have nothing to compare it to.

title: Works great, great price.
text: Fifteen feet and no loss of signal. I use this to connect my Kindle Fire HD to my HDTV and it works great.

title: Good Basic Case
text: This is a good basic case that takes a little getting used to. Nothing fancy here, but it works well. The case holds the kindle securely. The kindle is secured in place on all four sides with one side held by a Velcro flap tucked underneath the kindle. I can't say that the kindle will never fall out, but as long as the stitching holds up, the kindle is not going anywhere. The case is thin and comfortable in use, but provides no protection if you drop it. You have access to every thing while the case is closed. Magnets keep the case closed and serve as the auto on/off function. The case does not slip in your hands, but there is no hand strap here. You can fold the cover back and tuck it in a flap for free standing horizontal viewing. You get one position. This feature seems flimsy when you look at it, but I have not had any problems. It feels secure in use. At start up and shut down of the kindle it seems like the case was designed upside down. This must have been done so that the camera is on the top when the free standing position is used. This puts the on/off switch at the bottom when the cover is held like a book. It took me a few times to get used to this, but now it's automatic. Once you are up and running the auto rotate feature takes over. The only other issue I have is as the case comes up to the edge of the screen in most places, I have problems pulling down the main menu at times. This could be because I'm a new user, or I lack coordination. To solve my problem, I rotate the unit so that the camera is up. The camera has a big window, so I can always pull the menu down from that area. Bottom line, if the stitching holds up over time this was a great choice. If it doesn't, it won't be the first time I wasted ten bucks

title: Good adapter.
text: Good adapter, no problems, easy to install. I've used it with XP, Vista, and Win 7 without issue. I use it to connect to speakers, headphones, my phone, and a mouse.

title: Great connector
text: This is a great connector for those small jobs where it makes no sense to invest in a crimping tool. I wanted a cheap solution to access cable t.v. in a spare room. With these connectors, I was able to drill a smaller hole in the floor than I could have with factory installed connectors. All you need to do is cut the cable to length, strip the ends, and twist on the connectors. They feel solid, no worries about them coming off.

title: Good cable
text: No problems with this cable. I don't see any loss in quality of signal and it "looks" like a well made cable.

title: Using this clamp for outside Blink Security Cameras
text: Adjusts easily. Nice wide jaws. Unsure of rust potential if left outside. Sturdy.. does not creep when set with light camera module and silicone Blink cover

title: Silicone doorbell cover
text: Not sure if doorbell dimensions have changed since original release.. but hood catches IR night light and reflection bounces back across lens face. Causes huge glare.. renders video useless at night. Ok on daylight.. hood protects from raindrops and snow

title: Tamron 18-400mm Soft Neoprene Pouch
text: A bit of a snug fit when reversed sun shade attached.. but correct size for the Tamron 18-400mm. Seems like it will protect from bumps without taking up a lot of space in your big bag or luggage... also I see it will be very useful in wet or dusty conditions when lens on camera.

title: Not for AA batteries... 4.2 V... charges big batteries as designed
text: Not quite a universal charger... inadvertently charged 1.5v EBL AA batteries... shut off when charged... no apparent damage to the AAs. Works ad expected with 4.2v batteries

title: after market plate for Peak Design travel tripod
text: Works as expected... great value for an aftermarket plate that fits well

title: Peak Design Travel tripod accessory
text: Purchased this to enable using a Small Rig fluid tripod head instead of the standard ball head. Same high quality found in all of the Peak Design products I own. Adds tremendous versatility to a great tripod

title: fluid head tripod for Peak Design Travel tripod
text: Purchased for use on a Peak Design travel tripod to supplement the original ball head. Handled a Nikkor 200-500mm lens on a Nikon D850 with good stability tracking some birds in flight. Not as perfect as a heavy tripod and gimbal.. but very impressed with quality and fluid action. Great portable option

title: Replacement short cord for Arseal V2 to Nikon
text: Replacement for factory supplied Arsenal V2 to Nikon body coiled cable. Functions 100% as original. Just enough length to not put too much stress on either of the USB ends

title: FUSION5 fWIN232 Pro S2 keyboard
text: Does everything it is designed for . Quick attach/detach

title: Article low profile head Artcise 46mm
text: Like the design and low profile. Locks tight...but ball really drags and catches when rotated in all directions away from center. As mentioned in another review.. seems to be in the design on the cup..not the ball itself. Would not recommend for anything that requires fluid ball movement. I bought this for iOptron star glider so once set..camera doesnt have to move... I feel that my medium heavy mirrorless cameras safe.. would not use with heavy dslr and big lens

title: Lumix LX100M2 neoprene case
text: Camera fits one way only. Best feature is the quick detach tether strap that let's you drop case and it hangs from camera strap. Feature not always found on cheaper cases. Excellent padding for travel and protection from weather and bumps...doesn't add much weight.. only improvement that would make this a 5+ in my opinion would be an inner pouch for spare battery or short USB charging cord. IT really likes cat hair!

title: 10 foot braided USB cable
text: Nice fit on both connectors. Braided shield nice and stiff.. pleased with quality. Heavy duty compared to most similar cables.. using in a permanent installation... would pass if for travelling.... doesn't coil up as good as most others

title: Wimberley MH-100 monopod pivot head
text: I am using this with a Sirui carbon fiber monopod to add additional support for a Nikkor 200-500mm and a Tamron 150-600mm . Doesn't replace a full gimbal head but really helps with keeping arms from getting fatigued as quickly when performing a cross-fit workout with these big lenses

title: Fit Bit replacement straps
text: Shipping time from China about 6 weeks. ORIGINAL band lasted about a year.. worn everyday then just split. This pair of replacements in 2 colors appears to be identical to original... maybe just a little bit stiffer.. but pleased with quality

title: Item not as advertised or pictured
text: Similar to others... the power supply pictured and labeled as for the Fusion5 FWIN232 pro S2 is not what was sent. Plug not designed for this computer tablet... now I have to return and try and find a different vendor. Seems like this is an ongoing problem with this item

title: Silicone case Sony A7R4
text: I have used many of this type of cases for various brands of DSLRs over the years. This Sony shell was easy to apply and gives a nice added layer of insurance to protect your expensive investment. As with all cases.. function and focus buttons are covered.. but once you get used to it there is no diminished function. Thickness is just right... any thinner and it might tear when stretching over body. Only major fit issue on mine is the battery door opening is just a bit off in design.. you have to pull the case back to get the door open and closed. As with any rubber/silicone surface it is definitely a dust and cat hair magnet.. but the added weather protection and grip makes it worth it for me personally. I would purchase this again or replace if lost for a similar Sony body

title: Mirrorless camera sensor cleaning
text: Swithcing from DSLR bodies to any mirrorless body... your first lesson will be that dust on the sensor is an ongoing issue if you have more than one lens. I do not live in a terrible dusty environment... just the opposite.. lots of rain. Even with the built in vibration cleaner on screen and atomic rubber air blasters... I have had to use a cleaner more in 6 months on my Sony A7 and 6500 than I had to in Nikon Dslrs in years+. Cost is reasonable. So value is good since you will likely use them frequently ( one time only!).. do not believe they will harm my sensor in any way.. Have full frame and APS.. no issues either...

title: Difficult clone with several software types
text: Changing WD 1 TB HDD in HP 17.3 AMD to Samsung 870 Evo 1 TB. Samsung Data Migration froze at 99%.. Never finished... 4 attempts. Aoemi Backer Upper appears to clone but un recognized when installed x 3.. 1st attempt with Macrium 100% successful. My first SSD boot disk. Major speed improvement... worth the frustrating transition. Also boosted Ram from 8 to 24 and added on board Samsung 970 Evo M.2 SSD 250GB.. Super fast processing of Raw photos in Affinity and several Topaz Lab programs

title: Sony RX100vii case and battery pouch
text: The case slips over a SonyRX100Vii easily... a little tight when you carry an extra battery. Wish the dimensions were a little wider to accommodate 2 spare batteries (esp for this camera) Pro... outstanding padding and protection for my expensive camera Con... There is no way to attach case to a neck strap like some other neoprene cases I have. A small loop with a clip would let you pull case off and start shooting... without having to stop and figure where to put the case... like the protection bur needs better design

title: Thin neck strap for Sony Rx100Vii
text: Thick enough to be comfortable. Doesn't slide around on neck or collar.. High quality upgrade for a Sony Rx100. Secure...won't worry about losing camera because of strap failure... good deal

title: SonyRX 100 vii pluses and negatives
text: [[VIDEOID:e542662f2c48429e6826ca5fee4b65a6]] Adding this pocket camera to a larger A7R4 and 6500... has pop up viewfinder (+).. full manual and shooting modes (+). Good electronic viewfinder EVF brightness with diopter adjustments and programable display seperate from back screen(+) popup flash(+)apature or shutter speed ring on lens (+)powers up faster than a dslr(+) Shutter speed is amazing. Full range of 4K and HD video modes and special dial to program slow motion (HFR)..Slow motion video is worth it even if you never take photos. (+) F 2.8 zeiss lens... speed adjustable zoom(+) I have customized the dials and buttons to mat ch the A7. Would be nice if Sony designed the function keys the same so you could react to changes without having to pause.. open menus..etc (-) battery life is miserable...buy several...Sony brand almost $50... think about a handful of aftermarket batteries for same amount(-) shooting outdoors is amazing...indoors in low light not so good like most compact cameras... my phone does better(-) have to purchase add on grip to paste on front.. should be designed to pop off but should be standard..not accessory (-) no neck strap at this price..just a little wrist strap.. another accessory you have to buy(-) Overall.. super pleased with camera for carrying in pocket... zoom to 200mm .. RAW and JPEG complements bigger DSLRs and lenses... EVF popup is outstanding...but add the front grip and remember to get extra batteries

title: Vivofit 4 large band replacements
text: Comfortable..doesn't slide around...doesn't need to be cinched down tight. Bought a small band with the Vivofit 4.. but couldnt get it past 1st or second notch... this one is comfortable on 6th notch... with 2 hold down loops..no regrets.. the blue is a good choice

title: Never lose power if you are remote or in extreme cold
text: Added a small 12v lead acid battery with alligator clips and 12v adapter... Battery is rechargeable and will outlive hundreds of AA batteries

title: OP/TECH tripod carry straps for tripods without cases
text: Typical OP/TECH quality that I never have to worry about protecting my equipment. With a heavier tripod like a sturdy old Bogen or metal Manfrotto... the ability to use the padded shoulder strap from my camera while it rides in a case is highly practical and saves having to purchase an additional pad just for occasional use with tripods

title: Bluetooth adapter for older car radios with a cassette
text: Purchased this to enable bluetooth playback of songs on my phone to a 2005 Chevy Silverado original radio/cassette/cd. These GM factory radios have a lot of CD issues. Problem solved... no more pile of CDs to fumble with or keep in truck. In years passed I tried the hardwired cassette that would plug into headphone jack on phones... but those jacks are disappearing... and quality was never perfect. Charges up via a usb. Only con is bright flashing blue led can be distracting and you cannot tell how much charge the bluetooth cassette has left. OVERALL happy that I do not have to replace entire radio as CD is shot...

title: high quality optical glass
text: Purchased this as protective cover for Sony 100-400mm G master. There are many concerns out there that Auto Focus and sharpness can be affected by any filter. I have experimented with AF-s, AF-c...multiple focus modes and meter combinations from a tripod with this filter on and off. I cannot find anything degraded by this particular glass. I use it for insurance against accidental impact... the cost of this lens warrants the best optical quality UV... no regrets. For less expensive lenses the X2 is just fine

title: sony sd 128 gb issues
text: These cards are now being recalled/replaced...I am giving fewer stars not for the performance but for quality control. Very inconvienient...fortunately found before video read failures. SEE SONY SITE for description of issues

title: Heavy Duty gooseneck clamps
text: Great idea... but so stiff...difficult to adjust... might loosen up over time but heavy and so stiff.. wont use enough to find out how long over time will be. One positive is that it can hold a heavy reflector without sagging...Clamps super strong

title: Macro extension ring set for nikon F mount and nikon lenses
text: Snug fit to multiple DSLR Nikon bodies..clicks in. Also accurate fit with several different brands of metal reversal rings or native Nikon lens mounts. No light leakage noted only use in manual focus so cannot rate autofocus speed or reliability

title: Lensball suction cup for tripod heads
text: Exactly as pictured in description.. Would be nice to have a step up adapter for tripod legs included.. as is you will have to use tripod head. Suction seems adequate with original 80mm lensball. Would prefer suction cup to be just a bit bigger for increased grip insurance

title: 6 ft usb
text: High quality usb replacement. Reinforced neck where attaches to cables...expect will hold up well over time.. tight fit

title: 60mm tripod head leveling base
text: Bought this for leveling tripod heads when on uneven terrain requiring different leg extensions. So far have used with 2 different ball heads, gimbal and fluid manfrotto head. NO creep wih Nikon DSLR 810 and 200-500mm lens (heavy load). Quality materials and machining...no regrets... you get what you pay for..Made in U.S.A.

title: Sigma 70-200 f/2.8 sport
text: Have had a few days so far to test on a Nikon D500 and D810. The optical stabilization seems to work great and the AF is quick and responsive. The 4 attached shots were of moving objects (eagle and seaplane)..the others were shot from moving boat holding this very stout lens. I look forward to getting sharper and sharper as I learn this lens. No regrets that I did not purchase the Nikkor. I have other Sigma(Nikon) 50-100mm Art and Sony e-mount Sigma lenses... Impressed with quality and output of this amazing lens. Other reviewers have thoroughly addressed the weight and mounting ring issues. Do not seem to have and front or back focus issues with this lens on either body that require the USB dock.

title: MB-D17 power base for Nikon D500. Go with Nikon brand
text: Battery base for Nikon D500. I have owned multiple Nikon Brand units for 6 different Nikon DSLRs. THE d500 seems to run through batteries faster than my D810, D750 or 7100. The AA battery tray is a life saver. If you are out in the cold where battery life is shorter or you do time lapse... this is a necessity. I purchased a used unit.. 100% complete and mint

title: Mirrorless Camera... dont leave home without these
text: If you have a newer mirrorless camera... this us a required part of you kit now... I have a Sony A6500 and A5000... Dust on sensor is a problem on all of these setups...blower just wont do it. Have used this brand on DSLRs likr D7000,D7100, D500. THE FULL FRAME requires a different size.. Recommend.. best value

title: NIKON ROUND EYEPIECE... not for rectangular viewfinders without adaptor
text: I have always used these eye cups on my Nikons..both film and digital bodies. The adaptor that turns the rectangular eyepiece to round are not as eye friendly...too deep. The identical magnifying eyepiece is a nice accessory and since it just takes a few seconds to spin one off my D810 and transfer to D500... having one if each is all you need.. Folds flat if you wear glasses... not a required accessory...you love em or hate em... personal choice...Nikon Brand.... 1st application requires pulling ring out of supplied eyepiece... but in a minute... you are done

title: Quick and compact XQD card reader
text: Least expensive alternative I found for accessing Sony XQD card from Nikon D500... much faster than direct camrea to laptop. So far I have used as card reader 4 to 5 times per day... several days a week while I get used to my new camera. No signs of giving up at 100 + uses...but imagine spring loading will be point of failure. As noted in other reviews... is so wide that blocks second usb port on my acer laptop...but I suppose I could use an extension cable to be able to plug in an external hd to direct copy card to Hard Drive. Have the identical device for SD cards and never failed after 2 years

title: Large Not for Nikkor 16-35mm if you want hood
text: Advertised that Size Large will fit Nikkor af-s 16-35mm 1:4... it will just fit the lens but not the hood... way too small..even with hood reversed... too narrow. Overall quality is good... can use with other lenses... no way to figure what the appropriate size is for this lens with hood. A wide angle lens like this almost always needs the hood if using outside... Inconvienieced and delay in being able to protect my lens.

title: Used sold as new B&W 77mm UV-haze MRC 010M
text: Very disappointed. This is the second time I purchased a B&W filter from Amazon the came with a broken seal on box... dust on the filter glass... the plastic hinge on the filter box appears to have been opened multiple times ( the stress fractures you see on plastic hinges... and the foam was obviously disturbed. Do not have time to return as I need to use lens now. Last B&W lens I will buy from Amazon... Obviously previously opened.. optics appear ok but wont know until I can process. Has the green reflective hue shown on other negative reviews.. 77mm uv for Nikkor ultrawide angle zoom. I have been purchasing camera lenses and filters since 1969... avoid this brand from this source

title: Bare portable HD case/cover-
text: Quick assembly. Tight fit. Small blue led when powered up. Snapped 1TB bare drive together in under 5 mins. Took longer to unbox than to fit new drive. Comes with new cable (USB)

title: Protective hard case with very minimal padding to fit Sigma 16mm e-mount lens
text: Bought this for a Sigma 16mm f/1.4 Sony e-mount lens with hood. Easily fits front down with lens hood reversed.. but also closes (with a little persuasion with hood attached (lens facing up). As noted in previous reviews... it is a case... but NOT a padded case. I solved this by cutting and adding the heavy foam that comes in my B+W filters both above and below to protect lens from minor bumps. I feel safe placing a $450 lens in this case. Only down side is the outside is slippery and almost shot out of my hands... add a few rubber bands to solve this. There is also a tiny loop and mini clip... would have preferred some larger loop to enable attaching options. plenty of room on sides of lens to carry a microfiber cleaning cloth. With any bottom padding I would have rated a 4 star

title: High quality UV lens ,.. best insurance for the price
text: This is my third purchase of a Breakthrough UV filter. Super high quality glass. no flare.. ring is easy to remove. 100% satisfied x 3. Cannot tell the difference between this and much more expensive German filters I have purchased through the years. I am willing to risk my very expensive Nikon, Sigma ans Sony lenses with these... Highly recommend.. been buying and using lenses for 46 years

title: Improved Mavic Pro gimbal locking protector
text: Very tight fit... hard to quickly remove but holds tight. Had to trim some excess plastic left over from injection mold.. sharp edges on latch. Like the one step / one piece feature.

title: Sony A6500 e-mount adaptor for all Nikon lenses
text: Bought this to use my older manual Nikkor lenses with newer Sony A6500. Construction and fit are excellent. Optics suffer slightly as they used to with extension tubes on SLR bodies. Some vignetting with Wide manual lenses. Still trying to find the right mix of manual f-stops/iso/shutter speed and have better success when in 100% manual mode with the A6500. The quality of the e-mount sigma and sony lenses are so amazing... the Nikon manual lens pics are a little disappointing. I have yet to try with large heavy telephoto lenses but would never think about using this without a lens with its own tripod mount. For price... cannot beat this... want to try one of the autofocus mounts before I buy... this is a great piece to carry in your bag... you can always borrow your friends' Nikon lenses.. Will continue to evaluate over time

title: Excellent insurance for your expensive lenses
text: I have purchased several Gobe lens filters for my Nikon lenses. For the price they are an excellent choice. No flare. My last one shattered when my lens slipped out of my hands and landed on the lens cap. No damage whatsoever to lens. Perfect lens insurance and high quality. Have used CP filter over this without removing the UV ... no issues

title: Cinema filter set... Mavic Pro
text: Excellent fit on my Mavic Pro with no interference with gimbal movement when placed properly. Take some stills and short clips to learn how to adjust camera settings.. These are not just standard ND filters... Know what you are purchaseing

title: Snowkids 6' braided USB to C cable pros and cons
text: Upgrading review Pros: The braided cable is a big plus for preventing flexing. The rubber collar at the connectors should prevent premature breakage. The length is a major advantage for charging ...(super advantage when traveling...think airports and hotel rooms)... and I am still able to perform both data and file transfers with a Galaxy S8+ without issue. Cons: reason for downgrading from 5 stars... The Larger rectangular USB connector is loose in my Acer laptop ports with some wiggle that causes loss of connection. If you could scale tightness of fit on a scale of 1-10 I'd give these a "6". Fitment with my supplied Samsung charging block is nice and tight (a "10"). Also nice and tight . Several other USB cables and external devices I use with the same computer USB ports are tight and without problems... USB works fine but I have to check the connection to ensure contact.ection. So.. if you just want to use for charging from a Samsung or other charging devices this is a great cable. If you need a tight fit on an Acer laptop for file transfers... I would be attentive. Frequently loses contact in the middle of large image file transfers Snowkids (vendor) immediately responded to my concerns and shipped me replacements. 5 stars for customer service and standing behind product. Second cables are a bit tighter.. Would give a 4.5 if possible

title: Phantom 4 friendly backpack
text: Purchased this based on amazon reviews. The bag arrived with a small zipper defect and Lykus immediately responded to me and quickly sent out a replacement. Bag holds my P4P.. batteries(In li-po safety covers)..prop bag .. landing pad...filters..cables.. controller and 7" Crystalsky. If I was traveling I could probably find a way to fit charger instead of rain cover. Backpack is well padded in shoulders, back pads and shoulder/waist straps. The shoulder straps will fit a large person comfortably with adequate room to fit over a large coat. The rain cover is a nice addition. The waist strap is clearly designed for a thin waist-ed person. I was able to easily find 1.5" male and female buckles to make a waist extender. If a pair of extra buckles was included it would have earned a 5 from me. rubber feet on bottom are nice feature. Would easily fit in overhead bin on a full size aircraft. On a regional commuter where you have to turn over your carry-on bags... I would have to pick a different bag.

title: Hero5 metal cage with 52mm Front filter
text: Excellent heavy duty metal protection for housing and lens (Hero5). Best features are screw on filters that you can use from your DSLR or old 35mm cameras (52mm). There is a flash type attachment that enables the addition of LED panel lights or a mic. Only downside is that it is little difficult to quickly remove my camera without removing the side screw.. which almost always falls out and I have to push on the front screen to remove which I would prefer not to do. On tripod or mounted securely makes amazing time-lapse vids

title: P4P DJI protector caps when propellers removed
text: Perfect fit on P4P and no interference with original foam case

title: Nikon D810 compatable 64 GB card
text: Bought for use in a Nikon 810.. thought I was done with CF cards as the last ones I bought were for a D200 and S5 Pro. Biggest I ever used was 8 GB and never meant to record video . Relying on Amazon ratings to make this purchase. Handling RAW and video just fine as far as I can tell. Do not use for hours a day so cannot speak to the heating issues mentioned in another review but handles cold of Alaska fine this winter. Never had any Lexar CF cards fail so far

title: Quality protection at resonable price for Nikkor 24-120mm VR Lens
text: Bought for use as protective filter for use with new Nikkor 24-120mm 1.4 VR Lens.. No distortion with ED lens.. good fit.. reasonable price.. no issues with quality

title: B+W xs-pro CP filter
text: B+W filter used with Panasonic Lumix FZ-1000 on outside of permanent UV filter. Minimal f-stop loss in this set up. Excellent clarity. Have not experienced any flare or glare issues. I have added and removed this from another high quality filter (Hoya) with absolutely no sticking issues. Lens cap hold on tightly even with thin profile. Surface easy to clean. Never disappointed with B+W

title: Arca plate adapter
text: This is an absolute irreplaceable accessory if you have manfrotto-type quick release plates on one tripod and arca-type plates on your camera or most ball heads. Can now jump from one tripod head to another without having to change plates. Well made. Ready for anything ...or a friend's tripod/monopod if you forgot yours.. So pleased I bought 2.. One lives in my glove box

title: FX D750 satisfies all my needs... pick this based on what you want this camera to do... Else buy the 500
text: I have owned 2 D100s, 1 Fuji/Nikon S5-Pro, a D300, D7000 and a D7100... Plus a few F2,3,4s and some in-betweens. I chose this over the 500... I am down to taking pics of Eagles, Bears and Whales... Have been experimenting daily for about a month. Have yet to have any quality or focus issues. 100% satisfied with the features, speed, dynamic range and finally I get to use all of those beautiful glass lenses I've accumulated since my first purchase in 1972.... Almost didn't buy another DSLR with all of the awesome 1" bridge cameras out there... but each tool has it's own special use. Look forward to some studio lighting/portrait setups... Still doesn't touch the Fuji S5 on people in my humble opinion... Solidly built. Using almost exclusively with the Nikkor 200-500mm and a Sigma 50-100mm (Dx) and it is smart enough to go FX or DX based on which lens you attach... so don't hesitate if you are loaded with DX lenses. I understand the Knobs and dials... that has been a harder transition for some reviewers... Time and practice fixes that. Don't use the articulated screen on something this big.. but one day with a little lens I might. For video I use a Lumix FZ1000... Didn't buy this for video...

title: BRASS step up ring Luzid
text: Top quality metal step up ring.. no problem separating a B+W and a Hoya and a Vivitar filter without a wrench.. Took a very long time to arrive... but that's an Amazon issue... Would purchase other rings without concern. Brass>Aluminum>plastic in my humble opinion Came in the same type of plastic case a quality filter would arrive in and an additional fancy box.. Can't beat that

title: Arca-Type Plate.. Breakthrough Photography
text: This is one of several item I have purchased from Breakthrough Photography. The quality and value are quite good. I am especially impressed with an ND filter and find it as good as any Hoya or B+W at significantly less $$. I have purchased 2 of these Arca-type plates. They fit perfectly in my Sirui 30x and 40x ball heads and support a Nikon D750 securely. For big telephoto lenses I would go with a longer plate, but I did put it on a Sigma 50-100mm Art lens and felt 100% secure that my rig would be secure. I also used it with a lighter camera/lens in one of those Manfrotto to Arca adaptors ...Beautiful fit. As long as screw is tightened.. the rubber/silicone pads keep the camera from moving.. I always give it a wiggle... take it off and tighten a little more then forget about it. Great follow-up from vendor asking if any problems.

title: Sigma f/1.8 50-100mm exceptional.. no regrets
text: This is truly a beautiful lens.The soft depth of field is amazing wide open. I have had a chance to use it on my Fuji S5 Pro, a Nikon D7100... but I am most happy with the results I'm getting on my Nikon D750. There is an intelligent mode that allows the camera to identify a Dx lens and use a crop factor that eliminates the vignetting. If I only had a full frame sensor, I would still consider this lens (nothing you can't fix with a little cropping and processing) So far I have not had any focus issues that would require the re-programming puck. I don't leave home without a tripod. The mono pod in this "kit" is more like a selfie stick... Not something I will ever use. I would use a heavier Manfrotto mono pod for more stability with a combo this heavy. The Vivitar filter kit is adequate.. but I have upgraded to a Hoya CPL as I believe a lens like this should get a high quality filter. It also works flawlessly with a Kenko1.4x DGX teleconvertor with just a slight loss of f-stop. The quality is beyond what I expected...already thinking about another Sigma Art lens in the wide angle arena. For a big tele I will stick with my Nikkor lenses vs the Sigma.

title: Nest Traveller Tripod Legs... 100% satisfaction all around
text: I started out using a Manfrotto 324RC2 light duty grip ball head (the side grip joystick) with a Fuji S5pro and Sigma 50-100mm Art lens. Not sure of the total weight, but did not notice any flexing or leg slippage once set. Once I changed over to my Nikon D750 w/ 200-500mm...I felt a little less secure that this was the right setup. Anything smaller (video camera, Lumix fz200, spotting scope ,etc) I am 100% confident in these legs. Not really fond of that particular tripod head but was all I had when the legs arrived. Big problem was that it would not fold back neatly because of the design of the head.... So, having recently purchased a Sirui K40x for my super heavy Bogen legs, I was so wowed by that head that I bought a smaller Sirui head k30x . I could not be more pleased with the function of either. I'd never heard of this brand or seen one, but took a chance based on the first few reviews. Really like the hook at bottom.. Never been a fan of the twist locks, but I can change. Only other CF I have is a small Monopod for traveling in a suitcase. I have no regrets ... I got a quality product.. Light and strong. Don't think I'll ever pull the leg off for a monopod, but it's nice to know it's there if I need to splint a leg or need a walking stick. Have yet to try it on a sandy beach... that will be the ultimate test for me. Have always used heavy aluminum pods that are easy to disassemble and clean from sand and salt water. Will update if find issues later

title: Sirui K-40x Ball Head Outstanding Quality/Value for Rock Solid results
text: I was looking to purchase a gimbel head for a Nikon D750/Nikkor 200-500mm lens that was rock solid with my older heavy duty Bogen 3011 legs. A salesperson at Pro-Photo in Portland guided me over to this and I was wowed at first sight. Sitting next to the $400 ball heads I could immediately see the quality and value at about 30% of the cost. That translates to me as part of another lens or a few B&W filters. I have also recently paired a Fuji S5Pro body and Sigma 50-100mm Art lens. Both of these combos are just too heavy to get tack sharp shots handheld... and my attempts with a heavy mono-pod have been ok.. but less than perfect. This is not a tripod head/leg combo I envision carrying on my next vacation or on a hike through the mountains... I am 60 and have been buying and using tripods since I was 15. I believe in the heaviest tripod I can carry when I'm shooting photos out at 300-500mm and further. When I pop a spotting scope on and try and track targets out at 300-400-500 yards, a solid, pin point image saves a whole lot of walking. There is always a little creep with that last twist to maximum tightness...but once you get the hang of the tension wheel... I have yet to see my focus point move even slightly when locked in on an eagle nest for 10 days. As with other reviews I find the panning a little stiff... but if I was filming and airshow or Indy Race I'd probably put on a fluid video head instead. I anticipate many years of service and it will still be working long after I am. Today I ordered a Sirui K-30 from Amazon because while the K-20 is probable adequate for a D300 and D7100 with smaller lenses... who knows what I will come to own in the future... That's the one I'll carry to Hawaii with the light carbon-fiber legs. There is a great review on DPREVIews called Battle of the Titans.. Excellent quality with the bonus of an outstanding price point. I also have a lightweight Sirui carbon mono-pod that travels in my suitcase. 5 stars because the pros overwhelm the small cons.. I can live with those George B Sitka, Alaska

title: Nikkor replacement rear caps.. tight fit
text: Nikon lens rear caps ... note the color will be hard to leave behind. Loose for the first quarter turn then grabs tight and have not fallen off Nikkor lenses. Have not tries with Tamron or Sigma Nikon lenses for correctness of fit.. Would not hesitate buy again. Like the different colors... will order more in a different hue for my older Ai/AIS lenses

title: Best case for a Nikon 200-500mm Lens and body
text: After reading several reviews... I chose this to carry a Nikkor 200-500mm Lens on a D750. A little snug but camera stays on the lens. Good shoulder strap. A clip on the flap and 2 side zippers. Very pleased with the side padding... maybe 4 stars for bottom padding. The lens hood makes it a little snug. Arca plates stay on tripod collar and camera and combo still fits. To be honest I do not think it would fit well if the battery extension were on body but I have not attempted that yet (too heavy for me to hold)...... no room for any other accessories... Don't think there are any other real options that hold this lens and camera. Lots of room with the d750 and a Sigma 50-100mm Art. The Ape Case is huge, but I feel my lens is as well protected as the old Nikon black solid tubes... which unfortunately are no longer offered

title: B & W ND filter 0.9
text: I have been using B&W filters for over 40 years. I have yet to be disappointed. This is at the very bottom of the ND filter range... Color is unaffected. Coating is very easy to clean. Auto Focus is not affected at this level. Stacks with a similar sized Hoya CP filter for beautiful effect. Comes apart easily... not so for $20 filters.. If you don't lose this ( like I have over the years)... It is a lifetime investment. Spend the extra dollars to get the best quality outcome. Nikon and Sigma lens caps fit securely. So pleased with this one just ordered a 10 stop ND

title: Nikkor 35-70mm replacement HB1 type Lens hood
text: I bought this to replace a long lost Nikon Hood for a Nikkor 35-70mm Lens. Fits as good as the original ( at a considerably more attractive price) for something I only occasionally use. Good job Pixco

title: Hot shoe protectors (pair)
text: Snug fit on D750 and D7100 but a good way to protect the flash shoe with a bonus bubble in case you are not on a tripod. If you lose one, the cost makes it worth buying some more

title: Quality step up ring.. Solid threads
text: Have used this with both a Hoya and B&W 77mm metal ringed filter with no threading or un-threading issues. The 62mm threads appear to be quite compatible with 2 separate Nikkor lenses. I am at the point where it is much more economical to buy a big filter and drop it down rather than having to buy multiple CPL and NDs

title: Hot Shoe levels x2
text: Protects flash shoe and saves having to work with tripod levels.. Seem to fit just fine... nice enhancement. Self explanatory how they work

title: Replacement Body Caps for Nikon digital and film bodies
text: Nice tight fit on a D200, Fuji S5 pro, D7100 and a few other film cameras. As good a fit as O.E.M. Value for price excellent.. hard to lose in this color

title: Nikon lens - Rear Cap replacements
text: Works perfectly on multiple Nikon and Sigma and Tamron lenses.. O.E.M. caps are my choice for an expensive investment like a lens.. The after market body caps are ok...but I have also found them to be too tight and occasionally too loose(fall off)... these are worth the money

title: 52 mm replacement lens covers
text: Price is excellent value for 4 pinch caps.. so far I have not found a new or old Nikkor lens (with and without) filters that it did not stay on. If you don't want the cap keepers... don't apply them... They do stay attached as good as any others I have tried. As good as O.E.M. at a fraction of the price ... unless you insist on having a brand name in silver on the face

title: Nikon D750 battery pack/grip MB-D16
text: Learned a long time ago that only a Nikon battery grip should be used with a Nikon. You really do get what you pay for.. No easily broken latches. Quality matches that of the camera. Vertical buttons and controls work when you need them. Each model 7000,7100,D750 requires a unique grip. Ergonomics and balance are great with the deeper grip of the d750. AA batteries add a little more weight, but for multiple long exposures and big jobs... no question you need one of these. Pops off easily when not needed. Add this with a 200-500mm lens and you do not need to carry a firearm in the woods... just swing this setup and you could drop a bear in his tracks... or at least scare him off. GB Sitka,AK

title: Poloroid Nikon DSLR corded shutter remote
text: Shutter release, interval timer... lock for B- mode.. All of the features I was looking for. No need to stand in front of camera like mini remote fob. As with other reviews... not sure why no power off switch... Cord and plug seem well made. Works fine on a new Nikon D750 and a 7100. Very good value at this price

title: Olympus LED Light Guide
text: Macro light ring powered by camera's led flash in constant mode. No real substitute for a good ring when getting so close that you shadow out the object.. but quality of light drops off significantly more than 6" away. Fortunately the TG-2 and 3 have amazing macro capabilities that I have never experienced in any other P&S camera. An expensive accessory... but worth it if you keep it with you. Remember you have to take it off to use the camera flash. It needs to come with a small protective pouch that can clip on strap and stay close but out of the way

title: 5" blue zip ties
text: Great price for this package of 5+ inch zip ties. Since it is often necessary to have a variety of sizes, this is a great size package at the price. Don't want 500 and 25 are not enough to have on hand for a bigger project. So far holding tight when applied with zip tie gun.

title: ePhoto ac swivel light holder E27
text: Bought for rather light LED spot lights. Mounts securely on light pole. Convenient switch on rear of unit. If mounting high it would probably be better to have in line power cord switch. Does not hold heavier CFL bulbs without a little slipping. Perfect for light to medium duty. Would not rely on for daily or professional use... I bought several and am satisfied that they are good for what they promise

title: Battery analyzer...outstanding features
text: The charger/analyzer works exactly as advertised. The included C-Cell and D-cell AA adapters are a nice bonus. Helps to identify if one of your batteries is not well matched to others by mAH or charge... I would highly recommend . Have used to test multiple brands of 1200, 1600, 1800 and 2200 mAH batteries UPDATE: 5+ years later and still working flawlessly...

title: Versitile multipurpose clamp for ContourHD and GoPro Hero cams
text: Have used this clamp with both a ContourHD camera (with and without waterproof case). Also have begun using with a GoPro Hero Camera and Tripod mount. These products are ideally suited for each other! I have used in aircraft, boat and recently on a stick to extend the camera down into the water for camera to eyeball view of fish. The pad popped off once and popped right back on. Solid construction... If I break one... I'll keep buying them... but so far looks like it was money well spent for a product that will last a long time. Only thing missing is a micro level or bubble.. that would make level images easier in the video world. I would not travel without this amazing tool.

title: Waterproof for snorkeling
text: Took this case with my ContourHD for Snorkeling in Hawaii. Not sure I agree with the postings that say you do NOT have to have switch in "ON/REC" position BEFORE you place in housing. Mine would not record with magnetic switch of waterproof housing UNLESS camera was first in REC mode before placing inside case. Stayed completely dry on 2 of 3 adventures where it was continuously submerged for 30 mins each time. On the 3rd trip I accidentally snagged part of the mask strap when I closed the case. 30 secs later the case leaked...Contour let out a continuous high pitched tone and would not turn off... Battery shorted... camera dead... card ok. Not wanting to spoil my trip I could only find a GoPro Hero cam as replacement... Not even close to the underwater shots available with the Contour. No way to mount a Hero on the side of your head (Mask) without a helmet! Used a wrist strap with Hero...very awkward as arms move more than heads... Contour captures what you look at naturally with less vertigo from watching the video. For diving or snorkel I would always opt for the Contour and this case (less that 10 Meters of course)

title: Nice clock, eay to operate and use. Bright green light that shows the time/date. Def a worthwhile purchase.
text: I read so many things about this clock I did not know what to expect. Some said cheaply made, some said worse and I will tell you what I go. I got a nice looking clock with everything I was looking forward to. Bright snooze light, easy to use buttons that do what they say they will, easy to read and operate, nice beeping alarm etc. It was easy to set up with the date and time and alarm time viewable. Big numbers that see and a handy feature I never have seen before.. there is cool green light that illuminates the time even when you are not hitting the snooze/light button that is on all the time and you can turn it off too if you choose. This makes it nice at night if you wake up you can tell the time... it is dim but bright enough to see. If I had to say one thing slightly negative is that one of the pads on the clock bottom has slightly come off when I was setting up the time, but there seemed to be enough glue left on it and I stuck it back on with no worries. If that is the worse thing I have seen I will take it, truth be told little padding or not you did not need them anyway. I like this clock a lot and would buy another in a heartbeat.

title: Hardware does not work - don't wast your money.
text: The original dac+ board comes with (4) standoffs, (4) screws that go into one end of the standoff, (4) nuts that go on the other end of the stand offs - all work fine. Notice (4). This kit comes with (2) standoffs that are too short (one with no threads), (2) standoffs that are too long, (2) short round head screws, (2) short flat machine screws, (2) long screws ~1+ inches. The boards, boxes all have (4) holes or threaded sites. I could find no way that worked (including using the original standoffs from the DAC+ kit) with this set of parts. There were no directions, but that is not the even the main issue. Any configuration of parts for this kit should have (4) of what ever is needed to connect the items together. Pic shows the hardware that was sent. Returning for refund. *** suggestion to the manufacturer: there is a much simpler way to do this. Look at your step 1. Put (4) standoffs in vs 2 and make them long enough so the Dac+ board does not bend. Now PI board is anchored to the base. Then put the DAC+ board on the (4) standoffs. Screw ((4) standoffs through the DAC+ board holes into the standoffs that you just put in. Now you have both boards secured and 4 open screw holes in the top standoffs to secure the case top with (4) short screws. Simple and likely you could have all standoffs the same.

title: Love that they are wireless but...
text: I was so excited to get these to avoid all the wires. The set up was easy and cameras work well, but one camera is not working well with the night vision/infrared. I think it has a flaw. It works fine in the day. I will be contacting customer service and hope that I can get a replacement. I purchased them in March and just set them up about 3 weeks ago, so the return window has ended. The faulty one is located in the house and worked fine for a few days, very clear with lights on and good enough when they are off, but now shows dark at night even with lights on. You cannot see any images and only a bit of light at the bulb when it is turned on. All of the others work fine. I purchases two complete systems with 2 cameras each, one for me and the other for my mom. They do take some time to adjust and like most others users said, there is a delay before the actual recording starts when there is movement whether by people, vehicle or otherwise, regardless of the angle. I am just hoping that if something happens, like a break in, that I do not miss the actual time of the initial event. I am hoping that there will be a fix soon for the lag in recording time. They are very sensitive and it is annoying getting alerts in 1 minute intervals when an insect is buzzing around the camera or if the wind blows and moves the trees on the one I have at the front of the house. I have adjusted the sensitivity but it still picks up the slightest movement. The other issue is that if the one I have with the fixed mounts, it is not possible to plug in my outdoor charger cord, since where the camera screws into the mount blocks the charger port, so I have to unscrew it to charge. I will update at a later time.

title: About what I expected for the price
text: I'm a broke audiophile so I had to settle for something cheap as my PC speakers were gacking. These seemed like the best solution overall for the lowest price. They are about what I expected. I would recommend them for people in a similar position: If you need cheap speakers but $9.99 ones are going to drive you insane and break your audiophile heart, and headphones hurt your ears and restrict your movement. These aren't good, but for cheap basic PC speakers I can tolerate them until I have the funds to upgrade.

title: Very portable, powerful volume
text: We're working on a cabin project with a partner out in the desert and music is a must. This speaker is very useful for us. It fits in my purse and a tiny corner of a work bench when in use. It has paired with and connected immediately with my Pixel 7Pro, a Pixel 4A, and one of the more recent Galaxy phones. The volume output is surprisingly robust for the size. We can hear all around the work site and music is clean from the speaker. We play a mix of mostly country, 80s music and some Tejano - nothing really with high bass. And the occasional audiobook or podcast sounds clear as well.

title: Fit is a smidge tight
text: My old kindle cover was getting worn and this one has the prop on it, so I was happy to try it out. The case does fit properly and all the buttons are easily accessible and work. However, when you push the interior flap in to hold the Kindle in place it's a bit too thick. What happens is the front cover doesn't lie completely flat and that interferes with the sleep function. I'm hoping with use, the material will soften and this problem will resolve.

title: Works perfectly on Xbox Game Pass
text: I'm not a "gamer" by any means, but I do enjoy playing some games via the Xbox Game Pass now and then. We don't have a console or physical games, just the online streaming option through our Samsung tv. However, you still need a real controller for this option. I chose the Luna over a regular Xbox controller simply because of the lower cost and the Luna was already listed as a compatible option on our TV. The controller paired with the TV quickly via Bluetooth and connects easily every time I go to play. The buttons all work immediately with almost zero delay and I haven't experienced any problems with any games. It is comfortable to hold and not quite as heavy as my old Xbox controller was.

title: Elegant simplicity
text: I really like this sleeve. The hunter green is classic and the design is simple. Walking into a boardroom with this definitely sets a different tone than a big bulky sleeve or just your computer. My 14" Dell fits exactly right and the sleeve closes easily.

title: Works, but better options are out there
text: I bought two other replacement remotes for our Frame tv after the puppy ate the original. One was completely garbage, but the second one paired up and has worked perfectly for months. This one was meant to be a back up to the back up remote since the pupper is still a pupper. However, I think I'll just stick to brand on the other one and not use this one. The buttons take longer to get a response from and sometimes it skips forward two selections with a single press on the selection button. Additionally, I have no clue what rakuten is and that same button on the original and the good replacement remotes is reserved for the Samsung Free TV app. And that's what I want instant access to from the remote. Everything else I want is an app - Netflix, HBOmax, Paramount, Hulu, Prime etc.

title: Good for small rooms
text: I'm using this sound bar with a 55" tv in a normal size bedroom. The TV's speakers are actually pretty good, but for some reason the volume had begun to fluctuate unexpectedly. This sound bar corrected that issue - I've used the ARC connection via an HDMI cable and no more sudden loud spurts while watch a movie. The overall sound quality from the bar is decent. I mean, this not a famous brand or high end unit, but it is suitable for movies and tv shows in the bedroom. The unit connected quickly and has a separate remote. My Samsung TV remote recognized this bar so I don't need to use the separate remote control at all.

title: Comfortable, clean sound
text: These are surprisingly comfortable and that's directly related the selection of different sized ear pieces. The physical buttons are easier to use than a phone only or touch sensitive only controls. Using these earbuds for audiobooks or music while outside doing chores is nice. The sound is crisp and clear even when my phone is 20 feet away. The noise cancelling feature works reasonably well when I'm out in the wind too.

title: Great for traveling
text: I wanted a light, inexpensive set of earbuds for traveling. Something that lets me do a Zoom meeting on my phone or just listen to music or an audio book on the go. These are reasonably comfortable and paired easily with both my Pixel and Note 20 phones. The sound quality id perfectly fine for my needs and if I lose this set, it's not a big deal. The battery life 2as still above 50% after a little over an hour.

title: Works with the Frame tv
text: Our puppy ate the original white solar powered remote for my 6 month old 55" Frame television. I have a different brand and style replacement that works, but doesn't have the pre-programmed channel buttons for Netflix, Prime and Samsung TV. I really like those instant buttons. This remote uses 2 batteries and the back slides off to change them. Except....it's such a tight fit it was nearly impossible to remove. That's the only negative I've found over two weeks of use. The remote did need to pair with the TV within seconds and everything worked immediately. The voice search is fine and Alexa still responds properly. The volume and channel toggles operate smoothly. It's a good replacement.

title: Works with The Frame
text: Our much loved puppy ate the expensive remote that came with my fancy Frame tv. Lesson learned for me while she's still learning her manners. Amazingly, this generic remote control actually paired with the TV via Bluetooth on the very first try. And it works! The volume, channel, pause/play, power, and settings buttons all do exactly what the original remote did. This one requires regular batteries rather than using a solar charge. However, the rechargeable batteries are doing well so far.

title: Useful and strong
text: We keep zip ties all over the ranch, the trucks, my office.... useful in a ton of situations. I even carry two in my saddle bags for emergency bridle repairs in the back country. These are holding up well so far. We used them to attach a privacy screen to a section of the fence to create more shade. The zip ties have held up in 30mph winds this week.

title: Charges fully
text: I have a set of 8 rechargeable batteries for the various tv remotes and the temperature monitor in our RV. My old charger had begun to take 8 hours or more to recharge 4 batteries at once. I thought maybe the batteries were getting old, but this unit charged them in just 3 hours. So it's definitely working better than the old one and my batteries are still functional.

title: Cables work
text: I'm just using these for a television and sound bar. They are working correctly and the sound bar functions now. I think these are pricey for my simple needs.

title: Next to useless
text: After a week, I am giving up on this sound bar and going back to my tv speakers. It worked well for 24 hours and then began to have glitches. The optic connection is ok, but the included cable is loose and doesn't want to stay out. The outlet plug is huge and the cord is short - there's no reason for that. Mostly though, the remote and overall functionality is driving me nuts. The power buttons on the remote do not work at all. I have to manually turn on the sound bar with a button on the side. If I pause a show and walk away for more than 4 minutes, the sounds shuts itself off. It doesn't restart when you hit play. The sound quality is ok, but actually not any better than my Samsung Frame TV speakers.

title: Beautiful matte screen is so easy to see
text: We have a high end Sony 55" in the living room and a sub three hundred buck off brand tv in the guest room and the difference between the two is instantly noticeable - image quality and sound are in two different lanes entirely. This Samsung Frame is in the master bedroom and I am in love. The matte screen means almost no reflective glare at night with lights on in the bedroom. That's something I did not realize bothered me about our other two tvs until there was no more glare. No matter where I look at the screen, it's clear and I don't see the reflection of my bedside lamp. This tv does weigh more than the other two we own in the same size. I would definitely not try to move this or wall mount it alone. The box has a complete wall mount ready to install, but I don't want this that high since it's a bedroom television, so we installed the feet and set it on a table. This also comes with an old school box for connections rather than just plugging everything in directly to the television. That's a little old school, but it makes sense because they intended for the tv to be used on the wall as an art display as well and you don't want visible cables hanging off that. As far as the art viewing goes, that's really nice if you are willing to pay for the subscription. I am not, but viewing the samples is pretty cool. This is a Google and Alexa friendly voice control set up and I do like that. The free Samsung TV app is very nice - it's sort of like Pluto TV, but proprietary to this television brand. Lots of free channels and a ton of choices at no cost. We use Netflix, Prime, HBOMax, and Paramount Plus as our paid streaming options - no cable or satellite here, just streaming. Everything works seamlessly and smoothly. My favorite thing here though, is so simple and small and I can't understand why every tv doesn't have this - the remote control is SOLAR powered!! No more buying batteries and it works well.

title: Comfortable, easy to customize
text: My old smart watch was much loved, but after two years, it stopped charging all together and I needed a new one. This one is a smidge bigger over all, but easier to see. I primarily use it for tracking steps, tracking sleep and the time at a glance. The sleep monitor is pretty accurate and let you see how much REM sleep vs light you're getting each night as long as you're wearing the watch of course. The corresponding app on my phone shows the week or month info as well. The pedometer seems to be lagging a bit when compared to another one we have - one of them is off. I have not set this watch up to do text messages, call notifications or to control music from it - you can do that, I just don't need all that when my phone is already in my pocket. However, connecting this watch to the app via my Samsung Note 10 was easy and relatively painless. I do love that I was able to customize the display so show a photo of my dog on the face and just the time & date. I don't need the other info all crammed into one screen. You can easily scroll through the watch menu for any data you need. So far, it's survived daily wear out in the desert, in my office, at home with the dogs and out riding horses.

title: Holds a 55" tv
text: This is a decent tv stand. It's actually a little ugly and fragile, but it works. I would never use this in the living room because it looks cheap. However, as a guest room tv stand, it's fine. It took about 40 minutes to put together and it seems stable. If you've got little kids or rowdy pets, this probably isn't the best choice....it is fragile and not heavy.

title: Heavy for a portable item
text: I have a Samsung View 17" tablet that I dearly love. However, typing on the keyboard isn't always the fastest way to write a real document. This wireless keyboard solves that problem and I can work anywhere at all since my tablet has a cell signal SIM card. This keyboard works just fine with the Android ecosystem and for my basic Word and Excel needs, it's been just fine. I will say this is heavier than I expected - a lot heavier, but the price point is very friendly and makes up for the weight.

title: Little bubbles on one end
text: Overall, this is a decent enough screen protector as long as you are not driven crazy seeing a few small bubbles. It fits properly and the screen on the tablet is responsive - no noticeable degradation in screen sensitivity. However, there are four small bubbles on the bottom right corner that just will not vanish.

title: Easy to use, definitely help cool
text: These are actually useful and easy to set up. My Dell laptop sits up 9n these comfortably and doesn't wobble even with fast typing. I did notice that my laptop was cooler than usual even after 2 hours of constant use while working on a project today.

title: Very useful
text: We use zip ties way more often than one might expect. These are holding up a sign at the main ranch gate until my husband gets around to re-welding a corner. And I have used them to stabilize water buckets in the horse trailer without any breakage.

title: Sturdy, fully maneuverable
text: I have a 43 inch smart TV in my office for use as both a Zoom teleconference monitor and a TV when needed. We mounted it high on the wall so it's out of the way when not in use. This mount worked perfectly and is sturdy. I'm not worried about the tv falling. We had to buy specific bolts and a new bit to install the mount - my wall is cinder block behind paneling rather than having traditional drywall and wood studs. The mount lets the tv sit flat against the wall or pull out, tilt and angle in multiple directions depending on my needs. I can have a board meeting or public meeting with 15 people and the tv can be angled precisely so everyone has a clear view.

title: Sporadic shutdowns, good for short recordings
text: I'm not thrilled with this recorder. Even fully charged, we experienced sporadic shutdowns and having to turn it back on at least 4 times in a single one hour meeting. My unit seems to want to record for about 10 to 14 minutes at most and then shuts down. If that's all your doing, recording a short conversation, this is probably fine. If you need something to backup a board meeting or something important, this should not be your first choice.

title: Fast Charging on two different phones
text: Nice extra charging cables for the office. They work well and don't get hot. My Pixel phone shows fast charging with these and an older Samsung did the same. My new Samsung Note shows regular charging speed which is perfectly acceptable.

title: Long battery, reasonable sound
text: These are comfortable enough for my uses and the overall sound quality for music is fine. I am using these out hiking or while working around the barn on chores. The addition of a memory card is certainly useful when you don't want your phone nearby for a bluetooth music link - like when you're cleaning water troughs. Calls are fuzzy though and that was with both a Pixel 5 and a Note 20 phone, so it's the headset rather than the phones or connections. That's not really a deal breaker for me though.

title: Working properly
text: This is a sturdy surge protector with lots of outlets. The USB plugs work and charge at a reasonable rate - not super fast, but not mindnumbingly slow either.

title: Very functional
text: This has been super useful for meeting minutes for a community program. The tablet is light, fits in a handbag and comes on quickly. The Office apps work seamlessly with the Microsoft 365 subscription. We can access the meeting minutes file from two weeks earlier in a few clicks as well as Auto save the current file.

title: Comfortable size for typing
text: Our secretary needed a light tablet for minutes at board meetings, but not a big old laptop. Something dedicated to just this task. So I got the new Fire tablet with Office 365 and this keyboard. (Saved a couple hundred bucks and solved the problem) The keyboard is sturdy and connects with zero drama. It just works like they say it will. The keys are big enough to actually type like normal - no hunting and pecking. So far we've all been pleased.

title: The cards just work
text: I bought two of these 128gig cards. One is in my new Note 20 phone and the other is in a new Fire tablet. The cards fit properly and seem to be working correctly.

title: Fits a Dell 2 in 1
text: I love the deep turquoise color of this bag. It doesn't look like anyone else's boring black laptop bag. My new Dell 14" 2 in 1 fits comfortably with a little bit of room left. There's space for the charger and my random nonsense like a little notebook and pen and a snack.

title: Fit well, decent sound & connection
text: These are inexpensive earbuds that actually work well for basic stuff. The buds do fit in my ears without pressure or pain after an hour. I primarily listen to audiobooks and 80s Rock or Country music, so I don't know or care about a lot of bass. For my needs, these are working well. I've only connected them to a Pixel phone and the range is about 20 feet line of sight before I notice any degradation of the connection.

title: More powerful than expected
text: I'm quite surprised by the power in this little blower. It has a knob to dial the strength up or down as needed. I've used this to clean out multiple fans and the storage compartments under our travel trailer. It really got the dust off the fan blades - we've noticed a significant performance improvement from all 5 fans. Since it's rechargeable, this definitely beats using those compressed air cans.

title: Fits perfectly, slightly thick
text: I have this cover and a different one that I like a lot. There are a couple of differences between them, but both work and fit correctly on my 10th generation Kindle. This one is a little thicker than my other case and that's noticable after reading for a long stretch of time. The magnet holds it closed and puts the Kindle to sleep like it should. This case is a decent option for protection.

title: Fits 10th gen perfectly
text: I updated my Kindle after my 8th generation version stopped connecting to the internet. That meant a new case as well. This one has a cute booth them and is easier to spot in a room than a plain black cover. It fits perfectly and the sleep cover does as it should - turns off the screen and reactivates it when opened.

title: Great replacement cord
text: Our Siamese cat is the devil. I walked in to see him wrapped up in my phone charger cord, happily killing it. He chewed it in 3 places.... because cat things. This cord works well with the charging block that came with my phone. My phone does the fast charge with this cord.

title: No English instructions, broken charger
text: Good grief. This thing is pretty bad. It came with instructions in 2 Asian languages, but nothing in English. The app looks sketchy as well. This is supposed to have a built in charging point that you insert to charge. I don't know what it inserts into though. It does not fit in any of the USB chargers that I own. It also looks like the attached piece is damaged. Maybe it was supposed to come with a port and didn't. Bottom line is I can't use this thing at all.

title: Fine for audiobooks
text: I listen to audiobooks through the day whenever possible. I have a pair of wireless earbuds and wired versions. But my wireless get staticky once they reach a 50% charge level and that drives me nuts. These are comfortable to wear and the sound quality is fine for books and basic music. Mostly though, the sound does not deteriorate as the battery discharges.

title: Works with a 32 inch tv
text: I'm using this with a 32 inch tv and it's working quite well. It installed easily enough - it did take two of us since it's attached to a ceiling. The drop is adjustable to some degree so you find the best height for your space. The entire thing tilts and swivels so you can move the tv for whatever your sitting arrangement needs to be. I'm happy so far and this got our tv off a table and out of the way.

title: Gorgeous picture, full rich sound, easy to set up
text: After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television. First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important. The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one. We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen. But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.

title: Sketchy app and overall poor construction
text: I'm not a fan of sketchy apps from companies no one has ever heard of. I installed this on a burner phone first and got a warning with it. No thank you. Additionally, the antenna snapped off before we could even install the thing. I'm not inclined to hardwire this when it's so poorly made on the exterior - who knows how bad the internal wiring actually is.

title: Just right for audio books
text: I'm working on a long term volunteer project in deep West Texas in 2 different state parks. I find myself spending long periods of time working alone, away from the public and my Audible books are a joy on those days. I have wireless bluetooth ear buds of course, but the recharging is an issue if I'm out in the back country. So I always carry a pair of corded buds as backup.....and I inevitably lose them. Often.
