title: Works just fine. Don't see any big difference from my 50-mile antenna
text: I didn't want to review this until I'd had a chance to use it for a while. We cut the cord on cable a few years ago, and went to antenna and a smart tv. The antenna I was using had a 50-mile radius. This one makes claims of 180 miles. I placed it next to my other antenna. I have a very large tree fairly close to the bedroom window, so I do have some difficulty with reception here. We are near the STL broadcast area, so no mountains or forests in our way. I first tried just switching the antenna connection without a new channel scan. Everything looked exactly the same as with my old antenna. No biggie. It has a nice, long cord, which helps for placement. The next day, I ran a scan for new channels. I really expected to see some new channels pop up with the additional 130 mile radius. Nope. I have exactly the same channels. Of course, your experience could vary greatly, depending on your location, topography, big buildings, etc. But I have to say that this 180-mike-radius antenna does nothing at all different from my 50-mile-radius antenna. So, not really better, and definitely not worse.

title: Works okay, horizontal footprint, very little memory, grunts a lot
text: I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review. First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything. Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die. I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that. I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb. I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs. This one is different. First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had. It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable. it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit. It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote. There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey... My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB. That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare. I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up. We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had will fit this one. *bang head on desk* The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own. I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough. This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could. But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk. Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet. But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts. Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.

The LED colors cycle through several shades and looks nice. I thought it might bother me and be distracting as I worked, seeing it out of my peripheral vision. There are precious few directions included with the mouse, and what is included seems to be a loose translation from someone who learned English on the internet. I have no idea how to set the side buttons or adjust the speed. My computer did recognize it simply by plugging it in, but there were no driver updates or other information. I'd like to know how to adjust the DPI house settings, which are not an option in my control panel for mice. The mouse is comfy for my hand - I like larger mice so my fingers don't cramp up - I am online for many hours a day. This helps. I don't ever use the wheel, so won't comment on the wheel function. Cons: This is something that definitely needs to be adjusted in the next "incarnation" of this mouse.... The bottom has very slightly raised areas on the bottom. The reason behind this isn't very clear, unless it covers up something on the inside. However, as I mouse back and forth, these raised areas are not smooth, and they catch on my Belkin gel mouse pad. I really don't like that at all. I am going to use it for a while longer before I decide whether to keep it or go back to my old mouse though. (A Logitec that has served me well for many years.) Not impressive in function, but the design is awesome. Overall, it is an okay mouse. My daughter loved the design so much she had to buy one as well.

title: I LOVE this router! Much stronger than my old Linksys.
text: Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back. This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small. There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.) Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care. The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before. The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost. Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal. In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.) It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there. I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.

title: Not my favorite by far
text: Well, this is the first time I have purchased a Buffalo product, and it will also be my last. I've had other brands of hard drives. What I was hoping for was one that I could just plug in, maybe click a couple buttons, and it would back up my hard drive. Nope! First off, this has a lot of miscellaneous software that it wants you to install. You don't have to, but it all says "Buffalo", so I installed several of them. So far, I don't see even one that was useful. It also offers to install other stuff like Picasa, but again, it's optional. The cord: ARGH! Someone was on drugs when they chose this one. It is VERY short, as in, it has to be sitting on my CPU in order to use it. You can't just buy a longer cord, because Buffalo has used a very unique plug-in shape so nothing you might already have will work. Sure, the USB part is the same, but the other end is unique. On backing up my hard drive - basically, you have to copy and paste, like this was 1990. There is no auto-backup, nothing that I've found that will work the way I choose for it to work. The minimal manual comes in something like 19 languages, and the English version is lacking in detail. It tells you how to install the software, how to find the drive, how to plug it in, but not how to get an automatic backup to work! Did I mention that it was also pretty? That's all I can really give it points for. It looks good. All in all, VERY disappointed, and won't purchase again. It's a pain in the rump. Right now, after the third time to use it, the backup "time left" is sitting on 1 min 50 sec, like it has been for the last 20 minutes. If I cancel it, I am sure I'll lose some files. It won't tell me which ones didn't copy, or which folder there might be a problem with. BAH!!! I'd return it, but I waited too long to do it (not sold by Amazon, but an off-site seller who doesn't want to accept returns after 20 days). Look elsewhere, and buy a different brand. Save yourself the grief of something that should be a simple plug-n-play.

title: Nice case,but photo color is off
text: This is our second purchase of this case, My daughter bought the blue case for her external hard drive back up. The blue shade in the photo is very accurate. I would assume that the black would also be fine. My monitor is very carefully callibrated, as I do some graphics work. I haven't had anything so different on the color in the photo as this one is in a long time. Go by the words in this case! They show a pink case, but the text says magenta. The text is closer to real color. The case I received is a deep purple/pink color. Since it will be in a drawer protecting my external drive, it isn't a big problem. However, if you are someone who wants to color-coordinate all your electronics, just be aware that it isn't actually pink. That being said, the case is nice enough. It zips shut, which is great. Note that the edges of the case are harder, and would protect against being smashed. However, if you plan to toss this into a crowded backpack or briefcase, know that the middle part of this case is NOT hard and can easily be pushed in. All in all, this is a nice case and will store your hard drive well.

title: Nice looking, but cheaply made
text: This is my daughter's third MP3 player. She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design. We figured how bad can a player be, right? After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player. Well, they do play music - for a while. They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see. As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it. My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often. However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out. She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly. She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore. They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now, and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player. However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.

title: Fine for cheap laptops - looks good too.
text: My daughter has used this cooler for almost three years. Yes, it takes a lot of special handling for it to last that long - it gets tucked back into a laptop case every night. It is an acrylic base, but not a thick one. It will definitely hold your laptop, but it really needs to be on a flat surface to work properly. The blue lights look really great. It isn't too noisy, unless you tip it - then it sounds like something grinding. My daughter kind of killed hers off from repeatedly using her laptop on an uneven surface. It caused the fans to stall out or grind, and burned them out. Right now, the cooler only has one of the three fans working, and doesn't really keep the laptop cool enough. Top points for looks - the acrylic and the blue lights are great. The price is good for what it is. Got an expensive laptop? Get a different cooler - look for one that blows heat instead of tries to suck heat (via the fans) away from the laptop. Try a Belkin. Forget Targus unless you don't mind going deaf while cruising the internet. Would I buy it again? Well, I think it would be a great low-cost alternative for a NETbook. For a laptop, it would really be better to get something that has a stronger air movement capacity.

title: Great radio, but very high battery drain.
text: This radio looks really good wherever you place it. Ours looked exactly as advertised. The design is not obtrusive, doesn't require a huge footprint, and the buttons are easy to use. The only DOWNSIDE I found is a major one - the battery consumption is apparently off the charts. I didn't put cheapie batteries in it either - I got the blue lithium Energizer batteries. That is the only one we use in our digital cameras due to their ability to last. I take an average of 500 photos a month between my home business and our family and pets, and get at least a month of camera usage from a set. (I date them all with a Sharpie so I know how long they last.) Even when they are spent for camera purposes, they still have enough power in them to get our haircutters going, so they are great batteries. Anyway, I put in a brand new set of the blue lithiums 24 DAYS ago. I had the radio turned on to program it, but other than that, turned it off until/unless severe storms were in the area. We hadn't had any, so it wasn't sitting in the "on" position, listening to the regular radio, etc etc. We had reason to use it this past Saturday, April 24th, when severe storms hit our area. (Part of that huge system of tornados that hit so many states.) I hadn't thought about it much, even though there were bad thunderstorms in the area, but there was no warning light on the radio. (It has three small lights on the left side that light up if there is a watch or warning in your area, and you can turn it on to hear the NWS warning.) However, suddenly, our town's tornado warning went off! We'd never heard it go off in the 3 yrs we've lived here, so it was a big deal. We headed downstairs for safety, and I grabbed the radio to take along. Guess what - dead as a doornail. THREE WEEKS without even being turned on, and the brand new lithium batteries were DRAINED!!! O-M-G. There ended up being a tornado only a few miles from us that did quite a bit of damage. I would hate to think what could have happened if I relied on this radio for our only information!! Once the worst had passed us, I sent my son back upstairs for more batteries. We popped them in and immediately had the weather warning lights and broadcasts. While that was good, it could have EASILY been too little too late. I cannot even believe how this thing ate the batteries already that power my digital camera for a month at a time with constant usage! There is NO low battery warning light at all, nothing to tell me that it was not working. No beeps, no lights, nothing but dead air when we needed it the most. If it had been nighttime and we were asleep, who knows what could have happened! Note to Midland - you NEED a low battery light! Make it blue, so it does not get confused with any weather warning lights! This is a potentially life-saving product - go the "extra mile" here and provide a notice of some kind when the power is gone. I never expected the batteries to be drained after about 3 wks without even using the radio. If you get this radio, I highly advise keeping it plugged in somewhere. I do not know if the batteries will continue to drain while it is also plugged in (without being turned on), so I'll revise my review when I know. I am now on a hunt for the adapter that was supposed to come with it. I do not remember seeing one in the package. I just got the original box back out this morning to get the adapter, and there's nothing in there. So, it is possible that the box I got didn't get one put in there. I hadn't planned on plugging it in, but now see that might be my only real way to get dependable notices. I'll check the radio to see what voltage the adapter should be, and see if we have an extra one from some other electronic item. This is the really bad weather season for us (Midwest), and it is very important this radio do its job! Do NOT rely on the batteries, and keep a spare set of batteries on each floor of your home (if you have an upstairs or basement, make sure you have some available for flashlights and radios on EACH FLOOR - I had not even thought about that, but we keep our batteries upstairs, and did not want to go back up during the actual tornado warning!). I have flashlights tucked every conceivable place in the home (including the bathroom, under the kitchen sink, etc etc), but never really gave a second thought to having extra batteries available per floor until last Saturday when we needed them. Lesson learned! S.A.M.E. technology is a must - don't consider any weather radio that doesn't have it, or you'll hear a lot of stuff that doesn't even pertain to your location. This radio has it. Note though that on this model, you have to choose the ALERT ON option to ON or you won't get the warning lights. (Odd that it is not a default to on, but it isn't.) You have the choice of a LOT of various types of warnings that will pertain to your area, which is great. You choose which warnings to turn on, except for tornado warnings. This is defaulted to the "on" position, although the manual does not tell you that. I wrote to Midland to ask about it. It took them two weeks to answer me, but they confirmed it was a default setting, which is why it was not included in the storm warning options lists. In summary - great radio, great look, beyond-poor battery usage. I've taken off one star for the poor battery life - I've never seen any electronic use them faster. The lack of a low battery light or beep is a huge mistake for this type of product. It takes four AA batteries, so be sure to keep a pack of them available on each floor of your home.

text: i would first off like to address some previous reviewers that have stated that they had a low humming or buzzing noise. i believe this was caused by these people not having a adequate subwoofer cable to shield against EMI and RFI. i have a very nice ATLONA subwoofer cable that is; double shielded, has oxygen free copper conductor and 24k gold connectors. i have had no humm or buzz. here is my review of the polk audio psw10 Pros: low cost, easy to install, aesthetically pleasing(looks very nice), porting, made from composite material that will last a long time, auto shut off feature when not in use, very good sound quality, nice and crisp not "boomy" bass, very good owners manual and customer support/service from polk audio. Cons: Low wattage, no cables included, not down firing port and no low-frequency effect (LFE)support. conclusion: I am very pleased with this subwoofer. It has a dynamic power rating of 100W but it sounds like more. the quality of the sound coming out is very good. I actually had to turn it down because it was so loud when i was first was setting it up and testing it( I have worked with Jet engines that require double hearing protection for years). I don't know how loud some people watch their TVs or movies but, this is way more than loud enough.It shakes my house. I really like the way this thing looks. this subwoofer also complements my sound bar very well. I have; watched movies, TV and listened to music. all sound superb to me.I highly recommend if you buy any subwoofer you buy a quality subwoofer cable. I highly recommend buying this subwoofer if you are looking for a good value or "best bang for the buck".

title: Very good tv for the size
text: I would first like to state that i own a Sony and Toshiba LED backlit LCD televisions. I have never seen the samsung LED DLP screens or the laservue DLP. I will be making this comparison solely compared to my other LED LCD televisions. I do not yet own any 3D movies or equipment. Pros: PICTURE:number one is the size of this screen, i love it! it is great for HDTV and HD movies. Image is very clear and crisp.it has 120hz witch is much better against motion blur. it has advanced video calibration options. i just went to [...] and used the settings there. INTERNET TV:I also enjoy the wireless Internet. it has movies and it has news. my favorite feature is the ticker option. you can have a ticker at the bottom of your TV with facebook on it as well as other apps. SOUND:The 16 speakers surround sound are very amazing! you can calibrate the sound with the microphone provided. SIZE/WEIGHT: This TV is very light its almost as light as my 46" LED TV. I could easily lift it with another person. i don't think i would have needed another person but its better safe than sorry. Cons: POWER-ON/off: During power on it takes a few moments to come on during this time it displays a Mitsubishi start up screen kinda like a computer.it also does this for powering off(shutdown screen like a PC) PICTURE: overall video is very good but not as good as my LED 120hz Toshiba. it is not as crisp and takes a few moments to fully brighten.Its not as good as my Toshiba for use as a computer monitor using the HDMI inputs.I would say the difference is very minimal. INTERNET TV: the wireless tv requires you to buy an additional proprietary Mitsubishi AzureWave AW-NU231 Wireless Adapter. It also takes a minute for the internet TV to initially load.you also have to type with the remote control, not very fun.usb ports for the wifi adapter are in bad spots(one on back and one on rear side). they should be on top or directly on the sides. there is one on the side but it is being obstructed by the screen. causing it to loose signal strength. on top would be the ideal spot. Sound: now that i have had a taste of the surround sound. I notice what it is lacking. A nice sub-woofer. now i gotta buy one because with one it would sound even better. Heat: this TV makes some heat out of the rear by the lamp area. it might be good for the winter but not very helpful for the summer. Conclusion: Overall this is a very good product i mainly bought it because they do not make a LED LCD screen in this size for this price.

Much "heavier" than others I've used in the past which tended to wear out after about 6 months of use -- printing essentially erased, holes developed in the most-used key covers, etc. This one is definitely thicker so it should last longer. I've had no issues with keys lining up: the keys-lock light is visible, backlighting isn't obscured -- really, just about perfect. I especially like the color-coded key combo shortcuts -- although I will admit that I have to switch to my high-octane reading glasses as my older eyes have trouble reading the tiny print. Overall, however, this is a very good keyboard cover and works perfectly with the older MacBook Air. Solid 5 stars.

title: Nice full-sized keyboard ...
text: No issues with this so far. It connects perfectly, and the case seems to be capable of providing some protection. I've used it a couple of times a day for 1 - 1.5 hrs each time and noticed no problems. Seems to be holding up -- I usually am rather "gentle" with my electronics, to bear that in mind. I'd like it even better if it has some sort of backlight. Other than that, no complaints at all. Solid 4 stars.

title: Fits my iPad Pro 9.7 (A1674) perfectly ...
text: An attractive case -- I tested the Rose Gold version -- nicely made with no obvious flaws. I've been trying various types of external keyboards as I like to use my iPad on trips and blog as I go. Having a full keyboard makes life a lot easier. This is the first integrated case/keyboard I've tried, and so far, I like it. It's easy to set up -- charge it (a cable is provided), pop in the iPad, turn on, pair, and you're set to go. The backlight is fully adjustable - brightness as well as color. That's a nice touch. Battery life seems to be excellent -- I've used it 2-3 hours every day for the past 10 days, and it's still going strong and it still hasn't indicated I need to recharge it. The keyboard size is a bit smaller than my MacBook Air laptop, but after a few minutes, I got used to the slightly tighter quarters and had no issues at all. Getting it into the case is easy; getting it out of the case takes a little more effort. When I take it along on my trips, I'll leave it in the case for the duration. My only complaint is that it's quite heavy but given the battery capacity, that's probably not too surprising. So the trade-off is a slightly heavier case with LONG battery life, or a keyboard-only solution with much shorter battery life. I think in the end, I'll appreciate the longer battery life and fully integrated case/keyboard. I'll continue to use this over the next few months, and plan to take it on my next couple of trips. If all goes well, it will come along on a 131-day world cruise early next year.

title: Plug and play simplicity...
text: I’ll admit it -- hardware intimidates me so I tend to opt for the simplest solutions I can find. I needed a better backup solution for my MacBook Air, and was happy to try this external drive. So far, I’m very happy, super easy to connect, easy to set up and use, and faster than my older (much older) 500GB external storage unit. I did a selective backup (music, photos, videos, and some important files), and found the performance to be better than I expected. I didn’t time it, but I’ll do that for sure on the next group of files/folders. The physical size makes it truly portable, so I purchased a hardshell case so i could transport it as needed. I’m really happy with this. Five stars!

title: Best of the group of comparably-priced earbuds ...
text: I own several pairs of earbuds. I just seem to accumulate them like I do my reading glasses -- several pairs in each room where I tend to use them. Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group. I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones. Good performance for the price. I like these.

title: Perfect for on-the-go journaling/blogging ... lightweight and portable, it travels well!
text: I purchased this to take along on vacations so I could journal (and ultimately blog) about my journeys. The first test was just completed: a 2-week cruise around Alaska (Ketchikan, Endicott Arm, Juneau, Hoonah, Anchorage, Kodiak, Homer, and Sitka). I wanted a full-sized keyboard, portable, and easy to manage that would work with my iPad Pro. I chose this for the size, the fact that it is powered via my iPad (rather than needing to be charged), and the fact that it's a wired connection via the lightning cable rather than Bluetooth. Nothing against Bluetooth, but not having to deal with pairing simplifies things a lot. This performed beautifully! Connected easily, and no problems at all with performance. It has some nifty shortcuts, many I didn't use, but at least they're available. Despite being a full-size keyboard, the small size means I can tuck this into my carryon along with other necessities and it doesn't take up much space at all. It's durable, too -- the wire connector appears to be sturdy. I used this a couple of times per day to record events and activities, so it was in and out of my bag often. No problems at all. It's coming along on my next adventure: a cruise around the North Atlantic (including Greenland, Iceland, and Norway) for 6 weeks.

title: My first fine-point stylus: I like it, despite a few issues ...
text: I have mixed feelings about this stylus. Overall, I like it. There are some very good things about it, but it has a few issues. I'm using this primarily with my iPad Pro, and to a lesser degree with my iPhone 6s. This is my first experience with a fine-point stylus, although I've considered purchasing one for awhile. First, the pros: -- I was able to get it charged with no problem -- Using the included quick start guide, I found my way to the Wacom website to get more details on set-up and apps that I might want to use with my iPad Pro. -- Found the apps in iTunes App Store and downloaded a few of them to my iPad, got them installed and ready to test. -- Pairing went smoothly -- no hiccups or issues at all. This was a pleasant surprise, as I've had problems in the past pairing things with the iPad. -- Was able to get it up and running with both Bamboo Paper as well as Sketches and ibispaint. -- Nice look and feel -- since it's the size of a fairly standard pen (ball point, gel, retractable, etc.), it feels "natural" in use. -- Surprisingly long battery life -- I used it almost constantly for 3 hrs, and still had a lot of battery charge left. Cons: -- it skips. My iPad doesn't have a screen protector, so the pen is operating on the bare glass. I thought maybe the problem was the glass, so I cleaned it -- twice. Didn't seem to help. It skips in all three apps, and in different parts of the screen each time. Still haven't figured out if it's operator error or problems with the apps or something with the stylus itself. I'll keep playing with it and see if I can find a common denominator cause. When it skips, it's only a short distance -- maybe 1/4" or so -- but it's enough to be annoying. -- the tip has an annoying tendency to retract during use, especially if I'm using it for writing longhand. In 3 or 4 lines, it has already retracted over halfway. I'm not exerting much pressure on it -- only enough for it to "register" on the screen, so I think it might be the combination of the motion -- writing loops, "twisting" to make some of the letters, etc. -- plus the minimal pressure. What it means is that I have to stop periodically to twist the pen to move the tip "out" again. Otherwise, I end up trying to write with the hard plastic external edge of the tip, which doesn't work that well. So why the 4-star rating? Despite the issues, I still like this stylus. I'm not a professional artist, but I do like to sketch, to annotate photos, etc. and it really does work nicely for that even with the skipping (I just move the image a bit and try again). If I were a student and I was looking to use this to take longhand notes in class or something, I'd probably drop the rating to 3 stars. But for my use, it's OK. I can work around the issues. So I DO like it.

title: Nearly indestructible, nice length ...
text: I was actually looking for a longer sturdier lightning cable when this showed up. I've been using it for a couple of weeks now, and I'm definitely a fan. First, it's very solid with reinforced plugs (both ends). I've worn out many lightning cables, and the place where they wear out first is where the cord connects to the plug (especially on the lightning end). That shouldn't be a problem here. The cord has a round braided nylon cover that helps prevent tangling. Yes, it takes up more room than either a flat cable or a smaller cord, but I think the durability outweighs that. Finally, the length is great. I use a shorter cable for my bedside recharging station, but when I travel (especially when I travel), I'm never sure where the outlet will be, and I like to have my phone handy on the nightstand just in case. A longer cable gives me more options and some reassurance that at least ONE of the outlets will be close enough with this longer cable to allow me to have the phone handy. Charging speed is just fine, too - comparable to my Apple-original cables. Basically, I have no complaints at all. With the quality and durability, this should last a long time. Solid 5 stars from me.

title: Solid performer, perfect for my needs ...
text: With a MacBook Air, I'm limited to 2 USB ports. One is reserved for my external 1Tb hard drive and that leaves only one for everything else (wireless mouse, etc.). Using a USB hub is really the only option. This small unit is as close to perfect as I've found. It has a small footprint, clean design, and it works beautifully. I'm not a "hardware junkie" -- I just want stuff that works without glitches or hiccups. This does exactly that. Four ports is just the right number for me, too (you can get units with more ports if needed). This isn't my first Anker purchase -- I've been very happy with the quality and will gladly purchase this brand again.

title: Works great with my iPad Pro ...
text: I recently got hit with one of the upper respiratory bugs going around and found myself having to spend considerable time in bed coughing/etc. I still needed to be able to keep up with emails/etc. so my iPad was my tool of choice. But holding it in the proper angle was difficult. Checked around Amazon, saw this, read the reviews, and decided to take a chance. I'm VERY happy with it. I have an iPad Pro in a slim case, and if fits perfectly with about 1" to spare on each side (see photo). I got the lime green to go with my bedroom decor. The fabric is good quality, seams are nicely stitched, no obvious problems or issues. I like that you can "unfold" it into various configurations to get different angles. The only thing I'd change or add would be another "fold" to add another angle into the choices. Would gladly purchase again, and recommend to my friends.

title: Super soft and lightweight -- but very warm and cozy ...
text: Wow! I didn't expect this blanket to be as nice as it is. I purchased the full/queen size in the "paisley" pattern (in the "group" photo, it's the one on the right side at the top -- sage/olive green with camel/rust paisley design). I washed it before using it and had no issues with shrinkage, shedding or pilling. The blanket is lightweight, but still very warm due to the plush texture. I don't like a lot of heavy bedclothes, so this is perfect for me. We've already started getting cooler nights here in the Pacific Northwest (I'm writing this in early October), so it's getting daily use now. Honestly, I can't find anything wrong with it so far. For the money, it's a nice bargain.

title: UPDATE: died too soon ...
text: UPDATE: DIED after 2 months of use. I'm not a heavy or careless user of this kind of stuff -- this was plugged into a connector on my nightstand that also handled a mini-USB cable for my bluetooth speaker, and wasn't moved around at all. I tested it initially with my iPad Pro and my iPhone, but after the initial testing, it was used ONLY for charging my iPhone 6s usually 3 times per week or so. The first 6 weeks, it worked perfectly, and I was thrilled with it. Unfortunately, it started malfunctioning after 6 weeks (lights flashing randomly); after 8 weeks of use, it no longer worked at all. CANNOT recommend. Sorry. ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've been living with this for about 10 days and I've had a chance to use it with my new-ish iPad Pro 9.7" and iPhone 6S. So far, no problems at all. Functions just like the original cable except this one is longer and has some extra features -- aluminum housing on both ends is much more "solid" than the plastic and everything is well secured with no manufacturing defects that I could find. Probably the best part of this cable is the LED light that tells you where your device is in the charging process. Pulsing red means it's charging; flickering green means it's almost done; solid green means it's 100%. The solid green light stays on for awhile (haven't been able to time it precisely as it seems to vary a little from charge to charge -- I'm thinking maybe a couple of hours or so before it goes off; then it stays off unless something "wakes it up" (a notification, a phone call, etc.). I charge the phone on my nightstand and I've had no problem with brightness, but then I sleep like a rock once I get to sleep and it didn't keep me awake, either. Some folks might have a problem, though, because the light is rather bright. It fits just fine with my Speck case on the iPhone and the MoKo ultra-light case on the iPad. I actually like this enough that I'll be ordering another one before I make my annual trip back home for the holidays so I can charge both devices at once. It's a nice cable, well made, great length, and I can tell by looking at it whether my device is finished charging.

title: Solid performance so far -- would purchase again ...
text: After doing some research, reading reviews, etc., I finally decided on this Transcend 64 GB flash drive. I just needed something I could use to periodically back up some of my non-critical folders (I take care of the critical stuff in other ways), and this was one of the more economical products I found. After two weeks of use, I'm reasonably happy with it. I'm using it with a MacBook Air 13" and a fairly high-quality USB hub (almost mandatory since you get only w USB ports on the MacBook). The outer housing seems a bit flimsy -- not sure it would hold up to much abuse -- but since I'll just be using it once a month, I think it will be OK. Transferring the files from the MacBook was smooth and quite fast. Reading from the Transcend presented no issues, either -- it seemed just as fast as reading directly from the MacBook. I didn't clock it -- as long as I'm not having to sit and wait too much, I'm fairly easy to please. Overall the design is fine -- the business end slides in and out with a locking slider -- it's small and relatively sleek, too. No issues at all. Solid 4 stars for quality vs cost. Would purchase this brand again if the need arises.

title: Excellent protection -- but maybe a little too much for light users ...
text: Whether or not you'll like this case depends to a large extent on two things: 1) how much of a klutz you are, and 2) how you use your iPad. Here's where I fit into that picture: I'm not generally klutzy -- I can count on one hand the number of times I've dropped any of my portable electronics in the past 10 years. I use my iPad mostly when I travel and don't want to bring my laptop, and it stays in my bag unless I'm using it. Otherwise, I bring it out now and again for games or to read (I have the Kindle app installed, and it works great for that). For me, this Otterbox case is probably a case of "overkill": perhaps a little more case than I really need. The basics: This is a multi-part case: the two-piece inner plastic "shell" with a clear window over the screen, the outer silicone "slipcover" that hugs the back and sides of the plastic shell, and another hard plastic snap-on outer "cover" that includes a pop-up stand, that snaps onto the back of the silicone cover. The good: This will definitely protect your iPad Pro 9.7. The thing is built like body armor -- solid, form-fitting, not too difficult to install. The colors "damson purple" and "hibiscus pink" aren't too garish, either, and match the photos on the page here. The concern(s): The only screen protection is the thin plastic "screen protector" -- that's all. I'm a little concerned about how protective it would be in an accident. It would have been really nice if they had designed the outer cover/stand to snap onto the FRONT of the case. I've tried it a few times, and it doesn't work. The corner "clips" get caught in the silicone slipcover so that it can't snap securely. It only fits securely onto the BACK of the case. Pity. Also, it's VERY heavy. I realize that you don't get this level of protection without adding weight, so that's a trade-off that you either choose to live with or not. Soooo ... bottom line: if you have klutzy tendencies, if you're looking for 5-star protection for your iPad Pro and you're willing to live with added weight, this might be a super option. If you're more like me -- light user, not of the klutzy persuasion -- this might a little more protection than you really need. For me, it rates 3 stars: "It's OK."

title: The PERFECT computer stand!
text: Why did I wait so long to get one of these? I have other Lifetime tables, but I never thought about getting one of these until ... I use a computer stand/table in the living room so I can watch television and just have a better outdoor view (the view from my office isn't great, and my living room window overlooks a park-like yard). I've been using a much fancier (and more expensive) "computer stand" for a couple of years, but it finally bit the dust (the weld that holds the desktop onto the central support column failed). So I started the search for a replacement, one that maybe wasn't so fancy but would last longer. Of course I came to Amazon -- they have everything! -- and found a number of options. This looked like the best fit, so I ordered it. I'm absolutely thrilled with it. Seriously, it's even better than I expected, even with my experience with Lifetime tables (which has been excellent). This little table is the PERFECT size for my laptop, a mug of coffee, and a couple of other items (reading glasses, etc.). It's lightweight enough that I can easily scoot it out of the way when I need to move around (get a coffee refill, etc.). My only quibble is that I wish it came in black, but that's absolutely NOT a deal breaker. This feels far more stable than my old computer stand even when it was new, and it's not likely to have any similar problems. I love that I can adjust the height, too. Overall, this is a solid 5-star item. Would happily purchase again if the need arises.

title: Small, but does what I need it to do ...
text: Since my MacBook Air has only 2 USB ports, and I have a bunch of external devices and gizmos that need to talk to the Mac via USB, I set out looking for something that would allow me to attach multiple USB-connectable devices at the same time. One of the 2 MacBook Air USB ports is dedicated to my 1TB external hard drive, but I also have a wireless mouse, a 25-key midi keyboard that I use for composing music, and a few other things that I may not use every day, but that I want to be able to use without having to disconnect my mouse. Saw this, read the reviews, and decided to give it a try. So far, we've been working together comfortably for just over a week with no hiccups or mishaps. I like the small size -- it's small and relatively "flat," so it stays tucked just behind my laptop on my desk without occupying too much real estate. I like that. I have the wireless mouse "receiver" plugged into the end, my midi keyboard plugged into the first of the 3 slots on the side, and I can add anything else (iPhone for syncing, etc.) in one of the other two slots. This summer, I'll be using it with a USB-driven personal fan when the weather warms up (no air conditioning here in the Pacific NW). I did test all 4 ports, and they are all working just fine. Very happy with it so far. If I start noticing any issues, I'll update this review.

title: Colorful kitchen convenience ...
text: Colorful, good quality. I needed to replace an older set of basic cooking utensils, and thought these might be a good set to try. So far, I like them. The pasta server is a good size, and the ladle is just about perfect. I wish they had a larger spatula, but this one works OK for eggs, burgers, etc. They clean nicely, too -- by hand and in the dishwasher. No complaints at all. Would purchase again.

title: So far, this is better than expected ...
text: I haven't used many wireless mice -- I've almost always just used the track pad on my laptop and was fine with that. But I've been having some problems with the track pad locking up on my new (Mar 2015) MacBook, so I went shopping for a wireless mouse. Clearly, this Logitech M325 model is popular -- hundreds of reviews, most of them good -- and the price is certainly reasonable (depending on the seller and color/print, prices are within a few dollars of each other). So, I ended up ordering this "Freespirit" model -- sleek black with a multi-color "splash" design -- primarily because I like the colors and the overall look of it. I'm not disappointed. In fact, I'm more impressed than I thought I would be. It performs just fine. I don't have a lot of room -- I use my laptop most fo the time on a small rolling stand with just enough room for the computer plus a beverage and a few pens in a pencil cup. No problem -- this thing works on a pad of paper, my leg, on the sofa seat beside me, etc. I wish the scrolling wheel operated a bit more smoothly, but it's not enough of a problem to warrant any drop in star rating. The color was a bit of a surprise, too -- the "splashes" are metallic/pearlized, so they really shine against the black background. Overall, I like this more than I thought I would. I've been using it for about 10 days, and I've noticed no problems at all. I'll definitely update this review if I notice any issues in the future. But so far, I REALLY like it. It's making my life a lot simpler, for sure.

title: IMPRESSIVE sound!
text: Holy cow! I was NOT expecting the sound from this little speaker to be as good as it is. I own 3 other Bluetooth speakers, one lower price point, one "moderate"/medium, and another that is comparable in price to this unit. None comes close to the sound quality. It's really unobtrusive looking, almost drab, slightly "retro" in a gunmetal gray with a darker gray screen. A single button surrounded by a ring on top of the unit controls everything that needs controlling (on/off, volume and skip). A thick rubber base keeps it from sliding around on polished tables (like a nightstand, where I'll be keeping this). It took just over 3 hrs to fully charge using the included wall charger and cable. I paired it with my iPhone -- nothing tricky there -- and proceeded to play music. I'm a conductor/composer and write mostly music for choirs, so that's what I tend to listen to most of the time. First up: the [[ASIN:B0018NQ066 Britten: War Requiem (2 CDs)]] I'm intimately familiar with this work, having performed it three times and conducted rehearsals for it on one occasion. It's one of my "desert island" recordings. It has a huge variety of "sound" from soft/slim orchestration to full out full orchestra and chorus. The LG performed beautifully. NO distortion, every slight nuance was audible. The recording is a quality recording but I've listened to it on all my other wireless speakers as well as my Bose surround wired speaker set up, and the performance of this small LG speaker is impressive. Seriously exceptional performance. OK, next up, something completely different: Fleetwood Mac [[ASIN:B00B1MHXY2 Rumours]] -- again, virtually flawless performance. All the "bits" of percussion come through crystal clear. It has a decent bass sound, too -- again something I wasn't expecting from a unit in this price point or of this size. I've been playing this almost non-stop for over 5 hours and it's showing no signs of low battery. The description here says it runs 9 hrs on a single charge; I'm beginning to believe it. Also, it shuts off after 20 minutes if these is no input (Bluetooth mode). You can also turn it off from your smartphone using the app downloaded from the iOS app store (there's an Android version, too). This has no built-in microphone, so you can't take phone calls on it. It's just a speaker but a VERY good one. I really can't find anything wrong with this so far. It's really that good.

title: PERFECT fit for MacBook Air 13"
text: Much nicer than I thought it would be. Construction is good quality, zippers all work without binding, and the interior definitely provides a lot of protection. I had been looking for a case for my new MacBook Air 13" (finally replaced my ca. 2007 MacBook Pro 15"), so when I was offered the opportunity to try out and review this one, I thought "Why not?" First things first: it is a perfect fit for my new laptop. It's snug, but not "tight." In other words, the laptop won't slide around in a too-big bag. The side pocket is large enough to handle the adaptor and power cable, with room for additional bits -- mouse, headphones, etc. -- if needed. The handles lie flat against the bag until needed; there's velcro that holds them together when in use. It weighs very little but provides a good amount of protection. Seriously, I couldn't be happier with this. It's exactly what I pictured for a laptop bag. (Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this item.)

title: Nice keyboard cover ...
text: I'm very impressed with the quality of this keyboard cover. I honestly was not expecting to be as nice as it is. I can speak from experience when I say that cats, coffee, and a MacBook are NOT a great combination. I lost an earlier MacBook Pro when cat and coffee collided over the keyboard, so when I purchased my new MacBook Air 13", I knew I wanted a keyboard cover. This one has a lot going for it. It fits beautifully -- lays flat, the key covers are precisely where they should be, there's no slippage or any feeling of insecurity about the cover shifting position. It's transparent except for the colored key caps, so the underlighting of the MacBook Air keyboard shines through. It's quite thin so it doesn't add much in the way of bulk, either -- but the material feels like it will survive heavy use without tearing or puncturing. I especially like having all the keyboard shortcuts printed right on the keys themselves. My version, the OX X shortcuts, is easy to read, and the colors actually mean somthing (blue = primary shortcuts, pink = finder, green = safari, orange = iWorks/Mail/MS Office). It's a nice touch that lends a bit of color to the rather drab aluminum face of the MacBook. If you've never typed on a keyboard with a cover, it might take a little getting used to. It has a "softer" feel, but key action/etc. is not compromised at all. Overall, I think this is a good product, a nice gift for someone with a new MacBook, with bult-in usefulness beyond protecting the keyboard from inadvertent spills and dust. (Although a sample was supplied for review purposes, opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.)

title: Economical solution, work great!
text: I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups. I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups. I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength. As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem. This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful. I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning. kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review. Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.

title: No problems with this so far ....
text: I purchased this after reading the description and some of the reviews, and I'm quite happy with it. No, it's not real leather -- the description clearly says "synthetic leather" so no disappointment there. The price (I paid less than twelve dollars) says it's not going to be Gucci quality, but it was actually better than I expected. I got the "Purple Embossed," and it looks a bit like tooled leather in a sort of lacy/jacquard pattern. Very attractive. Most important, it fits my older iPad 2 perfectly. The sleep/wake feature works, and, after 4 months of daily use, it's holding up just fine, with no sign of durability issues at all. I would purchase this again, and probably will if the current one wears out. It's becoming more and more difficult to find cases for my older iPad, and this one works for me.

title: Good basic screen protectors ...
text: I'm not the most skilled at applying these sticky screen protectors. I usually end up with bubbles, so I rip it off, and start over with a new one. Obviously, I migrate toward the lower-priced ones since I usually end up wasting at least one in a 3-pack. I'm happy to report I got the first one of these installed without a single bubble. Either I'm getting better at this, or there's something different about these protectors. The process is a bit different from others I've used, but the instructions are clear and application was easy. Can't speak to the durability of these as I've had mine installed for just 10 days or so, but for inexpensive basic screen protectors for your iPhone 5 series, you can't do any better than these. Highly recommended!

title: Apple-certified, solid performance ...
text: I've been using this cable daily for over a week, and I have to say I'm impressed so far. It's a solid, sturdy cable -- "thicker" than the original, not quite as flexible, but that doesn't bother me. The USB and lightning plugs are securely attached, and it doesn't look like there will be any problems with the cord cover fracturing at either point (I've had that problem with other cables, including the original one that came with an earlier iPhone). The plugs seat securely into my charger and iPhone 5S, too. I have a Case Logic rubber case [[ASIN:B00JMPXGOQ Case Logic CLIPH5-3203 iPhone 5/5s 2-piece Hand Grip - White/Gray]] on my iPhone, and the cord fits just fine. The cord is 10' long -- that's longer than any of my other cords, and will come in handy for those times when I need to recharge from a plug that's not nearby. This is NOT a "small" cord -- it's going to take up some space while traveling, but to me, it's worth it. So far, I have noticed no issues at all. It plays nicely with my iPhone, with no hiccups or problems. I'll be traveling with it soon, and will update this review if I notice any issues at all. Otherwise, so far, I'm impressed. I received a sample for review purposes, with no assurance of a positive review. My opinion is based solely on my experience with the product.

title: Compact, good performer ....
text: I got this to store the back-up of my external hard drive, and it does that job very well. I have a key chain on which I store a number of flash drives for various purposes that I leave hanging on a hook in my office, so it doesn't get a lot of abuse. So far, I've noticed no problems with quality -- it's VERY small, and fits VERY snugly into the USB port on my laptop, but once I get it right-side up, it's easy to insert and retrieve. Speed is adequate for my needs. Very happy with this so far. If that changes, I'll edit this review.

title: Super performance for a reasonable cost ...
text: OK, let's get this straight at the beginning: I'm not an audio expert. I don't work in the industry, I haven't studied this stuff, etc. But I DO know what sounds good especially when it comes to classical music recordings. I've been involved in classical music my whole life, I've played and sung with orchestras, so I know how things should sound. Bottom line: this unit produces very good quality sound over the range of dynamics and timbres that come with a variety of classical music. I have a few recordings that I use as "tests": Carmina Burana (the opening "O Fortuna" section); Bach "Magnificat"; Stravinsky "Firebird"; Mozart piano sonatas; Beethoven String Quartets; and various choral works (Eric Whitacre, Brahms, etc.). I got none of the tinny sound that sometimes happens with piano works; the softer sections of the Eric Whitacre choral works were clear and precise; the range of dynamics in the opening O Fortuna of "Carmina Burana" was crystal clear with no distortion. Really, this outperformed my expectations. The unit is smaller than I expected, which is a good thing, since I intend to take it along when I travel. It's attractive (I got the orange color), and has a nice "feel" to it. The controls are easy to manipulate on the top of the unit, and I really like the ability to take phone calls via the unit (it has a built-in microphone). Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase. I paid less than forty dollars for mine, and at that price, I consider it a super deal. I've had it only for a couple of weeks, so if there are issues with durability, I'll update this review. For now, it's definitely worth 5 stars.

title: Works great with my iPhone 5S ...
text: Got this to use while traveling, when a longer cable comes in handy. I've been using it daily for two weeks, and so far, no problems. I use the [[ASIN:B00ESJGILE AmazonBasics Case for iPhone 5S & iPhone 5 - White / Grey]], and it fits just fine. Absolutely no issues or complaints; would definitely purchase again.

title: No problems at all; works fine ...
text: I got this to use as a back-up cable for my iPad 2 when I travel. I've used it in two trips so far, and it's holding up just fine. Everything fits snugly, nothing looks like it's about ready to fall apart, and it performs just like the original Apple cable. The 4-foot length is nice, too. Very happy with this, and would purchase again.

title: Great sound in a little package ....
text: I did a LOT of research before purchasing this little speaker. My needs were pretty simple: I wanted a wireless speaker that could connect with either my iPhone or iPad to use on the nightstand. I like to play music before I go to sleep, so it needed to be small, but have great sound. Based on the reviews here, I finally decided on this one, and I'm happy to say it's PERFECT! It charged quickly connected to my MacBook Pro -- about 2 hrs, maybe a little less. Turned it on, turned on the iPhone, went to the "Settings" on the phone, found Bluetooth, and there was the JAM XT. Selected it, and voila! they paired. Entire set-up took about 10 seconds. I listen to a lot of classical music, so my first "test" was the Brahms "A German Requiem" -- lots of highs, lows, soft, loud, etc. Strings, voices, woodwinds, brass -- it's all in there. I listened carefully for distortion -- everything was set on "medium" volume -- and I'm happy to say I heard NO distortion at all. Everything sounded great -- nearly as good as my Bose system, but without the bass resonance. OK, so I haven't had this very long (about a week), so its durability remains to be seen. But I'm impressed with the quality and style of this. If I notice any issues, I'll update this review. Meanwhile, I can now fall asleep to great sounding music from a small-footprint speaker. And that's exactly what I wanted.

title: Split backing makes a difference ...
text: I have an Epson LW-300, and this tape is specifically designed for use with the Epson LabelWorks series. The 1/2" size is perfect for my needs, and the white with black print works great. The BEST thing this has going for it is the split backing. I can print a label, then peel off the upper half of the backing, leaving the lower half in place. This way, I can easily get proper placement before peeling off the lower half of the backing and making the placement more permanent. Very happy with this -- definitely will continue using it for all my labeling needs.

title: TERRIBLE instruction booklet ...
text: I like the basic design of this -- the small sleek size, nice layout of buttons, large display. The radio reception seems to be decent, although mounting it on the wall is not possible in my area, since I have to turn it various directions to get a couple of local AM stations. Weather band reception is OK, as is FM reception. That's about where my positive feelings for this little radio end. It is way too difficult to set up, NOT with regard to the physical aspects of hitting the correct buttons in the correct sequence, but rather in terms of deciphering and understanding the instructions. The instruction leaflet, such as it is, is written in such small type that it's nearly impossible to read. I finally went to the Eton website and downloaded the instruction manual there, then "zoom"ed it so I could read how to set the time, store radio stations, etc. Then there's the issue of the S.A.M.E. codes. I had never heard of this technology before I got this radio. NO WHERE in the included instructions is there any mention of NOAA, or even the "S.A.M.E." designation. On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions. This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county. And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. DISABLE: Displays the message on the LCD when receiving a message" -- does that mean that when it's enabled, you DON'T get a message displayed on the LCD when receiving a message? What kind of Alert happens when it's enabled? the flashing light? the siren? what, precisely, am I "defeating" with this??) I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. We've had one National Weather Service-issued high wind warning here in the Pacific NW since I received and programmed the radio, and it didn't set off the alert -- no light flashing, no "message," nothing. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works. Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.

title: Nice size, nice quality ...
text: So far, so good -- this is a very nicely made stylus that works perfectly with my iPad. I really like the "slim" profile, especially the smaller tip that allows for greater precision. I'm prone to losing my styluses (styli?), so having the little gizmo that fits into the earphone jack to tether the stylus to the tablet is a very good thing. I'm recommending this one to my friends who are new to tablets. The price is good and the quality is better than expected.

title: Nice sound ...
text: I've used this with both my iPhone and my iPad2, with generally good results. As others have mentioned, the dock accommodates only "portrait" orientation for an iPad, so if you want to watch movies in "wide screen" landscape orientation, you're out of luck. Still, the sound is really good -- I have several other JBL speaker products in my home, and this one seems to match in terms of quality of audio. It's not overly large, either. Definitely would recommend. I've had mine for awhile now, and it's still going strong, with no issues at all.

title: So far, so good ...
text: I wanted to give this a good try out, so I took it along on a cross-country train trip, where my iPad was the only way I had to stay in touch. It weathered the trip quite well. It worked well whether I was using the iPad on my lap (in the train stations during layovers) or on the drop-down table in the sleeping compartment, where I could prop it up using the flap/stand. My only quibble is the lack of just a bit more space to accommodate a stylus. I use a stylus that has a "toggle" that fits in the earphone jack on the iPad so I don't lose it, and it *almost* fits in snuggled between the iPad and inside case spine, but not quite. The cover won't close quite all the way with the stylus there. Still, it's an excellent case, and holds up well to a lot of use/abuse.

title: Works fine for me ....
text: I got this to replace the original cable that came with my iPhone 3GS which had more or less disintegrated (both ends were coming loose). So far, it's working just fine. I use it every day or so to recharge the battery, and I've used it to sync my iPhone with my Mac. I like that it's 6' long, which gives me a little more play. It seems sturdy enough, too.

title: Dependable, no problems at all ...
text: I don't go through a lot of CDs, but so far, I've burned maybe 20 or so, and I've not had a single failure. I use CDs mostly to make copies of mp3s of my own choral compositions (done in Finale) to help my singers learn their parts easier. Playback has been perfect on each disk -- at least, my singers have had no complaints at all. Someone else mentioned the amount of surface space available for adding label info on the disk -- this has been really helpful for me. On many brands, the brand logo and extras are printed in multiple colors (or black) on the surface, and take up a huge amount of real estate. The printed Verbatim logo/etc. on this disk is silver on silver -- relatively plain -- so you can write all over it easily. And I do. Amazon's price is very good, too. Good product, good price, serves a specific purpose -- for casual use, I'd say these are an excellent choice.

title: Small, works great ...
text: I got this to "expand" my MacBook Pro laptop. The MacBook Pro has only two USB connections, one on each side, and I usually have my printer and midi keyboard connected. I often found myself having to unplug something so I could upload photos or sync my iPhone. This little Saitek Mini UFO Hub solved the problem. I can plug it into one of the two USB outlets on the laptop, and immediately I have four new usable connections available. This lets me keep connected everything that I use regularly. It doesn't take up much room, either. This is a great little problem solver.

title: Small, but surprisingly powerful ...
text: I am amazed at how good these speakers are for the size. I've been using them with my iPod nano as well as my laptop, and they're really quite good. Others have mentioned the lack of bass, and I agree -- it could use a little more "oomph" on the low end. But it's not that bad, really -- and the overall sound is really excellent. This little unit is truly portable, with its own little drawstring bag. I've been able to fit everything -- the power cord, the unit, and the device cord -- into the bag. It's a tight fit, but it works. I'm very please with the On Tour speakers -- definitely recommend them if you need something portable to provide more/better sound than your internal laptop speakers or something to connect to an MP3 player. Look for them on sale (I got mine via a Goldbox special).

title: Great addition for your digital camera
text: If you can get only one add-on for your digital camera, let it be this one. I took my Kodak digital camera decked out with this 128MB CompactFlash card on a 6-week road trip. I used the "middle" quality setting for the pictures, and managed to take over 130 photos (the equivalent of 5-6 24-shot rolls of film), filling not anywhere close to half the card (at that setting, the card will store over 300 photos)! I'm not a digital photography technoid by any stretch of the imagination -- I just like capturing memories of the places I go and the things I see. Having the extra memory afforded by this little card meant that I could relax and not worry about running out of space for all my photos. Transferring the photos to my laptop was a piece of cake, and took very little time -- partially a function of the card. I highly recommend this as the *first* accessory/upgrade you purchase for your camera!

title: I *LOVE* this camera!
text: I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal. That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line. After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake! The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name. I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures. For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.

The positive is that the magnetic hold is solid. I think Apple should have perhaps put a slit at the bottom so you can push the cards up from the bottom.
