title: My fourth OMOTON Glass screen protector
text: I have used OMOTON glass screen protectors on my Galaxy S5 and Note 4 Smartphones, my Galaxy 8" ATT tablet and now this Galaxy S2 9.7" tablet for videos and Skype. So count me as a satisfied customer. Included in the sturdy shipping packaging are wet and dry cleaning fabric swatches, a dust cloth, clear directions --everything you need to apply the protector with maximum efficiency and minimum grief. I can't tell you how many film screen protectors I've wasted money on --only to have them show bubbles or rainbows or scratch really easily-- or inadvertently destroyed trying to apply them because of lousy engineering and/or materials quality. OMOTON screens are easy to apply (with common sense preparations of a reasonably dust-free environment), look great, protect well, and ...wait for it... can be re-applied! In my book all that makes OMOTON worth the extra expense...and believe me, nobody paid me for this review.

title: Basic enough for a 1980s set up, but not webOS, 4K UHD or DirectTV...
text: I have a 60" LG webOS 4K UHD TV, a Samsung soundbar, a Sony Blu ray player, and a DirectTV cable box. I'm not a gamer, but I use Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hulu, etc. a LOT. I didn't find this Logitech Harmony remote to be even remotely (pardon the pun) sophisticated enough to handle the series of commands required to change inputs. (I never did find a way to add and name an HDMI 2 input based on the downloadable set up instructions.) Logitech's hardware setup interface is attractive enough, but I didn't find it particularly user-friendly or adequately interactive. Once I had the remote set up, I realized that one has to start from ALL COMPONENTS OFF (including the cable box) to move through the various commands to get to the activity intended ...and, as I said, even that won't take you all the way through without grabbing the old remote. No point for the universal remote then, is there? Returning this item for a refund. Keep trying Logitech.

title: Easy and Classy!!
text: I've used Omoton tempered glass screen protectors for two tablets and three of my most recent smartphones. Trust me, the ease with which these excellent screen protectors are applied --without bubbles, and their capacity for being repeatedly remove and re-positioned perfectly FAR exceed those of flimsy film screens. Omoton screens are pricier, but you absolutely get what you pay for. Outstanding. I recommend them. Make sure you're getting exactly the right size, and order with confidence!

title: Worked adequately --for about 3 months...
text: Lasted for approximately three months, but never really worked as well as expected. I don't know why or how (and maybe I got a lemon), but it appeared to me that the M510 stopped working because the laser and opening thru which it "beamed" became mis-aligned. Got to the point where the cursor wouldn't move at all. I also kept having to go into Control Panel and re-adjust the mouse settings. I switched back to my Logitech M305 mouse and it worked perfectly under the exact same conditions. VERY disappointed; first time I've ever regretted buying a Logitech product.

title: GREAT quality; could be a bit larger
text: Rugged, outstanding quality. The main selling point for me was the inclusion of heavy duty velcro-fastened loops for carrying a collapsible tripod. For a "Large" it does turn out to be a bit smaller than I'd like, since serious digital photography these days requires enough room for batteries, filters, lenses, flash, etc. Very pleased overall.

title: Marketing promises KEPT!!
text: I'm not a buyer of high-end ear buds. At my age my hearing isn't acute enough to hear much of the nuance of music through headphones, but I do like the sound to be much better than if I were holding a can and string up to my ears. That being said, these are the best earphones I've ever owned. When I first put them on, the bass response actually startled me and the middles and highs were present and clear --without any adjustment to my player. The "stays in your ears" feature actually works; you give them a twist in your ear and they stay put, as well as keeping out sweat. You can hear ambient noise just fine, but unless there's a high wind or other competing sound, you continue to hear the audio just fine. I don't agree with other reviewers who report that the plastic earbuds fall off easily. I think those reviewers must be actually pulling the buds off to clean them and I don't believe that's the manufacturers' intentions. I clean mine with a mini-fiber cloth well moistened (but not soggy) with rubbing alcohol without removing them from the actual earpieces. The reason I didn't give these earphone five stars is that there is no inline control --no mute off, or volume control. I like them VERY much, and would buy them again if I needed to replace.

title: After a pair of disappointments, I like it
text: The specifications imply that this tablet is designed to accept a wireless sim card if the user decides to add an additional wireless telephone line. After spending half a day trying to register my purchase with Dell, I was told that, since Dell itself was not the seller, they are not bound to provide warranty coverage. So, Amazon Warehouse buyers might want to figure a Square Trade or other third-party warranty into the purchase price for this Dell. When I asked about the fact that a card slot for a wireless phone sim card is engineered into the Dell Venue, the Dell rep informed me that the Dell engineers originally designed a separate card slot for this purpose, but "in recent models it has been DISCONNECTED!" Which is just about the most nonsensical thing I've heard in a long time. Several years ago, I worked as a technical telephone support person for Denon home theater systems, and realized at that time that audio and telecommunications engineers frequently make completely mystifying. unnecessarily complicated design decisions, so this was not news to me ....It WAS however, a disappointment that cost the Dell Venue 8 two stars on this review. That said, the 2GHz processor and Jelly Bean OS are wicked fast for simple gaming, texting (with "My SMS" or other texting apps from Google Play, synched to your Android phone), etc. It can be synchronized via Wi-Fi, USB tether or Bluetooth. It's a nice size (although a little heavy), and makes a very good Kindle-type unit for reading news, books, online magazines, etc. I've decided I like the tablet very much, but would be a LOT happier with if I could get Dell updates and downloads or install a wireless phone card.

title: New competitor to Square Trade?!
text: The two-year protection policy for my Sony shelf stereo unit was only $8, and was easy enough to buy on Amazon along with the unit, so...why not? As with many service insurance type policies, the proof will be in the repair pudding, when and if necessary.

title: Outstanding sound and value
text: Although I don't use/have any iOs products, I am glad that this compact shelf stereo unit has a COVER for the iPhone/iPod connector to keep out dust. This is certainly not a mini-unit, but it is small enough to fit a deep shelf. It was easy to set up and program, mostly with the remote that works quite well at about a 40-degree angle to either side. I loaded a USB thumb drive with around 390 music files, all of which are playing flawlessly (mp3 and/or WMA), with a way to shuffle or random play from one artist or from all files. The different EQ settings could be more varied in tone and effect; however, I'm 67 years old with some mid-range hearing loss, so that might be my fault. The bass response is fine even without the bass boost feature, and vocals, especially high male and women's voices, can seem a little harsh. Volume is fine without distortion, even at enough cranking for me --not sure how it would satisfy a head banger! My only "like to haves" for this unit include a way to mute the radio or CD playbacks; however, the volume control is very responsive so that's not really a problem for the radio, and one can pause the CD and USB file playback. And of course, I can't imagine what Sony was thinking not including a regular headphone jack. It's not the most elegant-looking set I've ever owned, but I'm quite satisfied, especially for the cost to value ratio I got on this unit. Very pleased!

title: Electronics can become TOO small...
text: After a career in advertising, during which I've been around video cameras of all sizes, weights and shapes, this is my first camcorder for personal use. After one day of monkeying around with it, I'm delighted --with a couple of reservations. It appears to be of very good quality, feels lightweight and yet sturdy (with the exception of the rather stringy hand-strap/lanyard) and the user interfacing seems straightforward and intuitive, once you figure out where things are. I'll be back in a few weeks or months to describe my experiences with the software, data downloading and manipulation, etc. The main criticism I have --more of an observation, really-- is that, for my somewhat arthritic hands, operating the controls are challenging because of their placement on the camera and because the thing is so darned small. (As in the length of a soft drink can --at only 2/3 of the diameter!) This may be simply because I'm unaccustomed to using camcorders, or indeed holding any camera as one does with the JVC GZ-HM550. Many reviewers have complained that this 2010 model still has scrolling and MENU, OK, and INFO buttons rather than Mac-style rolling touch screens. This doesn't bother me, although it takes a very delicate touch to get to the right menu selection on this camera, because they zip by so rapidly under a man's stubby fingers. Low light results seem more than adequate, especially for daytime indoor shooting, and the shake reduction seems to me to be working very well. The zoom function is smooth and quiet, but --for me-- will be difficult getting used to because the toggle from wide to close-up is at the top rear, where it's difficult for me to reach with my admittedly somewhat inflexible fingers. As I said, I'm new to these mini-cameras, so they may be designed for two-handed use...?? All in all, I think it will be a very good mid-range camcorder with the advisory that people with large hands might find a somewhat physically larger brand/model easier to handle. GET A WARRANTY. (Square Trade offers a good policy against damage, etc.) This JVC model is small enough, the finish glossy enough, that I feel it would be fairly easy to drop it.

title: Works like a charm!
text: Based on the reviews of these wireless phones, I was concerned that they might not be large enough for my head and neck, and if said head and neck were any larger/thicker, they would likely be too small. (I wear a size 7-1/8 hat and my neck is 16 inches in diameter.) However, they fit fine, and seem nicely comfortable and lightweight. The phones do seem rather delicate, so I'm not sure they'd do well at the bottom of a gym bag or left unprotected in direct sunlight on a hot car seat or dash. I had no problem charging and pairing the headset with my Samsung Infuse 4G i997. The sound quality is not bad for the price point. I found I had to dial back on the bass settings using my Poweramp player, but the player seems to work well with the phones. I also bought a Kinovo Bluetooth USB adapter for my laptop, but haven't attempted that pairing yet. (Also haven't made or received any phone calls, but music quality and comfort are my primary focus.) Overall, three hours after receiving the items I'm very happy with the "Kinovo Experience." Will re-post if my opinion changes.

title: Surprisingly good sound REVISED
text: I just received this Sanjean RCR-10 and set it up. The good news is that the sound is wonderfully rich and balanced for a little radio. First bedside table clock radio I've ever had that sounds good enough to crank up loud to fill my whole apartment with music. I'm impressed, and I'm not easily impressed. On the other hand, it seems that, the more sophisticated these digital electronics get, the more challenging and puzzling they are to set up. It could well be that these companies need to shell out a little more money for decent technical writers to produce more thorough step-by-step setup instructions. OR, they could simply design the units so they're easier to set up for those of us who are not geeks or electronics engineers. It's not all that terribly frustrating; just be ready for several minutes of trial and error ...and pray you don't have a power outage! (The unit also offers a back-up batteries feature, so I wouldn't forget to do that.) The RCR-10 is solid, substantial (not flimsy or lightweight) and attractive. The display also includes basic metadata indicating station and artist. The only thing missing for me --since I use an Android phone as my personal music player-- would be a little close-able cover for the empty iPod docking slot. It's going to be a dust collector in my house. UPDATE: I'm revising my five star review down to three stars, because after a couple of months' use, I've realized this thing is REALLY a pain in the butt to re-progam. Even turning the alarm pre-set volume down a notch requires that you go through a big long procedure, as if you were setting the alarm for the first time. The same thing is true if you think you'd like to awaken to some other type of music station. Hard to do anything on the fly; if you need to make a change, be prepared to sit down for twenty minutes with the OM open for reference to accomplish even the most simple adjustment. Sanjean needs to make these beautiful radios MORE USER FRIENDLY!

title: Fast, compact, dependable
text: There's not much more to say about this little Patriot Xporter 16GB thumb drive, other than it fulfills all its marketing claims. I had been using an HP thumb drive to back up my work (graphic and text) and found it surprisingly slow, the plastic housing flimsy. This is the second of two Patriot drives I've now purchased, and find them blazingly fast, and very nicely designed. The quality is heartening when there are so many cheap, unnecessarily oversized thumb drives for sale both online and in office supply and big box media stores like Best Buy. You won't be disappointed with a little Patriot Xporter Rage!

title: Streamlined and versatile
text: I use a small, older Toshiba laptop with a cooling lap desk. I wanted a device that would give me additional USB ports without the clutter of a long cord sticking out to get tangled or a loose-hanging dongle. This notebook hub plugs directly into one of my side USB ports and adds FOUR more, one of which can be adjusted to a different angle. I added a Patriot XT Rage 16GB stick drive for auto backup of my work files. Works GREAT for synching my Android phone, etc. I looked for a long time for precisely this configuration, and I've been Very Pleased with it.

title: Excellent gift idea!
text: After purchasing a larger Logitech cooling pad (with speakers) for my laptop and being very pleased with it, I purchased this N200 as a Christmas gift for a dear friend. She doesn't spend as much time on computer as I do, but she reports that she really likes how this lightweight, quiet pad "cools down" the computing she was experiencing while working with the notebook directly on her lap. So, I'd conclude from my happy camper's reports that the N200 is all it's cracked up to be!

title: Spent more time buffering than actually streaming music
text: Everywhere I looked online, there were nothing but the highest words of praise for this radio. It's an attractive, compact unit, with reasonably good sound and lots of options for add ons, additional speakers, usb ports, etc. However, I had such a difficult time getting it to find my home network, I had to completely reconfigure my router (and two computers as a consequence) in order to get the radio to "find" my home network and accept my password key. The enclosed setup instructions are so inadequate that most of the information and procedures required to sign up for services like Pandora, I Heart Radio, Rhapsody, NPR, etc., were completely missing from the manual. The only indications of how to start appeared in the radio's display window, instructing me to go online to do the setup. After some perseverance, I finally figured out how to use the Reciva Internet Radio site to connect the radio with the services I've been using with my computers for years. Once I finally got the thing to start streaming (about 4 frustrating hours after I began the set up) I realized that, even less than three feet from my router, the unit stayed in buffering mode more than it actually played music, no matter what bps settings I tried. I don't really know much about the technical end of audio streaming, but my MediaLink router works fine with my two portable computers, and streams video and music from services like Pandora and Rhapsody with no glitches whatever. I didn't see much point in listening to 10 seconds of a song, then waiting through 15 or 20 while the unit's memory silently buffered so it could continue. Even if you're not a digital audio newbie, if you're looking for straightforward setup and easy operation, this AIN'T IT. I may look further into wireless digital radio --but I doubt it, at least not in the near future.

title: Nifty little mouse!!
text: I purchased this USED-LIKE NEW from a seller who either didn't have or didn't bother to include installation instructions and other materials with the mouse. But I found that the Logitech website [ ] has all the necessary drivers, matched to your Operating System. Very easy to download to my Windows XP laptop and install. The mini-USB receiver is small enough not to interfere with other USB devices on a row of closely-spaced ports. I like the compact size of the mouse, and I'm planning to buy another one to go with my desktop PC running Vista. Might be too small for the hands of some people with very large hands. Otherwise, what's not to like!

title: Be patient while setting up...
text: I purchased this router to create a small two-computer network in my apartment. My PC is a refurbished and souped up Gateway running Windows Vista, and I bought an older Toshiba laptop, also refurbished and running Windows XP Home Edition. I wanted to be able to sit in my living room or on the patio while working once in awhile, rather than being chained to my home office PC. No gaming consoles, DVRs, or other components to connect. The setup literature and accompanying CD shipped with the router are invaluable, easy to understand, even for a non-techie like me. However, don't expect your setup to proceed with no glitches! You may have to reset your cable modem two or three times, or restart the various components two or three times. Take your time, follow directions, keep your wits about you, and think about possible causes and likely solutions and you should have no trouble setting up this router. The day after my order, I also received a lengthy, substantive email from Mediabridge Products, thanking me for my order and supplying me with all kinds of background, links, and telephone technical support information, so I felt confident that I had resources handy during the setup if necessary. So far the router is working like a charm. I recommend it, especially if you're interested in a fairly simple LAN setup!

title: Amazing value at this price!
text: I'm not a digital photography geek, and I've been working with lower-end Olympus and Canon A-Series Powershot cameras, primarily for static close-up work (for ebay postings). I never found those cameras to be easy to use or at all useful for on-the-fly, outdoor shooting. With little or no absorption of the Panasonic DCM-FZ35 owner's manual, I've been able to shoot some really nice outdoor snapshots using both the LCD and the viewfinder. The various settings are almost fun to find and experiment with on the DCM-FZ35's display. Overall, an exciting lower-to-mid range camera for amateurs who can't afford a DSLR! I LIKE IT!!

title: TERRIBLE picture quality and mediocre design
text: I purchased this player as a replacement because I clumsily killed my Toshiba SD-P1900 9" player. I figured, even with a half-inch loss of screen size, I'd still be in the game, right? Panasonic's a great brand name, right? WRONG. This particular Panasonic model not only has lousy picture quality and no remote, but there are no fast forward or fast rewind functions other than skipping all the way ahead or all the way back to the beginnings of scenes. I'm a film buff, so I like to be able to back up two or three seconds to check out that explosion in fps detail, or to move forward or backward at 2X or 4X or 8X, etc. Plus, if you extend the adjustable screen forward as shown in most illustrations, you cannot see or reach the control buttons without moving it out of your way. I'm no video product engineer, but I hope my impression of the VERY inadequate picture quality and overall poor design of this player makes you think twice. Go for the Toshiba instead!

text: I got this with my smart lightbulb. I've enjoyed it a great deal. It was very easy to set up.

title: Not intended to be a computer monitor.
text: I was hugely disappointed when the first one that arrived had a shattered screen. I didn't have my hopes up when I hit the replace button, but the second one came and the screen is fine. I now have it mounted on my wall next to my primary monitor. One strange quirk is that my universal remote turns both of my TVs on and off with one button. With this TV, I have an additional step of selecting what it's to be used for from the main menu before it's ready to go. Overall, it's lightweight and the design is fairly clean looking.

title: MUCH faster loading!
text: I have two of these drives in my computer now. One for the operating system and "work" type applications and the other for my games. Everything stored on these drives loads a great deal faster than any of the things stored on my SSD. If you can only get your hands on one of these, I recommend using it for your OS and the programs you'll spend the most time on.

title: Not an upgrade from M570 for me.
text: I was looking to upgrade my gaming mouse. I was excited to try this one, but when I got it plugged in, there were two things that immediately upset me. First, it didn't use the Logitech SetPoint software all my other Logitech devices have used for many, many years. Instead, I had to install a new software to customize the buttons. Second, the mouse acceleration I've become accustomed to was eliminated from this mouse in the software. In its place, they added a "precision mode" button that required me to take my thumb off the trackball to toggle between fast movement and slow movement. As a gamer, this is unacceptable. I loved everything else about this mouse, but it didn't work for me, since my primary use is gaming.

title: NOT for people with astigmatism!
text: I have astigmatism, so for me, it was impossible to "dial in" either lens for a good viewing experience, let alone both. I was really excited to try it and very sad it didn't work for me.

title: NOT for gaming.
text: The extra buttons (back and forward) are in an awkward place. For me, that meant I could either be using those or the ball. As a mouse for things like browsing the web, checking email, watching movies, etc. it wasn't bad. It just isn't laid out to make an effective gaming mouse.

title: NOT FOR GAMING!!!
text: Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email: "Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support. We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications. We appreciate your time and patience." To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised. Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.

title: Relatively easy to get Google Play store on without rooting.
text: My phone is getting nearing the end of its life. I don't need all the features of a phone, so this was an inexpensive alternative. I was hesitant, because it's advertised that it's not compatible with Google Play. Out-of-the-box, that is true, but with a PC and a quick search of the directions, it is readily available. For me, that is a HUGE bonus, because if my phone had died completely, I would have lost access to all my 2 factor authentication apps. Also, I love Alexa. In my experience, she's vastly superior to Cortana and Siri. With Alexa, I can find out what time it is without having to sear my retinas looking at a painfully blinding phone screen.

I'm still not even sure what it was that finally fixed it. The whole time I was trying to set it up, it would emit a loud scratchy sound for about a second, then be silent for half a second, and this would repeat with the sound getting louder and louder each time. I'm still worried it may have done damage to my headset speakers and my soundbar. Once it started working, it was fine, but getting to that point was a huge hassle.

I’ve tried troubleshooting this multiple ways including, forgetting the device completely and pairing it again (exactly according to instructions in box) and turning my phone completely off and on again to no avail. That had finally started to fail in some of the plug ins, and I was also reducing the items plugged into it. Now I just have the TV, sound bar, DVR, and DVD player that needed to be plugged in. On a side note, I had thought I would be able to remove the cover to my wall plus as this screws into the wall plug space, but the gap on top of the unit does not cover the opening in the wall, so I had to put the cover back on, but just removed the screw that attached the cover and used the screw to attached this unit into the outlet.

title: A good computer, after some tweaking
text: Not a bad laptop for the price. The laptop itself is in brand new condition. But because it's a model from 2016, it did require a Google search and a visit to the HP support website for a BIOS update for the computer to recognize the latest Windows 10 updates, and the computer also required an update there to fix a VCRUNTIME140.dll error. I also kept getting an error message requiring an update to HP 3D DriveGuard after the latest Windows 10 updates. In other words, expect to do some tinkering with your computer to get this refurb up and running properly. (One other little thing: When Amazon shipped the laptop, they overlooked removing from the box the original owner's receipt from a well-known national department store chain, which showed that buyer paid about $80 less for this laptop than I did as a refurb.)

So recently added ethernet cable by using this dongle from Amazon: Plugable USB 2.0 to 10/100 Fast Ethernet LAN Wired Network Adapter for MacBook, Chromebook, Windows, Linux, Wii, Wii U & Switch Game Console. To get it to work, I plugged into USB port with ethernet cable. Then to get the TV to stop using the Wi-Fi connection, I reset wireless network and left it blank in settings. But now that I have heard the sound I will plainly state that I will not be updating my speaker system anytime soon. I am extremely happy with the sound. Voices were also quite true. Amazing. I also played a few latin jazz albums and they were magnificent. Ella Fitzegerald also never sounded so good. What a find. Purchased the speakers without hearing them, strictly on the expert reviews. Best speaker system for less than a thousand dollars, and I only paid 400.00 Great find. I guess I was very lucky.

title: Great tablet... TERRIBLE keyboard/case
text: The tablet is quite good. A real improvement over previous models. While the concept of a dex keyboard is nice, this execution is lacking if you want to use it as BOTH a tablet and laptop alternative. Moving around will cause the keyboard to attach and detach quickly, which will in turn cause the tablet to go to sleep. The placement of the pen holder makes is absolutely certain that thing will be gone within a day or so. The price for what you get here is outrageous. It is a cheap case and cheap keyboard, stuck together. If you are ONLY going to use this as a laptop and NEVER a tablet, this might work, but you can still find alternatives for 1/4 the price. If you plan to interchange use... don't buy this.

title: Protection and Functionality
text: This cover is actually perfect in so many ways, to protect the tablet from the tough use my 6 yr old son gives it. He has had this tablet for nearly 2 years, and I think after the previous demise of several other tablets, he may have actually learned not to drop it, so I can't say how well this case would have fared in his 4 yr old hands, for protection of the tablet, but so far...so good, for now. The grooves are deep enough to actually hold the tablet up, unlike other cases. The strap that closes it, for transporting is great, because it assures that the cover doesn't fall open and expose the tablet to a direct/unprotected fall. All the cut-outs are where they should be, but the negative, if there is one, is that the power cord has to be positioned just right to get the proper contact for charging, and the portion where you put the tablet isn't snug enough to keep it from obstructing camera, without constant adjustment, and it may even get worse with wear.

title: Doesn't Stay Plugged in Most Devices - Not Comfortable
text: I purchased this for my son, to replace his previous headphones, because he had nibbled through the cord sheathing. I liked that this was cheaper, cute, and had one wire off one of the ear pieces, instead of the kind that look like a necklace that come from each ear and rest on your chest. I started using these headphones on his E-Reader and it just doesn't stay plugged in, because the L-shaped plug doesn't allow it to go in far enough, and it easily pulls/falls out. Now, I am going to go buy the slightly more expensive, but much better quality Kidz Gear headphones. I couldn't have known that this was really going to be an issue, until I got them, so I just wanted to help let others know. My son, today, after using the headphones for the first time of more than 20 minutes, he declared, "These are hurting me." So, my four year old would like to add that to this review, as well. He was always really comfortable in the other headphones, even able to fall asleep with them on (even though they look bulky, they were even comfortable to me).

title: Kind of the gold standard on Earbuds when used with Apple Macs/iPhones/iPads
text: The Apple AirPods Pro are a definite step up from the regular AirPods, stay in your ears well (the Beats Fit Pro does slightly better here, but the microphone is not as good as on the AirPods Pro), have good noise cancellation (Bose and Sony might be a tad better, but these are very good), and excellent microphone pickup. If you are going to be in a loot of phone calls, eMeetings (Zoom, Webex, Facetime, etc.) these are very much the ones to get. About the only thing these are not good for would be high head movement activities (athletics), there the Beats Fit Pro does better, but these are on a par or better than the competitive Sony or Bose variants (which are larger, so easier to dislodge). Also, once paired with Apple devices, you can just move them around to be used with whatever you happen to be doing, iPad or iPhone or MacBook, they autoswitch, don't have to be re-paired, and also handle Siri commands.

title: Decent Kindle Oasis case at a great price

The texture on the MoKo case makes it extremely easy to carry and hold onto, you are unlikely to have it slip and drop the e-reader. Protection appears to be top notch. The case has the further advantage of being able to fold and sit on a table or desk such that you can read easily. I would have given this five stars, if the magnets had been just a little stronger. They are adequate and work, in terms of the e-reader turning off and on, but you have to get the alignment just right in terms of the stand function. Still, at the price, this case is hard to beat. A great value.

title: One of the best cases for an iPad Air, particularly if you have apps that run in Portrait mode
text: The rooCASE Oragami Case seems to be currently at or near the top of the cases, the big advantage of this case being the number and variations of orientations, including both portrait and landscape, and at the price point, is hard to beat. The oragami cover is ingenious, you can fold it up all sorts of ways, the iPad Air has a lot of applications that fairly beg for portrait orientation (reading a book, newspaper, etc.). The conventional Apple case supports only landscape, as do a number of competitors (the CaseCrown Omni is one of the better conventional ones). The Moshi and O!Case are also oragami cases, although the designs differ some. The rooCASE has a more rubberized or grippy exterior, key because it's less likely to slip and get dropped. Protection is generally pretty good, but the CaseCrown does a little better on edge protection, the openings on the rooCase tend to be U-shaped, the CaseCrown is more O-Shaped, but otherwise they are very similar. The Moshi has one advantage, in that it has a back magnet, that lets it stay open better in book mode. The rooCASE actually has magnets that keep it closed pretty well, but it lacks a back magnet. The rooCase front cover of course folds up to support quite a number of variations or angles, which is a big advantage over conventional cases, and on a desk or table, is plenty stable. The microfiber front interior is nice, it tends to help keep the screen clean, but it is worth noting that the orgami pattern tends to show up in the fingerprints and grease, so you do need to clean the screen from time to time. rooCASE also shuts off the iPad Air screen when you close it, a very useful feature. The end result is still pretty light and easy to carry, in keeping with the iPad Air design point. Why not 5 stars? rooCase is very close, but they could improve the edge coverage/protection, and add a back magnet (ala Moshi), and NuGuard KX probably has the better back protection (at the cost of some bulk), but at its price-point, front and back protection, oragami design that lets you pick multiple orientations and angles, the rooCASE is pretty much unbeatable, and worthy of consideration at any price.

We have a fair number of projectors and older large displays around the place, and you run into them also when traveling to other companies, this lets you jack into them. title: They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can contro
text: This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused. I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on..... So, the radio.... This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time).. This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in. There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle. I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes. This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No. When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio. Some cons: No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine. This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really. Antennas: Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from. Verdict: This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come. I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner. I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner. Edit: Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver. Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner. The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed. The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer. See my photos. The photos ended up sideways.... trying to fix this..... Amazon, can you turn my photos upright?

title: Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between ...
text: I received this cooler today and installed it along with two new 140mm front panel case fans. I have an AMD based system running stock cooling that came with the case and hardware components. My system temps running stock cooling were way to high, idyling at temps around 45c to 50c and when running demanding applications temps would shoot way up into the 80's and 90's sometimes causing shutdowns. I kept remembering statements from AMD advising consumers to keep the down blowing fans installed but I decided to try a liquid cooling solution out of desperation. My case is a Corsair Spec 02. My motherboard is a Asus Sabertooth 990FX R2.0. The processor is a AMD FX-8320. The graphics processor is a Sapphire Radeon R9 380. That AMD FX 8320 runs hot, extremely hot also the NB and SB components on the Asus MB run very hot. My system temps were way to high, I had to do something. Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between the two 120mm fans does fit in this case. I followed the manufacturer recommendation and configured both fans to push air inward into the case. This case has perforated holes in the roof for ventilation and this allows used air to evacuate out of the case assuming the fans are configured to blow inward which will push air out those top vents. The two big 140mm red LED fans I installed in the front panel are configured to pull air inward and I set them to run at 100% speed (1000 RPM), they are Cougar Red LED's, very high quality fans that move a lot of air silently. This Corsair H80i V2 has got to be the best liquid cooler available for smaller cases like mine, it has dropped my system temps by 20 to 30 degrees C instantly. I am seeing system temps lower than I've ever seen them since I built the system back in December 2015. This fridge is rocking my system. Cool is good, the cooler the better when it comes to computer systems. I have Core Temp 1.0 RC6 installed and it is showing my CPU temps idling at 13C - 15C... That is chill. Chill is good. Thanks Corsair, this liquid cooler system is awesome. Thanks Amazon for the excellent service and thanks UPS for being the most dependable carrier on earth. My system purrs away at 15C, OMG this is awesome.

title: Astounding powers........
text: Install this on your compatible motherboard and you will think you have installed the heart of Superman in your computer. I am in awe of this prodigy of modern computer technology. Edit: I've had this processor running in my new build for about a month now. I was being annoyed by the stock cooler fan buzzing at very high rpm whenever the heat rose to moderate levels like 52C. The fan was really buzzing like a little aircraft prop at full throttle for takeoff. It would crank up to 6600 rpm at the slightest provocation like CPU temp hitting 50C. I decided to take everything apart down to the motherboard coming out and all components attached to it. When I pulled the cooler off the CPU and looked at the thermal paste situation, OMG what a mess. The stock thermal paste was not covering the whole area, it was reduced to a gummy, sticky glue. I had to pull very hard to get the cooler off the CPU. I cleaned the cooler base and the CPU thoroughly and applied a pea sized spot of Arctic Silver 5 then reassembled everything. Instant cure. Instant quieter fan. Instant low CPU temps andQUIET!AMD needs to stop using whatever they're putting on the coolers and just include a syringe of a high quality thermal paste for customers to apply themselves because whatever they're using is junk. The stock cooler and fan they include with the fx 8320 are very high quality but the pre applied thermal paste is garbage. Just apply new first quality thermal paste, you don't need to spend big dollars on third party hardware and I suspect those of you who have installed new coolers and seen great results is because of the new thermal paste used during installation. The fx 8320 is a very powerful processor don't smoke it because of 10 cents worth of cheap thermal paste, use the best for your investment and this hot CPU will give many years of great performance.

I took it out today to take some pics and there is a thick, black line through the LCD screen that comes through on the pics! I have NEVER dropped or so much as roughly bumped this camera. I was always thrilled with the pic quality, but for the money - I should have been able to get many, many more pictures for the life of the camera. I will NEVER AGAIN buy another Olympus camera. It's sad that we cannot expect quality products anymore!

title: I BLAME THE KINDLE FIRE!
text: I purchased 2 of these, as I have had enough of buying Amazon's charger at more than twice the cost - none of the power sources lasts very long and I believe there is a problem with the Fire itself that causes this failure. The Kindle Fire is completely useless without a power source, so I just have to keep buying them. However, as I have said before, I will never buy another Kindle - KINDLE IS POOR QUALITY!

title: Not great
text: I received my Fire on Dec 31st 2011 as a B-day gift. I was thrilled! Sadly, my elation was short-lived. Less than five months later I had blown pixels in the display and had to have a replacement. Before you assume I'm a careless person with my 'toys' - I'm not, just the opposite in fact. I received my replacement Fire, reloaded all the stuff I needed and went on my merry way, sure that I would use it until I wanted to upgrade - NOT SO! About three months later, I was again on the phone with a service rep explaining that the charging port was loose and the unit no longer charged. So, I am on my THIRD Fire. A few days into my third Fire, literally, I had to call and get a new charger, as the one they sent only charged for about 30 seconds at a time and that was it. My complaint is that Amazon is selling poor quality electronics and I was nothing more than their guinea pig and I don't appreciate it at all! I will NEVER buy another Kindle of any kind. To be fair, Amazon's customer service, for the most part, throughout this ordeal has been acceptable to good, but my gift was not Amazon's customer service! I have no reason to believe that Amazon's latest and greatest are better tested or higher quality than their last series. Not happy!

title: Fantastic

title: Love this card!
text: I almost always buy MSI video cards and motherboards but this is by far the nicest video card I've owned. It immediately pushed my Win 7 graphics performance to 7.9 and runs my dual HD monitors at max settings on every game I've tried. I do admit though I'm not big on first person shooter games so I haven't tried it a lot with those, but for the games I do play it's great. I have one game which uses over 75% of the 2gb of video ram and it runs as smoothly as any other. I also love that it overclocks by itself. I can watch the speed change as it needs to; much better than having the card overclocked all the time. Now I'm saving up for a 2nd one!

text: I am very pleased with this monitor. As others have mentioned, the stand is great. Sometimes I sit up while using the computer, other times I lean back and this stand makes it very easy to get the perfect view no matter my position. I also like the onscreen menus which are controlled by buttons on the side. I find that much easier to use than the little pivot button some monitors have. And, unlike some monitors which are labeled 24 inch but are really only 23.6, this one is actually 24 diagonal inches. I love it and based on this monitor, BenQ is now my brand of choice.

text: This power supply came nicely packaged and looks great. It feels and looks solid and I rest easy knowing it is powering my computer. The only con I can think of is I don't care for the sata connector wires, they are flat and rather stiff cables instead of being pliable and wrapped. Update: After just moving my drives around and installing a couple new ones I loath the sata power cables included with this. They are too stiff and the connectors are upside down for a bottom mounted power supply. Using extension/splitters was the only way to get power to all of my drives. At this point I very much regret buying this thing and certainly won't buy another. If you only have 1 or 2 hard drives it's no problem, but if you have a bunch of drives, it will be a nightmare. Find something with more pliable and correctly oriented sata leads.

text: It also works with Harmony remotes. It just doesn't do anything especially well. But for 7 bucks I don't see how anyone can complain. I took C. Watson's advice and set it up in my harmony software with the model he suggested and then did a little personal tweaking and it works fine, not perfect, but good enough. Having tried over the years numerous hand held mouse controllers I have found them all hard to use and unreliable. This one is probably the worst but then I don't use it to control the mouse pointer, just to control media player; pause, play, next, previous, full screen or not and mute. For these functions it is adequate and I don't regret buying it. For those who need and want full mouse functionality from a remote control, this is sure to disappoint. But for those with needs similar to mine, this is a reasonable choice.

title: Mine had a problem, will be returning it
text: This card is exactly what I wanted, small with low power requirements. I used it in a home theater computer and it played every HD movie I tested smoothly and cleanly. The problem is there is something funny with it's temperatures. At first it was fine, running 42 to 53 degrees but then on the 3rd day I turned it off to install a network card and burned myself on the video card's heat sink. When I had the computer back up and running I checked the video card's temperature and it was idling at 103 degrees, Celsius. I let it run for a few more minutes while I installed Evga's precision software to verify that temp and it agreed with hwmonitor. I shut it down. A couple hours later I brought it up again, this time it was idling at 63 degrees and didn't vary much from that temp for the next several hours. The next day it was up in the eighties and then again nineties. Today it stayed around 71. I really don't have a good idea what is wrong with it and I'm not going to spend anymore time worrying about it for a brand new card. It's going back.

title: Impressive
text: I have put together many, many computers using cases of all shapes, sizes and costs. Dollar for dollar this case is hands down the best value I've ever seen. As others have noted the materials are a bit flimsy but this is a computer case, not the frame for a tank. As long as it isn't abused it should last and give good service for years. And I like that is fairly light weight, many cases that are "sturdy" are also on the heavy side. By the time you have them loaded with a good power supply and several hard drives they begin to feel like a tank when you need to move them. The cutouts and gaps to make routing cables easy are nice, they not only improve the appearance but also help air flow freely through the case. I was a little worried about sharp edges but have not found any, which is good because knowing me if there was even one I would have cut myself on it. I read several reviews which mention the hard drive rails being difficult and backwards so I wasn't sure what to expect. At first I was a little confused about how the hard drives are meant to be installed but once I understood it, it makes perfect sense and is no problem to work with. If you have right angled power and data cable ends you can mount the drives facing left or right which might make things easier if you have several drives installed. Another thing that both surprised and pleased me was when I was installing the power supply I noticed there were two extra holes which makes it possible to mount the ps either right side up or upside down. I am not a huge fan of bottom mount for power supplies and as others have said, it can cause problems if the leads for motherboard power are not long enough. Mine just barely reached to the cpu power connector after running it up the rear of the case, resting as it is on the motherboard and running under the video card. I have extensions on order though I'm sure I could get by for the life of the ps as it is now. I like the long, thin blue light on the front for power on though the green light for hard drive activity is a bit hard to see. Most of all though, I love the paint. No more of that ugly, dingy looking gray metal with thoughts of how I want to paint it black. I am not an expert on such things but I believe the paint is baked on giving it a very nice texture and appearance. This is a case I would not have been disappointed by if I had paid 60 dollars. Getting it from amazon for 36 with free prime shipping is one of the best deals I've ever found. Three cheers to NZXT !!! title: Very Pleased
text: I bought this to sit on top of my i5-2500K and I couldn't be happier. I love the way it looks through the case's side window and it is so quiet and smooth. The installation was easy enough, anyone with mechanical ability should have no trouble and the chrome and polished metals are great and give it a much better appearance than most cpu coolers. I was surprised when I first saw the box, it is not as big as I expected. Though not small it is not huge and doesn't feel like a brick in your hand. I think other coolers available could keep temps a bit lower but mine are fine. I keep my 2500 overclocked to 4.2 and it idles at 42c and under load gets up to about 60c on a hot day. I don't believe in "burn-in" or "stress" testing but would expect core temps to near or pass 80c during such tests. I also love that it is from Intel - who better than them to know what their processors need? I would recommend this fan to all except possibly severe gamers who need every bit of cooling they can get.

title: Not great, I sent it back
text: This card was mostly a disappointment. The performance was no where near what I expected and it was so loud I could scarcely stand to be in the same room with it. I sent it back and got a gtx 460 which I am very happy with.

title: Great Hard Drive
text: I have 9 or 10 Hitachi 1 tb drives and am very pleased with them. They may not be the fastest or quietest drives in the world, though I never hear them and they seem plenty fast to me, but in two years the only one I've had fail had been improperly packaged by amazon and was beat to death in shipping. I am currently using a pair of these in my main computer in a raid array. Using raid 0 on the first array partition, to boot from, and raid 1 on the 2nd for mirroring. Before I started using hitachi drives I was losing a wd or seagate roughly every other month. It was all I could do to keep up with the rma's and I completely lost track of how much data I'd lost. I should note I have approximately 20 hard drives spread over 5 computers. With the size of modern hard drives an effective backup method is very hard to achieve. Few people can afford tape drive backups for home, I certainly can't and dvdrw disk simply do not hold enough to be cost or time effective. After so many wd and seagate crashes I have begun using many drives simply for mirroring and I am pleased that with the hitachi drives I have not lost a single byte. The only issue i have noticed is occasionally, maybe once a day, the subwoofer will make a light 'thump' one time, even if the TV is off. This didn't happen before switching to this unit. title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
text: I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation. The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did. After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great. Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

title: Just WOW!!
text: Cut the cord with cable 2 days ago but wanted local channel access. Streaming services are nice but you are forever going from one platform to another to channel surf which I find super frustrating. Good old tv with antenna is so much easier. This antenna took less than 5 minutes to set up. I put it up in the window. Channel scanned and was watching 43 channels like that! All crystal clear pictures. I must say that most towers are about 40 miles away from my home ,all kinda clustered together. They sit southeast of me and where I have the antenna sitting is close to southeasterly. Kind of a no brainer but I would suggest looking up tower locations in your area. The map will display channels broadcast by this tower... and try to configure your antenna in that general direction. Makes sense to me. Very pleased with this antenna and purchase. Cut the cord with cable. You won't be disappointed :) UPDATE: This is an indoor antenna and they work best in a window and pointed towards the transmission towers in your area. You will get max channels that way. That's been my experience but I opted to use the double stick tape provided and mount mine outside taped to a beam on my metal pergola. Channel availability jumped up immediately upon rescanning so outdoor antennas are the way to go...and yes this is not truly recommended for outdoor use.. I went from 36 channels inside to 55 mounted outside the same window..3 months and I have had no issues with outside use. It hasn't fallen once..the weather has been all over the map..from sunny, rainy, and even the current blizzard conditions we have experienced...that includes rain, freezing rain, and snow. Maybe it will crap out over time but I paid 15 bucks for over 50channels. If it lasts a year thats only $1.25 a month to watch tv which is hella lot cheaper than cable. I'm super satisfied!!

title: Acer gets 5 stars....Amazon gets a zillion.
text: I did a little homework and this machine, especially at the price looked excellent. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them. Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon. And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load. The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.

The picture is pretty good--when it works--but too often I cannot finish playing a 4K movie Blu-ray before it stutters and then stops. After that, the only way to get it going again is to unplug the player, wait a minute, then plug it back in... which is what Sony Help Line said to do, but is intolerable. Unit also will not detect Dolby Vision discs; you must know the disc is so encoded, then manually activate that feature, THEN manually de-activate it after the movie is over! I applied all online updates, yet none fixed these issues. Returned the player for refund, as it is a not something I want to struggle with for another minute--no matter how inexpensive it is or how good the picture is (when working).

So, maybe they will work if you don’t run your iPad or iPhone at the same time, I don’t know. Maybe this one cord was a dud. However, I was seriously annoyed. This set my whole morning off as I need the iPad charged. I swear, why on earth does it seem an impossibility to find cords that work and work for a long time. I’m not hard on cords and yet they either don’t work or die very soon. Yes, the colors are great but I don’t care about that. I want cords that do their job. This one most certainly didn’t. I purchased due to the glowing reviews. I am sorry I cannot add my name to that list. My advise: look elsewhere if you need your iPad to charge while you use it.

title: Fantastic
text: Ok, for some reason...and I blame my own stupidity, I thought I was just ordering the ear loops (it clearly says headphones with ear loops so I have no idea what I was thinking) and thought "the price is a bit steep" but I needed them and so coughed up the dough. I got the package and thought "It came with earphones?" (yeah...that stupidity was still hanging on apparently) and then I read the packing invoice and "poof" my idiocy (at least about this) vanished. I groaned, thinking "oh yeah, I need another pair of ear buds like a hole in the head" but I needed the loops. So...I attached the loops to another set of earphones and thought "Ok. They fit. This will work" and then I thought I should check and see if I wanted to keep the ear buds so I plugged them into my computer and turned on iTunes. WOW. Let me just say these are the best ear buds I have ever had (to think I thought "maybe I should just toss the ear buds as I don't need any more...ok so the stupidity was still clinging to me somewhat). They sound is sharp and crisp. They come with different heads for different size ear canals. They are...in short, just amazing. So as it turned out,the clips were the bonus. The clips work FANTASTIC and you can put them on other ear buds but these buds are truly amazing. As it is....for the price....this is a steal. I have had headphones that cost over $100 and these are better (I prefer buds to the over the ear headphones). I have also had ear buds that cost A LOT of money and these beat them, hands down. I recommend these HIGHLY. The ear loops and earbuds are fantastic! You won't be sorry. I have not tried to jog in them so I cannot answer to that but for me, these are worth double or triple what I paid for them

text: I paired this cord with an Apple brand lightening charger after reading MANY horror stories of sparks, overheating, charging failures, etc. and I’m really pleased with it. It flexes, but is still quite stiff. The little adapter is nice, but so far is living in a drawer. My only complaint, which is minor and will not apply to many users, is that the actual lightening tip end is longer than I need it to be. I’m sure this is to accommodate cases that don’t have any cut-out design where the port is. Mine does, so there is a lot of tip before the barrel it’s mounted in. title: ... for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase
text: I've been using this product for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase! It provides a strong breeze of air to keep me dry despite the extreme Arizona temperatures. My only challenge is my daily driver is a 67 Mustang and this product will not mount on the dash too tall and too wide. I don't have the long center console in my car, so the only thing I can stick it to is the carpeted floor - and I would rather not do that. For the most part it stays put with nothing holding it, but if I hang a sharp right it goes sliding. Not the company's fault-but for anyone driving a 67 mustang, this won't sit on the dash. Other than the challenge with placement, i would definitely recommend this product. It's not a cure for the 110 degree heat but I have tinted windows to dim the sun and this to keep the air moving in the car. A huge help to get me through one more summer before I get an AC installed! Edit: forgot to mention - it is not noisy! Obviously there is a little bit of a buzz but it's not annoying and nothing that can't be drowned out by your radio. Also, I like that the two fans can be adjusted up, down and side to side. So it can sit in the middle and one fan be pointed at the driver and the other at the passenger. It can tilt up or down depending if you have it sitting up high on the dash or low on the floor like I do. Anyway - great buy! Not sure why people have any issues with it dying on them but I will update if anything like that happens.

title: It absolutely works, but you can do a lot better.
text: This cord is an identical replacement for the one that comes with the monitor. This is a pro and a con. My husband and I have used it every night after our son moved into his own room, and we absolutely love it. It’s so much nicer than the one we had 10 years ago when our daughter was born. The only issue we’ve ever had with it is the cord that connects with the screen. It started fraying at the end near the plug after 2-3 months. We were able to tape it and continue using it for several months after that. Eventually you could see the copper wiring coming through and it only worked when positioned perfectly. A couple weeks later, it was done. I desperately tried to salvage it, but it wasn’t happening. My Mom ordered us a replacement cord and all was well again. That didn’t last long though, because history tends to repeat itself. I learned my lesson and didn’t wait until it became useless before replacing it. This time I bought a universal adapter. It was actually cheaper than this cord and can be used for just about anything requiring an ac adapter. Use your money wisely. Why pay the same price for a cord that will just fall apart? There are a ton of options when you search for a universal adapter, but they seem fairly similar. I bought one for less money than this cord, it came with about 10 adapters, and is much sturdier.

I was told that even though a charger should have been in the box, there was nothing they could do. They said I should just return it, but it was a Christmas gift for our daughter and that wasn’t an option. Even though there were numerous chargers available to purchase (which is what they suggested I do) I was told they couldn’t simply send me one, I’d have to purchase it and they would not expedite shipping. Eventually, I was given a $30 credit to my account. The computer itself is great and I would definitely recommend it, but this whole experience left a sour taste in my mouth. I would not recommend buying refurbished. The hassle is not worth saving a few bucks!

title: Not bad, but ANNOYING pairing and audio interface
text: I've had a number of Bluetooth headphones and the overwhelming majority of them have an "audio interface" that makes sense - some bare bones, some quite pleasant. This interface is in the form of sounds the relate to each of the functions - power on/off, paring, etc. These headphones have a TERRIBLE interface. When you power them on an annoyingly loud series of tones blares in your ear. The tones rise in pitch. When you continue to hold the power button, to access the paring mode, all you hear is an extremely brief, muffled tone. Apparently, the makers thought this was enough of a signal to indicate you're in paring mode. Believe me, it is NOT obvious at all. When you power off the headphones, you hear the same annoying loud series of tones. In this case, the tones do not decrease in pitch, which one might expect. By comparison, the audio interface of my other Bluetooth headphones are a joy - unfortunately, they do not have volume controls or skip and rewind. When powering them on, a pleasant female voice says, "Hello", and when you enter pairing mode, the same voice says, "Ready to pair." When pairing is established, the voice says, You're connected", then tells me how much charge I have - either full, medium or low. These Cootree headphones do none of that. You'll be lucky if you're able to tell if they've been turned off properly. In terms of sound quality, they're okay - nothing exceptional. In terms of fit, they're okay as well. Again, nothing exceptional. To my knowledge, they do not have an active noise cancelling function, other than what little noise they may happen to muffle by covering your ears. I mention this only because the rating form asks about it.

title: Very Disappointed In The Sound Quality

title: Make sure your device supports aptx
text: I bought this to use with my LG TV and a couple of Anker Bluetooth speakers. Connecting the speakers to the transmitter was confusing because you have zero interface. Once I did get it connected, the latency was not good. The audio was not in sync at all - a god half to a full second behind the video. I'm returning this for a refund. If you're planning to use this with a TV and Bluetooth speakers, be sure they support the BT 5 aptx low latency codec. EDIT After returning the device, the manufacturer sent me a message. I almost deleted their email because it looked like spam, with emojis in the subject line. Anyway, they informed me that the problem I experienced was likely because the BT speakers (Upgraded, Anker Soundcore Boost) I used I paired with their device did not support the low latency aptx codec. This may have been the case, but I was unable to find specs for the speakers to confirm this. I must say their customer support is extremely accommodating. In their email, they offered a number of options to make things right, including a gift card or a different BT transmitter. Unfortunately, I've already purchased wired speakers to replace the ones I had bought. Although I won't be taking advantage of their offers, I do give them high marks for service and have changed my rating from 2 stars to 4 stars.

title: Button functionality ruins this device. You get what you pay for.
text: I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected. The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering. Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages? The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again. There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name. There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect. Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust. The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it. Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation. The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible. The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing. On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black. Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”

title: Inexpensive, but lousy UI
text: For the price, this device is okay, but the user interface is pathetic. The touch interface is annoying because it only applies to half the screen. What's worse is when the device screen goes blank (to save battery life), you have to touch the screen - which performs one of the functions, like play or pause. It's quite annoying. The buttons of the touch screen are at the bottom and you can only navigate the interface by tapping up/down/left/right. So doing things on the device is a chore I bought this for a friend and didn't spend much time with it - only to set it up. So I don't have an opinion of the sound quality or the build quality. However ... one comment on the latter. I've seen a number of reviews for this and similar products which reference the weight of the device and correlation it to the quality of the build. The 2 don't always to hand in hand. The Chinese have been known to add lead weights to devices to make them heavier so that people will believe it's better build quality or material than it really is. I don't know this to be the case with this device - just wanted to point out that weight may not be the telltale people think it is BTW - the USB cable is SHORT. Probably only a foot at most. Also, it's micro USB, which is a pain in the butt. The radio function required the use of headphones - as an antenna. Kind of a pain for Bluetooth headphone users. Also - if the headphones are plugged in, I presume you can't listen through the device's built in speaker (which is lackluster) or through an external Bluetooth speaker. I can't confirm this because, as I said, I only spent about an hour using the device. FYI - the device has no internal storage. The 32GB is in the form of a micro SDXC card. This means if you opt to purchase a larger card to use with the device, you won't be adding to the 32GB, you'll be replacing it.

No next/back buttons, no tilt scroll wheel. This mouse is best for emergencies or for temporary use until you get a new mouse with better features, etc. Bottom line - you get what you pay for.
