title: Okay for $25. Still a little disappointed.
text: Let me start by saying I don't use the cell phone features of these headphones, so this review is not all encompassing. That said, I was a little disappointed in these headphones. Although the sound quality is good, the build quality and attention to detail in design could be better. The control buttons on the right ear are difficult to use as you can't easily feel with your finger where one starts and another begins, You just have to press in the general area, which is not very reassuring. The buttons themselves have no raised symbols or any physical element you can touch to let you know you're on a button, let alone the correct one. The build quality is not the best. The control buttons fit together less tightly than other Bluetooth headphones I've used. The main play/pause/on/off/pairing button, located in the center of the right earphone in particular seems loose and misaligned. The functions of the buttons work well enough. However, with some functions, there is no audio feedback. Having used other headsets that provide a short beep each time a button is pressed, I was a little confused when I first tried these - I'd press pause and the audio would just stop, with no beep. I suppose some users would find this preferable though. Some of the button functions, such as play/pause, are not instantaneous. There's a slight delay (about a second) between the time you press it and the time the audio actually plays or pauses. I've experienced this with other Bluetooth headsets and it seems to be a common annoyance. Because the fit is somewhat tight, getting the earphones on requires a little manipulation. I often find I have to guide the tip of my ear into the space between the neckband (the part that holds the earpieces and wraps around your neck) and the earpiece.This is mainly due to the padding on the earpieces. Once the headphones are on though, they've not uncomfortable. However, a little more space between the neckband and the top of the earpieces would be an improvement. Wearing the headphones lying down or with your head against the back of a seat is not uncomfortable for the most part. The charging port is has a rubber cover. Although it serves a purpose and some might find this helpful, I find it just gets in the way and will likely fall off. The charging cable is VERY short - about 3 feet, and it comes with no AC adapter, so you'll need to plug it into a USB port for charging - or acquire an adapter so you can use an electrical outlet. Due to the shortness of the cord, it will likely be inconvenient for use with some outlets. Attaching the charging cord is somewhat difficult. This is to be expected, I guess, due to the micro-USB size of the plug that goes into the ear piece. The end of the cord that plugs into the ear piece is tapered on one side, so there's some visual indication of which way it should go in, but it's always a pain trying to insert these kinds of plugs, no matter what the device. I haven't used the headphones for any great length of time, so I can't comment on the battery life at this time. The fact that these headphones can fold up to a fairly small size is nice and may be helpful to some when traveling. Typically, I wear them while walking or taking public transportation, so no real advantage for me. I purchased 2 pair of these - 1 for myself and one as a gift. The ones I bought for myself were to replace a pair of Motorola Bluetooth headphones I thought were malfunctioning. Whenever I wore them, if I turned my heard too far to the right, the sound would cut out or it would seem to skip slightly. The first time I tried the Kinivo BTH240 headphones, they did the exact same thing. Is this something common to Bluetooth devices? All in all, I suppose the negatives I've noted are minor and are likely more personal, but they still prevent me from rating these higher than 3 stars.

title: Would have been 5 stars but ...
text: This is a nice little unit. I was surprised at how small it was - about the same size as one and a half packs of cigarettes. I gave the unit a full charge before testing it and the sound was pretty good - playing music from my iPod Touch via Bluetooth and via the included aux audio cable. BTW - that cable and the power cable are very cheap and I don't expect them to last long. My biggest problem is with the sound quality when the product is connected to my laptop via the aux audio cable. The sound was horrible. There was a constant "white noise" type sound in the background. This sound was almost as loud as the music and it was very annoying. My laptop does not have Bluetooth, so that was not an option. I do plan on buying a USB Bluetooth adapter and testing that as well. Hopefully, I won't encounter the same poor audio. One other thing I knew about prior to buying the product - it does not have a user replaceable battery. This means when the battery no longer holds a charge, you'll have to throw it away. My understanding is that these type of batteries will last a few years. However, throwing the product away is crazy, because it's bad for the environment - even if disposed of properly. It would be nice if the battery were user replaceable, so all that plastic and electronics didn't have to end up in a landfill. So, as I mentioned, I like the product and would have rated it higher if not for the flaws I've noted.

title: Don't waste your money.
text: OK, take 2. My original review of this product got hijacked somehow. After writing it, I checked back a couple hours later and my screen name and original title were there, but my review got replaced with what seemed like some guy's journal entry. It had absoluterly nothing to do with this or any other product. Strange. Anyway - as mentioned in my original posting, this review is more a condemnation or earbud headphones in general than the Sennheiser CX300-B, which I decided to try after my "over ear" style Sony noise canceling headphones went on the fritz. My past experience with earbuds was not good, although I had only ever tried the type that come with the iPod and not the "ear plug" type that go in the ear canal, like the Sennheiser CX300-B. However, having owned a pair of Sennheiser over the ear headphones back in the 70's, my impression of the company and their products was good. So, I decided to take the plunge. What a mistake. After opening the package (no easy feat - damn sound welded plastic clamshells!), I popped on the medium-sized bud covers (appropriate for my size ears) and inserted them into my ears. I turned on my mp3 player and listened for a few minutes. The sound was adequate - nothing spectacular. I did notice they had decent bass and did block some external noise. I kept listening as I stepped outside to go to the store. I couldn't believe what I heard. Every step I took was amplified in my head - like a booming bass drum. Even the gentle bumping of the cord against my chest was amplified - a constant thump, thump, thump that was impossible to ignore. As it turns out, the very feature that blocks a modicum of external noise, also amplifies any sound that travels through the body. Even breathing is amplified! As I walked, it sounded as though I was listening to someone breathe over a PA system! I had hoped to use these while running, but there's no way that's going to happen. In fact, the problem with amplified sound is so bad, I won't use them at all. I am very disappointed in this product and will never buy any ear plug style headphones again. I don't understand why anyone would sell them, let alone use them. They may have great sound reproduction, but the listening experience is totally ruined by the sounds that get amplified through the body. It amazes me that people buy similar style products that sell for hundreds of dollars. The only way you can enjoy the sound they produce is to sit perfectly still. I'm glad I only paid about $16 for these things. I won't return them because it'll be too much of a hassle - probably cost more to ship them back than I paid. BTW - The photo of the product is misleading. The cord looks thicker than it actually is and there's no way it can be coiled as is shown in the photo. It gives the impression the cord is more supple and flexible that it really is. Also, one end of the cord is longer than the other. Not sure why this is, but the thinness of the cord makes it prone to kinking and tangling. In fact, since one side of the cord is longer than the other, it makes it even more prone to tangling. Bottom line - steer clear of the Sennheiser CX300-B and all ear plug style earbuds.

title: Works - poorly
text: I bought this because the cable of my wired iPod remote was coming apart. I thought I'd kill 2 birds with one stone. I got this product for less than a new wired remote would cost and it gave me the added functionality of wireless. Only problem is it rarely works properly. I sometimes have to press the forward button 5-6-7 times to get the thing to advance to the next song. The volume control is also problematic - sometimes turning the volume all the way up or all the way down without stopping. The pause control works fine, except that once paused, it rarely is able to resume play. The range of the product is also a problem. I carry my iPod in my inside jacket pocket and carry the remote control in my outside jacket pocket - a distance of 12-15 inches. The iJet has trouble traversing this distance. I sometimes hold the remote 1-2 inches from the receiver and it still doesn't sense that I'm pressing a button! If you're thinking of buying this product, don't bother. It's a waste of money. Thankfully, I didn't waste much.

title: Noise Canceling Is Useless Outdoors
text: I bought these headphones from an Amazon vendor and am glad I did because I didn't have to pay Amazon's price - $25 higher at the time. However, if I had to do it again, I wouldn't buy them. I use my iPod while commuting on public transportation and thought these headphones would be a good replacement for another pair of Sony noise-canceling headphones I had been using for 3 years. However, when I'm outdoors and have the noise-canceling function turned on, any wind is magnified tremendously. The function is virtually useless outdoors. I've resorted to turning the feature off and turning up the volume. The only other complaint I have with this product is that they're not portable enough. I may be wrong, but I thought the product features indicated they were foldable - they're not. This makes carrying them around a little tougher than foldable headphones. Again, I'm glad I didn't pay full price for these things.

title: A Maintenance Nightmare
text: What should have been on the front of the BOX: Warning, Charge this Device up Immediately before install. During it's use, you will have to unscrew it from the wall and disconnect the doorbell wiring and throw it on a charger for 5-10 hours from time to time to keep it working properly. The engineers who developed this product weren't smart enough to make it run off of power supplied by your doorbell alone, or trickle charge the battery fast enough during usage. From the factory, there wasn't enough charge on it to install it and test it's features completely out of the box. The hard-wiring will trickle charge a battery but if there's a lot of motion it will run it down and you will have to de-install and re-install the Ring device. The engineers didn't provide any sort of quick electrical connection disconnect mechanism either for the hard wiring XD!! The should have had some sort of automotive style quick-disconnect plug. Or even better yet, an external USB charging port that you could run an extension cord and charge up the doorbell in place or some sort of external solar charger. If the doorbell is on the side adjacent to the door, you will most likely need a 45 degree mount (separate purchase) in order to get a better view of the visitor. Very Very displeased with this company not being forthright with key installation and usage information. I didn't buy this device here, I installed one purchased by a customer from Amazon. The fish eye lens and picture are great, works great, but the battery/power situation was a big disappointment.

title: Delivered a Refurb Unit that Did Not work
text: Not sure if this was an Amazon Issue or a Supplier Issue. I ordered this unit a while back and set it aside to when I could get back to my Hobbyist Project. Opened box and screen had scratches on it. Then pluged it in, and unit wouldn't connect to the Raspberry PI. The green led came on saying there was power, and it would flash a rasbperry pi icon, but it wouldn't connect to video. It's now an expensive paperweight. There was a green card in the box for an email address to contact if there was any issues, and so I wrote them. But I am posting here too, because I saw others that posted that had the same exact issue that I have. So I decided to flag it and see what the company does to remedy this issue.

title: You'll hate the product when you need to change the battery.
text: Product does it's job, sometimes too well. Rain will set it off, and so will rabbits and birds. For this reason you may want to get a buried driveway probe otherwise you will get a lot of false alarms. I have both this optical sensor and a probe and when I get dual notification, then I know something is out there. Here's what needs to be improved: #1 There are 4 Recessed screws to get to the battery, and when you flip it over so you can see where to put the battery they will fall into the dirt. How Stupid of a design can you get!?!. How about a simple battery compartment access door or something that just snaps in place or a single screw. #2 Who remembers obscure tones? IF you have multiple gates on your property, how are you going to remember which tone goes with what gate? How about a voice over that says something like : Area 1 or Area 2. Or better yet, allow the user to upload or record their own tones or something: "Someone at the Front Gate!"

title: Works like it should, quality product, 3 gripes
text: So the range works, very few false alarms. 9v battery will take some time to replace in the receiver. At least the electronics inside are protected from the elements with a rubber gasket behind 4 screw plate. Receiver unit doesn't have a rechargeable battery backup. This would have been nice to carry it to the gate for testing so that you can hear it go off when the sensor is tripped. Also if power goes out, you can still hear the chime. I have a plug in outlet in my truck as well as an inverter and a portable electric battery with 110v capability, just would have been nice for those without. Programming the transmitter/receiver with dipswitches is a bit of headache especially getting the cover off the reciever. Should have just been exposed on the underside rather than have to pull apart the plastic housing. Maybe some sort of phillips head rotatable dipswitch settings. I do like the versitility of the current setup thought to prevent collisions with other systems. Like the mounts, especially the swivel mount for gate post adjustments so that windy day swinging gates don't trip the sensor.

Website always "Request Timed Out" after 30 seconds of video feed, you can't really monitor cameras for more than 30 seconds through their sucky website. Don't rely on this is an emergency situation. No real forward thinking people involved in the design, they probably just paid a contractor to slap something together, now that he's gone and profits are gone, they don't give a rats ass about updating the software.

title: When Power Goes Off, Firmware gets Corrupted, and Router will not work
text: When the router is working ,it's awesome. Range, speed, and setup are very easy. However, just like a bad musical performance, when things don't perform well, that's what people remember. Here is why I cannot' give the product 5 stars. There have been two situations where the router lost power and the firmware got corrupted and I had to reflash the router to make it work. I have NEVER had a device EVER get corrupted firmware. What a JOKE! Probably corrupted data issue as nothing will bring a system down like bad data. Google: Router Power LED Blinks Slowly and Router No Longer Works So rather than issue a RECALL on the defective merchandise, they do the next worst thing possible and give you some funky software called TFTP to download and fool around with to get the router re-flashed. Well, I thought the re-flash would correct the corrupted firmware. I got news for them, IT DIDN'T. I was moving my Router yesterday while the cable guy was here and then when we tried to hook everything back up, I got the blinking light of death again. I knew it was going to be a hassle to get the firmware downloaded and reflashed, so I switched back to an older working router for the time being. In my opinion, NETGEAR should have done a 2 things amongst other things... 1) As an interim solution, Made special re-flash software that made upgrades a breeze. A one click solution to read the router's make/model MAC address and current firmware, and auto-magically download the new one and install it while PRESERVING all existing settings. It should also remember the OLD mac address and use it when you were migrating the settings to a router with a new MAC address. If their software engineering department can't do that, they need to be replaced starting with the Manager. 2) Recalled and Replaced the defective equipment for FREE, send out a new unit, and a postage paid return box for your old unit. Then use the above software to migrate the settings and old MAC address to the new unit so it works seamless with your existing cable model and service provider. What do you call a router that does not work? An expensive paperweight? Can you say Regression Testing? Can you say Error Trapping Netgear? Words for the day for your Engineering Department. who worked on this product line.

title: Excellence in Engineering and Delivery
text: Money well spent for this device. I had an ASUS laptop that had the HDMI port too close to the VGA Port. Therefore, I couldn't only use one or the other. I wanted 3 monitors. (Company provided laptop, I would have never bought the machine myself if I would have seen such a lame display arrangement in advance.). I decided to give a competitor's cheaper USB3 to HDMI inline converter a try, but it failed horribly. I paid a few more dollars for this unit from Anker after reading some of the positive reviews, and it worked perfectly. I installed the CD ROM it came with, and it recognized my 2ndary Samsung monitor connected via HDMI instantaneously. I pushed the limits and tried to use the HDMI and the DVI on the unit at the same time, but couldn't get it working, it's unclear whether they support that modality. It could be a bad cable or something else I forgot, I didn't fiddle with it too long. USB 3.0 seems to deliver the 60Hz refresh rate, I don't see any lag or ghosting at 1080p, so I am well pleased with the performance. I plugged my headphones in, and it immediately transferred the audio. Looks nice, feels like great engineering. It's been going strong for about 2 weeks now without a hiccup. I recommended this product to 6 other co-workers.

title: Very Very Disappointed
text: I see a lot of people stoked about this product, and at first I was. Until I tried to use it. Perhaps I just got a defective unit. Too many CONS to keep: The biggest problem I had with the unit was inserting the MicroSD card, it just did not function properly. It was spring loaded and sometimes would shoot the micro sd card a few feet into the air. That can't be good for the card, and if it happens to go down a storm drain or get lost in a gravel bed, that's not good either. I would try to press it in, it wouldn't 'stick', do it again, and again, 15 minutes later I realized something wasn't quite right with the unit. Endless fumbling. The unit should have an LED that when the card is inserted properly should glow green or something. (When the case was shut, it could stop the LED to save batteries or something.) The unit has cryptic LED blinks for diagnostics, doesn't help a lot when you don't have the manual handy and are missing the action you are supposed to be recording. It was a non-stop fumble trying to get the device to recognize the card. I bought good quaility SanDisk 32 gig chips, it seemed to recognize them after much fumbling, but only recorded 2gb out of the 32gigs before I had to change them. That's terrible. When you are on a backpacking trip, you don't exactly have access to a computer to see what's going on with the memory, you have to wait until you get home to find out you recorded nothing. If I put a new Memory stick in, it should perform a format/check sum to make sure the card is good and then let the user know it's been tested /accepted and the media is ready to be used. Not wait until your action moment has arrived, then just blink off. The unit is durable, waterproof, and works sometimes....but not when I really wanted it to. The video looks grainy, it lacks much detail. I know my miniDV tape recorder 10 years ago was better. Forget about sound quality...it's terrible, unit needs external microphone. PROS: Unit recorded in .MOV and was accessible by my Mac and PC via USB. Unit is tough. Unit seems to be waterproof, had it down about 8' in a stream under a waterfall. Although the unit said it was recording, it recorded nothing. I'm sooooo livid about that part. Units going back. There are some other helmet cameras that are about 2x the money that I will gladly buy. Expensive is when the product is not worth the money. Caveat Emptor!

title: I like it
text: I was looking for a simple sort of cd clock radio to keep on a nightstand. It's amazing how difficult it was to find something like that that fit my needs, and I ended up with this unit although I really wasn't intrested in the iPhone/iPod connections. I went to a local electronics store and first tried a litte Sony machine, was set to buy it, and then the salesman showed me this Phillips unit. The sound was overwhelmingly better on the Phillips unit. I admit I'm not an audiophile, but I just want something that sounds good when I played CDs at bedtime. I quickly dismissed the little Sony and went for this unit. Since having it about a week now, I really like the sound from the CD player. I did try my iPhone 4 on it to see if it would connect, and it did and it played music like a champ. Strong and clear. I have a rubber bumper on my iPhone and had to remove it to make the phone fit properly but that's no big deal. In fact what I'm thinking of doing is reprogramming my older iPhone (first generation) with nothing but music on it and leaving that plugged in the Phillips unit. I keep my iPhone 4 in a different charger in a different room so it doesn't disrupt my sleep AND so I won't forget it when I'm leaving the house. So far I'm a happy camper with this little Philips unit. The only con is the brightness of the backlit display which is rather bright. I placed the unit in a different part of the room where the remote still works but the brightness of the display doesn't affect my sleep. I like a dark room!

Not a sound like the usually FM transmitter that is not broadcasting strong enough and/or getting inference from another station. Just something else I thought "Damn another waste of money" I then plug back into the charger thinking maybe it needed longer to charge.Still not the case. So I plugged it into my phone with the charger plugged into in. WOW! Perfect! Crystal clear. No engine noise. No station interference noise. No weak signal noise. Awesome!. Unplugged it from the charger..hissing noise again. So it looks like the charge and unplug is not 100%. But if I plug it into DC charger runs perfect. Best one I have ever had. title: Pass on this one--you can get better in this price range
text: I bought into the hype and some early favorable 'professional' reviews on this product (and am now convinced the website that posted it was probably paid by Whistler to hype up the release) and purchased it back in late June. I could have easily gotten a similar quality product for much less...or better yet, spent more and got a better, more reliable unit. Convinced that it wasn't working as advertised, I purchased a V1, the 'King' of radar detectors, and compared them in my car side by side. First off, the 78SE gives TONS of false alarms. Often it would go off when the v1 wasn't making a peep. Sometimes, it would go crazy when I was out in the middle of a road surrounded by corn fields! Is this because it is more sensitive? I think not. I had tested them on some speed signs set up in my area, and the V1 would go off a 1/4 mile or more before the Whistler made a detection. A 1/4 mile in the world of radar is an eternity--the difference between getting a ticket and not. By the time the 78SE starting making weak little burps warning you to start being on the lookout, the V1 was already going off at full blast. The v1 would also detect the speed radar when it was up and over a hill--presumably from the minute signature bouncing off different objects alongside the road. Again, not a peep was heard from the 78SE. I am not saying I expect the 78SE to be as good as a $400 V1. I do, however, expect the performance to be enough to serve its purpose, which is warning you of radar before the cop has your speed. This detector simply won't do that, which makes owning it more or less pointless IMO. The numerous false alerts make you on guard when you don't need to be, and eventually you will simply ignore all the warnings--even the legitimate ones. When the real threats arise, it is doubtful you will know before the cop has your speed--MAYBE it will provide a small benefit in the most optimal conditions (a flat road going perfectly straight)...but how often is that the case? Save your hard earned $$ for a detector that will work...or if your dead set on spending less than $200, do more research and see if you can find something better or at least cheaper!

I develop websites using Adobe Dreamweaver and MS Expression Web with lots a graphic content and have managed fine (OK) on my previous system except that it wore out. (I guess, hard drive failure, DVD drive failure, motherboard, one after another.) This system also comes with Windows 10, which I hate a lot. A joke! Maybe that's a contributing factor to my totally unimpressive more expensive, less capable new computer. Bottom line, the fastest processor and faster DDS RAM and solid state drives don't seem to add any power or performance so save your money and look for a Windows 7, Intel i5 if you can find one. title: I like these, however...
text: These are nice speaker/mics Definitely pretty good quality for the low price. However, I have run into an issue when used on RT21V MURS radios. They seem to work fine for a while and then the radio locks up with no transmit or receive. I have not seen this lock up on these radios using the standard PTT buttons. I also have other model Retevis radios and don see this issue. Not sure why these RT21V radios do this an=nd am trying to find out. Maybe there's a sensitivity adjust in programming?? Don't know. I'd give these 5 starts if I could get around the lock up issue on the one model of radio,

title: this is an amazing little device
text: For its size and price, this is an amazing little device. This thing is tiny and pretty easy to conceal. I only wish it came with some type of bracket to help mount in a vehicle. It has a very strange shape and some grooves on the side which appear like they were designed for some type of bracket to slide into. Ultimately, I will probably make something. Video quality on the highest quality is amazingly good. It even does pretty well in low light conditions. Better than some similar devices I've tried. It has some default modes that will work without the widget, but you pretty much need to download and use it to take advantage of all its features. The widget seems pretty well designed and is fairly intuitive. I've had no problems using it. Audio could be better and in some situations it works pretty well, while other time its almost unintelligible. I believe this is just the nature of the little pinhole mike pick up. Results will vary based on the situation. I have found that sometimes the audio appears out of sync, but I'm not sure that doesn't have something to do with playback software. On the best quality, the files are pretty big and it will keep a processor busy watching the video. Overall, it's a great little package that includes cables, power pack and just about everything you'll need except the mini SD card. Some of the earlier mini DVRs were poor quality and lacked features as well as cost a lot for the size convenience. This device takes the mini DVR to a whole new level that is light years beyond some of the earlier stuff. Having tried many other little minis, I can say that this just blows them all away and clearly has been developed to a much more advanced level. Once you have played with it for awhile, you'll find endless uses. With a bit of creativity, concealment is pretty easy and battery life is quite good.

title: Good quality taps, great price.
text: These seem to be pretty well made taps. How they would hold up with frequent use, I'm not sure, but they are nicely machined, sharp and seem to cut good. If you are using mainly to clean up threads, they will probably last a lifetime. Nice little wooden box. Hard to beat for the price, you get the whole set for less than the price of a single 1 1/4" tap of a high quality brand name. For Chinese made taps, these seem to be high end.

title: Another non-standard use
text: I decided to take a chance and use this a bit differently than designed. I have a Foscam WiFi security camera in a steel pole barn. Even with a high gain antenna on the camera and a fiberglass door, my connection was pretty bad. Choppy video and lost connections were common. I needed to get the antenna outside. Although this antenna isn't outdoor rated, it is pretty easy to make watertight. Some tape over the mounting screw holes on the back and a little self vulcanizing rubber electrical tape around the antenna joint and no water is going to get in. You could use something like RTV silicone too. Keep the moisture out and you now made it outdoor capable. It was pretty close the way it comes and I'm sure it would probably be fine for a long time, but sealing it completely is pretty easy. The magnet mount works great on the steel siding. The camera I have, like most, comes with a standard SMA connector vs.the SMA-RP (reversed pin), but you can get an adapter here on Amazon. [[ASIN:B005H488Y4 SMA Male to SMA-RP Female Adapter]] Added a 20 foot cable with standard SMA male and female connectors and now I have a great outdoor antenna for an indoor camera in a steel building that is great for blocking radio signals. It works very well and the results exceeded my expectations. I've bought another antenna for the same setup on another camera. Although it isn't exactly what they intended it for, it works extremely well.

title: Seems very well made
text: These seem to be very well made, high quality adapters. Make sure you understand the terminology to get the right type. There are a few different types/sizes of these small connectors. Do some research to make sure you are getting the one you need. That said, these are well made and work fine. The only reason I didn't give these 5 stars is because the pictures could be better showing detailed views of both ends. If you understand the terminology, it isn't necessary. But I suspect that the average person needing one would benefit greatly with better views of both sides. For clarification, this particular one has male and female SMA threads with male pins on both sides.

title: Works pretty well
text: Let me start out by saying this is a well built fixture. It is all metal, sturdy and the adjustments enable pretty fine agjustment of the angle. I am using mine with a Foscam outdoor camera with a built in IR illuminator. The built in works pretty well, but doesn't have a lot of distance to it. I wanted to be able to see farther down the driveway. I mounted this about fifteen feet up, a couple feet above the camera. It took a few attempts to get it aimed correctly. The only way you will see where the light falls is in the dark through the camera. I ended up just less than 90 degrees to the ground so it reaches out down the driveway but not directly below it. This works pretty well as the built in lights things up close pretty well and this lights up beyond that. If you have it aimed closer, this light will be too bright in the camera and you will lose any detail. Depending on what type camera you are using, this could easily vary. It takes some tweaking to get it just right. As for 400 feet, that might be a stretch, but it could depend on the sensitivity of the camera. In my situation, I can see adequate detail out to about 300 feet. The camera doesn't have a long focal length lense so things are getting small out at that distance, but are adequately lit. I am looking at picking up another camera with a zoom for another location and I'll probably light it with one of these. I suspect each situation might be a bit different depending on the camera you are using. The fixture looks a lot like a standard quartz floodlight in the daylight and when it is lit at night, (photocell turns it on and off), the LEDS glow red. To the unaided eye, they aren't very bright looking and they are pretty unobtrusive in darkness. This is a quality product at a reasonable price. I will very likely be getting another one for a different location, Maybe the next one up in range which isn't much more in price, as I could use the added distance for that one. I might even use one to put night vison on my golf cart!

title: Big, but does extend the range
text: This antenna is about 16" long, but it does seem to do what it is supposed to. It looks a bit weird attached to the camera because it is long, But as far as I can tell it works pretty good. I have some Foscam FI8910 W cameras. I set one up in a steel pole barn with a fiberglass garage door. I couldn't get it to couple with my router in the house with the standard antenna. I put this antenna on and bingo it connected right away. I don't think it can punch through steel and the fiberglass door helps I'm sure, but still, the standard antenna wouldn't get there and this one does. I can't speak to how far it will extend the range and there are a lot of factors that can impact that, but I am convinced that it will get you farther than the standard antenna. I plan on trying some experimenting this coming Summer with an outdoor camera to see just how far it will extend the range line of sight. I will just add that among the various factors that can impact wireless range, other wireless traffic in the area can be the biggest one to cause problems. Sometimes different channels work better than others. This antenna will not solve all problems by any means, but it should help. Whether or not it is enough can not be predicted reliably. Your specific set of conditions means a lot. Sometimes you can also get high gain antennas for your router too. These might even fit depending on the connector. Keep in mind that increasing the range of your router also makes your router more vulnerable to being intercepted. Use security.

title: A lot of camera for the price
text: I am a bit of a digital camera nut, having evolved from a film camera nut. I have more than few digitals including some top of the line Canons. This is a great camera for the price. (In fact it would be a very good camera at twice the price.) I was attracted to it because of a very good experience with a much earlier version of a similar designed Fuji. I bought it about 10 years ago. I beat the daylights out of that camera. Even had a set of batteries leak in it. Cleaned it up and it was fine. It looks horrible now. All banged up and I use tape to keep the battery door closed on it. I used it as a "work" camera. My work takes me into some pretty nasty environments. But that old Fuji still works today. I wanted something just as good but with higher resolution. The S4500 fulfilled all my wishes and more. This thing is packed with features, many found only on top of the line cameras. Great 30X zoom and 14MP. One key feature I was looking for is the electronic viewfinder. I grew up with film cameras and I still struggle to compose shots with a screen on the back. This gives you the choice of using the bright, easy to see, real through the lens, viewfinder or the built in 3" display. The electronic viewfinder does a couple really good things for you. For one, using a viewfinder instead of holding the camera in front of you, provides an incredibly stable shooting position. You can take shots at pretty low shutter speeds without blur, much better than you can suspending the camera in mid air so you can look at the display. The second big advantage is hugely extended battery life. That LCD display on any camera, eats up a lot of power. With the display shut off and using the EVF, battery life is incredible. One of my Canons is a very nice Powershot. Great 3" display too, but no EVF. That thing eats batteries. Now if you are looking for a pocket camera, this isn't it. It has the look, feel and basic size of a traditional SLR 35mm film camera with a motor drive. It's not huge, but it isn't small enough to stuff in your pocket. It does have the feel of a film SLR which is something I find very desirable. That design is not just an accident and it produced some of the best photographs ever taken by film photographers. It is a great natural feel to me, but then I grew up with film. I have been nothing but pleased with this camera. It is very high quality at an amazingly reasonable price. You can easily pay a lot more and get a lot less. All of the features are very nice if you are into photography as I am, but you can just as easily use it as a point and shoot camera and produce excellent photos. It is a great camera for someone looking to advance a bit in their photographic skills. This camera can take you there if you want to, but you don't need a degree to use it either. Use it point and shoot out of the box and then try different features as you go. I have a lot of cameras, and for the money, I'd give this one "six stars" if I could. My previous experience with Fuji's tells me they are "bulletproof". Just one last note. I would suggest getting a case for this camera. It is big enough that a case makes it easier to carry and provides some protection. The standard Fuji case for this camera is on Amazon for a surprisingly good price. It's pretty well made and a good investment.

title: Great addition to a great tablet
text: I bought this at the same time I bought an Infinity TF700. I'm glad I did. I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. It's not bad, but it isn't great either. But I'm not a big fan of mouse pads anyway so I might be a bit over critical in this regard. . The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit. It gives you another battery too that adds 4.5 hours of uptime. You also get a standard sized USB 2.0 port and SD card reader. The USB port can operate in "host mode" allowing you to connect a variety of devices that should couple automatically. Can't say that I've used the USB a lot yet. It is a very nice addition to a great tablet that gives you a laptop PC feel. It is tapered a little in thickness being a bit thicker at the back, but overall not much thicker than the tablet itself. Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs. The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.

title: Great piece of technology
text: I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on. That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive. So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad. The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree. As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best. I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt. Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop. Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!

title: Not Great, but cheap
text: At $13 it's a decent buy. It isn't the greatest, the instructions are poorly written and the build quality is marginal, but it does work pretty well. I'm giving it 4 stars just because it's price is so good. This thing is sold elsewhere for as much as $90. The user interface, (button) is a bit confusing but once you play with it for awhile and figure it out, it does seem to work as described. The alignment of the camera with the little hole on mine was a bit off, but it was pretty easy to "tweak" it into alignment. The video quality isn't too bad as long as you have adequate lighting. The sound pick up is amazingly sensitive. Need to buy a micro SD to use it. It doesn't come with one. It is an ingenious design but could have been implemented just a bit better. Still it is convincing enough and unobtrusive, The way it is made, it completely comes apart quite easily and I can see opportunities to retrofit the electronics into any number of other objects. Overall, if you're not a little bit tech savy, you may have probelms with this, but it's a great buy for the money if you don't mind having to play with it a bit to get it to work the way you want.

title: Well made, great price
text: Reading some of the reviews, there have obviously been some issues with this item that I believe where another case being sent instead. Looking today at the Amazon listing, there is something wrong because the "Product Description" is obviously for something else. I reported it. All I can say is the item picture and the details are correct. I got what I was looking for and it is great for the price. Nice and roomy, very secure with an adustable padded divider that you can move where you want it. Fits my Fuji S series camera with room to spare. You can easily put a couple extra sets of batteries, communication cables or other items and not be crowded. Pretty well made and I like the flap that covers the zipper area. They don't call it weather proof, but I think it would hold up to some rain or snow and keep things dry inside. Being a camera nut I have tried all kinds of cases from exact fit, hard cases, soft cases and big camera bags. This is a nice size. Not too big and not too small. I've already used it for some of my other cameras too. Main things I'm looking for is protection from dust, dirt, a surprise rain or a little snow, and some moderate protection from bangs and "bruises", and a bit of room for appropriate accessories. This case fits those need quite well. At ~$8 it's hard to imagine finding anything better for that low a price. If you have a Fuji S series or any other similar sized camera, you won't be disappointed.

title: Great fit, good value!
text: Very well made. Nice leather and seems to be a leather "sandwich" that has a reinforcing material in the places you want it to be a bit stiffer. Very good look and feel. This is not some cheap faux leather plastic cover. I use mine with the keyboard dock exclusively. I question a few other comments as to whether they got the right cover or not. I does have a speaker hole which lines up perfectly. If the Infinity TF700 has a flaw it is that the speaker could be better, but I don't see the cover contributing anything negatively to that weakness. The front facing camera hole could be just ever so slightly larger as you can sometimes just see it in the edge of the frame. A bit of very slight adjusting of the tablet in the holder fixes this pretty easily. It could also probably be quickly remedied with an exacto knife or needle file slightly opening up the hole where it is close. Another comment about the keypad holder straps being a bit loose solves itself with some use. The "spine" of the cover where it folds gets a bit more pliable with use and once loosened up a bit, it bends where you want it to and then the little straps are fine. It's not like it can fall out when it's docked anyway. But you can easily get it off the keypad to fold back as a stand. Frankly, Using the keypad dock, there's little need for the folding stand because you can very easily adjust the viewing angle mated to the dock. If I have any issues with it, the tablet holder leather "pocket" keeps the tablet with dock attached from "snapping" tightly shut. They actually must have tried to address that by thinning down the leather right in the hinge point. Making this thinned section just a bit longer would probably make it perfect without sacrificing any strength. Note that this is a very minor issue and most probably won't even notice it. It does not seem to be a problem and it closes OK and quite snugly when you put the closure strap around it. Closed with the dock installed, it measures right at 1 inch thick, making for a very nice comfortable carry. You can easily plug in and charge with it closed up. It is stiff enough that I wouldn't worry about stacking a few books on top of it. Overall, it exceeded my expectations being very high quality at a very reasonable price. I don't think you could find anything better for the price. It is made to fit the Infinity TF700 specifically and it is executed extremely well. I am very happy with it doing what I wanted to compliment the top of the line Android tablet. Had I hand picked it and tried it out first, I probably would have been willing to pay twice as much for it.

title: Not fantastic but OK
text: If you expect things to look like daylight, you'll be disappointed. It is far better than an old Russian unit I have which was an early generation light amplification unit, (green glow type). What you have here is a lot like a B&W security camera with an IR illuminator built into a hand held portable unit. As some of the other reviews indicate, in the beginning it will seem somewhat cumbersome and clunky getting used to the controls and finding the most pleasing contrast settings. Takes a while, but once you get used to it, it gets a lot easier to make it work like you want it too. One problem is that if you are just moving around in very low light and want to take a better look at things, it takes time for your eyes to adjust from darkness to the brightness in the viewfinder and then going back. The best way to use it is looking through it for an extended time scanning the area of interest, keeping your eye on the eyepiece. Different types of scenes will take some adjustment to optimize the appearance. Some things reflect light better than others so the best scenario is watching a particular area for an extended period. Once your eyes adjust and you get the contrast dialed in, it works pretty well. The IR illuminators are surprisingly pretty powerful. At short distances the high powered one will "wash out" what you're looking at, but it does seem to reach out pretty good. The claimed 600 feet is a bit of a stretch except under the most ideal of conditions. If you have some ambient light, I think it is better without it. But in really dark country night where you can't see your hand in front of your face, it does a great job of lighting things up. My feelings on it are mixed. The basic idea of a monocular fits that role of "occasional use" where you want a quick better look at something, but I think that is asking too much from such a device. Plan on spending some time to get a better look at things because your eyes need adjustment time. Once you get the unit dialed in for the scene your watching, it will work pretty well. It's not cheap by any means, but it does work and it's a nice compact package. If you want really high performance night optics, plan on spending a lot more. It will definitely allow you to see reasonable well in darkness, but you have to fiddle with it. A lot has to do with the application. The pros and cons have given me some ideas about building a special purpose device. Overall, it's a big improvement on some of the early night vision technology. The more I use it, the more I like it and learn tricks about using it effectively. I am happy with it, but for the average person with little experience with night vision, your expectations may not be met and that's why I'm giving it 3 stars. You will need a little patience to go through the learning curve using it.

title: Stereo Bluetooth headsets are way better than they used to be ...
text: I've only had the August EP650 for a couple days now, and there are a number of quality, comprehensive reviews -- so I thought I would write something specifically from the perspective of someone who hasn't owned a stereo Bluetooth headset since they first came out. The tech has come a long way, and I'm really quite pleased by how good these are for the price. If you're like me and have a bad recollection of the early days -- with the flaky connectivity and the terrible, tinny sound -- you'll be pleasantly surprised. Build quality feels pretty decent for the price; comfortable; buttons are easy to find with the headset on, and I've been putting them on while taking public transit, without playing anything, just so I can concentrate on reading, and not the prattle. So, thumbs up. If you've not been happy with Bluetooth cans in the past and don't want to spend too much to check them out again, the August EP650 is a very good option.

title: PROBLEMS getting it to work
text: I bought this to back up my LG phone because I was forced to buy a new phone since LG no longer supports their phones and I was already starting to have issues with mine. In buying a new phone, I was particularly freaked out about the possibility of losing my photos and other important files since the newer phones no longer have MicroSD cards for backup. This seemed like a great option--along with backing up to Google and Amazon cloud services, it added another layer of protection. The problem is that the C port didn't even fit into the C port on my phone--even though I took the case off my phone. After essentially having to cram it in the port, I kept getting a warning that my data would be corrupted if I kept "ejecting" it. It also wanted to back everything up to a MicroSD card, since it did not recognize that the SanDisk was even inserted into the phone. Since I'd spent a considerable amount of time moving everything from my SD card to the internal memory of my phone in anticipation of having to transfer it to a new phone without a card slot, I most definitely didn't want to back up everything back onto my card, so I took the card out. Even so, it still took quite some time for the phone to recognize the SanDisk, and finally start the back up. From there, the process was fairly easy, BUT it should have never been so difficult to get the phone to recognize the SanDisk in the first place. After the backup, I of course plugged the SanDisk into my laptop (without issues) and everything was indeed backed up. It should NOT have been that difficult to plug the device into my phone however! I will also mention, not that it's a big deal, but the device is considerably smaller than it looks to be on the Amazon website (less than .75x1.5"). At least I have an additional backup, but not as easily as I would have liked. Given the issues I had with it I don't think I would purchase this particular device again.

title: MOVE THE CHANNEL GUIDE AMAZON!!!
text: The GOOD: 1. Set up was pretty easy and the Recast actually pulled in about 6 channels I never received before--even using the same antenna! 😊 2. The ability to use Alexa to navigate is nice (although I don't use it) - - especially since the user interface is awful (see below) . The BAD: 1. The absolute WORST thing about this is that the Channel Guide is buried and you have to scroll through several menus to actually find it. AMAZON, IF YOU'RE LISTENING : MOVE THE CHANNEL GUIDE! It should be the first thing you see on the home page, or at least put a link up in the top bar where you put everything else (Home, Live, DVR, etc.) 2. The user interface needs to be streamlined--it is way too busy. 3. Along those lines, there is no way to delete the apps you don't want on there, so we're stuck navigating through a bunch of stuff we are not interested in and will never watch. 4. A minor issue probably, but the channels are listed by name and not number in the Channel Guide, so if you're used to punching in numbers on a remote, this takes getting used to. I would prefer it if there was a number pad on the remote to punch in the channel number, but there isn't. You can tel Alexa to "tune to channel #___, but I prefer to do this the old-fashioned way. 5. Even though there are 4 tuners, you can only WATCH on 2 devices at a time. If Amazon would make the channel guide more accessible, this could be a 5 Star review!

text: Frame is a tad slow to respond to the remote; that could be better. It isnt always slow, just sometimes it doesnt pic up, other times it is fast & perfectly fine. I think it has to do with distance from frame. Dont be too close! They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am. Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded. Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed. if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY Can set up calendar, weather, location, an alarm, play music, load videos. Can set time and make it a clock, can choose clock face. Can choose 12 hr or 24 hr format. Can create slide shows, decide on length of time, random or sequential or based on when taken. Very cool. Oh, and even incorporate music. Can label/add words/text too. Easy on, easy off. Can operate basic stuff directly from the frame. Including very quickly rotating a pic. No need to use remote for everything! Has headphone jack on back It really isnt bad as an entry level frame. Would be nice as a gift if preloaded for someone. Now that I have been using this, I know what to look for in an upgrade. But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it. I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos. Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive. Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle. Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. I wouldnt buy it for that anyway. I got it for use on a side table so I can see pics of my dogs and cats all day long.

title: compact, mighty 5 blade fan w/ attached USB cord, 3 speeds, easy to use, travel worthy
text: Dont need to pay much for a basic fan. This is a little guy, really quite nice for use at desk, at bedside, or on table next to favorite spot on couch. Simple press to turn on to low speed, then press again for a step higher, then press again for high speed, then finally press again for off. The fan can be tilted any which way. Fan has 5 blades. **Attached** USB power cord. Good long length! But just know that the one end is permanent part of the body. No swapping out for even longer cord. Very slim profile. Doesn't create room moving air flow, but I didnt expect it to. But I can feel the air when it is very close by. I have several small fans of this sort, and they tend to perform in similar fashion. Manage your expectations and use this for up close gentle air flow. Or even use as a sound machine. Nice natural white noise. FYI it is a tad loud at high speed We dont have AC, save for a couple of window units (one in bedroom, one in office) but other than that, we rely on dressing for the weather, keeping hydrated, and making use of fans. Sometimes all I need is a little air movement near me. I love the small fans for their small footprint. This is the smallest yet as the casing is just a band of plastic. No feet (just flat grip strips), no clips, no excess. And this will be able to be powered up by a power bank or generator if the power goes out. Just 3 watts. Can even use it in car! Although it doesnt have a clip or a real base, it might be useful near or on exercise equipment (home or at gym). I am giving it 5 stars for the class of fan it is (OK, 4.5 but we cant do halfsies). Small, personal, low watt, easy to travel with/carry around. Works for personal close use. It has its purpose. While I dont rate on price, I know that there are listings for the exact same product (some call it "upgraded"-- know that this is the exact same item) for a few dollars more. This is a good price point at $10 or less. As they get pricier, so do my demands and expectations, haha

title: worth the try, gorgeous clear display, ease of use, fits my 7" wrist,
text: It's pretty good, especially if you dont need a name brand. It has a beautifully clear display. Easy to install app and pairs well with no hassle. Has all the bells and whistles of name brand products. While I prefer fitbit due to familiarity. I havent put it entirely through its paces. I noticed that it was registering nearly same heart rate as my fitbit sense. I havent it worn it long enough to determine blood oxygen. There is still a lot to learn. The learning curve feels a little clunky compared to my fitbit. Has ability to connect to Alexa, take and make calls, music. Can make changes through app or scroll through the screen face. The watch band fits my 7" wrist and feels comfortable enough. Typical silicone band. It is attached via pins, so I imagine it is possible to swap it out but not sure. I may try some old bands to see if it is doable. I'd also prefer for it to have a soft protective cover (bumper guard) to protect screen and edges. I still prefer the ease of using a name brand, but this has a good looking interface. Main thing is to see how accurate it is. I think it has been fine for heart rate, steps, but will need more sleep time for seeing how well it tracks sleep and oxygen. I dont rate on price, but I comment. This is pretty reasonable, but it looks like there are many similar products for less. So compared to a name brand of similar features this is a bargain. Compared to other no name generics, this is competitive. Some are easily $20 less. I noticed the price on this vacillates. I think I got it for $70, and have seen it as low as 35-40.

title: trusted brand, always holds up, lightweight hard cover, folds back, attractive, comfy in hand
text: Great case. I have been buying Moko products since my first Kindle some 10 years ago. The cases last longer than the Kindle does, haha. I get the same style and same design-- I like what I like, and so when it came to choosing another case for my new Kindle Paperwhite Signature edition, I simply went with Moko again. Design and colors hold up too! I noticed they [[ASIN:B09HCFFP63 have a listing for half the price]]. I wasn't immediately aware of the difference between that one and this one. It took a little poking around to determine that this is a hard cover (like all my others) and the other is more of a firm soft cover. I think either would be fine, but I really just wanted to go with what was familiar to me. I mention this in case you are also noticing the 2 products and are curious of the difference. I noticed one review over on the other page saying that the quality was different and they were disappointed. But what I concluded is that they were used to THIS product, and bought THAT product. It is two different products! Nothing changed! This is a hard cover and that is a soft cover. If all you do is keep your kindle at the bedside, then the other is just fine as a dust cover and added grip. If you tend to travel with your Kindle or are more likely to drop it or bump it, then the hard cover such as this is great. It isnt heavy. The cover folds back. Adds just enough additional grip to feel much better than a plain/naked kindle. Just pop the kindle into the cradle, and then that's it. I do not have a wireless charger, but this is supposed to work with it without need to pop the kindle out. I trust Moko and will assume that is true if I ever get one.

title: ultra comfy, the most comfortable of any band I have ever used in 8 years of fitbit use
text: Been wearing mine for a couple of weeks now, and I am very pleased. I only take it off to charge and to shower. Just a good fit and feel. I can customize how snug or loose I want it with ease. Very happy! Two reasons that led me to ordering new Fitbit Sense bands: 1. I usually use the silicone bands, but the last set I bought weren't quite long enough leaving me fearful that I would lose my pricy smart watch. So I wanted a band that felt secure. 2. My last set of bands didn't have holes that made for a perfect fit. Always seemed like it was too loose feeling or too tight. It was irritating. I hoped to find a new band that offered a better fit. As one with sensory issues, having a good fit is important. I don't care for elastic style bands (they stretch out, feel sloppy), but I began sniffing around them thinking that it would at least feel more comfortable over what I had been using. But then I stumbled upon these "Bcuckood Nylon Loop" wristbands. I saw that they arent stretchy (yay!) but that they do have a velcro closure. I was intrigued! I figured that would give me the option for a custom fit, that I can loosen or tighten with ease.. so I went ahead and ordered them. Also chose them because they say they fit wrist sizes 6.3" to 8.7". My wrists are exactly 7", but all the wrist bands that only mention it fitting up into the 6-7.5" wrists aren't long enough when you consider that the band needs to overlap in order to be securely on (as well as fit over width of hand & thumb). I figured this was a winner when I saw 8.7" These are GREAT. Very happy. Love the colors. Easy on, and for the most part, easy off. I have wide pals, so sliding this off means that I am really loosing it up to do so, but I have gotten used to it and it isnt weird. The velcro are neat. They are in little disks. Really grabs the material securely. I really like how secure this band feels. I love the best off all how I dont feel like I am wearing a watch. This band makes my wrist feel free. So far, no stink. But Ive only been wearing it a couple of weeks during the winter. So not much sweat to consider, and frankly I havent been engaging in sweaty exercise.

title: flexible fit, both fit my 16" neck, truly does have cooling effect, freezes quickly
text: Ok, I' sold, and wish I had these earlier in the summer. I thought this was a goofy idea. But I was curious so I put in an order. I placed them in the freezer, and kinda forgot about them. I came back an hour later and they were totally frozen. I put the larger of the two (blue) on my neck. I was surprised that it didnt feel like a burning cold. Even though it said that there is no concern for skin burn, I was still apprehensive. So I can say, direct from freezer totally frozen it felt comfortable. Not just comfortable, but refreshing. And, later, I learned that they freeze in the refrigerator too. What is this sorcery? I'm not sure how long it lasted. Seemed like I wasnt feeling a sensation like I started with shortly after, but then I also noticed that I wasn't as run down hot feeling (summer is still hanging in in NY, higher temps with humidity). I continued to do big chores around the house and felt good. I could see little floating chunks of frozen bits inside as it melted. Still felt coolish a couple hours later it seemed. But maybe I just felt coolish. I will love this for when I am working outside or mowing the lawn (with my push lawn mower). I may try this against my forehead and hold it in place with a sweat band. If these continue to work out, I would buy another set to be able to swap out to as they melt. I truly thought these seemed gimmicky but now that I have tried it, I see the value in having them available. With the uncertainty of power grid, brown outs, etc, I think this is nice addition to ways to try to keep cool with out AC (thinking especially of folks in the southwest). The main thing that makes these so doable is that they can be direct against skin and there is no skin burn. Flexible fit. I have a 16" neck, and both fit fine Lavendar is listed as being 15" Blue is listed as being 17.7"

title: responsive touchscreen, sharp looking! wireless keyboard (no dongle needed), & wireless mouse
text: This review is for the 12th Generation Intel Core i3-1215U w/ Intel UHD graphics I like it so much that I would buy this again if I didn't already have a high performance gaming desktop, and a new lap top of similar specs to this Dell All in One. Know what you need your computer for. No fair in comparing it to a high end system required for gaming and huge programs when it is designed for home office use. This is excellent for typical web browsing, youtube watching, solitaire/mahjongg playing, video calling, office basics. It is plenty enough memory and processing power for shopping and watching cat videos. It's lovely. Would I try to run an MMO-RPG or a huge photo editing studio on it? Probably not. I love it though, it is gorgeous, responsive, and I love the touch screen. It feels so intuitive. However, I got it with my mom in mind as she hasn't had an actual computer in several years (been living off tablet only). I set it up very quickly. Very easy. Some observations off top of my head: --The legs of the stand just snap on. Very sturdy, and attractive. --The wireless keyboard just takes three AAA batteries (included) NO DONGLE REQUIRED. Just turn on, and it instantly pairs with the computer. As for the mouse, it takes one AA battery (Inlcuded) and uses a usb dongle. Also needs to be switched to on position. --Windows 11, has many of the typical bells and whistles. Free Disney+ for 6 months (no idea of what is expected for that, I didnt check into it other than seeing the icon on the desktop) --Very quiet. Is it on? is it off? very quiet. --Love the white and silver appearance. Nice change from black. While I dont mind what color the computer is, my mom always preferred a lighter color for use on her large kitchen counter. This fits that need. Clean looking motif. --Touch screen is just way too cool. I havent had experience yet with using a desktop with a touch screen. It just feels so intuitive. Just touch the screen to make things happen. LOVE! --Web Camera is a "pop up" out from the topside of the monitor. So you will know if it is on or not. I like this for that reason, and it makes the overall appearance look nice and clean. But since it is an extra part of the sort, it brings to mind chance of breakdown. Just press down and it pops up. Takes picture and video as expected. Resolution of both is typical. Clear but nothing fancy. --Sound is fine, visuals are fine. --Built in card reader, 2 HDMI ports, 4 USB ports, 1 USB C port, Ethernet port, 1 audio port --Good amount of weight-- it feels secure. At no point did I feel like it was going to move, or tip over. --Screen tilts back or forward. I found this nice as it is sitting on a large kitchen counter, and sometimes it will be used while standing, and other times with butt parked on a bar stool. --Keyboard tucks in between legs for cleaned up look. --Information that comes with it is sparse. Very basic start instructions (I didnt need), warranty info (detailed), and a card that provides directions on downloading a Dell app for added assistance and information. I thought maybe a PDF would be available on this product page or on their website, but I didnt see one. I will have to try their app and see what sort of info is available. I really wont need it myself, but I want to make sure my mom has access to info. Overall, it wasnt hard for me to conclude that this is a nice computer. It will take more time with it to truly see how it does. For that, I will come back to update if/as needed. My instant love of the touchscreen and how responsive everything is made me a little envious. At this time, I would recommend it. If you find you might want to spring for a little more hard disk size, then they also offer a 512 GB with 8 gig memory. This has 256 GB hard disk with 8 gig memory. Going with 5 stars as it meets or exceeds my expectations. Again, know what you want this for and choose accordingly. I dont rate on price, but it is a reasonable price for what you get, how it looks. Ooh, and that sweet sweet touchscreen!

title: responsive, quick. Good machine for most needs, see data sheet link for details
text: Not sure why anyone thought this is a touchscreen. Nowhere does it mention it. Take a look under "Product Guides and Documents", which you can find just above the review section. There you will see is a highlighted link to the "SPECIFICATION SHEET (PDF)". Click on that, and it will tell you even more detail about this machine than what is already outlined in the product description. And because of that, I wont rehash all what this has. But look for that link so you can decide if it has what you need!!! For those saying that this does not have a finger print ID? YES IT DOES. Search for it in your settings. IT IS A SETTING that you must set up. Hit the magnifying glass icon, then type in "fingerprint sign-in". Follow instructions. Can also set for using a PIN, which I do. Overall, it is a good basic laptop. Enough memory to load some photos and videos, plenty of processing power for a lot of basic uses: watching video, email, internet browsing, low end games. Likely good for most school needs, and some office needs. I haven't pushed it to the max because my needs are fairly low end. I have a separate high end desktop for true gaming needs, and for mega storage. Cant blame a machine for not doing what you want if you dont know anything about it to start. Learn what 8 gb ram is and what 512 gb ssd can do for you, and know what your needs are. Work up, or down from there. This seemed to be the sweet spot for my casual needs. It runs smoothly, quietly, and cool. Battery lasts a long while, which is nice for on the go use. Your experience may vary. Depends on what you are doing, your settings, etc. Very responsive, though like I said I havent put it through the paces. Even Microsoft Edge is blazing quick and easy to use. I had it on my last laptop (half the memory and processing) and it was all I could run. I figured I would be switching to firefox, but I keep using Edge without issue. Responsive touchpad, though since I prefer using a mouse I turned off the touchpad. Optional backlit keyboard. Can turn on or off, or up at any time with press of button Quickly boots up, good instant connectivity Speakers are fine. Crisp. They are perfectly good, and offer some mild range. They dont make my ears bleed when I watch a music video. ONLY thing I have experienced that has been bothersome is that sometimes my "m" key doesnt register. I will be typing along, and the letter m did not actually type. However, it is hit and miss, and it might be a matter of how I am sitting or something. I havent had the experience while writing this review. Unless you notice missing m's that I didnt. I' pleased. So far so good. I am giving it 5 stars (4.5 if we could do half ratings), and am giving it that for the CLASS of laptop, and that it is what the product description says it is. Minor annoyances regarding anti virus, updates, microsoft stuff is typical across computers. All in all, it is what I expected, nothing negative that I can think of, and if I experience anything else worth sharing--good, bad, or otherwise-- I will do so. I keep up with my reviews. I am an avid reviewer and aim to be helpful as much as possible.

title: great batter life, battery level indicator on the storage case (which is also charging base)
text: Nice set of ear buds. I use them primarily for when I am working outside, and especially when mowing the lawn. I didnt want to risk losing, damaging my pricy pixel earbuds, so I looked for an inexpensive pair. I didnt expect these to be as nice as they are. title: perfect replacement for my old remote. Exact match. Just add batteries, no pairing needed
