title: game changer for comfort. Mouse and Arm are in natural alignment, instant relief
text: This is my first ergonomic mouse. Wish I had tried one way before now. I dont know what my hold up was, maybe because they looked weird and uncomfortable, haha. Well I know what prompted me to try one: my wrist has been bothering me, and it seemed to be made worse with mouse use. I guess all my gaming years have added up. I didnt know which to try. So many! I didnt know what would fit. There are some really small looking ones and some that look bulky, some that are nearly same in appearance as a standard mouse, and some that have a deeper cut out where hand rests. Very confusing. So I just spent some time reading through various reviews of a wide assortment of ergonomical mice. While I think some of it is trial and error for getting the right fit, I think I happened upon a really good fit and feel with my first try. I really have nothing to compare it to, but so far I am really quite pleased. --I dont have small hands, but they aren't exactly big either. Size can be in length and width. I have quite small fingers, but wide palms (3.75"). So typically a size "large" in gloves, but the ends of the fingers always dangle quite a bit. Hope that gives impression going forward with my review: --My hand easily grasps the width of this mouse. Feels very comfortable. My pointer finger just reaches the scroll wheel. I dont need to reach for it; my finger pad sits directly on top of apex of the wheel. --Press of left or right side is easy and comfortable. Plenty of length to accommodate even the smallest of fingers. Yet plenty of spare room for fingers longer than mine. -- Not a loud click, but I can feel the click. I personally find that satisfying. Gentle yet makes me feel my action. --Scrolling is smooth. --No stuttering or jerkiness --Instant connect when I first got this, and no problems since --Impressed with how natural it feels. Didnt realize how much the wrist and forearm twist to use a standard mouse. With this, the mouse and arm are in a natural alignment --Charging is quick and easy. Comes with cord for charging. I charge it directly through use of my laptop. It can be used as a corded mouse with ease. Can store dongle in the mouse if need be. Has on/off switch. When in the ON position, it will go to sleep when computer shuts down (or after x amount of time when not used), and wake up along with computer. Typical for rechargeable mouse. If this is anything like any other rechargeable mouse I have had, it should hold a charge for a very long time. --Haven't used this for gaming yet as I have it for use on my laptop, but may try it out on my gaming PC. If I like it, I will just buy another. I think it will work out. This is just so comfortable and easy to use. Take a little getting used to, yet at same time feels really natural. Good grip, good responsiveness, all around good experience in the short time I have had it. Your experience may vary in terms of fit, but I think the quality is evident. I will update if I have anything else worth sharing :) EDIT/UPDATE: Seriously love this mouse, and this company is great. They are VERY RESPONSIVE and helpful when I inquired about an issue I had. WOW really good customer service. Rare these days, thank you. Truly, 5 STARS ALL AROUND.

title: versatile velcro, cut to preference, hook on one side, soft latch on other, self gripping
text: What can I say, it is legit brand name Velcro! One of my must have items alongside duct tape, twine, cable ties and the such. This is hook on one side, latch (soft) on the other. Slender. You have likely seen this attached to cables and cords on devices for cable management. Think of it as a soft cable tie, but instead of a fed locking mechanism, the "hook and latch" do their thing. Press and go. Makes for easy peasy cheap curtain tie backs. Keep in mind that this is one long single strip of velcro. 45' of velcro. 3/5" width. It is double sided. Meant for self gripping. Other styles include non adhesive two separate strips, or two separate strips with adhesive. This is hook on one side, soft latch on the other. Simply bundle something up, then wrap this around. The overlap of one wide to another will lock it in place. Useful as a means to attach things to hiking bags (when dont need, want a D-ring), or in something that goes around wrist or waist.

title: comfortable and pretty
text: So far so good. I almost always buy bands beyond what comes with the fitbit. I have the Sense, and these work just fine with it. Pop on. Cute little cut outs and scalloped edging add visual appeal. Has two loops for added security. Fits my 7" wrist.

title: easy set up, all looks good, slim profile, lightweight
text: Basic DVD player, and that is pretty much all I needed. It is not complicated to set up at all. title: decent power bank, charges quickly, charges phone in good time, terrible solar
text: Works fine as a power bank, just make sure you check your device as I often found it not charging. I had to wiggle the cord, or plug and unplug. Really annoying. Maybe it was my cord. Anyway, powered up my GooglePixel 6 from 54% to 81% in a reasonable amount of time. I didnt time it, but it wasnt as fast a typical quick charge, but it wasn't slow either. It was enough to make me feel comfortable to rely on this as needed. (4 stars) Flashlight works (low beam, high beam, flash) . Not a super impressive light, something akin to flashlight feature on phone. (3.5 - 4 stars). Works in a pinch, like seeing it as an addition to the power bank. Solar panel? eh, not enough to say it is worth it. Too weak. It never picked up any power even set in a sunny window. Next time I will try it outside and hope for enough sun. I want it to at least charge this up enough to be useful, otherwise, why pay for this feature? (1-2 stars) Overall? eh, wish it worked better. Wish I wasn't influenced by a youtuber to pick one of these up. I did shop around a little, and nothing stood out as better, and the prices were all about the same. I'm going with 3 stars, it's "OK".

title: solar charge actually works, good assortment of features,
text: [[VIDEOID:17a58332b933800fe99b76e58398768d]] We have a few of these emergency radios. I am the main prepper in the household, but even my husband bought one at random recently. He showed me his, then I showed him mine. Then I got this one to add to the collection. Different brands, all very similar. The one feature that STANDS OUT to me on this FORTECLEAR is that there is a light that indicates that it is being charged. I can see it glow brighter when using the hand crank, as well as when I have it sitting in a ray of sunshine. If in the sun with the light glowing, once I cover the solar panel with my hand, the indicator turns off. Really nice to see that working. Like others, there is also an indicator that shows about what percent of power is has (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) which will light up when it is being actively used. Really nice to be able to see this important info. For that I recommend this as an emergency item (or even casual use, why not?) Has typical features such as flashlight (low beam, high beam, and flashing), has a flip up "reading" light, and radio bands such as alert, WB, FM, and AM. Nice long antennae, knob tuning, knob volume control. USB port, USB C port, comes with a cord & instructions, wrist strap, has SOS alarm- which requires pressing for a couple of seconds to activate, SO much better than another where I have accidentally triggered it by a simple short press. Scared myself. LOL. SO LOUD. When looking for weather band, you may need to walk around to get a signal. I find this true of all emergency radios, or any radio with WB/NOLA option. As with most all other radios, FM comes in the best, the easiest. I am a big fan of having multiple options for lighting- whether it be solar, battery operated, internal battery that can be charged, etc. This has the ability to be charged, to be hand cranked, and to be solar charged. Nice to have a few options in one device. I also keep regular flashlights, rechargeable flashlights, battery powered radios, etc on hand. Multiple options for when it is needed. But this will be one I will rely on. I would get it again, and I would get this for someone else. I tend to give functional gifts, stuff that most folks dont want to buy for themselves (preps, fire extinguishers, smoke alarms, car care kits, etc), and this would be a good one to give. Really pleased that it works so well because it happens to be a few bucks more than most options out there. I will continue to play around with this. If I think of anything else, or experience anything else (good or bad) I will be sure to come back to update. So far so good!

title: good price for a must have prep item, keep one at home, at office, in car, on person, etc
text: Another good one. Been restocking my radios, making sure I have a couple in the house, one in each car, and even one on my person. A basic radio is a must have for shelter space, emergency kits, keeping in car, having as part of Get Home or Bug out Bag. I have a thing for battery operated radios, and recently acquired a few more at the same time (2 is 1, 1 is none). I keep them everywhere because you never know when the need for info from the outside world will be needed, and right now that seems more relevant than ever *vaguely waves arm around*. I have to say, other than price and a few details, the functions and overall performance are the same. This is a (refreshing) bargain at $9.99. For that, I recommend this. I have found that radios of this style pretty much all work the same, sound the same. Just look for details that are of interest to you. When it comes to this Prunus radio, I like the small size. Not as small as another one I have, but close. It fits in palm of my hand, almost reminds me of my old portable cassette player. My thumb desperately wants to push a button, haha. Easily will slip into a pocket, hiking bag, purse, glove compartment, desk drawer, etc, . Roughly 5" x 2.75" x 1.25". Has AM, FM, and WB. I can tune in to the weather band with some effort--so be patient. I tried it on a dark rainy day from inside my house, and with antennae fully extended I just moved it all around until I caught a signal. The sound was faint, but I got it. It will suffice in an emergency. As for FM, that is clearest (usually is), followed by AM. Works well and as expected. Sound overall is clear. I find that it could work as a portable sound machine. Just find a station or range of frequency that doesn't have a working channel. White noise! Takes 2 AA batteries (not included), and has a standard ear phone jack port. Includes a wrist strap, and also has a belt clip (clip to whatever you want, nice addition for on the go use). I find the belt clip adds appeal as I keep a tactical back pack in my car, and this would slip no problem into a molle loop. Another pro: Big numbers/letters--easy to see! Overall dimensions fit nicely in my hand. Adjustable volume is plenty loud. Very long antennae. 5 stars. No problems, works well, easy to use/manipulate, meets expectations, glad to have it. I'd buy it again, buy it for others.

title: charges quickly, good cord length, nice for Apple & Android users in same household

title: so many features, easy to use face & app, responsive to touch, waterproof, check it out!
text: This product description doesn't do this product justice. I am impressed. I am already a fan of Sanag products, so I expected this to be good. It is. I'll list everything I can think of below. I have been looking for an easy to use fitness watch for my 70+ years old mom. She mentioned interest in one, but I am not sure how much she will enjoy it. While I like fitbit (been using that brand since 2015) I didnt want to get her one if she wouldnt like the technology. I looked through what I already own, but nothing seemed right. I have a garmin that I wouldnt have anyone new to fitness watches use (hate that thing). I have an Amazon Halo, which is great but its attached to my account so I cant have her try it. And I have a weird off brand tracker that I got a few years ago that it too complicated to use (clunky app, slow to respond swiping). I basically need a tracker to be easy to use (both the tracker and the app) and be something I feel comfortable having my tech adverse mom use. I chose this based on what I read in the description AND my positive experience so far with Sanag. I figured I would try this watch for a couple of weeks before deciding if it would work for her. I have been wearing it day and night for a little over a week, and I may not give it to her.. because I love it. haha I'm just going to bullet point the features I have noticed so far: --waterproof. I wear it 24/7. Though I do take off for showering, I am just used to doing that. I also clean homes for living, and this can take a beating. -- easy to find, install, and use App (da fit), many customizations, options to set up. --pairs easily with bluetooth; no hassle. --interesting color, nice feeling band. Very secure feeling. Though, I'd prefer the band to be a little longer. I have a 7" wrist, and this just fits. Will be fine for my mom who has very petite bone structure. --super long battery life. I charge my fitbit sense every other day. Other than initial charge, I have not yet had to charge this. I'd say they are accurate on their 7-14 day charge on normal use, or 30 days on standby. That being said.. -- blood O2 measurment is on demand. Not automatic. Just go into watch face or app to measure. It keeps track. Heart rate can be continuous measurement or on demand. --Can choose from many many many watch faces. So many different styles, some are super cute. Different faces depending on what you want to see, ie just the time, time and date, time, date, steps, hr, cals burned, etc. If you have a few that you like, then you can scroll through what you have used in your watch itself to to select one, or you can go to the app to select one. --steps are accurate as far as side by side with my Fit bit Sense. Same steps (within 20 steps) when worn side by side on same wrist. --gorgeous display- very colorful and easy to read --easy to navigate with swiping; very responsive. Easy to back out from selections. --on watch can see time, date, steps, heart rate, 02, blood pressure (havent checked yet for accuracy but I will), weather, sleep data, exercise specific date (and tracking), alarms, timers, music control, camera shutter control, and settings notifications (can set up to see notifications from many sources such as email, phone calls, texts, FB, IG, Whatsapp, etc etc ect-- huge list that can be turned on for notifications to allow to come through if you want. Can pick and choose). --on watch can select options such as "do not disturb", brightness settings, lock option, --can connect to google fit --can keep track of other health trends (menstrual, for example). --can set a step goal, reminders to move, reminders to drink water I am not sure if there is a spot to adjust how long the face stays lit when looking at something. As of now, it goes black after a few seconds. Much like other fitness watches. --App has all this same info, with ability to look at more details --VERY easy to navigate app. REALLY an impressive gadget. I think some of it will come down to preference. I am still getting used to it, and sometimes I find the outer button is easily pressed by my bent wrist. I have accidentally changed my watch face that way, but I am seeing now that if I end up on that screen I have to make sure I am setting the face by swiping up (otherwise navigates to another face by swiping left/right). Litte annoyances that will vary. For all that it offers, for the ease of use especially compared to some name brands, I am compelled to go 5 stars. If we could do half stars, maybe 4.5. But I like it more than 4 stars. Overall nothing glaring bad or super negative comes to mind. I'll update as I learn more or think of more, or experience something different (good or bad). reasonable price at $79 (though I had a coupon which really helped make my decision), any higher and I would go with namebrand.

title: Six, 6' (USB to USB-A) cords, convenient length, performs well, so far so good!
text: Six pack of 6' long cords. USB on one side, USB-A on the other- for Apple products. Just add your own wall adapter if needed. Six feet length is the sweet spot for me. title: easy to set up, grab an SD card (up to 128 GB), then enjoy the added security & viewing
text: Overall, I'm pleased with the features. Really no major cons, and the pros are solid. 4.5 stars (well, 5 stars since we cant so half rating and I like it better than 4 stars since I may buy another). I cant see why anyone would dislike it, and so far haven't seen any reviews saying anything that gives red flags. We have several security cameras, but I have a couple of spots that I want to incorporate some redundancy, and a better angle/view. This being solar powered helps greatly to achieve that. Make sure to get the CloudEdge app, and from there just install and follow all directions. Makes for a nice entryway camera if you dont want to install a doorbell style. We have been having some bad winter weather, so it took me awhile to get it set up, and the spot I put it has had so much snowfall that no one is walking near where it is installed, not even me. However imaging is good. Same or better than my current set up. Audio is good, if not better. Main aspects I like.. EASY set up. No fancy skills or tools needed. No need for power source other than some sun. That can be tricky for stretches of darkness, but the big battery stores a lot of power. No issues thus far. The 4dbi dual antenna ensures that the solar security camera has stable network reception, and quickly connects to 2.4Ghz WiFi from a longer distance. If you dont want to pay for cloud storage, then grab a 128 GB storage card. I dont rate on price, but I do comment. For the price with $50 coupon, this is something I am considering buying another of for another area of house. Could be a trail cam if you have the wifi connectivity to reach. I might get one for my 70+ years old mom so she can have the added security of seeing who is coming to the door. I also appreciate all the information on the product page. That always factors into my rating. I also appreciate that they seem to be open to contact if need be. That is reasurring in terms of customer service, and is what helped me decide to go with this Jeeber product over others. So far so good, if I experience anything else I will be back to update

title: comfortable, good sound, sits securely over ears, plenty of options, very pleased
text: LOVE these over the ear air conduction earphones. I have a pair of bone conduction earphones that I fell in love with, and I wanted another pair of different style to for use when working out (my others stay at bedside for evening podcast listening, music, meditation). These looked like they hook over the ear securely, and they do! If new to this style, be prepared to play around with them a bit, and take advantage of the ear plugs as they help deepen the sound. I personally find the sound to be good and clear. I have some auditory sensitivities, and these just feel right- no irritations, aggravations, or off sounds. The reason why I dont use IN ear ear buds is because they always bother me- usually pain or some headache or nausea ensues. I can wear them for short periods of time as needed, but I do not enjoy them for longer duration- ie listening to music while working out. I can never find just regular headphones that hook over the ears without going in. So that is basically how I got to know bone conduction. Now that style is my go to. I also like that I can still sense/hear what is around me with these, again perfect for working out. Being waterproof puts me at ease when I sweat profusely. Pair with a bluetooth MP3 player, or add to memory card for direct play through the headset. Good price, good quality, so far really good experience. I recommend!

title: comfortable, easy to use, easy to pair for BT, good sound esp when paired w/ ear plugs
text: I'm pleased with these bone conduction headphones. I almost never use ear buds because they can give me a headache (I have a one piece bud for use while hiking), and over the ears are really hard to find. They are always ear buds. The headphones that have the strap over the head are ok, but they can be bulky, and over a period of time a give me a headache too. I basically have been searching for an over the ear outside sitting headphone where the strap also goes behind the head. Last time I was able to find one was like 10 years ago. So another search brought me to bone conduction. They are pretty much what I am looking for. I noticed that the sound is way better with use of the ear plugs, and the sound can vary depending on how the headset is placed. When everything is lined up perfectly, the sound is really impressive. When the line up isnt perfect, the sound it doable but not perfect. I find that these are great for use when I am lounging and just want to listen to music or a book or podcast. I have not tried them in water, doubt I ever will (unless I am walking in rain). I have a big head (23.75" around) so that might contribute to the placement, and how well it sounds. Very easy to pair with my phone, easy to adjust volume, and easy to move up or back a track. 4stars for the variability in sound depending on placement (and definitely best is used with ear plugs) 5 stars for comfort, and never ever produces a headache. That was my primary concern, and so I am extra pleased with that.

title: durable cords, long length, plug & play- works seamlessly w/MP3 player in our Jeeps

title: 1 sleeping bag, 1 poncho, 1 emergency whistle. Bright orange w/mylar lining. Nice kit!
text: 1 sleeping bag- mylar 1 raincoat/parka (has a hood)-mylar 1 drawstring nylon bag with toggle, mini D-ring clip, AND emergency whistle (sounds toy like, but it makes plenty of noise). Sleeping bag is 84" long, and measures 36" wide (so 72" around). Depending on your gear, can be used as bivi sack for use over existing sleeping bag, or possibly as a makeshift tube tent. Or cut fully open for use as a blanket. Mylar material helps trap body heat. Options for use to keep you warm. I always keep an emergency blanket in my car, and hiking packs. I got this because I like that ONE of the items is a RAIN COAT with hood (40" wide, about 80" around. Length including hood is @49", measured from shoulder down is roughly 37"). One way to not get chilled to the bone is to not let clothing get wet. These are reusable. Whether you will want to try to reuse them is another thing. The material is durable enough for more than one use, it is really just a matter of getting it flattened out and folded to fit back into the bag (good luck). I unfolded and opened mine to make sure I had what was described and to make sure it would fit my 5'10" 265# body frame. But I just held it up to me, and all looks good there. Then I carefully folded it back up and was able to just get it back into bag. I doubt I would be as successful if I had fully fluffed out the material. Alas, all looks good, mylar looks fantastic. Pleased to have this. Whether one use or multiple, I find these products a must have for any car kit,hiking pack, get home kit, bug out bag, camping supplies, etc. This bag is tiny, and takes up very little space.

title: so far so good, excellent clarity, accurate steps & heart rate, easy set up
text: Probably want to select reviews based on "most recent" as that will provide you with most up to date and relevant information pertaining to this product. I acquired my Fitbit Sense in June 2021, it has not yet been a month, but so far so good with 24/7 use. I am slow to check out and use all the features, but what I have interacted with so far has been stellar. I have been using Fitbit products since April 2015- kinda have a love/hate relationship with this brand. I use the activity tracker constantly, and I greatly enjoy the app. So I have stuck with it as I upgraded over the years (Charge x2, Blaze x2, Versa 2, and now Sense). As with many Fitbit users, there is a known frustration with the products. Despite some of my own qualms, and having the ability to spend whatever I want on any fitness tracker I want, I still end up (so far) with this brand. Mostly because I haven't found a tracker and app that I totally like better. I even have a Garmin, but I find that so far off base of accuracy (save for HR), that it is a glorified watch. Garmin seems to do best for actual intended activities (going for a run, going for a long walk, going cycling) where it seems to not be accurate in steps for any other part of the day (only counts about 1/3 of actual steps unless engaged in a longer duration activity, and even then it takes a few minutes for it to start). Also, the app seems to have a lot of info, but doent really tell me anything. That being said, when it was time for me to buy another fitness tracker--I went from Versa 2 to Garmin.. back to Fitbit. I went with the Sense because the price was right, and it was an upgrade over the Versa 2. After my underwhelming experience with the Garmin, I would have happily taken over a 2nd hand Charge from 2015. At least my steps would be accurate. Ok, so back to the Sense. WOW, the visual on the screen is really clear and precise. Even way more so over the Versa 2, and I had no issues with that. Set up was EASY, and QUICK. Basically, just like in adding any other fitbit, just let it pair and it will very quickly be all set and ready to go. I didnt have any weird upselling offerings, or at least nothing that wasn't fantastically easy to opt out from. Nothing shady that I saw. ONE POINT that I DO think is important to know is that if you happen to have a Versa 2 (Not sure if this also happens with regular Versa, Versa Lite, or Versa 3), but this could not be added alongside my Versa 2. I had to take the Versa 2 offline in order to add this Sense. I know this is the case with trying to add more than one of the same products, yet I have always been able to have several Fitbits paired no problem, as long as they were different models. SO, I guess the Fitbit app sees Sense and Versa 2 as the same. Not a big deal as my Versa 2 had essentially died after I wore it on a hot humid day and my sweat killed it (then I brought it back to life after putting it in a bag of rice for about a week, Then afterward the battery was never the same. It drained to nothing daily.. and I needed to not have to worry about daily charging.. hence my picking up a Garmin in the interim to see if I liked them enough to spring for a more fancy model--nope-- and ended up buying the Sense.) Hope it lasts. I love the look. The band is way better than the old pin style. Swapping out bands is so much quicker, easier, less need for super fine motor skills. LOVE the charger. It just sort of magnetizes to the fitbit. No need to clip in. SP02 wasn't the main feature I was drawn to, but in order to have accurate use it seems a special clock face is needed, and that clock face will drain battery quicker (from what I have read). That being said, Battery life has been excellent for me. Love being able to add other apps, and features. Scrolling is easy, turning face on/off is not complicated. HEART RATE is accurate. I have tested it against my garmin, two blood pressure devices, and a doctors appointment. All saying the same. Also, I the voice assistant is great. You can choose GOOGLE Assistant, OR Alexa. This is why selecting most recent reviews on this sort of stuff is important, as the early release of Sense did not have Google Assistant, but would soon with an update. True, and they followed through as I have it. AT THIS TIME, I have ZERO issues, concerns with this Fitbit Sense. I will be back to update as I learn more, or if I have anything worth sharing that is bad. I keep up with my reviews as needed.

title: shimmery but subtle, nice upgraded look over my usual sport bands. Stainless Steel!
text: These bands are very pretty. I have a huge assortment of bands, most of them for easy active wear (ya, know.. casual looking). But I wanted something a little different, more like a watch band when I dont want to feel as sporty. The shiny purple colors drew my attention. So a little less casual looking but still fun looking. I love how this is a pack of two, as I had been hemming and hawing which style to get, and this option made it easy. I get both!. I found the directions easy enough for making adjustments. I didn't have to adjust much as I have large wrists. Both bands are stainless steel with a subtle but shimmery oil spill purple color. I really like the flat band, so that is what I have been using most. Easy on, easy off. I dont use them daily, but I like having the nicer looking option when I depending on what I am wearing and where I am going. No problems or concerns with these Versa 2 bands.

title: COMFORTABLE & CUTE! no fuss, super comfy, adjustable, stays in place, would buy more!
text: If you want added comfort and easy of taking on and off, then try this elastic band!! Finally, a nice elastic band that isn't a scrunchy. I actually keep a hair scrunchie on my wrist, but I dont want it to compete with my fit bit. So I'm pleased to have found a band for my Versa2 that is not only elastic, but is cute, AND adjustable. What is not to love? This elastic band has lots of room to accommodate various sized wrists. My wrist is just at the 7" mark, and it is very comfortable. Can easily be made more loose or snug for a perfect unique fit. It is so comfortable, I barely feel like this is on my wrist. It just sits so naturally on my wrist, like it moves with it. Yet is so perfectly snug, that it doesn't move around (unless I intentionally loosen it up). Best feeling band I have ever used (and I have had fitbits since 2015!) I bought the "Black Colorful Floral" band, and it is lovely. If you like printed bands, I want to point out one very important consideration that makes this stand out over other printed bands. I have tried wearing other colorful bands, but they are usually a design printed on a silicone band. What happens after awhile is that the print wears off the band, and what is left is a solid color band that looks junky. I have tried a few over the years (because I always hope that something changed, and I really want a print) and I am always disappointed after a short while. SO with this band being an actual cloth material (just elastic), the print wont be rubbing off. I'm so pleased with this band :) Then lastly, I always have a "bumper" (protector) on Versa2, and I have lots of colors that I can switch to, so between this band and all my color options with the bumper, I have a different look whenever I want it! The bumpers, for reference :https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0859VXSPH/ I love this band and may add more to my collection. I definitely recommend!!

title: works to add security to fitbit watch band
text: Good. I have been using these bands as extra security on my fitbit bands since I first got a fitbit dating back to 2015. I have had several styles since then, and I always make sure to have a pack of these security bands on hand. First it was because the fitbit band was just a pressure close band that easily popped off, then it was a matter of keeping a regular watch band style extra secure. These work on the regular width bands. When I was ready to buy more of these security bands, I was about to buy some that are made for fitbit, but then I realized that those have a protrusion for locking into the band. I really just wanted something to slip on with no need to make use of the band holes to secure it. These are exactly what I wanted. Nice variety of colors.

title: easy to use, comfortable, fits my 7" wrist, has TWO security bands- extra secure!!
text: Probably the best band I have used for my fitbit. I dont know what made me decide to buy the slim style- just looking for something different that the usual wide band. I figured it would be a nice change for the summer- just a lighter look and feel. I was impressed with how easy the pins worked. Usually I am fumbling with the pins for a biut before they get attached correctly. Easy in, and very sturdy. THEN, the next thing, which is a HUGE deal to me, is that security bands. So you know how once you decide which hole you will place the stopper in, there is excess band? That always gets tucked into a security band. I have found that the watch band usually benefits from a second one just incase the band loosens out from it. I actually purchase separate bands for this purpose. This has a second band already on it! It is a very inexpensive addition that makes all the difference. I really like that this brand just includes it. I feel like this is so much more secure than it it just had one. This band is very comfortable, and it fits my large 7" wrist. I use the half way mark for the hole.

title: petite, light, digital display, front controls, remote w/ batteries, plug n play
text: I'm very happy with this blu ray player. I was so pleased with an Arufuna DVD player, that when it came time to look for a BluRay player, I was very open to trying it from this brand again. I could get a brand name for same price or cheaper, but what drew me to this one is that (besides being very happy with their DVD player) is that this is smaller than many others on the market. I already have a huge, heavy blu-ray player, and I wanted something smaller, lighter, and easier to move around. The small size of this is perfect. It is bigger than their mini DVD player, but smaller than nearly any other blu-ray player. It also has similar features that made me first select their DVD player (still small, but still has remote and front display). This Blu-ray disc player is petite but still has full functionality- ie; remote, front digital display, and controls. It works. It comes with HDMI cable as well as an RCA cable, and coaxial cable. I dont need the latter two. Good size remote comes with batteries. Easy for me to set up-- I just plugged the HDMI cable into the port on the player, and one into the back of my TV. Then plugged the player into the wall. ALL WORKS WELL. I popped in a variety of movies, and had no issue having them play. I dont often watch DVDs or Blu-ray discs, but I want the option. We have a few smart tvs, and our main already has an old Blu-ray player, but I wanted something for our other tvs. I put a DVD player (by arufuna) in my spare room, and am using this in our smaller den. Now I feel like I can grab a DVD off the shelf and not have to always stream something. 10.2" x 7.7" x 1.3"

title: top load, front display, comes w/ remote (INC batteries!), HDMI, USB power, inc Earbuds
text: Compact, super lightweight, easy set up. There is an HDMI cord, and a USB power cord. Depending on how you plan to power up, you can use the USB side, or you will need to supply your own wall adapter, or your own USB-C adapter. I wanted a DVD player for our spare room tv. I was looking at plain DVD players, and wanted something on the small side as well as something I could use with another tv or computer. This came up as an option, and I decided to take my chance on it (initially thought it pricey for a mini DVD player--but if it worked, then it would have been a good purchase). It meets all my needs. I wanted it to have a display, and a remote. It has both. It is super easy to set up-- just plug in the two cords --HDMI from DVD player to TV/monitor and power cord (plug mini USB into DVD player, then plug USB into a USB port or wall adapter). DONE! There is a small front display to show track time. There is a power button, volume dial, pause/play, forward, reverse. So remote can be used or can make adjustments directly on unit. Headphone port. Comes with ear buds! Top load. Included a sturdy remote that comes with batteries! Picture quality and response is spot on. No issues with sounds. No issues at all! Everything works. I tried everything on it. I tried it on two tvs and a monitor (it is that easy to use). I kept a DVD going for a few hours (season 1 the office) and no issues. I have tried both a store bought DVD and a rewritable. Both worked fine. I noticed a slight pause when I was messing around with the cords (working on cord management when putting in the main spot I plan to keep it). So I am not sure how it would be for "active" use. I dont plan to move around with it. So far, I am quite pleased with this unit. Meets all my needs. If I learn anything else, or experience anything else worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

title: great color & design, for the few days its lasts
text: Comfortable, cute, lovely design and great fit.. BUT, the color wears off rather easily.

title: NO dead pixels. Loved the first one so much, came back to buy a second one!
text: This quick review is for Style: 34" 1440p 144hz 21:9 GNV34DBE. Be sure to check which each review is for since they are all lumped together for the different styles. No missing pixels! Picture looks great. Works well for gaming or basic computer use ie shopping, scrolling FB, etc). Super slim bezel, sturdy base. We bought two! First my husband purchased one and immediately loved it. He does a lot of gaming and I used to, but my eyes have been bothering me a lot-- but I am still on the computer often and will engage in short gaming sessions (rip nightmare raids). So when his worked out well, I knew I had to also get one. It looks and works better than I expected. I love the new aspect ratio. Love it for everything I have seen so far. We've had them about a month so far. So far so good, if anything changes in that regard I will be back to update.

title: all these styles no matter who its bought from lose their color/design
text: The band quality and functionality itself is fine. Works perfectly with my Versa2. Good length, good secure band, plenty of holes. BUT, the design comes right off. Boo. Here's the thing. This style is just like that. So it isn't a one off situation. I took a chance on this because my experience with a similar style and from a different company for a different fitbit had exact same result- the design wears off quickly. Too bad because I think a lot of us would like a cute colorful band. And so, I am here to say that you should expect the design to wear away, particularly at the point of where you secure it down through to the end. It isn't a matter of not taking care of it or exposing it to harsh chemicals etc. It is just a color printed over the base material and it can't stay on for long. My colorful band is dwindling down to a solid white band. Buy it if you don't mind the design wearing off quickly. Buy it if you need/want a certain look for about a week before it disappears. But don't buy if you think it will last It just wont.

title: works perfectly. Super thin, easy to apply, easy to use, does not impeded closing laptop
text: I have nothing to compare these to. In the past I have used a piece of tape. This is better :) It works, it doesn't impede opening or closing my lap top cover. It is super small, thin, delicate-- but does the job. I am not even sure if I have it on correctly, but it works. When I have tried using the camera with this in the closed position, it blocked out everything. When I use the camera with this in the open position, I can see everything- no halo effect. Ooh, I think I did install it correctly. Looks like how it is in the product description pictures. When closed, the red dot shows. When open, red dot disappears and camera is exposed. It may not matter, so long as you know what is what. Cheap: 3 come in a pack.

title: responsive buttons, VOX oe Push to Talk HDX, durable feeling unti
text: For testing, we have been using these around our property. As expected, it is a half-duplex system. We each tend to use the physical push to talk button rather than the VOX option -- same principle, just that the unit detects voice/change in atmosphere/adjusts signals to allow talk. Still person at a time to speak. I'm not a fan of reading directions or deciphering technology through instructions. I tend to just poke at something and figure it out. This took me a mix. I figured some stuff out then needed to look at instructions to figure out other functions. Overall, it isn't hard to figure out how to use it, but give it a few practice runs before you really need it. If you are already familiar with products like this, then it doesn't seem to have anything wildly unique. If you need more info than what is in the box (and in the product page), there is a user manual and guide on this product page under Product Information. Look to the far right and you will see Technical Specifications. There are two html pdf links. It recommends to keep on charger when not in use. Possibly a good set of walkie-talkies for hunting with pals. Too early to tell. Outside of that, the main use is at the house- either within our two story house or when one of us is outside and one is inside. It is a convenience item for that reason. I think it will become a part of our camping or hiking items. Just a redundancy in ability to communicate as needed. The units look and feel durable. They have the heft of a cordless phone and the buttons are responsive. Can have more units added on. Nothing stands out as far as concerns go. It works! 4 stars because we haven't put it through its paces entirely. Will update as we learn, experience more.

title: impressive noise cacelling, easy set up, hurts my ears after awhile
text: My primary use is simply to have a set of headphones for listening to music or watching videos. It has a built in microphone but I haven't used it for phone calls or giving commands. Not sure if I will. The set up is easy. 1st, my pair came fully charged, and it has yet to need a charge, so I do not know how long it takes to charge from dead. It has a USB charging cord and it came with some other audio plugs. It paired easily with my phone. Just had to press and hold the center button for it to turn on the bluetooth function. The box did not come with instructions, but there is a link to their PDF manual on this product page under "product information" and then to the far right is, "Technical Specification". The link is under that. The headphones can be used as a regular set- you will hear your music, as well as other environmental sounds, OR you can turn the Noise Cancelling feature to ON, and then you will notice a drastic reduction in other sounds. It says that it will reduce most sounds but human voices may still be heard. I had them on in our bedroom. My husband likes to watch tv, and I find it distracting, and loud. We also have the AC on, which adds to the noisy atmosphere. When I put these on, the sounds were mildly muffled. When I turned on the Noise Cancelling feature, the sound of the AC pretty much disappeared. So weird. The sounds from the tv were greatly reduced, though I could actually hear the person talking a little more clearly since the AC sound pretty much disappeared. So yeh, it all functions as it should. The controls on the side take some getting used to--figuring out which button does what without having to take the headphones off. I recommend practicing- long press to advance or back up a song, short press to turn up/down volume, etc. The headphones are comfortable and accommodate my big head. They are adjustable. I like that they can be folded. My only dislike, which can be a big one is that they hurt my ears after awhile. Not sure what it is, but my head feels like it is dragged down and my ears along with it. I really dont know what causes that, and if it as feature of these or something with my structure. Has a low level pain/discomfort associated with it. I can maybe use them for 45 minutes or so, then I need them off or simply take a break. You may not experience this. To turn Bluetooth off (and save charge), you must remember to press that center button again. Turning the noise cancellation feature on/off does not do anything in that regard.

title: 10 ft is the perfect length for charging Kindle & still be able to read in bed
text: Exactly what I needed. While I have a plug next to my bed, I need the extra length to comfortably bring my device to my level (high bed, plug is at floor, so that is a few feet of space taken up before it reaches nightstand or my face). I have it primarily for my Kindle/reader as well as for my rechargeable book light (I like options). So if my battery on either is low or drained, I can comfortably still use both because of this extra long cord. Seriously, this is exactly what I wanted and it is performing exactly as expected.

title: vertical laptop sleeve w/ option to carry it like a back pack. Attractive, functional.
text: I see this as a vertical laptop sleeve with the option to carry it like a back pack. I like that the back pack straps tuck away so flatly and completely that it looks like a sleeve and doesn't look or feel clunky. You won't notice the straps until you decide to use them. There is also a strap for sliding over luggage handle. It fits my 14" laptop with a little room left over. When kept as a sleeve (and not opened into the bigger bag option), I can tuck my mouse and charging cord in with the lap top. The interior is soft and padded and is about what I expect from a sleeve, maybe even more secure. No issues. There are two front zipper pockets while it is in the sleeve configuration. An option to unzip a compartment that makes it into a bigger bag (or backpack) then provides even more space and storage options. Including two mesh side pockets for water bottles or whatever. Additional storage isn't significant, but it is functional. Can easily be used as a day bag (pack some snacks, and few other essentials), maybe pushing it as an overnight bag (unless super minimalist), but it is definitely great as a sleeve that can be opened up to carry more treasures. Doubt I would have used this as my high school or college pack pack because I usually carried a lot, and I dont think this will carry much more than a book or two. It simply isn't a traditional back pack, but I dont think you would be looking at this if that is what you were after. The material has a smooth canvas feel. Very clean lines. Minimalist look. I have this in wine red, and it a great color. I like it, and it is much nicer, sturdier, and attractive than I expected. Unless it falls apart on me soon, I see no reason not to give it full rating. If I experience anything else, I will be back to update. "Slim & Expandable Design: Slim style for light travel and commute, 200% Expandability when more belongings and easily to switch between the both."

title: old kindle has Moko case, bought a new kindle & came right here to buy MoKo
text: My husband bought me the 10th Generation 2019 Kindle to replace my Kindle Paperwhite of 2013. I needed a case pronto, so I immediately came here to find a Moko case. I remember back in 2013 looking for a cover, and found MoKo. I have been using that case ever since, with no problems and very little wear. I use my Kindle daily, and I would often tuck it into my bag when I left the house, because emergency situations call for having a good book hahah. Anyway, between the attractive options, the quality, and the longevity.. I wanted to continue with that by purchasing another MoKo case for my new Kindle. Why chance it on another brand when this one has been SO GOOD. As expected, it is attractive, has a texture that provides grip and visual interest, has a soft interior, closes snug, and is as thin and light as my other beloved case. I think this time around I may purchase couple more just because some of the designs really caught my eye and it was hard to choose which one I wanted. If anything changed- good or bad- I will be back to let you know. In mean time, I recommend a MoKo case :)

title: helped clean up my seriously gross keyboard, smells fresh & clean, scent doesn't linger
text: EDIT: added pictures. Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!). I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know! It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice. The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced. Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows. There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here: Directions say: -- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?) --Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces --Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it --Ingredients: Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin. --Made in China

title: perefectly good HDMI set of cables
text: Package of two, 6ft HDMI cables. Quick delivery, exactly as expected. We had needed an HDMI cable for a computer, and the extra one we had tucked away didn't work, so my husband took one from a tv/roku set up. That meant I had to replace the cable asap. That is where this came in. I was happy to see a 2 pack, because there is one more spot that I needed one (another tv/roku situation). So now I am set. 6 feet is ideal for my needs.

title: good little budget friendly MP3 player, no issues
text: I bought this simply to play music, primarily mp3. I don't use any of the other functions, but it has several such as e-reader, FM radio, pictures, video, alarm, pedometer. Lots of extras if you like that sort of thing. I just load it up with music from my computer, then either listen to music through a set of wired headphones, or I connect to a bluetooth speaker, or my main reason.. listening through speakers in my truck. It's an old truck with no current technology. I use one of those cassette adapters to play this music. Or when I borrow my husbands newer car, I use the bluetooth or more often, use an auxillary cord to connect. I never intentionally listed to it through the built in speaker. I like that there is that option despite not making use of it. Since I use it primarily while driving, I needed to be able to get to the music without having to look at the screen or buttons. The only MP3 player I ever really loved was the old ipod classic circa 2005- so easy to navigate. I have yet to find anything quite like that, but at least this RUIZU Mp3 player is easy enough to navigate, so that makes me happy. It takes a little getting used to though. For my driving experience, I have a made a couple of folders of music. Occasionally I just let the mp3 player shuffle everything I own. I have no idea if it skips a lot of music. It does seem to like to bring up a few of the same songs frequently. Overall I don't care.. I just want music playing. This is my second Ruizu. First one of a different model lasted a year, then it began to not play right, or at all. So when it came time to buy another MP3 player, I looked at so many-- then circled back around to Ruizu since I was already familiar with it. The price makes it worth trying. I am pleased with this one so far. I have been using it for a few months now, no issues. Battery life is good- I don't need to charge it too often. It is providing me with music when I want it, and that is all I really need it for. If I learn anything new, or experience anything worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

title: slim profile, smooth tracking, plug & play connection, can charge & use at same time
text: Slick, small. The main aspect that I like about this is not having to change the batteries. It seems to hold a charge for quite some time (I have been using it nightly for a couple of weeks straight out from box; have yet to actually charge it). I use it entirely with my lap top because I can't stand using the touch pad. So I always use a corded mouse or a cordless mouse. Usually the batteries last a good while, but it is extra nice to not even have to worry about them. When it comes time to charge I can still use it AND charge it by using the USB charging cable. When not in use, the dongle is stored on bottom of mouse. It has a little magnetic port that it slides into. Overall, it works perfectly fine. Smooth-- I use a colorful mouse pad most of the time, but sometimes solid black. Can change DPI, so that will make a difference in smoothness and tracking. "Featuring 5 adjustable DPI (2400/2000/1600/1200/800)" What I don't care for, and this is entirely a personal preference, is that it is very sleek and flat. I am used to a beefier mouse-- both a cordless for my lap top as well as a corded for my desktop. I am used to that hump in the middle, and this is rather flat. I don't have huge hands, but I have wide hands. So for short term use it is fine. For longer term use, it could be tiring on the hand. Since I use it with my laptop, and I usually only use it for a little while before bed to check out the internet or play a silly game, it is ok. But for more intensive activities, especially gaming- I need a mouse that fits MY hand better. I do like it though for my short term use. Again, I really like that it is a rechargeable mouse. That is the selling point for me. So if you are ok with a slim profile mouse, this should be just fine for your needs. If you are used to a beefier mouse with that hump in the middle, you may not care for this for long term use.

title: easy set up, adds boost to sound/dimesnion/volume compared to internal smart tv speakers,
text: I am using this strictly to boost the sound on our smart tv- a secondary but often used tv. I had purchased a similarly looking sound bar for my smart tv several months ago that works well. When this item came up as an option for review I figured it would an interesting item to try out since it has the addition of a subwoofer. Maybe it would be louder? Maybe it would sound more dynamic? We would see.. er, hear. So I tasked my husband with replacing our other sound bar with this set. It took him very little time to get it set up (less than 10 minutes, and it only took that long because our cat was helping. "helping"). The sound is definitely better and clearer than just using the speakers the tv comes with (which is usually the case). The sound is on par with the sound bar we had been using, except with the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. Without the subwoofer, it sounds just louder. With the subwoofer, it adds some depth and a nicer overall sound. We really just needed our tv to be louder. Cable is typically loud, but some programs on the various streaming services we have all have different levels of audio, with many being much too quiet. So better speakers have helped a lot. The subwoofer connects to the soundbar via bluetooth. Both plug in, so plan to have 2 open spots in your power bar or wall receptacle. We have this system set up so the volume can be adjusted using the smart tv remote, rather than having to use the remote it came with. No issues there at all. Easy! While I have the soundbar directly under the tv, I have the subwoofer set up in a corner a few feet away The soundbar has spots in the rear in case you want to mount it to a wall. Subwoofer, does not. Both are basic and minimalist looking. Subwoofer is black on black, soundbar is black with dark gray. No obnoxious branding or colors. The instruction booklet is thorough, including information about the remote, battery info, placement and mounting, general operation, bluetooth operation, AUX in operation, Line-in operation, Optical-in operation (which is what I am using for use with my tv). Overall sound is decent. Not home theater experience, but it definitely provides a sound and volume boost to internal tv speakers. I haven't yet tried it as a speaker for music. I really only purchased my original soundbar for use with tv (and replaced it with this for same purpose). I may give it a try anyway sometime soon. If I do, I will report back on how it does. I like the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. I like the overall aesthetic. And because the combination of the two allows me to hear shows better than just using the tv speakers (on low audio streaming, as cable is always loud), I am pleased to use this. I don't know hat this product costs, so I can't compare it. But, in short, it is about the same as just about any other low to mid priced soundbar. This is better sounding with addition of subwoofer. Not amazing, but definitely adds to my listening experience. 4 stars so far.

title: decent, lightweight holder; multi pack offering is best value; not anti skid
text: I'll keep it simple.: decent, lightweight holder; multi pack offering is best value PROS: These are super light weight stands that will prop up pretty much any phone or tablet. They are adequate for their purpose. The stand can be adjusted to any position, and the spot that the device rests on is generous. Small, light and easy to carry around these have convenience in portability. Also, as I have the multi pack, you can place them all over or share. Or lose some, haha. Best value is multi pack. Single price is too much for quality of this product. CONS: They claim anti-skid, but it fails in that feature. So lightweight that if you intend to tap at your device often, depending on what surface you have this placed on, it will scoot around some. I recommend modifying it with a couple beads (or line) of hot glue to give it a rubbery bottom. Or use a scrap of rug pad (that non slip material), or simply use it on a less smooth/hard surface. If just needing to prop up phone or tablet, then it will stay put. The kickstand is solid. I am most comfortable using it on a smaller device if only because these have barely any weight to them. I have a much heavier stand that I prefer to use, but the price for one is significant. These are basic, light weight and super budget friendly (for multi pack). Would make for a good stocking stuffer! In my pics, I am demonstrating this product with pixel phone and LGtablet

title: works as intended, using w/ Pixel4xl, plug n' play, no need for separate power or charging
text: Not to shabby of a gadget. It's just a wee little thing- fits in the palm of my hand- a little smaller than a deck of cards. Is powered through whatever device you are using. Does not need to be separately powered or charged. What's in the (generic) box: --Amplifier unit (roughly measured at 3.5" x 2.5" x .75") --Type C to Type C Cable --Type C to USB Cable --3.5mm to 2rca Cable --User Manual (a piece of paper with info) I also received some other cable assembly in the box that I do not know what it is for. Appears to be used in Optical port. Bonus in terms of what is listed in product description, I guess. What is on the Amplifier unit: --One end of unit has: Headphone input, On/Off Switch for Bass, Volume knob --Other end of unit has USB C port (in), Optical port (out), Gain (H/L) Switch, Line Out port. Connection Diagram shows use between SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES, and Mobile phone, Laptop, computer, or PS4. States that it does not work with tv. I haven't tried it yet, but I may attempt a work around- I'll let you know if I am successful. In mean time, I have tried it between my smartphone (Pixel4XL) using AmazonMusic and two different types of speakers. The first set of speakers is a nice plug in variety. They are circa 2004 CambridgeSoundWorks- where one cord is plugged into wall receptacle , and the other plug goes into a headphone port. They sound nice with use with my phone, so I didn't expect much difference when adding this amplifier. True enough, they have similar quality. My speakers without the amplifier are loud and I can hear some range. The addition of the amplifier allowed me to manipulate the bass, which can be nice depending on what I am listening to. I switched between High and Low on the gain switch. High boosts the overall sound, and low brings out a more mellow tone. Either are good. Next, I tried it with a pair of novelty speakers circa 2002. Little SONYspeakers that are really just a headphone style output. So for purpose of review, using these is to mimic a set of basic headphones. They just happen to be in the shape of a speaker sitting on a desk rather than on the head. Cute little things, and when plugged into anything they really produce no further sound advantage over a basic set of headphones other than they aren't on the head. Thought these would be perfect to see how much this amplifier can help a bare bones basic sup par listening item. The sound went from a very low, just make out the music sound to truly being amplified. I could boost the volume and the sound opened up- not just got louder. So, while I will likely never use it with these, I thought hearing the difference on a terrible set of "speakers" (again, really just non head headphones) was absolutely worth mentioning. Tells me that this product IS working as intended. Now, my Pixel4XL has fair sound already- not nuance, but not sounding like a tin can either. Using this with my nicer plug in speakers is great. Using my phone, with my nicer speakers AND this amplifier is a little nicer, but not hugely so. Perhaps in a larger room, or in other conditions where I may need a more dynamic sound to carry. This isn't a knock on the product, I think it is a nod toward the quality of my old speakers. I definitely can hear the improvement with ability to boost bass. High to high sounds similar. My speakers can't display a low end gain. So good for this product to offer that. I do happen to have a speaker hooked up to my TV, and I am going to try to make that work if it doesn't complicate my wire management. As for cord length.. if you are using it with your headphones, this is fine. You would otherwise be plugging it into the headphone port on your device, so really, with addition of the amplifier and the other cord to connect to device, you gain several extra inches of length. Beyond that, your mileage may vary in terms of what will work for you. So far so good. PS, I had low expectations of this unit, so I am impressed with my experience so far. As I continue to try it out with various devices in various environments, if I learn anything new-- good, bad, helpful, enlightening, I will surely be back to share. I think it is worth trying out. I can't comment on price as I am not sure what these are really worth, and if there are true differences among the options out there. So my rating is based purely on effectiveness of product and accuracy of product description. If I had one wish on the options provided on this product, that would be to allow some additional range in the High/Low gain switch. I'd give this 4.5 stars, but since it is whole numbers only- 5 it is (unless I need to change it over time through learning something new about it).

title: handy gadet when wanting bluetooth capability on something that normally isnt
text: Kinda neat gadget. Not new to most people, but new to me. My truck is too old for this to be useful (still has a cassette deck!), and my husbands car is too new to be useful (already has Bluetooth tech). but I have been borrowing my moms car (late model Hyundai something or other) this week, and hers has some new technology but not bluetooth connectivity. So this came in hand for me to play music from my phone. I use AmazonMusic on my Pixel4XL, so after plugging in one end to the AUX port and the other end into the USB port in the car, I just went into Bluetooth settings on my phone. This brand comes up in the list, and I just click connect. Then hit play on my music of choice. EASY!! The USB side lights up when it is plugged in. It had me concerned that it may stay powered on once I turn car off, but so far the light on it goes out when I turn the car off. For the most part, I have been unplugging it when I am done driving for the day. --just in case it does draw on battery-- I only noticed one initial hiccup in the connection the very first time I used it, and it has been absolutely perfect ever since. This is multiple car trips, multiple unplugging/replugging in, etc. My music pics up right where it left off. The car happened to have the AUX and USB ports side by side, so the cord was plenty long enough. This comes with an additional cord length if needed. My experience so far has been perfect. It does exactly what it needs to, and easily.

title: good price, nice bundle size, works exactly as I need them too
text: You know you are an adult when you get excited to add a big bag of zip ties to your home tool box. I have an assortment of zip ties in various sizes for various tasks. If you didn't know, it is better to go a little larger than what you think you need as the length indicated is entire length and not just working length. I just so happened to have had a need for the smaller size (6" or less) zip ties to secure some corners on a multi tier wire crate. I ratcheted them tight and trimmed off the excess. In all, I used about two dozen immediately. With a pack of 500 I should be set for awhile. Always better to have too many of these than not enough. I'll be using them for sure to secure snow netting. Not on the posts (need 10-12" ties for that), but to hold together the overlap going from one roll or piece to the next. Since a section of netting always gets blown apart at some point during the winter, I just head out with a handful of zip ties and put it back together again. So yeh, 500 seems like a lot, but when you have them you need a bunch of them. The 6 inch size is also great for wire management in general, and just about any small sized securing needs. No complaints. Happy to have them!

title: works mostly as intended, inc 4 aa batt, 2 cords (car and home), details in review
text: This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around. Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out. I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine. (edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details.. DETAILS! --This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter -- The cord measurement for each is as follows: 74" wall charger cord 41" car adapter cord --Charging Time Per Battery Capacity: AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours --So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy. --On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O --Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything. --The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm). MY THOUGHTS: --I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord. PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do. In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.

title: USB C to USB C cables work as expected
text: Since these are not USB to USB C, but rather C on both ends, make sure to have a USB C port on your charger, or wherever you intend to plug it in. If you have that, you are good to go with using these. Works as expected! Package contains three USB C to USB C in different lengths (10', 6.6', & 3.3'). The bright blue nylon braided cords are attractive and sturdy. Each comes with velcro tape attached for wire management needs. I love the 10 ft cord. It provides me with lots of wiggle room as to where I use it. The 6.6' is a good size for most uses, and the 3.3' cord is perfectly fine for plugging in where you don't need your item too far away from base. I only use these to help in charging. I have no comment on data transfer speed. It's a good pack to have, especially as we see more and more items coming out with USB C. Our household has been switching over to USB C since getting our Google Pixel 3XLs. Now that we have been using USB C products, I'm looking forward to other items switching over.
