title: Light, basic, efficient thanks to Windows 10 S Mode (which is optional, read review for more info)
text: Update!!: my review below was originally written 07/2019. I wanted to add an update THREE years later, 07/2022. This little laptop is still kicking. I use it every single day from comfort of my couch to write reviews, do basic doomscrolling (lol), write emails, etc. Camera still works. Speakers still good. No major issues. I never did do any adjustments to it. Just sort of kept using it as is. I;m maxed out for memory, so it isnt something I would rely on for loading pictures onto, but as mentioned.. if you just need something to get online with and do some shopping or searching, then this is fine. Has been worth it. I happen to be sniffing around for another laptop so I can go more photo work with it, but I havent been in a rush. I came back to this review so I could refresh my mind on the specs. It was then that I realized 3 whole years has gone by! OK.. back to orginal review: It's a basic laptop. The price is right. You aren't paying a lot for a little. You are getting quite a bit of what you need for a couple hundred dollars. Cheaper than most tablets. If you just want something to get you online, to browse the internet, watch some videos, listen to some music, write some messages, play some basic games, do some video chatting, then this might be for you.I think most people want that. It doesn't have a lot of memory or speed, or a slew of storage- but it will get you far if you don't expect a lot from it. I'm a gamer, so I won't be playing any MMOs on this (nor on most prefabs that are out there). But I will use it to play a variety of offline and online games such as those found on FB or POGO (ie; puzzles, word games, board games, hidden object, casino style, etc). I use youtube to listen to music, watch videos, listen to podcasts etc.. the speakers are fine. I can hear what I need to, clearly and loudly, if I wish. Some of the sounds that come through are more dynamic than I expected, so that is a plus. I do a little bit of office stuff, so I will continue to make use of Google docs but there is an option to activate a free 1 year trial of Office 365 which includes 1TB of storage (One Drive); after that there is a fee. The Microsoft website breaks down the pricing options, which include pay for the year, or by the month, if that is of interest to you. This Windows 10 is in S mode, which is a special mode that essentially limits Windows 10 in a variety of ways to make it run faster, provide longer battery life, and be more secure and easier to manage. YOU DO NOT HAVE TO KEEP IT THIS WAY! The idea is that there is less security with non proprietary items (apps, browsers, internet security), and greater chance of phishing, slower processes, decreased PC health, etc. So "S Mode" isn't a different version, it is simply a different mode, with the usual Windows 10 home, underneath. From what I understand, you can take it out of S Mode, and you will have Windows 10 Home (and then you can use browsers of choice, apps of choice, security software of choice, etc) BUT you CAN NOT switch back to S Mode. It is a once and done deal. S Mode default browser is Microsoft Edge, the default search engine is Bing. I'm used to using a different browser, and having more freedom of choice, but I am curious how this S Mode will do, as I have noticed in my time of using it that it never bogs down. It is likened to Chrome on Chromebook- it seeks to streamline all the while being as secure as possible. If at any point I just don't like it, at least I know I have the option of just using Windows 10 Home. But again, it is a ONE WAY DECISION. The laptop itself is super light weight. It comes in at just 3.24 lbs according to description. Full keyboard, touch pad, USB 2.0, USB 3.1, headphone/microphone port, media card reader, web cam, 3 prong charge plug with long cord. Attractive black textured design. I've got some fingerprints on the lid/cover, but doesn't look bad. No dvd/cd player. I bought a cheap external for those times I want to use it for storage, watching a video, or listening to a CD. Hey, I like options. Set up is quick and easy. When Cortana (Microsoft virtual assistant) came on, I let her guide me through the start up process. I could answer a lot of her questions with speech. It did well with recognizing my words. I still have quite a bit of learning to do about this laptop. One thing that I find interesting is that it has an option to use a phone app- where it will link your laptop and phone to each other, so you can (according to Microsoft website) -Link your phone and PC to unlock a variety of cross-device experiences for Android and iPhone. -See recent photos from your phone on your PC for Android only. -View and send text messages from your PC for Android only. Again, the price is right. This does come into play for me in terms of rating. For a couple hundred dollars, I am able to scroll through FB endlessly, add some comments without tapping them out on my phone or tablet, can access full webpages, can take pics, or video call with web cam, can play some lightweight games, etc.. At this point in time, I give it a full rating. I mean, I wouldn't go below a 4 for this anyway, and a 5 might be pushing it, but it is a nifty little machine, and I am happy so far. Once I realized that I am not stuck with S Mode, that boosted my opinion of it (not all PCs or laptops are given this S Mode option). If I learn anything more that I think you will find useful, I will come back to update. I hope what I have provided thus far has been helpful to you. Take care :)

title: good volume, use friendly, comes with remote, works on charge or with power cord
text: I bought it for use with my tv. We have a smart tc with terrible speakers. Well, more like the sound is terrible with some apps, like Netflix or Amazon Prime- where the volume is sometimes not able to go up enough to really hear it, and I have sound sensitive ears. So I bought this thinking that it could lend a boost to the sound. I was able to get it to work with the cable, and the DVD player (the two areas that really don't need help), but could not get it to function with the tv itself. I tried all options, and I am either missing something or it just doesn't work with the tv. So while that issue *may* be on my end alone, I will just rate it on the actual sound. The sound it produces is definitely a boost over what I am used to with the tv speakers. It doesn't have a dynamic sound, but it isn't flat either. Not directional, more in the front sound. Clean though. I think it would be better for use with a phone, tablet, or even lap top- where you just need some clean volume. It is long, but it is sleek. It can be controlled from the unit, or with the remote. The remote is uncomplicated and makes sense it its layout. So while it ultimately isn't working (right now) for MY purpose (I aim to figure it out), it is a nice speaker, at a decent price point (I wouldn't got higher), and the options it provides is nice. Normally I go into mega detail on items like this, but there are already plenty of reviews that go over the specs nicely. So in short, -Long charge -Easy blue tooth connectivity -Comes with connectors -comes with remote for volume, power, and switching between outputs -easy to follow short instruction pamphlet -TF card option -USB -AC adapter -built in microphone (which I haven't used, and have no intention of using) --slim, sleek design --has great volume capacity, not super dynamic- but different ears will pick up different sounds. I am attuned to nuances, so I can tell that this speaker doesn't go there.. BUT I still recommend it, overall. I figure out anything else, or if I get it working for my needs, I will be back to update. I hope my little bit helped, even if it was just reinforcing the more detailed reviews. Take care, and enjoy your day :) EDIT!!! Perfection!! OK, so I took one more try at trying to get the sound to work with Netflix & Prime. I was watching Captain America last night, and could barely hear it despite the volume turned way up. I realized that the last time I had tried to use this speaker for that, I may have had the tv volume down and of course it wouldn't pick up on sound. For cable, you want volume on tv down as it is running through cable box and you the sound to only come through this speaker. For roku, etc, you would just plug it into the headphone slot, and hence want the volume up. The addition of the speaker totally amplifies the sound AND it did a great job with the sound nuances of the movie. It didn't just add volume, it enhanced the overall sound. SO this really impressed me and I knew I had to come back to update my review. I already liked the speaker at 4 stars, but now I am really happy to have this in my life. It makes ALL the difference in our program watching as we typically use Netflix and Prime daily and it is frustrating that the volume is greatly reduced. Now it is better than ever. The sound is large and fills the room, and I can hear various other tones and bass within the movie- so I guess it depends on the source not just the speaker..

title: awkward design, hard to get used to, finding it irritating to use
text: So, I have this backpack, and it is kinda weird. You have to see my pictures as it is a different style than what is pictured in the description. I don't really care for it as it is awkward to handle. --It is a basic looking back pack. I like the bright orange in contrast to the black. That is likely the only feature I really like. --The bag is deep. It measures roughly 21" long, this includes the top portion being unfolded, as that is usable space if need be. @17" wide --The access to the main compartment is a velcro closure with adjustable hook straps for added security (and to keep added length folded down). Unlike many backpacks, there is just one slit opening across the top with velcro to close. Most backpacks have a zipper closure, as well as going a bit down the sides, for ease of access. I'm not fond of how my bag is styled in that way. --Inside the great nylon cavern of the main compartment, it splits into several more compartments and pockets, including a lightly padded pocket. --exterior pockets included two open side pockets that would be great to stick a water bottle in or an umbrella. --two good sized compartments on the front- one zippered, one velcro flap closure. --one rear zip pocket, as well as what appears to be a pass through strap of material- perhaps for use on a luggage handle? --padded shoulder straps are comfortable. Straps include d-rings for clipping keys, or whatever to. --overall feel is good -I cant for the life of me find the USB port that it claims to have. I don't see anywhere for headphones, etc.. so I don't know what is going on. The part that makes me really not like it is the main opening. First, it is deep, which can be good or bad depending on your needs. But, the top folds over way to easily. So it takes some major rooting around to find stuff, and the flap wants to fold down, and if it manages to fold down, it is easily closed tight by the velcro. This is super annoying if you want to get into and out of the bag repeatedly. I'm just like STAY OPEN. If it zipped, it would be better, then at least if it folder over it would be easy enough to get it, but with the velcro closing it up, it is irritating. The other aspect that I dont care for is the hooks on the front. Well, they are anchored on the front, but since they are used to help keep bag closed (in addition to the velcro), when they aren't hooked, they are dangling down the front. So you have those kicking around in the front, and the shoulder straps and all its extras kicking around in the back. It isn't as clean or stream lined as it could be. It feels frumpy, I am sorry to say. I was hoping to replace my every day carry bag- I like to have a little cross body purse, plus a back pack for all my additional daily needs. This might get old quick as I try to get used to the odd features.

title: clear, loud, water resistant, high quality blue tooth speaker, 20 hour charge
text: YES! A blue tooth speaker that has volume, bass, mids- all without distortion. Heading into summer, this is going to be a well used piece of equipment. Out of box, first thing you notice is the heft. Also, it comes pre-charged, so with smartphone in hand I was immediately able to test this thing out. WHAT A BEAUT! It beats every single other bluetooth speaker I have ever used. Basically everything I have tried just makes the noise come out but doesn't allow for the details of the song to come through. This isn't absolute perfection in that way, but it is super solid in terms of sound quality. I can't see anyone disliking the clean, clear sound it produces. I love the analogue dials. I can make adjustments as I feel like. The battery/charge indicator is easy to check in on, and I love that it is shows a range- so you can see about how much charge is left. With a 20 hour expected use on charge, I imagine I won't need to plug it in too often. Speaking of which, you will need the wall plug to use the included USB cord. Or use it in a wall receptacle with built in USB port (which we have) Multi directional sound is evident. I can clearly hear both in front of and in back of the box. Some changes in sound as I walk around it, but that is also a matter of acoustics. We used it inside as well as outside. It sounds good wherever it is placed. It will do just fine to accommodate large spaces, and the sound will travel for outdoor use. I haven't let it get wet, but I appreciate that it is water resistant. This is not a low end, low budget item, so I wont comment on price. I have spent half this for only a tenth as good (just a sound maker not a quality sound). I'm glad this at least lives up to its description (and if you have the budget, the price). I have noticed that the price fluctuates, so keep an eye on it. I have some more playing around to do with it, if I learn anything new I will be back to add to this review.

title: Extremely clear reception and pulls in many channels!
text: I live in a heavily forested area not near any towers. As soon as I received my new HDTV antenna, I removed my 8 month old HDTV antenna that was only getting four channels, two of which were useless. The two I enjoyed were FOX and Bounce. The old antenna also needed a coaxial cable extension and coax cable adapter to reach the window. U MUST HAVE's HDTV antenna is the best in many ways and I'm completely thrilled with it. It was easy to install, following the included well-written and diagrammed setup guide. I have experience with installing indoor antennas in my apartment, so I knew the optimal location to place my new antenna. With my new antenna, I pulled in a whopping twenty-two (22) gorgeous channels, all with great reception, including the major broadcast channels. The long cord is a wonderful addition to the antenna and has made a big difference. No more having to use coax extension cables. I'm also very happy that the cord is white because my old white antenna had a black cord. The white cord doesn't even show when you're looking from the outside of the window. This is very important for apartment dwellers. Every channel is clear and crisp and comes in perfectly. I took a picture today, Saturday, the day before the Super Bowl, showing the newscaster discussing the Super Bowl commercials. The photo shows the very clear closed captioning that I require to enjoy TV. When closed captions come in clearly, you know you have excellent reception! U MUST HAVE is the best HDTV antenna I've ever had! This is the seventh indoor antenna that I've tried over the past year and a half. This is my final HDTV antenna purchase! The pre-delivery letter with tech-support tips was extremely helpful, very impressive and instills confidence in the seller. This seller is very professional and helpful. I highly recommend that you try their antennas.

title: Nice high quality 360 degree antenna, read my review for interesting vintage tv applications...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * High quality, sturdy build. * 360 degree omnidirectional, allows you to place the antenna virtually anywhere. * 2 inch magnetic base. * Standard coaxial F-Type male connector. THE BAD: ----------- * Nothing bad at all, but just a FYI. I collect vintage tvs, and I broadcast my own analog signals for fun. When I see an antenna, I grab it for testing purposes. To broadcast a signal, you need a modulator, and an antenna attached to it to act as transmitter. I tested this antenna as a transmitter, and you can see in my photo, my vintage tv gets the signal crystal clear. But as I move away from it, I don't get as much mileage as I do versus when my modulator is attached to regular rabbit ears. I'm sure this is a good antenna if you're going to use it for its intended purpose, which is to receive OTA channels. But as a transmitter for modulators, rabbit ears are still king. No reason to dock any stars. 5-Stars.

With this MicroPack version, due to a taller design, it took less time to get used to. * The scroll wheel is perfectly placed. * There is also one more button, it's the DPI sensitivity switch button. * The track ball/marble size of the MicroPack is the same size as the L brand blue version, but they ARE NOT interchangeable. * Battery compartment also has a magnetic compartment to house the 2.4 receiver. THE BAD: ------------ * No bluetooth, then again, the L brand doesn't have bluetooth either and it cost twice as much. * Now, I've gone through many L brand ones in my life. If you don't believe me, look at the picture I uploaded with the 5 blue marbles. That's 5 L brand versions that have gone bad, but I saved the marbles. So I'm anticipating the same sort of life span for this Micropack version, which is about 1 to 2 yrs. * The L brand also beats the Micropack with it's unifying receiver system, as well as a dedicated software. This Micropack mouse simply uses your windows software for configuration. * The L brand also has 2 more buttons next to the scroll wheel that you can customize. title: Beautiful desktop power supply, but you'll need your own 3M adhesives...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Aesthetically, a very nice and clean design that you can proudly display on your desktop. Standard power strips are too ugly to be placed on a desktop, but this design is very sleek. * You got two 3-prong outlets on each side, and a 2-prong outlet on the top. * The power button is also on the top and illuminates when you power it up. * At the front end, you get one USB port, and two 20w usb-c PD ports, so 40w total. * GaN technology. * 5ft heavy duty power cord with surge protection. THE BAD: ------------ * Similar products made for a desk would include adhesives so you can immobilize it. There was no such accessory in the box. Nevertheless, I'll still rate this charger 5-Stars! DEC 14, 2022 UPDATE: --------------------------- * This will be a non-issue for the majority of you out there. However, I found something that was an issue for me. You cannot automate this strip with a smart plug. I have devices that I want to turn on all at once by Alexa, Siri, etc. So I use a smart plug. When you cut off power at the smart switch, this power strip automatically goes to "OFF" state. So when you turn the smart switch back on, you still need to manually touch the on/off button on this strip. Most power strips will resume it's "ON" state when you turn on the smart plug. But not this one, it automatically goes to "OFF" state. I suppose this has something to do with having a "touch" button. Most strips have no buttons, or an actually switch that you flip from off to on. So when you cut power at the source, it doesn't automatically flip to off by itself. But I guess this is the behavior of a "touch" power strip. Just food for thought.

title: Cheap little HDMI to composite signal adapter that works like a charm...
text: [[VIDEOID:9f151672fa05f9a18577c5f8c9ec33a9]] This adapter converts HDMI signals to old school composite (RCA) analog signals. The brand here is NEWCARE, but as I discuss in the video, it's a white label product, meaning many sellers sell the same thing under a different name. Regardless, they all work great! No complaints. HERE IS MY SET-UP: ------------------------- 1. Fire TV stick HDMI into this converter. 2. Composite out from the converter to the composite in of a RF modulator, or agile modulator for wireless signals. 3. RF coaxial out from modulator to a 75-300 ohm adapter on the back of the TV. Works perfectly. Build quality is kinda cheap, but it's price accordingly. So it's 5-Stars!

title: Terrific battery pack, good build quality, gets the job done...
text: [[VIDEOID:69c0ecbe3e08e9f74f14d7b043495fbc]] THE GOOD: --------------- * 31,200mah capacity. * 120W AC, 45W Type-C PD, and 18W dual USB-A QC. * Nice build quality, round corners. * Charger and USB-C cable included. * Everything housed in a nice fabric case. * Perfect for travel. title: Dollar for dollar, best media stick in the game, this version has the newer remote...
text: We all know the fire stick rocks! I grabbed a few of these over prime day sales. I collect vintage tvs, and wanted to attach a few of these sticks to old tvs for fun. So these LITEs without the 4k is the best bang for the buck, since old tvs can't do 4k anyway. But I noticed something peculiar about the remotes. This listing with over 16,000 reviews gives you a newer remote WITH shortcut buttons for Hulu, Disney, Netflix and Prime. If this matters to you, then you're in the right listing! For some reason, if you prefer the remote without these buttons, then you'll want to order from the listing with over 245,000 reviews. Here is the link to that listing: https://www.amazon.com/fire-tv-stick-lite/dp/B07YNLBS7R/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8&th=1 As for the Fire TV sticks themselves, they remain the same. It does not matter to me. I use Plex for my purposes. 5-Stars!

title: More than enough for a grade school notebook with gaming capabilities...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Aesthetically, a very cool looking laptop. Looks menacing, looks high tech. Makes me think of Alienware. * Ram is not soldered, and is upgradeable. * SSD drives are upgradeable too. * Windows 11 Home out the box. * Comes with 3 months of Ultimate Game Pass from Xbox/Microsoft. Doesn't say this anywhere in the listing, so it was a pleasant surprise for my kid. You find this out during the process of setting up the laptop. * Advertised for gaming, but hardcore gamers will find it a little light. But for a child using it as a school laptop, this is perfect. Much better than the Chromebooks, and for Roblox and Minecraft, which is all my kid does, this is more than enough. * Nevertheless, if you want to boost the ram and ssd, you'll need to know how to remove the bottom cover. Search YT for, "Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3i (15", 2022) - disassembly and upgrade options." Click on the very top search result. The video is by LaptopMedia. They disassemble several similar models, but this is the term you want to search to get to the exact model. However, keep in mind that he's disassembling the intel version which uses DDR4 ram, you'll be using DDR5 for this Ryzen model. THE BAD: ------------ * Screen is only 1080P. * Ram is only 8GB, but again, you can upgrade this. * If truly using for gaming, you'll need more than 256GB. My son will mainly use it for school, so this won't be an issue. * No touchscreen. * Regarding power supply... Not necessarily a bad, but a tip. If you have children, then you know when they take their tablets and notebooks to relatives or friend's house, the power supply goes too. Instead of constantly unplugging the one that is supposed to be stationary at their table, I always buy a second power supply. For this model, it's a 170W with the Lenovo rectangle usb head. You can buy any 3rd party, just make sure it's 170W with the rectangle head. Despite listing some items in the bad list, I understand it's par for the course in terms of the price you're paying. If you want all of those features included, your price would go up. My kid loves it, we'll go 4-Stars overall for now.

title: Amazing value for Lexar branded 128gb micro sd cards...
text: I don't get too technical with SD cards. What's the point when they're all so cheap nowadays. Nothing to lose sleep over about if the speed is less than a milli second than advertised. LOL! It's pretty insane now that you can get two 128gb Lexar brand cards for $26 bucks. You can't complain about anything. LOL! 5-Stars!

title: Bad instructions, but overall stand is very nice and sturdy...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * The board pieces are nicely finished. All the pieces were perfect. No dents or cracks. * I suspect this is some sort of MDF or particle board with a layer of wood veneer on top. * If you use a notebook as a main computer, and outputs to a monitor, then the center shelf is perfect for that purpose. * Approximately 42" W x 6" H x 10.5" D when fully assembled. * Compartment closes via magnet, and is a nice "push to open" design. * Non skid rubber feet are included. They are the adhesive kind. * Nice convenient hex bit is included so you can use your power drill. If you don't have a drill, the standard "L" wrench is included as well. THE BAD: ------------ * The instructions for this guy is pretty bad. If you follow their manual, you might get confused because they got some of the numbers labeled incorrectly. Some of the board pieces are missing number stickers too. They do have a picture of an exploded overall view of where all the pieces are supposed to go. I just look at that picture, as well as the product photos. You don't have to be Einstein, it's pretty easy to figure out even without the instructions. * Because of it's unique design, there are exposed screws on the surface. They are drilled in and flushed with the table, so aesthetically, it's fine. But I wouldn't slide unprotected notebooks or smartphones across the top, you may scratch your devices. Normally with exposed screws, I've seen other furniture provide stickers that are camouflage with the veneer, but no such stickers were included. * The "push to open" latch that sits inside the compartment is pretty big. The space is so small, so this thing taking up a lot of space seems like an inefficient design. We still like this stand a lot. 4-Stars overall.

title: Versatile, invaluable, must have power supply...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * High quality 3v to 12v power supply, 5A and 60W max. * Comes with a plethora of interchangeable DC tips. * Awesome to have around, invaluable. * Though there is no polarity labeling, I've confirmed with the seller that it is positive inside, and negative outside. A reverse polarity cable is included if you ever need to make it negative inside, positive outside. TIPS ABOUT POLARITY: ---------------------------- * If you mess around with vintage stuff, the reverse polarity cable is important. I've noticed many of my vintage stuff from the 70's to 90's have negative inside, positive outside. Whereas most modern gadgets and adapters, including this one, have positive inside, negative outside. This cable allows you to make it so your adapter is now negative inside, positive outside. If you don't match polarity with your device, YOU WILL FRY YOUR DEVICE. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing. 5-Stars!

title: Our HP notebook now has a back-up charger...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Wide ranging output from 15v to 20v. Take a look at your power adapter to see what the voltage is. If it falls in this range, you should be good. We're using this for my son's HP laptop. The original brick is still good, we just don't want to unplug it every time he wants to take the laptop to a friends house. * A plethora of connecting tips. They are universal. So if your notebook uses 19v, then the 19v tip here will be compatible. * On each tip, if you examine closely, the voltage is stamped on it. I took a close up picture to show this. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. Gets the job done! 5-Stars.

title: This capture device came with a HDMI cable, it's a lot of bang for your buck, and works great...
text: [[VIDEOID:6fbb7930c23f2b3918bfee62b7dbdebc]] THE GOOD: --------------- * Price. Wow, less than $20. I just reviewed another usb capture device for $60. I'm not sure it does anything better than this one, except in the looks department. This $20 version even came with a HDMI cable. What? Compared to the other, this is a crazy deal. * Plug and Play for people familiar with these devices. If not, you'll need to learn about capture software. If using this at the PC, then a popular software people use is OBS. * However, there are higher quality capture devices for your desktop. These little usb versions are better fro DSLR camera users who want to create a second monitor screen with their smartphones. * Personally, a fun use case scenario for me, is turning spare phones into mini tvs. USING YOUR SMARTPHONE TIPS: ---------------------------------------- * The type of USB adapter you use will matter. If your phone has a USB-C port, then you'll need a female USB A to USB-C adapter. If it has a micro usb port, you'll need a female USB-A to micro usb adapter. I found that the ones with a little cord are finicky. A solid one piece, cordless usb to usb-c adapter solved the issue for me. Watch my video to understand what I'm saying. * Many USB Camera Viewer apps won't work. It's not an exact science because you're dealing with so many variables such as app version, phone brand, android version, not to mention your hardware. Some apps gave me video, but no audio, some slam you with so many ads, it's annoying unless you pay. The best paid app is USB CAMERA PRO by Shen Yao, their free version is good too, but has ads. The best free app that virtually has no ads is USB CAMERA VIEWER by Homesoft, LLC. This is the app you see in my video demo. I'm using a Pixel 6 Pro. * If connecting a media device such as fire stick, roku, etc., you will need to bypass HDCP, and you'll have to trial and error with the different types of splitters on the market. The GOXMGO splitter in my video demo worked nicely. THE BAD: ------------ * Well, as mentioned above. I had reviewed another usb capture device that cost $60. The only advantage it has is that there is no dangling cord, and it's a colorful red. In terms of function, I don't see an advantage. At $20, you get the usb capture device and a HDMI cable. This is an amazing deal compared to the other. This product is 5-Stars!

title: Versatile rackmount, install it vertically or horizontally under your table...

title: Good bang for your buck, and my PS5 can display 4k through this switcher...
text: [[VIDEOID:a7a9d66e53e5179d8dcca6d8e9fe8d3b]] THE GOOD: --------------- * Price. They have a 4x4 matrix that can cost close to $200. For a 4 in, 2 out, $46 seems like a bargain. * Build quality is great as well. You're getting a nice brushed metal casing. * This HDMI Matrix is the only device so far that solved my PS5 4k issue. My display is a 4K projector, but I use a Caavo universal remote/HDMI switcher. The Caavo is capable of 4k and has 4 hdmi inputs, but for some reason when my PS5 goes into this Caavo, then out to the projector, the PS5 4k doesn't work. But if I out my Caavo into this Matrix switcher, then out to the projector, the PS5 4k works. I'm essentially daisy chaining my Caavo switcher with this Matrix Switcher. Everything works, and I have a total of 8 inputs now. Before, I had to connect my PS5 directly to the projector to get 4k. I don't know how, but this switcher has solved my PS5 issue. * Easy to operate. Very intuitive. You don't even need to read their manual. Each output can display a different source. I collect vintage tvs, and I have a nice little 1976 Toshiba 9" sitting right below my 120" projector screen. People always ask if it works, and this Matrix Switcher allows me to demonstrate it. In my video, that's two different Twilight Zone episodes playing at the same time. LOL! Of course my vintage tv doesn't have a HDMI input, so there are other adapters involved. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. What a bargain! 5-Stars!

title: You can never have too many cable fasteners...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * You get 120 pieces in this package. * They are 6" by .5". * Velcro works extremely well. * Comes in 5 colors, so you can color coordinate your cables. * Must have if you are into tech and electronics. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. I have drawers and buckets filled with cables going back 20+ years. I've always been into electronics, and I never throw away any cables or power cables. It's my OCD. LOL! Anytime I think of throwing a cable out, I would think, "What if I need this cable down the line?" LOL! 120 velcro strips isn't even enough to be honest. LOL! 5-Stars!

title: Make a second LCD screen for your DSLR camera, or turn old phones into mini TVs...
text: [[VIDEOID:7c51c8affe21df7ad48095fb4eeeab3b]] THE GOOD: --------------- * Plug and Play if you know what you're doing. LOL! If not, you have some software learning curves. If you're using this to capture on your computer, then a popular software people use is OBS. * But there are better quality capture devices for your desktop. Most people use these little usb versions on their smartphone to create a second monitor for their DSLR cameras. Watch my video, I demo two use-case scenarios. * Colorful! Not your usual boring usb capture stick. I love red! USING YOUR SMARTPHONE TIPS: ---------------------------------------- * The type of USB adapter you use will matter. If your phone has a USB-C port, then you'll need a female USB A to USB-C adapter. If it has a micro usb port, you'll need a female USB-A to micro usb adapter. I found that the ones with a little cord are finicky. A solid one piece, cordless usb to usb-c adapter solved the issue for me. Watch my video to understand what I'm saying. * Many USB Camera Viewer apps won't work. It's not an exact science because you're dealing with so many variables such as app version, phone brand, android version, not to mention your hardware. Some apps gave me video, but no audio, some slam you with so many ads, it's annoying unless you pay. The best paid app is USB CAMERA PRO by Shen Yao, their free version is good too, but has ads. The best free app that virtually has no ads is USB CAMERA VIEWER by Homesoft, LLC. This is the app you see in my video demo. I'm using a Pixel 6 Pro. * If connecting a media device such as fire stick, roku, etc., you will need to bypass HDCP, and you'll have to trial and error with the different types of splitters on the market. The bi-directional ones DO NOT work, at least they didn't work for me. I have a splitter by VIEWHD I bought years ago that worked for me. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. At first, I thought mine was defective, but as mentioned above, I realized the adapter was the culprit. This product is 5-Stars!

title: Very nice thin profile cooling pad, but it's loud, especially for a bedroom...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Only an inch thick when folded, which is what I needed because I wanted to fit a laptop on top of this pad, then both of it will slide into a low clearance shelf. * However, if you're using it traditionally, then you have 9 levels of height adjustments. * Six levels of fan speeds. * 7 RGB light modes. Lights up around the edges, looks very cool. * 2 usb ports in the back. THE BAD: ------------ * Feels a little cheap, everything is plastic. * It advertises 25dB, which they say is "very quiet" and will provide a "noise free" environment. Uh, this thing is loud, especially at the highest speed, and especially for a bedroom. My older Cooler Master pad is much more quiet. I would say that with this Ice Coorel version, at its lowest level, which is supposed to be the quietest, the sound is equivalent to my Cooler Master at its highest. My Cooler Master at its lowest is like a ninja, you cannot hear at all. So in terms of noise, there are better ones on the market. I'll go 4-Stars overall.

title: Easiest no lag method to project your smartphone to the big screen...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Feels high quality. The braided jacket is much easier to manage and move around than the thick vinyl ones. * 6.6 ft from USB-C port of your phone to any HDMI port of your display. * Great way to enjoy your phone on the big screen with no lag. * In your Window's settings, you can also extend instead of mirroring your screen. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing so far. 5-Stars.

title: I gave Ryzen 7 a chance, but this is my new daily driver...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * This is a very nice midrange desktop replacement. Loaded with i5 10210U processor, 16GB ram, and 512GB SSD for storage. * Loaded up my old photoshop CS6 program, as well as Cyberlink Power Director. PC handled it with no issues. * Terrific as a Plex Server as well. Friends have tested from outside the home. Not a hitch. There are other variables here, I do have 500/500 service from Frontier. * It's great that they gave us one 16GB stick, leaving the second slot open. So if you want to add a second stick, the term you'll want to search for when shopping is, "DDR4 SODIM." * Aesthetically, the mini pc looks very nice as you can see by the pictures. It is a super space saver that packs a punch. * Out the box, it is Windows 11 Pro, no installation required. * This does everything I need it to do such as running photoshop, power director, plex server, etc. But at this price point, it can also be a very nice starter PC if you have a child in grade school. * No lock-up or freezing, which I've been experiencing with my other mini pc that runs on Ryzen 7 AMD. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing so far. This is 5-Stars, but I'm a reasonable person. If you compare apples to apples, you will be very happy. If you compare this to a $2000 gamer rig, then of course, you won't be happy. Kids who play less intensive games like Roblox, Minecraft, etc. This is no problem!

title: Nice mini tripod worthy of your consideration...
text: [[VIDEOID:59ed67f3002b3afb6581350d115258a1]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Tripod is mostly plastic, but it's sturdy abs plastic. The ball joint is aluminum alloy. * 3 adjustable heights (more on this below). * Upper housing that holds the ball joint is removable, so you can put it on a different tripod if you wish. The bottom of the ball joint housing has a 1/4 thread. So whatever tripod you use has to have a plate with a 1/4 stem. Which is pretty common anyways. * It is sturdy and stable when in use. THE BAD: ------------ * Though there are 3 different height levels to the tripod, there are no markings, and there are no detents, or any sort of tactile click. TIPS ON MAKING A HOLDER FOR THE WEMAX 300 GO: ----------------------------------------------------------------- * I mistakenly got this tripod for the Wemax 300 Go projector. It does not work for this projector, but watch my video to see how I made it work. Maybe you can apply the same ideas for your situation. Overall, I'll go 4-Stars.

title: Must have accessory for vintage tv collectors...
text: [[VIDEOID:dde0289960c7064afa16b2d94a0b5ae4]] I collect vintage TVs, so whenever I see a HDMI to RCA converter, I grab it. This has a male end HDMI connector, so for something like a Fire Stick, Chromecast, etc., which also have male-end connectors, this won't work. For this version, it works with mainly set-top boxes that have female HDMI ports such as an Apple TV, Fire TV box, etc. In my video demo, I'm using a Fire TV box, and my connection is as such: 1. HDMI out from Fire TV box to Ablewe adapter. 2. RCA out from Ablewe adapter to RF modulator. 3. RF coaxial out from modulator to 75-300 ohm adapter on the back of the TV. Works perfectly. 5-Stars!

title: Heavy duty, and aesthetically, a very pleasing minimalistic look...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * High quality, heavy duty, gooseneck for your smartphone or tablets. Mixture of aluminum and plastic. * Will take 4.5" to 13.5" devices. * The gooseneck itself is about 24 to 25". I'm not counting the clamp, or the holder. * Nice box packaging makes the product giftable. * Clamp is strong and sturdy. * Has a minimalist design/look to it. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing. 5-Stars.

title: Very high quality plastic cable management raceway...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Nice sturdy, heavy duty, plastic cable management raceway. * Will fit standard 19" rackmount cabinets. * Cover is removable, so you can easily organize your cables, then snap the cover back on. * M6 cage nuts and screws included, as well as screw caps/washers so you don't mar your rails. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. 5-Stars.

title: Heavy duty, this should be a five star product...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Heavy duty metal shelf. * Fits standard 19" width rack mount cabinets. * Approximately 17-3/4" deep. * Complete with rackmount cage M6 nuts and screws. THE BAD: ------------ * Mine came badly dented. It's kind of fascinating to me the amount of companies selling rackmount stuff, but having lackadaisical quality control. I'm not just talking about this brand or seller. Almost every rackmount product from different brands and sellers will come to you dented in some shape or form. * So instead of bothering with a return, I decided to get a hammer. I whacked everything in place, and it works. But as a customer, I rather not have to do this. I will go 3-Stars. This would be 5 if not for the troubles.

title: Good to have spare micro SD cards around the house, also a good bang for your buck...
text: Amazing how cheap micro SD cards can be today. This comes out to about $7 per 64GB card. Nice to have some spare cards around for non important jobs. I would stick with reputable brand-names for surveillance, or jobs where data is important. Sometimes I need a card to build something for a raspberry pi, extra storage for my kid's tablet, music for portable speakers that has a micro sd slot, etc. All 3 seem to be working fine. 5-Stars.

title: You need to provide your own OPEN END power cord...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * All 8 ports are gigabit. * Mainly plastic, but seems sturdy and well made. * 130w total. Each port has a 30w max. But again, it's 130w total, so you cannot have all 8 ports at 30w each. * IP65 weatherproof with accessories to mount on wall or poll. * A template is provided for wall screw locations. * Built-in surge protection, which is why receptacle does not have ground terminal. THE BAD: ------------ * No power supply. After contacting seller for advice on power, they've since included a video. However, the video doesn't really help. It's just a video of them plugging in the wires. I just wanted advice on a power supply to buy, or what type of power cord? Gauge thickness? I'm guessing I'm thinking too much, and the thickness doesn't matter, otherwise it would have been mentioned in the manual, or the video they uploaded. So the term you want to search for on Amazon is, "open end power cord." At 12awg, there seems to only be 3 prong cables available. You can still use this, and just ignore the ground wire. I do see a 2 prong version at 14 awg. That's the one I'll get to complete my project. This would be 5-Stars if we didn't have to hunt down our own power, or strip our own power cord. So I'll go 4-Stars.

title: The most fickle cable I've ever experienced...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Braid type shields are much more flexible than the traditional vinyl, or thick rubber cables. * 48gbps, 8K ready, HDCP 2.2, etc. * 15 ft, and gold contacts. * Customer service top notch. I "thought" the cable a I got was defective, and they sent me another one no questions asked. More on this below. THE BAD: ------------ * This is the most difficult cable I've ever experience. It is very fickle. I have reproduced this fickleness with many gadgets, not just one. So, I am fairly certain this isn't user error. Now the first cable I got wouldn't give me any signal between my HDMI switch and my PS5. I wanted to make sure the Switcher isn't the problem, so I tested it with my Nvidia Shied directly to my 4k projector. Still no signal. Took it upstairs to test between Fire TV cube and another Switcher upstairs, still no signal. So it is reasonable for me to think the HDMI cable is defective. I asked for a replacement, and the seller sent me one quickly. With this new cable, I tested it with the Fire TV cube and switcher upstairs, and I got a signal. Great! So I took this new cable, and went downstairs back to the original location I wanted to use it... Guess what, no signal! LOL! This confused me, perhaps I mixed up the old cable, so I tried that cable as well, and guess what... I got a signal! But now I'm dubious of these cables because I'm fairly certain I did not mix up the cables. In any case, I took this cable that I just recently received signal, took upstairs to confirm, and guess what... no signal! LOL! See, what I'm trying to do to eliminate all doubts is for the cable to get a signal both upstairs and downstairs. Ultimately, I realized the original cable that I asked for a replacement for, I guess, was never defective. It is just fickle, like the new replacement. Good customer service is why I won't rate this any lower than 3-Stars. I'm pretty tech savvy, and I've never had this much trouble with a cable. This might be a case of YMMV (your mileage may vary.)

title: Very high quality tripod if you're willing to invest in the PD ecosystem of accessories...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Peak Design is a very nice brand. I'm familiar with this brand back when I was buying a lot of accessories for my DSLR camera. I knew they make high quality stuff, and this tripod is no exception. This is a nice slab of aluminum with good heft to it. Not cheap plastic stuff. * Works with their "mobile universal adapter," or any case with a metal shim in the back, such as magsafe cases. * Very functional, especially useful for taking shots using the timer. No more needing to ask a stranger to take the picture. * If you don't want it to cling to the back of your phone, then it comes with a very nice drawstring pouch. THE BAD: ------------ * If you have a magnetic mount in your car, and you're hoping this thing will cling to it along with your phone, I'm sorry to report it won't work. The magnet is on the side that will cling to the back of your phone. The back is neither magnetic, nor steel. Your magnetic mount may hold it loosely due to the vicinity of the magnets in the tripod, but it is a very weak hold. Overall, I'll go 4-Stars.

title: Wasn't able to video edit and browse at the same time before, now I can...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Two sticks of 8GB ram. * DD4 Dram 3200MHz, PC4-25600, CL16, 1.35V * 288 pin. * XMP 2.0 overclocking support. * Low profile with aluminum heatsink. * My desktop can be sluggish at times, and I've definitely felt the improvement, especially when multi-tasking. Video editing, while browsing the internet has improved drastically for me. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing so far. It's getting the job done. 5-Stars!

title: Aesthetically, the best looking key finder set out there...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Aesthetically, I gravitated towards all the colors of this set. It's one of the better looking key finder sets out there. * You get to keep track of 6 items with this set. * Button batteries are included for all receivers. They are CR2032 model. * 3M adhesives are also supplied for your receivers if you want to stick them to gadgets like your phone, remote control, etc. * Sound volume is 75 to 85db. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing really. The transmitter takes two AAA batteries which you need to provide yourself. Other than that, there is really nothing bad. It works really well. 5-Stars!

title: Neat little projector, but it's not a good value proposition...
text: [[VIDEOID:121051b82f50880623cdf0499f74c575]] THE GOOD: -------------- * 1080P native and extremely small, so it's very portable. The size is the whole reason I got this. It's for traveling and being able to project bigger screens in hotel walls. * 300 ansi lumens, ALPD laser tech. * 25000 hrs lamp life. * Airplay, Miracast thru wi-fi. * Aesthetically, very nice minimalist design. * Picture quality is good, but I'm not a videophile. I do have a more serious Vava UST 4k projector in my living room, so all these portable projectors will never compare. They serve as a traveling device for me, and will not be the go-to video source at home. * Very nice case is included to hold everything. THE BAD: ------------ * Onboard 1W speakers are very weak to say the least. You will definitely want to hook up a portable speaker. It has a headphone jack, which is basically the same as an aux out jack. I hooked it up to a cheap little speaker and the sound improved drastically. Watch my video. * No remote. * No smart OS, so I have a chromecast connected in my video demo, and I just cast from my phone. * No Bluetooth, so you must use aux if connecting a speaker. * No mounting solution or tripod included. Depending on your situation, you might not even need it. Just set it on a coffee table and you're good. * No built in battery. * Lastly, the price. There are so many features lacking, so I do not understand the price point. If you're willing to spend $600, then check out the Nebula Capsule Max that's less than $500. It is also compact, the size of a coke can. It has a built in battery, 8w speakers, smart interface, bluetooth, and remote. The only thing it doesn't have is native 1080p, it is native 720p. But it's hard to even tell the difference with these little projectors anyway. So I am not sure that paying more money, and having less features is worth that 1080p. And if you have to also lug around an external speaker, a chromecast or fire TV, then it really defeats the purpose of being completely portable. With the Nebula, everything you need is inside a device the size of a coke can. In conclusion, this is a neat little barebones projector, but the onboard speakers are so bad, you'll need to carry around a portable speaker as well, so it's no longer as portable as I anticipated. At its price point, I assume they're saying it's a premium to have a projector at this size that is 1080p.. But again, that size feature is almost negated by the need to bring along external speakers, and smart devices like a Fire TV stick. And if the Nebula Capsule products doesn't exist, then I guess this price point is justified, but the Nebula does exist, and it's a much better buy. I'm going 3-Stars.

title: Very nice flash drive, no cap to manage, good bang for your buck...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * So much capacity in such a tiny form. 512 GB. * Lights up when at work. * Built in key loop. * Lever to protrude or retract usb is a great design. This way you don't need to worry about a cap. * USB 3.1, backwards compatible to 3.0 and 2.0 as well. * 400MB/s read, 300MB/s write. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. 5-Stars!

title: A lot of bells and whistles at this price range, but build quality could be better...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * I won't go through the specs because you already know from the product listing. * Beautiful picture quality, but I'm not a videophile. This is for my bedroom, and I'm coming from a TCL 65R613, which is a great budget tv. * TV has a layer of film covering the entire screen, allowing you to get your finger prints on it while you set-up. Then when you're finished, peel it off. * Comes with accessories for placing the Samsung on a table. The base is extremely heavy duty and weighted. * You can wall mount using your own brackets, which is what I did. * The remote is very unique. It has a solar back. I've never seen this before. So it will charge by light, or by usb-c. The fact that you don't need alkaline batteries is a first for me. * Smart Home interface has a lot going on. There will be a little learning curve, but this could potentially replace my Fire TV Cube. * Voice recognition allows you to choose between Bixby, Alexa, or Google Assistant. That's very nice of them to not force Bixby on you. * No dark corners, which were present in my TCL. If there are, they are imperceptible. Dark corners are a hallmark of budget tvs. I'm definitely stepping up in picture quality. THE BAD: ------------ * This is just something superficial, but I'm not in love with Samsung's build. This may be subjective, but I really love TCL's design. I have a picture comparing the side profile between the two tvs. The Samsung has a 3/4" side profile, but it's misleading, it's not really 3/4" thin, it has a hump back, which is all plastic btw, so the entire width is really 2". Whereas my TCL has a side profile of 1-1/8" all around. It's amazing that they can make a TV that thin all around, and the brush metal on the TCL looks better too. What I'm saying is that, aesthetically, this isn't the best TV out there when my budget TCL can beat it in looks. Then again, like I said, this is subjective. * Picture Presets are: Dynamic, Standard, Movie, and Film Maker Mode. They are all underwhelming besides for Dynamic which is the brightest and has the most pop. I can tweak them all except for Standard. Something is wrong with the Standard preset right now. It is less bright than Dynamic, but once you choose it and exit the menu, it becomes even dimmer, much more dimmer than what was previewed to you. If you go back to the setting to see if you can up the brightness, you'll see that it's already at 50, which is the brightest. There is something wrong with this Standard preset, hopefully a firmware can fix this. I just use Dynamic. * Smart Home navigation lag. Not sure if this can be fixed with firmware, I hope it can. The remote is pretty sweet, but lag can make or break whether or not you stick with an O.S. Right now, I still prefer to go to my Fire TV Cube. Hopefully, with firmware updates, they can improve the OS navigation and convert me. * The storage in this TV I'm guessing is 8GB. Because after downloading a few apps, as well as the apps they force you to have, it says I've used about 3.5GB, and I have less than 2GB of space left. Why do TV makers continue to go cheap on this? They plaster you with all these apps in their home, all these ads, they want you to download games, this and that... yet they give you a measly 8GB, half of which is already used up for the OS and their forced bloatware, which you cannot delete. And I'm wondering if this has anything to do with the lag. It's truly comical sometimes, the decision making process of a multi-billion corp. HOW TO GET RID OF THE SOAP OPERA EFFECT: -------------------------------------------------------- * Wow, I spent a long time trying to figure this out. YT tutorials say turn off "Picture Clarity Settings" would turn this off, but it had no effect. I had this issue with the TCL too, when you make these adjustments, sometimes the TV just doesn't respond. The trick for the TCL was to unplug the tv, then replug and the motion clarity would be eliminated. I tried that trick with this Samsung, and it still didn't work. Ultimately, I found out turning off PICTURE CLARITY doesn't work, so you need to set it to CUSTOM, then turn off everything one by one, especially the BLUR and JUDDER reduction. 1. From your Home, go to MENU on the left side bar. 2. Then go to Settings, then ALL SETTINGS. 3. Go to PICTURE. 4. Choose your picture mode, I like DYNAMIC. 5. Then go to EXPERT SETTINGS. 6. Scroll down to PICTURE CLARITY SETTINGS. 7. Change it from Auto to CUSTOM. 8. Then reduce the Blur Reduction to 0. 9. Then reduce the Judder Reduction to 0. 10. You can also set the "Noise Reduction" to OFF, instead of AUTO. I can't tell the difference with noise reduction off. It's not like all of a sudden, your tv looks grainy. The difference is imperceptible, so I leave it off. Because a little noise makes the movies look more like theatre quality. * Another tip I have is to NOT use "intelligent mode." If you enable this, it over-rides your custom settings above, and it will turn on the soap opera effect as it pleases. Overall, I'll give this tv 4-Stars! Knocking a star for the navigation lag issue. I'm just using my Fire TV Cube for the moment. Hope this review has been helpful.

title: Not a lot of bang for you buck, but it is a very nice cable...
text: THE GOOD: --------------- * Very nice HDMI cable with a premium price tag. * The braid type shields are much more flexible than the traditional vinyl or thick rubber ones. * 18gbps, high fidelity arc. * Gold contacts. THE BAD: ------------ * Pretty strange that they spend so much making their packaging beautiful, but force you to rip apart the outer sleeve to get to the black box. I would have liked to keep the entire packaging intact. * I'm not sure why a cable has to be $60, but I was hoping because it's $60, it might solve my situation. I have a 4k Caavo Universal Remote/HDMI Switcher. It has 4 inputs, and 1 output to my 4k projector. I have the Nvidia Shield Pro, Fire TV, and PS5 going into my Caavo. I get 4k content from my Nvidia Shield and Fire TV, but for some reason, the PS5 doesn't like my Caavo, I can only get 1080P. I figure it must be the cable, a $60 cable should fix it. LOL! Unfortunately, it did not, and this $60 cable feels no different than the others I already have in my collection. Perhaps the PS5 is just not compatible with the Caavo because when I connect it directly to the 4k projector, I get my 4k signal back. So I think it's just not compatible, and no matter how much you spend on HDMI cables, it won't make a difference. It's not this cable's fault though. But it just feels like an overpriced cable to be honest. Lets go 4-Stars.

title: Not just for Dell, if your computer use usb-c for power, you can use this...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * 65W usb-c, compatible with 45w usb-c chargers. * Despite being advertised for Dell and showing you a list of specific model numbers, the fact is no matter what brand you have, if it uses usb-c for power and if it's also 65w, then you can use it. We're using this for our Lenovo. * Great quality, so far so good. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing so far. 5-Stars!

title: Adidas brand earbuds, high quality, great sound quality too...

title: Perfect 2 prong power cords for some of my vintage electronics...

title: Very versatile camera mount with infinite angle capabilities...

title: For those who still have cassette players, this is a must have...
text: [[VIDEOID:965384c821866d92d79f7efd5009542]] THE GOOD: --------------- * Non-abrasive. * Improves playback sound, provide more clarity. * Dirty heads can eat tapes. Cleaning your tape heads will reduce those chances. * This tape cleaner works exactly like the tape cleaners from the 70's, 80's, 90's,. Nothing has changed. LOL! * Both sides can clean. I haven't looked, but can you even get tape cleaners at Best Buys or something anymore? Anyway, this works, and it's 5-Stars!

title: A very nice mouse, but a very infuriating experience...
text: [[VIDEOID:b16291f439f0a8f55991c25ab956bec0]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Aesthetically, a very unique build. * USB dongle housed in the bottom with a unique compartment door that simply connects by magnets. Watch my video. The usb dongle also stays in its slot via magnetism. * 7 customizable buttons. * No need for a mouse pad. Works on any surface. * Can drag and drop work across devices. Read below... THE BAD: ------------ * For instructions, they might as well give us a sheet that says, "Search Youtube to learn. Good luck!" * I could not connect to my Pixel Pro 6, it kept saying, "Cannot connect to HP Creator due to incorrect pin or passkey." There is no such pin for us to enter. You've all connected bluetooth devices to your phone, right? It just works. This is a rare case, where it didn't work, and it gives you this message. So there is some firmware issue that HP and Google need to iron out. * The feature I'm most intrigued about is the "WORK ACROSS DEVICES" feature. You can supposedly drag and drop content across different operating systems. When you advertise something, and you give no directions, then it better be something that simply works, but it's not. I connected the mouse to a PC as well as a mobile device, and I cannot drag and drop. I've connected it to two PCs and I cannot drop. To use either device, you need to switch devices on the mouse. Once you switch, you can no longer control the other machine. There is obviously something I'm not understanding, perhaps a setting I need to turn on, perhaps a software I need to download. It would be helpful if HP gave you some directions. This is so annoying and so infuriating to be honest. * Then a lightbulb went off.. Youtube!!! So after searching Youtube, I did eventually learned how to do this. Search YT using this phrase, "HP 930 Creator Mouse - Everything you Need to Know." At the 6:56 mark is where he discusses this across device feature. * I think it's pretty funny HP, Apple, Dell, etc. All the big boys now don't feel they need to teach their consumer base about their products. They just know that all us Guinea Pigs will be smart enough to eventually make our way to Youtube. LOL! I'm usually not this harsh on products, but the reason I'm so upset is because I wasted so much time tinkering and searching their useless HP website. This is a Vine product, so it didn't occur to me that this product has already been selling and there are already youtube reviews. I didn't think it be on YT yet. I'm knocking off 3 stars for the lack of direction. Hey, I'd have more respect for HP, if they just include a card that says, "To learn how to use our product, search Youtube." LOL! 2-Stars.

title: High quality NVR, but requires some trial and errors if you're not fluent in networking...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Terrific build quality. I've seen cheap ones that come to you with dented cases, and the internal circuitry looks like a half baked job with messy wires and bad soldering jobs. This is a real professional NVR. * 4TB Hard Drive is included, but you can install a 10TB drive if you wish. That's the max capacity. * Records 4k video, and 8MP images. * Instant feed, no delay like wireless cams. * App works well provided you have everything set-up properly. * If you're not sure of what you're doing, like I was, it's easy to restore the HD back to factory default again. I had to trial and error many times, and the good thing was that he factory reset was very quick each time. It's basically like restarting the device. THE BAD: ------------ * No cameras provided, but you knew that when you bought it. * Manual font is for little ants to read. But it's readable. It's just my pet peeve when manufactures make it uncomfortably small. * Just like any other network product, the manual doesn't spend anytime with what to do if your service provider goes by 192.168.254.XXX versus providers that use 192.168.1.XXX. A lot of network products go by 192.168.1, and so I get a lot of headaches being a Frontier customer. Granted I'm not fluent in networking. A networking expert reading this might say, "easy, all you have to do is this, this and this..." Well, you see, that's what I was hoping the manual would do. LOL! Having said that... I actually got everything to work properly. I don't know how, but I did it. As mentioned above, I'm with Frontier and they use 192.168.254.xxx, so depending on how I hook up the NVR to my network, the DHCP will generate a proper working address, or it may not. Here are some noteworthy things I discovered. This pertains to my personal network/situation, but if you find yourself in the same boat, maybe this info could be useful: 1.) Connecting the NVR directly to my frontier router causes the NVR to use it's default IP address 192.168.1.XXX. This is fine if I'm viewing the cams on my ethernet connected PC. But the app over wi-fi will not work. It will say my NVR is offline. 2.) For some reason, using a POE SWITCH between my NVR and my Router makes all the features work properly. I can view on my PC, and I can view on my APP via wi-fi. So if any of these issues sounds familiar to you, then this is what worked for me... Connect the UPLINK port of the POE SWITCH to a port on the home router. Then, connect an ethernet cable from the Network port of the NVR to any of the POE ports on the POE Switch. Once I hooked it this way, the NVR's DHCP created an IP address that is in line with my Frontier network 192.168.254.xxx. Now I can view the cams on my ethernet PC, as well as my wi-fi app. 3.) Ideally, you want to connect all POE cameras directly to the NVR which has 8 ports, but if for whatever reason, you need to connect a camera to the POE SWITCH, then understand that it'll require 2 ports of the POE Switch, one for the camera and one going back to any 1 of the 8 ports on the NVR. And remember in step #2, one of the POE port is already connected to the network port of the NVR. So 3 ports total have been taken up in this scenario. Love the quality of the hardware, as well as the streams. I also attached a screenshot of the App's live view page. You'll see I tested 2 cameras. You simply tap a camera to get the full screen view of it. I'll rate this NVR 4-Stars overall.

title: This dash cam checks all the boxes for such a great price...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * 3 Channel dashcam: 4k Front, 2.5k Rear, 1080P Cabin. * Aesthetically, very good looking dash cam, and build quality is great. * Front camera uses a Sony sensor. * G-Sensor, Night Vision, Loop recording. * 64 GB microSD card included. * Last feature that's noteworthy is the battery. title: These boosters are YMMV... your mileage may vary...
text: I like messing around with old TV's, so I like to keep some of these boosters around. They did improve signal a bit to an old 1977 Zenith. There are no more digital signals from our government, so I use agile modulators to broadcast analog signals in my home. These are not strong signals, so instead of using the built in antenna of my vintage tvs, I would hook up an external antenna as well as a booster, such as this product. To be honest, with some sets, I see no difference, and with others I get an improvement such as my 1977 Zenith. There are so many variables in getting a good reception, so it's really hard to review these things. The biggest obstacle is all the interference in our homes. We all have different amounts of gadgets in our homes, using wifi and sharing the same power lines. What might not work for me, may work for you, and vice versa. So the best thing is to just try it out. If it doesn't work, return it. I'll go 4-Stars.

title: If you're a beginner like us, this set is more than enough to get you started...
text: THE FACTS: -------------- * Complete set to get you stargazing right away. * Is this a refractor, reflector, or catadioptric telescope? This is a refractor telescope! * 700mm focal length. This length is equivalent to the length of your actual refractor telescope. * Aperture: 90mm aperture. * Maximum magnification of this telescope is 180x. You derive at this number by multiplying the aperture (90mm) by 2. * Eyepieces included: 25mm, 9mm. To calculate magnification of your telescope. Take 700mm divide it by the eyepiece you're using. So if you're using the 25mm eyepiece, your magnification is 28x. So you shouldn't buy eyepieces less than 4mm focal length since 700/4= 175x. So a 4mm eyepiece gets you to the max essentially. * 3x barlow lens included. Used to increase the magnification of your telescope 3x. How do you use this? Eyepiece goes inside the barlow lens, then everything goes inside the telescope. Using a 25mm eyepiece in the example above, we get 28x magnification. So if you combine the 25mm eyepiece with the barlow, you get 84x magnification. * 1 Finder scope and 1 finder scope bracket included: Some googling, I found this.... "A finderscope uses low power with a wide field of view and assists you in locating objects to observe through the main telescope. Crosshairs aid in centering the object you seek." * Smartphone adapter included. * 1 tripod tray included. There are lots of YT tutorials. I'm just sharing with you info I've learned. From a newbie's perspective this set is very impressive, and more than enough to get going. Once you get more experienced, then I believe you can compare and contrast telescope qualities as you try out others. For now, I have no experience to compare this to anything else. Just getting my feet wet. This is 5-Stars for a beginner!

title: A very nifty piece of tech, which will surely be a conversation piece...

title: If you're having issues with the music, read my review...
text: [[VIDEOID:5907d2aee5d78cfb7242549be379253f]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Pretty unique. I've never seen a Hologram fan at work up close. * Image is very vibrant, and music is loud. * It turns on with music at default, but there is a mute button you can press. More on this below in the important advice section. * You get a metal spring socket to help you turn it into a tree topper. * USB-C charging port. THE BAD: ------------ * I've seen ones where you use an app to change music and images, I guess those are more expensive. You cannot change anything with this version. * There are only 4 animations, and the only song is We Wish You A Merry Christmas. * There is no volume control. It's pretty loud. So you're either going to have the music on or off. No compromise. No quiet sound while you're sipping hot chocolate. LOL! IMPORTANT OPERATION ADVICE: ---------------------------------------- * It may come to you undercharged, so charge it first before playing with it. * It takes 5 to 8 seconds after you turn it on, for the music to kick in. This is not mentioned in the manual, so I didn't know this. I was pressing the music button immediately after turning it on, which then actually takes it to mute. So for awhile, I thought mine was defective. I kept fiddling with it, I just didn't understand it. I eventually gave up, and thought mine was defective. But I turned it on again, just to see the animations. Then after awhile, all of a sudden, I hear music. So I finally understood there is a 5-8 second delay for the music to kick in. Watch my video. Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars. I'm knocking 1 star for it's music and video limitations.

title: Terrific outlets, but keep in mind, there are no screws in the middle...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * You get two outlet units in this package. * The outlets are nicely placed so all my little bricks fit. title: Just like a HDMI to RCA converter box, but minus the box...
text: MAY 15, 2022 UPDATE: ---------------------------- * My original review simply discusses use case scenarios. I didn't have a need for this cable yet at the time. Now I actually do, and I realize it DOES NOT work. Like many have mentioned, it needs a converter chip inside, which it does not have. I am not sure what the use case scenario is for this cable. Downgrading to 1-Star. ORIGINAL REVIEW NOV 21, 2001: --------------------------------------- Why would you need something like this? Use case scenarios will vary. Here's an Amazon link of that if you're interested: https://www.amazon.com/review/R3O6M7ZZ2A894I/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B096Y9FQRM As for this cable, it's 5-Stars!

title: Very good looking thermal pad that you can cut to size to cool multiple CPUs...

title: A smaller kit for 1 to 2 bedroom homes, by a reputable brand we all know, ADT...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Very easy to set-up, app is intuitive to use and follow. * This is for a smaller home with just the hub, 2 entry sensors, 1 motion sensor, 1 yard sign, and 3 window decals. * Hub is not obtrusive size-wise. It has a control panel at the top. I have it next to an Amazon Echo for size reference. * Sensors work really well. Anytime you open the door where you've installed a sensor, there is a chime that goes off on the hub. You can disable this chime if you wish. * For those who are not sure yet how much security they need, but do know that they at least one something as a deterrent, then this no subscription required DIY system is perfect. * You can turn on system once outside your house via the app. You can also turn it off via the app before entering your home, or turn it off at the hub during the "entry delay." THE BAD: ------------ * The sensor and the magnet has to be half an inch or less apart. Installation will be tricky for those who have a door frame with a raised decorative trim. You'll need to put the sensor at a strange angle, or come up with a better solution yourself. Raised, or irregular door trims is something ADT should have thought about, and should have included for us adapters, spacers, etc. * If you choose not to subscribe, then the system is nothing more than a deterrent. * The instructions assumes we all know the industry lingo. For example, "Entry or exit delays." I had to search online for more info. It's basically the time the system allows for you to properly turn off the alarm before it goes off. That's my understand from YT videos. * Whenever you arm the system, it takes forever, like 60 to 90 seconds, and during this time, there is a CHIME that's counting down with the seconds. There doesn't seem to be a way to mute this. This means if you arm the system late at night while people are sleeping, the chimes may wake them up. I will update review if I can find more info on this. There has to be a way you can mute this. * Although the yard sign is great, the window decals are small compared to others I've seen. Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars for now.

title: 4 in 1 cables really change your habits, makes life a little easier...
