title: Complete DIY alarm kit from a known brand name...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Very easy to set-up, app is intuitive to use and follow. * This is a very complete kit with a hub, 6 entry sensors, 2 motion sensors, and a keypad. You don't need to use everything, or install everything in one day. I started off just my garage door and the front door. Same thing with the extra keypad. There is already a control panel on top of the hub. The idea of they keypad is for quicker access to the control panel. So ideally, the keypad will be next to your bed on a nightstand or something. * Hub is not obtrusive at all. I have it next to a soda can for size reference. * Sensors work really well. I was concerned about the garage door sensor because usually I get bad wi-fi in the garage. I put the hub near my living room. The garage sensor worked flawlessly. Anytime you open the door where you've installed a sensor, there is a chime that goes off on the hub. You can disable this chime if you wish. * No need to subscribe to a service, which is perfect for us. We live in a fairly safe neighborhood, knock on wood. But there are times when everyone is gone, and no cars are parked in the driveway. So these are the times, I'll arm the system. THE BAD: ------------ * The sensor and the magnet has to be half an inch or less apart. Installation will be tricky for some of you. My front entry door has a raised decorative trim that makes this impossible. I made it work by having the sensor at a weird angle, and half the 3M backing isn't even attached to the trim. I will need to think of a solution for this. Or better yet, ADT should have thought about this ahead of time and given us adapters, spacers, etc. * If you choose not to subscribe, like in our case, you should understand the system is nothing more than a deterrent. You hope the loud sound will be enough to deter would be criminals. If it's not, then no authorities are coming unless you called them yourselves. * The instructions assumes we all know the industry lingo For example, "Entry or exit delays." It would have been nice if the manual explained what this means. I had to search online for more info. It's basically the time the system allows for you to properly turn off the alarm before it goes off. That's my understand from YT videos of other brands. I couldn't find an exact "Blue by ADT" video on this matter. * Whenever you arm the system, it takes forever, like 60 to 90 seconds, and during this time, there is a CHIME that's counting down with the seconds. Once the system is armed, then it shuts up. There doesn't seem to be a way to mute this. You see, I'm a night owl, so I don't need to arm the system until very late like 1 or 2 am. People are asleep at this time, the chimes will wake them up. I have contacted customer service, we'll see what they say. * The 2 yard signs and stakes are great, but the 4 stickers they give for your windows are tiny. My Brinks windows stickers were bigger. Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars. And base on the customer service response, this might go up to 5-Stars, or get bumped down to 3-Stars. There has got to be a way to mute the chimes when arming the system. If there isn't a way, then I will bump the rating down because that would be ridiculous. So, 4-Stars for now.

title: High quality 2 pack RG316 cables with BNC connectors...
text: Very good BNC RG316 cables. Keep in mind these are not double shielded, you'd need to search for RG316DS on Amazon. Love the quality and flexibility of these cables. They are 50 ohm and are 6 inches each. 5-Stars!

title: Very good 5 inch display with all the bells and whistles...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * They provide you with both external and internal accessories to connect a raspberry pi. * Once up and running, 800x400 pixels is very adequate for a 5 inch screen. * 10-point capacitive touch. * Built in dual speakers. * Monitor has onboard control as well with display menu. * I tested it with a PI running RasPlex. It ran with no issues. THE BAD: ------------ * The bezel for this 5 inch is bigger than others on the market, and that's due to having the internal speakers. This is not necessarily a bad. * No fan. You might want to buy a fan for the cpu. * Manual only shows you the easy set-up, which will have you running cables all over the place, and it looks messy. * They do include accessories that will eliminate the external HDMI cable, eliminate touch usb cable, as well as eliminate the need for the monitor to power itself. But they don't explain or teach you how to do it. I didn't make a video for this review, but you can watch my review for the 7 inch version for an idea. * However, for some reason, the internal touch cable did not work for me in this package. The external micro usb version worked fine. But every time I hooked up the internal cable, it killed the display, it just won't turn on. But once I unhook it, and I use the external cable, the display is back. * Lastly, not a pro or con, just a FYI.. the packaging and instructions are from USPARKLE. I'll go 4-Stars overall.

title: Another terrific Android TV box by Mecool running the latest Android 11 and bluetooth 5.0...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Google certified Android TV. This means no need to side load, no need to use an air mouse, etc. All the usual suspects will work properly: Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+, Youtube, Youtube TV, Plex, etc. * Terrific remote with shortcuts for Youtube, Netlfix, Amazon Prime and Google Play, as well as Google Assistant. * Amlogic S905Y4 Quad-Core ARM Cortex A35... I won't pretend to know what that exactly means, but whatever it is, it allows smooth navigation and a very responsive user interface. Watch my screen recording video demo. * Running Android 11 and Bluetooth 5.0. * Add more storage via SD card, or external USB drive. * Built in ethernet port. One of the things people do with the Google TV dongle, the Fire Stick, or the Tivo 4K stream, is rush out and buy an ethernet adapter. Well, you don't have to do that here. It's already built in. THE BAD: ------------ * The ram is only 2GB. I haven't had any stuttering, glitching, or lagging experiences yet. So maybe it's unnecessary, but it would have been nice for this thing to be a little more future proof. Final thoughts... I really like these Mecool smart devices. They are giving you a lot of bang for your buck. Not too long ago, unknown brands could only provide unofficial Android boxes. Those products require air mouses, keyboards, sideloading, etc. As Google certification become more widely available, that's only going to bring more competition, which means lower prices and more choices for everyone. This is a lot of features for less than $80. This is 5-Stars!

title: A very nice complete kit with 16.9 oz. of solution...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Bottle is an ample 16.9 oz. * High quality microfiber cloth included. * 2 types of spray nozzles included. * Some robot stickers... good to give to the kids I guess. LOL! THE BAD: ----------- * Nothing at all. A pretty impressive kit that I started using immediately. Been seeing some smudges on my screen. I've seen these smudges for over 500 reviews now. LOL! Yes, I can be lazy. But now that this bottle is on my desk, those smudges are gone. 5-Stars.

title: A functional 64 gb usb flash drive, as well as a cool conversation piece...
text: [[VIDEOID:9b34c2bb90472e36fced99d8faed8f5f]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Awesome retro inspired usb drive. There were no usb flash drives in the 1950's or 60's, but if there were, I'd imagine they look like this in a sci-fi show like Lost in Space or something. * 64 GB makes this flash drive not just for decor but actually useable. * Awesome colorful lights activated when plugged into your pc. * USB 3.0 speed. THE BAD: ----------- * Not really a con, more like a feature request. I think they missed out on not adding some sort of computer "beep, boop, beep, beep, boop" sound when it's powered. You know the sound of a retro computer thinking or processing. LOL! That would have been awesome! 5-Stars.

title: Awesome heavy duty power strip with cord management clips...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Heavy duty construction. * Power cord manager clips on both ends. * Power cord is an ample 9ft. * 12 total outlets with individual on/off switches. * 1020 Joules. * Yellow cord clips is a nice color touch, since I have many Dewalt tools. THE BAD: ----------- * Nothing at all. 5-Stars!

title: Cool little 5 inch display for your raspberry pi, not too difficult to figure out...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Everything you need to get started, except for the PI of course. It even includes a fan for your PI. * PI connects to board via 60v ribbon. * Tool-less thumbscrew installation. * At 5 inches, anything you view on it is going to look good. * Tested with RasPlex and it works very well. THE BAD: ------------ * Though it is tool-less, the thumbscrews are tiny, and there are areas where your fingers are too big. If you look at my pictures, I had to use a tweezer in some locations to turn the screw. * Though it's not hard, and there are a plethora of resources online, instructions doesn't teach beginners where to plug in the ribbon or the fan. Between my pictures, and the GPIO diagram, you should be able to figure it out. I like this little thing... 5-Stars!

title: Invaluable tech accessory that will allow you to place your gadgets exactly where you want them...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * High quality build. The cases are metal, and each unit weighs approximately 5 ounces. * Only one unit needs to be powered, it doesn't matter which. * I tested my FIRE TV cube with direct connection to a display. Worked perfectly. * A HDMI switcher should work, but I haven't tested that out yet. I'd like to move multiple sources away from the display, so hopefully an HDMI switcher will work. I'll update later. THE BAD: ------------ * In my main entertainment room, it's a little more complicated. I tried testing my Nintendo Switch. I have a Caavo universal remote/HDMI switcher. It has 4 HDMI sources connected to it, one of which is the Nintendo Switch. So my Nintendo now goes into this extender, and this extender goes into the Caavo. This Caavo unit then OUTS to a HDMI Multi-Viewer Switcher. This Multi-Viewer then outs to a display, which is a 4K projector... This was one too many intermediaries, and I kept getting static and a vanishing image. When I removed the Multi-Viewer, and went from the Caavo to the projector, everything worked. Maybe there are settings in the Multi-Viewer that I need to explore to make it all work. Anyway, I plan to put all my set-up back to normal including my Multi-Viewer. I will skip feeding the extender into the Caavo, I will go directly to the projector because it does have spare HDMI ports. So despite it not being able to completely work the way I want it to work, fact of the matter is, it does work as advertised. If your set-up is a bit complicated, such as mine, then it's YMMV. This is still 5-Stars! This is a must have accessory that will open up a whole new world of furniture arrangement for you.

title: The only one so far that delivers a decent picture to my vintage GE television...
text: [[VIDEOID:7aefece1e131fe9296e341bb71fdfbf2]] I like to mess around with vintage VHF television sets. I got a 1980 something G.E. set that's been giving me a lot of issues. It does a poor job of picking up the wireless analog signal I'm broadcasting from an agile modulator. For this TV set, this Vuelve antenna has given me the best results. You'll see in my video, when I move the antenna to the right, picture gets worse, to the left, picture gets better. That's all you can ask for, an antenna that actually responds. This means there is exist a sweet spot, so I will find it and mount it at that location. I believe the signal booster included in this package is the reason it has performed better than others that I have tried on this TV. 32.8 ft cord means ample cord for you to set the antenna anywhere you like. 5-Stars!

title: Beautiful retro design Bluetooth 5.0 speakers with a real wood cabinet...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Beautiful retro decor speaker. Well built with real wood, not lamination. * Sound quality is super, though I'm not an audiophile. * Dual 4 inch subwoofers, 50 watts. * Bluetooth 5.0, lossless audio. * Might be the best speaker you can find in this price range. * Can link multiple Studiofinix speakers. THE BAD: ----------- * No remote control. * No controls on the front, top, or sides. Everything is in the back, if you need to make adjustments, it is a hassle if this isn't hooked up in an open environment. * The glossy lacquer makes it a fingerprint magnet. Despite the few cons, I can't get myself to subtract any stars because this speaker is too cool. Me, being a retro guy, it is exactly my cup of tea. 5-Stars!

title: Watch my video to learn how to eliminate all the unnecessary cables...
text: [[VIDEOID:7ab1952320e567f5f1fd3159ac818111]] THE GOOD: -------------- * All necessary cables and essential accessories are in the box to get you going. * Even accessories that will allow you to use less cables. More on that below. * Once up and running, screen looks great! 1024x600 IPS. * 5-point capacitive touch. * Built in dual speakers. * Monitor has onboard control as well with display menu. * I tested it with a PI running regular PI OS, as well as a PI running RasPlex. The screen was great for both scenarios. THE BAD: ------------ * No fan. You might want to buy a fan for the cpu. * Manual only shows you the easy set-up, which will have you running cables all over the place, and it looks messy. * They do include accessories that will eliminate the external HDMI cable, eliminate touch usb cable, as well as eliminate the need for the monitor to power itself. But they don't explain or teach you how to do it. So watch my video, it should be helpful for those wanting to install a Pi on the back, but also wanting a clean look. No soldering required. This is 5-Stars, but subtracting 1-Star for a manual that's a little lacking.

title: A very complete and versatile smartphone or camera holder...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Good quality kit with lots of articulation points. * C-clamp included has a max opining of 3.4 inches. * Phone/Tablet holder has metal extending bars. The really cheap ones are all plastic. * The main stand, aka monopod, is telescopic and goes from 13 to 22 inches. * Use the magic arm by itself, or attach it to the monopod. * Terrific high quality little mini ball-head included. * Universal 1/4 inch hardware, which makes it easy to combine with other camera accessories. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing really. It's a combination of plastic and metal, and priced just right. I highly recommend you add these clamps to make your kit even more versatile, here's an Amazon link: https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R1Z5WE52M3ZYXE/ref=cm_cr_getr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B089VY9PLX 5-Stars!

title: This is a complete bundle with 5 hdmi and 5 usb link cables, but it is not a high end switch...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * 4 HDMI port in, 4 USB link ports, 1 HDMI port out. * You can share up to 4 usb accessories * 1 usb calculator included. * 4 hdmi cables included. * 4 usb link cables included. THE BAD: ------------ * Case seems to be metal, but it's a little light. Doesn't feel has sturdy and robust as the Avstar. * You're getting a lot in this bundle, but there is a reason for that... this is a very basic kvm switch. * No usb 3.0 or 3.1. The usb ports on this switch are 1.1 and 2.0. If you don't need 3.0, then you should be happy with this switch. * No mic port. * No audio ports. * Included calculator is a gimmick to create value, but it's pointless and lightweight plastic, very cheap. Depending on what your needs are, you might want to check out the Avstar kvm switch that I recently reviewed. That one is $10 less, but it is more future proof, and more of a premium product. That one has 3 usb ports to share but they are 3.0 and 3.1. The Avstar also has an optical audio port, a stereo audio port and a mic port. The Avstar also has a remote control to switch inputs. So it is a better kvm switch overall, but it does not include any hdmi or usb link cables. Here is an Amazon link to that switch: https://www.amazon.com/review/RR34E657C5MOF/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B09D6Y2CFL USE CASE SCENARIO: -------------------------- * Why would you need a KVM switch? You can share a single set of keyboard, mouse, speakers for multiple pcs. You can use your same PC monitor to view the Fire Stick, play PS5, Xbox, etc. There is no need to hook up different speakers, as long as you hook up your main speaker to the optical or stereo ports. I was ready to give this switch 5 stars because of all the cables provided, but now that I've used both switches, I understand why the Avstar didn't include any cables. The Avstar is a higher end product, so they're keeping the cost down by not providing any cables. I use the Avstar with my higher end pc, and I'm using this Basicolor switch for master bedroom pc that has lower needs. I'll rate this switch 4-Stars as well.

title: Pretty good digital antenna, but I'm using it for analog purposes...
text: I collect and try different antennas, to figure out which ones work best with old VHF tvs. Right now I'm testing this as transmitter antenna for my Blonder Tongue agile modulator. In my pictures, you can see it wedged between books and boxes. LOL! That's not the most ideal position, but it's the best I can do right now. The cable for this antenna is ample long. I don't really know how it does as a digital OTA antenna because where I live, I get really bad OTA reception, so I didn't even bother testing that aspect. I'm using this for broadcasting analog signals inside my home. No complaints so far. It functions just like any other antenna. 5-Stars!

title: Mid Century style retro radio with a 5 yr warranty...
text: [[VIDEOID:3f4b028ed4887ded77fba90586e9150]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Beautiful retro design. Don't quote me on this, but I believe this is called Mid-Century style. * These retro radios are first and foremost, display props. Don't expect the world in terms of sound quality for something that's less than $100. The sound is decent and par for the course. * ClearClick is a name I've come across before when I reviewed their capture card products. They are base in the US, and have been in business since 2010. The reason I'm mentioning this is because this product has a 5 year warranty. Normally, I would say warranties from fly by night overseas companies are worth as much as the paper they're written on. But the warranty here, provided by a company based in the US, should have real value. THE BAD: ------------ * No built in battery. This is corded. * About that warranty I discussed above. Keep all your records, you may need it down the road. I got two vintage radios from ClearClick and they both had QC issues. I had to do a replacement for one radio because the distortion was unbearable. Now for this version, I can hear some humming, but since these are novelty items, and I won't be seriously listening to them, I didn't bother to do a replacement for this one. Plus, with some volume, the humming is drowned out. Nevertheless, to have issues on both radios was a bit concerning. Maybe the experience is just unique to me, unlucky perhaps. I'll still rate this radio 4-Stars due to the warranty. If the humming should get worse over time, I'll put their 5 year warranty to the test.

title: Turn multiple coaxial cables into one...
text: Useful to have a few of these around. Sometimes you don't have long coaxial cables lying around and you need to create a long run from multiple cables, these will get the job done. 5-Stars!

title: Good looking amplifier, but how well it works is very YMMV...
text: I'm always messing around with old vhf tvs. I have an agile modulator and I broadcast my own analog signals in the house. OTA is now all digital, so you can't get any channels with old tvs. Just for kicks, I created a twilight zone 24/7 channel and I use an agile modulator to broadcast it in my home. You'll notice in many of my review videos, the old school tv in the background running twilight zone shows. My agile modulator is in the garage, so vintage television sets upstairs do not get a good reception. Yes, I have more vintage tvs. LOL! So I'm always looking for things to boost reception. This amplifier actually helped just a little, not much. I know there are many variables that factor into these things, including so much interference in our homes nowadays. So I won't be too hard on it. I'll rate it 4-Stars.

title: Was able to extract audio from a 1977 vintage tv...
text: [[VIDEOID:592b47703198d12fb0a0be93c48f521c]] My use case scenario is a bit unique. I've been using a pricier one by LDEX, and I've been happy with it. But when I tried to extract audio from an old 1977 tv, it couldn't do it. I thought perhaps what I wanted to achieve was unreasonable since the tv was so old. So I didn't have high hopes for this Ainostone version, I basically gave this version a try to confirm that these types of bluetooth adapters won't work with old tvs. To my surprise, the Ainostone proved me wrong. It was able to do what the pricier LDEX couldn't do. The LCD screen on the Ainostone is smaller and the overall build quality is not as nice as the LDEX, but who cares now... this is the best bluetooth adapter out there. Watch my video if you're interested in achieving the same thing. The first speaker had some lag, but when I hooked it up with a higher end speaker, there was absolutely no lag. This Ainostone bluetooth adapter is 5-Stars all the way! Amazon link to LDEX bluetooth adapter: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2Q63ZXOQS7ZSJ/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08DR1FJD2 Amazon link to the the Muzen speaker seen in the video: https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R2Y4DGZE3IQZ3C/ref=cm_cr_getr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B094D5Q8ZP

title: External power switch, but keep in mind, you install it on your motherboard...
text: Very nifty idea, but keep in mind "EXTERNAL" does not mean external installation. I made some assumptions without fully reading the product listing. For some reason, my brain associated the word EXTERNAL with USB, but this will need to be installed on your motherboard. If you are not comfortable opening up a PC, then don't buy it. I actually got it for my notebook. LOL! So I'll save this switch for a rainy day when my desktop needs it. It looks like it's well built, and good quality. 5-Stars.

title: Awesome telescopic radio antenna bundle with 10 ft. cord...
text: I like fiddling with vintage televisions, so I always need some antennas on standby. This antenna feels very robust. The base has a good heft to it, and it's magnetic. I have it clinging to the side of my fridge. It's telescopic and extends about 47 inches. The coaxial cable connected to it is generous at 10 ft. long. The bundle came with 5 useful adapters including a 75 to 300 ohm adapter. No complaints here. 5-Stars!

title: These RCA adapters allow you to hook up both red and white to one composite jack...
text: My use case scenario is to hook up composite audio to a Blonder Tongue Agile Modulator. The modulator only has a single composite jack. I could simply hook up either the red or white cable, but I figure lets tidy things up by connecting both red and white to this adapter cable. I don't think it makes a difference in audio, nor would it change mono audio to stereo. Like I said, just to tidy things up. If I hook up just one red, and leave the white dangling, it makes me uncomfortable. LOL! Anyway, these adapters got the job done. 5-Stars!

title: Hands down, this is the best value out there for a media player...
text: [[VIDEOID:febac65bc03346f5a045d4e36b5eaaec]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Officially licensed Google Android TV. This means no need to side load, no need to use an air mouse, etc. All the usual suspects will work properly: Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+, Youtube, Youtube TV, Plex, etc. * Terrific remote with shortcuts for Youtube, Netlfix, Amazon Prime and Google Play, as well as Google Assistant. * Amlogic S905X2-B Quad core cortex-A53... that's a mouth full. I don't pretend to know what it exactly entails, but I can say this cpu allows navigation to be responsive and buttery smooth. Watch my video demo. * Add more storage via SD card, or external USB drive. * Built in ethernet port. One of the things people do with the Google TV dongle, the Fire Stick, or the Tivo 4K stream, is rush out and buy an ethernet adapter. Well, you don't have to do that here. It's already built in. THE BAD: ------------ * I don't mind the 8GB of storage due to the onboard TF/SD slot as well as the USB ports. Adding storage will be easy. But the ram is only 2GB. I haven't had any stuttering, glitching, or lagging experiences yet. So maybe it's unnecessary, but it would have been nice for this thing to be future proof a little with some extra ram. Final thoughts... Think about how the Amazon Fire TV Cube also only has 2gb of ram, the Fire Sticks only have 1gb of ram, and the cylinder Nvidia Shield also only 2gb of ram/ 8gb of storage and costs $150. You need to move up to the Shield Pro that will get you 3gb of ram, but will cost you $200. For less than $70, I think Mecool has hit a home run. If you're thinking of spending less than $50 for the dongles like the Fire Stick or Google TV dongle, I suggest you spend a few more dollars, and get this Mecool that has built in ethernet, awesome remote, SD slot, USB ports, etc. It's a no brainer. Forget about it! This is 5-Stars!

title: High quality KVM switch, but no cables are provided...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Nice build quality. Good metal case. * 4 HDMI port in, 4 USB link ports, 1 HDMI port out. * 3 usb ports to share * 2 audio ports to share (1 optical, 1 regular stereo) * 1 Mic port to share. * Remote control included. THE BAD: ------------ * I've seen other packages that provide you with all necessary cables. This package has no cables. For the price, I feel cables should have been included. I'm going to review another set that's only $10 more yet they provide you with 5 hdmi cables, 4 usb link cables, and a usb physical calculator. It's going to cost more than $10 for you to buy 5 hdmi cables and 4 usb cables. I'll provide a link to this other set once I'm done reviewing it. USE CASE SCENARIO: -------------------------- * Why would you need a KVM switch? You can share a single set of keyboard, mouse, speakers for multiple pcs. You can use your same PC monitor to view the Fire Stick, play PS5, Xbox, etc. There is no need to hook up different speakers, as long as you hook up your main speaker to the optical or stereo ports. I will subtract 1-Star for including no cables. A remote is included, but when you use a KVM at the table, your hand just reaches out to press the switch, so a remote is unnecessary. 4-Stars.

title: Gets the job done connect 1/4 stereo port to RCA composite cables...
text: The equipment I needed to connect didn't have RCA ports, but had a 1/4 inch stereo port. This adapter got the job done! I was able to connect my composite speakers with these adapters. No complaints. 5-Stars!

title: This is hit or miss depending on your equipment...
text: I think something like this is YMMV, hit or miss. For me, it was a miss in one scenario, but a hit in another. I could not get audio to a bluetooth speaker that didn't have aux in, but it had a usb port. So I gave this a shot, but it didn't work. When I tried it with a different speaker, it worked. So unfortunately, it's not working with the targeted speaker. But since it works with a different speaker, I don't think there is anything wrong with it. I'll say 5-Stars.

title: Premium drawing tablet with very convenient shortcut keys and roller wheel...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * High quality premium build. * Direct usb-c connection, or Bluetooth connection. * There is no delay with Bluetooth connection. My drawings are instantaneous. If there are any delays, it is imperceptible to my eyes. * 8 shortcut keys, and roller wheel. Once you use this tablet, you'll never use another writing tablet without these shortcuts. They are so convenient. * Roller wheel can be assigned as a zoom in/out function, a scroller, change brush size, or rotate images. I have mine set to change brush size. This is so much more convenient than going to the upper left menu in photoshop to change brush size. Plus, at default from the factory, the 8th shortcut key is programmed for you to access and change the roller functions quickly. So even though I have my roller set to change brush size, if I hit the 8th key, I get a pop-up menu of my choices again. * Top of the roller wheel is a touch pad, so you can assign it as a mouse. * Pen is housed in a cylinder with storage on both ends. On one end is the actual pen, and on the other end is storage for the Bluetooth usb dongle, and 10 replacement pen nibs/tips. * As is, the idea is you write with your right hand, and your left hand controls the wheel and shortcut keys. What if you're left handed? In the XP-Pen software, you can flip the layout 180, this will allow you to flip the tablet so the roller and shortcut keys are on the right. You must set this in the program. If you don't, and you flip the tablet, everything will just move in reverse. THE BAD: ----------- * We will all have a different experience because we all use different apps and programs. I use Photoshop CS6 and the roller was quirky. None of the roller functions worked. So I switched programs and used Windows Paint, and everything worked fine. When I went back to CS6, the roller started working. As if it learned something from the Paint program. LOL! I uploaded a bunch of screenshots of the software so you can see what setting and features are available. I will rate this 4-Stars for now. I'm pretty sure it's the tablet that's quirky with CS6, and not user error. But I'll be using this a lot in the next few weeks, and I'll bump this to 5-Stars should I learn that it was user error. But so far, I don't think I'm doing anything wrong, the roller is just really quirky in CS6.

title: Only for Raspberry Pi 4 and devices with USB-C...
text: I thought this would work for my raspberry pi 3's, but I didn't realize the power input for the raspberry pi 4 had changed to usb-c. This adapter is made with usb-c, so it cannot plug into older raspberry pis with mico usb. That's my bad, I didn't read the listing carefully. In any case, I will eventually get a Pi 4. For what it's worth, the adapter looks like it's good quality. But it won't be in the drawers waiting for a Pi 4. I'll put it to use since you can use it with pretty much any device that takes usb-c. 5-Stars!

title: HDMI to RCA, and it gets the job done...
text: [[VIDEOID:9790246fcc2bdbcd0e24455aad5325f9]] My use case scenario was changing the HDMI output of a Fire TV pendant to RCA analog so I can feed it to a RF modulator, which then coaxials out to a 75 to 300 ohm adapter, which then connects to the VHF terminals of a vintage tv. Perfecto! 5-Stars!

title: Invaluable nifty accessory that will turn AA battery devices into AC powered devices...
text: In case you're wondering what these are for, here's my use case scenario. During Christmas season, I have a few snow globes that I'd like to display 24/7, however they only take alkaline AA batteries. There are no AC adapters, so they would eat up a lot of batteries. Well, with this nifty accessory, I can now turn my battery only snow globe into AC power. It comes with one main battery connected to the AC adapter, and three AA dummies. title: Great for dash cams, good bang for your buck...

title: This has been a pleasure to use, love it...

title: No frills microSDHC card that gets the job done...

title: Very capable smart device from an up and coming tech company...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Officially licensed Google TV OS. Which means you'll be able to watch all the usual suspects without any hassle of side-loading, or watching from a web browser, etc. When I say usual suspects, I mean Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney, etc. * EKO is the real deal. It's the same OS as what the Nvidia shield uses, the same as Google's very own Android TV dongle uses, the same as Tivo's 4k Stream stick, etc. * EKO is an Australian audio/visual company, and a quick look at their site shows that they're very professional, and won't be a fly by night. They seem to aspire to be like Vizio, TCL, etc. * 2GB ram, 8GB of storage is on par with all the low end streaming sticks on the market. * Remote is terrific with short cut buttons to Youtube, Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Google Play Store, and Google Assistance button at the top. THE BAD: ----------- * The charging port is micro-usb. It's all about usb-c now! * In terms of pricing, they do not separate themselves from the more established brand names. So there's not a lot of incentive to try out a new company. I'll rate this 4-Stars overall.

title: Good solution to mounting your Orbi to the wall...
text: I want to move one of my Orbi satellites to improve reception. This looks like it'll get the job done. With exposed garage ceilings, installation will be a breeze. The quality and thickness of this holder will hold the Orbi with no issues. 5-Stars!

title: High quality poe NVR system with 4tb pre-installed, plug and play if connecting directly to NVR...
text: [[VIDEOID:1190b451faf9653857f6725f71e2a33c]] THE GOOD: -------------- * This is the real deal! Every component is high quality, and the NVR unit is externally and internally immaculate. Why do I have to even say this? Because I've tried other NVR systems. I have encountered NVRs with flimsy dented cases, and messy soldering jobs on the motherboard. * 4TB is pre-installed. * You get 8 POE cameras! A mistake I made as a newbie was thinking all I have to do is get POE switches, then I would be able to get rid of power adapters for any camera. That is incorrect! A camera has to be designated as a POE camera in order to use POE switches and POE NVRs. * You get eight 65 ft ethernet cable. If you can run those cables back to the NVR, which has 8 ports in the back, then you won't need to hook up any intermediary POE switches. I plan to use at most four cameras, so If I need to hook up a POE switch, the four extra cables will come in handy. However, more on this issue later. * Included are also outdoor plugs to protect your wire connections. * PLUG & PLAY... As long as you run the ethernet cable back to the Ethernet ports of the NVR, it is plug and play. If for any reason, you need to find the IP in your service provider's router admin, look for HEROSPEED DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY. That's the name it shows up under. * Unlike most security cameras, the live feed of this NVR system has no delay, it's real time, or pretty close to it. * If you're using a KVM switch at your computer, so you can switch back and forth between different sources... I said in my video that once I get a USB cable to link up the KVM switch with the NVR, then I should be able to use my PC's mouse and keyboard, which are connected to the KVM switch. Well, since then I've learned that what I said is half true. I'll be able to use the mouse, but not the keyboard. The NVR doesn't respond to any keyboards no matter if it's through the KVM switch, or directly connected to the NVR. It only uses the onscreen pop-up. You will need to use the mouse to select the letters and numbers from the virtual keyboard. THE BAD: ----------- * Like I said above, it's plug and play as long as you connect each camera directly back to the NVR ports. It goes without saying, but the NVR also needs to be connected to your router or nearby switch to be online. I'm running into issues testing POE switches. If the camera is not directly connected to the back of the NVR, the system cannot find it. There are 16 channels available in the NVR, and only 8 ports in the back, so obviously, this should be compatible with POE switches. But so far, I can't get it to work. I've asked for help from OSI, so we'll see... * No guidance or instructions on how to install the actual cameras. For a moment, I was SMH. I was looking for the bases. I thought my package was missing them. But I realized the bases were already threaded onto the cameras. For each camera, you need to unthread the base, drill the base onto the ceiling of your choice location, then thread the main camera body back on it. * Another nitpick is that installing under a ceiling will not always be ideal, or possible. It would have been great if they had included some adapters so that we can install them onto walls like bullet cameras. Despite the little nitpicks, I still rate this 4-Stars right now. Might bump it up to 5-Stars if we can get the POE switches sorted out. I'm a newbie, so I know this might be easy for experienced networkers. The manual is a bit lacking. There were no discussions on how to install the cameras, and it assumes you'll be directly connecting all cameras back to the NVR, so it doesn't discuss the use of POE switches at all.

title: Got the job done in delivering picture to my vintage television...
text: [[VIDEOID:88b2a22f3cf2b2d541a2f015e493cf06]] This 75 to 300 ohm adapter got the job done! They seem fragile, but they work, and you get 5 of them so you got plenty of back-ups. For my purpose, I simply wanted to feed a smart device to my old tv. Watch my video if you want to see what equipment is needed to accomplish this. You will need an RF modulator, and if it's an older unit like mine, it won't have any direct HDMI ports, so you'll need a HDMI to RCA adapter as well. In my video, you'll see some shadow that scrolls through the screen, but it's actually not there in person. I don't know what the technical jargon for this is, but it has something to do with the camera shutter. It captures the rolling shadow in the video, but it's not there in real life. So trust me, this ohm adapter works great! 5-Stars!

title: Awesome little Director's clapper board for your movie room, or man cave...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Nice quality. * Perfect for movie room decor, or man cave. * You get two white dry erase markers. * Dry eraser, as well as a microfiber cloth eraser. * I tested it out, and it was works perfectly. title: A well balanced laptop with enough power for most people...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Terrific build quality. A very sturdy magnesium chassis. * Intel i7-1165G7. This is the 11th gen Tiger Lake processor. * 8 GB of ram, 512 GB of storage. * Storage is NVMe SSD so it's very snappy. * Iris Xe Graphics. title: Good mp3 player with limitations, please read my review regarding playing folders...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * It does a lot: MP3 player, video player, FM radio, voice recorder. * Touch screen. * Super compact, the size of a minimalist wallet. * Easy to use. * Micro SD slot. It has a max capacity of 512 GB card. THE BAD: ----------- * Very light, seems like a cheap build. * Internal storage is 8gb. * No folder play, but I have a workaround below. ADVICE REGARDING PLAYLIST: ------------------------------------ * The user interface for the music app has 4 main categories: Artists, Albums, Songs, Playlists. If you're like me, then you like organizing your music into folders, and would like the player to simply play what's in a folder. Because the folder is essentially your true Playlist. Unfortunately, the app cannot play from folders. There is a FILE MANAGER app that will allow you to drill into your folders. But you can only click one song at a time. You cannot tell it to play all the songs in a folder. You have to create a Playlist by scrolling through your thousands of songs and add each songs one by one to a playlist. It is tedious. My solution is a program call MP3TAG. For example, I have an OLDIES folder, an 80's music folder, a Hip-Hop folder, Soft Rock folder, etc. I organize all my music into these folders. I then run one folder at a time in the MP3tag editor. So for my Oldies folder, I tell the editor that all the songs in this folder is from an ALBUM called OLDIES. Now when I move all my oldies mp3 to the MP3 player, and I go to the ALBUMS category, there will be an album called Oldies. I just hit shuffle an enjoy. I'll rate this player 4-Stars.

title: Good camera, easy to set-up, but read my review for potential issues...
text: NOTEWORTHY FACTS: -------------------------- * Solid build. The camera is about 1 lb. * POE, so you only need an ethernet connection. No power adapter necessary. If you do not have a POE ethernet switch, you can use a power adapter (sold separately). * If you do not have a dedicated NVR, you can simply use H.View's software. You download the smart client app onto your PC. You can get this software from their website. * You can access via smartphone too via the AVIEW app, which is in the Google Play Store. * Instructions are very good. They included several mini booklets for how to access via PC, via Smartphone, as well as a quick start. * Though the instructions are very good. It did not touch upon the issue I had with the IP address. As a matter of fact, no tech product I've ever used have ever discussed this potential issue. As you may know, IP addresses will look something like this... 192.168.1.XXX. That's the pattern that he H.VIEW camera goes by. But my service provider goes by 192.168.254.XXX. So when you plug in the camera to your POE switch, it's never going to connect. The troubleshoot in the manual suggest changing a setting to DHCP. This doesn't solve the problem, the manual is still assuming your IP address follows the 192.168.1.XXX protocol. So if you have this issue, you simply need to login your router admin and find the IP address of the H.View camera. It will be under the name AUDEARA PTY. If the name isn't listed, you can always find the camera by the mac address. This will be on your box, as well as under the camera. Look for the same mac address in the admin, and use the IP address that's associated with that mac address. Go into the Smart Client software and modify the IP address and your camera will show up. FINAL VERDICT: ------------------- * This is a solid camera. But I must say the smartphone app is sort of unprofessional because all the different names is puzzling. The camera is H.View, the app for the PC is Smart Client, the app for the smartphone is AVIEW, and the company listed under the app is some dude name Jack Bobo. Does that sound trustworthy? If I want to download Alexa, the company listed will be Amazon. If I want to download Youtube, the company listed will be Google. If you want to be taken seriously, you need some more consistent branding that will inspire trust. It's a solid camera, but the company is a bit green. I'll rate this camera 4-Stars!

title: Perfect 10 inch screen for building retro arcade or TV cabinets using Raspberry Pi's...
text: [[VIDEOID:2c900a75fd5453701d2f39b71f21f534]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Checks in at 1 lb. 4 ounces, so it has decent weight to it. * Back of the LCD has a built in case for you to install a Raspberry PI3 or PI4 internally with touch screen function. All necessary parts are included. If you choose to solder, then you need to provide your own soldering tools. However, soldering is not required. title: Magnificent Bang & Olufsen Portable Speaker with a unique design...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Beautifully crafted high end speaker. * Built like a tank, it weighs about 7 and a half pounds. * Three ways to position the speaker: Flat, on it's end, or mount it on a wall (bracket sold separately). * From what I can tell, it produces beautiful sounds. However, I'm not an audiophile. * 105 watts, 79dB bass, and 96dB mid-range. * Awesome charging design. The round object you see in the pictures is the charger. The usb-c goes into this object, it then docks magnetically to a round slot in the back of the speaker. Contrary to other reviews that said you're in trouble if you lose this charging device, the back of the speaker has another usb-c port for charging. So if you lose the round object, you're not in trouble. I think it's there for tactile purpose. Without it, you have to constantly turn the speaker around to look for the charging port. With this magnetic charger, mounting and dismounting is a breeze. BTW, Ethernet and Line In is hidden under the rubber cover of this round charging slot. * Works with Airplay, Chromecast built in. If you have a google smart home, you'll like this. My wife is an Apple person, I'm Android. She's been taking over the speaker with Airplay. * 16 hours of play time after fully charged. THE BAD: ------------ * Not necessarily a bad, but more like a reality nowadays. You have to hunt for the user manual at their website. No user manual is included. * Bluetooth connection was easy with some of my devices, and was very difficult with others. My MP3 player took forever to find the Level. Not sure if the issue is with the Level or with the player. * Tested it with my Fire TV Cube. Does not work well. I have to connect/disconnect several times to get audio to the Level. But when I change apps, I lose audio again. To be fair, this wasn't made for TV. But cheap $50 Bluetooth speakers can work flawlessly with media players, why not a $1300 speaker? * On the speaker, there are 4 touch buttons that are for favorites that you can customize. Such as spotify, pandora, etc. You can also long press to save a Google Voice command for each button like Play some music, what is the weather, etc.. Initially, I thought this meant Google Assistant was built in, but it is not unfortunately. It's only good for four phrases. Upon further research, I realize that they do offer this same speaker on their website with Google Assistant built in. They have an option that you can choose with or without Google Assistant, and it's for the same price. I guess this option is available because some people don't like smart devices listening in their homes. This Amazon listing is WITHOUT GOOGLE ASSISTANT. Even with some of these "BAD" things I've listed and discussed, I still rate this speaker 5 stars because it's the most magnificent speaker I've ever owned.

title: A terrific photo box, but you'll need to clear your living room to put this thing together...
text: SEPTEMBER 23, 2021 UPDATE: ------------------------------------ * Loving this thing more and more every day. But I wanted to discuss a little more about the floor space that you'll need to assemble at home. I listed this as a "bad" in my initial review. Recently, I was able to dismantle it and reassemble it in my garage. You have to dismantle because a 40 inch square isn't going to fit through any of your doors. I absolutely did not have 13.3 ft by10 ft worth of empty space in my garage to lay down the material that covers the frame. But because I am now familiar with the material, the orientation of it, where it zips up, etc... I was able to just let the material sit all bunched up. I then rebuilt the frame inside the material. It was a bit funny cause I'm working inside out, a 40 inch square is huge, I found myself inside the frame zipping the material up from the inside. It's a weird scene if you were to walk in on me. LOL! So it is possible for you to do the same, you don't need to clear a 13.3 ft by 10 ft floor space. However, do follow my advice in setting up the backdrop last. Please read the original review below. ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW: ------------------------------- THE GOOD: -------------- * Led lights provided are very bright. That's also due to the fact that you're trapping light in a box with reflector material on all sides. * Assembly isn't difficult to understand at all, it is easy. But more on this in the BAD section. * You get a carrying bag as well as 5 pvc color backgrounds. * 40" square shooting space is huge!!! * 3 types of shooting angles, depending on how much light you want to trap. THE BAD: ------------ * A little QC issue... My led light came with a broken clip, and instead of bothering the seller since the light still worked, I just used sugru to mold a new clip. * Think long and hard if you need this 40 inch version. There are smaller versions. It can be unwieldy to handle this 40 inch version. Like I said above, it's not difficult to understand how to put it together. It's just you need a lot of space. It doesn't come to you in a square form. You first build the 40 inch square pvc frame. Then you lay the main material that makes the box on your floor, you put the frame on it, then you fold it up, wrapping it around the pvc frame and zip everything up. It isn't difficult at all, the problem is the floor space you'll need! 13.3 x 10 ft worth of empty floor space to lay the material down. For some people, especially people with kids, it is not easy to find this much open floor space. LOL! I included a picture from the manual to show you what I'm trying to articulate. MOST IMPORTANT TIP: --------------------------- * Don't follow the instructions in laying the background on the floor, and then putting the frame on it. If you do it this way, you'll never change backgrounds again because it is a hassle. Secondly, the background will then be under the frame, so the back bottom frame will be exposed in the pictures. What you should do is follow the instructions, except for the background part, just leave it out. Then when everything is done. Choose the background you want. It has velcro on both upper left and right corners. Inside your box will have the velcro counterpart on both the upper left and right corners as well. So you simply stick your background on it. It is pvc and doesn't crease easily, you can bend and curve it at the bottom to achieve a seamless look with the frame hidden underneath. Not only will your pictures be nicer without the exposed frame, but if you change your mind about the color, swapping the background will be much easier too. Here is an example of product pictures I took for another Amazon review using this light box. https://www.amazon.com/review/R3FM8X6Z2ZFY7E/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8 I'll rate this 4-Stars! It would be 5-Stars if not for the QC issue.

title: High quality headphones with some great features, but you're paying a premium...

title: Budget tablet with great features, but unacceptable wi-fi issues...
text: [[VIDEOID:bb1b31acd3cedf3d01bf5f12246299fd]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Budget tablet with a lot of bells and whistles such as: Octa core cpu, 4gb of ram, and sim card feature to use your cell phone services. * 4gb of ram allows the tablet to be quite responsive. * 64gb of storage, but SD slot can take an additional 128gb card. THE BAD: ----------- * Build quality, but keep in mind you're talking about a sub $150 tablet. Watch my video, towards the end you see me squeeze parts of the tablets, you can hear a lot of creaking. I think it is when it's been sleeping for awhile, that's when it can vanish. Weird. My son's Fire HD 10 broke, and we were out of our warranty period. So he's been using this tablet. For games such as Roblox, Among Us, etc., this tablet is very responsive. He hasn't complained to me about lag. Something he complains a lot with his Fire HD. The wifi issue is the biggest negative. But like I mentioned above, the wifi seems to only go bad if the tablet has been inactive for awhile. We'll rate this tablet 3-Stars. They fix the wifi issue, it would be 5-Stars for a budget tablet.

title: Important to understand this is a mouse cursor mover, not clicker...
text: I actually needed a mouse clicker, and for some reason I just thought all these "jiggler" products would have that option, but they don't. All they do is jiggle or move your mouse. It is completely plug and play, no software. Your PC should set-up device automatically, when it's done, this is how you operate: 1. Long press the only button on the device. It will turn on to A3 mode. This is the slowest mode. The mouse will move imperceptibly. 2. Short press button again to toggle to get to A1 mode. This is the fastest mode. Your cursor is flying around fast. 3. Short press button again to toggle to A2 mode. This is the medium speed mode. 4. If you want to leave this thing connected, but don't want to use it all the time, then simply long press again to turn jiggler off when not in use. In every mode, there is a timer that shows you how long it's been moving. If you're looking for a cursor mover, this guy gets the job done. But don't make the assumption that I made. These things do not have an option for clicking. That's not the product's fault, it never claimed that, it was my assumption. So I'll still rate this product 5-Stars for doing exactly what it advertises to do... move your cursor.

title: High quality, beautiful, European style, gramophone record player...
text: [[VIDEOID:708940a88783befff0f67e8b642b493d]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Gorgeous European style gramophone record player made of mostly metal. * Lever to drop the needle works very smooth. * Plays all 7, 10, or 12 inch vinyls at 33 or 45 rpm. * Bluetooth, FM, usb, 3.5mm Aux in/out jack. * Approximately 23x14x12 and hefty. title: Plenty loud for indoor use, but for outdoors, they could have made it louder...
text: [[VIDEOID:bc7d953b53202cbc545b59aabfc6aabf]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Tiny, but packs a punch. * IP67 waterproof, so just relax by the pool with it. * Touts 16 hrs battery life. * USB-C charging port. THE BAD: ----------- * It might not be loud enough. Especially if you're outside, around a noisy pool, etc. In a quiet house, it's sounds pretty good. The speaker is supposed to specialize in bass, so what better song to test it out with than LL Cool J's Going Back to Cali? Watch my video. I'll go 4-Stars!

title: Your rechargeable batteries no longer have to take turns charging, there are 16 charging slots...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * The capacity! 16 bays for AA or AAA batteries, and 2 bays for 9v batteries. One on each side. * Build quality is nice. * Over charge, Over heating, Over voltage, Over current, and short circuit protection. * A a battery is fully charged, it will show full bars and it will stop blinking, which indicates it is no longer charging. THE BAD: ----------- * I think their numbers are based on lower capacity batteries. The majority of my rechargeable batteries are over 2000 MAH, and it takes much longer than 5.5 hours to charge. Sometimes I feel it's too long because I can feel the batteries are really hot, so I'll unplug it to give it a break. * Which makes me wonder if the "Over heating" protection is really working? I haven't seen the system stop charging a super hot battery. I've had to manually stop it ever time. This charger works, but I recommend you keep an eye on it. If your batteries get too hot. Turn it off. I'll rate this charger 4-Stars.

title: The red color of this record storage case really pops...
text: When I removed it from the box, my first reaction was wow! Because the red color really pops at you, it is beautiful. It can hold up to 30 records. Has very nice metal corner accents, and 4 rubber feet at the bottom. It is lined with soft black felt inside. The only issue is the clasp, it's a little rough/sharp. Be careful opening and closing it, and never let your finger be caught in it. Other than that, this thing is great and would a be good addition to your retro decor.

title: Great looking retro speaker with bluetooth and micro sd card slot...
text: [[VIDEOID:748dadc4eb3c0bbb35a3038599986d95]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Bluetooth speaker * Micro/TF SD card slot * Retro decor * Nice light up silver dial * Sound quality is decent. THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at all. Keep in mind, this is just a speaker. Most of these retro stuff involves radios, but there is no radio here, just a speaker. The wood lamination was done very well. Nice little speaker for the price. 5-Stars!

title: This little retro radio has some shortcomings, but it's a nice option in this class...
text: [[VIDEOID:3b4cba0ea20288ccf2ad3e623b33d2c5]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Bluetooth * AM/FM radio... Many of these retro radios only offer FM. This one includes AM as well. * Retro decor * AC power * Nice glass light-up dial. * Cool rocket emblem representing the space age era. * Sound quality is decent. THE BAD: ------------ * No Aux jack * Not portable. Must be powered by outlet. * Silver plates and knobs scream plastic. * Wood laminate clearly obvious. Most of these retro radios give the retro look with lamination, some of them are done very well, that it can fool you. This one, not so much. Whenever I get a chance, I pick up these retro radios. This one has some shortcomings, but for the $40 price range, it's par for the course. I think they could have spent more time on the silver plates and dials to make the plastic not so obvious. I'll go 4-Stars.

title: High quality 4k Multiviewer, so many uses, this is too awesome...
text: Wow! This thing is awesome, especially during the Olympics. Please do not mistake this as just a HDMI switch, this is a 4k Multiviewer! A HDMI switch only allows you to switch HDMI sources and watch one source at a time. With a Multiviewer, you can split your screen into 4 sections and view 4 different sources at the same time. We use an UST projector in our home with a 120 inch screen. So with this Multiviewer, I can view four 60 inch screens at the same time. In my photo example, I only inputed 2 sources (Nvidia Shield and Chromecast) because connecting all 4 sources requires reorganizing my wires and cables, which I'm not ready to do yet. But in playing around with just 2 sources, I can already tell how awesome this is and how useful it will be. Especially gaming during games! For example, you can play your Nintendo Switch, while the Olympics is on quietly. Which source gets the audio is your choice. Perhaps on the 3rd screen will be my front door surveillance because I'm waiting for a package and the house is noisy. The 4th screen is a connected PC to browse the net! What you'll be using it for is only limited by your imagination. I already know one cool thing we will certainly be doing... You see we have multiple Nintendo Switches in our home, and we love Splatoon. However, Splatoon does not have split screen for multiplayer. Everyone is playing together, but everyone has to stare at their own little screen. Well, with this Mutiviewer, we can play side by side on the big screen! Lastly, the build quality of this device is very nice. It has good heft to it, not cheap lightweight stuff. Can't wait to set everything up. This is an enthusiastic 5-Stars!

title: A very nifty back-up solution, but you'll need some items on hand before you can use it...
text: THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED: ---------------------------------------------------------- 1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb. 2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter. 3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone. 4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone. SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO: --------------------------------- * This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited. * It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little. * Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case. * Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc. * After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again. In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!

title: Astounding build quality, this tiny radio weighs one pound...
text: [[VIDEOID:7f5cce7b86d6e54b2ddffb9c3236af76]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Bluetooth * FM radio * Aux/Ant input jack * Metallic retro decor * Great sound quality for how small this thing is. * Very neat collectible briefcase as storage for the radio. * Nifty attachable micro usb antenna * Heavy duty. Here's the link: https://www.amazon.com/review/R172FC0QNHFOC9/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8 As for this Muzen... despite the micro-usb port, I'm still giving this 5-Stars because the quality is absolutely astounding. title: Awesome little radio for your retro collection...
text: [[VIDEOID:9a46ccf3467f6614354786e48a2fd3eb]] THE GOOD: -------------- * Bluetooth * FM radio * Aux/Ant input jack * Charging base * Wooden retro decor * Both the radio as well as the charging base has USB-C charging ports. * Good sound quality for how small this thing is. * Radio is 6.8 ounces * Charging base is 2.3 ounces THE BAD: ------------ * Nothing at this price point. title: Heavy duty UPS with 6 outlets, simply plug and play...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Solid build, very heavy duty. * 6 outlets (3 with battery back-up) * LCD screen with easy to see icons. The manual explains the meaning of all the icons. * Can be managed with software if you intend to use with PC. * Simply plug and play. THE BAD: ----------- * Nothing really. But I do find the manual a bit lacking, especially for newbies. For example, it says, "Do not plug in Laser printers, or non computer peripherals to the UPS." I think what it means is that you shouldn't plug those types of things into the outlets with the battery back-up. My understanding is that the term UPS is often used to refer to the whole unit. So when it says don't plug in non computer peripherals to the UPS, that's a big confusing. Because I'm sure the 3 non battery outlets could be used for non computer related electronics, simply for surge protection. I did ask for clarification in the Q&A, which is yet to be answered.

title: A bit inconvenient if you're buying this for kids under 10...
text: This is pretty nifty, but it's not as convenient as they make it sound. Here are some things to consider... 1. You can't be handsfree like a microscope, unless you set up your phone with a mini tripod and stuff. 2. It's advertised for kids, but I don't think so, not if they're under 10. My children were very interested, but I had to do all the holding and focusing. 3. Most likely you'll need to take off your phone case for the lens to stick to your camera lens, especially if the case rises above the phone lens. With the case I'm using, there is a very slight rise, almost imperceptible, yet the microscope lens won't stick to my phone because it's sitting on top of part of the case. 4. The lens stick to your phone via some sort of suction/sticky pad. After awhile, it will no longer stick. However, the manual has a solution that did work. You simply use clear tape to clean the dirt off the lens as well as the lens on your phone. It's like when you're putting on a screen protector for you phone, and they provide you with stickers to pick up the dust. Same thing here.. you're using tape to pick up the dust. It actually works. My lens was able to stick again to my phone. All in all, it's nifty, it's something you're curious about, but after going through with it. I'm 100% sure we won't be using it much. We have a dedicated microscope at home for the kids, and to me, that's still much more convenient. I don't want to take off my phone case, focus the camera for the kids, etc. If you're buying this for yourself.. go for it! If you're buying this, thinking you'll be using it a lot to keep your kids busy, think again. Because it'll end up keeping you busy. LOL! I'll rate this 4-Stars.

title: Mixing and matching with the older MM1000 isn't working...
text: Did not work for us. We're using two older MM1000 units. Removed one and replaced it with this newer MM1025, and it did not work. I know sometimes tech isn't straight forward as we'd like. title: If you're a Frontier customer, or any other service for that matter, my review should help...
text: I've been trying to get good coverage in my garage so the security cams and smart devices don't get dropped connections, or long wait times when I try to connect from my app. This is finally the one! Frontier uses and all in one gateway, Arris NVG468MQ. In order to use the Netgear as the main router, I would need Frontier's help to put the Arris in bridge mode. I'm not sure if they can even do this, and since I purchased my own Arris to save rental fees, I wasn't sure how much they'd be willing to help either. So I didn't bother to try, instead, I set up the Netgear router in AP mode. To do this... 1. Go to Frontier's admin to turn off all wi-fi modes. Turn off both 2.4 and 5.0 modes. 2. Connect ethernet cable from the WAN port of the Netgear Router, to any available lan port of your Frontier gateway. Turn it on. 3. Using your smartphone or PC, connect to the Netgear wifi using the credentials labeled on the Netgear Router. 4. That's it. You should be online with the new wi-fi, but you'll want to change some things such as the orbi's admin password, your SSID's, etc. When you launch a browser under this new wi-fi, Netgear's admin should pop up allowing you to login to change your credentials, if it doesn't, then use routerlogin.net or orbilogin.net. 5. Since you've disabled Frontier's wifi, all your connected devices at home no longer works. But if you change your orbi's SSID to the same SSID that you were using, all your devices will work again. Keep in the mind, the Orbi system allows 4 different SSIDs. So you can still create other networks with different security levels. 6. Place the Orbi Satellite where you need better coverage. Power it on. Go back to Orbi Router and hit the sync button, within 30 seconds, you need to go back to the satellite and hit the sync button as well. Once they sync, which is indicated by solid blue for a few minutes, all lights will then be turned off. So keep that in mind, when it's up and running, there are no lights on the orbi router, or orbi satellite. I'm used to seeing some sort of lights on router equipment, so when there wasn't any lights, I was wondering if it was working properly. As it turns out, all lights are turned off when everything is up and running properly. Even if you're not Frontier, the process I laid out above, to connect the Orbi in AP mode, should be similar. Hope this has been helpful! This is 5-Stars all the way!

title: Nice entry level laptop for elementary school...
text: Understand the price point... at $400 this is perfect for elementary school kids, perhaps for adults as well to do basic surfing and shopping if you can stand the fan noise. Personally, It was just too loud for me. After the basic set-up, the fan was roaring. We haven't done anything yet, a browser hasn't even opened and the fan was going good. Granted, I admit I was doing the set-up on my bed, so the heat dissipation wasn't good. Still, I was a little disappointed how it couldn't handle being on fabric for just a few minutes. This will be for my 6 yr old, sitting on her table, so I'm sure the fan won't be kicking in quite as often. Even if it does, kids don't know how to nitpick about these things yet. LOL! Getting to classlink launchpad was no issues. Running all her school apps with no issues. Again, at this price point, you can't ask for the world. We'll rate this 4-Stars.

title: A very adequate notebook for elementary and high school, possibly college too...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Massive 17 inch screen (1600 x 900 pixels) * Latest 11th gen i5-1135G7 chip * 256 GB SSD * 8 GB Ram * HD web cam * Dual Mics THE BAD: ----------- * Not touchscreen * Not 1080p screen * Seems a little washed out. Interestingly, I need to push the screen back a little to get better contrast. So instead of sitting at a perfect 90 degrees, it sits greater than 90 for better contrast. * Others have mentioned the ram isn't easy to confirm or upgrade. I have no plans to upgrade ram now, so this isn't a big issue. This is a fairly new product, so you don't have many people on TY talking about it, or tearing it down yet. I'll be patient and wait for the YT'ers to tell me whether or not ram can be upgraded. Overall, this pc is more than adequate to get a teenager through HS, possible even for a college student who isn't doing any intensive encoding programs. Tech has come a long way, and we now get to nit-pick something like this that would probably cost you $5,000 at the turn of the century. My kid is in elementary school. We tried the chromebooks, but they are finicky. Besides for school settings, they encounter windows pc everywhere else, and since Windows can do everything a chromebook does, why not let him learn both worlds. We get to the class link launch pad with no issues. He can get into his google classroom, and google drive with no issues. And he gets to play Roblox properly with a Windows PC. We could never get Roblox to work properly on the Pixel Slate. Overall, I'll give this notebook 4-Stars!

title: Drawers are hard to pull, especially the bottom drawer...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Strong enough for monitor, copier or scanner. I have a scanner on it. * Functional THE BAD: ----------- * Sliding action isn't smooth at all. You'll need to brace the frame with one hand, while pulling with the other. If you don't brace the frame, you'll just be pulling the entire unit, and you might end up unplugging whatever you have sitting on top. Yes, it is that tight. I tried WD40, but that didn't help. The bottom drawer is worse than the top drawer. Knocking 2 stars for this issue.

title: Nifty tech with a lot of quirks that you have to get used to...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * It will do as it says.. capture videos from your sources. * Video quality seems fine to me. I'm not that picky, the stuff I record isn't important. * You can install a micro SD card, or connect a hard drive via usb. THE BAD: ----------- * Consistent with their products, they cut corners when it comes to the remote control. It's just a terrible clunky experience. I can't even put into words what's wrong with it. I guess there is a delay. So if you're impatient, you'll be pressing too many buttons, and you'll be in the wrong menu, navigate to the wrong places, enable the wrong features, etc. So my advice is to be patient. Press the button you want to press, then wait a week for it to respond. I don't know what inner components make a great remote control. Whatever they are, they are not inside ClearClick remotes. I've reviewed some of their other Clearclick products that are $150 and less, and so I was more forgiving. But at $250, really? You're going to still skimp out on the remote at this price range? * If you toggle into PLAYBACK mode... good luck getting out of it. Back button doesn't work, and it's always thinking you want to delete files. Everytime I escape playback mode, I'm relieved, but also have no clue how I got out. * Power on/off is weird. There are scenarios that will make your heart stop because you'll think the device shorted out. Just like their terrible remotes, I've noticed this power issue with their other models too. The quirk is this... sometimes when you power off and on too quickly, it just goes dead. It will not respond for a long time. Don't panic. Stop pushing the power button. Just unplug everything. The hard drive, the HDMI, the power, unplug everything. Go walk your dog, and when you come back, and connect everything again, it will power up. This happens to other Clearclick devices I have, so when it happened with this device, I didn't panic. I knew what was up. * Power port is micro usb. Again, at $250, I'd like to see USB-C. Micro usb is antiquated, and their cords are prone to get damaged. * You will need a HDMI splitter to bypass HDCP, as well as be able to turn off your Clearclick when you're not recording, and still watch TV. In my scenario... my source goes into my splitter, and my splitter has TWO outs. One goes into the Clearclick, and the other goes to my projector. This way, I can turn off my Clearclick if I'm not recording, and still watch my projector. If I connect the source directly to the Clearclick, and then go OUT from the Clearclick to my projector, then I would get their ugly icons on my projector. In my pictures, the source is my Nvidia Shield, you'll notice a row of white icons at the top. There is no option to hide these icons in passthrough mode. So if you use the Clearclick as a passthrough, you will get those ugly icons on your big screen. So even if you're recording sources that do not need a HDMI splitter. I'd still get one anyway because using the hdmi passthrough is not pretty. However, the good thing is that the files you record, will not have those icons. In conclusion, if this weren't a Vine item, I would send it back. Having said all that, it's possible that my expectations may be unreasonable for a very niche product. If a big company like Sony or Samsung create a polished standalone capture device like this, maybe it'd be $500-$600. In which case, you'd be pretty happy with the ClearClick. If you learn to live with the quirks, it's a nifty piece of tech. Hopefully, they can improve on the user experience through firmware updates. I'll go 3-Stars this time.

title: Very cute Among Us cable protectors...

title: Awesome iPhone X/XS case that may breathe new life into your phone...
text: THE GOOD: -------------- * Shutter works very well, great grip indeed. * The thick shutter grip doubles as a 3000 mah power bank. So it can be charging your iPhone while you shoot pictures. * Thin shutter plate is included in case you don't need that big of a grip, but this thin one does not have a built in battery. * The thick grip can be used as a stand to watch movies. THE BAD: ----------- * Instructions make removing and installing the plates sound simple and easy. In reality, it wasn't easy for me, especially the thin plate. You're supposed to press and slide it, but the fit is so tight, it's very difficult. The thicker grip is easier to slide out, but both grips require force. Both grips have these sharp plastic feet on them which slides onto the grooves built in the case. When they eventually slide out, these sharp plastic feet can scrape your hands due to the force you're using to pull them out. So be careful, or wear gloves if yours is tight like mine was. * The thick grip power bank uses micro-usb to charge. Would be better if it's usb-c. BTW, I included a picture that explains how this case is able to move the shutter button to the opposite corner of the iPhone. We've moved on to other phones, but always felt the XS has a nice camera. This truly nifty accessory has repurposed our iPhone XS as a dedicated camera. We'll go 4-Stars overall.

title: Underwhelmed, and at this price, I expected USB-C...
text: It's a neat little duster, but for the price, I will have to dock a star. The price along with the Jet Engine description in the listing... title: Worth it, and much easier than binoculars...

title: Terrific unmanged 4 port gigabit switch...

title: Not plug and play, some research and learning curve involved...
text: THE GOOD: ------------- * Build quality is superb * POE meaning you do not need to use the power adapter that's supplied if you have a POE switch THE BAD: ----------- * For mobile client, they tell you to download Cloudlens from the playstore. title: I forgot how slow and tedious buttons are...
text: When society was transitioning from keyboard phones to touch phones, I held out as long as I could. I just thought touching letters was weird, and not accurate. After converting to touchscreen for several years, I tried to go back to a Blackberry with buttons and man, it's not like riding a bike at all. You simply cannot go back to buttons. Everything just seem so slow with buttons. That's because your brain has conditioned your fingers to touch. Pressing buttons will now feel extremely slow, we've lost that finger pressing muscle memory. Which brings me to my point, this is a slow and tedious way to save your credentials/passwords. LOL! The onboard software, if you can even call it that, doesn't help you differentiate password vs username vs websites. It would be nice to have folder levels where you can then drill in. For example, create a folder call Amazon, tap it to go inside and see the username and password. There is no such organization. You need to input the name of the website, your username, your password all on one string. So when you turn on the Pinmaster, you'll immediately see the first string you created. On the back of the retail box, it says ILLUMINATED DISPLAY as a feature. I take that to mean the screen has a backlit, but there is no such backlit. I don't think they claim backlit on the amazon product listing, so it's probably just an error in packaging design, a feature they decided to scrap or something. Lastly, you should know that all the special characters are in the 1 and 0 buttons. That's where you can find the @,&,%,^, etc. Maybe I'll entertain this thing when I have spare time, watching a movie, and this thing is in my hands like a fidget device. LOL!
