title: Frontier customers, this is plug and play...
text: I did not get mine on Amazon, so this is not a verified review. I got mine on a famous auction site, but I'm hear to assure you this is plug and play. I was confused by the product photo saying you need a MEB1100. Basically, if you're a current Frontier customer, and you don't have and don't know anything about the MEB1100, and everything has been working fine in your house with just the Arris, then don't worry about the MEB1100. However, if Frontier set you up with both the Arris and the MEB1100, then I recommend buying both. You want the set-up to stay the same. I do use moca adapters to bring internet to rooms with coax cable. These are the ones I use: https://www.amazon.com/Motorola-Adapter-Ethernet-2-Pack-MM1002/dp/B078HMDDVS/ref=sr_1_2?dchild=1&keywords=Motorola+moca&qid=1617140900&sr=8-2 With the Arris router, you do not need to put an adapter next to it. My connection is like this: * Ethernet from ONT in my garage goes to WAN port of the Arris router in living room. * Coaxial from ONT goes to a 4 way splitter, one line goes to the living room, I connect this line to the coaxial on the Arris. * Coaxial line in my bedroom goes to the network coaxial port of my moca adapter. I then hook up an ethernet hub to the ethernet port of the moca adapter. Voila! That's how I bring ethernet to my bedroom. * I do the same to the other coaxial lines in my home to bring ethernet hubs to those rooms as well. This has been how my home has functioned. All connections were left untouched. I simply swapped out the Frontier Arris for this identical Arris. I then made sure to go into the new Arris admin and create the same wifi SSID with the same password as before. All your wifi and network devices will function as normal, no need to re-enter any passwords. I contacted Frontier, and they are sending me a box with pre-paid envelope to ship back their router, and I was assured I will no longer be charged with rental fees. I'm happy to report every customer rep I've talked to have been very nice and accommodating. The FCC ruling to allow consumers to use their own routers have been in effect since December, so I think they've been given a memo that they need to accommodate us, instead of selling us on why we should use their router, or say they cannot remove the rental fee. The process has been painless. 5-Stars!

title: Possibly a solution to a problem that may not exist...
text: [[VIDEOID:d627772a0010114e2d1717866c6d430e]] I don't know how long stainless steel zip ties have been around, but I thought this was curiously interesting. The tool feels high quality and heavy duty. The issue is that I don't see the point if the tool can barely outperform the hands and a pair of scissors. When you squeeze the handle to tighten the cable tie, everything feels super tight, but when you release the handle the slack comes back. So the idea is to squeeze the handle until there is no more slack, until it's super tight, then you use the built in chopper to cut the excess cable. That's the idea, that's the intention of this tool. But in reality, once you cut off the excess cable, some of the slack comes back. In my demo, you'll see it barely outperforms me manually tightening it and cutting off the excess with a pair of scissors. That's only because it was awkward for me to wrap my arms around my camera and tripod to record what I was doing. When I did it off camera, my manual method was just as strong as the tool method. Bottom line, this tool and the ties help keep things in place, it doesn't provide a super tight tie. You can already accomplish this the traditional manual way with standard zip ties. Actually, zip ties with grooves will lock in place and keep the tension better than these stainless steel ties. The problem is that they are smooth. Maybe if they make these ties with a little grooves it would help. But then gain, if it had grooves to lock in place, then you don't need the tool. LOL! We're going in circles. Like I said in the video, seems like a solution to a problem we don't have. I'll give it 3 stars because it does hold things in place, and it is more convenient than manually tightening and then using a scissor to cut.

title: If you're a NVR newbie like me, I think my review has good info...
text: Prior to getting this NVR system, I had already started researching on POE switches. For some reason, I assumed all NVR cameras are POE. I knew this Dragon Touch NVR had no POE ports in the back, but it didn't matter because I had planned to use POE switches. If you're a newbie like me, here are some noteworthy things before you make your decision: 1. The four cameras in this set comes with four power adapters. I thought how nice of them to include this option. But as it turns out, this is NOT an option. You need to use the power adapters for each camera. I learned that getting POE switches is only half the battle, the other half is making sure the cameras are POE compatible. I didn't know that. I thought POE switches would allow me to get rid of power adapters to any camera, any brand. Sadly, this is not the case. So this Dragon Touch system is designed for wi-fi. You only need to hook up the power adapter to each camera. But the whole point of me going to NVR is to use ethernet for more dependable connections. You can still do that with this system, but you'll still need to connect the power adapters, so you're running two cables for each camera. Had I known that, I would not have gotten this system. 2. You can use other brand cameras with this NVR if the cameras are ONVIF. However, I'm betting they still need to be the non-POE kind. I'm trying to connect a H.View POE camera, but I'm getting a black screen. Dragon Touch said that model is not compatible. End of email. I had to follow up with "What POE cameras are compatible?" I'll update when they respond. 3. It goes without saying, but in case you don't know, you need to connect NVR to a monitor for viewing. The back of the NVR has options for VGA or HDMI out. Alternatively, you can view via their Homeviz app. 4. No hard drive is included, but a hard drive is not necessary for you to start learning, testing, and setting things up. You can live view without a hard drive, but to record you'll need to install a hard drive. 5. Lastly, I'll talk about the build quality of this system. The Dragon Touch is very professionally packaged, the NVR is small and light, but that's without a hard drive currently. The cameras feel real nice, has good heft to them. I am not going to subtract any stars because of my newbie assumptions. As a matter of fact, I'm learning that if you want NVR systems with POE cameras, they would be much more expensive than what you're paying here. If I can figure a way to run both ethernet and power adapters, I may end up using this system. However, I will subtract a star for the lack of info in their listing, and emails. A product like this should clearly state whether or not their cameras are POE, and whether or not the NVR can handle POE cameras. 4-Stars.

title: Awesome camera! My review includes tips should you have issues accessing the ADMIN page...
text: Feels like a very solid camera in terms of build quality. Nice and hefty. Everybody's networking ability is different. Some may find this very difficult to set up, some may find it a breeze. I hit a snag, and was SMH for awhile, but I figured it out, and I'll share with you my issue, and how I solved it. So if you happen to run into the same issue, these notes may help. So H.View provides you with an ADMIN IP address which should work once your camera is connected to your home network. In this case, it's 192.168.1.120. You punch this into you browser, and you should be able to get to the ADMIN page to change your password and view your camera. But what happens when this IP address doesn't work for you? You will need to change it accordingly to your IPV4 gateway. I found out the easiest way is to simply let the IPC Manager modify it automatically by DHCP. I posted 3 screenshots to hopefully guide you. Here are some worthy notes... 1. Google "IPC Manager H.View" to find your way to their site to download the software. Top result with the headline DOWNLOAD CENTER should be the correct one. Be sure to download the version for your device, Linux, Mac, or Windows. BTW, they keep this in a Google Drive folder, so don't worry, you're in the right place. 2. Connect your camera to your network via POE switch. This set DOES NOT come with a power adapter, it is meant for POE switch users. 3. Install and launch the software and login in the lower left corner. Default is ADMIN and 12345. You can change this later. The login is strange because it doesn't give any feedback. Usually after logging in to a software, something changes or refreshes, such as a "log out" option, this lets you know you're logged in. But there seems to be no reaction in this software. After you hit enter, nothing changes. So don't fret, you're really logged in. 4. If you don't see any cameras, right click and hit refresh. Once you see your camera, check the box to SELECT your camera. Now, if you right click on your camera, there is a menu with a "OPEN HOME" option. If you click this, it "should" launch you to the admin page at 192.168.1.120, where you can change your password and view the camera. You can also manually punch the ip address in your browser. 5. This is where I ran into a snag. The default IP did not work for me. The browser would load an error page, "This site could not be reached." Proceed to #6 if you encounter this issue... 6. Go back into the IPC software. Make sure the default login credentials are still present, make sure your Camera is still Selected. Now, SELECT the DHCP box, and hit MODIFICATION. There should be a pop-up indicating the modification was successful. The IP address should now have changed from 192.168.1.120 to whatever new address that your router assigned. If it's still the same, try hitting refresh. 7. So now, you right click on your camera and hit OPEN HOME again, and you should be able to get to the admin page now. Or as mentioned before, just manually punch in the new IP address into your browser. When you successfully reach the admin page for the first time, you will be prompted to change your password. Now you can view your camera. Next time you go back tin the IPC software, make sure to use your new password. I included 3 screenshots to supplement these notes. Hope that helps! This is a 5-Star product!

It only pushes the heads of the cable out. You'll need to then manually pull out the head you need. It's a little tight and requires some effort. And if you have sweaty hands, it might even be more difficult to get a good grip. You're trading convenience for organization because having this telescopic casing does not make using the cables convenient, since it requires some effort to get out the cable you need. I'll knock off 1 star.

title: Awesome lights! Changing the color is like changing the volume on your remote...
text: [[VIDEOID:89264e39427324856b7ddd263cbd128]] Awesome light! Please check out the video to see operation. Changing color or brightness is like changing the volume on your tv remote. Best of all, this is usb-c! This light is only 3.5 ounces, so your mini tripods won't be overwhelmed. But the plastics and build quality is superb. It's a very nice, very smooth casing. No complaints. 5-Stars!

title: Sloth mouse pad only, no mouse...
text: At the advertised price, I knew I was only getting the mouse pad, but I feel the mouse in the stock photo could mislead or confuse people. You're only getting the mouse pad! It works as it should, very smooth pad. If you're a sloth fan, go for it! 5-Stars!

title: High quality mini tripod at just 6.1 ounces...
text: This is a great little tripod! It weighs only 6.1 ounces. I normally equate heft with quality, but not in the realm of tripods. You want it light so your backpack doesn't weigh you down. Ball head can move 360 degrees and has a cold shoe for attaching light accessories. From bottom to the top of the ball head plate, it can extend to as much as 17.2 inches. As a selfie stick, the legs have nice rubberized grips on them giving your hand a good hold. I like it. 5-Stars!

title: Awesome ps5 charger that matches your console...
text: The color scheme of this charger matches the ps5 perfectly. Charges with no issues. It has anti-slip pads at the bottom, and you can put it on top of your ps5 if you wish. This charger is only 2.8 ounces without the cable connected to it, so it feels kinda cheap. But in my experience, a lot of these 3rd party chargers are very lightly built. I'll give this 5 stars!

title: Simple battery tester for people who don't own multi-meters...
text: These are nice battery testers, but if you own a multi-meter, you probably don't need these. My multi-meter gives me the actual volts. These testers give you bars to indicate if something is bad or good. It is perfect for those who don't know how to use a multi-meter, and small enough to keep in the kitchen drawers. In my experience, in terms of accuracy, it's more about the gadget, and not the tester. For example, my dish soap dispenser stopped working, but all the AAA batteries tested as GOOD on these testers, not 100%, but still good. So does this mean these testers are bad? No, not at all. I put the batteries in my remote controls and they work. So the tester was right, there is still juice in them. The soap dispenser is just a battery hog. Once the battery drains a bit, it's hungry for fresh batteries. So this is what I mean when I say it's more about the gadget than the tester. Not complicated at all to use, so perfect for anybody in your household who doesn't like tools or complicated tech. 5-Stars!

title: More dust blowing than for vacuuming...
text: Nice light duty vacuum. The purpose of this vacuum will strictly be for around the table and keyboard. I think it functions better as a dust blower. As a vacuum, I can barely feel the suction, especially if you use any of the nozzles. You'll get a bit more power if you don't use any of the nozzle. As a dust blower, it's pretty strong. As I'm writing this, I'm wondering if it was fully charged when I was playing with it? I'm leaning towards giving this 3 stars for being a weak, and high priced. I'll give it a 4 for now, and see if the issue is because I didn't charge it enough. I'll demote this to 3-stars if that's the case.

title: Wow, this thing packs a punch...
text: [[VIDEOID:bfe3c40ef78de3ddfe2a47dd05e1975e]] This bluetooth speaker blows the phone speakers out the water! Listen to the difference in my video, the phone in the video is a Oneplus 6t. The holder portion of the speaker, is simply a rest, which can actually incline or decline, but there is no clamp. So if you had any thoughts of putting it on your car's dashboard, that's NOT going to work. The only negative thing about this device is that it's micro-usb, yuck! LOL! For such a bad cable that is prone to going bad, micro-usbs have dominated the market for way too long. I'm glad usb-c is starting to take over. I'll give this a 4 stars. It would be 5 if it had usb-c.

title: 80cm version fits my Manfrotto tripod with ball-head...
text: Very nice tripod case, but you know what? When I got it, I didn't pay attention to the size. I didn't even see that there were size options. The one I got is the 80cm version, which is approximately 31.5 inches, and luckily for me, it fits my Manfrotto with ball-head perfectly. So I recommend measuring how long your tripod is when it's completely collapsed, then choose the size you need. I suspect 80cm will be the most universal size. The bag feels nice and durable and even has a zippered compartment inside. The interior red lining matches Manfrotto's color scheme too. This is awesome. 5-Stars!

title: Nice magnetic SD and Micro SD card holder...
text: Nice magnetic SD card holder. It holds 12 SD cards, as well as 24 micro sd cards, otherwise known as TF cards. And in case you're wondering, no, it does not fit Nintendo Switch cards. Well, the switch cards are smaller than SD cards, so they fit, but loosely. It does what it's designed to do. No complaints here. 5-Stars!

title: Awesome mini speaker that packs a punch...
text: These speakers are so much fun! I can't believe the sound it packs in such a small body. We hid this under the Christmas tree, under the skirt as well. We played Christmas music during the holidays, and people would wonder where the music was coming from. It was fun to yank their chains and say, "It's the latest tech in trees. My tree has a built in music player and speakers." But the funny thing is, their jaws drop even more when told the truth because they can't believe how small the thing is. Best of all, it's usb-c. I hate it when I love a gadget so much, but it has the antiquated micro-usb. So because I like this speaker so much, I was so happy it came with usb-c! 5-stars!

title: Awesome power strip with clamps that can move side to side...
text: Very nice power strip with 6 outlets and 3 usb ports. One pleasant surprise about this outlet is that the clamp is adjustable from side to side. By releasing 2 side stops, you can slide the clamp left or right. That is nifty! These will definitely be integrated into my new table build. 5-Stars!

title: Gorgeous walnut wood retro radio...
text: Pleasantly surprised by the quality of this radio. The walnut wood is beautiful. It also has a nice heft to it at approximately 22 ounces, so they did not skimp on the materials. Perfect for dining table or end table decor. We played Christmas music during the holidays. As for the FM/AM, it's hard to pinpoint a clear station because you have to dial it in with the knob. I wouldn't have it any other way though. It needs to be a knob for the complete retro feel and look. 5-stars!

title: This HDMI 2.1 ready cable solved my connection issues...
text: Using this cable to go from my Caavo universal remote to the Vava projector. I honestly don't know what all the specs mean. LOL! All I know is that this is HDMI 2.1, so I am future proofing myself. I did have connection issues with my previous HDMI cable, and this one seems to have solved the problem. 5-Stars!

title: High quality plastic power cord organizer, not flimsy plastic...
text: Large: 15.9 x 6.2 x 5.4 Medium: 12.6 x 5.3 x 5.1 Small: 9.3 x 4.5 x 4.7 High quality plastic, not flimsy. Not just for power strip management, I use the smallest one to hide my ethernet hub on my table. Everything looks sleeker and cleaner now with the hub and all its ethernet cables out of sight. This is 5-Stars!

title: Power strip with built in circuit breaker, on/off switch and braided cord...
text: High quality power strip with 4 outlets, 3 usb ports, built in circuit breaker, and an on/off switch to completely stop power. The 5ft power cord is ample long, and has a unique braided jacket, something I rarely see in power strips. Works as advertised. 5-Stars!

title: Versatile tablet stand with unique cable management...
text: The arm and the base of this stand is mostly metal. All the white things you see are plastic. It's a little unique than most because the holes are for cable management. So if you're someone who likes to keep their phone or tablet plugged in at all times, then you'll appreciate the built in cable system. The arm and base weighs about 2.2 lbs. The holder is 3.6 ounces and all plastic. The 360 rotation at the neck requires loosening and tightening of the wingnut. I'm a stickler for higher quality holders. Maybe there is an engineering purpose to make the holder all plastic, but I've seen higher quality holders that is made of both plastic and metal, especially the extension spring part. I've seen metal rods for this part, and that's what I would have preferred. Overall, I give this stand a 4-Stars! Now if you don't care for the cable management holes, you might want to check out another tablet stand that is all metal at the base and arms, but it also has an all plastic holder. But where it has an advantage is that it can hold tablets/ipads up to 12.9 inches. This Bracwiser version only holds up to 11 inches. This other tablet is more heavy duty at 3 lbs and the 360 rotation does not require loosening or tightening of a nut. Both are vine items for me, so I have no dog in this fight. You can check that out here: https://www.amazon.com/review/R1JCXQ06T6Z7W9/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8

title: High quality stand with metal arm and base, but the holder is plastic...
text: To use a baseball analogy, this is a triple base hit. The arm and the base are heavy duty all metal, and weighs about 3 lbs. The holder is 3.6 ounces and all plastic. If they gave us a higher quality holder, this would have been a home run. Nevertheless, it is very useful, and has plenty of articulation for your desired angle. Maybe it's by designed that the holder cannot be metal due to weight issues tipping over the stand, but I've seen high quality holders that are a mixture of plastic and metal, especially the spring extension part. The higher quality holders will have metal rods for this extension part. Overall, I give this stand a 4-Stars!

title: Wireless charging top, 2 high speed usb ports, 3 outlets, bracket, all in the form of a cube...
text: Nice power cube in the size of a rubik's cube. I love the included bracket that adds so much versatility. With this bracket, you can install this cube on the wall, or even under your desk. Cord length approx. 6 ft. long, which is very adequate. Wireless charging, 2 high speed usb ports, and 3 outlets.. this is a perfect variety of charging options for home or travel. 5-Stars!

title: Nifty modular desktop organizer with power outlets...
text: Very nifty modular desktop organizer. I took pictures of the "modulation" every step of the way. Not pictured is a micro usb cable they included. The product listing doesn't say whether the USB ports are 3.0 or 3.1, so if it's not bragging, then you can bank that it's old tech usb 2.0. But at this price, it makes sense. There is a usb cable cord management in the back and some sort of tablet or folder stand. The power outlet is a super cool idea. Looking forward to organizing my table. 5-Stars!

title: High quality faraday bag...
text: Quality, fabric, stitching... everything is great! Bag is about 9.5 W x 15 H. For reference, In my picture, you can see a 10.1 inch screen tablet which is 6.25 W x 9.25 H inches. Zippered compartment in the back for a few accessories. Protect your tablet or laptop, as well as start a conversation about EMPs, data theft, etc. Because it truly is a conversation piece. 5-Stars!

title: Clamped to 2x4s in my workshop...
text: Another terrific power clamp! I have this one clamped to the underside of my shelves made of 2x4s. Christmas decoration cords then feeds into it. Very useful because I was able to avoid extension cords by bringing outlets near the entry point for the power cords to plug. These power clamps are not just useful at the table. You got a workshop with lots of 2x4's, you'll find plenty of ideas to use these. 5-Stars!

title: Very helpful in certain cabling predicaments...
text: My speakers are on a shelf with all of the outlets and even outlets on a nearby strip occupied. This was exactly what I needed. It is super useful. You can see in the picture how it looks like on the underside of the shelf. It's not even clamping to my shelf, but rather, to the frame of my shelf. Regardless, it works great. 5-Stars!

title: Produces great sound quality!
text: I love my Sony surround system from 2008. I still use it today, but it lacks the bells and whistles of today's tech such as bluetooth. This product solved the issue! It was easy to install. They provide you with both regular composite cables, as well as an optical audio cable. I connected the optical audio to one of the available ports in my AV system. I also used a regular smartphone type power adapter. They do provide you with a usb-c cable for power, but it requires usb power adapter, which is NOT included. Any adapter with a usb port that you normally use for smartphones will work. Then turn it on to either Transmitter or Receiver mode, in my case, Receiver. My smartphone was able to see the adapter immediately and paired. Music sounds super! 5-Star item!

title: Neat out of sight, out of mind dock...
text: I like how this thing can be under your desk, out of sight out of mind. I tested it with my Google Pixel Slate, and everything works as advertised. For a PC without usb-c, you can use a usb to usb-c adapter, however, your monitor may not work. They give you adhesives to test out the mounting plate at your desired location, then if you like it, you screw can screw it in permanently. I think you scan skip the screws and just use it with the adhesive as is. If it ever falls off, get stronger 3m. So far it's holding up for us. From the packaging, which is shrink-wrapped, to the dock and all its accessories, everything is very professional and giftable. One annoying thing though, they put label stickers over the usb-c ports. If you're going to do that, you need to use stickers that are easily removable. These stickers were a pain to remove. After I had a fun time removing the blue sticker, I thought I learned my lesson and would go extra slow when removing the red sticker, so the layers don't separate. Even going super slow, I managed to separate the red sticker as well. LOL! Got myself some wd40 to remove the rest of the whites. We could do without these stickers folks! Just an annoyance, not enough to knock a star. I'll still rate this 5-Stars.

title: Perfect headphone size for kids...
text: These headphones are perfect for our 8 and soon to be 6 yr old kids. For the shortest setting, from the inside top of the headband to the bottom of the earmuffs is about 5.5 inches. For the longest setting, it's about 7 inches. Check out the pictures. Believe me, this matters because not all "kids" headphones are created equally. There doesn't seem to be any universal measurements that manufactures have to abide by in order to label something "kids" headphones. We tried another "kid" set, and the shortest setting for that headphone was 7 inches, which is the longest setting for this headphone, go figure. You can see that one here: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2AMQ3TWPOCRII/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8 Anyway, this set is perfect! The colors of this headphone is so vibrant, and has a lot of pop. Most importantly, it has the automatic volume limiting feature that keeps it at 85 db. 5-Stars!

title: Not like any other digital picture frames out there. This is next level!
text: In terms of hardware, this is the best as well as biggest picture frame we've ever owned, and believe it or not, it's not even their biggest offering. This is next level stuff, not comparable to the plethora of unknown 10 inch digital frames in the market. It is also by Netgear, a well known brand. However, the app is not intuitive at all. It's not impossible to get used. Someone who is used to tech, like me, will fiddle around with it and eventually get it. But if you're giving this as a gift to your parents or aunties? You better be there to set it up for them, and walk them through. So they decided to make this gesture base instead of touchscreen, I guess to keep your screen free of fingerprints. But gestures require a knack, so it will be hit or miss with friends and family trying to do the gesturing. But for the owner, it's a knack that you an easily master. There are basically 2 gesture sensor locations. If it's in landscape position like ours, then they'll be in the middle of the top frame, and in the middle of the left frame. I have a picture illustrating this. The palm of your hands should be facing yourself, and the back of the hand toward the frame, gesture up and down at a pretty good speed, and be as close to the frame as possible without touching it. That's why I say this is a knack only owners will master. Friends who try it will be less aggressive because they don't want to knock over your frame, so their hands won't come as close to the frame. So it'll be hit or miss for them. For owners who are used to it, response rate can be 100%. The Meural app is not intuitive. For example, you have an UPLOAD button that will have access to your phone's default CAMERA folder. Once you make your selections, you hit SEND. In the Meural app, your uploaded photos will be found under YOUR LIBRARY, and at the top under RECENTS. If you browse your YOUR LIBRARY and view the pictures you just SENT, it will prompt you to SEND again. Which is confusing. Because I've already uploaded the pictures, why do I need to hit SEND again? It should be PLAY. So for whatever reason, it likes to use the word SEND. You'll be doing a lot of sending. LOL! It's just like Amazon's photo app, Google or iPhone, there is a learning curve that is not impossible to understand. Lastly, it seems to be a ploy to make money off of premium art pictures via membership or one time purchase prices. Like in-app purchase in games, you have in-app purchases in Meural for premium photos. They have free pictures labeled SAMPLES. Here is a big tip, DO NOT hit send. I realize once you stop viewing the SAMPLES, and switch to your own family photos, those SAMPLES are gone. They are not in YOUR LIBRARY. You have to go look for them again in their picture store. What what you should do is hit FAVORITE. This way it will stay in YOUR LIBRARY under Favorites, and you don't have to go searching for it again. At the end of the day, if you would like something less expensive, but more intuitive, and is 100% geared towards your own photos, and has nothing to do with selling you photos, then look for frames made for the FRAMEO app. Feel Care is a popular brand that uses the Frameo app. As a gift for non-tech relatives, those will be a much better option: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2VC33MUEW4RFN/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08DFW6R9F As for the Meural Frame, I'll give it 4-Stars! I like it a lot, it's next level stuff in digital photo frames, but the decision to go with gesture is interesting. Maybe Gesturing is more higher end than Touching? LOL? It's like they're trying to drive that point home that they are in another league. Why not give us the option of touchscreen too with gesturing? People are giving bad reviews, but I think those are impatient people. Like I said this is no different than Google photos, Amazon, or iPhone, there is a learning curve. I will take 1 star off for the app being counter intuitive, which could make non-tech people frustrated.

title: Great dashcam, but read my review for alternative installation method.
text: This is a terrific kit, complete with everything to get you started... Some important notes... 1.) If you already have a camera in place that uses mini usb, then half the battle is already won. Most of these cameras use mini usbs. 2.) The Viofo has a capacitor battery, which is what you want, especially if you live in the hot areas. They are not prone to ballooning like lithium batteries. 3.) Instructions say to slide the camera onto a mounting plate, which has an adhesive backing, you then remove the adhesive cover and stick entire unit on the glass. But it comes to you preinstalled, at least mind was. All you have to do is peel the adhesive cover and stick the unit onto your glass. Out of curiosity, I tried to remove the plate, but I couldn't, it is very tight. So if you stick the unit to your window, taking it down for whatever reason will be a pain. I don't see how you can dismount the camera and leave the plate on the window. You would have to take the plate with you, which means ripping the adhesive from the glass. So here's my tip... I'd like to be able to remove the camera, fiddle with it, change settings, etc. without hassle. Or perhaps, even dismount and hide my camera in the glove compartment when I need to. If you install it the way they tell you to, you will never take this camera down. My solution for this is using strong round earth magnets. I installed a round earth magnet on the back of the unit. This is easy, since it already has an adhesive back, just remove the cover and stick a magnet on it. Then I install another one directly onto the glass. These neodymium magnets are very strong and the hold is absolutely solid. This is how I install dashcams for myself and family. I have not installed the rearview, but I'll be using the same method. This is another review using the same method: https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/RETFFEWXHSOJ6/ref=cm_cr_getr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B088B6372Z This is a 5-Star kit!

title: High quality vintage style case...
text: Great case! High quality, sturdy. Reminds you of the old days. Isn't apropos that I have oldies but goodies vinyl in there? LOL! Handle is useful when you want to take it with you to share with friends and family. Very nice vintage look. We love it. 5-Stars!

title: Sleek design, nifty tech, and terrific sound quality...
text: Replacing my altec lansing speakers from the early 2000's. Honestly, I'm not an audiophile. My altec speakers were pretty good speakers too, and I can't tell the difference. My upgrade is simply cosmetics. This logitech set is black and sleek, looks more modern. My altec speakers were grayish, very early 2000's design. I like the nifty wireless controller that looks like a little echo dot, but it's smaller. So coming from speakers in the early 2000's, my first question was.. Can this function like old school speakers if I don't care for all the tech? So I simply used the 3.5mm connection method from my dell to the logitech, but there was NO SOUND. So you have to at least power up the wireless controller for the first time. Because under the controller is a button to switch from bluetooth to wired. Press the WIRE option, and you will then get audio. After this, if you remove the batteries and take away the wireless controller, the speakers will continue to work as 3.5mm connected speaker. You just have to turn on the wireless controller on the initial set-up. So this is good. My concern was what if the wireless controller is lost or damaged? If that happens, then you would like the speakers to go on like old school speakers connected simply by 3.5mm. So I'm happy to report, this will function without the wireless controller module. I'm not even sure turning on the wireless controller in the initial set-up is absolutely required. Your PC my pick-up sound the moment you plug in the 3.5mm jack. For me, I had to turn on the wireless controller during the initial set-up. Another thing I wondered is if I connect a bluetooth device, say my smartphone, to these speakers, then disconnect, will the speakers automatically revert back to wired? The answer is no. To connect to a bluetooth device, you have to press the bluetooth pairing button under the wireless controller, and it will stay in this mode even after you disconnect. You have to press the "wire" button to get back to 3.5mm. One more thing, the left and right speakers have 2 slots in the back to insert the stand. So you can configure it to stand vertically or horizontally. Conclusion... I love the sound, the sleek design and the technology. 5-Stars.

title: Sleek, but no built in speakers...
text: The S2421HS has adjustable stand, but no built in speakers. The S2421H has built in speakers, but no adjustable stand. So I got the no speaker version. I think about a decade ago I was very curious with monitors that can rotate both horizontally and vertically. 10 yrs later, I finally got one. LOL! The monitor is very sleek looking. The bezel is very thin. Some 24" monitors can be bigger because of thicker bezels. This monitor is approximately 21 1/8 x 12 1/2. Very sleek and compact. 5-Stars!

title: High quality product, but batteries not included...
text: Something I didn't realize is that batteries ARE NOT included. You will need to get power from your camera as well as your receiving sources. Or, purchase separately L-series batteries. Some things to note... -0.08 latency -Full metal body construction -400 ft line of sight from transmitter to receiver -300 ft line of sight from transmitter to the app. -Can transmit simultaneously to three devices.. one to the receiver, and two more to smartphones running the app. -NP F550/F570 L-Series Batteries NOT INCLUDED. Construction of the devices are very high quality. I could not get up and running because I didn't realize batteries were not included, and my dslr is old tech, and has no way of accommodating power. The cables provided by Hollyland was no use with my camera. I will need the L-Series portable batteries. Everything looks high quality. I will give this a 4 Star for lack of batteries. Once I get up and running, I'll update this review.

title: High quality Cat 7 cable...
text: No issues whatsoever. Network speed is optimal. Just needed an extension to an adjacent room, and this cable got the job done. BTW, it's the flat kind, not the round kind. Hope that helps you figure out what sort of clip you need to get to hold it against the wall. 5-Stars!

title: No PC required, no need to bypass hdcp, the best standalone capture device!
text: [[VIDEOID:378d5548ce50f90f868da94f7017d6b7]] Nobody has mentioned this yet, maybe it's because this is their first capture device, so they don't realize how awesome this thing is... But the best thing about this device is that you DO NOT need a hdmi splitter to bypass hdcp. If you've tried other capture devices, you might have ran into this issue. You will get a black screen. I was pleasantly surprised no splitter was necessary. There are so many use cases for this device, mostly people will use it to capture game play. My use case is recording Laker games. Frontier no longer carries my Lakers in Southern California, so I'm using my relatives Spectrum credentials. LOL! But doing that, I don't have any DVR functionality. This clone device doesn't give me dvr functionality, but it gives me the next best thing, which is a recorded game I can watch again WITHOUT taking the file back to my pc. You can just watch your recordings on the same tv, because this cloner is a playback device as well! The playback screen, has a nifty picture in picture preview screen. Watch my video for a little demo. Regarding sources, you can connect 1 source at a time to the Cloner, or connect multiple sources using a HDMI hub. I have the Caavo, which is a universal remote as well has a 4 port HDMI hub, connected to this cloner and it works very well. The only con is that some remote functions are laggy. Recording will take 3 to 4 seconds before it actually starts recording, but that's understandable because your hard drive is probably asleep and it needs to wake it up. BTW, you need to attach a hard drive to this. I have a 4tb WD passport attached to it and it works very well. But when accessing the playback menu, I feel this should be snappy, but it takes about 3 to 5 seconds. Once you're in the menu, when you click on a file to play, it is pretty fast. Just getting to the menu is slow. Overall, I still give this 5-Stars.

title: Feelcare makes some of the best digital picture frames...
text: Although the quality of this picture frame is top notch, it doesn't really feel like a picture frame. It looks like a mini TV. My personal feeling about digital picture frames is that they should be disguised to look like real picture frames, not technology. But that's just my personal taste. If someone is into the more modern look, then they will be super happy with this frame because the build quality is superb! Frameo is the app that is used for this and it's super easy to use. Normally, I would knock a star for a digital picture frame that is lazy in design. Meaning it just looks like a used tablet with big black bezels that turned into a picture frame. But I won't do that here because the quality is superb. There was some thought in this design and it was purposely made to look modern. So this is 5-Stars! If you prefer more of an old fashion look, check out this one: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2CMMW83H5X04G/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08BKYZZ94

title: Premium product, lackluster app and instructions...
text: Very nice high quality item, but you're sort of left in the wind to figure things out yourself. Here are some things to note, so you don't encounter the same issues as I did. -The app to download is called PRINT MASTER. You'll naturally want to download Phomemo app, but you'll soon realize it won't connect with your printer. Then you'll notice there is a specific Phomemo 110 app, so you download that as well. But after installing this app, a pop up says "we are discontinuing this app, please download PRINT MASTER." There, I saved you from the run-around I encountered. LOL! -You are given a starter roll of labels, but to use the templates in the Print Master app, you'll need to choose the proper dimension. It would be nice if this info was given in the manual, but the manual doesn't even mention the free roll. Everything is in mm, but I happened to have a mm ruler and measured the labels to be 40x30mm. -Lastly, the most important advice you need to know is you need to turn on AUTOMATIC. You might ask AUTOMATIC what? My reply is.. EXACTLY. LOL! You see, once you go to print your label. There is a setting called AUTOMATIC. There is no explanation as to what this means. The default is WHITE, which is OFF. What it means is where it will stop after it prints your label. If it's OFF, it will NOT stop. It will continue spitting out blank labels. I saw a YT reviewer who had this issue, and I didn't think anything of it, until it happened to me. LOL! You need to turn this to GRAY, which is ON. It will then automatically stop after it prints your label. Why in the world is the default set to continuously print blanks? We all tend to use default settings because we trust the manufacture knows what's best for us. I mean why would you turn something on if you don't know what it does? So I can see why many make this mistake. But now you know. Turn it on! Even if you need multiple copies, for example 5 copies. You still need to turn it on, so that it will stop after 5 labels. I would love for someone experience with these things, or the seller, to comment below what that setting is for, and why is the default off? The hardware is 5 star. The app is okay, it's a little slow. There is some lag after you make your selections. So I'll subtract a star for that. Then I'm subtracting another star for the lack of useful instructions. 3-Stars.

title: High quality, but very light weight...
text: Very high quality accessory, but at 1.7 ounces, you're not adding much weight to your gear. Just thread the bottom adapter on the gear you most often use, then thread the plate onto your camera and you're good to go! Installing and removing your camera from your gear will be easy and super fast! 5-Stars

title: Almost as good as the originals, and you save money...
text: These are almost identical to the originals except for the ergonomic bump in the back to allow for a better grip. The originals are flat on the back. The black top covers with the wrist lanyards are compatible with the originals, and vice versa. These are great to save yourself some money. But make no mistake, the originals are still better. These have a lighter cheaper build. The controller with cover and lanyard weighs 2 ounces each. The originals weigh 2.5 ounces each. The sliding mechanism to remove the black top cover is also a bit rougher. The original slides on and off more smoothly. But for the price compared to what you have to pay for originals, this is 5-stars!

title: High quality super versatile arca swiss plate...
text: High quality aluminum, but not heavy at 2.7 ounces. Jaws can hold smartphones up to 3.5 inches wide and .55 inches thick. If you have a ball head that takes arca swiss plates, this versatile accessory is a must have. 5-Stars!

title: Must have invaluable clamps!
text: These clamps don't just pertain to photography, their uses are only limited by your imagination. They are 6.6 ounces each and are very strong. In my photos, you'll see that I trust it to hold a mini projector while clamped upside down to a particle board. I have one clipped to plantation shutters to hold a surveillance camera recording the outside through the window. Even if you have no use for them now, just clip them in your garage, anywhere visible. Because one day, you'll need to do something, and these clips just might be your solution. 5-Stars!

title: Read my review to avoid my mistake...
text: IMPORTANT ADVICE... do not thread the mini ball head onto anything too tightly. This stand is actually fine, it's the cheap ball head that has given me headaches. The ball head has a... I'm not sure what the technical term is for this kind of bolt, but lets call it a "dual bolt." 1/4 bolt is threaded inside a bigger bolt, I presume 1/2. I threaded a mini projector onto this thing, I guess a little too tight. When I unthreaded the projector, the 1/4 bolt was stuck, meaning it was unthreading WITH the projector. So the 1/4 bolt came off the 1/2 bolt. You would think that all it takes are some pliers, but surprisingly, pliers even with teeth, have a hard time gripping this bolt. I had to use my drill press vise to get it off. To properly use that ball head, you want to thread it onto whatever device you're using, but don't thread it on too tight like me. Then tighten with the lower knob. You might think, this reviewer isn't using common sense. I don't think so at all. Anybody would like his/her electronics threaded securely. The amount of strength I used was reasonable. The issue lies in that inner 1/4 bolt not being secured enough inside that bigger bolt. But I fixed that. Once I was able to unthread the projector from the vise... with the 1/4 bolt now free, but secured by the vise, I then took the ball head body to the vise and threaded the bigger bolt onto the 1/4 bolt a "wee bit" tighter than the manufacturer did. If you don't have drill press vise like I do, then you better be extra careful using this. 3-Stars.

title: Relatively easy to set-up. If you can't access the user interface, read my review...
text: I had my concerns because I've researched Powerline Adapters before, and there is talk about how your home's electrical wiring may cause your adapters to work or not work depending on where you plug in your adapters. For me, the process was pretty painless. I plugged the main adapter (GPL-2000PT) to a wall outlet next to my Frontier Gateway. Then an ethernet cable connects my Gateway to this adapter. BTW, the GPL-2000PT is the smaller of the two adapters. For some reason, my brain correlates MAIN as being BIGGER. So without looking at the model numbers on the device, I connected the bigger adapter next to my router initially and got it wrong, and had to start over. Anyway, so remember the smaller one is the one that gets tethered to your router. Next you plug the bigger adapter (GPL-2000WAC) to wherever you want to have the new wi-fi network. Press the Security button on the main adapter, then press the Security button on the other adapter.. wait for them to pair, and voila, you have a new wi-fi network. In my case, I was pleasantly surprised that everything worked because I needed better wi-fi in the garage, and there weren't any wall outlets available. Manual specifically recommends using wall outlets. I have these outlet boxes that the previous homeowner had installed along exposed 2x4 beams. I plugged the adapter into one of these and crossed my fingers, and amazingly, everything linked up. Speeds are super fast and snappy too. The hiccup I run into, which is the same hiccup I run into every time I play around with gadgets of this kind whether it be powerline, meshes, or wi-fi extenders.... is the part where I would like to change the SSID and password. The default they give you is always something that's hard to remember, so you always want to change this. I can never get to their user interface with their provided IP's. The idea is that once you're on the adapter's network, you should be able to go to the provided address to access the user interface. It never works for me, no matter the brand. Either there is something about my network that I'm not understanding, or there are many consumers in the same boat as as I am. In any case, I will tell you what does work for me every time.. I simply go to my own router ADMIN. So if you're Spectrum, go to your Spectrum admin, if you're Frontier, Verizon, etc., go to their router admin. Then look for your new Nexuslink adapter. Your router would have assigned it an IP address. Type that ip address into the browser, and it will take you to the Nexuslink user interface. So whenever you can't get to a user interface provided the manufacturer of a powerline adapter, wifi extender, etc., just go to your own router admin and get the IP address that it was assigned. BTW, when you're browsing your router admin for the IP address of the adapter, you might not know what you're looking for since it may not be labeled by your router properly. So you'll need to find it through a process of elimination. All the IP addresses listed will show whether the device is connected by wi-fi, moca, or ethernet. So you can ignore all the wi-fi and mocas. Look for the ethernet connection that is unfamiliar to you. Mine showed up as "UNKNOWN." I have several devices connected to my network as UNKNOWN. I simply tried them all out, and one of the addresses eventually took me to the Nexuslink user interface. If any network expert is reading this, I'd love for you to chime in below in the comment section and explain when it comes to this part regarding accessing the user interface of an adapter whether it be powerline, wifi extenders, etc., why the default given address in the manual never works for some of us. This hiccup doesn't deserve a star subtraction since I've experienced this with every other brand I've tried. Anyway, I can now access my garage camera blazingly fast, versus the 50/50 hit or miss connections before. This is 5 stars!

title: This is a 480p projector with an awesome on/off design...
text: [[VIDEOID:a1ea9dee5ef92897a45e22f1f1942100]] When it comes to mini projectors, the Nebula Capsule 2 is still the best in my book, but you'll be spending more than twice the cost of this Walnutt DLP. If money is not an obstacle, then go check that one out. Who is Walnutt? I don't know, but I think even the big boys like Anker (who makes the Nebula) would be impressed by their design. This isn't quite small as a soda can, but it's still a nifty beautiful design. You twist the top to form a shape that looks like those right angle PVC elbows, and your projector turns on. Twist it back to form a cannister, and it turns off. That is a very neat design. It doesn't seem like it's a white label product either since I can't find any similar projectors under different brands. Walnutt is the only one selling this. So kudos to them for their unique product. Because of the built in 3200mah battery as well as a USB port, you can be completely wireless watching the fire stick, the chromecast, etc. You simply use the USB port to power the fire stick. For how long, maybe just one movie, before you need to plug in the projector power adapter, but you'll never need to find a power source for your fire stick as long as you use the USB port. However, the native resolution is 854x480. I was completely fooled by the 1080p in their product headline, when it actually said "1080p supported." That's my fault for skimming, not reading. But this means you can play 1080p, it will just be scaled down. This is a 480p projector. The speakers are 2.5 watts x 2. There are no controls, other than the focus wheel, on the projector unit. So you better make sure you never lose your remote. At this price point, you can't ask for the world. If you want to pay double and get the Nebula Capsule 2, that thing is 720p, has a 9700mah battery, android, and has 8w speaker.. all in a soda can size body. But for all that, you're paying over double. So at the end of the day, this is a good 480p projector, at a proper price with a nifty design. I'll give this 5 stars. My video demo is in a garage with no white screen, just the garage door material, you can see the garage door hardware. LOL! It was about 4 pm, sun was still out. I simply turned off the lights.

title: PCs with regular USB ports can now use USB-C accessories...
text: Absolutely handy to have around. The market is starting to get flooded with accessories focused on USB-C. These adapters worked for me in getting a USB-C dock to function on pc with no usb-c ports. Just plugged this adapter into my windows 10 pc, then I plugged a usb-c dock into this adapter, and everything is working. You should have these in your tech tool box. 5 Stars.

title: Perfect gigabit ethernet adapter for old computers...
text: Nowadays, USB-C adapters are flooding the market, but we have an old dell laptop that needed a regular usb to ethernet adapter. This adapter got the job done! For what it's worth, the ethernet cable is not coming from the router, it is coming from an ethernet hub, and this adapter connected with no issues! 5-stars!

title: Awesome pass thru modular crimper...
text: Excellent tool! Great heft to it at 10.3 oz. There are plenty of YT videos to learn how to use crimpers. If you are not a professional, the quality of this brand is good enough. A homeowner who occasionally needs to fix an ethernet cable, believe me, this will last you a lifetime. Search YT for "pass-thru modular crimper" and you'll get plenty of reviews and tutorials for this type of crimper. They may be different brands, different names, but just watch the videos that have the same appearance as this crimper, and you'll be good to go! 5-stars.

title: One solid power tower, the cubes do not separate...
text: This is about 7 inches high in total from top to bottom of base. The round base has an approximate diameter of 5.5 inches, and the tower itself is about 3 inches wide. In case you're wondering, the divided lines between each outlet cube/row do not separate. There is a different power tower on Amazon where the cubes can separate and be used individually. You can check that product out here: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B089PRBZWM/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1 Even though the other one can separate, this one has an extra USB port and a built in flashlight. This item is also 5 stars in my book!

title: You will be getting the Triple AAA version, not Double AA.
text: Not sure if the seller is incorrectly naming his batteries because what you're getting are triple AAA batteries. Or, if in fact he is trying to sell double AA batteries and there is something wrong with the inventory. In any case, I can still find use for this AAA version. My remote controls are the things that eats up batteries the most, and they all take AAA batteries. I could have this adapter bedside, and use it for my TV remote. Your wireless keyboards most likely take AAA batteries too, so you can use it for that. Basically, anything that requires AAA batteries, but can somewhat be stationary. I'm only subtracting 1 star because I can still use these, but I can see how someone can really be upset if they really needed the Double AA version.

title: Cool idea, but the app didn't work for me...
text: Time stamp for this camera is incorrect, so I downloaded the OD Cam hoping to be able to set the time. After the camera has been powered up, you single click the power button to activate wi-fi. You will hear a voice say wi-fi on and you'll see a blue led light blink along next to the solid green light. But it would never connect to the camera. The app is pretty quirky, half-baked. Once you turn on the app, it's immediately working, it will say "Connecting device..." But what is it doing? I haven't even selected their wi-fi SSID yet. Well, even after selecting the "EP7_XXXX" id, the password of 12345678 doesn't work. It keeps saying "check wi-fi and try again," then you'll hear the lady voice saying, "Wi-fi off." So it automatically turns off the wi-fi once you can't connect. So I've been using this without the app, and without proper time stamp. There is a learning curve to understanding the camera angles when you're wearing it on your head. The camera can swivel, so you can record your funky toes, or point it up and record your water stained ceilings. LOL! Once you're happy with your recording, you can take it to your pc to view your files. There is no need to remove the micro sd card. When you plug it into your pc, the lady voice will prompt you to press the video button for removable storage mode, or the photo button for webcam mode. Video quality is not that great, so I'm subtracting 1 star for that. I'm also subtracting another star for the half-baked app and connection process.

title: Nifty idea, but slower charging speeds...
text: [[VIDEOID:79526b07ccdde970c8fc7ce20ed2a28]] This is pretty nifty, but at the end of the day, I'm not sure how practical it is. I think we now live in a world where we have a gazillion cables in our home, so most likely you are still going to reach for whatever cable you need. Theoretically, these could be useful when you're in a bind. For whatever reason, lets say your lost your iphone cable, these will come in handy. But if you have a choice of the real cable or using this cable with the adapter, the choice will always be the real cable simply because they charge faster. You lose a bit of speed using these magnetic adapters. I know myself, I know my habits, and I'm 100% sure that I won't be able to find the box with all the adapter heads when I need it one day. LOL! These little heads looks like they can easily be lost. Very nifty, and I give it 5-stars for being something that is a reflection for the sign of the times.

title: Perfect dock for older thunderbolt Macbook...
text: Nice compact dock. Hooked up my brother's 2015 Macbook with no issues. Two usb ports, usb-c pd port, display port, hdmi, and a headphone port. Just for curiosity, we testing on windows laptop without thunderbolt, but we couldn't get the display to work on either HDMI or Display Port. The biggest con of this dock is the short and permanent thunderbolt cable. It is challenging to set up your desk exactly the way you want it when the cable is so short. Seems like they designed it with mobility in mind. 4 stars.

title: Of all the surveillance cameras I've used, this one has the best software...
text: I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders. Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!

title: Nice Cat 7 cables...
text: Ran these cables from garage to upstairs bedroom. No drop in speed. True shielded Cat-7. Not much to say, they get the job done.

title: Not as nice as their 8 inch frame...
text: This is our 2nd FeelCare picture frame. It works just as well as their 8 inch frame and the Frameo app is simple and awesome to use. However, my gripe bout this 10 inch version is that it doesn't look like a picture frame, it looks like a tablet. With a little effort, tablets can be turned into picture frames, so I think digital picture frames should separate themselves from tablets by actually looking like picture frames. Here is my review on the 8 inch version, you'll see that version actually looks like a picture frame. https://www.amazon.com/review/R2CMMW83H5X04G/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08BKYZZ94 I'll give this 10 inch version 4 stars.

title: You can access motherboard from the top...
text: I do not have time yet to build out this case, but the #1 reason why I grabbed it was because you can access the motherboard I/O from the top. This is due to the vertical layout. This game changer potentially means, no more dragging out the pc and having to unplug things so that you can reach the back. Everything looks great! High quality metal or aluminum, consistent powder coating of the black color, and it isn't too heavy at 13 lbs 5 oz. I can't wait to build this out. 5-stars!

title: USB-C dock that works with my pixel slate chromebook as well as my old laptops!
text: Hey Guys, this is it! A lot of USB-C docks do not play nice with older computers with no usb-c port. You would need to use a usb-c to usb-a male cable, or put a usb to usb-c port adapter on your laptop... but these are just solutions that are hit or miss. I tried these solutions with another dock and it was a 100% miss. Now even if you have a usb-c port, it still might not work if your device is a chromebook due to the Chrome OS. So a lot of these usb-c docks on the market were made specifically for windows pc with usb-c port. I do not own a new laptop with usb-c port. I only have older laptops with regular usb ports and the device which does have a usb-c port happens to be a chromebook. This pluggable worked for all my devices! My chromebook works perfectly with this! Not only that, using a usb-c to regular usb cable, my old dell inspiron worked with this dock as well. Instead of using a usb-c to regular usb cable, I even tested a usb to usb-c port adapter on the dell, then I plugged the usb-c cable from the pluggable into the usb-c adapter on the dell... and that worked too!! This simply works! It is night and day compared to another dock product I was trying out that did not work for any of my devices. This is mindboggling to me actually. How could one dock not work with any of my devices, with any of my solutions and adapters, but another dock works with all my devices, all my solutions and adapters! Wow. Both docks were Vine items for me, so I have no rooting interest in either. This is 100% honest and ecstatic review! This is the one to get. Avoid this one... https://www.amazon.com/review/R32SN4BPM7SPAA/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B088F7SY6S

title: High quality cables...
text: It's hard to get in depth about ethernet cables. LOL! What is there to say? I think most people just want to know do they work? Do you see a drop in speed? And to those questions, it's a Yes and No. Yes, they work as they should. No, I did not see a drop in speed. If you just need something that works, get it!

title: Perfect the curious elementary school kids...
text: We have two kids, so a great feature about this microscope is that the kids waiting for their turn can see what the person using the scope is seeing through an app. That has helped tremendously! You don't know how useful the app is unless you have multiple kids. LOL! My son is into space and the universe, so the opposite world, the microscopic world is a great supplement to his curiosity. The scope is approximately 1 lb 8 oz without batteries. So it's not heavy duty, but the quality is adequate for the price and the age range of the users. The slides are pre-made and are interesting. We will definitely purchase blanks to do our own experiments. 5 stars!

title: Awesome cat 8 cables...
text: We wanted our NAS server to have the best cable connected to the router. This cable did the job. Checked our speed online and we're getting our advertised speeds. No complaints. 5 stars!

title: Doesn't play nice with my service and router...

title: I'm getting top speed...
text: Needed to run ethernet from ONT in garage to adjacent bedroom. Got the job done. No speed slow down. We have fiber optics 500/500. Highly recommended.

title: Gets the job done...
text: Ran this cable from living room to garage. No issues whatsoever, getting my usual top speed via ethernet. Highly recommended!

title: No zoom, but best price in this class...
text: In this $30-50 price range, I think you should stick with this one. We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus: 1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up. 2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment. 3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.

title: Beautiful picture frame...
text: Aesthetically, a digital picture frame should look like a picture frame, and this product knocks it out of the park. It is a beautiful looking picture frame. Everything about this item screams premium from the packaging to the frame itself. The app that this frame uses is called OUR PHOTO, and I've attached the picture to show what the user interface looks like on your phone. It is nice simplistic app. I've seen lazy products out there that want to sell as picture frames and they just look like tablets. This is what you want! 5 Stars!

title: Gets the job done...
text: I needed another ethernet hub. I have multiple PCs at my desk, but only 1 ethernet line, so one of my PC is on wi-fi. This solved my problem. My use case... 1. Ethernet goes into this adapter, then this adapter is plugged into a dock via the USB. The PC that uses that dock now has wired internet. Lets call this PC ONE. 2. PC TWO on the same desk can now get wired internet by connecting an Ethernet cable from PC TWO's ethernet port to one of the three remaining ethernet ports on the adapter. Awesome product!

title: Super handy!
text: These ethernet couplings are super handy when your ethernet cord doesn't quite reach your destination. I have a mix bag of cables at home, cat 5, cat 6, cat 7, cat 8, you name it. I test them all and they all work! Not much to review here. They get the job done. 5 star.

title: High quality microphone, plug and play...
text: Plug and play, no issues. Very sensitive, so on a conference, be sure to mute your mic if you wanna say something that's only meant for certain people in your room. For us, it's just a distance learning mic for our children. They love it because it also looks like a UFO. The weight, the material, everything about it is high quality. 5 stars.

title: Helpful if you're the tech guy in the family...
text: I don't have any long term need to share accessories with two computers. But I tinker a lot, and often times are asked to troubleshoot family and friend's computers. Instead of having to swap out cables, this makes setting up a new PC a breeze. Not just minor peripherals, you can connect docks to this and it will share it between your computers. Everything is connected to my dock.. the monitor, the mouse, keyboards, etc. So I take up only 1 port on this switcher, the usb that's coming from the dock. Highly recommend this product. 5 stars!

title: High quality multi-purpose stands...
text: Super nice set of stand/risers. They are made of metal and built to last. The legs have detents that will allow the pins to click into place. Use them in the kitchen or the office, very versatile. 5 stars.

title: High quality camera, but it runs very hot currently...
text: Okay, you know the saying about first impressions? Presentation matters in a "premium" product. Anything north of $200, I expect good packaging. This Panacast is priced over $500 and has a retail of nearly a $1000. This is iPhone territory, yet the thin cardboard box with creases looks like packaging you'd find on any other white label gadget coming outta China. It was smushed a little cause it was shipped in an Amazon white padded envelope. If it weren't for the fact that this is a Vine item for me, I'd be so upset. As for the camera itself, it is pretty nifty and the quality is what you'd expect for something over $500. It is small, but when you hold it in your hands, you feel the heft of the metal. It is definitely not one of those cheap lightweight plastic cameras. However, they got to do something about the heat. After a few minutes, you can fry eggs with it. It runs hot! I hope future firmware can do something about this. There is nothing obvious in terms of picture or video quality that would separate this from the $100 stuff on the market. They all look the same to me. The 180 degree is the reason you're getting this. If you download their JabraDirect software, you'll have more control over the camera. For instance, you can lock in at a certain degree. I like to play around with the 180 degree, so initially I was annoyed that it kept automatically zooming in and out on me due to movement. The desktop software will allow you to lock in on any degree you want. I'm sure this will make a fine camera for business settings, but for us, it's simply for video calls with relatives overseas. Grandparents will often say, "what's my little boy doing over there?" Well, now they get to have a wider view. The price, the underwhelming packaging, and the heat issue... I'm knocking 2 stars.

title: Soft quiet keyboard....
text: Some don't like the keyboard saying it's mushy, but to me, it's quiet, which is perfect if you're a night owl but your significant other isn't. LOL! Wrist pad perfect for average hands. The media controls work very well with youtube, netflix, etc. For some reason, I always struggle looking for the calculator app, so I like the calculator button in the far right that launches the app for you. Overall, a pretty nice user experience. The mouse is pretty standard, nothing to write home about. I do have a recommendation for the Logitech Unifying Receiver software... it would be nice if the software would tell you, "This mouse or keyboard has already been unified." I was trying to sync this keyboard, but I had forgotten that I had done it already. So when I was turning the on/off slider to sync, there was no reaction and I was puzzled for the longest time. It turns out nothing is wrong with the hardware, but something is wrong with my short term memory. LOL! So again, a pop-up notification saying the device is already paired would be nice.

title: Nice screen, but the buttons won't be kind to big hands/fingers...
text: I don't know how these things are made, but I thought it was kinda strange that it's touch screen when you connect it to a computer, but the screen itself is not touch screen. So to mess around with the screen's settings you have to use these side buttons on the left. One of the button is designated as the back button, the other allows you to toggle by sliding the button up or down, then pushing in to select. I don't have the biggest hands or chubbiest fingers in the world, I'm relatively skinny, yet I found it difficult. If your fingers are muscular, you might not like these controls. If you're selling in the US market, it would be nice if the default language was set to English, but it is not, it was in Chinese, and it took me awhile to finally set it to English. I'm not sure what's my use case scenario for this yet. I wanted to hook up a fire stick to see if this can be used for movies on the road, but there is only a mini HDMI port. I do have a USB-C to Female HDMI adapter, but it did not work. I was getting "NO SIGNAL" when I hooked up the fire stick to my adapter. As a PC monitor, it works very well. I also hooked up the Nintendo Switch and confirm it works, so that's something you can do, play the Switch on the road with a bigger screen. The stand is magnetic and very slim. I'll give this 4 stars.

title: Very versatile!
text: This tower strip is very versatile. I think the only thing that beats it in versatility are the power strips with pivoting outlets. You can use the lower base by itself, and you can plug the top base directly into a wall outlet too. The only thing they could have improved was perhaps more usb outlets because this thing is huge, and for it to only fit 2 usb outlets is puzzling. I put a coke can to show you how big it is. In any case, it needs to be big so power adapters don't get in each other's way. 5 star item!

title: A little more versatile than the standard strip...
text: My headline says "a little" because I tried several adapters that wouldn't fit next to each other. But as you can see in their stock photos, smaller profile adapters like apple may fit side by side. The most versatile power strips are the ones with the pivoting outlets. This donut strip gets the job done and even has 2 usb ports, but since it's an odd shape for a power strip, I thought there may have been a reason for it, but since it provides no advantage, it's just a different shape for the sake of being different. Nothing wrong with that. I'll go 4 stars.

title: Windows 10 Pro with energy efficient hardware...
text: We've been grabbing a few of these mini pcs to test them out and see if they're good for Distance Learning. We have a lot of spare pc peripherals including old school 4:3 screens. But for many, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But if you do have these accessories laying around, and you're curious how this Minix works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great! I just reviewed a Beelink mini pc that is very capable too. The 1080p camera, microphone, speakers and monitor connected with no issues. Windows did all the firmware work. The only software we had to fetch was Logitech's unifying receiver for the keyboard and mouse. In California, many k12 schools are using CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy. It's mind-boggling that Windows 10 Pro is $200 alone. Of course if you're going to pay full price for Windows 10 pro, you wouldn't put it in a low end computer. Nevertheless, it is awesome that it's included here. I recently reviewed the Beelink T4 which has the Z8500 cpu. On paper, that's slightly a faster cpu, but interestingly, the Z8350 in the Minix is a newer cpu. They may have made the Z8350 more efficient or something. In any case, normal human beings won't be able to tell the difference. LOL! The MINIX Z83-4 Plus is a little bigger than the Beelink T4, but comes with a wifi antennae, and a built in micro SD reader. Basic activities such as web browsing, watching Netlfix, Youtube, kids doing work on ClassLink, etc., this mini pc is very capable.

title: All plastic, no 1080P recording, and read my advice regarding micro sd card insertion...
text: I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls. For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces. I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it. IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!! ------------------------------------------------------------ Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling. This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.

title: Perhaps not compatible with older computers and Chromebooks...
