Unfortunately the seller is a problem who feels they don’t have to abide by the Amazon promise of 2 day delivery which is definitely a bed way to do business. My recommendation is to get the product but stay far away from VM Express and purchase from a reliable seller

title: Works well in southern USA
text: Found this unit and app to be easy to use and reliable in the area we are. Not being global we cannot comment on that aspect but honestly for the southern eastern section of North Carolina it is just what the doctor ordered for full time Rv use.

title: Doesn’t work as well as advertised
text: Delivered in timely fashion but the item doesn’t work as well as advertised

title: Does tip easily at certain angles
text: Very handy table. Fast delivery. Does tip easily at certain angles, but I expected that. I like the versatility of the adjustable top.

title: Look elsewhere
text: This was almost half the price a few months ago, and then it was worth it. Issue here is that the keys squeak and make noise, like they need lube. It's irritating and I will soon replace it. The letters on the keys fade quickly into thin air. Not a good keyboard.

title: Good Overall - Some Quality Concerns
text: This is a good screen, but not quite as.... quality as I'd hoped for. For example, the screen blinks out every now and then. It also won't turn back on sometimes when the PC goes to sleep, so have to power cycle it. The color depth is good, better than a less expensive screen but not as great as others. I am not familiar with all the terminology. This is a good middle of the road display. The response time is not as great as I'd like, still a lot of blurry motion. Durability is yet to be determined. It is heavy, which I like, and it swivels and tilts etc.

title: Good Overall
text: I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply. To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you. The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking. Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

title: Work From Home & Gaming (updated)
text: At first I thought this was great, I even ordered a 2nd and 3rd. Now I am finding dead pixels in 2 of them after just 6 weeks. If I did not use two for work, I'd surely return them, but the dead pixels don't bother me when I am working. They would however, bother me a whole lot if it was on the one I use for games. After a while of use now, I've also concluded that these bleed way too much light. Adjusting for gamma and brightness hardly does anything to correct it. As much as I want to love these, I can't recommend them anymore. Otherwise these are great, if you can get by the bleed and pixel issue.

title: Waste of Money
text: If your plan is to work from home, stay away from this at all costs. It is totally flimsy and cheap. Aside from that it is extremely small and you can't see your work environment on it. I went against my better judgement and got this thinking I could get away with it, boy was I wrong. No HDMI ports either, just VGA and DVI. This belongs on the shelf of a thrift store.

title: OK But Lots of Bleed through
text: This is a decent monitor, but a ton of light gets through and it does not produce darks or blacks at all whatsoever. Looking at it without any image, you can clearly see the light coming through. In the night it's like a glowing night light. It has a kind of cheap feel to it, but the thing works. Hoping it will last a few years at least. This will get you by, if you don't really care about a 2nd screen but need one for whatever reason.

title: Good Laptop
text: This is a good and quick system. However, it needs a couple more USB ports. The mini (flimsy) display port and power port are on the back side of this, which is awkward. The power cord has come out on it's own and I did not realize we were running on battery power until it was about to shut down. If this had a standard display port, more USB's and better placement for the power/display port, then it might get stars.

title: Good System
text: I'd recommend this for a small house. The setup is easy and it's everything I'd want and expect in a home security camera system.

title: Fairly Decent Upgrade From Gen 1 - But not quite their.
text: We originally purchased a first generation Alexa when they came out. It is a great device that we still use in another part of the house now that we have this newer generation version. Aside from it being a little shorter and more stout, it's otherwise no different whatsoever from the first generation. The one exception to that is the sound. The bass is just slightly better on the new device, but not a lot to make an impact. Sound is still dull, with no defining highs or lows, just more a blaring mid range sound. If they can fix this or offer a device with much better audio, we'd get that. Is it with the money to upgrade from a Gen1? I'd say no, not yet.

title: Not Enough Pressure
text: I got these to blow out my computer. It has little air pressure to effectively clean it out. Disappointment.

title: Bland, Unremarkable & Ads :-/
text: The tablet itself is decent, nothing too special. The issues I have are the special offers, which you can't turn off unless you are willing to pay Amazon an additional 15 dollars to remove advertisements. I think that is total bull. Amazon claims that they sold you this tablet at a reduced price, so they support the loss by providing paid advertisements. I have a real problem with that, especially with how well Amazon is doing and how much money we spend with them annually. Additionally, the Operating System (OS) is very bland and lacks features. I pretty much regret buying this tablet over an android version like a Samsung. I was just feeling cheap when I got it, now I have to live with it. If you are just looking for something cheap, don't mind advertisements and really don't use a tablet for anything important, this one may be it for you.

title: Pretty Good - Don't Use Batteries
text: These should be pretty convincing to wannabe thugs or criminals. However, my REAL CCTV cameras do not have blinking red lights, so I would definitely NOT put batteries in this. A blinking red light is a dead giveaway that this is fake. Other than that, the mount is metal, not plastic, which is good. The protective cover on top of the camera is rather flimsy and slides too easily. Should do the trick overall so long as the red light is not flashing.

title: Fantastic Radio
text: To mention right off the bat, I am not even an amateur radio operator, just someone who enjoys radio. I find radio to be far more romantic and compelling than modern methods of broadcasting. Staying up late in the night and turning the dial with the soft glow of the tuner, the sound of static and mystery that can sometimes accompany radio broadcasts offers something truly genuine that you can't get anywhere else today. That feeling is priceless and not duplicable (If that was even a word). Anyway, this radio is good quality and contains the capability needed to reach further than most others. If you enjoy radio as I do, a clock radio, ghetto blaster or home stereo won't cut it. If you know what I am talking about, then this radio is for you. I've stayed up many nights listening to Coast to Coast AM on the internet, but it lacked the feeling something like this radio will bring you. I was unable to pick up a station on my home stereo to listen to CTC and was forced to use the internet. The internet provided a clear, stereo sounding broadcast and was very clear. The CC Radio has been spoken about on the program for many years. I finally picked one up and am very pleased with it's performance. I can now pick up the radio broadcast of Coast to Coast AM and with all the nuances I expect of a a late night radio broadcast. When interesting speakers talk about compelling topics, a crystal clear internet broadcast does not move you inside. However, using the CC Radio, the slight static, the slight fading in and out and all other fantastic experiences you can only receive using a real radio, it has the ability to make you feel and even send chills up your spine. There is just something a good solid radio can do for you that nothing else can and the CC Radio delivers on that 100%. You will not be disappointed and I really need to get my license.

title: Good Card
text: Good card, plug and play. I can take videos and pictures and my camera does not hiccup.

title: Don't need anything else
text: Great mouse for the price! No need to get an expensive one unless you are into graphic design or CAD.

title: Good Case
text: We gave this case as a gift to my brother in law. On the same day we gave it to him, he dropped it in the ocean (with phone in of course) to a depth of about 5 feet. Protected the phone just fine. Good case!

title: Great Accessory
text: Used this on my baseball cap, on my bare head (full of hair) and on a motorcycle helmet and it worked flawlessly in each application without slipping or otherwise being annoying. Would highly recommend.

title: Highly Recommend
text: This is awesome and the first thing I noticed was the high quality of it's construction. We are going to use it snorkeling and swimming in the Philippines this year.

title: It's ok, nothing special
text: I bought this for my 7 year old daughter. Not sure why radios like this are so pricey nowadays, especially those that use string or bands on the inside (analog tuners) to tune radio stations, gives it a cheap feel, one without durability. The selector switches feel cheap, not sure how long the switches and tuning knob will last, they are probably the weakness on this radio. Overall it is just ok, the sound is not as tinny as some competitor models, which is nice. In the end this is for my 7 year old daughter, just feel a product like this should be priced at about $25.00 - $35.00, not it's current price.

title: Great SSD
text: Great drive that will breathe new life into your laptop or desktop. Samsung has traditionally had great solid state drives and this is my 3rd. Have had no issues at all with installation or compatibility across several desktop and laptop systems. The one I purchased before this is on it's 3rd year of flawless service and undiminished performance.

title: Great Camera
text: Overall a really good camera with great video quality. The software it comes with to manage the device is thorough and self explanatory. Have to agree with other reviewers on the install/setup though, it is not fun and takes some time depending on how you access the video. Would definitely buy more in the future.

title: Fantastic
text: Easy install, easier setup and much faster than Roku. What else need be said?

title: Great Product
text: At first I was skeptical about this product, something about it did not appeal to me in the images. Since it had quite a few good reviews, I decided to give it a shot since I needed something like this for work purposes. Fits my Galaxy S3 perfectly and works exactly as stated in the product description. The belt clip is surprisingly sturdy and works very well. Definitely recommend.

title: Fantastic Player
text: We love this player. We've owned cheap players in the past and this time we spent a little extra for something better quality and it by far outperforms the others we've had. Crisp picture and quick loading make it a must have.

title: Doesnt work right
text: I have a bunch of Alexa products that work just fine. For some reason this one doesnt seem to hear well. Alot of commands are ignored and it freezes up. Attempted to get help replacing this item through Amazon but they only want me to return it for refund and repurchase. Since i got this item for $10 with the purchase of my Ring Doorbell, a $10 refund will not rebuy this item. So now we have to replace ourselves.

title: Works great
text: Packaged well and easy to connect. Sound quality is not bad for the price. I just got these and will update more as I use them.

title: Stopped working
text: We have barely had this computer for a year and it just stopped working. My son plays minecraft on it, thats it. I guess you get what you pay for and i shouldve bought a better computer for him. Very disappointed, do not buy this

title: Great product!
text: This is a very nice radio. Lots of functions and easy to use, this will definitely come in handy in the future with the hurricanes we get here and even for camping. I like the 2 light functions and the siren and the fact that you can charge in multiple ways!

title: True to the picture
text: I loved this case! It fits my HP laptop like a glove. It's perfect to take to school everyday!

title: Feels nice and decent print
text: This feels nice and holds the device as advertised. The print quality is decent and it made a nice present for my dad to go with his new tablet!

title: Excellent charger for several different electronics
text: This was easy to assemble with a single click and a plug in. It does not come with a block charger and instead has a USB to plug into a block or other power source. It charged my iphone 11 and Apple Watch perfectly overnight. Plus it has the ability to charge other items such as AirPods and over the ear headphones. Great value for the price. It looks nice and isn’t too clunky and it feels sturdy.

title: High quality picture
text: These are fantastic in our office. They are high quality and the price point for a pack of four is great. These easily compare to our nest cams in terms of picture quality and ease of use, if not a little better.

title: Easy to set up and go
text: These were a breeze to install and connect to our iPhones. We used it in our office space to monitor for in and out traffic and it works fabulously. There is a slight delay and the picture quality is not as nice as other ones we have had in the past (Nest, Arlo, etc) but the price is decent for this camera.

title: Comfortable, difficult to pair
text: Overall, I do like these, they are functional for the most part, and the color is very attractive. I frequently have issues with these pairing with my laptop and sometimes they disconnect despite having full battery. The left one of my set frequently cuts in and out so I have taken to just using the right one as it gets to be too irritating after longer uses (class or watching a movie).

title: Great if you get the right size
text: Fit on our iPad Air 2 just fine. I did have a little trouble with bubbles initially but managed to get it to lay flat. It didn’t come with the dust protector film or the line up guide. It feels thick but I am worried about getting it off when the time comes. It seems very very sticky. Also looking at other reviewers, buyer beware the sizing inconsistencies.

title: Great for privacy and reducing migraines
text: These are great for privacy and maintaining HIPAA compliance in our pediatric office. Everything is visible from straight on but you can’t make it out from the side. This fit on our 24” monitor perfectly and the little sticky pieces have keep it flat and flush to the screen. These are also good for reducing brightness and migraines (another tip for screen induced migraine is the change the display settings to reduce blue or simply manually drop it). Very pleased with this one and will be ordering more for the other computers in our office.

title: Not as great as I had hoped
text: This is a beautiful watch, if a little big. I wasn’t expecting it to be so big so I’m afraid I won’t get much use out of it as I have pretty small wrists. It essentially eats my wrist when I put it on. It also seems to run out of battery really fast. I have an older fitbit blaze that I am very used to using and it will hold a charge for 3-4 days, this needs to be charged daily which I really don’t like. I can’t track both steps/activity and sleep because it needs to spend some of that time on the charger. It looks really beautiful and fits in wonderfully with my other rose gold jewelry. There is a heck of a learning curve with this thing though. I have another fossil smart watch with a manual watch face (not a screen) and that thing is impossible to use for me. This is better but I still don’t have the hang of it after spending over an hour trying to figure it out.

title: Thick case and a good value
text: This is a sturdy, nice feeling case. It fit our iPad Air 2 perfectly. I love that it comes with a strap as we use these in our therapy office for children to work with and I have no worries about them damaging the iPads with these. Our clients like it because it almost looks like they have “kitty ears”. We liked it so much we bought one for each therapist in our office. The screen protector is a little difficult to use as it rests over the screen and causes a gap that means you have to press down fairly hard for a movement to be read. This isn’t ideal for working with a child on an AAC program or a taker board and we have had a few kids get frustrated with this.

title: Bright, easy to clean, and a good value
text: At a little under $10 per cushion and the crate, this is a pretty good option for a small group seating arrangement in a classroom or in a therapy space. As a play therapist, I am always looking for things that can do multiple things or that I can use in multiple ways because with all the stuff I accumulate, I need to make the most out of my space. These have multiple colors which is great for having a kid pick their favorite color to sit on and talk about it. The foam works well with my foamnasium sets and these have become little “roofs” and stepping stones in imaginative play. These clean up easy and can be sanitized quickly with some wipes on both sides which makes it easier to keep kiddos safe in the office. The only thing I don’t love about these is that there Is the same material on both sides. It is a slippery vinyl which can slide around really easily on my floors. If a kiddo wants to use this as a stepping stone or as a part of an obstacle course, I have to break out some rug tape or find another way to keep it from sliding out on them.

title: Beautiful curl but be careful!
text: I was a little nervous to use this because of the heat aspect plus all of the inner booklets/instructions have no English translation on them. It was super straight forward to use. One click on, each subsequent click gets hotter until it’s off. I only used the first heat setting and it was more than enough to curl my lashes. I’m not sure I’ll be using the hotter ones until I get better with it as I don’t want to risk burns. My curl lasted about 6 hours before I really noticed it had gone down. That might have been largely because of the mascara I was using but I will experiment with others. Very pretty “lash lift” type of effect. You do have to put on mascara first, then use this curler so make sure you clean it well after each use. It comes with a little clear cover for the end which is nice for keeping it in my makeup case.

title: Cute and functional
text: I love this sleeve. It's cute but VERY sparkly, which was something that I wasn't sure I'd like at first but I ended up loving it. Ithas thick padding to protect my Mac book Air 13", and arrived quickly. The only negative is that the Kate Spade metal "label" on the side is slightly crooked. It isn't horrible, so I'm keeping it, but I do find myself trying to straighten it sometimes. Otherwise, I haven't had any issues, though I've been babying my laptop, so I haven't had to test to see how well it protects just yet.

title: OMG I love alexa
text: We’ve all experienced with Siri. Alexa it’s her much smarter sister. She’s funny she’s always on and she understands me every time. She’ll tell a funny joke she’ll find the exact song I ask for she helps with homework she is like having Mrs. Doubtfire in your living room. Did I tell you I love her I want one in every room of my house now

title: Wires break
text: Bought this in March. Wires are very thin and crack like hard plastic but just slightly thicker than hair on your head.

title: Life changing for me.
text: I have always fallin asleep to the tv on. I wore the wired ear buds but had to only wear 1 as It hurt to lay on your side wearing it. And you had the wire you get tangled in when I rolled over and I had to switch ears and locate the other bud to fit properly thus disturbing my sleep longer. This is so comfortable to wear. Blacks out light completely. I am able to open my eyes and look around while wearing them. There is a velvet roll fir the nose you can adjust for the gaps there completely blocking al light. My ears do not hurt in the morning and I am getting better quality of sleep. I started sleeping to brown noise rather than a tv show as it is constant not up and down loud noises. My only downside I could find was the placement on the ears. I must have a big head as it does not fit perfectly over my ear as I would like but not enough to hate them. Thet last all night 9-10 hours and I recharge them every morning when I get up so they are ready.

title: NOT JUST FOR KIDS
text: I bought a blue one for my sons and he has thrown his ipad and dropped it and not so much as a scratch. He is 6. So I bought this one for me cause I am prone to drop things and be a little careless and I have dropped my tablet and do not worry as I know this will protect it. Best thing out there.

title: Lightweight, Compact, and Sturdy
text: I tried this handy, handsome hub with both my Chromebook and my iPad Pro. It worked perfectly. It is nicely designed and provides extra connections for thumb drives or peripherals on the go. It's very nice-looking small, and sturdy without being heavy. I added it to my computer case right away. You may want to do the same.

title: Lightweight, Compact, and Portable
text: I'm using this hub to connect devices like my keyboard, headphones, and mouse that don't draw much power. It's also great for thumb drives. I use powered hubs for my big external drives. It might work for them too, but they are hooked up and I didn't want to unhook them. The little hub is fast and efficient. It would be great for laptops too. It's small and would tuck easily into a laptop bag or even a purse. Handy little device!

title: So pretty, so practical at a great price
text: So far, these generously sized thumb drives have worked perfectly for us. They are very pretty, and the price is hard to resist.

title: For its size, this little player has amazing volume
text: Great for listening to stories and lectures, this little portable battery-operated cassette player is easy to use and puts out surprising volume. I wouldn't say the sound quality is great for music, but what do you expect? I use it to listen to audiobooks in my studio.

title: An old-fashioned design, but perfect for places with no electricity or Internet
text: I needed a CD player for my studio, which has no electricity at the moment. This works great. The sound quality is what you'd expect from a smallish portable unit, but it's good enough for what I need. It has a carrying handle which would make it great for picnics or camping. It's not tiny. It's about the size of a loaf of rye bread, which makes the speakers better than the phone-sized units. It's pretty sturdy. I'm ashamed to say it fell out of the box onto the floor when I was unpacking it, but it's fine. (I wouldn't recommend doing that, but just sayin'.) In addition to the CD player, there is an AM/FM radio. All of the controls are easy to use. Perfect.

title: Powerful magnetic mount, but goes on the ourside of most cars
text: If your small camera accepts a screw mount and you have a lot of faith, you can attach it to your car, or any other metal surface, with this powerful magnet mount. I say a lot of faith because, though the magnet is very powerful, and the unit is very well crafted, there aren't any metal surfaces on the dashboards of most cars, so the camera would have to attach to the outside of the vehicle. It does really stick well, but if you want something for your dashboard, this probably won't work.

title: Compact, attractive, lightweight
text: This versatile unit provides multiple plugs and charging ports. The four-sided design allows for transformers. It's great at home. I can keep my smart speaker plugged in the kitchen, along with appliances. It has a surge protector too. I'm not traveling right now, but when I do, this will be wonderful. Hotels never have enough outlets, and airports? Please! It's lightweight and atrtractive. The cord length is just right too. This is a winner. It would make a great gift for a student headed to dorms in the fall, someone off on a road trip this summer, or someone setting up new digs.

title: This little digital microscope is lots of fun
text: It works easily with the camera on my PC. It's easy to use. Just plug it into a USB slot and press the power button. You don't need to install any software. There's a wheel on the side to focus on your subject. It does have a little problem with my AMD display driver sometimes, but it seems to work itself out. (actually, it shuts down my driver and reverts the system to a more primitive one while I'm using it--hmm. Well, it doesn't do any lasting damage, and that's just on my machine.) The picture quality is fine for exploring and great for kids.

title: Makes My iPad Pro much more versatile
text: It charges, shares the screen with HDMI, has an audio connector, and makes sharing files much easier with two card readers and a USB3 port. I found out you can't use the transfer media while you are using the charging port. If you have trouble seeing your thumb drive, unplug the charging cord. Maybe it's just me, but it's no big deal anyway. It works! I like it.

title: Nicely designed, works fine
text: This handy charger with a long cord is great for extended sessions with my iPad. It does everything it is supposed to do. It looks very much like the original charger so it's easy to pack for travel. Great for use at home or on the road.

title: Great design!
text: Why hasn't somebody thought of this before? I love this handy plug station. The four-sided design is brilliant. It's also a charging station for several devices at once. It's great for any room. It looks great and it's very functional.

title: Love this slender, bright easy-to-set clock
text: This clock radio has a large, easy-to-read display. Its slender curved design takes little space on my bedstand. It's easy to set, which I really appreciate. It will make the transition to Standard Time easy in the fall. The projection feature is easy to use too. It projects on the wall. The numbers are clear and bright. The radio's sound quality isn't terrific, but it will wake you up. I don't use that feature very often anyway.

title: Well-built ball head for a professional monopod or tripod
text: Before ordering this, make sure the head of your tripod is removable. Many cheaper models have heads that do not come off. That said, it's easy to attach this to a high-end monopod or tripod (if the original head has been removed.) This professional head is sturdy and well-made. It's easy to tilt, pivot, and fasten down. It has a loop to tighten the quick release base to your camera, but you might want to tighten it a little more with a coin if you're going to be carrying it around. The knob on the quick-release mount is a nice idea. It's easier to use than the usual flip clamp. I like it!

title: Great sound, compact size, good price
text: This soundbar provides great sound and is very easy to install. It's nice-looking, small, and fits under our monitor. We like it very much.

title: Fantastic deal for the price
text: I have some very good cameras that take video, but they are large and heavy and getting them to do time-lapse is tricky. I wanted something to film the development paintings in my studio, and later in the season, in the field. So far, I am impressed. This kit comes with an external microphone, a remote control (uses aaa batteries--not included), two rechargable batteries, a charger and cable, a bracket, and a compact case with a belt loop. It does not include a memory card, so you will need to order one if you don't have one on hand. It accepts a variety of sizes (larger is better.) It will prompt you to format the card the first time you use it. The camera is so small and light it fits in the pocket of my winter jacket. Its shape snuggles into the palm of my hand. It has a lot of features that take a while to explore. You can adjust the resolution and the asa, which is amazing for a camera at this price point. It also has a hot shoe, but you probably won't need a video light in most situations because there is one built in. The viewing screen is bright enough to view in full sun and tilts for convenience. It shows you how much battery life you have and whether or not it is recording. So far, I haven't been able to tell what mode I am using by looking at the screen. I also need to figure out how to keep the date and time from recording, but that's on me. I'm sure there's an easy setting. I just need to find it. If you want to film things closer than 2 meters, this isn't the camera for you. There's no automatic focusing. It's set at infinity. You can zoom a little. Of course, the wide angle setting has the greatest depth of field. I think the video quality is just fine for the Internet, which is why I ordered it and the built-in mic worked fine in my test videos. The only thing I had trouble with was the single photo feature. It worked once, but when I tried it again, the camera locked up. I don't really need that anyway. I look forward to making time-lapse artist-at-work videos for my site with this nice little camera! For the price, it's amazing, and it's lots of fun.

title: What a beautiful keyboard!
text: My husband likes to work on his photographs in a darkened room, which makes it hard for him to see the keys on the keyboard. This amazing keyboard lights up and everything is easier for him. It is also more compact than a standard keyboard while offering all of the essential keys, He is very pleased!

title: The 16 x 16 size of this light tent allows you to photograph larger items
text: Many light boxes using this collapsible cube design are 12 x 12, which is a little small. This nice box is just enough larger to accommodate a wider variety of products, natural items, and artwork. It's easy to set up and folds away instantly for storage. There's even a convenient nonwoven storage tote. You can shoot either through the open front or through a hole in the top of the unit (in the middle of the ring of led lights.) Six two-sided flexible matt backdrops are included. The colors are basic and beautiful. This is a great addition to my small studio. It's thoughtfully designed and well made. Anyone who does product photography is sure to find uses for it.

title: Easy set up, take down, and storage
text: This light box is easy to set up and use. It's a great size for photographing small products such as jewelry and miniatures, The lighting is built-in and adjustable. After use, it folds flat. You don't need to be an origami expert to figure it out. This is a very useful accessory for anyone who photographs items for online sales or for recording possessions for insurance purposes. It's well made and does what it was meant to do. I like it!

title: Quality filters
text: These filters are available in many sizes. The 58 mm fits perfectly on my Nikon 50mm 1.4 lens. Like all circular polarizing lenses, once mounted, it turns to provide different levels of filtration. The mount is thin, so this takes a little getting used to, but the glass is fine quality and the results are nice. In certain kinds of light, it enriches color. It's especially good for clouds and water. (If you haven't used the kind of filter before, be aware that it does cut down the amount of light reaching your sensor, especially when turned to maximum. Steady your camera. The set comes in a nice storage box with a drawstring fabric pouch and metal caps for the front and back of the filter unit. The metal caps protect the glass from dust and scratches during transport and storage. Some might like to use the front one while shooting. I don't like it myself. It's very protective, but it's too hard for me to fiddle with when I want to grab a light effect. My regular snap-off lens cap works fine on the front of the filters. Very nice filters! Arrived quickly in fine shape. I'll use them a lot for winter landscapes this year.

title: For a Chromebook or comparably-sized tablets
text: This beautiful padded sleeve is lightweight. An Acer Chromebook is a very close fit. The charger fits in an outside pocket. (It bulges, but it fits. Most of the time, you won't be carrying the charger with you. Chromebooks have a long battery life so that doesn't matter. The case is also good for any medium-sized tablet. An older iPad fits inside with its keyboard case. The metallic-toned rubbery case has handles and a detachable shoulder strap (you may need pliers or a strong friend to help you attach it the first time. The plastic do-hickies are stiff.) The zipper works smoothly and easily. A great way to pamper your Chromebook (or a friend's.)

title: A padded sleeve for tablets
text: Without its accessory keyboard case, my iPad Pro slips easily into this classy padded zipper sleeve. (Smaller tablets fit as well.) There's a separate matching zipper pouch for the charger and bud-style earphones. The set is great for storing your tablet at home or protecting it in a suitcase. It's simple, uncomplicated, and adds very little weight or bulk.

title: This little camera is amazing
text: My husband wanted a camera to put on an HO flatcar and run around his model railroad layout. He'd seen some videos friends made and was eager to try it. This unit is extremely versatile and comes with all sorts of features we didn't need and haven't tried, so you'll have to check other reviews for those. For example, there is no wifi at his layout and he hates smartphones, so we haven't bothered with that, at least not yet. We also did not need the waterproof case or some of the other amazing mounting brackets. When we unboxed the camera and got it out of the waterproof case (took a little figuring out), the next challenge was to find the plugs for the charging cord and the card. The design is sleek and beautiful so that's a trick. Turns out,it's a black rubber flap on the bottom which hinges up. Inserting the memory card was the next trick. At first, I didn't push down hard enough. (it won't go in much at all if you have it turned the wrong way, so don't worry about that--I did.) You have to push down really hard with your fingernail to get it to go in. It has to be all the way in so the outer edge of the card is flush with the outside of the unit. Once we did that, it was easy to turn on and worked great. The camera resolution is absolutely amazing. It's hard to believe something this small and inexpensive could work so well. It isn't the best for the layout because my husband's model railroad has a lot of tunnels. As small as the camera is, it's too tall to fit through them, at least when it's upright. Now, the description says it can be turned. Maybe there's a way to do it that we haven't discovered yet. On that point, I need to add that, while the directions that come in the box are hopeless, there are lots of terrific how-to and unboxing videos for this camera on YouTube. If I can ever get it away from my husband, I'd like to record some of the beautiful hikes and drives we take here in western Colorado. There's a lanyard for your neck for outdoor activities and a bracket for the car. You can also use it as a nanny cam or to monitor your doggie with your phone when you are out. I think everyone is going to have one of these things eventually. One last point, when I was having trouble getting the card in right, I contacted customer service via email. They got back to me with a very polite and useful reply within 48 hours. This camera would make a great gift for almost anybody!

title: Well Made and Very Useful
text: I just bought an iPad to use with Procreate. I write picture books and am taking classes to learn to illustrate them (I'm also an artist.) I have scanned sketches on my PC and need to transfer them to the tablet. These thumb drives do the trick. I can save my files to the thumb drives, then transfer them to other devices easily. Constructed with silvery mat-finished metal, they are sturdy and handsome. There's a loop at the top of each so you can add a tag or attach them to a key chain. They would make a nice addition to a gifted iPad.

title: Fits my iPad Pro 12.9" with WiFi Only Perfectly
text: This handsome, sturdy case fits my new 12.9" iPad Pro and I'm delighted. It snapped right in. The tablet holder swivels if you want to display your screen to someone else or use it as a stand. To remove the tablet from the case, release two small latches at the base of the iPad holder. All of the controls, cameras and connections on my iPad are easy to access with the tablet in the case. The keyboard charges with the same kind of cord as the tablet (but you will need two to charge both at the same time, of course. A charger cord is not included, but you probably have one.) I love it!

title: A mini professional lighting kit for products or portraits
text: This versatile kit is small and easy to store in a drawer, but the lights are bright, easy to set up, and great to use. LEDs make them bright and easy on batteries. If you've used professional lights, you'll recognize the setup. For smaller-scale projects, instructional/sales videos, item photography, spare-bedroom studios, this could just be the lighting solution you are looking for. Impressive for the size and the money.

title: Cleaned up the mess under my desk
text: Some people just have a laptop on their desk. Not me. I have so much to plug in and everything has a cord. Some of the cords are way longer than I need. The result is a tangled black mass. To the rescue, this generous pack of self-adhesive "ties." Ahh--relief. Great buy, especially if you have a lot of corded gear in every room.

title: Easy to install, Comfortable to wear, Great Sound
text: As someone who wears headphones often (I've worn out more than one set) I really appreciate these. They are so comfortable. The sound is wonderful and the mike works perfectly (great for recording and dictation.) Best of all, the USB connection makes set-up a breeze. I have several microphones and a set of speakers--no confusion! Everything just works when I want it too. LOVE!

title: a classic addition to every camera bag
text: If you don't have one, or need a spare, this classic blower is the perfect accessory for every camera nut. Just sueeze a couple of times to blow most dust off your lens and, sometimes, camera body. Lightweight, portable, and practical. It's in my bag. Fewer pesky dust spots to remove from pictures.

title: Not exactly lightweight, but that's a good thing
text: Actually, for a professional tripod with lots of adjustments and a very sturdy footing, this really is about as lightweight as you can get. A young guy wouldn't mind lugging it with his gear to a shoot, but I wouldn't want to carry it very far. However, and this is important, it is very stable. It sits firmly, tilts and pivots smoothly, and does everything a good tripod should. It also has two levels, a carrying strap, and a hook for a weight, if you need it. The feet pivot for firm purchase on uneven ground and the leg adjustments snap in place. It's well-made and stable. :-)

title: Great camera for Demos and Classes
text: I'm going to start taping my painting sessions for online broadcast and this camera is better for the purpose than either my bulky SLR or my cheap Android phone. It provides even light and a quality picture. It even comes with its own handy tripod. It is portable and practical, perfect for my studio.

title: Add USB ports to your laptop
text: This portable, lightweight docking station is powered to give all your devices the juice they need for top performance. You can even plug in HDMI devices, a speaker or headphones, and a mic. It comes with an easy-to-attach stand for table or desktop use, or you can lay it flat. Take it anywhere your laptop goes. A useful addition to an on-the-go or limited space office.

title: Reads all cards except the one I needed
text: If you don't have a Nikon D850 you will love this handy card reader. It has slots for speedy reading of most memory cards, and it even says it would read the kind I use in my D850. Turns out, the reader takes cards that size, but only ones that load on the long side, not the short side. It is well-designed and useful for all my other cards (phones, computers, and other cameras), but I was disappointed that it wouldn't read the card for my beloved 850. It's okay. There are a couple of work-arounds, but that's why I dinged this one star.

title: Easy to use
text: If you want to transfer family VHS tapes to DVD, this is the easiest solution we have seen. You need a VHS player, which isn't easy to get anymore, but if you have one, just attach the device and follow the directions. The video will transfer to a thumb drive (not included.) You can then plug the thumb drive into your computer and write the video to your DVD. (If you don't have a DVD reader/writer in your tower or laptop, you will need one. My husband and I both have them. External drives are easy to find and to use.)

title: We bought this because some people said it captured in AVI. It doesn't
text: The device works fine and the software was easy to install. It has some nice features, but it doesn't capture in AVI, so the quality is just okay.

title: Fantastic Addition to any Photographer's Gear
text: These handy, reusable cloths are not wet, so they'll never dry out as lens wipes can. They don't have fibers or hairs to fall out as air puffers do. They are silky soft, reusable, and even washable. Each one comes in a sealed disposable pouch. (I kept mine and am reusing it.) I have a terrible time with dust on my lens filters, especially on windy days, and cloning out spots with Photoshop takes valuable time. These wipes provide that ounce of prevention we all need. They are also good for eyeglasses, goggles, sunglasses, tablet screens, smart phones, and monitors. They are designed for scratchless cleaning. Good for yourself or as a thoughtful addition to a gift.

title: The sling style isn't the best for me personally, but the size and quality are great
text: I thought I'd like the sling style, but I haven't been able to make it work for me yet. I can't find a comfortable way to carry it, but I suspect a guy might have more luck. I'm just in a rut with conventional cases. That said, this is light-weight and perfect if you need a case that will let you keep your long lens on the camera and grab to shoot on trail treks. It's nice-looking and well made. I may, with practice, or advice from a fellow shooter find out what I'm doing wrong. If you already like or are using this kind of case, you'll probably love this one. Its water-resistance is a terrific feature, and a motivating factor for getting used to it. We have afternoon showers around here, and it would be nice to have protection.

title: A handsome, sturdy padded bag for your DSLR
text: This feather-weight padded carrying case has room for a DSLR with a 200mm lens attached or a body with a lens and a flash unit or external mic. (There are three sections--padded dividers are easy to push aside. There are also compartments on the outside for filters and card cases. It's just the right size to sling over your shoulder as you head out the door. I've used it every day since it arrived.

title: Cuts Wind Noise on Cameras with External Mic Jacks
text: It took my husband and me a while to figure out that not all of our cameras have places to plug in external mics. Before ordering, check your camera body and locate the mic jack. Many point and shoots just use built-in mics. Most DSLRs should be fine. Just use the supplied cord with the little camera picture on it. The other cord is for phones and tablets. Yes, it does work with those. The only problem my husband had was looking through the viewfinder with his ever-present baseball cap on. The cap's bill bumped into the mic's fuzzy cover. Things were fine when he turned the cap around. (more 'tude anyway.) I don't know what "sheerness" or "warmth" mean in regard to this product, but my husband and I like the way it improves our outdoor videos. It's easy to attach to cameras with top shoes and external mic connections. Love it!

title: Well Made and Easy to Use
text: This USB hub is beautifully crafted. It includes a power cord to deliver maximum energy to all of your devices. Each port has a separate on and off switch giving you full control. Blue lights let you know which ports are on. With ten ports, you can keep everything plugged in. No more swapping-out drives or devices. I've purchased many of these hubs over the years, and this one is one of the nicest so far.

title: Never Run Out of AA or AAA Cells Again
text: This handy charger, along with sets pf AA and AAA rechargeable batteries will keep all your compatible devices ready to use. It uses a cord like the one you use to charge your phone to plug into a power adapter (neither included, but we all have lots of those things, right?) When you put the batteries in, (plus and minus not marked, but not hard to figure out) the top front section of the unit turns into a little screen showing the charging status of each battery. Slick! You can do four AAs, four AAAs, or any combination at once. It's fast and turns off when charging is complete. It goet a little warm while charging four AAs, but not hot. My husband and I are going to wonder how we got along without this! A big step up from the last time we tried rechargeable AA cells.

title: Never Lose Your Connection with the Ourside World
text: This great radio picks up AM and FM stations with clear bright sound. There is a separate National Weather Service station. It runs on regular AA batteries or you can generate power for it by turning a crank. It doesn't take many turns to make it work. There is a flashlight with bright steady light, or several flashing patterns to summon help. A metal loop on the side allows you to attach it to a belt or backpack with a carabiner or strap. It's made of lightweight but sturdy plastic. There's a power output and a socket for a headphone. In an emergency, batteries may well run down. Electricity may fail, but you will usually be able to turn a simple crank to keep in touch with news and weather.

title: This is gorgeous and works like a charm
text: I've now had a chance to connect the Bluetooth keyboard in this case to my iPad and it works great. (I have to admit, I had to read the instructions carefully, but once I did, it was easy.) A few hints for connecting the keyboard. 1. Make sure the keyboard is fully charged before you try to sync the Bluetooth to your device. The little red light in the middle on the top right section of the keyboard will turn green when it is ready. 2. Press fn and C (not command) at the same time for up to three minutes. The iPad keyboard should show up under other devices on your iPad when it is connected. As I'm sure you know, you only have to do that the first time you connect. After that, it will sync automatically. I love the features of this keyboard. It has lights under the keys so you can use it in dimly-lit spaces. It fits the new iPad perfectly. Check the model number on the back of your iPad before ordering. You will need a magnifying glass. It is really small. That said, all the buttons and cameras are accessible while the iPad is in the case. It has a full keyboard with full-sized keys, and even has a delete key. If you add your Office and Adobe subscriptions to your iPad and place it in this handsome case, you have a computer to go!

title: Why Didn't Someone Think of This Before?
text: We use long extension cords for seasonal decorations, our snow blower/leaf blower, lawn mover, and electric trimmer. Between uses, they lay tangled together on the garage floor. It took as long to untangle them as it did to complete the chore we needed them for. Finally, we bought plastic reels and wrapped each cord around one of those. It took a long time to wind them though, and, again, they lay in a heap on the garage floor. These heavy-duty velcro-fastening straps are a genius solution. You just gather the cord (or garden hose) into a few loops, attach the strap, and hang it up on the garage wall! (You will need heavy-duty hooks if you want to do that. They are not included.) Next time we need our cords, they will be easy to find, easy to use, and easy to put away. Brilliant!

title: I Love These Little Gadgets
text: Why don't devices come with something like this? I don't know about you, but for quite a while I had a piece of tape over my laptop camera. Now, that's unnecessary. These little sliding lens covers are paper thin, easy to position, and just as easy to use. You can't even see them on your phone, tablet, or computer. I have them on my laptop computer, my Chromebook, and my smartphone and use them all the time. Once placed, you just slide the cover aside when you want to use the camera. The rest of the time it stays covered and remote viewing of your life is disabled (at least visually.) Great invention!

title: Cute Little Mini-easels for your Phone
text: These little easels are sturdy and easy to use. They support your phone at several angles. Once you choose the angle, it stays in place until you change it. I'm going to use it to hold my phone while I film myself painting to share online. I have a flexible device for that purpose, but it's much harder to use. One of these would also be good to hold your phone while you listen to podcasts or watch sports. However you use them, these little beauties will free up your hands.

title: Keep this one in your kit bag at all times
text: I shoot photos for several royalty-free sites and I need a sharp, dependable lens. This one is hard to beat. Sadly, my camera fell on the floor during a recent trip and landed on the front of my older version of this little beauty, smashing the front frame so it would no longer focus. (I had to shoot most of the trip with my $50 Kindle Fire, which did remarkably well (not good for stock sales, but great for memories, sharing online, and painting reference). Anyway, while still on the trip, I ordered this lens so it would be waiting for me when I got home, ready to record the glorious autumn colors in our part of the country. I was delighted to see the box with my mail when I arrived home. It's even better than my old one (which was terrific). It's smoother and quieter with all the sharpness a 50mm can deliver on a full-frame SLR.

title: Destined to be your favorite travel backpack
text: This is a terrific laptop backpack. It is lightweight, but sturdy. My Dell desktop-replacement laptop doesn't fit in some backpacks, but it slips into this one perfectly. I bought a briefcase-style case which does fit, and that one has room for my Fire too, but not much else fits into it except the charging cables. This one is different. Not only is there plenty of room for (in addition to the tablet, phone, wallet, and glasses) noise-canceling headphones and snacks, but cables, a camera, a sweater, your personal travel pharmacy, a magazine or two, and more. In fact, if you're just going somewhere overnight, this might be all you need. There are many well-crafted pockets, all accessible from both inside and out. The padded backpack straps are strong and comfortable. There's also a handle on top and a wide strap along the back so you can slip it onto your wheeled bag for those dashes across airports between planes. Wonderful backpack for business travelers, writers, or anyone who can't do without their electronics.

title: Great Deal on a Travel Classic
text: I haven't had time to explore all the features on my new Fire (my old one died right before a trip a couple of weeks ago--sniff), but it came quickly, in perfect condition, and was easy to set up. It charged enough to use in a flash. I've already set it up for Twitter and Facebook and have downloaded my most recent book purchases (useful during my husband's dental appointments and trips to hobby shops). I like this size better than the larger ones because I use tablets most on trips or in waiting rooms. This is big enough to see (you can change the print size), but not awkward. I see that it accommodates removable storage, but I haven't tried that yet. I haven't used Alexa either, but that doesn't mean I won't. I use dictation software for writing on my laptop, so talking to the computer isn't completely foreign. I'm not used to having it talk back yet, though, and it isn't that great a feature on a plane or in a waiting room where I usually use it right now. So far, though, overall, I am very pleased with my new Fire, and the price is perfect!

title: A lightweight, sturdy mono-pod for hikers, birders, bikers, and other camera buffs needing portable support
text: For times when handheld isn't steady enough and a tripod is awkward, this compact, lightweight, but sturdy mono-pod is a great addition to an amateur or semi-pro's gear bag. It adjusts down to 17 inches for storage, carrying, and tabletop use. It has four snug-fitting but easy to twist adjustment wheels (not clips). Fully extended, it's five feet long. A screw-on rubber tip is on the foot when delivered. An alternative substantial screw on metal tip for use in loose ground is also included. If you need greater stability, you can purchase accessory "feet" from Amazon. A handy wrist strap is attached to the mono-pod (removable, if it gets in your way). If you prefer, the unit comes in a beautiful sturdy black nylon zipper pouch with an adjustable shoulder strap. The camera mount has two screw sizes (one screw with two different ends). My Canon DSLR wouldn't fit the way it came, but I just unscrewed the top, turned the screw around, and put it back together. Perfect.

title: Whatever you want to take with you, this thumb drive will do the job
text: Small but mighty, this thumb drive holds tons of information. It loads and downloads with lightning speed. The retracting design means there is no cap to get lost when it's in your bag or pocket. Whether you're keeping documents, photos, or novels, this handy transfer and storage device will be your new best friend.

title: Compact, lightweight tote for electronics
text: On my last trip, while juggling a heavy bag on one shoulder as I pulled my new Amazon wheeled carry-on, I noticed that other travelers had their computers in bags that slipped over the trolley handle. There and then I decided I needed a new bag for my electronics. This one fills the bill. My Dell laptop fits perfectly (and it isn't a skinny one). There's also a pocket in the front for my Fire tablet in its keyboard case, with room for my cables. There's a strap in the back that slips over my wheeled carry-on's handle, just like the ones I saw other people using. No more sore shoulders or cramped up fingers for me. Thanks, AmazonBasics!

title: Handy way to back up and transfer files
text: These great thumb drives are big enough to transfer lots of photographs, research, and manuscripts from one computer to another, or to back them up. Great also for mailing. They are fast to use and a handy size to carry. The plugs retract into the sleek black bodies (big enough not to disappear into your pocket, purse, or camera bag.)

title: Make More Room in Your Office--Share One Monitor, Keyboard, and Mouse between Two Computers
text: If you remember the old game unit switches that allowed you to use multiple devices on one television set, this is like that, only for two computers sharing one monitor, keyboard, mouse, and other peripherals. The simple switch box connects to your monitor ("console") via the kind of cord with plugs on both ends you currently use to connect your monitor to your computer. (You will need an extra cord like this for the the purpose--not included. If you don't have a spare lying around, you should order one with the unit.) You will need the cords you are currently using for each of the two computers to connect them to the box. There are four USB sockets in the "console" section of the box. You plug your keyboard, mouse, and anything else you want to share between the two computers into those. (By the way, KVM stands for Keyboard, Video,Mouse.) The unit is powered, and offers multiple plug styles for international use. There is a place to plug in speakers and a mike for each computer. This switch has made it possible for me to streamline my office space considerably. Previously, I had two monitors, two keyboards, and two mice. It was very awkward. I kept my old computer because it has Adobe CS4, which is fine for my needs and saves me the $50 a month the Creative Cloud would cost. I have not used it much, though. Firing up the old machine was just too much trouble. This new arrangement allows me to flip a switch and access programs I have not been able to use in a long time.

title: Handy beginner's recorder for dictating text for transcription
text: I have another portable digital recorder, which shall remain nameless because it came with no directions and fought with my computer when I tried to download files. This one is SO much better. It is like night and day. It is easy to use and came with clear instructions. It downloads files to my Windows 10 computer (Windows Media format) with the included USB cord (short, but works fine). It's on Dragon's approved list and the files were transcribed like a charm (Dragon 13 Professional), It will make dictating the rest of my novel while on winter walks much easier. It has plenty of storage and long battery life. I used the memo mode for dictation. I spoke directly into the mike at the top of the unit. There's also a place to plug in a microphone, if you want to do that. It is small, light and does everything I want it to do. It will also record musical performances and lectures. There are other settings for that. I love it!

title: If you have a new ultra-thin laptop, you need this fast, handy hub
text: If you have one of the new ultra-thin computers, you have found out that your old usb accessories, such as external drives, won't plug into it. That's because the computer case is, well, ultra-thin. Here's the answer to your problem. This lightning-fast powered hub allows you to plug in three old-style accessories, plus one with the new skinny USBc. (The plug is the same top and bottom, so you won't have to fiddle around trying to find the right way to insert it.) Because it's powered, you can use juice-hungry devices like drives. For travel, it's light as a feather and pocket small. The kit even comes with a universal power adapter for globe-trotters (universal power adapter -- NA/EU/UK/AU).

title: Great Connection! Watch Prime (or your own slide shows) Whatever Your Computer Shows Can be on the Big Screen
text: This great cable connects your computer or other HDMI device to a television. You can watch slides, presentations, web content, or anything you can see on your computer on the flat screen. It's small and easy to pack for on-the-go compatibility. The length is just about right to set your device on a nearby table or chair. The quality of the connection was great between my Dell Windows 10 laptop and my Vizio smart TV. Very easy set up. Just plug in, find the input on the TV and navigate with your computer or device. Love it.

title: Practical Hub for External Drives
text: I bought this hub for my husband's computer and he loves it. He appreciates the indicator lights and the switches so he can turn the ports on and off.

title: Lose Weight, Feel Great--No Subscription Fees
text: I love this gadget! It's very comfortable. I probably would have bought it just for the watch--time and date synched to the Internet--with no metal touching my skin (I'm allergic to nickel and watches make me break out.) It keeps track of my footsteps and movement while I'm asleep, It syncs to a free fitness community where I can enter everything I eat. (I admit, I don't always do this, but I've learned how many calories were in some foods I thought were healthy snacks. No wonder I gained so much weight!) Anyway, in a little more than a month, I've lost 10 pounds and I'm getting in shape for spring hikes, in spite of 27 degree high temps in our area. I don't have a smart phone. You don't need one for this. You sync the device with your computer. There's no subscription or any charge outside of the price of the band. It lets you know how many steps you have walked, how many miles you have gone, and how many calories you have burned, as well as the date and time. It's easy to read, and a red line tells you when to get up and move, if you've been sitting at your computer for too long. I recommend it!

title: I love this SDHC card
text: I love this SDHC card. I have two of them for my travel cameras. They hold tons of stills and videos. They have been fast and dependable for me.

title: I especially like the pivot feature
text: We have a lot of outlets in our house, but there are never enough. This surge protector plug set helps. I especially like the pivot feature.

title: at least they are easy to replace
text: Why do these always get lost? Well, at least they are easy to replace.

title: This great little filter protects my lens and cuts glare without ...
text: This great little filter protects my lens and cuts glare without changing colors or adding distortion of any kind. I love it.

title: Five Stars
text: These inexpensive little speakers are simple to install and work very well.

title: Strange Problem with my Desktop
text: When I plug this into my computer something strange happens. The driver installs, and it works, but when I try to turn my computer off, the computer goes to sleep and won't either turn off or wake up until I disconnect it. I leave hubs plugged in with external drives connected and this one won't work that way. I am going to use it with my laptop. I will unplug the hub each time with that computer, so it won't matter, but I'm going to have to buy another one for my desktop.

title: Works great
text: So far, this device is terrific. It adds ten ports for printers, thumb drives, camera usb cords and more. Even better, it's USB3 with its own power supply, so its fast. I've been using it about a month.

title: Beautiful
text: From the time I opened the elegant package I was impressed. The tablet was easy to connect and works perfectly with my Windows 7 machine. It comes with some wonderful graphics software, including Adobe Elements 11. You download it when you register the device. The registration process was simple. I haven't had time to explore all of its possibilities yet, but am looking forward to doing illustrations.

title: Western Digital Rocks
text: This addition to the My Book line works as well for me as my previous external drives from the same company. So far, it is fast,, cool, and quiet. It really is about the size and shape of a paperback thriller, so you can store it on a shelf. Three terabytes is a lot of space! I haven't made a dent in it yet.

title: I love these marble mice!
text: These little goodies are getting hard to find in our neck of the woods, so I really appreciate being able to order them from Amazon. I am left-handed and for some reason regular mice drive me nuts. These (this is at least my fourth one over the years) are amazing. They are easy on my hands, fingers and wrists. They don't scoot all over your desk. The marble moves. The mouse doesn't. I don't know why anybody uses anything else. The only thing that might be better would be a tablet, because it would be easier to draw.

title: Thousands of Pictures
text: I used this card in my travel camera on a recent trip to New York and it performed perfectly. There's room for stills and videos and space to spare. If you need more room, its tiny size allows you to pack a spare or two. In my Canon point and shoot, it was lightning fast and dependable.

title: Works great!
text: When I ordered my Canon point and shoot travel camera, it was "reconditioned". It was sent with an off-brand battery instead of the original. It would not hold a charge and stuck in the camera. It would come out, but with great difficulty, so I ordered this one, which works great!

title: Super Powered Hub for 12 Devices
text: I used to have three different smaller hubs to connect my printers, scanner, external drives, keyboard, mouse, speaker headphones, etc. I have replaced all of them with the Satechi 12 Port USB hub. I've been using it for about a month now and am delighted. In fact I bought another one for my husband's computer. It has its own power supply, so it doesn't slow your computer down the way hubs without a plug can, and it runs all the peripherals at lightning speed. It has two switches so you can use 6 plugs at a time or all 12. You can tell when they're powered on because beautiful blue lights come on. So cool (runs cool too)! Looks like a space ship. Its design is simply elegant--light and slim. It even has a sticky strip to attach it to your computer, if you want to. I am very pleased.

title: Great to Have a Spare
text: I'm always misplacing my cords. It's great to have a spare. This one does what it was meant to do.

title: Came fast, works great!
text: We couldn't find the charger that came with the camera, so we ordered this one. It's great! Does the job. (Of course, as soon as it came, the other one showed up, but it is handy to have a spare.

title: An excellent haze filter
text: I use it mainly to protect the front element of my telezoom, but it subtly cuts haze in landscapes without distortion or color bias. I like it very much.

title: A Winner
text: I shoot western Colorado landscapes for microstock sites. I need a camera with low image noise, smooth focus, long battery life, and durability. I love Nikon. I have had Nikon SLRs since I started shooting stock in the late 70s. They are dependable, quality instruments. The D80 is no exception. No point-and-shoot, it feels like my old F2. It takes beautiful pictures in all kinds of weather. You will need at least one extra battery. The battery life is long--three or four 2 gig cards worth of RAW pictures, for me--but you will want this baby with you all the time. I bought the body only, because I had the lens from my D70, but you will want a VR zoom or a fixed lens for maximum sharpness. I don't like tripods and don't use them as often as I should. The remote is useful for closeups. It helps you avoid camera shake, especially in low light.

title: Sound is important it sounds great
text: Out side on the deck for the tv

title: It's a great little thing to have . We love it.
text: We love this little black ball (eco dot) it can answer your questions look up an answer play music and it sound is great. What did we ever do without it.I would buy it again.

title: That it works to rid my neck from pain
text: For virtue teaching this is great. The height is perfect no more neck pain from looking down.

title: That it does what it said it would do
text: Works great electric bill is already down

title: Great toy to draw on and erase.
text: My grandson loves this he plays with it for hours.

title: sylvania 10 inch portable DVD playet
text: My husband loves it good sound nice picture.Takes it yo work to watch during lunch or fown time.He loves it.

title: Exceeded my expectations
text: I got this watch for my 12 yo father who is very active. It works well and I like it had a setting menu both on the watch and the app. I am not sure about the accuracy of the body temperature and other physical elements but it looks accurate for steps and sleeping monitor. Good value for the money.

title: Perfect size!
text: The band is beautiful, it clicks perfectly in the Fitbit charge 2!

title: Great for all sizes
text: Each of our kids have a pair, they adjust to all size heads and are comfortable.

title: App is Amazing, Watch is Garbage
text: I am torn when it comes to this smartwatch. First, you track everything through an app on your phone, which I like a lot better than just the watch itself. I can keep up with everything on the app and see my progress and how my blood pressure, steps, heart rate, and all that stuff is doing over the course of months. It helps to see the changes and non-changes. I love that and more smartwatches need these types of details. The major problem I have with this smartwatch though is the actual watch itself. You are supposed to be able to swipe through the different things on the watch but you literally can't most of the time. You have to press down so hard and hope that it swipes but usually, it doesn't and you have to keep trying and trying. It's so freaking annoying and complete trash. It's just a high tech watch that you can't use for anything else that it says you can use it for. Such as taking pictures, using it as a remote, and even control your music from the watch. I have managed to get to the program on the watch but unable to use it because of not being able to swipe or use the watch at all. Oh, and there is only one button on the watch itself, which controls the power and turning the light on and off. That's it, doesn't control anything else. So while I am super impressed with the app and all the functions this offers the watch is freaking useless itself. It does, however, track your steps, heart rate, blood pressure, and even how long you sleep, but don't expect to see much of these through the watch itself but mainly through the app. Such a disappointment.

This has another zipper on the side. Inside the reflector's zipper is a diffuser which you will need to remove from the larger pouch to use. This is where the mounting tab is located. You will need the mounted clip that is available as part of the kit, or you may purchase it separately. That's not all. The large, outer pouch is reversible, so you then reverse the large pouch and you have a gold reflector one one side or a solid white on the opposite side. This is how you have black, white, gold, silver and a diffuser all in one. The diffuser has it's own tap to clip on your tripod, which pokes through from a button hole to mount the entire piece. You will need to make sure it's pulled through if you remove the outer layer of the reflector. This is a good purchase for the value. I'm a hobbyist, and sometimes take photos of my projects. My problem comes from being a night-shift worker. I live and work at night. I must make my own lighting setup if I want to photograph anything at night, even in my home. It's light weight, and folds to a small circle, so this is also portable. It weighs less than a pair of jeans. Here's a free tip: Only use the gold if your subject is brown. I don't find the gold reflector so useful. I'm glad it's available, but I doubt it will get much use for me. Also, place the reflector in a way that would mimic the sun's light, and your subject will look more natural. This is where the clips and extension arms from your tripod can come in handy if you are working solo. Of course, you can always enlist the assistance of another for outdoor shoots. Sometimes this is a best option if it's available. In the movies, they tend to show someone holding a reflector with it facing up towards the subject, but that's only because it does look silly holding a big disc over your head. If you hold it, you will need to hold it up over your head, and it will look silly but your photos will not. It's a good tool to have on hand for any level of photography. I mostly photograph my doll collection. Once or twice a year, our doll collectors group will gather outdoors for shoots. We've not had a reflector available to us before, so this will help us immensely finding good spots to make photographs, even if the clouds are moving or we want to setup under trees. I also ordered the 2-pack clips. These are nice because they come with an adapter on them. If you remove the threaded black female cylinder and threaded ring, you are left with a standard sized male mount that will fit a tripod base. You do not need to make a separate purchase for an adapter, it's already there. The ball joint swivels all the way around and there is a groove in the base to tilt the clip in towards the base, so you can use these clips for holding the reflectors, diffuser or even a backdrop on a side or top mount adapter of your backdrop frame. title: Worst Tripod I've Ever (Tried)! Poor Engineering!
text: I really wanted to use this. I absolutely hate this tripod. I own several. Upon extending the legs to set it up, it broke and I cannot fix it. There are these little thin, plastic tabs inside each piece of tubing that extends. The washer came off, the plastic tabs went flying, I placed them back, and the leg was stuck. I tried to retrieve them to try placing it again, and they were lost in the larger section of tubing. I carefully and methodically removed the larger washer to find the tabs, and they were so far up inside I couldn't retrieve them, so I replaced the plastic tabs from the larger piece, carefully placed it back... and low and behold those disappeared inside as well. This is the worst engineered product I have ever encountered in my life. I cannot fathom paying anything for this. It's worthless garbage to me now. It cannot be used. I feel sorry for all the people that spent precious time of their life designing, manufacturing, selling and shipping this piece of trash. An entire tripod leg will no longer fix into place, because of these thin plastic tabs. Maybe this could have been saved by threading the adjustment washers differently, or even a piece of tape holding the plastic tabs. I cannot say for sure. What I can say is, this would be a waste of money. It's much too easy to unscrew the washers, then those tabs come out. They cannot be placed back. Once they are inside the tube, they are gone. If I can somehow manage to fix this, I will update. Until then, don't waste your money. I would not even recommend this to someone I don't like. Thanks for reading my review. I hope you have found it helpful.

title: Great Microphone for Hobbyists, Gamers and Bloggers
text: A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones. The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup. I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point. Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
